parts.prose: MFA is enforced for all users with privileged rights (e.g., administrators). Recovery codes are provided in case the user loses access to their second factor.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The application checks at login if a user belongs to the administrators group. If so, and MFA is not enabled, the user is forced to set up MFA before they can proceed. During MFA setup, the user is shown single-use recovery codes, which they must store securely.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: An attempt is made to log in as an administrator without MFA enabled. It is checked whether the application denies the login and forces MFA setup. The process for using recovery codes is tested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to TOTP, modern, phishing-resistant MFA methods such as FIDO2/WebAuthn are supported. The implementation of MFA is robust against bypass attempts, e.g., by exploiting the recovery function.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to or as an alternative to TOTP, users can register a security key (e.g., YubiKey) via WebAuthn for authentication. The account recovery process itself is multi-layered and strictly logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The implementation of WebAuthn is checked for compliance with the standard. The account recovery process is analyzed for potential vulnerabilities that could allow an attacker to bypass the MFA requirement.

controls.title: Prevention of resource blocking (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Resource-intensive operations are generally avoided. If they are necessary, basic protective measures are implemented, e.g., a simple limitation of the result size.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data export function limits the number of exportable records to 1,000 to prevent database overload.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: It is checked whether resource-intensive functions exist and whether basic limits (e.g., for data volumes or execution time) are implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To protect against Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks, resource-intensive operations SHOULD be avoided. If they are necessary, they SHOULD be specially secured, e.g., through asynchronous processing and rate limiting.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A complex reporting function is not executed synchronously. Instead, the application accepts the request, processes it in the background (e.g., via a message queue and worker processes), and notifies the user when the report is ready. The invocation of this function is additionally protected by a strict rate limit.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The architecture of resource-intensive functions is analyzed to check if they are processed asynchronously. It is tested whether the rate limits for these functions are effective.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For web applications, a possible overflow of logging data SHOULD be monitored and prevented. The application's resource usage is actively monitored, and alarms are triggered when thresholds are exceeded to detect DoS attacks early.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Log rotation is configured to prevent uncontrolled growth of log files. Monitoring tools continuously monitor the application's CPU and memory usage as well as response times. If defined thresholds are exceeded, a warning is automatically sent to the operations team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The log rotation configuration is checked. The monitoring system and the configured alarms for resource usage are analyzed. A load test is performed to observe whether the monitoring responds as expected.

controls.title: Cryptographic protection of confidential data (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Confidential data (except passwords) is encrypted in the database, but a key hard-coded in the code is used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Sensitive user data is encrypted with AES before being stored. However, the AES key is stored as a constant in the source code or in a configuration file that is delivered with the application.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The source code and configuration files are searched for hard-coded cryptographic keys.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Confidential data of a web application SHOULD be secured by secure cryptographic algorithms. The algorithms and key lengths used must comply with current recommendations (e.g., from the BSI). Key material must be managed securely.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For encrypting data at rest, AES-256 in GCM mode is used. The necessary key is not stored in the source code but is loaded from a secure external source, e.g., an environment variable or a dedicated secret management system (like HashiCorp Vault or AWS KMS).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The data encryption code is checked for the use of recommended algorithms and modes. The key management process is examined and it is verified that the keys are not stored with the application code.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cryptographic keys are rotated regularly and automatically. A Hardware Security Module (HSM) or a comparable cloud service is used for key management to provide the best possible protection for the key material.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The application is integrated with an HSM. All cryptographic operations take place within the HSM, so the key never leaves the module. An automated process is established that rotates the used Data Encryption Keys at regular intervals (e.g., every 90 days).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The configuration of the HSM connection is checked. The key rotation process is analyzed and it is verified that it works automatically and reliably. It is checked whether the HSM logs prove correct usage.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Web applications provide specific functions and dynamic (changing) content. To do this, web applications provide documents and user interfaces, e.g. in the form of input masks, on a server and deliver them on request to corresponding programs on the clients, e.g. to web browsers. Web applications are usually developed on the basis of frameworks. Frameworks are reusable program templates for frequently recurring tasks. Frameworks also exist for security components.
Web applications must implement security mechanisms that ensure the protection of the processed information and prevent its misuse. Typical security components or mechanisms are authentication, authorization, input validation, output encoding, session management, error handling, and logging.
Developers must be familiar with the relevant security mechanisms of a web application. For this reason, the development process has a decisive influence on the security of the subsequent software.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The goal of this module is to develop secure web applications and to protect information that is processed by a web application.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module is to be applied to every development project in the information network in which web applications are developed.
This module considers the specific threats and requirements that are relevant to the development of web applications. Requirements for the secure use of web applications are not considered in this module. They can be found in module APP.3.1 Web Applications and Web Services. Likewise, general requirements for the secure development of software are dealt with elsewhere. They are covered in module CON.8 Software Development.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Bypassing authorization in web applications
parts.prose: In an attack, an attempt is often made to access functions or data of web applications that are only available with specific access rights. If the authorization is implemented incorrectly, it may be possible to obtain the permissions of another account with more extensive rights and thus access protected areas and data. This is done, for example, by specifically manipulating inputs.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Insufficient input validation and output encoding
parts.prose: If a web application processes unchecked input data, protection mechanisms may be bypassed. This risk increases if, at the same time, the output data of the web application is transmitted directly to the web browser, the calling application, or to downstream IT systems without sufficient encoding. Such output data can contain malicious code that is interpreted or executed on the target systems. For example, in an attack, JavaScript code can be entered into form data. This malicious code is then unintentionally executed by the IT system that processes the web application with the data.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Missing or deficient error handling by web applications
parts.prose: If errors occur during the operation of a web application that are not handled correctly, both the operation of the web application and the protection of its functions and data can be compromised. For example, an error can lead to the web application no longer being executed correctly and becoming unreachable for clients. Furthermore, actions may only be carried out incompletely, cached actions and data may be lost, or security mechanisms may fail.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Insufficient logging of security-relevant events
parts.prose: If security-relevant events are insufficiently logged by the web application, security incidents can be difficult to trace at a later time. The causes of an incident may then no longer be determinable. For example, configuration errors can be overlooked if they do not lead to error messages in the log files. Vulnerabilities are also difficult or impossible to detect and fix with insufficient logging.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Disclosure of security-relevant information by web applications
parts.prose: Web pages and data generated and delivered by a web application can contain information about the background systems, e.g., details about databases or framework versions. This information can make it easier to carry out targeted attacks on the web application.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Misuse of a web application through automated use
parts.prose: If functions of a web application are used in an automated way, numerous operations can be executed in a short time. With the help of a repeatedly executed login process, an attacker can, for example, try to guess valid combinations of accounts and passwords (brute force). In addition, lists of valid accounts can be generated (enumeration) if the web application returns information about existing accounts. Furthermore, repeated calls to resource-intensive functions, such as complex database queries, can be abused for Denial-of-Service attacks at the application level.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Insufficient session management of web applications
parts.prose: Insufficient session management can make it possible to determine the session ID of accounts with extensive access rights without special access rights. Subsequently, in an attack, this ID can be used to access protected functions and resources of the web application, e.g., in the form of a session fixation attack. Here, a session ID with limited rights is first obtained from the web application. This ID is transmitted to persons with higher legitimacy, e.g., via a link in an email. If the persons with higher legitimacy follow this link and authenticate themselves to the web application under the session ID, attackers can then use the application with the full access rights of the legitimate accounts.

groups.title: Confidentiality Protection VS-NUR FÜR DEN DIENSTGEBRAUCH (VS-NfD)

controls.title: Compliance with the principles for processing classified information with IT according to § 3, 4 and 6 and No. 1 Annex V of the VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is known that special rules apply to the processing of VS-NfD, but systems declared as classified IT are only used sporadically. The 'need-to-know' principle is implemented only sporadically and mostly at an organizational level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, there is often no central policy. Individual departments try to implement the requirements, for example, by using a separate notebook for VS-NfD tasks, but this is not formally approved as classified IT.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks employees in various departments how they handle VS-NfD information. It is checked whether individual, isolated measures for processing classified information exist and whether there is an awareness of the 'need-to-know' principle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Classified information of the secrecy level VS-NfD is generally only processed with IT that is declared as classified IT, but the approval process is not yet fully formalized. The 'need-to-know' principle is consistently enforced organizationally through instructions, but not yet by technical means.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A list of systems used as classified IT (VS-IT) exists. Approval is granted by the IT department, but without a complete security concept. Access permissions are set manually at the file system level by administrators upon instruction from the specialist department.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the list of declared classified IT systems with the systems actually used. Spot checks of access permissions to classified data are taken to verify that they correspond to the 'need-to-know' principle and are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: CI of the classification level VS-NfD MAY ONLY be processed with VS-IT that is approved for this purpose. Private IT MUST NOT be used for processing classified information. When processing CI with VS-IT, the "need-to-know" principle MUST be observed. ONLY persons who need to know about a piece of CI to perform their duties MAY be given access to it. According to the principle of defense-in-depth, personnel, organizational, physical, and technical measures MUST be taken. If deviations from the BSI TL are intended, this MAY ONLY occur in exceptional cases and in agreement with the BSI.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The implementation is carried out through a formal security concept for the VS-IT, which includes an approval process. The "need-to-know" principle is implemented through a combination of organizational policies and technical access controls (e.g., Active Directory groups). The relevant Technical Guidelines of the BSI are taken into account in the design and operation of the VS-IT.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of a valid approval document for the VS-IT in use. It is checked whether a documented authorization concept exists and whether the technical access permissions correspond to it. Conformity with relevant BSI TL is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the "need-to-know" principle is primarily ensured through technical measures. The effectiveness of the defense-in-depth security measures is regularly reviewed and assessed, at least annually. All BSI Technical Guidelines used are fully implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Access to VS data is controlled by technical systems such as Identity and Access Management (IAM). The review of security measures is carried out as part of internal audits. The configurations of the VS-IT are managed using configuration management tools to prevent deviations from the BSI TL.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the IAM system to validate the technical enforcement of the "need-to-know" principle. The logs of the regular security measure reviews are inspected. Automated configuration scans are evaluated to confirm compliance with the BSI TL.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to VS is controlled by a comprehensive, automated rights management system that dynamically enforces the "need-to-know" principle. The entire VS-IT is subject to continuous monitoring, which detects and reports deviations from the security concept and the BSI TL in real time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Privileged Access Management (PAM) system is used. The conformity of the VS-IT is continuously monitored by a Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platform. Any access attempts to VS are logged and automatically analyzed for anomalies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration and effectiveness of the PAM and SOAR systems. The alerting and response processes for detected deviations or anomalies are reviewed. The complete and automated monitoring of the VS-IT is demonstrated using live data and logs.

controls.title: Creation and updating of the VS-IT documentation according to § 12 and No. 2.2 Annex II of the VSA (Security Regulations for Classified Information) (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rudimentary documentation exists for individual VS-IT systems, such as installation guides or network diagrams. However, a coherent VS-IT documentation according to VSA is missing. Updates are only made sporadically when major changes occur.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Documents are stored by various administrators on local drives or in different team directories. There is no uniform structure or template.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation for a specific VS-IT system. It is checked whether any documents exist at all and whether they provide a basic insight into the system. The last modification date is requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VS-IT documentation is created that covers the most important aspects of the VS-IT. It is updated when significant changes are made. A regular, formal review process every three years has not yet been established.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The documentation is maintained in a central location, e.g., a wiki or a dedicated file server. There is a rough outline that is based on the VSA requirements, but may not yet cover all points.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the central VS-IT documentation and compares its structure and content with the requirements from Annex II of the VSA. Samples are taken to check whether the documentation reflects the current state of the systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every agency that uses VS-IT MUST create VS-IT documentation as part of the security documentation for classified information. The VS-IT documentation MUST include all documents listed in No. 2.2 Annex II of the VSA. The VS-IT documentation MUST be updated for all security-relevant changes. It MUST also be reviewed at least every three years for currency, completeness, and the necessity of existing and future security measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A person responsible for maintaining the VS-IT documentation has been designated. A template is used that covers all points of Annex II of the VSA. Changes to the VS-IT trigger a defined process for updating the documentation. The three-year review cycle is scheduled and tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the complete VS-IT documentation and checks it for completeness according to Annex II of the VSA. The currency is verified using the change log of the VS-IT and the documentation. Proof of the last scheduled review (not older than three years) is requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VS-IT documentation is integrated into a central Document Management System (DMS) or CMDB that supports versioning and approval workflows. The review process is automatically triggered and monitored by the system. Essential parts of the documentation, such as the system components, are generated from the CMDB.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DMS like SharePoint or IT documentation software like i-doit is used. Changes to configuration items in the CMDB that belong to the VS-IT automatically trigger a task to review the dependent documentation parts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the DMS or CMDB, especially the workflows for updating and approving the VS-IT documentation. It is verified that the system and inventory lists in the documentation match the data in the CMDB. The audit report of the last automatically triggered review is inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VS-IT documentation is maintained as a 'living document' and is largely automated. Configuration and topology information is read and visualized from the systems in real time. Continuous compliance checks ensure that the documented target state corresponds to the actual state of the VS-IT and that deviations are reported immediately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools for automated network discovery and configuration analysis are used. The results are fed into a central CMDB or a specialized documentation tool. A dashboard visualizes the current compliance status of the VS-IT documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor observes the process of automated documentation creation and updating live. Targeted configuration changes are made to a test system to verify the real-time updating of the documentation. The logs of the compliance checks and the response to reported deviations are analyzed.

controls.title: Use of IT security products according to §§ 51, 52 VSA (Security Regulations for Classified Information) (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For obvious security requirements, such as virus scanners or firewalls, commercial IT security products are used. A systematic identification of all relevant security functions or a comparison with BSI requirements does not take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Product selection is based on market research or existing framework agreements, without specific examination of suitability for VS or approval.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks which IT security products are in use. It is checked on a random basis whether a BSI approval is known for the products used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on an informal analysis, the most important IT security functions are identified. An attempt is made to use products with BSI approval for these functions, provided they are known and readily available. The BSI's VS product catalog is consulted occasionally.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A list of essential security functions (e.g., encryption, VPN) exists. When procuring, a BSI approval is mentioned in the requirements list, but it is not always enforced as a mandatory criterion.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the list of identified security functions. For a selection of functions, it is checked whether the products used are listed in the BSI's list of approved products (BSI publication 7164).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the structural analysis, all IT security functions relevant to the VS-IT MUST be identified. These MUST be assigned to the respective sub-components, taking into account the BSI's VS product catalog. If an approval statement according to BSI TL - IT 01 is required for a product type, a corresponding product according to BSI publication 7164 MUST be used. If no products are listed there, the BSI approval body MUST be contacted. The BSI's provisions for use and operation (SecOPs) MUST be adhered to.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The identification and assignment of security functions is an integral part of the VS-IT security concept. There is a defined process that prescribes consulting the BSI list 7164 and the VS product catalog when selecting security products. The relevant SecOPs are procured and their requirements are implemented in the VS-IT operating manual.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies in the security concept that all relevant IT security functions have been identified and assigned to the system components. For all components identified as requiring approval, proof of the use of an approved product (e.g., by comparison with BSI publication 7164) or of contact with the BSI is requested. It is checked on a random basis whether the SecOPs requirements have been implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process for identifying, selecting, and deploying IT security products is standardized and supported by checklists. Compliance with SecOPs is checked not only during implementation but also regularly during operation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central product management for IT security products maintains a list of approved and certified products for use in VS-IT. The configuration of the products is centrally managed and monitored for compliance with the SecOPs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the checklists and process documentation for product selection. It is checked whether regular audits are conducted to ensure compliance with SecOPs and how the results are handled. The configurations are spot-checked against the specifications from the SecOPs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of all IT security products is managed automatically (Infrastructure as Code). Compliance with SecOPs and other security requirements is continuously monitored through automated compliance scans. Deviations lead to immediate alerts and can trigger automatic corrective actions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration management tools such as Ansible, Puppet, or SaltStack are used to define and enforce the configuration of security products. A SIEM or compliance dashboard visualizes the compliance status in real time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the scripts and playbooks of the configuration management system. The configuration of the automated monitoring system is checked. The logs are used to demonstrate complete monitoring and the response to detected deviations. It is verified that a command such as `ansible-playbook --check playbook.yml` runs successfully on the relevant systems without any planned changes, which proves the conformity of the live system with the code.

controls.title: Procurement of classified IT in accordance with § 49 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before classified IT is procured, it MUST be ensured that its security is guaranteed throughout its entire lifecycle. The tender documents MUST be formulated in such a way that the requirements of the VSA can be fully met. In particular, the aspects of retention, archiving, deletion, decommissioning, as well as maintenance and repair MUST be taken into account in the formulation. Contracts MUST be designed in such a way that data carriers from defective or leased IT products remain in the possession of the agency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Standard text modules are developed for tender documents that cover all VSA-relevant aspects of the IT lifecycle. These modules are used on a mandatory basis for every procurement of classified IT. The legal department is instructed to include the clause on the retention of data carriers in all relevant contracts as a standard practice.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the tender documents for a recent procurement of classified IT. It is checked whether the requirements of the VSA, particularly regarding lifecycle management, are completely and correctly represented. The corresponding contract is then checked to see if it contains the clause on the retention of data carriers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During procurement, it is explicitly required that products from the BSI's list of approved IT security products be offered for assigned IT security functions. In addition, the provider is required to submit a declaration on supply chain security.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The tender documents contain a requirements matrix in which the IT security functions are assigned to the products to be procured. For functions requiring approval, the 'BSI-approved' requirement is defined as a mandatory criterion. There is a standard template for the required supply chain security declaration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the tender documents and the bids received in response. It is verified that the requirement for BSI-approved products was correctly implemented and taken into account in the award decision. The received declarations on supply chain security are checked for plausibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the tender, for products without existing approval, the manufacturer's contractual obligation to cooperate in an approval procedure with the BSI is required. The security requirements for the entire lifecycle are secured by contractual penalties for non-compliance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The procurement and legal departments, in cooperation with the security officer, have developed watertight contract templates that include the obligation to cooperate in the approval procedure and staggered contractual penalties for security breaches. These are used on a mandatory basis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the contracts for procured classified IT and checks them for the presence of clauses on cooperation in the approval procedure and penalties. It is checked whether these clauses were subject to negotiation during contract talks or were enforced as non-negotiable.

controls.title: Commitment upon access to classified information according to § 4 VSA and Annex V to VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before a person is granted access to classified information of the classification level VS-NfD, they MUST be committed to Annex V. A copy of Annex V to the VSA MUST be made available to each person against a confirmation of receipt. If personnel from non-public bodies are granted access to classified information, No. 6.6 of Annex V to the VSA MUST be observed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The commitment process is part of the onboarding process for new employees and is carried out by the HR department or the security officer. The signed acknowledgements of receipt are kept in the personnel file or a separate security file.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly selects employees who have access to VS-NfD and requests the corresponding, signed acknowledgement of receipt for the commitment according to Annex V. It is checked whether the date of the commitment is before the date of the first access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The status of the classified information commitment is recorded and managed in a central system (e.g. HR system). Refresher training on security protection is conducted regularly, at least every five years, and participation is also documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The HR system has a dedicated field for the date of the classified information commitment. The system automatically sends reminders for upcoming refresher training. The training is offered as e-learning or in-person events.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown an extract from the HR system that documents the commitment status of the employees. The evidence of the implementation and participation in the refresher training is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to classified IT systems is technically linked to the commitment status recorded in the central system. A user account is only enabled for access to classified resources after the commitment has been marked as 'completed' in the system. Failure to participate in a required refresher training leads to an automatic deactivation of access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Identity Management (IDM) system reads the commitment status from the HR system and, based on this, automatically controls membership in the corresponding access groups (e.g., in Active Directory).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the IDM system and the workflow for automated rights assignment. A test case is run through (e.g., creating a new user) to verify the process live, from the missing to the completed commitment and the associated rights activation.

controls.title: Supervision and accompaniment of external personnel for classified IT according to §§ 3, 4 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Non-committed external personnel working on classified IT MUST be accompanied and supervised at all times. The accompanying persons MUST have the necessary expertise to be able to monitor the activities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a service instruction regulating the handling of external personnel in security areas. Before work begins, an accompanying person with the appropriate expertise is appointed. The accompanying person is instructed not to leave the external personnel's workstation and to observe all activities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the visitor logs and the corresponding instructions for accompanying external personnel. The accompanying persons are randomly questioned as to whether they had the necessary expertise to monitor the work performed and how they specifically implemented the supervision.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to personal supervision, the activities of external personnel on classified IT are logged by technical measures (e.g. session recording, extended system logging). The logs are evaluated by a competent person after the work is completed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For maintenance work by external personnel, dedicated, temporary user accounts with minimal rights and extended logging are used. Screen session recording tools are used. The evaluation of the logs is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the configuration of the extended logging for external personnel accounts. The recorded session logs and the corresponding evaluation reports for a recent maintenance operation are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Work by external personnel on classified IT takes place exclusively via a hardened maintenance interface (bastion host) that offers live monitoring and the option for the accompanying person to immediately terminate the session. All actions are analyzed in real time and suspicious activities lead to an automatic alert.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Privileged Access Management (PAM) system with session management functions is configured as the sole means of access for external personnel. The accompanying person receives a console on which they can follow the session live and terminate it at the push of a button if necessary.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the PAM system and has the functionality of live monitoring and session termination demonstrated. The logs of the real-time analysis are checked for their effectiveness.

controls.title: Labeling of electronic classified information and data carriers according to §§ 20, 54 and Annexes III, V and VIII to VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Electronic classified information MUST be labeled according to the specifications of the VSA, so that the label is recognizable at all times and is retained during copying processes. E-mails MUST be labeled according to pattern 11 of Annex VIII to the VSA. Data carriers with unencrypted VS-NfD MUST be labeled with the classification level. If the compilation of classified information on a data carrier results in a higher protection requirement, the data carrier MUST be labeled correspondingly higher (e.g. VS-VERTRAULICH).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users are instructed to add the abbreviation 'VS-NfD' to file names (e.g., 'VS-NfD_Protocol.docx'). For e-mails, a template or signature is provided that contains the labeling block. Data carriers such as USB sticks or external hard drives are labeled with physical labels ('VS-NUR FÜR DEN DIENSTGEBRAUCH').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects file directories on classified IT systems on a random basis and checks the file names for correct labeling. Sent e-mails are checked for correct labeling in the subject and body. The inventory of mobile data carriers is checked for physical labeling.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The labeling of electronic classified information is supported by technical means. The file name of an electronic classified document SHOULD contain a label that allows the classified nature to be recognized without having to open the document. It is checked whether IT security products can adopt and enforce the labeling (in the sense of metadata).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Office templates are used that automatically insert a header or footer with the VS-NfD marking. An email add-in forces the selection of a classification level before sending and automatically adds the corresponding marking. Data classification tools are being evaluated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the Office templates and email add-ins demonstrated. It is checked how the system reacts when a user tries to send an email without classification. The evaluation report for the data classification tools is reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A consistent data classification system is implemented that stores the CI marking as metadata in the files themselves. This system enforces labeling at creation and can automatically suggest classifications based on content or context. Other security systems (e.g., DLP, encryption gateways) use this metadata to automatically enforce security policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A solution such as Microsoft Purview Information Protection or Titus is in use across the board. The classification policies are centrally defined. A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) system, for example, prevents files classified as 'VS-NfD' from being copied to unencrypted USB sticks or sent to external email addresses.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the central policies of the data classification system. It is tested whether the system prevents the creation or storage of unclassified documents in CI areas. The integration with the DLP system is verified through practical tests (e.g., attempting to send a file classified as VS-NfD).

controls.title: Management and verification of electronic CI according to § 21 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the management of electronic CI, the principles of proper records management (according to the registry directive) and the requirements of the VSA MUST be observed. Electronic CI classified as VS-NfD MAY ONLY be managed in open (electronic) registries in compliance with the 'need-to-know' principle.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The CI is managed in the normal electronic file (e-file) or in the usual file directories. However, access to the corresponding files or directories is restricted to the group of people who need to know. This is ensured by appropriate authorization groups.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the file plan and authorization concept for the electronic registry demonstrated. It is checked on a random basis whether access to registry areas with VS-NfD content is restricted to the necessary group of people. It is checked whether the federal registry directive is observed.

controls.title: Storage of electronic CI according to § 23 and No. 5 Annex V to the VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Electronic CI MUST be stored encrypted with an IT security product with a statement of approval or be physically secured in accordance with the VSA requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Storage is either on hard disks encrypted with a BSI-approved product (e.g., BitLocker with correct configuration) or on systems located in a physically secured area according to VSA specifications (e.g., a locked server room with access control).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor either verifies the configuration of the disk encryption and compares the product used with BSI list 7164, or reviews the documentation and implementation of the physical security measures of the server room.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Electronic CI is protected by a combination of encryption and physical security (Defense-in-Depth). All data carriers of the CI IT, both servers and clients, are without exception encrypted with an approved product AND are also located in physically secured areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All servers are located in a certified data center. All clients are disk-encrypted. The keys for the encryption are stored securely in a Hardware Security Module (HSM). The status of the encryption is monitored centrally and automatically.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies both the physical security measures and the configuration of the encryption. The configuration of the central management system for the encryption and the HSM is checked. Proof of complete monitoring of the encryption status of all systems is requested.

controls.title: Electronic transmission of CI according to §§ 24, 53, 55 and No. 6.2 Annex V to the VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CI-IT of all communication partners MUST be approved for VS-NfD. If CI is transmitted electronically, it MUST generally be encrypted by an IT security product with a statement of approval. Encryption MAY ONLY be omitted if CI is transmitted exclusively via dedicated lines in a protected area or if the transport network is also approved for the processing of CI.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For transmission over insecure networks (e.g., the internet), a VPN gateway with BSI approval or S/MIME with approved certificates is used. The approval of the communication partner's IT is obtained and documented before the exchange. Internal transmissions in a physically protected LAN can be unencrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network topology and the configuration of the encryption products (VPN, S/MIME). It is checked whether the products used are approved. The documents for the approval of the communication partner systems are reviewed.

controls.title: Carrying of electronic CI according to § 28 VSA and No. 7 Annex V to the VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Electronic CI MAY ONLY be taken on business trips if this is necessary for official purposes. It MUST be adequately secured against unauthorized access. This can be done by storing it on: CI-IT approved for this purpose, a data carrier in a sealed envelope, a data carrier encrypted with an approved product, or a data carrier whose contents are encrypted with an approved product. If VS-NfD is to be processed in private homes, it MAY ONLY be processed electronically with CI-IT approved for this purpose.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For business trips, employees are provided with notebooks that are approved as CI-IT and have disk encryption with an approved product. Alternatively, approved encrypted USB sticks are issued. Taking them along must be approved by the supervisor.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the concept for the mobile CI-IT and the corresponding approval documents shown. The configuration of the encryption on the mobile devices and data carriers is checked. The policies and approval processes for carrying CI are reviewed.

controls.title: Archiving of electronic CI according to §§ 30, 31 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: CI MUST be disposed of in accordance with the Federal Archives Act in the same way as unclassified information. When introducing systems for electronic records management, the technical procedures for disposal MUST be agreed with the responsible archive at an early stage. If the archive does not wish to take over CI, it MUST be securely deleted or destroyed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A disposal concept for electronic documents has been agreed with the responsible archive (e.g., Federal Archives). The electronic file or the DMS supports the disposal deadlines and can create corresponding data packages for the archive. The deletion concept is coordinated with requirement CON.11.1.A13.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the disposal concept, which has been agreed with the archive, presented. The technical configuration of the DMS or the e-file regarding the disposal functions is checked. Proof of a completed disposal or a completed secure deletion after the retention period has expired is requested.

controls.title: Deletion of electronic CI, destruction of data carriers and IT products according to §§ 32, 56 and No. 8 Annex V to the VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To delete encrypted CI, the key MUST be deleted in compliance with the SecOPs. Unencrypted CI MUST be deleted by erasing the entire data carrier/IT product using an IT security product with a statement of approval. Data carriers MUST be erased before they leave the secured environment. If they cannot be erased, they MUST be physically destroyed. For destruction, products or procedures according to BSI TL - M 50 MUST be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented process for secure deletion and destruction has been established. For the deletion of hard disks, software is used that is approved by the BSI for this purpose. For physical destruction, a certified service provider is commissioned or a suitable shredder is kept on hand. The deletion and destruction processes are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the deletion and destruction concept and the corresponding logs shown. It is checked whether the deletion software used and the commissioned service providers have a corresponding BSI approval or certification. Compliance with the requirements for defective data carriers is also checked.

controls.title: Access and entry protection according to § 3 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: CI-IT MUST be protected in such a way that access to the CI-IT and access to CI is only possible for obligated persons. The protection MUST be ensured by a combination of IT security products with a statement of approval, physical, organizational, and personnel measures. Multi-factor authentication SHOULD be used for access and entry protection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Access to rooms with CI-IT is regulated by access control systems. Access to the IT system itself is protected by username and password. The complexity and length of the passwords are specified by policy. Access to CI data is controlled via authorization groups that follow the 'need-to-know' principle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the physical protection measures (doors, locks). He checks the password policies and the configuration of the authorization groups in the system. It is checked whether all users with access to CI-IT have been formally obligated (see CON.11.1.A5).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is mandatory for all users for access to CI-IT. Access to CI data is reviewed regularly, at least every six months, as part of a recertification campaign.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the password, logging on to the CI-IT clients and applications requires a second factor, e.g., a smart card or an authenticator app. An automated process regularly prompts the respective data owners to review and confirm the access rights to their data.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the technical implementation and the mandatory configuration of MFA for all user accounts. The logs and results of the last recertification campaign for access rights are reviewed.

controls.title: Handling of data carriers and IT products according to § 54 and Annex V to the VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data carriers and IT products MUST be stored in locked containers or rooms when not in use if they themselves are classified as VS-NfD, store unencrypted VS-NfD, or store VS-NfD encrypted with a product without a statement of approval.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Laptops, USB sticks, and other mobile data carriers with classified information (VS-NfD) are stored in lockable cabinets or rolling containers after business hours. Servers and other stationary classified IT are located in locked rooms.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: After business hours, the auditor conducts a walk-through of the office premises and checks whether all classified IT devices and data carriers are securely locked away ('Clean Desk Policy'). The access control regulations for the server rooms are checked.

controls.title: Interconnection of classified IT according to § 58 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before classified IT is interconnected with other classified IT, it MUST be checked if and to what extent information may be exchanged, taking into account the protection level and the 'need-to-know' principle. IT security functions MUST be implemented to protect the system interconnections. It MUST be assessed and documented whether the interconnection is absolutely necessary, whether a special threat arises, and whether the total data set is to be classified higher.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before each interconnection, a formal risk assessment is performed and documented. The connection is made via a firewall or another approved security product whose rules restrict the information flow to the necessary minimum.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the risk assessment and the security concept for the interconnection. The configuration of the coupling element (e.g., firewall rule set) is analyzed and checked for compliance with the documented, permitted information flow.

controls.title: Maintenance and repair work on classified IT according to § 3 Para. 3 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintenance and repair work SHOULD be carried out within the agency's own premises. If this is not possible, it MUST be ensured that the VSA requirements are met during transport and external maintenance. Upon completion, the classified information security officer MUST assess whether any changes relevant to security classification have occurred.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process for maintenance work on classified IT is defined. This clearly prioritizes on-site maintenance. For external maintenance, approval must be obtained from the classified information security officer, which includes conditions (e.g., secure transport, removal of hard drives). Each maintenance task is concluded with a report that is countersigned by the classified information security officer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the process documentation and the maintenance logs from the last few months. It is checked whether external maintenance was correctly approved and the conditions were implemented. The assessment reports of the classified information security officer are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During maintenance and repair work, the processing of classified information in the affected area SHOULD be stopped. If this is not possible, it MUST be ensured without interruption that no classified information can be leaked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: By default, the affected systems are disconnected from the network for the duration of the maintenance. If this is not possible, dedicated monitoring of the system interfaces (e.g., by an Intrusion Detection System - IDS) is activated for the maintenance period.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the maintenance logs and the network or IDS logs to verify whether the systems were isolated or monitored as required during maintenance.

controls.title: Remote maintenance of classified IT according to § 3 Para. 3 VSA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If classified IT is remotely maintained, the connection MUST be encrypted. IT security products with a statement of approval MUST be used for this purpose. The remote maintenance IT and the transmission links MUST be treated as classified IT. The connection MUST be established and terminated by the agency. The agency MUST also be able to interrupt the connection during maintenance in case of irregularities. An information security concept MUST be created for remote maintenance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated security concept for remote maintenance exists. Remote maintenance is carried out via an approved VPN product. The connection is initiated manually by an administrator of the agency and terminated again after the work is completed. An employee with technical expertise observes the remote maintenance session.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the remote maintenance concept and the approval documents. The configuration of the VPN system is checked. The logs are used to verify that the connections only existed when needed and for the necessary duration and were controlled by the agency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Remote maintenance is carried out exclusively via a dedicated remote maintenance solution (Bastion Host / PAM system) that logs all keystrokes and records a video of the session. The connection is only permitted for explicitly approved commands or actions (Command Filtering) and is automatically interrupted in case of suspicious activities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM system with session recording and command filtering is in use. The remote maintenance logs are automatically analyzed after each session and submitted to the classified information security officer for review. The connection can only be established according to the 'four-eyes principle' by two administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the PAM system, especially the rules for command filtering and automatic session recording. The logs and the reports of the automated analysis are reviewed. The connection establishment process according to the 'four-eyes principle' is verified.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
State secrecy protection comprises all measures for keeping information secret that has been classified as classified information (Verschlusssachen - VS) by a state body or at its instigation. VS are facts, objects, or findings that require secrecy in the public interest, in particular for the protection of the welfare of the federal government or a state, regardless of their form of representation.

State secrecy protection is regulated by provisions of federal and state law. The legal basis for the state secrecy protection of the federal government is the Security Clearance Act (Sicherheitsüberprüfungsgesetz - SÜG). The General Administrative Regulation on the Material Protection of Classified Information (Verschlusssachenanweisung - VSA) is decisive for the material protection of classified information of the federal government. This is aimed at federal authorities or federal public law institutions (offices) that work with VS.

If information technology is used to handle VS (VS-IT), then the requirements of the VSA must be observed. A prerequisite for the use of VS-IT is an information security concept in accordance with the BSI standards of the IT-Grundschutz of the Federal Office for Information Security in its currently valid version. In addition, there are the secrecy protection requirements described in this module, which go beyond the IT-Grundschutz.

The interconnection of VS-IT refers to the direct or cascaded connection of two or more VS-IT systems for the shared use of data and other information resources (for example, communication).

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The goal of this module is to ensure that the requirements of secrecy protection are taken into account at an early stage in the information security concepts (Security-by-Design). This module is intended to support the secrecy protection officers in defining the requirements of the VSA for the electronic processing of VS up to the classification level VS-NUR FÜR DEN DIENSTGEBRAUCH (VS-NfD - RESTRICTED) and integrating them into the information security concept together with the information security officers.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module CON.11.1 Classified Information - FOR OFFICIAL USE ONLY (VS-NfD) must be applied once to the entire information network of the classified IT if information classified as VS-NfD is or is to be processed. This module is aimed at federal authorities or federal public law institutions that are subject to the VSA (Security Regulations for Classified Information).

If the module is to be applied, it should be noted that this module does not represent an independent set of rules, but is only intended to support the implementation of the VSA. A fundamental distinction must be made between requirements for ensuring information security and for the protection of classified information. IT-Grundschutz serves to implement information security and the VSA serves to implement the protection of classified information. For this reason, an ISO 27001 certification based on IT-Grundschutz does not replace the approvals according to VSA. In order to implement consistent protection of classified information, the requirements of the VSA must be observed.

The requirements of this module are derived from the VSA and cover the following aspects:

• general principles of the VSA,

• access of persons to classified information,

• classified IT documentation,

• handling of electronic classified information,

• use of classified IT, and

• maintenance and servicing of classified IT.

The requirements of this module build on the requirements of information security and extend them to include the requirements for the protection of classified information. In order to secure the information network under consideration with classified IT and to ensure that information security is implemented, the entirety of all modules must generally be considered. In addition to the relevant system modules, this module presupposes the implementation of the following process modules, among others, as these are extended to include the requirements for the protection of classified information:

• ORP.1 Organisation,

• ORP.2 Personnel,

• CON.6 Deletion and Destruction, and

• OPS.1.2.5 Remote Maintenance.

This module does not cover:

• the requirements of the VSA to secure classified IT that is to be used for processing classified information of the classification level VS-VERTRAULICH or higher,

• the structural and technical security of buildings and rooms in which classified information of the classification level VS-NfD is processed; these are dealt with in the corresponding modules of the INF Infrastructure layer,

• the general requirements of the VSA that have no direct relation to classified IT, and

• the approval process for classified IT.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Unauthorized disclosure
parts.prose:
A significant threat to the protection of classified information is the access to classified information (CI) by unauthorized persons. This can occur if the requirements of the Classified Information Directive (CID) are not observed.

Examples:

• The classification and labeling of CI is omitted, incorrect, or incomplete.

• CI is deleted by IT products that do not have an approval statement.

• The classified IT documentation is missing or poorly maintained.

If the requirements of the CID are not observed, this can lead to the following:

• Due to incorrect handling of CI, some information security measures are mistakenly considered unnecessary, resulting in them not being implemented or not to the necessary extent.

• CI is deleted in such a way that its content is recoverable.

• Due to missing or inadequate classified IT documentation, it is not possible to verify whether a required level of information security is being achieved, whether necessary measures to protect the classified IT have already been taken in the past, or whether currently planned measures are compatible with those already implemented.

• CI is processed with IT that does not offer sufficient protective measures.

Applications can store or duplicate data unnoticed.

Examples:

• Swap files or swap partitions sometimes contain data worthy of protection, e.g., passwords or cryptographic keys.

• When processing CI with a word processing program, temporary working copies can be created that, under certain circumstances, for example after a program crash, were not deleted.

• Many applications also generate files during operation that are not needed for productive use (e.g., browser history). These files can contain security-relevant information.

As a result, such files can be read if the data carriers are removed and installed in another IT system. If the swap or application files or temporary files have not been securely deleted, unauthorized persons can gain knowledge of CI. Passwords and keys can be misused to gain unauthorized access to classified IT or CI.

The effects of unauthorized knowledge of CI at the classification level 'VS-NfD' (RESTRICTED) can be detrimental to the Federal Republic of Germany or one of its states. These can vary depending on the type of information classified as CI. For example, if classified network plans or information security concepts are disclosed, this information can be used to penetrate IT systems. If, for example, unauthorized persons gain knowledge of diplomatic information about another country, this can strain diplomatic relations between Germany and that country.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Conspiratorial Attacks
parts.prose:
A conspiratorial attack is a form of espionage in which information is covertly obtained from non-publicly accessible sources by foreign intelligence services. In conspiratorial attacks, intelligence services aim to obtain information of interest to them, such as classified information, as stealthily as possible.

In conspiratorial procurement activities, intelligence services conceal their true intentions. The information is acquired through the use of human sources (e.g., social engineering), by technical means (e.g., eavesdropping measures or cyber attacks that exploit backdoors or use malware), or through a combination of both.

As a result, foreign intelligence services can access classified information and gain a strategic advantage over the Federal Republic of Germany or one of its states. For example, other states could use this information to strengthen their negotiating position with the Federal Republic of Germany. Other groups, such as terrorist organizations or organized crime, can also use the information obtained from conspiratorial attacks to plan and carry out potential activities more effectively.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Attacks by Insider Threats
parts.prose:
In an attack by so-called insiders, internal information, such as classified information, is deliberately stolen by internal or external employees and possibly sold to third parties or published. Insiders have extensive knowledge of their institution's internal processes and workflows. In addition, they have entry, access, and usage rights that outsiders do not have. They can use this knowledge and the rights granted to them for their official duties to increase the probability of a successful attack. Furthermore, they can control the timing of the attack so that it is carried out when it is difficult to detect, for example, during maintenance windows.

The reasons why employees decide to steal information vary individually.

Examples:

• The insiders feel morally obligated to publish information that is classified in order to expose wrongdoing, for example.

• The insiders have been recruited by an intelligence service.

• The insiders want to enrich themselves by selling information.

As a result, third parties can gain unauthorized access to classified information. This can be detrimental to the interests of the Federal Republic of Germany or one of its states. The conditions under which insiders operate make it difficult to protect against such an attack. Many of the measures used to protect against attacks are not effective against attacks by insiders.

controls.title: Implementation of the Standard Data Protection Model (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only sporadic, ad-hoc efforts are made to comply with data protection laws. These efforts are incomplete and not systematic. The Standard Data Protection Model (SDM) is not used, and there is no documented justification for this.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Compliance with data protection regulations may only be checked for individual processes classified as high-risk, while other areas are disregarded. There is no central responsible person or established process to ensure data protection compliance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: A sample of data processing activities is checked. It is checked whether a data protection impact assessment or a legal review was carried out for these samples. The lack of a systematic approach or the use of a recognized model such as the SDM is documented. Automated auditing is not possible at this stage.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organization generally tries to comply with the legal provisions on data protection (GDPR, BDSG). The Standard Data Protection Model (SDM) is known, but not systematically applied. Basic data protection principles are considered, but a structured methodology for selecting and implementing technical and organizational measures (TOMs) is lacking.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data protection officer has been appointed, but their recommendations are not consistently integrated into the processes. Measures are often selected primarily from an information security perspective and not based on the rights of the data subjects.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The data protection officer is interviewed and it is checked whether a register of processing activities exists. It is verified whether basic legal requirements are met, but the lack of a systematic framework like the SDM for deriving measures is noted. Automated auditing is limited to checking for the existence of the 'Register of Processing Activities' document.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The legal provisions on data protection (GDPR, BDSG, the data protection laws of the federal states, and, where applicable, relevant sector-specific data protection regulations) MUST be complied with. A defined process is established to ensure compliance for all data processing activities, using the SDM methodology by default to systematize and select measures based on the protection goals.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The organization uses the SDM to analyze processing activities, assign them to the protection goals, and select suitable reference measures. This process is documented for all relevant processing activities and is carried out in a repeatable manner.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: It is checked whether all legal data protection provisions are complied with. Documented evidence of the systematic application of the SDM methodology is sought. The register of processing activities and the associated documentation of measure selection are reviewed. An automated script could search document repositories for keywords such as 'SDM', 'protection goal', and 'reference measure' and verify their existence for all processing activities listed in the register.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All legal data protection provisions are complied with and the SDM is systematically applied. If the SDM methodology is not considered for a specific process, a formal, documented justification including a risk assessment SHOULD be created and approved by management. The effectiveness of the selected measures is regularly reviewed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formalized process for deviations from the SDM standard is established. This includes a documented risk analysis and an alternative methodology for ensuring data protection. The results and approvals are tracked in a compliance management tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The documentation for processes where the SDM was not applied is checked. It is verified that a comprehensive justification and risk analysis exist and have been formally approved. The records of the regular reviews of the effectiveness of data protection measures are inspected. An automated script could query the compliance tool to list all registered deviations and check whether the required justification and approval artifacts are linked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with data protection regulations is ensured by a highly integrated and partially automated Data Protection Management System (DPMS). The SDM is fully integrated into the development lifecycle (Privacy by Design) and procurement processes. The selection and review of measures are supported by automated tools that continuously monitor compliance with the SDM's reference measures and legal requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance) tools are used to automate the mapping of legal requirements to internal controls based on the SDM. Continuous compliance monitoring is implemented, which generates automated reports for the data protection officer and management. Deviations are automatically reported for review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The integration of the DPMS into the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC) and procurement processes is checked. The configuration and results of the automated monitoring tools are controlled. The automated workflow for processing reported deviations is verified. An automated audit could query the GRC tool's API to confirm that all processing activities are linked to controls and that the compliance status is continuously tracked.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
In contrast to information security, which primarily serves to protect the data-processing institution, the task of data protection is to protect natural persons from institutions or bodies excessively interfering with the fundamental rights and freedoms of individuals through their processing activities. The Basic Law for the Federal Republic of Germany guarantees the right of citizens to decide for themselves, in principle, on the use of their personal data. The data protection laws of the federal government and the federal states refer to this when they emphasize the protection of the right to informational self-determination. Article 8 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights directly formulates the right to the protection of personal data (paragraph 1), emphasizes the need for a legal basis for data processing (paragraph 2), and prescribes the monitoring of compliance with data protection regulations by an independent authority (paragraph 3). The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) further details these requirements of the Charter of Fundamental Rights. Of central importance here is Article 5 of the GDPR, which lists the principles for the processing of personal data, some of which can also be understood as protection goals. In addition to the GDPR, the Federal Data Protection Act (BDSG) and the data protection laws of the federal states, as well as other sector-specific regulations such as the Telecommunications Telemedia Data Protection Act (TTDSG), must be taken into account.
Specifically, in the context of operational data protection, four types of risks, which are to be reduced with different levels of protective measures, are to be distinguished:
• Risk type A: The interference with the fundamental rights of natural persons through processing is not designed to be sufficiently mild.
• Risk type B: The measures to reduce the intensity of interference of a processing are, in relation to the assurance objectives, not complete or are not operated with sufficient effectiveness or are not continuously controlled, audited, and assessed to a sufficient extent.
• Risk type C: The measures that are required by information security (cf. e.g., IT-Grundschutz according to BSI) are not complete or are not operated with sufficient effectiveness or are not continuously controlled, audited, and assessed to a sufficient extent.
• Risk type D: The information security measures are not operated in a sufficiently data protection-compliant manner, in the sense of risk type A and risk type B.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The objective of this module is to illustrate the connection between data protection requirements, operationalized by the Standard Data Protection Model, and IT-Grundschutz.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose: The CON.2 Data Protection module must be applied once to the information network if personal data is processed under German or European law. The CON.2 Data Protection module, and in particular the extensive explanations in the introduction, thus support users in Germany and Europe in finding their way when components are identified in the protection needs assessment that process or otherwise use personal or personally identifiable data. It should then be checked whether the module should not only be applied to individual information networks or procedures, but to the entire institution.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Disregard of data protection laws or use of an incomplete risk model
parts.prose:
Under the GDPR, the processing of personal data is prohibited in principle. The processing of this data is only lawful if the requirements of Article 6 of the GDPR are met, for example, if the data subject has given consent or if a legal provision permits the data processing. Processing is also non-compliant, for example, if an institution does not sufficiently specify the purpose of data processing, overextends the purpose, or carries it out without any purpose at all. The same applies if the respective institution processes personal data non-transparently or without measures to ensure integrity and without opportunities for intervention by data subjects.
From a data protection perspective, an institution that processes personal data (e.g., collects, stores, transmits, or deletes it) is fundamentally a risk to the data subjects concerned. This risk exists even if the institution's data processing is designed to be compliant with the law.
A common risk in practice is access to data that does not serve the purpose of the original data processing. This can typically involve access by foreign parent companies, security authorities, banks and insurance companies, public benefit administrations, IT manufacturers and IT service providers, or research institutions. In these contexts, it is often not checked whether the access is authorized, for example, because a long-standing practice is being continued. Another possibility is that subordinate employees shy away from the personal risk of questioning whether a sufficient legal basis exists. Furthermore, controllers often draw no consequences from (partially) negative audit results from a legal department or a data protection officer. If controllers ignore audit or consulting results, questions of liability may arise.
Another risk for both individuals and responsible institutions exists if there are no standard processes for lawful access to IT services or the transmission of data sets by third parties. The same applies if no proof of regularity in the form of logs and documentation can be provided.
Inadequate data security is also a major danger for individuals or employees. Recital 75 of the GDPR describes the risks associated with the processing of personal data and thus the threat situation from unauthorized access as follows: "The risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons, of varying likelihood and severity, may result from personal data processing which could lead to physical, material or non-material damage, in particular: where the processing may give rise to discrimination, identity theft or fraud, financial loss, damage to the reputation, loss of confidentiality of personal data protected by professional secrecy, unauthorised reversal of pseudonymisation, or any other significant economic or social disadvantage; where data subjects might be deprived of their rights and freedoms or prevented from exercising control over their personal data; where personal data are processed which reveal racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, or trade union membership, and the processing of genetic data, data concerning health or data concerning sex life or criminal convictions and offences or related security measures; where personal aspects are evaluated, in particular analysing or predicting aspects concerning performance at work, economic situation, health, personal preferences or interests, reliability or behaviour, location or movements, in order to create or use personal profiles; where personal data of vulnerable natural persons, in particular of children, are processed; or where processing involves a large amount of personal data and affects a large number of data subjects."

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Determination of an insufficient protection level
parts.prose:
Another danger for individuals or employees is an incorrectly set protection level for their personal data. This protection level, which is typically determined by the institution responsible for processing personal data, can be set incorrectly or too low for various reasons:
• The institution has not considered the data protection's extended catalog of protection goals compared to information security.
• In determining the protection level, the institution has not distinguished between the risks to the implementation of the data subjects' fundamental rights and the risks to the institution.
• Although the institution has distinguished between the two protection interests, it has designed the functions of the procedure and the protective measures in favor of the institution and to the detriment of data subjects.

controls.title: Survey of influencing factors for data backups

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Factors influencing data backup are only collected sporadically and exclusively for systems classified as absolutely critical. The collection is informal, for example, through verbal agreements, and is not documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, an administrator typically relies on their own knowledge of a system to define a backup strategy. There are no formal requirements from the business departments. The collection is often limited to the expected data volume.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds that there is no documented process for collecting data backup requirements. Spot checks on various systems show that no or only very rudimentary, informal requirements (e.g., in emails) exist.

parts.name: statement
