parts.prose: This module deals with all relevant security aspects that institutions must consider when developing their own software. It examines how an institution can prepare and carry out software development. Corresponding threats are identified and requirements are formulated.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The CON.8 Software Development module is to be applied to every development project in the information network where software is to be developed.
If software is being developed, there is very often a client-contractor relationship. In IT-Grundschutz, this situation is reflected by the fact that the APP.7 Custom Software Development module covers the client side and the CON.8 Software Development module covers the contractor side. The requirements of this module must therefore be met by contractors. The requirements relevant to software development (functional and non-functional requirements, requirements for the secure procedure, and the security profile) are collected by the client within the scope of the APP.7 Custom Software Development module.
This module does not provide a complete guide or general procedure for software development; instead, it focuses on the relevant aspects of information security in software development. The module also does not cover aspects of patch and change management. For this, the OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management module must be applied.
Acceptance and related testing of custom-developed or commissioned software are regulated in the OPS.1.1.6 Software Testing and Release module. Further aspects of testing within the scope of software development are covered in this CON.8 Software Development module.
The ORP.5 Compliance Management (Requirements Management) module must also be considered, as this module regulates how legal and internal institutional requirements, as well as customer requirements, are taken into account.
If the software development includes cryptographic aspects, the relevant requirements from the CON.1 Cryptographic Concept module must be considered.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Selection of an unsuitable process model
parts.prose: Process models structure and plan the course of software development by specifying certain action steps and their sequence. If an unsuitable process model is selected for software development, the course of development and the associated development project can be significantly disrupted. Depending on the characteristics of the chosen model and the scope of the development project, either important aspects could be neglected or irrelevant aspects could be overly focused on. Both of these problems increase the workload in project management and restrict productive work. If no process model is used at all, the risk increases that relevant aspects, particularly those concerning information security, are not adequately considered in software development. This can lead to relevant security functions not being implemented or tested at all, so that the developed software does not meet the security requirements.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Selection of an unsuitable development environment
parts.prose: If an unsuitable development environment is selected or chosen individually by employees, urgently needed functions may be missing or not implemented in a sufficient form. Furthermore, an unsuitable development environment can also have errors or vulnerabilities that can cause significant disruptions in the course of software development. If no specific development environment is selected and specified, different developers may work on the software with different, self-chosen tools and thereby cause compatibility problems. For example, different compilers can trigger such compatibility problems.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Missing or insufficient quality assurance of the development process
parts.prose: A lack of or insufficient quality assurance during software development can delay the development project or even cause it to fail completely. If it is not checked whether the custom-developed software is implemented securely, vulnerabilities threaten the delivered software. If quality assurance is not firmly anchored in the development process, errors and manipulations in the conception or implementation may go undetected. Attention should be paid not only to self-developed components but especially to external contributions and adopted components.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Missing or insufficient documentation
parts.prose: If the software is not documented or is insufficiently documented during the conception or development phase, this can lead to any errors being diagnosed and rectified only with delay or not at all. If the development is documented improperly, the software can also only be updated, adapted, or extended later with great effort. With insufficient administration or user documentation, the software could be incorrectly managed or operated in productive use. This can, for example, disrupt IT operations, cause incorrect work results, or delay the workflow.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Insecure Use of Development Environments
parts.prose:
If the development environment is insufficiently secured, the software being produced can potentially be manipulated. Such manipulations are subsequently difficult to detect.
If it is not known which users can and could access the development environment and at what time, the software can be manipulated anonymously. If the manipulated parts of the software are discovered, it may not be possible to trace which users manipulated them.
With missing or insufficient source code version control, it is not possible to reliably track changes or restore previous, functioning versions of the software.
If source codes are inadequately protected against accidental or intentional changes, parts of a source code or even the entire source code can be damaged, and the work already invested can be lost.
If the source code or the version control system is not sufficiently protected against data loss, various threats arise, regardless of whether the data loss is caused by a technical defect or human error. It may become impossible to continue developing the software at all because the data is completely missing, or only an outdated and possibly faulty intermediate version is available, which can only be used with very high effort.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Software Design Flaws
parts.prose:
The more extensive the functional scope of a software becomes, the more extensive its program code often becomes. If the program code is not structured by suitable measures and if it is not based on an appropriate software architecture, it can usually only be maintained with great difficulty. Thus, security vulnerabilities can be difficult to close, or outdated program parts can only be replaced with very high effort, for example, if the protection requirement of the processed data changes and thus also the security requirements for the software.
Software design flaws not only complicate the maintenance of the software, but they can also lead to security vulnerabilities and threats themselves. If the program code is not sensibly structured and the software architecture is not comprehensibly documented, conceptual errors can be very difficult to identify in software tests. As a result, security vulnerabilities can exist at the most diverse levels of the software.
In practice, software design flaws are often historically conditioned, for example, by using legacy systems for tasks and environments for which they were not originally designed. Also, in the software development of very old applications, aspects such as maintainability and modifiability were not considered to the extent required by today's state of the art.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Missing or insufficient testing and release procedure
parts.prose:
If new software is not sufficiently tested and released, errors in the software may not be detected. Such errors not only endanger the productive use and information security of the new software itself, but possibly also other applications and IT systems in the production environment.
If security functions or the basic security requirements are not tested, it is not ensured that the developed software meets the security requirements of the deploying institution. As a result, sensitive information could be disclosed, manipulated, or destroyed, for example, by unauthorized third parties accessing the software due to faulty authentication functions.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.8. Software testing with production data
parts.prose:
When new software is tested with production data, unauthorized persons could potentially view confidential information, such as particularly sensitive personal data.
If the testing is not done with copies of the production data, but with the originals (e.g., in database systems), even more extensive threats arise:
• Software malfunctions during testing can lead to the confidentiality of the production data as well as its integrity or availability being compromised.
• Unwanted changes to production data can also arise from the software being tested or operated incorrectly. It is possible that this change will not be detected promptly. Such errors can also affect other IT applications that access the same datasets.
These circumstances are very often exacerbated by the fact that while the software is being tested, the focus is not on the protection of the test data, but on whether the software behaves as desired or as defined by the requirements.

controls.title: Definition of authorized recipients (B) [Central Administration]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Permitted recipients and transmission channels are only defined in a rudimentary way for individual, particularly critical types of information or departments. A formalized process for approval and documentation is completely absent.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The definition is made on an ad hoc basis via email or verbal agreement when an information exchange is pending. There is no central overview or policy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines by interviewing employees whether there are isolated, informal arrangements for information exchange. It is checked whether at least verbal agreements exist for critical areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a central list or document that names permissible recipients for the most common types of information. However, the transmission channels are only described in general terms and the list is not regularly reviewed or updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central body (e.g. IT department) maintains a simple list (e.g. in a text file or a wiki), but it is updated reactively rather than proactively. The parties involved are instructed to consult this list.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the central document with the permissible recipients. It is checked on a random basis whether the regulations for common exchange processes are in place and whether the document shows signs of basic maintenance (e.g. modification date).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central administrative body MUST ensure that the transfer of information does not violate legal frameworks. The central administrative body MUST define who is allowed to receive and transfer which information. It MUST be defined which channels may be used to exchange the respective information. All parties involved MUST ensure before the exchange of information that the receiving party has the necessary permissions to receive and further process the information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The regulations are documented in a formal policy on information exchange. This policy clearly defines responsibilities, the information categories to be protected, the approved recipient groups and the permissible transmission channels for each category (e.g. encrypted e-mail, secure data transfer platform).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the official policy on information exchange. It is checked whether there are clear rules for defining recipients and transmission channels. It is verified on the basis of random samples (e.g. logs of data transfers) whether the parties involved check the authorisations of the recipients before the exchange.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process for defining and updating recipients and transmission channels is formalised and is reviewed regularly, at least annually, and adapted as necessary. A documented and traceable workflow exists for applying for and approving exceptions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is managed through a formal review and approval process. Requests for new exchange relationships or changes are handled via a ticketing system or a dedicated form that requires approval from the responsible bodies (e.g. data protection officer, information security officer).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the process documentation for the maintenance of the exchange rules. Evidence of regular reviews (e.g. minutes) and of the handling of change requests (e.g. tickets) is checked to verify compliance with the formalised process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The defined rules for permissible recipients and transmission channels are largely enforced automatically by technical systems (e.g. Data Loss Prevention, e-mail gateway rules, Identity and Access Management). Any attempt to violate the policy is automatically blocked and triggers a security alert.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DLP system is configured to check outgoing data streams based on content analysis and recipient address. E-mail rules route messages to unauthorised external recipients to a quarantine. Access to secure data transfer platforms is controlled via a central IAM system that dynamically manages permissions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyses the configuration of the technical control systems (DLP, e-mail gateway). Its effectiveness is checked using test cases (e.g. sending a test e-mail with sensitive data to an unauthorised recipient). In addition, the logs of the security system are evaluated for blocked attempts and triggered alarms.

controls.title: Regulation of information exchange (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The need for protection of information is only informally assessed for individual data records classified as highly critical. There are no specifications as to how this information should be protected during transmission; this is left to the discretion of the individual employee.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The assessment is carried out on an ad hoc basis and is not documented. Employees decide on their own initiative whether an e-mail should be encrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks employees how they decide whether and how to protect information when sending it. Examples are requested of how information identified as sensitive is handled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All exchanged information is roughly classified (e.g. public, internal, confidential). There are general recommendations for protective measures during transmission, but these are not binding and not specifically tailored to the classification.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple classification policy exists. For protection during transmission, for example, 'encryption if required' is recommended as a general rule, without specifying technical requirements. Recipients are not systematically informed of the need for protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the classification policy and checks exchanged documents for existing markings on a random basis. It is examined whether the recommendations for protection during transmission are known to the employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before information is exchanged, the institution MUST determine how sensitive the information is. It MUST determine how the information is to be protected during transmission. If sensitive data is transmitted, the institution MUST inform the recipients how sensitive the information is. If the information is sensitive, the institution MUST inform the recipients that they may only use the data for the purpose for which it was transmitted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal classification scheme is established. A policy on information exchange specifies which protective measures (e.g. transport encryption, end-to-end encryption, digital signature) are mandatory for which protection requirement class. For the exchange of sensitive data, templates (e.g. for e-mails or cover letters) are used that contain information on the need for protection and purpose limitation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyses the information exchange policy and the classification scheme. On the basis of random samples (e.g. e-mail traffic, transfer logs), it is checked whether the prescribed protective measures have been applied and the recipients have been correctly informed. This can be done by using `grep` in e-mail headers for encryption protocols or by inspecting the configuration of transfer tools.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The classification of information and the allocation of the required protective measures are documented in detail in a central policy. The recipient of sensitive data is requested to formally confirm compliance with the handling regulations before transmission.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The classification of documents is carried out using metadata. When using data exchange platforms, the recipient must activate a checkbox before downloading, with which they confirm the terms of use and confidentiality obligations. This confirmation is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the central policy. The logs of the data exchange platforms or e-mail archives are examined to determine whether the confirmation of the handling regulations by the recipients can be proven. This can be done automatically by parsing log files for corresponding confirmation events.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The classification of information and the application of the required protective measures are automatically enforced by a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) system. The system analyses outgoing data and can automatically block or submit for approval transmissions that do not comply with security policies (e.g. unencrypted transmission of confidential data).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DLP system is configured with rules based on keywords, regular expressions and document metadata. In the event of a policy violation, the transmission is blocked and the sender and a security officer are notified.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyses the configuration and rule sets of the DLP system. The effectiveness is checked by means of test cases (e.g. attempting to send a file classified as 'confidential' unencrypted). The system logs are evaluated to verify correct blocking and alerting. A script could check the DLP rule base for completeness against the classification policy.

controls.title: Instruction of personnel on information exchange (B) [Specialist managers]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As part of their induction, new employees receive a one-off, brief introduction to the general security guidelines. Specific rules on information exchange with external parties are not covered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The instruction is part of a general onboarding presentation. There are no refreshers or specific training materials on the subject of information exchange.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the onboarding documents for new employees. By interviewing recently hired employees, it is determined whether and to what extent the topic of information exchange was covered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a general, annual security training for all employees, which covers the topic of information exchange superficially. However, the specific framework conditions of individual exchange processes are not communicated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standardised presentation or a web-based training is carried out once a year for all employees. Participation is logged, but understanding is not checked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the training documents and the attendance lists from the last security training. The content is checked to see if it covers the topic of information exchange.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Specialist managers MUST inform the employees about the framework conditions of each information exchange. The specialist managers MUST ensure that the employees know which information they are allowed to pass on, when, where and how.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to general training, the specialist managers conduct targeted briefings for the employees concerned as required or when new, specific exchange relationships are established. These briefings are documented (e.g. by means of a protocol or e-mail confirmation).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews specialist managers and their employees about specific information exchange processes. Evidence of the briefings carried out is requested (e.g. meeting minutes, e-mails, training certificates).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The instructions are repeated at regular intervals, at least annually, and include practical exercises or tests to check understanding. Participation and successful completion of the tests are documented and tracked for all relevant employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Interactive training modules (e.g., web-based training with a final test) are used. The results are managed in a Learning Management System (LMS) that sends automatic reminders for due training sessions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests excerpts from the Learning Management System to check regular participation and test results. It is verified whether a process exists for follow-up in case of non-participation or failure. A script could query the LMS database to determine the training status per employee: `SELECT user, course_status FROM lms_db WHERE course_id = 'CON.9-training'`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training courses are role-based and tailored to the specific tasks and permissions of the employees. The effectiveness of the instructions is continuously checked and improved through targeted, realistic tests, such as simulated phishing attacks with attachments intended to entice unauthorized data disclosure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A phishing simulation platform is used to conduct regular campaigns. Employees who fall for the simulation immediately receive clarifying information and are automatically scheduled for follow-up training. The results are incorporated into the design of future training content.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the planning, execution, and results of the phishing simulation campaigns. It is assessed whether the results lead to an adjustment of the training programs and whether a measurable improvement in employee behavior is discernible over time. The configuration of the simulation platform and the assignment of follow-up training are checked.

controls.title: Agreements on information exchange with external parties (S) [Central Administration]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Formal agreements on information exchange exist only with a few selected strategic partners. For most external communication partners, there are no written agreements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Agreements are only drawn up at the explicit request of the external partner or for very large projects. There are no templates or a standardized process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests a list of external partners with whom information is regularly exchanged and asks for the corresponding agreements to be presented. The degree of coverage is determined.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A standard template for non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) or data exchange agreements is used. However, it is not adapted to the specific risks and requirements of the respective partnership.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A legal or administrative department provides a standard NDA template that is used unchanged by the specialized departments for all partners. A review of its appropriateness for the individual case does not take place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the standard template for agreements shown to them and compares it with the requirements from several concrete exchange relationships to determine whether specific risks (e.g., type of data, transmission paths) are taken into account.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the case of a regular exchange of information with other institutions, the institution SHOULD formally agree on the framework conditions for the information exchange. The agreement for the information exchange SHOULD contain details on the protection of all confidential information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal agreement is concluded for all partners with whom information is regularly exchanged. This agreement is created based on a template and contains at least clauses on the confidentiality of the exchanged information, the purpose limitation, and the basic security requirements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests an overview of the regular information exchange relationships and the corresponding formal agreements. On a random basis, it is checked whether the agreements contain the required information on the protection of confidential information.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The agreements are reviewed regularly, at least every two years or in the event of significant changes, by the legal and security teams. They contain specific clauses on liability, reporting obligations for security incidents within a defined period, and audit rights.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process is established that ensures the regular review of all external agreements. A contract management system is used to monitor deadlines. The clauses are adapted on a risk-based basis to the type and scope of the data exchange.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation for contract management and checks evidence of reviews carried out (e.g., minutes, updated contract versions). It is verified whether the agreements contain the extended clauses (liability, reporting obligations, audit rights).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The agreements are managed in a central contract management system. Compliance with the agreed technical and organizational measures is monitored automatically wherever possible (e.g., by checking encryption standards for incoming data streams or scanning the partner infrastructure).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A third-party risk management system is used. It automatically checks the compliance of partners, for example, by analyzing the TLS configurations of partner servers or through regular questionnaires, the evaluation of which is partially automated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and reports of the contract management and third-party risk system. It is checked whether the monitoring processes are established and whether an escalation and remediation process is initiated in the event of identified deviations. An automated test could query the TLS configuration of the partner endpoints: `nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 partner.example.com`.

controls.title: Removal of residual information before disclosure (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A few employees are aware of the problem of metadata and residual information and try to remove it manually in particularly critical documents. There is no organizational support or directive.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For example, employees convert Word documents to simple text files to remove metadata, which often leads to format loss.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks employees if they are aware of the problem of residual information and how they deal with it. It is checked whether there are individual cases of conscious action.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an awareness campaign or a written recommendation that points out the dangers of residual information. Manual procedures for cleanup (e.g., 'Save as PDF') are recommended, but their application is not checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a brief guide on the intranet on how to use the 'Inspect Document' function in common Office programs. The application is the responsibility of each individual employee.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the available instructions and awareness materials. Based on recently sent external documents, a random check is carried out to see if residual information (e.g., author's name, comments) is still present.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to general training measures, the institution SHOULD inform about the dangers of residual and additional information in documents and files. It SHOULD be taught how residual and additional information in documents and files can be avoided. The institution SHOULD provide instructions that specify how to exclude unwanted residual information from exchange. Every file and every document SHOULD be checked for unwanted residual information before being passed on.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution not only provides instructions but also actively trains employees in handling document metadata, comments, and the revision mode. A policy stipulates that a check must be carried out before any external disclosure. Simple tools or on-board tools (e.g., the Office Document Inspector) are made mandatory.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and training materials. A sample of externally sent files is examined with a metadata analysis tool (e.g., `exiftool`) to verify that the check and cleanup have taken place. `exiftool -a -G1 file.docx` can be used to display all metadata.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution provides dedicated software tools (metadata scrubbers) that partially automate and simplify the process of cleaning up residual information. The use of these tools is integrated into the workflow for document release.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An add-in for the Office suite or a separate client tool is installed on all workstations. When saving or sending a document, the user is actively prompted to perform a metadata cleanup. For certain document types, this step is mandatory.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration and distribution of the metadata scrubber software. The process documentation for document release is reviewed. By observing an employee sending a document, the integration into the workflow is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automated system, such as a 'Content Disarm and Reconstruction' (CDR) or a metadata-scrubbing gateway, automatically inspects and cleans all outgoing files of residual information at the network boundary before they leave the network. Exceptions must be explicitly approved.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A solution is implemented at the email gateway or web proxy that analyzes all outgoing files. Based on a policy, metadata, comments, embedded macros, and other potentially dangerous or unwanted content are automatically removed. The cleaned file is then forwarded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and policies of the CDR or gateway system. The effectiveness is checked using test cases in which a file with various residual information is sent. The auditor intercepts the file outside the network and verifies that the cleanup was successful. The system logs of cleaned files are evaluated.

controls.title: Compatibility check of the sending and receiving system (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The compatibility of systems is only checked after a transmission has failed. There is no proactive approach.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: If a recipient reports that they cannot open a file, the sender tries to send the file in a different format (trial-and-error principle).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the helpdesk ticket history for incidents related to failed data transfers and analyzes the reactive approach.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When setting up a new, regular exchange relationship, a single test transmission is carried out. However, this is limited to the basic data format and does not take into account edge cases or encryption methods.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before starting a new data exchange, a sample file is sent by e-mail and the recipient is asked to confirm that they could open it. This is documented informally.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks those responsible for new data exchange processes how compatibility is ensured and requests evidence of test transmissions performed (e.g., email correspondence).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before an information exchange, it SHOULD be checked whether the IT systems and products used are compatible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a new regular exchange relationship is established, the technical framework (e.g., file formats, versions, character sets, transmission protocols, encryption algorithms) is formally agreed upon and documented between the partners. A test transmission is conducted to verify the agreements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation for setting up new exchange relationships. It is checked whether the technical coordination and the results of the test transmission are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal test plan is executed for the establishment of a new regular exchange relationship. This plan includes tests for file formats, encryption algorithms, transport protocols, authentication methods, handling of large files, and error handling.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A test plan template exists that is adapted for each new exchange relationship. The test results are recorded in a log and approved by both parties before productive exchange begins.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the test plans and acceptance protocols for recently established exchange relationships. The completeness of the tests and the formal acceptance are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compatibility is monitored not only initially, but also continuously through automated 'heartbeat' or 'canary' transmissions. A central register of compatible partner systems and their configurations is maintained and automatically consulted before initiating an exchange.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring system sends small test files at regular intervals via the established channels and checks for successful transmission and correct processing by the partner system. In case of errors, an alarm is triggered automatically. Changes to one's own or the partner's infrastructure trigger a new, complete compatibility test.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the monitoring system and the logs of the heartbeat transmissions. The timeliness and completeness of the register of partner systems are checked. The alerting and escalation processes for detected compatibility problems are reviewed.

controls.title: Backup copy of the transmitted data (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Individual users occasionally save copies of important sent files in their personal local folders. There is no organizational regulation or central backup.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees rely on the 'Sent Items' folder of their email client as the sole archive.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks employees how they ensure that sent information can be recovered in case of loss. The lack of a central regulation is noted.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A policy exists that recommends creating a backup copy of transmitted data. However, the process is manual and is the responsibility of individual users, leading to inconsistent application.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An instruction on the intranet requires employees to save important outgoing files on a network drive. There is no control over compliance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy. The degree of (inconsistent) implementation is assessed through random checks of network drives and interviews with employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD make a backup copy of the transmitted information if the information cannot be recovered from other sources.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process is defined that specifies for which types of transmitted information (based on classification and recoverability) a backup copy must be created. The storage is in a central, secure location that is regularly backed up (e.g., a dedicated directory in the document management system).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process definition. Using examples of recently transmitted, otherwise non-recoverable information, it is checked whether the backup copies exist at the defined location. It is also checked whether the storage location is part of the regular backup process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a defined process for creating and storing backup copies of transmitted data. The retention period for these copies is clearly defined and documented based on business and legal requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The retention rules are anchored in the institution's archiving policy. The document management system or storage location is configured to implement the defined retention periods (e.g., protection against premature deletion).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the archiving policy and checks the configuration of the storage system for the implementation of the retention periods. It is verified whether a process for controlled deletion after the deadline exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A gateway system or an integrated archiving solution automatically archives all outgoing information transmissions (that cannot be recovered from other sources) in a secure, audit-proof, and searchable archive.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An email archiving solution is implemented at the mail gateway, which stores all outgoing messages and their attachments in an audit-proof manner. For other transmission paths (e.g., SFTP), the transmitted files are automatically copied to the central archive by scripts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the archiving system. The audit-proof nature of the archive (e.g., protection against manipulation) is assessed. The completeness of the archiving is checked using test cases. The search function and the process for restoring data from the archive are tested.

controls.title: Encryption and digital signature (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encryption is used ad hoc by some technically savvy users, but there is no organizational policy, training, or support for it.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Individual employees use private PGP keys or ZIP encryption with weak passwords to protect files.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews that there is no uniform or supported method for encryption and that its use is random and uncontrolled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A policy recommends the use of encryption and digital signatures for sensitive data. However, the choice of tools and algorithms is left to the users, which leads to weak or incompatible implementations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A list of free encryption tools is provided on the intranet, but without specific configuration requirements. There is no central key exchange.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and randomly checks encrypted communication for the algorithms and key strengths used to uncover inconsistencies and the use of weak methods.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD check whether information can be cryptographically secured during exchange. If the information is cryptographically secured, sufficiently secure methods SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A policy clearly defines from which protection requirement class encryption and/or digital signature is mandatory for data exchange. The policy also specifies the secure methods and algorithms to be used (e.g., S/MIME, PGP, TLS 1.3). Users are trained in the application of the specified methods.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the policy for clear specifications on encryption methods. External data traffic (e.g., email headers, SFTP logs) is randomly checked to see if the requirements for sensitive data are met. A scan of the mail server could check the supported TLS cipher suites: `nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 25 mail.example.com`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution has a formal policy that defines approved encryption algorithms, key lengths, and signature standards. A centrally managed Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) or a similar infrastructure is provided to users to simplify and secure key exchange.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An in-house certification authority (CA) or a managed PKI service is used to issue and manage S/MIME certificates for all employees. These certificates are automatically integrated into the users' email clients. Public keys of communication partners are managed in a central directory service.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the PKI policy (Certificate Policy / Certification Practice Statement). The configuration of the CA and the directory service is checked. It is verified by means of random checks whether the issued certificates comply with the specifications and whether the key management processes (e.g., revocation) are functioning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encryption and digital signatures for all external communication containing sensitive data are automatically enforced by a gateway solution. The system prevents unencrypted sensitive data from leaving the network and can automatically apply transport or portal-based encryption if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An email gateway is configured to analyze outgoing emails based on content and metadata rules. If an email is classified as sensitive and end-to-end encryption (S/MIME, PGP) is not present, the gateway automatically forces a TLS connection or forwards the email to a secure web portal where the recipient can retrieve it after authentication.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and the rule sets of the gateway. The effectiveness is checked by test cases (e.g., sending a sensitive email to an external partner without an S/MIME certificate). It is verified that the email is correctly encrypted or redirected to the portal and that the sender receives a notification of the process.

controls.title: Confidentiality agreements (H) [Central Administration]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Confidentiality is assured informally via email. This assurance is not legally binding and there is no standardized procedure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees add a sentence like 'Please treat this information confidentially' to their emails when they think it is appropriate.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines by analyzing external communication that no formal confidentiality agreements exist and that the protection of confidentiality is based on informal and legally non-binding requests.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A standard template for a confidentiality agreement (NDA) is used whenever confidential information is exchanged. However, the template is not reviewed or adapted to the specific context of exchanging highly sensitive information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For all exchanges classified as 'confidential', a standard NDA is signed by both parties. It is not assessed whether the clauses are sufficient for the specific case (e.g., exchange of research data vs. personnel data).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the standard NDA with the requirements arising from the exchange of highly sensitive data and identifies potential gaps (e.g., missing specific regulations for data storage or access control).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before confidential information is passed on to other institutions, the central administration SHOULD be informed. The central administration SHOULD conclude a non-disclosure agreement with the receiving institution. The non-disclosure agreement SHOULD regulate how the information may be stored by the receiving institution. The non-disclosure agreement SHOULD specify who at the receiving institution may have access to which transmitted information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal process is established that requires the involvement of the central administration (e.g., legal department) before confidential information is exchanged. Based on a customizable template, a specific non-disclosure agreement is created that contains detailed regulations on storage (e.g., location, duration) and access (need-to-know principle).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the defined process and the associated documents (e.g., application forms). Based on samples of confidential information exchanges, it is checked whether a specific, signed non-disclosure agreement exists and whether it contains the required regulations on storage and access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The non-disclosure agreement contains specific technical and organizational security requirements for the receiving party (e.g., encryption of data at rest, standards for access control, obligation to conduct employee training). The sending institution is explicitly granted the right to verify compliance with these requirements (audit right).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The non-disclosure agreement refers to an appendix with a detailed catalog of security measures (based on standards such as ISO 27001) that the recipient must meet. The legal department works closely with information security to create and negotiate this appendix.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the concluded non-disclosure agreements for the presence and adequacy of the required security measures and audit clauses. It is checked whether the audit rights have already been exercised. A script could search the contract texts for keywords such as 'audit right' or 'encryption at rest': `grep -r 'Auditrecht' /path/to/contracts`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process of initiating, negotiating, signing, and managing non-disclosure agreements is controlled and tracked by a dedicated legal or compliance software platform (contract management system). Technical controls (e.g., in a data exchange portal) are automatically configured to enforce the access rights specified in the signed agreement.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After an agreement is marked as 'signed' in the contract management system, a secure data room is automatically set up for the partner on the exchange platform via an API interface. The permissions for the named individuals and the permitted actions (e.g., read-only access) are derived directly from the contract data and configured in the IAM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the access rights documented in the agreements in the contract management system with the actually configured permissions in the IAM system and on the exchange platform. The functionality of the automated interface between the systems is checked. A configuration audit script can export the permissions from the IAM system and compare them with the specifications from the contract database.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose: Information is transmitted between senders and receivers via various communication channels, such as personal conversations, phone calls, postal mail, removable media, or data networks. Rules for information exchange ensure that confidential information is only passed on to authorized persons. Such regulations are particularly necessary when information is transmitted over external data networks.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of this module is to secure the exchange of information between different communication partners. With the help of this module, a concept for secure information exchange can be created.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The CON.9 Information Exchange module is to be applied once to the entire information network if information is to be exchanged with communication partners who are not part of the information network.
The securing of network connections is dealt with in other modules of the IT-Grundschutz Compendium, see layer NET Networks and Communication. Requirements for removable media (see module SYS.4.5 Removable Media) and further processing in IT systems outside the information network are also not considered in this module.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Information not available in a timely manner
parts.prose:
The exchange of information can be disturbed, delayed, or interrupted.
Information arrives late or incomplete or is processed too slowly if the technology used generates transmission errors. Under certain circumstances, the exchange of information may cease completely because interfaces or equipment are not powerful enough or fail.
Business processes can be significantly affected if required deadlines for the delivery of information are not met. In extreme cases, contractually agreed deadlines are broken because a data transfer fails due to technical or human error.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Unregulated disclosure of information
parts.prose:
Sensitive information can fall into the hands of unauthorized persons.
It cannot be controlled who receives and uses information if, for example, a confidentiality agreement was not concluded prior to an information exchange. The risk of data misuse also increases if the confidentiality agreement has been formulated imprecisely or incompletely.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Disclosure of false or internal information
parts.prose:
Sensitive information can be sent to unauthorized recipients.
Sensitive information can accidentally fall into the wrong hands if staff are not sufficiently aware and trained. For example, data carriers can be passed on that contain residual information such as insufficiently deleted old data. Other residual information includes undeleted internal comments that are accidentally transmitted in an electronic document, e.g., as an e-mail attachment. In other cases, for example, confidential documents are accidentally sent to the wrong person because there are no clear instructions for handling confidential documents.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Unauthorized copying or modification of information
parts.prose:
Information and data can be surreptitiously intercepted or influenced by attacks.
In attacks, information can be intentionally stolen if it is not sufficiently protected. For example, in an attack, a data carrier can be intercepted in the mail or the content of an unprotected e-mail can be read unnoticed. In addition, in attacks, unprotected information can be altered while it is being transmitted, and thus, for example, malware can be introduced into files.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Inadequate application of encryption methods
parts.prose:
The protection of information during transmission using cryptographic methods can be circumvented by attacks.
If the cryptographic method is known in an attack, the encrypted data and the associated key can be intercepted if the encryption methods are not applied correctly. Employees who have not been sufficiently trained could, for example, send the key together with the data on the same data carrier. In addition, for example, keys are often used that are too easy to guess.

controls.title: Definition of Tasks and Responsibilities for IT Operations (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Responsibilities for IT operations are only vaguely defined for individual, historically grown areas. There is no clear delineation of tasks, rights, and duties. Many IT components do not have a clearly designated responsible person.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Knowledge of responsibilities lies only with a few long-term employees. In their absence, ambiguities and delays in troubleshooting regularly occur.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines that in the event of a failure of a randomly selected IT component, a responsible contact person cannot be immediately named. There is no documentation of responsibilities whatsoever.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the most important IT systems, main responsibilities are defined, mostly at the individual level. However, a formal, process-based regulation of tasks and authorities is missing. Interfaces and escalation paths are only informally known and not systematically documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Responsibilities are often recorded in emails or meeting minutes. A central, maintained document does not exist. Escalation often occurs 'by word of mouth' to the next higher manager.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews IT operations staff to determine if they are aware of their responsibilities for critical systems. It is checked whether at least rudimentary documentation (e.g., a simple list of responsibilities) exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all operated IT components, it MUST be defined which tasks arise for IT operations and who is responsible for them. For this purpose, the corresponding rights, duties, tasks with the necessary activities, authorities, and associated processes MUST be regulated. Furthermore, the interfaces and reporting channels as well as the escalation management between different operational units and towards other organizational units of the institution MUST be defined.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The responsibilities are documented in an organizational handbook or an IT operations policy. RACI matrices (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) are used to clearly assign roles and responsibilities. Escalation paths are visually represented and stored in relevant systems (e.g., ticketing system).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the organizational handbook and the IT operations policy. It is checked on a random basis whether responsibilities are clearly defined for selected IT components and whether the documented escalation paths are known to and followed by the employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All responsibilities, processes, and interfaces are not only documented but also stored and linked in a central management system (e.g., CMDB, ticketing system). The regulations are reviewed regularly, at least annually, for their timeliness and effectiveness and are adjusted as needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ticketing system automatically routes requests to the responsible group based on the affected IT component from the CMDB. Changes to responsibilities trigger a formal review process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies in the management system that the stored responsibilities and processes are up to date. It is checked whether the last formal review has taken place and the results have been documented. Automated assignments in the ticketing system are spot-checked for correctness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management of tasks and responsibilities is fully automated and integrated into the Identity and Access Management (IAM) process. Role-based access controls are automatically granted and revoked based on the assigned operational responsibilities. The effectiveness of the regulations is continuously monitored through automated controls and evaluated based on KPIs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An IAM system reads the responsibilities from the organizational handbook or the CMDB and provisions the necessary technical rights in the target systems. A SIEM system monitors compliance with the escalation paths and alerts in case of deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the IAM and SIEM systems to verify the automated assignment and monitoring. Reports and KPIs on process effectiveness are reviewed. An automated audit run could compare the configuration of the IAM system against the documented responsibilities (`grep 'Rolle: Datenbankadmin' /config/iam.conf | verify-against /docs/orga.xml`).

controls.title: Definition of Roles and Permissions for IT Operations (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all operated IT components, the respective role and permission concept MUST also define roles and associated permissions for IT operations. A role and permission concept MUST also be created for the operational resources. The role and permission concept for IT operations MUST separate the IT use from IT operational tasks. Administrative tasks and other operational tasks MUST be separated by different roles. The roles and permissions MUST be regularly reviewed and adjusted. In particular, the permissions of departed personnel and for decommissioned IT components MUST be removed. Shared accounts MAY ONLY be set up in justified exceptional cases.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The role concept is documented as part of the general IT security concept. A need-to-know principle is implemented. The separation of administrative and operational tasks is realized, for example, through dedicated admin accounts. A regular, e.g., semi-annual, review process for permissions is established.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the role and permission concept. It is checked whether a clear separation of administrative and other operational tasks is in place. The correct implementation of permissions in the target systems is spot-checked. It is verified that a regular review process exists and is carried out (e.g., through minutes/logs).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD define different roles for different operational activities, which have the necessary permissions for the respective activities. The review process for permissions is supported by automated reports that show which users have which rights. The use of shared accounts is technically restricted to the absolute minimum and their usage is strictly logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An identity management tool is used to define roles and manage permissions. The tool generates automatic reports for the permission review. For shared accounts, Privileged Access Management (PAM) solutions are used, which enable personal attribution and logging of usage.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the roles defined in the identity management tool and their granularity. It is checked whether the automated reports are used for the review process. The configuration of the PAM solution for shared accounts is checked for secure handling and complete logging.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A fully automated process, based on a central Identity and Access Management (IAM) system, ensures role-based granting and revocation of permissions (Role-Based Access Control, RBAC). Permissions are granted Just-in-Time (JIT) for the duration of an activity and then automatically revoked. Continuous, automated controls (e.g., via a SIEM) monitor the use of permissions and alert on anomalies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IAM system is coupled with the HR system and the ticket system. In the event of an approved change request, the required rights for the admin are automatically provisioned for the planned period. All permission changes and uses are reported to a SIEM system, which detects suspicious activities using UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the IAM and SIEM systems and their integration. The rules for JIT provisioning and UEBA anomaly detection are checked. An end-to-end test is performed, from the request in the ticket system to the automatic revocation of the permission. An automated test could analyze the permission logs in real time: `tail -f /var/log/iam.log | grep 'GRANT_PRIV' | check-ticket-system-api`.

controls.title: Creating operational manuals for the operated IT (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all operated IT components, the operational tasks SHOULD be planned and recorded in operational manuals. The operational manuals SHOULD always be available and address at least the following topics: relevant system and contact information, required and permissible resources, general configuration specifications, configuration specifications for hardening, roles and permissions, IT monitoring, logging and alerting, data backup and emergency concepts, IT incident management, and specifications for regular and unscheduled activities. The operational manuals SHOULD be reviewed and adapted regularly and on an ad hoc basis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The operational manuals are stored in a central, version-controlled system (e.g., a wiki or SharePoint) to which all relevant employees have access. A template for operational manuals is created to ensure a uniform structure. For every significant change to an IT component, an update of the corresponding manual is required.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly selects some critical IT components and checks the existence, completeness, and timeliness of the corresponding operational manuals. It is checked whether the manuals cover all required topics and whether the last change to the system was also documented in the manual. The access permissions to the manuals are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational manuals are dynamic and are partially automatically generated and kept up-to-date from central data sources (e.g., CMDB). For example, contact information and system details are embedded directly from the CMDB into the manual. There is a formal review and approval process for all changes to the manuals.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The wiki system uses plugins to display live data from the CMDB or the monitoring system. Changes to manuals must be approved by at least a second person (four-eyes principle) before they become effective. The review of the manuals is a fixed agenda item in regular team meetings.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the technical connection of the operational manuals to the CMDB. It is checked whether the review and approval process is documented and adhered to (e.g., by inspecting the version history and approval comments). It is checked whether the regular discussion and review of the manuals is minuted.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Operational manuals are treated as 'Documentation-as-Code'. The contents are stored in a markup language in a Git repository. Changes to the configuration of an IT component (Infrastructure-as-Code) and the associated documentation are made in the same commit and are validated and rolled out through a CI/CD pipeline. The documentation is interactive and provides direct links to management consoles and relevant monitoring dashboards.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The documentation is written in Markdown and converted into a static website with Hugo or MkDocs. A CI pipeline (e.g., with GitLab CI) checks on every commit whether the documentation was changed if code was also changed (linting rule). When an incident is resolved, a ticket to update the documentation is automatically created if this is relevant.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the CI/CD pipeline and the validation steps it contains for the documentation. The Git history is spot-checked to verify the coupling of code and documentation changes. The interactivity of the documentation is checked by testing the integrated links. A script could automatically check whether all systems marked as 'critical' in the CMDB are referenced in the documentation: `for asset in $(cmdb-cli list --critical); do grep -q $asset /docs/repo || echo 'Missing link for $asset'; done`.

controls.title: Providing sufficient personnel and material resources (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD have sufficient personnel resources to ensure proper IT operation. For this purpose, the effort for all IT operations activities SHOULD be determined. Personnel resources SHOULD be planned with appropriate redundancies and reserves and also take into account short-term staff shortages and temporarily increased personnel requirements. Suitable material resources SHOULD also be available. Resource planning SHOULD be reviewed regularly and on an ad hoc basis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Annual planning for personnel and material resource requirements is carried out. Personnel requirements are estimated based on the number of systems to be supported, their complexity, and the expected number of incidents/changes. Substitution arrangements are defined for all key positions. For material resources (e.g., laptops, servers), stock levels or rapid delivery contracts are maintained.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the personnel and material resource requirement planning documents. The traceability of the planning methodology is checked. The defined substitution arrangements are checked. It is checked whether the planning is reviewed and adjusted regularly (e.g., annually), for example, by inspecting the minutes of the corresponding planning meetings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Resource planning is based on measurable key performance indicators (KPIs) from the ticket system and monitoring, such as processing times, number of incidents per system, or system load. Strategic personnel development planning is carried out to cover future competence needs. The procurement of material resources is integrated into an automated workflow.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monthly report from the ticket system shows the workload per team and employee and serves as a basis for short- and medium-term resource planning. Each employee has an individual training plan. The ordering of standard material resources is done via a self-service portal with a subsequent approval workflow.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the KPIs used and their derivation from the source systems. It is checked whether the KPI-based findings demonstrably flow into the resource planning. Individual training plans are reviewed on a random basis. The workflow for procuring material resources is checked for efficiency and control.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Resource planning is carried out proactively and predictively using trend analyses and simulations. AI-supported tools are used to predict future workloads and the resulting resource requirements. The institution operates an active skill management system that ensures that critical competencies are redundantly available and up-to-date. Framework agreements exist with service providers to cover peak demands flexibly and quickly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A workforce management tool analyzes historical data and forecasts personnel requirements for the coming quarters. A skill matrix is centrally maintained and integrated with training management. If a competence is only available from one person, a training measure for a substitute is automatically initiated. The framework agreements with service providers are designed in such a way that additional experts are available within 24 hours.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor evaluates the methodology and results of the predictive analysis for resource planning. The functioning of the automated skill management processes is verified. The framework agreements with service providers are checked for the agreed response times (SLAs) and the suitability of the service providers. A test call-off of external resources is simulated to check compliance with SLAs.

controls.title: Defining hardened standard configurations (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD categorize the operated IT components and define and provide hardened standard configurations for these categories. The configuration specifications SHOULD implement the institution's security requirements and consider the recommendations of the respective manufacturers. Each standard configuration SHOULD be tested before deployment. The hardened standard configurations SHOULD be reviewed regularly and on an ad hoc basis and adapted to the current state of the art according to the available information. IT operations SHOULD ensure that the current configuration specifications are always available.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Hardening specifications are documented in configuration policies (e.g., for Windows Server, Linux Server, databases). These are based on recognized standards such as CIS Benchmarks. The standard configurations are provided as system images or configuration scripts. Before production deployment, each new version of a standard configuration is tested for functionality and security in a test environment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration policies and compares them with manufacturer recommendations and recognized hardening standards. It is checked whether a process for regular review and adaptation of the policies exists. Production systems are spot-checked to see if they comply with the defined standard configuration. The test documentation for new configuration versions is inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The hardened standard configurations are automatically rolled out to all systems using central configuration management tools (e.g., Ansible, Puppet, Chef, DSC), and their compliance is continuously monitored (Configuration Drift Detection). Permitted deviations from the standard configuration must be formally requested, approved, and documented. The hardening also extends to specialized systems such as virtualization hosts.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ansible playbooks or Puppet manifests define the desired state of the systems. A central server regularly executes these configurations and ensures conformity. Deviations are displayed on a dashboard and trigger an alert. A formal process in the ticket system governs the application and approval of configuration deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the hardening specifications stored in the configuration management tool. It is checked how the system reacts to configuration deviations (Report, Auto-Remediation). The process for approving deviations is checked for its traceability and adherence to the four-eyes principle. The configuration of virtualization hosts is explicitly checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration specifications are managed as 'Policy-as-Code' and tested in a CI/CD pipeline before they are rolled out. Every configuration change is automatically validated against compliance requirements (e.g., BSI-Grundschutz, ISO 27001). The systems actively enforce hardening (self-healing) and prevent non-compliant states. The hardening is verified through regular, automated vulnerability scans and penetration tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration rules are managed in a Git repository. A CI pipeline tests the rules in a virtual environment and checks them against security policies using a tool like Open Policy Agent (OPA). The configuration management tool runs in 'enforce' mode and immediately corrects deviations. The results of nightly vulnerability scans are used directly to adapt the hardening specifications.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the CI/CD pipeline for the configuration rules and the automated compliance checks it contains. The configuration of the configuration management tool in self-healing mode is checked. The results of the automated scans and tests are analyzed to assess the effectiveness of the hardening. An automated audit could directly compare a server's configuration with the Policy-as-Code repository: `ansible-playbook --check /repo/hardening.yml -i server.inventory`.

controls.title: Implementation of IT Asset Management (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD create, regularly review, and maintain an overview of all existing IT assets. In IT Asset Management (ITAM), all productive IT components, test instances, and reserve IT components SHOULD be recorded. Existing but no longer used IT assets SHOULD also be recorded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: IT assets are recorded in a central database or a specialized CMDB (Configuration Management Database). Recording takes place upon procurement or commissioning. A manual inventory is conducted at least once a year to verify the data.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the CMDB and checks its completeness and structure. It is checked whether a process for data maintenance exists. On a random basis, physically existing assets are compared with the entries in the CMDB and vice versa. The logs of the last inventory are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ITAM tools that enable central management of IT assets SHOULD be used. The recording and updating of asset information is largely automated through discovery scans. The CMDB records not only hardware, but also software, licenses, and the relationships between the assets.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An ITAM tool like Snipe-IT or a commercial solution performs daily network scans and automatically updates the CMDB with new devices and changed configurations. Software agents on the clients report installed software. The relationships (e.g., 'Application X runs on server Y and uses database Z') are modeled in the CMDB.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the ITAM tool and the discovery scans. The quality of the recorded relationship data in the CMDB is assessed. It is checked how deviations between scan results and manual entries are handled. The completeness of the software and license inventory is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ITAM is fully integrated into all relevant IT Service Management processes (Incident, Problem, Change, Vulnerability Management). The CMDB is the sole 'Single Source of Truth' for all configuration data. Unknown or unauthorized assets, which are detected on the network, automatically trigger a security incident and are quarantined if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When an incident is opened for an asset in the ticketing system, all relevant data (configuration, recent changes, known vulnerabilities) are displayed directly from the CMDB. A vulnerability scanner accesses the CMDB directly to define its scan targets. A Network Access Control (NAC) system checks every connecting device against the CMDB and moves unknown devices to a quarantine VLAN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the deep integration of ITAM into other ITSM processes, e.g., by tracking the lifecycle of a change from request to CMDB update. The configuration of the NAC system is checked for its effectiveness in fending off unknown devices. The rules for the automatic creation of security incidents are analyzed. An automated test could introduce an unknown device into the network to verify the NAC and SIEM response.

controls.title: Ensuring Proper IT Operations (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD develop operational concepts for all IT components and regularly review and adapt them. The security-relevant configuration specifications (hardened standard configurations) SHOULD be implemented. The release of installed or modified IT components into production SHOULD be verified using defined criteria. All IT operations activities SHOULD be comprehensively and traceably recorded, for which a suitable tool such as a ticketing system SHOULD be used. Reports SHOULD be created regularly to serve as proof of proper IT operations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An operational concept is created for each essential application or system group. A ticketing system (e.g., Jira Service Management, Zammad) is used comprehensively to record all requests, incidents, and changes. Before a change is put into production, a checklist (verification criteria) must be completed and documented in the change ticket. Monthly reports on ticket volume, resolution times, and SLA compliance are created and presented to management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews operational concepts on a random basis. It is checked whether all IT operations activities are recorded in the ticketing system. Based on completed change tickets, it is verified whether the release checklists were used. The monthly reports are checked for completeness and traceability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations systematically records the quality of operational processes, compliance with SLAs, and user satisfaction, e.g., through automated surveys after ticket closure. System tests before commissioning are conducted in dedicated test environments with defined test coverage and depth. For the replacement procurement of IT components, an active reserve stock or fixed supply contracts are established.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After a ticket is closed, an email with a link to a satisfaction survey is automatically sent. The results are fed into process improvement. There is a separate staging environment that is an exact replica of the production environment. Critical hardware components are kept in stock or are covered by supply contracts with a 4-hour replacement service.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the results of the satisfaction surveys and checks if measures have been derived from them. The architecture and state of the test environment are assessed. The documentation on reserve stock or the supply contracts are inspected and checked for their adequacy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational processes are largely automated and are controlled by an integrated IT Service Management tool.
