The release of changes is handled via an automated CI/CD-pipeline with automated tests (unit, integration, security tests). The process quality is continuously monitored through Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), which are visualized in real-time dashboards. Deviations from KPIs proactively trigger improvement measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A CI/CD pipeline (e.g., with Jenkins or GitLab CI) automatically compiles, tests, and deploys changes. If a test fails, the rollout is stopped and the developers are informed. A BI tool accesses the ticketing system's data and displays KPIs such as 'Mean Time To Resolution' (MTTR) or 'Change Failure Rate' in a dashboard. Exceeding a threshold (e.g., Change Failure Rate > 5%) automatically creates a problem ticket for root cause analysis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the CI/CD pipeline and the test stages implemented within it. The KPI dashboards are checked for their significance and the correctness of the underlying data. It is verified that KPI deviations actually lead to documented improvement measures. An automated audit could check the configuration files of the CI/CD pipeline for the existence of security test stages: `find /etc/jenkins/jobs -name config.xml -exec grep -l 'security-scan' {} +`.

controls.title: Regular Target-Actual Comparison (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD regularly and on an ad-hoc basis check for all operated IT components and resources whether the current configuration corresponds to the target state. Furthermore, it SHOULD be checked whether the actual practiced processes implement the defined IT operations processes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Manual, random audits of system configurations are performed, e.g., quarterly. The target state is documented in the operational manuals and configuration guidelines. Process conformity is checked by observing employees in their daily work (shadowing) or by analyzing ticket data. The results are recorded in an audit report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the audit reports of the last target-actual comparisons. It is checked whether the identified deviations have been tracked and resolved. The auditor conducts their own random comparisons of system configurations with the documented target state.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The target-actual comparison of configurations is automated by using configuration management or specialized audit tools. These tools regularly check the systems against the stored target configurations and report deviations (configuration drift). Process conformity is monitored through the systematic analysis of log data and process metrics from the ticketing system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A tool like Ansible or a Security Configuration Management (SCM) tool performs daily compliance checks. A dashboard shows the current compliance status of all systems. Deviations automatically generate a ticket for the responsible team. Process mining tools are used to reconstruct the actual process flows from the log data and compare them with the target process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the audit tool and the target specifications defined within it. The tool's reports and dashboards are checked for correctness and significance. It is verified that automatically generated tickets for deviations are processed promptly. The results of the process mining analysis are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The target-actual comparison is a continuous, fully automated process. Configuration deviations are not only detected but also automatically corrected (self-healing), provided this is possible without operational disruption. The compliance data is reported in real-time to a SIEM system and correlated with other security events to detect complex attacks. Process conformity is enforced through continuous controls within the executing systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration management tool (e.g., Puppet, Chef) runs in 'Enforce' mode and restores the target state with each execution. Any configuration drift is reported to the SIEM as a high-priority event. The ticket system only allows process steps in the predefined order and only by authorized persons, which makes process deviations technically impossible.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the configuration management tool in self-healing mode. In the SIEM, it is checked whether configuration drifts are correctly received and processed as events. The ticket system's workflow engine is checked for its correct implementation of the target processes. An automated audit could try to manually change a configuration file and verify that the change is automatically reverted within minutes: `echo 'PermitRootLogin yes' >> /etc/ssh/sshd_config; sleep 300; grep 'PermitRootLogin no' /etc/ssh/sshd_config`.

controls.title: Performing IT monitoring (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All IT components SHOULD be integrated into a unified IT monitoring system that includes all relevant parameters of the IT components. IT operations SHOULD perform IT monitoring according to a predefined monitoring plan. For each IT component, appropriate thresholds SHOULD be determined that trigger a notification or an alarm. The monitoring data SHOULD only be transmitted over secure communication channels. Regular reports SHOULD be generated on the findings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central monitoring system (e.g., Zabbix, Icinga2) is used. For each system category (e.g., web servers, databases), a template with standard checks (CPU, RAM, Disk, reachability) and thresholds is defined. Alarms are sent by email to the responsible operations group. Communication between monitoring agents and the server is encrypted with TLS.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the list of assets in the CMDB with the hosts configured in the monitoring system to check for completeness. The defined thresholds are assessed for their appropriateness. It is checked whether the alarm paths are documented and functional. The configuration of the communication encryption is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT monitoring is coordinated with the overarching service management. Not only technical parameters but also the performance of applications from the end-user perspective are monitored (Application Performance Monitoring, APM). Based on monitoring results, it is checked whether the infrastructure needs to be expanded or adapted (Capacity Management). The concept of IT monitoring is regularly reviewed and updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The monitoring system automatically creates tickets in the ticket system when alarms are triggered. APM tools are used to measure the response times of web applications. The monitoring data is stored long-term and used for trend analyses to identify capacity bottlenecks early. The monitoring concept is reviewed at least once a year.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of the monitoring and ticket system. The configuration and the significance of the APM measurements are assessed. The capacity management reports are reviewed to check whether the trend analyses lead to concrete measures. The logs of the monitoring concept review are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT monitoring uses predictive analysis methods (e.g., based on machine learning) to predict failures and performance bottlenecks before they occur. The system can automatically react to specific events based on predefined rules (e.g., restarting a service, scaling resources in the cloud). The monitoring is part of a comprehensive observability concept that correlates metrics, logs, and traces to enable in-depth problem analysis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring solution like Prometheus in combination with Grafana and Alertmanager is used. AI-based modules (AIOps) analyze the metrics and detect anomalies and trends that indicate future problems. An Alertmanager is configured to execute scripts on certain alarms that automatically fix simple problems. Logs (e.g., via Loki) and traces (e.g., via Jaeger) are collected centrally and linked with the metrics.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses the configuration and effectiveness of the predictive analysis and auto-remediation functions. The implementation of the observability concept and the ability to correlate metrics, logs, and traces are checked. A simulated error is used to verify whether the automatic response works as expected. An automated audit could check the Alertmanager configuration for the presence of auto-remediation rules: `grep -r 'webhook_configs' /etc/alertmanager/alertmanager.yml | grep 'remediation-script'`.

controls.title: Maintaining a vulnerability inventory (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD maintain a vulnerability inventory in which the vulnerabilities of all operated IT components and the handling of these are centrally recorded and maintained. IT operations SHOULD initiate, track, and ensure the remediation of vulnerabilities. A process SHOULD be defined that specifies how to deal with vulnerabilities and at least specifies by when updates must be installed and when components must be decommissioned.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central vulnerability inventory is maintained in a table or a specialized tool. The results of regular vulnerability scans are manually transferred to this inventory. For each vulnerability, a responsible person and a deadline for remediation are set. Tracking is done through regular meetings.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the vulnerability inventory and checks it for completeness and currency. It is checked whether a remediation plan exists for all recorded vulnerabilities and whether the set deadlines are being met. The minutes of the vulnerability management meetings are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The vulnerability inventory is automatically populated and maintained by a central vulnerability management tool. The tool correlates scan results over time and prioritizes vulnerabilities based on severity (e.g., CVSS score) and the criticality of the affected asset. The process also specifies whether and how IT components with non-remediable vulnerabilities must be separated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A vulnerability management tool like Tenable.sc or Greenbone Security Manager is used. Critical vulnerabilities on public systems automatically create high-priority tickets in the ticket system. The process describes how a system with a critical vulnerability for which there is no patch can be isolated by additional firewall rules or by moving it to a quarantine network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the vulnerability management tool, especially the automation and prioritization rules. It is checked whether ticket creation for critical vulnerabilities works reliably. It is checked whether the process for isolating systems is documented and has been applied when necessary.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Vulnerability management is deeply integrated with the CMDB and patch management. The prioritization of vulnerabilities is risk-based, incorporating threat intelligence and the actual exploitability in the specific context. The remediation of vulnerabilities is largely automated. The entire lifecycle of a vulnerability, from discovery to verification of remediation, is tracked seamlessly and automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The vulnerability management tool uses data from the CMDB to assess the business impact of an asset. Threat intelligence feeds are subscribed to, which provide information on which vulnerabilities are being actively exploited. Patches for critical vulnerabilities are automatically rolled out via the patch management system after they have been successfully validated in a test environment. A subsequent verification scan confirms the successful remediation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of vulnerability management, CMDB, threat intelligence, and patch management. The methodology of risk-based prioritization is assessed. Using a recently remediated vulnerability, the entire automated process is traced, from detection to verification. An automated audit could compare the vulnerability scanner's configuration with the list of rolled-out patches: `scanner-cli report --unpatched | patch-manager-cli check-applied`.

controls.title: Defining and adhering to SLAs (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all IT components and all activities, IT operations SHOULD define and monitor Service Level Agreements (SLAs) that correspond to the protection needs of the IT components and are coordinated within the institution. The defined SLAs SHOULD consider the roles and permissions as well as any dependencies of the respective activity on other organizational units.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: SLAs (e.g., for availability, response time, recovery time) are documented in a service catalog. The ticket system is configured to monitor compliance with SLAs for response and resolution times. Regular reports show the SLA performance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the service catalog and the SLAs defined therein. It is checked whether the SLAs correspond to the protection needs of the respective services. The configuration of the SLA monitoring in the ticket system is checked. The SLA reports are checked for their correctness and the response to any violations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The SLAs are not only defined internally but also coordinated and legally anchored with external service providers in the form of contracts (Operational Level Agreements, OLAs) and with the business departments (Underpinning Contracts). Compliance with SLAs is monitored in real time by automated monitoring tools. In the event of an impending violation of an SLA, an escalation is proactively triggered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ticket system is configured to automatically escalate tickets that have reached, for example, 75% of their allowed resolution time. The monitoring system measures the actual availability of services and compares it with the SLA specifications. The OLAs with service providers are an integral part of the contracts and include penalties for non-compliance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the contracts with service providers and business departments for the OLAs and SLAs they contain. The configuration of the proactive escalation in the ticket system and the real-time monitoring in the monitoring system is checked. It is checked how past SLA violations were handled (e.g., assertion of penalties).

controls.title: Specification and implementation of clear operating processes (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD specify operational processes for all tasks, which include all activities and dependencies and are traceable. It SHOULD be defined who is allowed to initiate and implement processes. Interfaces to other groups must be specified. The personnel SHOULD be instructed in the processes. Process runs and results SHOULD be logged. A process for handling exceptional situations, including fallback processes, SHOULD exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The most important operational processes (e.g., Incident Management, Change Management, Service Request Fulfillment) are documented as flowcharts and text descriptions in an organizational handbook. The personnel receive regular training on the processes. The ticket system is used for logging the process runs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation and checks it for clarity and completeness. It is verified whether evidence of employee training exists. Compliance with the documented processes is checked on a random basis using completed tickets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational processes are implemented as workflows in the IT Service Management tool, which guide the operator through the necessary steps. The processes are regularly reviewed and improved based on KPIs and employee feedback (Continual Service Improvement). The fallback processes are practiced regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ticket system enforces compliance with certain process steps, e.g., a change ticket can only be closed after a risk assessment and a test report have been attached. There is a CIP board (Continuous Improvement Process) where suggestions for process optimization are collected and evaluated. Fallback scenarios are tested as part of emergency drills.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the workflows implemented in the ITSM tool. The logs of the CIP process and the resulting process adjustments are reviewed. The documentation and results of the fallback process exercises are checked.

controls.title: Securing operational resources and documentation (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only authorized IT operations personnel SHOULD be able to access the operational resources, documentation, and operational manuals. IT operations SHOULD ensure that the operational resources and documentation are available at all times. If the IT systems and applications of the operational resources communicate via the production infrastructure, secure protocols SHOULD be used. Confidential data SHOULD be transmitted exclusively via secure protocols. The operational resources SHOULD be integrated into vulnerability management and IT monitoring.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The operational resources (e.g., management servers, monitoring systems) are located in their own protected network segment (Management VLAN). Access to this segment and to the documentation platform (e.g., Wiki) is restricted by strict access permissions to a defined group of administrators. Availability is ensured by a redundant design of the central operational resources and regular backups of the documentation. Communication is consistently encrypted with TLS.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network architecture and the firewall rules for the Management VLAN. The access permissions to the operational resources and the documentation platform are checked. The backup and recovery concept for the operational resources is reviewed. The network traffic is randomly checked for the use of encrypted protocols.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to the operational resources requires two-factor authentication (2FA). All access and administrative activities on the operational resources are logged in detail, and the logs are stored centrally and in a tamper-proof manner. The operational resources themselves are subject to the same hardened standard configurations and patch management processes as the production systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the password, an OTP token is required for logging in to the management server and the wiki. A Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution is used to control access to the operational resources and to record the sessions. The log files of the operational resources are sent in real-time to a central SIEM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the implementation of the 2FA. The configuration of the PAM solution and the quality of the session recordings are checked. In the SIEM system, it is verified whether the logs of the operational resources are arriving and are stored in a tamper-proof manner. It is checked whether the operational resources are recorded in the vulnerability and patch management tool and are updated regularly.

controls.title: Considering operability during design and procurement (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For IT components, requirements for efficient and secure operation SHOULD already be considered during design and procurement. For this purpose, the requirements of IT operations SHOULD be collected and considered. IT operations SHOULD also consider the complexity of the IT.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: IT operations creates a checklist with requirements for operability (e.g., presence of monitoring interfaces, logging capabilities, automatability of configuration). This checklist must be completed and evaluated as part of procurement and development projects. IT operations is a mandatory participant in all relevant project and procurement committees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the checklist for operability requirements. Using recently completed projects, it is checked whether the checklist was used and whether IT operations was demonstrably involved in the process. It is checked whether non-compliance with operability requirements led to consequences in the project.

controls.title: Planning and deployment of operational resources (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD plan, procure, and deploy operational resources for all IT components as needed. The networks in which the operational resources are positioned SHOULD be at least logically separated from the other networks of the institution. The network for the operational resources SHOULD be further subdivided depending on the security policy and functional dependencies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated management network (e.g., VLAN) is set up, in which all central operational resources such as monitoring, configuration management, and log servers are placed. Access to this network is strictly regulated. Segmentation within the management network is done, for example, by operational groups (network admins, server admins) or target systems (Windows management, Linux management).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network plan and the firewall configuration to verify the logical separation of the management network. The internal segmentation of the management network and the corresponding access rules are checked. It is checked whether all operational resources are correctly placed in the intended segments.

controls.title: Training of operations personnel (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For IT operations, a training plan SHOULD ensure that several people have the required skills and qualifications for all IT components and operational resources. The training measures SHOULD particularly address the topics of hardening and standard configurations, specific security settings, possible interferences, and dependencies and interfaces of the processes. When new IT components are procured, a budget for corresponding training measures SHOULD be planned.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual training plan is created for IT operations, which includes both internal (knowledge sharing) and external training. For each key technology, it is ensured that at least two employees are trained. When planning the budget for new projects, an item for training is provided as standard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the training plan and compares it with the technologies in use. It is checked whether there is redundancy in qualifications. The completion of the training is proven by means of certificates and participation confirmations. In project proposals, it is checked whether training budgets have been considered.

controls.title: Planning of IT operations with special consideration for shortage and emergency situations (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD define for the operated IT components when a shortage or an emergency situation exists. For these situations, it SHOULD be determined, in accordance with the specifications of the general emergency management, which IT components are to be operated with priority or are needed for minimum operation. The emergency planning SHOULD include a disaster recovery plan, an emergency manual, and the handling of critical incidents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In coordination with emergency management, a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) is conducted to identify the critical IT services and their recovery priorities. Based on this, an IT emergency plan is created. This plan contains technical recovery plans for the prioritized systems and an emergency manual with contact details and immediate actions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the IT emergency plan and checks whether it is consistent with the BIA and the general emergency concept of the institution. It is checked whether the technical recovery plans are detailed and understandable. The up-to-dateness of the emergency manual is checked.

controls.title: Planning the use of service providers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD coordinate the use of service providers and, among other things, manage them via SLAs so that the service is provided to a sufficient extent. The use of different service providers SHOULD be coordinated with each other, especially if they are intended for the same area of activity. For such situations, a clear communication interface SHOULD be defined in each case. IT operations SHOULD document, regularly review, and adapt the provisions for service provider management and the activities intended for the service providers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A service provider management concept is created that regulates the selection, management, and review of external service providers. For each service provider, there is a designated contact person (Service Owner) in IT operations. The SLAs with the service providers are reviewed regularly (e.g., in monthly service meetings).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the service provider management concept. Based on contracts and minutes of the service meetings, it is checked whether the management and monitoring of the service providers takes place as documented. It is checked whether the communication interfaces are clearly defined and known.

controls.title: Regulations for maintenance and repair work (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT components SHOULD be maintained regularly. It SHOULD be regulated which security aspects are to be observed during maintenance and repair work. It SHOULD be determined who is responsible for the maintenance or repair of IT components. Performed maintenance and repair work SHOULD be documented. It SHOULD be ensured that work by third parties is coordinated and that internal employees authorize, observe, or accept it.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A maintenance plan is created for all relevant IT components. Every maintenance or repair action must be requested and approved via a change ticket. The execution is documented in the ticket. For work carried out by external service providers, there is a defined process that requires them to be accompanied by an internal employee.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the maintenance plan. Based on completed change tickets, it is verified whether the processes for maintenance and repair work have been adhered to and documented. Especially for work carried out by third parties, it is checked whether authorization and acceptance have been carried out by internal employees.

controls.title: Checking for Vulnerabilities (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD regularly obtain and analyze information about known vulnerabilities. IT components SHOULD be tested for vulnerabilities regularly and on an ad-hoc basis. The vulnerabilities SHOULD be remediated as quickly as possible. As long as no patches are available, other protective measures MUST be taken for severe vulnerabilities. If this is not possible, the IT component SHOULD no longer be operated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Information sources such as manufacturer newsletters and CERT warnings are subscribed to. Regular, e.g., monthly, authenticated vulnerability scans are performed. The results are analyzed and the remediation of vulnerabilities is managed via patch management (for patches) or change management (for configuration changes or other measures).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and reports of the vulnerability scanner. It is checked whether the scans take place regularly and cover all relevant systems. Based on the vulnerability inventory and the change tickets, it is checked whether the found vulnerabilities are dealt with in a timely and appropriate manner.

controls.title: Integrating assets into security monitoring (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT systems and applications used as assets are included in the basic security monitoring. Their log files are collected centrally and monitored for critical events such as failed logins or configuration changes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The assets (management servers, monitoring systems, etc.) are configured to send their logs to a central syslog server. Simple rules are defined that trigger an email notification for certain security-relevant log entries.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the assets are sending their logs to the central server. It is checked which rules are defined for alerting and whether they are working. The retention period and the protection of the central log files are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT systems and applications used as assets SHOULD be integrated into security monitoring. If the institution uses a system for central detection and automated real-time verification of event messages, the assets SHOULD be integrated into it. Assets such as IT management and IT monitoring systems SHOULD be used as a data source for security monitoring.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All assets are connected to a central SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system. The SIEM correlates events from the assets with events from other systems (firewalls, servers, clients) to detect complex attack patterns. Alarms from the IT monitoring system (e.g., 'Service X not reachable') are also sent to the SIEM and linked there with security events (e.g., 'Potential DoS attack on Service X').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the data sources and correlation rules related to the assets in the SIEM system. It is checked whether the data from IT management and IT monitoring systems are successfully used as context information. Using a simulated attack on an asset, the entire detection and alerting chain in the SIEM is verified.

controls.title: Automated Vulnerability Testing (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All IT components SHOULD be tested for vulnerabilities regularly and automatically. The results of the tests SHOULD be automatically logged and made available to other tools in security monitoring. For critical vulnerabilities, an automated alert SHOULD be triggered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central vulnerability management system performs daily or weekly, authenticated scans of all systems. The scan results are automatically imported into a database. If vulnerabilities with a CVSS score of 9.0 or higher are found, a high-priority alarm is automatically generated in the SIEM and a ticket is created in the ticket system. The scan results are made available to security monitoring to, for example, detect attack attempts on known vulnerabilities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the automated vulnerability scan, especially the frequency, depth, and scope of the scans. The rule for automated alerting for critical vulnerabilities is checked and its function verified. In the SIEM, it is checked whether the vulnerability data is available as context information for the analysis of security incidents. An automated audit could query the scanner's API to ensure that scans are running regularly: `scanner-cli get-last-scan-time --target-all`.

controls.title: Conducting Penetration Tests (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Penetration tests SHOULD be conducted for all IT components. For this purpose, a concept SHOULD be created and implemented that defines the test methods and test depths to be used, as well as the success criteria.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual plan for penetration tests is created, which provides for both internal and external tests for critical systems and applications. The concept for the tests is created by qualified internal employees or external specialists and follows recognized standards (e.g., OSSTMM, OWASP Testing Guide). The success criteria define when a test is considered successful (e.g., obtaining administrative rights). The results are tracked and lead to concrete improvement measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the plan for penetration tests and the associated test concepts. The qualification of the testers is checked. The final reports of the last penetration tests are analyzed. It is checked whether the identified vulnerabilities have been remediated and the effectiveness of the measures has been verified in a follow-up test.

controls.title: Comprehensive logging of process steps in IT operations (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the operational processes, every process step SHOULD be logged in a traceable manner.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT Service Management tool is configured in such a way that every single status change, every comment, every assignment, and every attached file within a ticket is logged with a timestamp and the name of the processor in an audit-proof manner. Administrative activities that take place on the target systems outside of the ticket system are recorded by session recording solutions (e.g., in a PAM tool) and linked to the corresponding ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the audit log functionality of the ITSM tool. On a random basis, the complete lifecycle of a complex change is traced by correlating the logs in the ticket system and the recordings of the administrative sessions. It is checked whether the logs are protected against manipulation.

controls.title: Ensuring autonomously functioning assets (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the assets, it SHOULD be ensured that they can be used even in the event of external disruptions. In particular, a failed internet connection SHOULD not lead to a disruption of the assets. The assets SHOULD be configured and located in such a way that the dependencies between the various assets are minimized. It SHOULD be prevented that the failure of one asset leads to a disruption of another asset that prevents its operation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Critical assets such as the central monitoring, IAM, or PAM system are designed to remain fully functional without a working internet connection (e.g., no dependency on cloud-based authentication services). The dependencies are documented in a matrix. It is avoided that, for example, the monitoring system depends on the database it is supposed to monitor (e.g., by using a local database or splitting into separate clusters). High-availability clusters are set up for all central assets.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture of the assets and the dependency matrix for single points of failure and external dependencies. As part of an emergency drill, the internet connection is cut to test whether the assets continue to function autonomously as expected. The configuration of the high-availability clusters is checked.

controls.title: Proactive maintenance in IT operations (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Proactive maintenance SHOULD be carried out for the IT systems, in which preventive maintenance measures are carried out at fixed intervals. In addition, it SHOULD be considered for each IT component whether predictive maintenance is used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Based on manufacturer recommendations and own experience, regular, preventive maintenance work is planned and carried out (e.g., restarting systems, cleaning up temporary files, checking database indexes). For highly critical systems, predictive maintenance approaches are pursued, in which monitoring data and logs are analyzed with AI methods to determine the optimal maintenance time shortly before a probable failure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the plan for proactive maintenance and checks its implementation based on the change logs. It is assessed whether the methodology for predictive maintenance is comprehensible and whether the predictions lead to measurable improvements (e.g., reduction of unplanned outages). The effectiveness of the measures is analyzed based on the incident statistics.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
IT Operations is an organizational unit and the associated business process within information technology. The process describes the tasks with all activities that are implemented by the IT Operations organizational unit. IT encompasses all IT components of an institution, in particular IT systems, services, applications, platforms, and networks. IT Operations includes, among others, the following tasks:

• Administration, including inventory and documentation
• Involvement in procurement
• Commissioning and decommissioning, including replacement of IT
• IT administration
• IT monitoring
• IT incident management

The proper, secure, and correct execution of IT Operations is essential to ensure the functionality of IT. For this purpose, IT Operations establishes frameworks, for example for process design, and ensures that they are adhered to.

Furthermore, IT Operations must also provide its own operational resources, i.e., the specific IT components used for the operational purposes of IT Operations, to an appropriate extent and ensure their functionality. The operated IT therefore always includes the operational resources of IT Operations itself. From a security perspective, these resources are of particular importance. They hold a lot of information that is important for the IT components and their functionality, which offers an attractive target for an attack and must therefore be protected. Moreover, their availability is essential for IT Operations.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of this module is to establish information security as an integral part of all generally applicable aspects of IT operations. By implementing this module, the institution ensures that the activities of general IT operations, which ensure the functionality of IT, are carried out properly and systematically.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module OPS.1.1.1 General IT Operations must be applied once to the entire information network.

To create an IT-Grundschutz model for a specific information network, the entirety of all modules must be considered as a matter of principle. As a rule, several modules are to be applied to the topic or target object.

This module deals with overarching aspects of IT operations. In larger institutions, it is also advisable to embed IT operations in the institution's service management. Standard works such as the "Information Technology Infrastructure Library" (ITIL) can be used for this purpose. Such service management is not limited to IT (IT service management), but also addresses business processes and specialist tasks such as "Portfolio Management".

The following contents are also important and are dealt with elsewhere:

• special aspects of IT operations from other modules in the OPS.1.1 Core IT Operations layer, in particular the performance of administration (see OPS.1.1.2 Proper IT Administration) and activities in patch and change management (see OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management)
• aspects of network and system management (see NET.1.2 Network Management and OPS.1.1.7 System Management)
• the proper management of users and rights (see ORP.4 Identity and Authorization Management)
• aspects of data backup and archiving (see CON.3 Data Backup Concept and OPS.1.2.2 Archiving)
• aspects that do not relate to normal operation, but to exceptional situations, in particular to an IT attack and the compromise of IT systems (Incident Management, see module DER.1 Detection of security-relevant events as well as modules from the DER.2 Security Incident Management area and module DER.4 Emergency Management)
• special requirements in the event that IT operations are carried out by third parties (see OPS.2.3 Use of Outsourcing and OPS.3.2 Offering Outsourcing)

This module does not cover

• the part of the operation of IT components for which not the IT operations, but e.g. a specialist department is responsible,
• special aspects of DevOps,
• aspects that are characteristic of the IT service, for example the interface to users or the provision of a hotline, and
• the implementation of IT projects.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Insufficient personnel capacity
parts.prose:
The operations staff is responsible for ensuring that the entire IT is functional, without which institutions are often no longer operable. IT is particularly at risk if IT operations do not have sufficient capacity.
If there is a shortage of personnel, e.g. due to incorrect or insufficient personnel planning, IT operations processes cannot be carried out properly. In addition to availability, the confidentiality and integrity of the information domain can also be restricted, e.g. if no suitable IT monitoring or security monitoring is carried out due to a lack of personnel.
If the required know-how is not sufficiently redundantly available to the operations staff, for example because other personnel has only been inadequately trained, the dependence on individual persons can lead to the availability of IT operations no longer being fully guaranteed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Loss of operationally relevant information
parts.prose:
Processes that are inadequately executed by IT operations can lead to operationally relevant information becoming outdated or even lost.
If IT operations carry out activities based on inadequate or manipulated documentation, this can lead to disruptions in IT functionality. If, in addition, the information required to resolve a fault is only available to an insufficient extent, these faults cannot be resolved or can only be resolved incorrectly. As a consequence of inadequate documentation, both the availability of the IT components and the confidentiality of the information can be impaired.
If the operationally relevant information is inadequately secured, e.g. by being disclosed or made easily accessible, its confidentiality is no longer guaranteed.
A cause for the loss of operationally relevant information can be, for example, insufficient coordination with the contracted service providers regarding the documentation to be supplied, which can result in the aforementioned consequences.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Limited availability of operating resources
parts.prose:
Operational resources, which include all IT components with which IT operations activities are performed, have a considerable influence on the efficient execution of IT operational processes.
If the operational resources are insufficiently redundant, only have limited hardening, or are overloaded, this can restrict availability. If operational resources are not sufficiently available, e.g. errors that have occurred on operated IT components cannot be rectified, which jeopardizes the availability, integrity, or confidentiality of the operated IT components.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Misuse of operationally relevant information and privileged rights by authorized persons
parts.prose:
Privileged rights of the operations staff allow for far-reaching effects on the entire IT. If operationally relevant information and privileged rights are abused by authorized persons to sabotage, manipulate, or spy on information, all information security objectives for the operated IT components and for the institution's information are at risk. This situation can have several causes.
If the operations staff has privileged rights that are too broad, these authorizations can be abused for attacks. Coercion, phishing, or social engineering can also be used to force the release of extensive rights or the disclosure of operationally relevant information.
If internal or external operations staff leave and the corresponding processes are inadequately executed, such persons can continue to use the privileged rights. Similarly, shared accounts can result in continued access to operationally relevant information and operational resources, e.g. when changing jobs.
Operationally relevant information can also be disclosed due to human error, for example by not implementing regulations that prevent espionage or theft.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Accessibility or espionage of operating resources and operationally relevant information by unauthorized persons
parts.prose:
If there is insufficient protection against unauthorized access to rooms in which operational resources are located, this can be used as a starting point for any type of attack or abuse. Consequently, all information security objectives can be impaired.
Interfaces or access points of IT operations that are inadequately secured can facilitate unauthorized persons to reach or spy on operational resources and operationally relevant information.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Misdirection of IT operations
parts.prose: If internal or external persons deliberately present false facts to IT operations, for example by falsely impersonating another person, IT operations can be tricked into incorrect reactions. For example, phishing e-mails sent to IT operations can trigger incorrect activities. Depending on how IT operations are misled, all information security objectives can be significantly endangered. Availability can be restricted if, for example, administrators are tricked into shutting down IT systems.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Obstruction of operational processes
parts.prose:
If the activities of IT operations are blocked and thus not carried out properly, the availability and integrity of the entire IT can be impaired.
A possible cause can be an inadequate design and procurement of IT components, for example, by not considering whether the applications can be operated well. Likewise, the incorrect planning of processes, e.g. due to unclear interfaces or responsibilities, can lead to IT operations being carried out inadequately.
Incorrectly executed activities by the operations staff, which are due, for example, to insufficient know-how about operational processes, can also cause operational processes to be prevented and thus the entire IT to be only available or functional to a limited extent.
Likewise, the behavior of the operations staff or the activities of various service providers with unclearly defined interfaces can prevent operational processes from being carried out correctly.

controls.title: Substitution rules (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Substitution rules exist only informally for a few administrative tasks that are considered particularly critical. There is no guarantee that the designated substitutes actually have the required knowledge or permissions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In practice, if an administrator is absent, improvisation takes place by colleagues trying to take over the tasks. This often leads to delays and errors, as access and knowledge must first be laboriously acquired.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews several administrators about the substitution rules for their tasks. If the answers are inconsistent or do not refer to any formal regulation, this is an indicator for this maturity level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Substitutes are named for most administrative tasks. The rules are documented but are not regularly checked for currency (e.g., regarding the permissions and knowledge of the substitute).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A list of substitutes is maintained, for example, in a wiki. However, the permissions of the substitutes are not kept up to date proactively, but are only adjusted as needed in the event of a substitution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the substitution rules. It is checked in random samples whether substitutes are named for selected administrative tasks. However, it is not expected that the technical permissions of the substitutes are ready for use at all times.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A substitute MUST be appointed for every administration task. The substitute MUST have the necessary administrative permissions (organizational and technical) to be able to carry out the activity. An appointed substitute MUST have the necessary knowledge in the context of the administration task. The substitution regulation MUST take into account shortage and emergency situations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The substitution rules are part of the role and authorization concept. At least one substitute person or a substitute team is defined for each administrative role. The necessary knowledge is ensured through regular handovers or shared documentation. The permissions are managed in such a way that the substitute is immediately able to act in case of need.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documentation of the substitution rules. On a random basis, it is verified for critical administration tasks that a designated substitute exists and has the necessary permissions. This can be done by inspecting the configuration of the authorization management system. It is checked whether the regulations also cover emergency scenarios.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The substitution rules are reviewed and formally confirmed on a regular basis, at least once a year, and on an ad hoc basis (e.g., in the event of personnel changes). The functionality of the substitution is verified through regular exercises or planned substitution assignments (e.g., during vacation).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of emergency drills, scenarios are specifically played out in which key administrators are unavailable. The substitutes must demonstrate their ability to act. The results of the drills are documented and feed into the improvement of the regulations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests evidence of the regular review of the substitution rules (e.g., minutes of reviews). In addition, the plans and results of drills in which the effectiveness of the substitution was tested are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The assignment of permissions in the event of a substitution is automated and just-in-time, for example via a Privileged Access Management (PAM) system. An administrator can request a substitution, which, after approval by a second person (e.g., a supervisor), temporarily grants the substitute the necessary rights. All activities of the substitute are separately logged and monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM system is used that is integrated with the HR system and the ticket system. Vacation or sick leave notifications can trigger the process for activating substitution rights. The substitute checks out the required login information from the PAM system, whereby the use is automatically and completely logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the PAM system and the workflows for substitution rules defined therein. Logs of past substitution cases are reviewed in order to verify the correct and logged assignment and revocation of temporary permissions.

controls.title: Termination of activity in IT administration (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When an activity is terminated, only the person's primary personal accounts are blocked. Privileged or shared accounts to which the person had access are often not considered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The offboarding process is ad-hoc and relies on the supervisor informing the IT department about the departure. There is no checklist to ensure that all access (e.g., to cloud services, special applications) is removed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the offboarding process. In a random sample, the case of a former administrator is investigated. It is checked whether active accounts or permissions still exist for this person.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a standardized checklist for offboarding administrators. Personal administrative accounts are blocked. Passwords for shared accounts known to the person are changed. The information is communicated to affected parties, but this is not formalized.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The HR department uses a standard checklist that also includes IT permissions. The process ensures that all known personal accounts are deactivated and passwords of known shared accounts are changed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the offboarding checklist. Based on a specific case, the completion of the checklist is reviewed, in particular the blocking of accounts and the changing of passwords.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a person is relieved of administration duties, all related privileged permissions MUST be revoked at the organizational and technical level. In particular, personal administrative accounts MUST be blocked and passwords of all administrative accounts known to the person MUST be changed. Furthermore, all affected parties MUST be notified that this person has been relieved of the respective duties and therefore may no longer have administrative permissions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The offboarding process is firmly defined and is triggered by the HR department. The process includes a complete list of all types of permissions (e.g., system access, physical access, cloud consoles). Formal communication to relevant stakeholders (e.g., team leaders, project managers) is part of the process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documented offboarding process. Using a case as an example, it is demonstrated that all privileged permissions were revoked, accounts were blocked, passwords were changed, and the relevant parties were informed. This is verified by inspecting system logs and email distribution lists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be regulated under which framework conditions it is checked whether the departing person has obtained additional, undocumented administrative rights. This check SHOULD be carried out in particular if the decision to relieve a person of administrative duties was not taken in agreement with the person. If such administrative rights are found, they MUST be revoked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The offboarding process includes a special step for administrators that provides for a review of system logs and configurations for unauthorized changes or self-created backdoor accounts. This check is performed and documented by another administrator.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the process description for the offboarding of administrators. In the event of an involuntary departure, proof is requested that a check for undocumented rights has taken place (e.g., through an audit report).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire offboarding process for permissions is automated and initiated directly from the HR system. As soon as a person's departure is noted in the HR system, all their accounts and permissions in all connected systems (on-premises and cloud) are automatically blocked or deleted. An automatic scan of the systems for accounts or configuration changes created by the person is carried out and the results are submitted to the security team for review.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Identity and Access Management (IAM) system is integrated with the HR system and all critical applications and platforms. The deprovisioning workflow is triggered and logged automatically. The results, including the scans for anomalies, are displayed in a central dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the IAM system and the automated offboarding workflow. The logs of a recent offboarding case are checked to verify the complete and immediate automatic blocking of all permissions and the execution of the anomaly scans.

controls.title: Traceability of administrative activities (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logging is only enabled on a few critical systems and is not collected centrally. The use of shared administrator accounts is common, making it impossible to uniquely assign actions to individuals.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators use a common 'root' or 'Administrator' account. Logs are only stored locally on the machines and are manually evaluated when needed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines that shared administrative accounts are being used. A query of log data from a system shows that actions cannot be uniquely assigned to a person.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On most systems, a basic logging of login processes and administrative events is activated. The logs are stored locally and are only manually evaluated in cases of concrete suspicion or for error analysis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default logging settings of the operating systems and applications are used. There is no central log management system. Although each administrator has a personal account, the use of shared accounts for certain tasks is still permitted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly selects a few systems and checks whether local logging is activated. They request the logs for a specific period and assess whether basic administrative activities are traceable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Administrative activities MUST be traceable. For this purpose, it MUST at least be recorded what change was made during an activity, who carried out an activity, and when an activity was carried out. The institution MUST be able to prove at any time which person has carried out which administrative activities. Every login process via an administration ID MUST be logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All relevant systems are configured to log administrative actions. The log data is sent to a central log management system to make manipulation more difficult. A policy is in place that prohibits the use of shared accounts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests an excerpt from the central log management system for a specific administrative activity. Based on the log data, it is verified that the three W-questions (Who, When, What) can be answered. It is checked whether logging is configured for all critical systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrators SHOULD have their own access credentials. Substitutes for administrators SHOULD also receive their own access credentials. The log data is evaluated regularly and on an ad hoc basis by an independent body (e.g., information security).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The use of personal administrative accounts is technically enforced. The logs in the central log management system are monitored through regular, automated searches and dashboards. Suspicious activities (e.g., logins at unusual times) lead to notifications.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that no shared administrator accounts still exist. Evidence is requested for the regular evaluation of the log data, e.g., reports or tickets that resulted from suspicious events.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative sessions on critical systems are fully recorded (session recording). The log data and recordings are stored in a tamper-proof manner and are correlated in real time in a SIEM system and analyzed for anomalies. Every administrative activity is linked to a ticket (change or incident request).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Privileged Access Management (PAM) system is used, which performs session recording for SSH and RDP sessions. The logs from the PAM are forwarded to the SIEM. Integration with the ITSM system ensures that administrative logins are only possible with a valid ticket number.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has a recording of an administrative session shown to them in the PAM system. In the SIEM system, the correlation of administrative logs with other events is checked. It is checked on a random basis whether administrative logins appear in the log without an associated ticket.

controls.title: Protection of administrative activities (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only some administrative interfaces are protected by passwords. Default passwords are still partially in use. Communication with administrative interfaces is unencrypted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators access devices via Telnet or HTTP. On some older devices, the manufacturer's default passwords have never been changed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a network scan to identify open administrative ports such as Telnet (23) or HTTP (80) for known administration interfaces. An attempt is made to log in with known default passwords.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative interfaces require authentication. The use of insecure protocols is avoided where technically easy to do so. There is a password policy, but it is not technically enforced on all systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Where possible, SSH is configured instead of Telnet and HTTPS instead of HTTP. Administrators are instructed to use complex passwords, but complexity is not checked on all systems (e.g., network components).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of randomly selected systems for the use of secure protocols (SSH, HTTPS). He asks administrators about the password policies used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Administrative interfaces and functions MUST ONLY be available to authorized persons. Suitable authentication procedures MUST be defined for these interfaces and functions. It MUST be ensured that IT administration activities can only be carried out if prior authentication has taken place. It MUST be specified which protocols may be used for administration interfaces, so that the communication taking place during administration is secured.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a mandatory policy that exclusively prescribes the use of encrypted administration protocols (e.g., SSHv2, HTTPS, RDP with NLA). All administrative access requires authentication with individual, complex passwords. Insecure protocols are disabled on the devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy for administrative access. Configuration reviews and port scans are used to verify that insecure protocols (Telnet, FTP, HTTP) are disabled for administrative purposes and that only encrypted alternatives are available. It is checked whether all access requires authentication.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Two-factor authentication (2FA) is enforced for all externally accessible administrative access and for particularly sensitive systems on the internal network. Administrative access is restricted to dedicated, secured network segments (e.g., an admin VLAN).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A RADIUS or TACACS+ server is integrated with a 2FA solution to secure logins to network components and servers. Firewall rules ensure that administrative interfaces (e.g., SSH, RDP, web GUIs) can only be accessed from the dedicated admin network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the 2FA solution and the connected systems. Firewall rule analysis and network tests are used to verify that administrative access is indeed restricted to the defined admin network.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative access is exclusively via a hardened bastion host or Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. Direct connections from client workstations to administrative interfaces of the target systems are prevented at the network level. Two-factor authentication is mandatory for all administrative access without exception.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM system is configured as the only permitted access point for administration. Administrators authenticate to the PAM with 2FA, which then establishes the connection to the target system. The firewall rules only allow administrative protocols from the IP address of the PAM system to the target systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network architecture and firewall rules to confirm that the PAM system is the only access path. He checks the configuration of the PAM system and verifies that 2FA is enforced for all users and roles.

controls.title: Regulation of IT administration roles (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are no formally defined administration roles. Permissions are granted ad-hoc and directly to user accounts, often according to the principle 'just give him admin rights, then it'll work'.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users are made direct members of highly privileged groups such as 'Domain Admins' or given 'root' access, even if they only need a small subset of these rights.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the memberships in highly privileged groups (e.g., in Active Directory). A high number of members indicates this level of maturity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are some roughly defined administration roles (e.g., 'Network Admin', 'Server Admin'). However, these roles are very broad and do not consistently follow the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Global groups for different admin teams are created in Active Directory. However, these groups are often given very general permissions on many systems, instead of fine-grained permissions per system or service.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the defined admin roles and their associated permissions. It is noted that while the roles exist, the permissions are broader than necessary for the tasks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Roles MUST be defined that are assigned exclusively for IT administration. Administration roles MUST be assigned based on the actual need in the IT administration's area of responsibility in a traceable manner. All necessary IT administration activities MUST be covered by permissions in the administration roles according to the principle of least privilege. The separation of different levels of IT components, e.g., the separation of operating system and application administration, MUST be considered in the design of the administration roles.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A role concept for administration is documented. It defines specific roles such as 'Backup Operator', 'Database Admin for App X', 'Firewall Rule Editor'. Each role has exactly the permissions required to perform the assigned tasks. The concept takes into account the separation between application and system administration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documented administration role concept. For a random sample of roles, it is checked whether the technically implemented permissions correspond to the concept and the principle of least privilege. It is verified whether a separation of, e.g., application and operating system administration has been implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The role concept and the assigned roles are reviewed regularly, at least once a year (re-certification). There is a formal process for requesting, approving, and revoking roles, which is logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual access review process is carried out, in which supervisors or system owners must confirm the administrative permissions of their employees. This process is supported by an IAM tool or a script and the results are archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the evidence from the last access review campaign. He checks the logs and confirmations and compares them with the currently assigned permissions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The assignment of administrative roles is done Just-in-Time (JIT) and is linked to an approved change or incident request. The permissions are granted only for the duration of the task and are automatically revoked afterwards. Where possible, Attribute Based Access Control (ABAC) is used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM or IAM system is integrated with the ITSM system (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow). An administrator can request temporarily elevated rights via the ticket. After approval in the ticket, the rights are automatically granted for a limited period of time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the JIT access workflow. Using an example, the process from the request in the ticket through approval to the automatic granting and revocation of rights is traced. It is checked whether administrative permissions can be obtained without a valid ticket.

controls.title: Separation of administrative and other activities (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Administrators use a single user account for all their activities, including email, web browsing, and system administration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The user 'max.mustermann' is a member of the 'Domain Admins' group and uses this account for his daily work. This poses a high risk, as a compromised account through phishing immediately gains extensive administrative rights.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the accounts of administrators and finds that their standard user accounts have administrative privileges.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a policy stating that administrators should use separate accounts for administrative and non-administrative activities. However, compliance with this policy is not technically enforced or regularly checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each administrator has a standard account (e.g., 'mmustermann') and an admin account (e.g., 'admin-mmustermann'). It is the administrator's responsibility to use the accounts correctly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks the administrators if they use separate accounts. The system logs are checked on a random basis to see if administrative accounts are logging into standard workstations, which could indicate improper use.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The person performing the task MUST know which part of their task constitutes administrative activities. Tasks that do not require administration rights MUST NOT be performed with administration rights. It MUST be ensured that administration tools are clearly recognizable as such. When an application is used to perform an administration task, the same instance of that application MUST NOT be used for other tasks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A mandatory policy is established that requires the use of separate accounts. Administration tools (e.g., special RDP clients, SSH clients) are preconfigured so that they can only be used for administrative purposes, e.g., through special shortcuts that use the admin account.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence and communication of the account separation policy. It is verified whether all administrators have separate accounts. It is verified on a sample basis whether administrative activities (e.g., according to the change log) were carried out using the designated admin accounts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The separation of administrative and other activities is technically enforced. Access credentials used for IT administration SHOULD be different from access credentials used in other contexts. The use of administrative accounts for non-administrative activities (e.g., surfing the web, email) is technically prevented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrative accounts are only allowed to log on to servers and dedicated admin workstations, but not to standard client PCs (Logon Rights). In addition, internet access for administrative accounts is blocked completely or filtered through a strict proxy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the technical configurations (e.g., GPOs in Active Directory, proxy rules) that enforce the separation. They attempt to log on to a standard client with an admin account or to access the internet.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative activities MUST be performed from dedicated, hardened Privileged Access Workstations (PAWs) or via a VDI solution for administrative purposes. These environments have no access to email or the general internet and are strictly segregated from the rest of the network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators use a normal PC for their daily work. For administrative tasks, they connect to a separate virtual machine (Admin VDI) or use a second, physical device (PAW). This admin environment is hardened according to the highest security standards and only has access to the management interfaces of the systems to be managed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the PAW/Admin VDI architecture. They verify the hardening measures and the network separation rules. In the system logs, it is checked whether administrative logons originate exclusively from the IP addresses of the PAW/Admin VDI environment.

controls.title: Regulation of IT administration activities (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are documented work instructions for recurring IT administration activities. It is informally regulated who performs which tasks, based on team affiliation and knowledge. Permissions are assigned on a role-based basis, but do not always strictly follow the principle of least privilege for each individual task.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An internal wiki contains instructions for standard tasks like 'create user' or 'restore backup'. Tasks are assigned via email or verbally to the responsible team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks to see work instructions for standard administration activities. They interview team leaders on how tasks are assigned and executed and find that a defined, though not strictly formalized, process exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every IT administration activity SHOULD be assigned to a clearly defined task. For these tasks, it SHOULD be regulated who is allowed to perform the task and who is allowed to request it. It SHOULD be traceable which processes include administration tasks. IT administration activities SHOULD only be performed with the permissions necessary to fulfill the respective task. It SHOULD be defined how IT administration activities are to be executed. The regulations for IT administration activities SHOULD be reviewed and updated regularly and on an ad-hoc basis. For every IT administration activity, it SHOULD be ensured that it can also be performed in an emergency, if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All administrative activities are mapped as defined services or changes in a service catalog or an ITSM tool. Each execution requires an order (e.g., a ticket). The regulations (who, what, how) are part of the process documentation in the ITSM system. Regular reviews of the process documentation take place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the service catalog and the process definitions in the ITSM tool. Randomly selected completed tickets are checked to verify that the activities were carried out in accordance with the defined regulations (commissioning, execution, permissions). Evidence of the regular review of the regulations is requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Standardized administration activities are largely automated and commissioned via a self-service portal or by systemic triggers. The necessary permissions are used by the automation system on a just-in-time basis. Manual interventions are limited to exceptional cases and require a special approval process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An automation platform (e.g., Ansible Tower, Rundeck) is used to execute standardized playbooks. Commissioning is done via a service portal that validates the inputs and starts the automation job. The execution is seamlessly logged and attached to the triggering ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the automation platform and the associated playbooks. They trace an automated process from the self-service portal to execution and logging. The access permissions of the automation system itself are checked for compliance with the principle of least privilege.

controls.title: Administration of specialized applications (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is documented whether a specialized application is administered by the IT operations department or by the business department (business application administration). The basic responsibilities are recorded in the application's operational documentation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In a central application directory, a technical and a business contact person is named for each application. The general division of tasks (e.g., 'IT handles operating system and database, business department handles user administration') is known.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor selects a specialized application and asks to see the documentation on responsibilities. They interview the named contact persons to verify that a common understanding of the division of tasks exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be regulated and documented which administration tasks for specialized applications are carried out by IT operations and which by business application administration. For specialized applications, it SHOULD be identified which access IT operations needs at the system level. All interfaces and dependencies between business application administration and administration by IT operations SHOULD be identified. Whenever administration processes are created and maintained, the responsibilities and dependencies of these interfaces SHOULD be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each critical specialized application, there is a detailed operating manual that contains a RACI matrix (Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed) for all administrative tasks. It precisely defines which tasks (e.g., patching OS, patching app, user onboarding, configuration change X) are performed by whom.
