parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the classification of the management infrastructure as highly critical. They check the configuration of the FIM and the log forwarding to the SIEM. In the SIEM, they have the corresponding correlation rules and dashboards shown to them and simulate a suspicious action to test the correct alerting.

controls.title: Test and acceptance procedures for new hardware (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: New hardware is procured and deployed directly in the production environment. Tests are limited to the basic function ('turns on').

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A new laptop model is purchased, provided with the standard image, and issued to a user. Compatibility problems with special software or drivers only occur during operation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Through interviews and analysis of trouble tickets, the auditor determines that the introduction of new hardware models regularly leads to an increased number of incidents, which indicates a lack of testing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: New hardware is fundamentally tested for compatibility with the standard operating system and the most important applications before widespread deployment. However, a formal acceptance procedure does not exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An IT employee tests a new laptop model for a few days in daily office life. If no major problems occur, the model is approved for procurement. The test results are not formally documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds evidence of tests performed (e.g., in emails), but cannot view standardized test plans or formal acceptance reports.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When new hardware is selected, it SHOULD be checked whether the software used, and in particular the relevant operating systems, are compatible with the hardware and its driver software. New hardware SHOULD be tested before it is deployed. For IT systems, there SHOULD be an acceptance procedure and a release declaration. The responsible persons SHOULD file the release declarations in writing in a suitable place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each new hardware model, a standardized test plan is followed, which includes compatibility, performance, and functional tests. The results are recorded in a test report. After a successful test, a formal acceptance report is created and signed by the responsible manager before the model is included in the hardware catalog.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: For a newly introduced hardware model, the auditor requests the test plan, the test report, and the signed acceptance report. They check whether the process was carried out as defined.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Tests of new hardware SHOULD take place exclusively in an isolated test environment to exclude risks to the production environment. In the event that errors are detected during operation despite the acceptance and release procedures, there SHOULD be a defined procedure for troubleshooting.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated test network is set up that is separate from the production network. New hardware is first commissioned and tested in this network. A process for 'Early Adopter' programs is established to collect feedback from a limited user group before a broad rollout. Problems are systematically recorded and reported to the manufacturer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and the logical/physical separation of the test network. They check the troubleshooting process for newly introduced hardware and review the corresponding documentation and communication with the manufacturer.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The test procedure for new hardware also includes specific security checks, such as analyzing the firmware for known vulnerabilities, checking the security of BIOS/UEFI settings, and evaluating supplied management tools. The results of this security check are a decisive criterion in the selection and acceptance process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the test procedure, the firmware of the new hardware is scanned with specialized tools. The default BIOS/UEFI settings are checked against a hardened baseline. The configuration of security features such as Secure Boot, TPM, and Virtualization-based Security (VBS) is verified.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the reports of the security checks for a newly introduced hardware model. They have the configuration of the BIOS/UEFI security features shown to them on a test device and compare it with the defined baseline.

controls.title: Ensuring the integrity and authenticity of software packages (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software is downloaded from various, sometimes untrustworthy sources. No check of integrity or authenticity is performed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator downloads a required tool from a random download website instead of from the official manufacturer's site.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds software on systems whose origin is unclear or which comes from well-known 'freeware' portals. There is no process for verifying downloads.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an instruction to generally obtain software and patches only from trusted sources (e.g., directly from the manufacturer). However, there is no systematic check of signatures or hash values.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators are instructed to use the manufacturer's websites. However, they do not perform any further checks and rely on the source being secure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the download sources are usually the official manufacturer sites. However, they find that no hash values or signatures are checked to rule out manipulation during transmission.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Throughout the entire patch or change process, the authenticity and integrity of software packages SHOULD be ensured. For this purpose, it SHOULD be checked whether checksums or digital signatures are available for the software packages used. If so, these SHOULD be checked before installing the package. Software and updates SHOULD generally only be obtained from trusted sources.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process is defined that requires checking the hash value provided by the manufacturer (e.g., SHA-256) for each downloaded software package. For important software, the digital signature of the file is verified. The performance of this check is documented in the corresponding change ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor selects a sample of recently deployed software. In the associated change ticket, they check whether the check of the hash value or signature is documented. They repeat the check themselves as an example.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central, trusted software repository is set up. Only software packages whose integrity and authenticity have been successfully checked are added to this repository. Software is deployed to the target systems exclusively from this repository.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated network share or a software distribution tool (e.g., SCCM/MECM) serves as the central repository. The process ensures that administrators must first verify packages before they can upload them to the repository and release them for distribution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the process for adding software to the central repository. They verify the access permissions to the repository and ensure that end systems are configured to only obtain software from there.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The verification of the integrity and authenticity of software packages is fully automated. The deployment tool automatically performs the verification of signatures and hash values before a package is cached for installation or executed. A failure of the verification automatically leads to the termination of the process and a security alert.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The software distribution tool is configured to enforce the specification of a hash value when defining a new package. Before installation, the client calculates the hash value of the downloaded file and compares it. In case of a discrepancy, the installation is denied and an event is reported to the central server and the SIEM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the distribution tool shown to them, which enforces the automatic hash value check. As a test, they manipulate a software package in the distribution cache and verify that the installation on a test client fails and a corresponding message is sent to the server and the SIEM.

controls.title: Continuous documentation of information processing (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: System documentation exists, but is rarely or not at all updated after changes. The documented state deviates significantly from the actual state.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is an outdated network diagram. New servers or changed firewall rules from the last two years are not included in it.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the existing documentation (e.g., system manual, network plan) with the actual state of the systems and finds significant discrepancies.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an instruction to update the documentation after changes. However, this is not systematically tracked or reviewed, leading to inconsistent quality and outdated information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators are reminded to maintain the documentation. Whether this actually happens depends on the diligence of the individual.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: When reviewing change tickets, the auditor finds that updating the documentation is not a mandatory step for closing the ticket. A random check shows that some documentation is up to date, while other documentation is not.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Changes SHOULD be documented in all phases, all applications, and all systems. Corresponding regulations SHOULD be developed for this purpose, which define what is to be documented, where, and how.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A system documentation policy is created. It defines the documents to be maintained (e.g., system manual, network plan, configuration data in a CMDB) and specifies that updating the documentation is an integral part of the change management process. A change ticket can only be closed once the documentation update has been confirmed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation policy. For a sample of closed change tickets, they check whether the 'Update documentation' step is marked as completed and compare the updated documentation with the change that was made.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The currency and correctness of the documentation is regularly checked, e.g., as part of audits or reviews. A central Configuration Management Database (CMDB) is used to manage configuration data in a structured manner.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Annual reviews of the system documentation are conducted and documented by the system owners. A CMDB is established as the central source for configuration information. Changes to configuration items (CIs) are controlled via the change process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the logs of the last documentation reviews. They check the structure and content of the CMDB and compare an entry with the real system to verify its accuracy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation of IT systems and configurations is largely automated. Discovery tools continuously update the CMDB. Deviations between the documented target state in the CMDB and the actual state captured by the discovery tools are automatically detected and reported (Configuration Drift Detection).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Network and system discovery tools regularly scan the environment and feed their data into the CMDB. A configuration management system compares the actual state with the baselines stored in the CMDB. In case of deviations, an incident ticket is created or the configuration is automatically corrected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the automated CMDB update process demonstrated to them. They make an unauthorized configuration change to a test system and verify that this deviation (drift) is detected and reported by the system.

controls.title: Use of tools in change management (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before a change management tool is used, it SHOULD be carefully checked whether it can distribute changes appropriately within the information system. This includes checking its suitability for all system types to be managed and its scalability for the size of the environment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before using a deployment tool, a proof-of-concept phase is conducted. During this phase, it is tested whether the tool supports all relevant operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS) and application formats and whether the performance is sufficient for the number of clients.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the proof-of-concept or the evaluation for the tool being used. They check whether the suitability for the specific information system has been comprehensibly assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Additionally, it SHOULD be possible to define interruption points at which the distribution of a faulty change is stopped. The tool must support functions for a staggered rollout (e.g., to pilot groups) to minimize risk.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The tool used is configured so that changes are always first distributed to a pilot group (e.g., the IT department). Only after a successful test phase in the pilot group is the distribution extended to other groups. The tool provides a function to pause or withdraw an ongoing distribution at any time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the pilot groups and the staggered rollouts in the tool demonstrated to them. They check the process for stopping a faulty distribution and review corresponding logs if such a case has already occurred.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The change management tool supports advanced deployment strategies such as 'Canary Releases' or 'Blue-Green Deployments'. It is integrated with monitoring systems to automatically detect a faulty change based on telemetry data (e.g., increased error rates, performance degradation) and trigger an automatic rollback.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A blue-green deployment strategy is used for critical applications. The tool deploys the new version on a parallel infrastructure. After successful tests, the traffic is switched to the new environment. Monitoring tools monitor the application after the switch. If error thresholds are exceeded, the traffic is automatically switched back to the old environment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the deployment pipeline and the monitoring integration. They have the process of an automatic rollback demonstrated to them by simulating an error in a test change. They check the telemetry data and the alarm thresholds that trigger the rollback.

controls.title: Success measurement of change requests (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To check whether a change was successful, the respective business owners for patch and change management SHOULD conduct post-implementation tests. This involves checking whether the system functions as expected after the change.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After each change, the technical implementer performs a functional test. Subsequently, the requesting business owner confirms in a User Acceptance Test (UAT) that the change has achieved the desired result and that no negative side effects occur in the process. The confirmation is recorded in the change ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: In a random sample of changes, the auditor checks whether the post-implementation test (UAT) was demonstrably carried out by the business owner and documented in the ticket.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For conducting post-implementation tests, the business owners SHOULD select suitable reference systems as quality assurance systems. The results of the post-implementation tests SHOULD be formally documented as part of the change process to ensure a traceable success control.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The post-implementation tests are carried out based on a predefined test plan that covers both the expected positive function and possible negative side effects. The results are recorded in a standardized test protocol, which is attached to the change ticket. A dedicated QA system, which is close to the production system, is used for the acceptance tests.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the test plans and the completed test protocols for a sample of changes. They check whether the tests were carried out and documented systematically and comprehensibly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The success of a change is measured not only by functional tests, but also by predefined, quantitative metrics and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs). This includes, for example, performance metrics, error rates, or transaction times. The measurement of these KPIs is automated and the results are included in a formal evaluation of the change.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each major change, success KPIs are defined in advance (e.g., 'The response time of the search function must remain below 2 seconds'). After implementation, Application Performance Monitoring (APM) tools measure these KPIs automatically. A dashboard visualizes the before-and-after values. A significant deterioration leads to an investigation or a rollback.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: For a change, the auditor checks whether success KPIs were defined in advance. They review the APM dashboards and reports to verify that the KPIs were measured after the change and that the results support the success evaluation of the change.

controls.title: Synchronization within change management (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the change management process, suitable mechanisms SHOULD ensure that devices that are temporarily or long-term unavailable (e.g., laptops of field service employees) also receive the patches and changes as soon as they reconnect to the network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The software distribution tool used is configured to cache distribution jobs for offline devices. As soon as a client reports back to the management server, the job is executed. There is a policy that field service employees must connect their devices to the company network (e.g., via VPN) at least once a week.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the distribution tool regarding the handling of offline clients. They review reports on the patch status to determine if there is a large number of devices that are permanently outdated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Active measures are taken to ensure synchronization. The compliance reports of the management tool are regularly evaluated to identify devices that have not received updates for a long time. A follow-up process is initiated for these devices.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A weekly report is generated listing all devices that have not contacted the management server for more than 14 days. The responsible administrator contacts the device user to clarify the issue. Repeated non-compliance can lead to deactivation of network access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the compliance reports and the measures derived from them. Using examples, the auditor checks whether the process for following up on non-compliant devices is working.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Technical solutions are used that enable synchronization even without a direct connection to the internal LAN or VPN. Devices that fall below a defined patch level are automatically denied access to company resources until they have reached the required level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Cloud Management Gateway (CMG) is used, through which clients can also receive patches and policies from the internet. A Network Access Control (NAC) or a Conditional Access Policy checks the patch status of the device with every request. If the device is not compliant, it is directed to a quarantine network where it only has access to the update servers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the Cloud Management Gateway and the Conditional Access Policies. The auditor uses a test device that is intentionally not up-to-date with patches and verifies that access to internal resources is blocked and the device is redirected to quarantine.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose: It is a major challenge to update the information technology components used in an institution correctly and in a timely manner. Practice shows that existing security vulnerabilities or operational disruptions are often due to inadequate or missing patches and changes. A missing or neglected patch and change management system therefore quickly leads to potential points of attack. The general task of patch and change management is to make modifying interventions in applications, infrastructure, documentation, processes, and procedures manageable and controllable.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: This module shows how a functioning patch management system can be set up in an institution and how the corresponding process can be controlled and optimised. In addition to patch management, however, the module also contains some core aspects of change management that are relevant to information security. Change management is the task of planning and controlling changes.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose: The module OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management is to be applied to the entire information network. The descriptions in this module focus on IT operations, and in particular on patch management, which is used to update software (e.g. through security patches, service packs, and hotfixes). The individual modules of the SYS IT Systems and APP Applications layers may contain more specific requirements regarding patch and change management. This module does not contain a complete change management system, but only the core aspects for information security. In larger institutions, it is advisable to also structure change management systematically. For this purpose, standard works such as the change management process of the 'IT Infrastructure Library' (ITIL) can be used. Such a change management system does not have to be limited to IT, but can also include business processes and specialist tasks themselves. In this module, 'change' includes everything that goes along with adapting IT components, such as 'changes', 'patches', 'updates', 'upgrades', 'installation', 'removal', etc. Software development, on the other hand, is covered in the CON.8 Software Development module. Requirements for testing and releasing patches and software are not dealt with in detail in this module. They can be found in the module OPS.1.1.6 Software Tests and Releases.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Poorly defined responsibilities
parts.prose: Poorly defined, overlapping or unclear responsibilities can, for example, slow down the categorisation and prioritisation of change requests. This can delay the overall distribution of patches and changes. Even if patches and changes are released prematurely without a test run and without considering all (technical) aspects, this can have a serious impact on security. In extreme cases, poorly defined responsibilities can affect the entire institution completely or to a large extent. Disruptions in operation have a negative impact on availability. If security-relevant patches are not distributed or are distributed late, confidentiality and integrity can be jeopardised.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Poor communication in change management
parts.prose: If patch and change management is not well accepted within the institution or if the people involved communicate poorly, this can lead to change requests being processed with delay or incorrect decisions being made about a change request. This can reduce the overall security level and seriously disrupt IT operations. In any case, poor communication makes the change process inefficient, as too much time and resources have to be invested. This has a negative impact on the institution's ability to react and, in extreme cases, can lead to security vulnerabilities or the institution's important objectives not being achieved.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Insufficient consideration of business processes and specialized tasks
parts.prose: Inappropriate changes can, among other things, impair the smooth running of business processes or specialist tasks or even lead to the complete failure of the IT systems involved. Even the most extensive testing procedure cannot completely rule out the possibility that a change will prove to be faulty in later productive operation. If the impact, category or priority of a submitted change request is incorrectly assessed in the change process with regard to business processes or specialist tasks, the desired security level may be reduced. Such misjudgements occur mainly when the people responsible for IT and the responsible specialist departments do not coordinate sufficiently.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Insufficient resources for patch and change management
parts.prose: Effective patch and change management requires adequate human, time and financial resources. If these are not available, the necessary roles could, for example, be filled with unsuitable people. It would also not be possible to create interfaces for certain information, for example between the IT department and the relevant contact persons in the specialist departments. The necessary capacities for the infrastructure of the test and distribution environments could also not be provided. While the human, time and financial shortcomings can often be compensated for in regular operation, they become all the more apparent under high time pressure, for example when emergency patches have to be installed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Problems with the automated distribution of patches and changes
parts.prose: Patches and changes are often not distributed manually, but centrally with software support. If such software is used, faulty patches and changes can be distributed automatically throughout the entire information network, which can lead to major security problems. It is particularly serious if software containing security vulnerabilities is installed on many IT systems at the same time. If only isolated errors occur, they can often be rectified by hand. However, it becomes problematic if IT systems are not accessible for a longer period of time. An example is field staff who rarely and irregularly connect their IT systems to the institution's LAN. If the tool is configured in such a way that the updates are only distributed within a certain period of time, and then not all IT systems are accessible, these IT systems cannot be updated.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Inadequate recovery options in patch and change management
parts.prose: If patches or changes are distributed without a recovery option being provided, or if the recovery routines of the software used do not work or do not work properly, incorrectly updated software cannot be corrected in a timely manner. This can lead to the failure of important IT systems and high consequential damage. In addition to the loss of data, the availability and integrity of the data and the affected IT systems are particularly at risk.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Misjudgment of the relevance of patches and changes
parts.prose: If changes are prioritised incorrectly, unimportant patches could, for example, be installed first. Important patches, on the other hand, are then installed too late. Security vulnerabilities thus remain for longer. Patch and change management is often supported by software-based tools. These tools can also contain software errors and thus provide insufficient or incorrect information about a change. If the information that such a tool provides about a change is not checked and tested for plausibility, the actual implementation of changes may differ from the assumed one.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.8. Manipulation of data and tools in change management
parts.prose: Patch and change management often operates from a central point. Due to its exposed position, it is particularly at risk. If an attacker were to succeed in taking over the servers involved, manipulated software versions could be distributed to a large number of IT systems simultaneously via this central point. Further points of attack often arise from the fact that these IT systems are operated by external partner institutions (outsourcing). There could also be maintenance accesses that allow access to the central server for the distribution of changes. These could also be used for attacks.

controls.title: Creation of a concept for protection against malicious programs (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A concept for protection against malicious programs exists only in fragments or is severely outdated. It typically covers only standard clients, while servers, mobile devices, IoT systems, or production facilities are disregarded. Formal documentation is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, there are often only verbal agreements or a short note in a general IT manual. Responsibility for protection is not clearly assigned, and action is taken reactively when an incident occurs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews with IT staff whether a formal, documented, and comprehensive concept exists. The examination of existing documents shows that essential parts of the information network (e.g., IoT) are not covered and the document has not been updated for several years.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic concept for protection against malicious programs is documented. It lists all essential IT system categories (clients, servers, IoT) that need to be protected. However, the description of HOW the protection should be implemented remains general and non-specific.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document exists that, for example, stipulates that 'an antivirus program must be installed'. However, it lacks details on specific products, configurations, or update strategies. The concept is not regularly reviewed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing concept document. It is found that although all system types are mentioned, no concrete, implementable protective measures or responsibilities are defined. A process for regular updating of the concept cannot be proven.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A concept MUST be created that describes which IT systems must be protected from malicious programs. IoT devices and production systems MUST also be taken into account. Furthermore, it MUST be specified how the protection is to be implemented. If reliable protection is not possible, the identified IT systems SHOULD NOT be operated. The concept SHOULD be comprehensibly documented and kept up to date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concept is maintained as a formal document approved by the Information Security Officer (ISO). It names the system groups to be protected, the intended protection technologies (e.g., Endpoint Protection, email filters), and the basic responsibilities for operation and configuration. It defines a cycle for review and updating (e.g., annually).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the concept for protection against malicious programs. It is checked whether the document addresses all relevant system categories (incl. IoT/production), defines concrete protective measures, and bears an update note that is not older than the defined review cycle. It is randomly checked whether the protective measures described in the concept are implemented on the systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The concept for protection against malicious programs is reviewed and updated regularly, at least annually and on an ad-hoc basis (e.g., in case of new threats or the introduction of new technologies). It contains specific protection profiles for different system classes and risk levels. The process for updating the concept is itself documented and formally approved by the management level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concept is more than just a document; it is integrated into the security processes. For example, there is a separate protection profile for developer workstations and one for servers in the DMZ. The update is managed by the ISMS team and the approval is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of specific protection profiles in the concept. Based on logs from change management or the ISMS committees, it is proven that the concept has been reviewed and formally approved in the last 12 months. It is checked whether an ad-hoc adjustment of the concept was made for newly introduced systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The protection concept is a living document that is fully integrated into the IT lifecycle and change management. Any commissioning of a new system or a major application automatically triggers a workflow for reviewing and adapting the concept. Compliance with the conceptual requirements is continuously verified through automated configuration and compliance checks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A CMDB or asset management system is linked to the concept. When a new IoT device is registered, the corresponding protection profile is automatically assigned and its implementation is enforced by a security configuration management tool. Deviations automatically generate a ticket in the helpdesk system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the automated process for concept adaptation demonstrated in the change management tool. The configuration of the compliance scanning tool is reviewed to verify that the rules correspond to the specifications of the concept. A report from the tool shows the current compliance status of the information network in relation to the malware protection concept.

controls.title: Use of system-specific protection mechanisms (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only the most obvious operating system's own protection mechanisms, such as a firewall that is active by default, are used. A systematic evaluation of other available mechanisms (e.g., AppLocker, ASLR, DEP) does not take place. There is no documentation as to why certain protection functions are not activated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When an operating system is installed, the default settings are adopted. Further security features included in the Professional/Enterprise version are often unknown to the administrators or their configuration is considered too complex.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Through a random check of system configurations, the auditor determines that advanced protection functions included in the operating system (e.g., Controlled Folder Access in Windows) are not activated. Interviews with administrators confirm that no formal evaluation of these functions has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A one-time inventory of available system-specific protection mechanisms has been carried out. Basic mechanisms are activated on most systems, but often only with default settings. The documentation on why a mechanism is not used is incomplete or informal.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a checklist for new server installations that provides for the activation of certain security features. However, these are not further adapted to the specific role of the server. A justification for non-use could be a simple email that is not centrally archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds evidence (e.g., a wiki entry, an old presentation) of a previous evaluation of protection mechanisms. A review of the systems shows that although they are activated, they are not configured to be hardened. The requested justifications for unused mechanisms can only be partially provided or in an informal form.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be checked which protection mechanisms are offered by the IT systems used, as well as the operating systems and applications used on them. These mechanisms MUST be used unless there is an at least equivalent substitute or good reasons not to. If they are not used, this MUST be justified and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This requirement is implemented within the framework of hardening guidelines for the respective operating systems and standard applications. A list of the relevant protection mechanisms is maintained for each system. The guideline specifies which mechanisms are to be activated. Deviations (e.g., for compatibility reasons) are documented per system or system group and approved by the ISO.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the hardening guidelines for a selected operating system (e.g., Windows Server 2022). It is checked whether these guidelines address specific protection mechanisms such as ASLR, DEP, Control Flow Guard, etc. It is then randomly checked on a system whether the guideline is implemented. In the case of an unused function, the corresponding, documented justification is requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The evaluation of system-specific protection mechanisms is a documented, recurring process that is part of the regular system reviews. The configuration of the used mechanisms is optimized for security and goes beyond the default settings. The documentation for unused mechanisms is detailed and is formally approved and archived.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The hardening guidelines are reviewed and updated at least annually or when new operating system versions are released. The configurations are distributed centrally via Group Policies (GPO) or Mobile Device Management (MDM) to ensure consistency.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the documented process for reviewing the hardening guidelines and checks the logs of the last review. The configuration of the GPO/MDM system is reviewed to confirm that the hardened settings are distributed centrally. The formally approved justifications for deviations are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use and configuration of system-specific protection mechanisms are centrally enforced and continuously monitored via configuration management tools. Deviations from the defined hardening guideline are automatically detected, reported and, ideally, automatically corrected. The effectiveness of the mechanisms is regularly verified through penetration tests or Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Security Configuration Management (SCM) or compliance tool is used to regularly check systems against the hardening policy. In case of deviations, an alarm is triggered in the SIEM system. The results of penetration tests are directly incorporated into improving the hardening policies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration and reports of the SCM tool shown to them, which document the compliance status of the systems. A penetration test report is reviewed to check whether the effectiveness of the protective mechanisms has been tested and evaluated. An automatic alarm in case of a configuration deviation is demonstrated.

controls.title: Selection of an antivirus program (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Various, inconsistent antivirus programs are used, often including free or consumer-grade versions. Selection is made on an ad-hoc basis, without central management or consideration of enterprise features.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Individual employees or departments install antivirus software at their own discretion. There is no support contract and no central console for monitoring the protection status.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During a spot check of IT systems, the auditor finds that different antivirus products, including consumer versions, are installed. A central management server or support contracts cannot be proven.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A uniform antivirus program suitable for corporate use has been selected and installed on standard clients. However, the selection was made without a formal evaluation process. Special systems such as gateways or servers may not be covered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT department decided on a product because it was well-known or was included in a package. A central management console was set up, but coverage on all systems is not guaranteed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that an enterprise product with central management is in use. However, a review of the asset inventory shows that not all systems (e.g., Linux servers, gateways) are covered by the solution. Documents for a formal selection process cannot be provided.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Depending on the operating system used, other existing protection mechanisms, and the availability of suitable antivirus programs, an appropriate protection program MUST be selected and installed for the specific purpose. For gateways and IT systems used for data exchange, a suitable antivirus program MUST be selected and installed. ONLY products for the enterprise sector with service and support tailored to the institution MAY be used. In addition to real-time and on-demand scans, a deployed solution MUST offer the ability to scan compressed data for malicious programs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The selection process is documented. It is ensured that the selected product supports all relevant operating systems used in the company (e.g., Windows, macOS, common Linux distributions). A valid support contract for the product is maintained. Before selection, it is checked whether the solution supports scanning of archives (ZIP, RAR, etc.).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the selection process for the antivirus program. The valid support contract is reviewed. It is checked on a sample basis on clients and servers whether the selected program is installed. The function for scanning compressed files is verified on a test machine.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection process for the antivirus program is based on a formal requirements catalog and comparative tests (e.g., from AV-Test or AV-Comparatives). Cloud services to improve detection performance SHOULD be used after a documented review has shown that this does not conflict with data protection or confidentiality.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a product decision is made, a 'Proof of Concept' (PoC) is conducted with several candidates. The use of cloud lookups is actively configured, and the corresponding data protection review is conducted and documented with the data protection officer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the requirements catalog and the PoC results that led to the product selection. The documentation of the data protection review for the cloud functions used is requested. The configuration of the antivirus program is checked to see if the cloud-based protection functions are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection process not only considers classic antivirus functions, but also evaluates and integrates complementary protection technologies such as Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Application Whitelisting, or behavior-based analysis. The selection process includes tests of API capabilities for integration into a SIEM system. The performance impacts are systematically measured on representative systems before the full-scale rollout.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Endpoint Protection Platform (EPP) or an Extended Detection and Response (XDR) solution is used that combines multiple layers of protection. The connection of the solution to the central SIEM is configured and functional. Performance baselines are created before and after installation to quantify the overhead.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of the endpoint solution into the SIEM by having the corresponding correlation rules and alarms shown. The documentation of the performance measurements is reviewed. It is checked whether, in addition to signature-based protection modules, behavior-based ones are also actively configured.

controls.title: Operation and configuration of antivirus programs (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The antivirus program is installed but is operated with the manufacturer's default configuration. Users with local administrator rights can change the configuration or disable the protection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After installing the agent on the clients, no further configuration steps are taken in the central management console. There are no policies to prevent users from tampering with the protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines on a client system that the user is able to deactivate the real-time protection of the virus scanner. A look into the central management console shows that only the default policy is active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic, uniform configuration is centrally rolled out to all protected systems. It is ensured that users cannot change the security-relevant settings. However, the configuration is not specifically adapted to different system types.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A company-wide policy has been created and assigned in the management console that enforces real-time protection and protects it with a password. However, the same policy applies to workstations, file servers, and database servers alike, without considering the different performance requirements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies in the management console that a central policy is active and password-protected. When reviewing the configuration, it is found that there are no differentiated settings for different server roles or for desktops vs. servers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The antivirus program MUST be configured appropriately for its operating environment. Detection performance SHOULD be the priority, unless data protection or performance reasons argue against it in the specific individual case. If security-relevant functions of the antivirus program are not used, this SHOULD be justified and documented. It MUST be ensured that users cannot make any security-relevant changes to the antivirus program settings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration is done via a central management console. Settings such as 'Heuristics' or 'Behavioral Analysis' are set to a high level. Exceptions (e.g., for performance-intensive database files) are defined specifically and restrictively and are documented. The configuration on the endpoints is protected from changes by users with a password or a policy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the central policies in the management console of the antivirus program. It is verified that the detection functions are maximized and that the policies prevent manipulation by users. For established exception rules, the corresponding documentation and justification are requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Different, optimized configuration profiles are used for different system classes (e.g., standard workstations, developer PCs, file servers, database servers, web servers). Changes to these configuration profiles are subject to a formal change management process. The justifications for specific configuration decisions, especially in performance vs. security trade-offs, are documented in detail.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Multiple policies are created in the management console for different organizational units or server groups. For example, on-access scans for read and write access are active for file servers, while for a performance-critical SQL server, only on-write scans are configured and the database files are excluded. Every change to these policies requires an approved change ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the different configuration profiles shown in the management console and compares them with the respective system groups. For a recently performed configuration change, the corresponding change ticket with justification and approval is requested. The documentation for the exception rules in the server profiles is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The effectiveness of the configurations is tested regularly and automatically, for example by using harmless test files (EICAR) or by advanced Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS) tools. The configuration settings are dynamically adapted to new threat information. The integrity of the antivirus agent on the client is actively monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script periodically distributes the EICAR test file to various directories to check the function of the on-access and on-demand scanner and to ensure that the alert chain works. A BAS tool regularly simulates attack behavior to validate the detection rates of the behavior-based modules. Threat intelligence feeds are used to specifically tighten configurations (e.g., blocking rules) for new campaigns.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the logs of the automated EICAR tests shown, including the generated alarms. A report from the BAS tool is reviewed, which shows the test results for the current configuration. The process for incorporating threat intelligence into the configuration is checked.

controls.title: Regular updating of the antivirus programs in use (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Updates of virus signatures and program versions are carried out manually and irregularly. A significant portion of the systems runs with outdated signatures for extended periods.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The clients are configured to get updates directly from the manufacturer, which fails in segmented networks. The central management server is not updated regularly, which is why the clients do not receive updates either.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through a query in the management console or through spot checks on clients that many systems have signatures that are several days or weeks old. The update history shows large gaps.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central update server is used, and the clients are configured for automatic updates. However, there is no active monitoring to verify if the clients are successfully receiving and installing their updates.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The update distribution is set up in the management console and runs automatically. However, administrators only look at the update status reactively when a problem is reported. There are no reports or alarms for outdated clients.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automatic update distribution. However, a query of the client status shows a number of systems that have not been updated for days, without this having triggered a notification or a process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On IT systems equipped with them, antivirus programs (both signatures and the software itself) MUST be updated regularly and promptly in accordance with the manufacturer's recommendations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central management server (e.g., WSUS for Microsoft Defender, or the vendor's proprietary console) is used to distribute signature and program updates. Clients are configured to fetch updates from this server several times a day. Program version updates are handled as part of general patch management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the update distribution in the management console. A report is generated showing the current update status (signatures and program version) of all managed clients. The age of the virus definitions on a client is checked on a random basis, which should typically be only a few hours.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The update status (both signatures and program version) of all protected systems is centrally and actively monitored. There is a defined process to investigate and correct systems that do not update within a specified time window (e.g., 24 hours for signatures). This process is documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An automatic report or a dashboard is configured in the management console that displays all clients with an outdated status daily. For these cases, a ticket is automatically created in the helpdesk system and assigned to an administrator. The process describes the escalation steps if a system is unreachable for an extended period.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the dashboard or the reports on the update status shown to them. The documentation of the process for handling outdated clients is requested. Compliance with the process is verified using examples in the ticket system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The update process for new program versions is staggered: Updates are first tested on a representative pilot group before being rolled out company-wide. Systems with severely outdated signatures (e.g., > 72 hours) are automatically isolated from the production network by a Network Access Control (NAC) solution until their protection status is up-to-date again.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Separate update groups are defined in the management console ('Test', 'Pilot', 'Production'). The rollout plan for new versions is documented. The antivirus management console is integrated with the NAC solution, so that the signature status can be used as a criterion for network access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the staggered update groups and the rollout plan for the last program version. The configuration of the NAC solution is inspected to verify the rule for isolating non-compliant clients. The function can be demonstrated by manually backdating a test client.

controls.title: Awareness and Obligation of Users (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A security policy exists that vaguely refers to dealing with malware. It is handed out to employees upon hiring but is not actively trained or reinforced.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Awareness is limited to a clause in the IT usage policy. There are no dedicated training sessions or campaigns on the topic of malware.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly asks selected employees about the correct behavior when faced with a suspicious email. The answers are uncertain or inconsistent. Evidence of regular training cannot be provided.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All employees receive a one-time, mandatory security awareness training that addresses the risks of malware. The responsible contact person for security incidents is documented in the intranet.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: New employees complete an e-learning module on information security as part of their onboarding. Existing employees may have completed this training a long time ago; there are no refreshers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies from training materials and attendance lists that new employees are being trained. However, it is noted that there is no process for regular refresher training.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users MUST be regularly informed about the threat of malware. They MUST adhere to the basic rules of conduct to reduce the risk of malware infection. Files, emails, websites, etc., from untrusted sources SHOULD NOT be opened. Users MUST be aware of the appropriate contacts in case of a suspected infection with a malware program. They MUST contact the designated contacts if they suspect a malware infection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Regular (e.g., annual) mandatory information security training is conducted for all employees. These cover current threats such as phishing and ransomware. The contact details of IT support or the incident response team are easy to find (e.g., as a desktop background, sticker on the monitor, in the intranet). The obligation to comply with the rules is part of the IT usage policy, which every employee must sign.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documents and attendance lists from the last awareness training. It is checked whether the training content is up-to-date. Users are randomly asked who they would report a security incident to. It is checked whether the reporting channels are clear and known.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security awareness training is conducted at least annually and is enriched with current, practical examples. In addition, regular phishing simulation campaigns are carried out to practically test and improve user awareness. The results of the campaigns are anonymized and evaluated to optimize training content.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specialized tool is used to conduct phishing simulations. Employees who fall for the simulated phishing email immediately receive an explanatory page with learning content. The anonymized click rate is reported to management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the reports of the last phishing campaigns shown to them. It is checked whether the results were analyzed and used to adapt the awareness measures. The training materials are checked to see if they refer to the results of the simulations (e.g., by discussing the tricks used).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A continuous awareness program is established that uses various channels and formats (e.g., newsletters, posters, short videos, gamification). The content is tailored to specific target groups (e.g., administration, management, development). The effectiveness of the program is measured and continuously improved using metrics (e.g., click rates in simulations, number of user reports of suspicious emails).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to phishing simulations, there are special training modules for developers on the topic of secure software development or for the finance department on the topic of CEO fraud. A 'Phish Alert Button' in the email client allows users to report suspicious emails to the security team with a single click. Employees who actively report threats are positively highlighted (e.g., through a 'Security Champion' initiative).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the annual plan for the awareness program and the target-group-specific content. Metrics and reports are viewed that demonstrate the effectiveness of the program (e.g., decreasing click rates, increasing reporting rates). The technical implementation of the Phish Alert Button is demonstrated.

controls.title: Reporting of Malware Infections (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Alarms from the antivirus program are only displayed on the user's local system. It is the user's responsibility to notice them and report them to IT. There is no central logging or alerting.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The agents on the clients are not configured to send events to a central server. IT only finds out about infections when a user calls.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the antivirus agent and the management console and finds that no central alerting is configured. Interviews with IT support confirm that reports are only made sporadically by users.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Alarms from the antivirus program are forwarded to a central console or by email to an IT administrator. There is an informal, undocumented process for handling these alarms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The management console is configured to send an email to the 'it-support@example.com' mailbox in the event of a detection. The administrator on duty occasionally checks this mailbox and takes care of the alarms.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the email notification. However, no documented procedure or response plan can be presented. The follow-up of processed alarms is not guaranteed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The deployed antivirus program SHOULD automatically block and report a malware infection. The automatic report SHOULD be received at a central point. The responsible employees SHOULD then decide on the further course of action depending on the situation. The procedure for reports and alarms from the antivirus programs SHOULD be planned, documented, and tested. It SHOULD be regulated in particular what should happen in the event of a confirmed infection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Alarms from the antivirus solution are sent to a central management console. A response plan (Incident Response Plan) for malware incidents is documented. This plan describes the steps from the initial analysis of the alarm to containment (e.g., disconnecting the client from the network) to cleanup and recovery. The responsible employees are named and trained.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the response plan for malware incidents. It is checked whether the plan contains clear instructions and responsibilities. Evidence of the plan's testing (e.g., protocol of a tabletop test) and employee training is requested. The configuration of the central alerting is checked in the management console.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Central alerting is integrated into a ticketing system to ensure that all alarms are tracked and processed. The documented response plan includes different procedures for different types of malicious programs (e.g., adware, spyware, ransomware). The plan is tested at least annually through tabletop exercises.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The antivirus management console sends alerts via an API or email to the IT ticketing system, which automatically creates a ticket with a specific priority. The response plan contains specific playbooks, e.g., 'Playbook-Ransomware', which mandates immediate system isolation and backup verification.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the integration into the ticketing system demonstrated by triggering a test alert. The response plan is checked for the existence of specific playbooks. The logs of the last incident response exercise are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The antivirus program's alerting is fully integrated into a Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) platform. Based on the type and criticality of the alarm, initial response steps, such as isolating the affected system from the network or blocking C2 communication on the firewall, are executed automatically. After every major incident, a 'post-mortem' analysis is conducted to improve prevention and response measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A SOAR playbook is triggered by a ransomware alarm. The playbook isolates the host via a NAC or EDR interface, searches the SIEM for IOCs of the attack on other systems, blocks the identified C2 IP address on the firewall, and creates a high-priority ticket for the SOC team with all collected information.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the corresponding SOAR playbook and its execution logs shown. The integrations with EDR, SIEM, and firewall are verified. Reports from 'post-mortem' analyses of past incidents are requested to demonstrate the continuous improvement process.

controls.title: Use of special analysis environments (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A documented process is established for forwarding suspicious files or email attachments to a dedicated team or a responsible person for manual analysis. The analysis is performed in a defined, isolated environment, for example, on a laptop disconnected from the network with analysis tools.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users are instructed not to open suspicious files but to forward them to a special email address (e.g., 'security@example.com'). The responsible IT staff has a dedicated computer, not connected to the production network, to securely investigate these files.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the process documentation for the analysis of suspicious files. The existence and configuration of the isolated analysis environment are verified. Based on ticket or email histories, it is tracked how such reports were handled in the past.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automated analyses in a special test environment (based on sandboxes or separate virtual or physical systems) SHOULD be additionally used for an assessment of suspicious files. Suspicious email attachments or web downloads are automatically submitted to this sandbox for analysis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A commercial or open-source sandbox solution (e.g., Cuckoo Sandbox) is in use, integrated into the email gateway or web proxy. Files classified as potentially dangerous by these systems are automatically executed in the sandbox and analyzed for malicious behavior. The results (e.g., 'malicious' or 'clean') are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the sandbox solution and its integration into the email gateway or proxy demonstrated. Examples are used to demonstrate how a suspicious file is analyzed and what the analysis report looks like. Logs of the latest analyses are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The automated sandbox analysis is fully integrated into the security infrastructure. Indicators of Compromise (IOCs) obtained from the analysis, such as file hashes, C2 domains, or IP addresses, are automatically distributed to other security systems to search for the threat network-wide (Threat Hunting) and proactively block it.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script or a SOAR platform extracts IOCs from the sandbox reports. The file hashes are searched for in the EDR solution to find other infected hosts. The C2 domains and IPs are automatically added to a blocklist on the web proxy and firewall. The IOCs are also fed into the SIEM system to retrospectively search for traces of compromise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the entire automated workflow demonstrated, from the sandbox analysis to the updating of blocklists on the firewall and the search in the SIEM. A concrete example is used to trace how an IOC found in the sandbox led to the identification of another affected system.

controls.title: Use of multiple scan engines (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT security policy stipulates that for systems requiring special protection, especially email and web gateways, solutions with multiple scan engines should be preferred during product selection. This requirement is a documented criterion in the selection process for such products.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the next tender for a new email gateway, 'support for at least two different AV scan engines' is included as a mandatory criterion in the requirements catalog.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the current security policy for a corresponding provision. In the case of a recent procurement of a gateway, the requirements catalog is reviewed to verify that this requirement was taken into account.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To improve detection performance, antivirus programs with multiple alternative scan engines SHOULD be used for IT systems requiring special protection, such as gateways and IT systems for data exchange. These engines should ideally come from different manufacturers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The email gateway and web proxy in use actively utilize a multi-engine scan function. The configuration ensures that engines from two or more different, reputable manufacturers are used in parallel or sequentially to scan content.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the email gateway and the web proxy shown. It is verified that the multi-engine functionality is activated and which specific engines are licensed and in operation. The logs are checked for entries from both scan engines.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A 'defense-in-depth' approach is pursued, where files are scanned at various points in the processing chain by different security products. For example, an email is scanned at the gateway by a multi-engine solution, on the mail server by a server-specific scanner, and on the client by the local endpoint protection solution after opening the attachment. The effectiveness of this layered scanning is regularly evaluated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The security architecture intentionally provides for the use of AV products from different manufacturers at different control points (perimeter, server, client). The selection of products is coordinated so that the technologies complement each other (e.g., a more signature-based product at the gateway and a strongly behavior-based one on the client).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the system architecture documentation for the planned, layered arrangement of different scan technologies. The actual implementation of this concept is verified based on the configurations of the respective systems (gateway, server, client). Penetration test reports are examined to see if they evaluate the effectiveness of this layered defense.

controls.title: Use of media scanning stations (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A policy and an associated process are defined that prescribe how to handle external storage media from third parties (e.g., USB sticks from service providers). The process stipulates that an authorized IT employee must scan the storage medium for malware at a dedicated, isolated workstation before the data can be copied to the internal network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The security policy contains a section on handling external storage media. A special laptop, not connected to the production network and equipped with up-to-date AV software, is available in the IT department for this purpose. Employees are instructed to contact IT support with external storage media.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the corresponding policy. The existence and state (isolated, AV up-to-date) of the scanning workstation are verified. Based on support tickets, it is randomly checked whether the process is being followed in practice.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before storage media from third parties, in particular, are connected to the institution's IT systems, they SHOULD be scanned by a media scanning station. A dedicated, hardened kiosk system is available for this purpose, and its use is mandatory for reading external media.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A terminal (kiosk system) is set up in the entrance area or in the IT department. This system is physically and logically separated from the production network. Users can connect a USB stick there. The system scans the content with several up-to-date virus scanners. Only if no threat is found can the data be copied to a clean USB stick provided by the company or to a special shared area on the network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the function of the media scanning station demonstrated. The system's configuration is checked for hardening, isolation, and up-to-dateness of the AV software. The policy mandating the use of the station is reviewed. Ideally, the USB ports on normal workstations are disabled, which is also checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The data transfer process via the media scanning station is fully automated and is comprehensively monitored. The kiosk system not only performs a virus scan but also a file type check and content filtering (Data Leakage Prevention, DLP). Only explicitly allowed file types can be transferred. All copy operations are logged centrally and in an audit-proof manner.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The media scanning station is configured with a whitelist for file types (e.g., only PDF, DOCX, XLSX allowed, no EXE or scripts). Additionally, a DLP function checks if sensitive data patterns are present in the files. Every transaction (who, when, which files) is sent to a central SIEM system for analysis and archiving.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor tests the station with a USB stick containing disallowed file types (e.g., an .exe file) and verifies that the transfer is blocked. The configuration of the file type filters and DLP rules is checked. The logs of the performed transfers are reviewed in the SIEM system.

controls.title: Handling of untrusted files (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A policy and a documented process exist, stipulating that users who need to open an untrusted file may only do so on a designated, isolated IT system. The process for requesting access to this system is also documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For users with a corresponding need (e.g., in the HR department opening applications), access is granted to a special virtual machine that is separated from the production network. Access is requested via the IT service portal.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence and content of the corresponding policy. The process for requesting access is verified in the service portal. The technical isolation of the provided analysis VM is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If it is necessary to open untrusted files, this SHOULD only be done on an isolated IT system. The affected files SHOULD be converted to a harmless format or printed out there, for example, if this reduces the risk of malware infection. Users are trained in the use of this system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An isolated system (physical or virtual) is available. Tools are installed on this system to, for example, convert a Word document with macros into a pure PDF file without active content (Content Disarm and Reconstruction, CDR). The cleaned file can then be safely transferred to the production network. The process is known to the relevant users.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the function of the isolated system and the conversion tools demonstrated. It is checked whether the target user groups are informed and trained about this process. It is checked whether the network isolation of the system is effective.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A browser isolation technology (Remote Browser Isolation, RBI) is in use. When users click on links to unknown or uncategorized websites, the website is rendered not on the local client, but in a remote, temporary container. Only the secure visual representation is streamed to the client, keeping any malicious code away from the endpoint. File downloads from these sessions are automatically analyzed in a sandbox or sanitized by a CDR solution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An RBI solution is integrated into the organization's web proxy as a cloud service or on-premise solution. Policies define which website categories (e.g., 'Uncategorized', 'Social Networks', 'Personal Email') are accessed via the isolation technology. The integration with the sandbox/CDR solution for downloads is configured and active.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the function of the browser isolation demonstrated by accessing an untrusted website. The configuration policies that determine which accesses are isolated are checked. The process for the secure download of a file from an isolated session is tested and verified.

controls.title: Selection and use of cyber security products against targeted attacks (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As part of strategic security planning, a process is defined to periodically monitor and evaluate the market for advanced security products (e.g., EDR, NDR, Application Control). Before a purchase decision is made, conducting a documented 'Proof of Concept' (PoC) is mandatory.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the annual budget planning, it is checked whether the existing protective measures against targeted attacks are still sufficient or whether new technologies should be evaluated. For each evaluation, a PoC plan is created that defines the test cases and success criteria.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the last strategic security planning meeting and checks whether the evaluation of new technologies was a topic. For a recently procured or evaluated solution, the corresponding PoC plan and the final report are requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use and added value of products and services that offer an extended scope of protection compared to conventional antivirus programs SHOULD be examined. Such security products against targeted attacks SHOULD be used, for example, for executing files in special analysis environments, for hardening clients, or for encapsulating processes. Before a purchase decision for a security product is made, its protective effect and compatibility with the own IT environment SHOULD be tested.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The organization actively uses advanced security solutions such as Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) or Application Whitelisting. The selection was based on a thorough 'Proof of Concept' (PoC) that evaluated not only the detection rate but also compatibility with business applications and administrative overhead.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the EDR or application whitelisting solution in use. The PoC documentation is reviewed to check the test criteria and results. It is checked whether the solution is rolled out comprehensively on the relevant systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An integrated suite of advanced security products (e.g., XDR) is in use, correlating telemetry data from endpoints, networks, email systems, and cloud services. The solution is used by a dedicated Security Operations Team (SOC) not only for reactive alert processing but also for proactive threat hunting. The effectiveness of the entire solution chain is continuously validated by Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS) tools.

parts.name: guidance
