parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the workflow system and the release processes mapped within it. It is verified that the defined release criteria are met and that all required parties have given their approval, as evidenced by the system logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The release process is part of an automated governance process (Policy-as-Code). Compliance with the release criteria (e.g., successful security scans, passed tests, no critical defects) is checked automatically. The software is only automatically released for deployment to production if all criteria are met. Manual releases are only possible in documented exceptional cases.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like Open Policy Agent (OPA) are integrated into the CI/CD pipeline to automatically check release policies. The results of all necessary scans and tests are collected centrally and evaluated by the policy engine.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the release policies defined as code (e.g., in OPA's Rego language) for correctness and completeness. The configuration of the CI/CD pipeline is audited to ensure that deployment is blocked in case of a policy violation.

controls.title: Conducting software tests for non-functional requirements

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Non-functional aspects such as security or performance are not systematically tested. Problems are only noticed in production through user complaints or failures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are no dedicated tests for non-functional requirements. Development focuses exclusively on implementing the required functions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: By reviewing test plans and protocols, the auditor determines that no tests for non-functional requirements (e.g., load tests, security tests) are being performed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Basic non-functional tests are performed manually as needed. This includes, for example, simple security scans with standard tools or manual usability checks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a release, a developer is tasked with running an automated vulnerability scanner with default settings over the application. The results are evaluated informally.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor looks for evidence of occasionally performed non-functional tests, e.g., reports from simple scanners or notes in project documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software tests MUST be performed to verify that all essential non-functional requirements are met. In particular, security-specific software tests MUST be performed if the application has security-critical functions. The test cases performed, as well as the test results, MUST be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Non-functional requirements (e.g., performance, security, reliability) are specified in the requirements catalog. Corresponding tests (e.g., load and performance tests, security tests) are an integral part of the test plan. The results are formally documented and evaluated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether test plans explicitly include tests for non-functional requirements. It is verified on the basis of test protocols that these tests have been carried out and their results documented, especially for applications with security-critical functions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Tests for non-functional requirements are largely automated and performed regularly. This includes automated load tests, resilience tests (e.g., using chaos engineering), and the integration of security scanners (SAST/DAST) into the development process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like JMeter or Gatling are used for automated load tests. SAST tools are integrated into the developers' IDE, and DAST scanners run regularly against the test environments. The results are collected and evaluated centrally.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the automated testing tools for non-functional requirements. It is verified that these tests are executed regularly and that their results are incorporated into risk assessment and bug fixing. The integration into the development process is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Tests for non-functional requirements are fully integrated into the CI/CD pipeline and are executed with every code change. Defined thresholds (e.g., for response times or resource consumption) are automatically monitored, and the build is blocked if they are exceeded. Regular penetration tests by external experts supplement the automated security tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The CI/CD pipeline is configured to include performance and security tests as 'Quality Gates'. Tools for monitoring these metrics are permanently integrated. Contracts with specialized security firms for regular penetration tests are established.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the CI/CD pipeline configuration to verify the implementation of Quality Gates for non-functional requirements. The reports of the external penetration tests and the follow-up of the findings contained therein are inspected.

controls.title: Use of anonymized or pseudonymized test data

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Unprotected copies of production data are used for software tests. There is no awareness or measures for the protection of sensitive or personal information in test environments.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A database backup of the production environment is directly imported into the test environment. Testers have full access to all real data.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the data sources of the test environments. Data samples in the test database show that unprotected production data is being used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an awareness of the protection of test data. Particularly sensitive data is manually altered on a simple basis (e.g., find & replace) before being used in tests. However, the process is not standardized.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator runs manual SQL scripts to change some personal data in the test database before it is released for testing. This process is not consistent for all data types.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews the administrators about the test data preparation process and reviews the scripts used. Random checks in the test database show that a basic but possibly incomplete alteration has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If production data containing information worthy of protection is used for software tests, this test data MUST be adequately protected. If this data contains personal information, it MUST at least be pseudonymized. If a personal reference could be derived from the test data, the data protection officer and, under certain circumstances, the staff council MUST be consulted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A defined process for creating test data has been established. This process provides for the pseudonymization of all personal data. A regular process for involving the data protection officer is documented and applied as needed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documented process for test data anonymization/pseudonymization. It is verified that this process is consistently applied by randomly checking test databases for the presence of personal data in plain text. The records of consultation with the data protection officer are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If possible, test data with personal reference SHOULD be completely anonymized instead of just being pseudonymized. The data masking process is automated to ensure consistency and repeatability and to avoid manual errors.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Specialized tools for data masking or ETL processes are used to automatically anonymize production data. The process ensures that referential integrity is maintained, but the data can no longer be traced back to individuals.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the automated data masking tool and the applied rules. It is verified that the process achieves complete anonymization where technically possible and that the process runs reliably.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of production data for testing is generally avoided. Instead, realistic but synthetic test data is generated. This process is fully automated and ensures that the test data reflects the statistical properties and complexity of the production data without ever containing sensitive information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Dedicated tools are used to generate synthetic data. These tools analyze the structure of the production database and, based on this analysis, create new, artificial data sets that are used for testing. The process is integrated into the provisioning of test environments.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process and tools for generating synthetic data. It is verified that only synthetic data is actually used in the test environments and that there is no connection to production data sources. It is checked whether the generated data has the quality required for meaningful tests.

controls.title: Orderly briefing of software testers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software testers SHOULD be informed by subject matter experts about the types of tests to be performed and the areas of a software to be tested. Furthermore, software testers SHOULD be informed about the use cases and possible further requirements of the software.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before the start of the test phase, a formal kick-off meeting takes place. In this meeting, the subject matter experts and developers introduce the software, the new functions, the use cases, and the test objectives to the testers. The test plans and requirements documents are made available to the testers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether briefing sessions are held for test phases. This can be verified by inspecting meeting minutes or by interviewing the testers. It is checked whether the testers have access to all relevant planning and requirements documents.

controls.title: Personnel selection of software testers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When selecting software testers, special selection criteria SHOULD be taken into account. Software testers SHOULD have the required professional qualifications. If custom software is reviewed at the source code level, then the testers SHOULD have sufficient expertise in the programming language to be tested and the development environment. The source code SHOULD NOT be reviewed exclusively by testers who were also involved in creating the source code.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Requirement profiles are defined for the role of the software tester, which describe the necessary professional and technical qualifications. When assigning testing tasks, attention is paid to the suitability of the individuals. The four-eyes principle is applied, especially for source code reviews, i.e., the reviewer is not the author of the code.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the requirement profiles for software testers. It is checked on a random basis whether the testers used meet the defined qualifications. For code reviews that have been carried out, it is verified that the four-eyes principle has been observed by inspecting the corresponding logs.

controls.title: Creation of an acceptance plan

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An acceptance plan SHOULD document the types of tests to be performed, test cases, and the expected results. In addition, the acceptance plan SHOULD include the release criteria. A procedure SHOULD be defined for the situation when a release is rejected.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before the start of acceptance testing, a formal acceptance plan is created, which is approved by the subject matter experts and IT operations. This plan lists all acceptance criteria (e.g., 'all Prio-1 test cases passed', 'no known critical errors'), the acceptance tests to be performed, and the process in case of non-acceptance (e.g., rework loop).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether approved acceptance plans exist for software releases. It is verified that these plans define clear acceptance criteria and a process for handling rejection. Compliance with these plans is checked using the acceptance records.

controls.title: Performing regression tests

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When software has been changed, regression tests SHOULD be performed. It SHOULD be checked whether existing security mechanisms and settings have been unintentionally changed by the update. Regression tests SHOULD be performed completely and also include extensions and tools. If test cases are omitted, this SHOULD be justified and documented. The performed test cases and the test results SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After every software change (patch, update, configuration change), a defined set of regression tests is performed. This test set is designed to cover the core functionality and important security functions of the application. The execution and results of the regression tests are logged. Any omission of test cases is justified in the log.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether regression tests have demonstrably been carried out after software changes. This is verified using change management records and the associated test logs. It is checked whether the logs are complete and whether omissions of tests are comprehensibly justified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The majority of regression tests are performed automatically. The test suite is continuously maintained and expanded to cover new functions. The selection of the regression tests to be performed is made on a risk-based basis based on the changes made.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated, automated regression test suite is maintained in a test automation framework. Before the test is run, an analysis of the code changes is performed to identify the most relevant test cases and optimize the test duration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existence, scope, and degree of automation of the regression test suite. The process for maintaining the suite and for the risk-based selection of test cases is audited. The results of the automated test runs are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The execution of automated regression tests is fully integrated into the CI/CD pipeline and is triggered with every commit. A failure of a regression test automatically leads to a build failure and prevents further delivery. Visual regression tests are used to detect unintentional changes to the user interface.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The CI/CD pipeline is configured so that the regression test suite is a critical 'Quality Gate'. Tools for visual regression testing (e.g. Applitools, Percy) are integrated and automatically compare screenshots of the UI with an approved baseline.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the CI/CD pipeline to verify that regression tests are run as a blocking quality gate on every commit. The configuration and results of the visual regression testing tools are also reviewed.

controls.title: Separation of the test environment from the production environment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software SHOULD only be tested in a designated test environment. The test environment SHOULD be operated separately from the production environment. The architectures and mechanisms used in the test environment SHOULD be documented. Procedures SHOULD be documented on how to handle the test environment after completion of the software test.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are dedicated environments for development, testing, and production. The environments are separated from each other at the network level (e.g., by firewalls or VLANs). The architecture of the test environment is documented. There is a defined process for resetting or decommissioning the test environment after a project.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the network plans and firewall rules to verify the separation of the environments. The documentation of the test environment architecture and the processes for its lifecycle management are inspected for completeness and implementation.

controls.title: Review of the installation and associated documentation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation of the software SHOULD be checked in accordance with the regulations for software installation and configuration. If available, the installation and configuration documentation SHOULD also be checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the test phase, the installation of the software in the test environment is carried out and validated according to the supplied installation instructions. The instructions are checked for correctness and completeness. The result of this review is recorded in the test report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the test reports contain a section on the validation of the installation procedure and the associated documentation. It is verified that any defects found in the documentation have been reported back to the manufacturer or the development team.

controls.title: Performing penetration tests

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For applications with high protection requirements, penetration tests are carried out by qualified testers as needed. The execution is based on a basic, but not necessarily formalized, concept. The security vulnerabilities found are documented and handed over to the development department for remediation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a new, critical application goes live, an external service provider is commissioned to perform a penetration test. The scope is defined in the contract. The results are summarized in a report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether penetration test reports are available for critical applications. It is verified that the vulnerabilities found therein are tracked and remediated, e.g., by inspecting the ticket system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For applications with increased protection requirements, penetration tests SHOULD be carried out as a test method. A concept for penetration tests SHOULD be created, which documents the methods as well as the success criteria. The test SHOULD be carried out according to this concept and the gaps found SHOULD be classified and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a company-wide, documented concept for penetration tests that defines procedures (e.g., according to BSI or OWASP) and scopes. Penetration tests are carried out regularly (e.g., annually and after major changes). Gaps found are classified according to a severity scheme (e.g., CVSS) and tracked in a central system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the penetration test concept for appropriateness and completeness. It is verified that tests are carried out regularly in accordance with the concept. The classification and the process for remediating vulnerabilities are checked using reports and ticket system entries.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Penetration tests are part of a comprehensive and continuous security program. This program includes regular external and internal tests, a bug bounty program to involve the external security community, and regular red team exercises to test the organization's detection and response capabilities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A public or private bug bounty program is established. An internal team or a specialized service provider regularly conducts red team attacks. The results from all test activities continuously flow into the improvement of security measures and development practices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policies and platform of the bug bounty program. The reports of the red team exercises and the improvement measures derived from them are inspected. A holistic process for continuous security validation and improvement is demonstrated.

controls.title: Security screening of testers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If testers need to access particularly sensitive information, their reliability is thoroughly checked as part of the hiring process. External testers must sign a confidentiality agreement.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Standard background checks are part of the hiring process. For external service providers, signing a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) is mandatory before they are granted access to sensitive data or systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the HR processes regarding background checks. It is verified that signed NDAs are on file for all external testers with access to sensitive data.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If testers need to access particularly sensitive information, the institution SHOULD obtain proof of their integrity and reputation. If this involves classified information, the software testers SHOULD undergo a security clearance check in accordance with the Security Clearance Act (SÜG). For this purpose, the ISB SHOULD involve the institution's security officer or security representative.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For access to highly sensitive data, internal and external testers are required to provide a police clearance certificate. For projects involving classified information, a security clearance check according to SÜG is initiated for all involved testers in cooperation with the security officer, and access is not granted until it has been successfully completed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the personnel files or project documents for proof of the integrity checks obtained (e.g., police clearance certificates). For classified projects, the documentation of the security clearance checks performed and the involvement of the security officer are verified.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
The use of IT in institutions requires that machine data processing functions as error-free as possible, as individual results can usually no longer be checked. Therefore, software of any kind must be tested before commissioning as part of software tests. These tests must demonstrate that the software reliably provides the required functions and, moreover, has no undesirable side effects. The subsequent release of the software by the technically responsible organizational unit grants the basic permission to use the software productively in the institution. At the same time, this organizational unit also assumes responsibility for the IT process supported by the software.
Software can be tested at different points in its life cycle. Software tests may be necessary during development, before release for productive operation, or as part of patch and change management. This applies to both custom software and standardized software. Regression tests play a special role here, because even if only minor aspects of the software are changed, there is a possibility that this will affect completely different aspects and functions of the software. Regression tests check software specifically for these effects.
This module describes the test and release process for any type of software. The test and release process is characterized by the fact that it can be run through several times depending on the result.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: By implementing this module, the institution ensures that the software used meets the technical and organizational requirements as well as the existing protection needs of the entire institution or individual organizational units. A key aspect of this is that security-critical software is systematically and methodically checked for existing vulnerabilities.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module OPS.1.1.6 Software Tests and Releases is to be applied once to the information network.
While the module CON.8 Software Development deals with the software development process and the software tests contained therein that are necessary during the development process, this module describes the special requirements placed on test and release management. This test and release management does not refer exclusively to software developed by the customer or on their behalf, but also to the testing and release of any software as described in APP.6 General Software, as well as all other software products of the APP Applications layer.
Software tests can also become part of patch or change management or software development. Corresponding requirements are specified in more detail in the module OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management and CON.8 Software Development.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Software tests with production data
parts.prose:
If software tests are carried out with production data, security problems can arise. In particular, confidential production data could be viewed by unauthorized employees or third parties who have been commissioned with the respective software test. If the 'original' production data is tested with and not copies of the data, it could be unintentionally changed or deleted.
Software tests in production operation could massively disrupt the entire operation. This is because malfunctions of the software to be tested can also affect other applications and IT systems, which are then also disrupted. In addition, software testers deliberately test the software at its limits and thus intend to uncover possible errors. This in turn increases the risk that the entire operation will be disrupted.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Missing or insufficient testing procedure
parts.prose:
If new software is not tested or is tested inadequately and is released without installation instructions, errors in the software may go undetected. It is also possible that necessary installation parameters to be observed are not recognized or not followed.
These software or installation errors, resulting from a missing or insufficient software testing procedure, can significantly endanger the IT operations of the institution. For example, important data can be lost when a software update is installed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Missing or insufficient release procedure
parts.prose: A missing or insufficient release procedure can lead to the use of software that has not been approved by the business side. In this way, the software may include functions that it should not contain, that do not work as desired, or required functions may be missing. In addition, the software may be incompatible with other applications.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Missing or insufficient documentation of the tests and test results
parts.prose: Software can usually be released as soon as all tests have been carried out and no deviations have been found. However, if the documentation of the software tests is incomplete, it is not possible to determine retrospectively what was tested. If detected software errors or missing functions were insufficiently documented and thus not taken into account during the release, these deviations can lead to the production data to be processed being unintentionally deleted or changed. In addition, other IT systems and applications can be disrupted.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Missing or insufficient documentation of the release criteria
parts.prose: If release criteria are not clearly communicated, this can lead to software being released prematurely or not being released at all, even though it could be. On the one hand, this could result in versions with undetected software errors being released, which can disrupt production operations. On the other hand, a lack of or insufficient documentation of the release criteria can lead to project delays and thus to financial damage.

controls.title: Requirement Specification for System Management (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Requirements for system management are only sporadically or roughly outlined for individual, non-critical systems. Neither security aspects nor interface definitions for compatibility are systematically considered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements are often communicated only verbally or recorded in informal notes. There is no formal process for capturing or coordinating them.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether any written requirement documents exist at all. Interviews with administrators determine whether there is a common understanding of the requirements, which is typically not the case.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The basic functional requirements for the system management infrastructure and processes are documented. Security aspects and interfaces are mentioned, but not specified in detail.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A basic document, for example in a word processor, lists the required functions. Security requirements are limited to general statements like 'must be secure'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing requirements document for completeness regarding the basic functionality. It is checked whether at least a superficial description of interfaces and security aspects is present.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Requirements for the system management infrastructure and processes MUST be specified. All essential elements for system management MUST be taken into account. The security aspects for system management MUST also be considered from the very beginning. In addition, the interfaces of the IT systems to be managed MUST be documented, e.g., to ensure the compatibility of the system management solution and the system to be managed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal requirements document is created that covers all points mentioned in the measure. This document serves as the basis for planning and procurement. The interfaces are documented, for example, by specifying protocols, ports, and data formats.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence and completeness of the requirement specification. It is verified that all essential elements, security aspects, and interface definitions are documented and serve as a basis for further planning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirement specification is formally versioned and subjected to a documented review process involving both technical and business departments. The compatibility requirements are supported by specific test cases.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements are managed in a wiki or a simple requirements management tool. Changes are tracked via a defined process. Test cases for compatibility are defined before implementation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks for the existence of versioning, review logs, and defined test cases for the interfaces. It is verified that relevant stakeholders were involved in the review process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirement specification is stored in a dedicated requirements management tool and is continuously maintained as a 'living document'. Requirements are directly linked to architecture models, risk assessments, and automated test plans. Changes are controlled via a formal change management process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like Jira with corresponding plugins or dedicated ALM (Application Lifecycle Management) platforms are used. The traceability from requirement to test case and to deployment is ensured by the tooling.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the end-to-end traceability in the tool used. It is checked on a random basis whether a requirement is correctly linked to the associated architecture components, risks, and test cases. The effectiveness of the change management process is reviewed.

controls.title: Planning of System Management (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Planning for system management is informal and ad-hoc, mostly in response to acute problems. There is no documented plan that covers essential aspects such as security, permissions, or logging.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Decisions to introduce system management tools are often made by individual administrators without strategic consideration. There is no project planning or budgeting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews that no planning documents exist. The selection and configuration of tools appear arbitrary and uncoordinated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic plan that describes the selection and introduction of system management tools. This plan focuses mainly on technical and functional aspects, while organizational and security-related topics are only superficially addressed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple project document outlines the rough steps for introducing a piece of software. The planning covers the basic points of the requirements analysis and a high-level concept, but neglects details such as the authorization concept or logging.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing plan and finds that important planning content (e.g., detailed authorization concept, network connections, logging requirements) is missing or inadequately described.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system management solution and the underlying infrastructure MUST be planned appropriately. The planning MUST include a detailed requirements analysis, a meaningful high-level concept, a comprehensive implementation plan, as well as milestones for quality assurance and acceptance. All topics mentioned in the module (e.g., separation, access permissions, protocols, network connections) MUST be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal planning document is created that presents all required content in a structured manner. This serves as a binding basis for the project team to implement the system management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the planning documentation for completeness based on the list of topics to be considered in the module. It is verified that the planning has been formally approved.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The plan for system management is integrated into the overall IT strategy and project portfolio management. It includes detailed resource planning, a risk analysis regarding the implementation project, and a communication plan for all stakeholders. The planning is regularly reviewed and adjusted as needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Planning is carried out using standard project management software. Milestones, resources, and risks are actively tracked. Regular status meetings ensure that all stakeholders are informed and that deviations are addressed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews project management artifacts such as the project plan, the risk register, and minutes of status meetings. It is verified that the project is actively managed and controlled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning of system management is based on an established architecture framework (e.g., TOGAF). It is dynamically adapted to changing business requirements and technological developments. Cost-benefit analyses for planned changes and extensions are regularly performed and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Architecture models and planning documents are managed in a central enterprise architecture tool. The impact of changes is analyzed with system support before they are approved. Planning is closely intertwined with financial controlling and strategic corporate planning.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the connection of the system management planning to the enterprise architecture and the strategic processes. The existence and application of formal processes for the analysis and approval of planning changes, as well as the execution of cost-benefit analyses, are verified.

controls.title: Time Synchronization for System Management (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system time is set manually or not at all on most systems. There is no central time synchronization, which leads to significant time discrepancies between systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators set the time when a system is first set up, after which it is no longer maintained. This means that log entries cannot be correlated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the system times of several randomly selected systems and finds significant discrepancies. The configuration of a time service is checked and found to be missing or inactive.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A time synchronization protocol such as NTP is enabled on most systems, but often an internal, not necessarily trustworthy time source (e.g., a domain controller) is used without a connection to an external reference time. The synchronization status is not monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The operating system's default NTP client functionality is used and pointed to an internal server. It is not ensured that this server itself has a correct time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the NTP configuration on the clients and the server serving as the source. It is determined that the server has no connection to a reliable external time source. There is no monitoring of the time services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All components of the system management solution, including the systems to be managed, MUST use a synchronous time. The system time MUST be synchronized for each system to be managed and for the system management solution with one or more trusted time sources using appropriate protocols.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Dedicated internal NTP servers are operated, which obtain their time from reliable external sources (e.g., from the PTB). All systems on the network are instructed via configuration management to use these internal servers as a time source.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the internal NTP servers and verifies that they use trusted external sources. Spot checks on clients show that they are correctly configured to the internal servers and the time is synchronous.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A hierarchical and redundant time infrastructure with multiple (at least two) independent, trusted time sources is established. The synchronization status of all clients is centrally monitored, and deviations above a defined threshold automatically trigger an alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least two Stratum 1 time servers are operated, which obtain their time from different sources (e.g., GPS and DCF77). The monitoring solution actively checks the status of the NTP service on all systems and the time deviation (offset). Alarms are sent to the central ticketing system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the design of the time infrastructure for redundancy. The configuration of the monitoring is checked and it is verified that test alarms are processed correctly. Monitoring log files are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The time synchronization protocol itself is secured by cryptographic mechanisms (e.g., Network Time Security, NTS, or NTP with symmetric keys) to prevent manipulation of time packets. The time infrastructure is highly available and hardened against attacks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: NTS (RFC 8915) is activated between the NTP servers and the clients. The keys for authentication are securely managed and rotated. The time servers are specially protected by firewalls and intrusion detection systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the cryptographic protection of the NTP service. It is verified that non-authenticated time packets are discarded. The security concepts for the time servers themselves are checked for adequacy.

controls.title: Securing system management communication (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The communication between the system management solution and the managed systems is entirely unencrypted and occurs over the regular production network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Protocols such as Telnet, SNMPv1/v2c, or unencrypted HTTP are used for management. There is no network-level segregation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts a network analysis and can capture the management communication, including potential passwords, in cleartext.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secure protocols are partially used, but the configuration is inconsistent or uses outdated, weak encryption algorithms. Segregation of the management network is not consistently implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Although SSHv2 and HTTPS are used, they employ outdated cipher suites or self-signed certificates without a proper PKI. A management VLAN exists, but many systems are accessible in multiple VLANs for convenience.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the protocols used and identifies weak algorithms. The network architecture is analyzed and gaps in network segregation are uncovered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As soon as the system management solution and the systems to be managed communicate over the production infrastructure, secure protocols MUST be used. If secure protocols cannot be used, then a dedicated administration network (out-of-band management) MUST be used. If this is also not possible, then supplementary security mechanisms MUST be employed at another level, e.g., tunneling mechanisms via encrypted VPN.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: By default, protocols such as SSHv2, TLS 1.2/1.3, or IPsec are used to secure communication. For devices that only support insecure protocols (e.g., SNMPv2c), access is enforced via a dedicated, highly restricted management VLAN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the communication protocols on all involved systems. It is verified that one of the mentioned compensating measures (OOB network, VPN) is implemented for insecure protocols.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of secure protocols with strong cryptographic algorithms is enforced company-wide on a policy basis and is automatically monitored. A dedicated out-of-band management network is the standard for all critical systems and infrastructure components.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration management tools enforce the correct crypto configuration on all systems. A compliance scanner regularly checks for deviations. The OOB network is implemented via separate switches and protected by strict firewall rules.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and the reports from the automated compliance checks. The effectiveness of the OOB network's segregation is verified through penetration tests.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All management communication is routed through a dedicated, physically separate network that is cryptographically secured at Layer 2 (e.g., with MACsec). All communication is mutually authenticated with strong, hardware-based identities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A completely separate physical network infrastructure is operated for management. MACsec is activated on all participating switch ports and endpoints to prevent eavesdropping and unauthorized devices on the management network. Authentication is performed using certificates whose private keys are stored in TPMs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the physical setup of the management network. The configuration of MACsec and the PKI for device identities is checked. An attempt is made to connect an unauthorized device to the management network, which must fail.

controls.title: Mutual authentication of system management solution and managed systems (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no authentication between the system management solution and the managed systems. Each component implicitly trusts the other based on the network address.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: System management agents are configured to accept commands from any IP address that is configured as a management server, without further verification.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor demonstrates that by IP spoofing or by compromising any system in the management network, commands can be sent to managed systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: One-way authentication is performed. Typically, the management solution authenticates itself to the managed system, but not vice versa. Often, weak, shared secrets are used for this.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A password identical on all agents or an SNMP community string is used for the server to access the agents. The agent does not verify the identity of the server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration files for the use of weak, shared secrets. It is demonstrated that an attacker imitating the server (man-in-the-middle) can intercept information from the agent.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication between the system management solution and the managed systems MUST be mutual. The authentication MUST be integrated into the overall authentication concept. The authentication MUST be carried out using secure protocols.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Protocols such as SSH (with host and user keys) or TLS with mutual authentication (mTLS) are used. Individual key pairs or certificates are created for each component and securely distributed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the communication protocols and verifies that mutual authentication is configured and enforced. It is checked whether individual and not shared credentials are used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Mutual authentication is consistently based on certificates issued by an internal, trusted PKI. The lifecycle of these certificates (issuance, renewal, revocation) is actively managed and automated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PKI solution (e.g., Microsoft CA, EJBCA) is used for issuing device certificates. Processes for automatic certificate enrollment (e.g., via SCEP or ACME) and renewal are implemented. Revocation lists (CRLs) or OCSP are used to check validity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the PKI and the endpoints. It is verified that the certificate lifecycle management process works, e.g., by testing the revocation of a certificate, which must prevent access.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Mutual authentication is based on hardware-backed identities. The private keys of the components are stored in tamper-proof Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) or Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs). Every failed authentication attempt immediately triggers a security alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: TPMs in servers are used to store and use the private keys for mTLS communication (TPM attestation). The monitoring solution is configured to report authentication errors to the SIEM in real-time, where they trigger high-priority alarms.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the keys are not extractable by attempting to access the private key in the operating system. The alarm chain for failed authentication attempts is tested by provoking an error.

controls.title: Securing access to the system management solution (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to the system management solution is protected only by a simple, often shared password. There is no differentiated authorization concept; all users have full administrative rights.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single administrative account (e.g., 'admin') with a known password is used. Communication to the web interface is unencrypted over HTTP.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks for the existence of shared accounts and weak passwords. It is verified that the login credentials are transmitted unencrypted.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each administrator has their own account for accessing the system management solution. Authentication is done via password. Authorization is coarse-grained (e.g., 'Administrator' vs. 'Viewer'). The data transmission is encrypted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The solution's user management is used to create individual accounts. HTTPS is enabled for the web interface. The roles are limited to the manufacturer's predefined, coarse-grained levels.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether personalized accounts are used and whether password policies are adhered to. The TLS configuration of the web interface is checked for basic security. The role distribution is identified as coarse-grained.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: User access to the system management solution MUST be secured by secure and appropriate user authentication and authorization, as well as secure encryption of the transmitted data. The strength of the cryptographic methods and keys used MUST be reviewed regularly. The system management solution MUST ensure via an authorization component that users can only perform actions for which they are authorized.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An appropriate authentication method (e.g., integration into a central directory such as AD/LDAP) is selected and documented. Permissions are assigned based on the principle of least privilege using defined roles. The encryption methods used comply with current recommendations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation on the authentication method selection process. The role and permission configuration is checked for compliance with the least-privilege principle. The strength of the cryptography used is assessed using current guidelines (e.g., BSI TR-02102).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to the system management solution is secured for all administrative users by multi-factor authentication (MFA). Authorization is based on a detailed, fine-grained role-based access control (RBAC) concept that is reviewed regularly. All access and administration attempts are centrally logged and analyzed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The system management solution is connected to a central Identity Provider (IdP) that enforces MFA. The roles in the RBAC model are specifically defined for teams and areas of responsibility. The logs are sent to a SIEM for monitoring of suspicious activities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the MFA configuration and verifies that it is enforced for all administrative roles. The RBAC model is reviewed for its granularity and appropriateness. The log analysis in the SIEM is spot-checked for its effectiveness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any administrative access to the system management solution is exclusively via a dedicated Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. This enforces just-in-time access, which is granted only after approval. All sessions are fully recorded and monitored in real time for anomalous behavior.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution such as CyberArk or Thycotic is placed upstream. Administrators authenticate to the PAM solution, which then dynamically generates short-lived credentials for the system management solution (credential injection). Session recording and monitoring is fully enabled.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the PAM solution and the workflow for access approval. It is verified that no direct access bypassing the PAM solution is possible. Samples of session recordings are reviewed.

controls.title: Definition of a security policy for system management (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A security policy for system management SHOULD be created and maintained sustainably. The policy SHOULD be known to all persons involved in system management and be fundamental to their work. It SHOULD define at least all points mentioned in the module, such as areas, tasks, configuration management, network segregation, access control, and logging. The implementation of the policy SHOULD be reviewed regularly and the results documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal policy document is created, approved, and published on the intranet. The content is based on the list provided in the module. The announcement is made, for example, via email to the relevant employees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence, completeness, and approval status of the security policy. It is verified through interviews or training records that the policy is known to the responsible employees. Documented results of reviews are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is formally reviewed and approved by management annually or upon significant changes. Employees receive regular, verifiable training on the policy's content. Compliance with the policy is systematically checked as part of internal audits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A fixed review cycle is stored in the document management system. The training sessions are conducted via a learning platform, and success is tracked. The internal audit department plans regular audits to check policy compliance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the annual reviews and the management approval. Training materials and participant lists are inspected. The internal audit reports are checked for completeness and the processing of findings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is stored in a GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance) tool and linked to the specific technical controls. Compliance with the policy's requirements is continuously monitored through automated technical checks (Compliance-as-Code). Deviations automatically lead to alerts or tickets.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy requirements are translated into machine-readable rules (e.g., in OVAL or Rego format). A compliance scanner regularly executes these rules against the target systems. The results flow into a central dashboard that displays the compliance status in real time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the mapping of the policy in the GRC tool and the correctness of the automated check rules. The effectiveness of the automated monitoring is tested by deliberately and temporarily introducing a misconfiguration that must trigger an alarm.

controls.title: Creation of a system management concept (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the security policy, a system management concept SHOULD be created and continuously maintained. At least all aspects mentioned in the module, e.g., methods and tools, security, monitoring, logging, automation, and emergency planning, SHOULD be considered as needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed concept document is created that describes the architecture of the system management solution, the processes used, and the configuration of the individual components. It serves as a manual for the administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the concept for existence and completeness based on the list of aspects mentioned in the module. It is checked whether the concept is up-to-date and corresponds to the actual implementation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The concept contains detailed architecture diagrams (e.g., network plans, data flow diagrams) and process descriptions (e.g., in BPMN). It is versioned, subject to a formal review and approval process, and updated with every significant change to the environment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Professional tools such as Microsoft Visio or draw.io are used to create the diagrams. The concept is managed in a document management system with versioning and an approval workflow.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the quality and level of detail of the diagrams and process descriptions. The version history and approval logs in the document management system are inspected to verify the concept's timeliness and formal validity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The concept is part of a dynamic, model-based approach (Model-Based Systems Engineering, MBSE). The documentation, including diagrams and configuration details, is automatically generated from a central architecture model and thus always reflects the current state of the implementation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Enterprise architecture tools (e.g., based on ArchiMate) are used, which are integrated with configuration management and the CMDB. Changes are first planned and simulated in the model before they are implemented. The documentation is a byproduct of the lived process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the central architecture model and its integration with the operational systems. It is verified that a configuration change made in operation is reflected in the model and that the documentation generated from it is up-to-date.

controls.title: Detailed and implementation planning for system management (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A detailed and implementation plan for the system management solution SHOULD be created. All points addressed in the security policy and the system management concept SHOULD be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Based on the concept, a project plan is created that defines the specific work packages, responsibilities, and a timeline for the introduction or modification of the system management solution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether a detailed implementation plan exists and whether it fully covers the requirements from the policy and concept.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The detailed and implementation planning is managed as a detailed project plan with clearly defined work packages, resource allocations, dependencies, and a risk register. Progress is regularly tracked and documented in project meetings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Professional project management software (e.g., MS Project, Jira) is used for planning and tracking. There is a designated project manager and regular status reports to the clients.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the project management artifacts, such as the detailed project plan, the risk register, and the minutes of the project meetings, for completeness and consistency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The implementation planning is managed with agile methods (e.g., Scrum, Kanban). The work packages are organized as user stories in a backlog. Automated tests are an integral part of the 'Definition of Done' for each story to continuously verify the correct implementation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like Jira or Azure DevOps are used to manage the agile process. The implementation is done in sprints, at the end of which there is a potentially shippable increment. Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipelines are used to automate tests and delivery.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor participates in sprint planning and review meetings. It is checked whether the agile processes are being followed and whether the automated tests effectively cover the implemented requirements. The state of the CI/CD pipeline is analyzed.

controls.title: Concept for the secure operation of the system management solution (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the security policies and the system management concept, a concept for the secure operation of the system management solution and the underlying infrastructure SHOULD be created. It SHOULD also be examined how the services of other operational units can be integrated and controlled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An operations manual is created that describes the daily, weekly, and monthly tasks. This includes, for example, patch management for the solution itself, backup and restore procedures, and monitoring of system health. Interfaces to other teams (e.g., network, security) are defined.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the operations manual for completeness and timeliness. It is verified through interviews with the administrators that the documented procedures are known and applied.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The concept for secure operation is documented in the form of detailed Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for all routine tasks and known incidents. The responsibilities and escalation paths are clearly defined. The execution of the operational tasks is logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SOPs are maintained in a central knowledge management system (e.g., Confluence). Checklists are used for recurring tasks. Execution is documented in the ticketing system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly inspects several SOPs for level of detail and correctness. Compliance with the documented procedures and escalation paths is verified based on the ticket history.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Operations are largely realized through automated runbooks and Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC). Manual interventions are the exception and require separate approval. The effectiveness of operations is measured and continuously improved using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Service Level Objectives (SLOs).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Automation tools such as Ansible, Puppet, or Terraform are used to manage the state of the system management infrastructure. A monitoring tool measures KPIs such as availability, performance, and the mean time to recovery (MTTR). The results are visualized in a dashboard and discussed regularly within the team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the code of the automation runbooks and the IaC definitions. The KPI/SLO dashboard is analyzed and a check is performed to determine whether a process for continuous improvement based on the metrics has been established.

controls.title: Regular target-actual comparison within the scope of system management (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD regularly check the extent to which the data, configurations, and scripts managed by the system management solution correspond to the target state. At a minimum, the configuration of the system management solution, the configuration of the systems to be managed, and the automation functions used SHOULD be checked. It SHOULD also be compared whether the software version of the system management solution is up to date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Manual or semi-automated, script-based checks are carried out at regular intervals (e.g., quarterly). The results are recorded in a log. Deviations lead to the creation of tickets for remediation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the logs of the target-actual comparisons performed. It is verified that the checks take place regularly and cover the defined aspects. The processing of tickets resulting from deviations is tracked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Automated configuration and compliance management tools are used to perform the target-actual comparison continuously or at short intervals (e.g., daily). All detected deviations (configuration drift) automatically trigger an alert or a ticket. The review process is formally documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools such as Ansible (in check mode), InSpec, or commercial compliance scanners are used. The target configurations are stored as code or policy in these tools. The results are displayed in a central dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the automated compliance tool and the definitions of the target configurations. The reports and the dashboard are inspected. The response to automatically generated alerts is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A system for automatic correction (self-healing) is implemented. The system not only detects configuration deviations but also corrects them automatically to restore the defined target state. All changes to the target state itself go through a formal test and release process (e.g., GitOps workflow).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration management tools such as Puppet, Chef, or Ansible are operated in enforcing mode. The target configurations are managed in a Git repository. Changes require a pull request, which must be approved by at least one other person and tested by a CI/CD pipeline before it takes effect.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the GitOps workflow and the configuration of the CI/CD pipeline. An unauthorized manual change is made to a system; this must be automatically detected and reverted by the system. The logs of this automatic correction are checked.

controls.title: Triggering of actions by the central components of the system management solution (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Actions that are executed on the managed systems by the system management SHOULD be triggered exclusively by the system management solution. For this purpose, only those management functions SHOULD be activated on the system management solution and the systems to be managed that are actually required.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A policy is established and communicated that administrators must use the central solution for changes. As part of the configuration, a review of the activated services and functions is carried out to deactivate unnecessary ones (hardening).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the managed systems and the management solution for unneeded, activated management functions. Through the analysis of audit logs and interviews, it is checked whether changes are made bypassing the central solution.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Technical controls (e.g., firewall rules, local agent policies) prevent direct management access to the managed systems, thus enforcing the use of the central solution. A regular, documented review process ensures that only the minimum necessary management functions are activated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On the managed systems, the local firewall is configured to allow SSH access, for example, only from the IP address of the system management solution. A quarterly review checks the list of active services against an approved baseline.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor attempts to access a managed system directly from an unauthorized system, which must fail. The logs of the review process for activated functions are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The principle of least functionality is strictly enforced by an automated system that deactivates any function not explicitly defined in the target configuration. All actions performed by the central solution are cryptographically signed and verified by the agent before execution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Compliance-as-Code tool continuously enforces a hardened configuration baseline. The system management solution signs its jobs (e.g., scripts, configuration files) with a private key stored in an HSM. The agent on the managed system verifies the signature with the public key before executing the job.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the compliance tool. An attempt is made to send an unsigned or incorrectly signed job to an agent, which must be rejected. The security of the key management for the signature keys is checked.

controls.title: Commitment to using the designated interfaces for system management (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Management access to systems to be managed SHOULD be exclusively via the designated interfaces of the system management solution. If direct access to systems to be managed is necessary, e.g., after a failure, both the direct access and all changes made in this context SHOULD be documented and, to the necessary extent, integrated into the system management solution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a clear policy on which interfaces to use. For emergencies, a process is defined that regulates the request, approval, and documentation of direct access. The documentation is done manually in a logbook or ticketing system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the policy and the emergency process. The logbooks or tickets for direct access are randomly checked for completeness and correct approval. It is verified that the changes were subsequently recorded in the central system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Technical measures (e.g., host-based firewalls) restrict access to interfaces not intended for management. The emergency process for direct access is formalized, monitored, and regularly audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration of the host-based firewalls is centrally distributed via the system management. Direct access (e.g., via the physical console in the data center) triggers an alert that initiates a review of the event.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the technical access restrictions. The effectiveness of the alerting for direct access is tested. The audit logs of the emergency process are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All management access, including emergency access, is enforced (brokered) through a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution or a jump server. The PAM solution ensures that only the intended protocols are used and logs all activities. The reintegration of changes made in an emergency into the central management system is automated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution is implemented that integrates with the ticketing system. Emergency access can only be initiated with a valid ticket number. After the session ends, a script is executed that reads the actual state of the system and compares it with the target state in the configuration management to detect deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the PAM solution and the downstream automation process. It is verified that no access is possible bypassing the PAM solution and that all sessions are logged without gaps. The automatic synchronization process is tested.

controls.title: Central configuration management for systems to be managed (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software and configuration data for the systems to be managed SHOULD be consistently managed in a configuration management system that allows versioning and change tracking. The associated documentation SHOULD be up-to-date and centrally available and be included in the data backup. The configuration data SHOULD be distributable automatically over the network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central version control system like Git or SVN is used to manage configuration files and scripts. Every change is documented with a commit message. Distribution is done by scripts that copy the configurations from the repository to the target systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the version control system and its history. It is randomly verified that the configuration on a target system corresponds to the state in the repository. The backup strategy for the repository is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) is used. Changes to configurations go through a formal review and test process (e.g., via pull requests and test environments) before they are deployed to production. The configuration management is integrated with a CMDB.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The entire configuration management process follows a GitOps approach. Changes in the main branch of the Git repository automatically trigger a CI/CD pipeline, which first tests the configuration in a staging environment and, after successful testing, rolls it out to production. The CMDB is automatically updated by the pipeline.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the defined workflow for configuration changes, including the review and test steps. The configuration of the CI/CD pipeline is analyzed. It is checked whether the data in the CMDB corresponds with reality and the Git repository.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire system configuration is managed as code (Infrastructure-as-Code, Configuration-as-Code) and serves as the 'Single Source of Truth'. The system continuously enforces this state (Self-Healing). Before a configuration change is approved, its potential security impacts are automatically analyzed (Security-as-Code).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The CI/CD pipeline is extended with static code analysis tools (SAST) for the configuration and infrastructure scripts (e.g., tfsec, checkov). These tools block the pipeline if insecure configurations are checked in. The configuration management tool runs in enforcing mode and automatically resets systems to the desired state in case of manual deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the integration and configuration of the Security-as-Code tools in the pipeline. An attempt is made to check in an insecure configuration, which must be prevented by the pipeline. The self-healing functionality is tested by intentionally misconfiguring a system manually.

controls.title: Status monitoring, logging, and alerting for relevant events in the system management solution and the systems to be managed (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The basic performance and availability parameters SHOULD be continuously monitored. Thresholds SHOULD be determined in advance (baselining), and in the event of a breach, staff SHOULD be notified automatically. Important events (e.g., failure, login attempts, critical states) SHOULD be defined and automatically transmitted to a central logging infrastructure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring tool (e.g., Nagios, Zabbix) is used to monitor CPU, RAM, disk space, and reachability. Static thresholds are configured. A central syslog server collects the logs of the most important systems. Alerting is done via email.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the monitoring tool and the definition of the thresholds. It is verified that the defined important events are sent to the central log server. The alerting is checked by a test alarm.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The monitoring includes application-specific metrics. The baselining is dynamic and adapts to normal patterns. Alarms are correlated to reduce the number of notifications and are automatically fed into a ticketing system. The log data is analyzed in a SIEM system with basic correlation rules to detect security-related incidents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Modern monitoring solutions such as Prometheus in combination with Grafana are used. The log data is collected in a SIEM (e.g., Splunk, Elastic SIEM). Rules are defined that indicate, for example, brute-force attacks or repeated system failures. Alarms automatically create tickets in Jira or a similar system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the extended monitoring and the dynamic thresholds. The correlation rules in the SIEM are checked for their effectiveness and logic. The integration with the ticketing system is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An AIOps platform (AI for IT Operations) is used for predictive monitoring and anomaly detection. Log analysis in the SIEM is supported by machine learning and the integration of threat intelligence feeds. The alerting is context-rich, provides suggestions for remediation, and can trigger automated countermeasures (SOAR).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The AIOps platform analyzes metrics and logs to predict future problems. The SIEM is coupled with a SOAR platform (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) that automatically performs actions for certain alarms, e.g., blocking an IP address on the firewall.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the AIOps platform and the ML models in the SIEM. The effectiveness of the automated responses is tested through simulated attacks or disruptions. The quality of the context-rich alarms is assessed.

controls.title: Integration of system management into contingency planning (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system management solution SHOULD be integrated into the institution's contingency planning. For this purpose, both the system management solution and the configurations of the systems to be managed SHOULD be backed up and integrated into the recovery plans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The servers of the system management solution are included in the central backup concept. The recovery plan for critical business processes mentions that the system management solution is required for restoring the systems. There is a documented plan for restoring the management solution itself.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the emergency and recovery plans and verifies that the system management solution is taken into account. The configuration of the backup for the management servers is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Detailed recovery plans for the system management solution are documented and tested practically on a regular basis (e.g., annually). The Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) and Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) for the solution are defined and compliance is checked during the tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed recovery plan with step-by-step instructions is maintained. An emergency test is conducted annually, during which the solution is restored from backup at an alternate site. The times are measured and compared with the RTO/RPO specifications. The results and lessons learned are documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documentation of the emergency tests, including the test results and the derived improvement measures. It is verified that the defined RTO/RPO values have been confirmed by the tests.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system management solution is highly available and designed for disaster recovery (e.g., through a geo-redundant cluster). The recovery is highly automated and can be triggered with minimal manual intervention.

parts.name: guidance
