parts.prose: The solution is operated as a clustered service across two data centers. In the event of a data center failure, the service automatically fails over to the second site. The automation of the failover is controlled by an orchestration tool and is regularly tested unannounced (Chaos Engineering).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the highly available design of the solution and the configuration of the failover automation. The logs of the regular failover tests are reviewed to confirm the reliability and compliance with the RTO/RPO values.

controls.title: Control of system management communication (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Communication between users and the system management solution, as well as between the system management solution and the IT systems to be managed, SHOULD be restricted to absolutely necessary connections using suitable filtering techniques.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Firewall rules are implemented at the network and/or host level, restricting access to management ports (e.g., SSH, HTTPS, WinRM) to the source IP addresses of the respective authorized communication partners.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the firewalls used (network- and host-based). It is verified that the rules follow the principle of least privilege and only allow the explicitly required connections.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A strict 'Default Deny' firewall policy is applied. The rules are specific (exact source, destination, port/protocol) and are regularly reviewed. The management of firewall rules is centralized and changes are subject to an approval process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central firewall management console is used. Every new or changed rule must be requested and approved via a documented change request. The rule sets are reviewed semi-annually for outdated or overly permissive rules.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the change management process for firewall rules. The rule sets are checked for their specificity and for compliance with the 'Default Deny' principle. The logs of the rule reviews are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Micro-segmentation is used to enforce communication policies at the level of individual workloads. The allowed communication patterns are automatically derived from a policy system (Policy-as-Code). Any deviation from the allowed communication pattern is blocked and alerted in real time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Technologies such as VMware NSX, Illumio, or eBPF-based solutions are used to implement micro-segmentation. The policies defining which application may communicate with which other are maintained as code in a Git repository and rolled out automatically. The system operates in 'Enforcement' mode.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the Policy-as-Code definitions and the automation process. An attempt is made to establish an unauthorized connection between two workloads in the same network segment, which must be prevented by micro-segmentation. The resulting alarm is checked.

controls.title: Checking the system state (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The consistency between the actual system state and the state assumed by the system management solution SHOULD be checked regularly. If deviations are detected, the state specified in the system management solution SHOULD be restored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Regular manual or script-driven checks are performed. For example, the list of installed software on a system is compared with the list in the CMDB. Detected deviations (configuration drift) are corrected manually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the consistency checks performed. A system is selected at random and its actual state (e.g., patch level, installed software) is compared with the data in the management system to verify the effectiveness of the checks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automated tool regularly scans the actual system state (e.g., installed software, running services, configuration files) and compares it with the data in the central CMDB or the configuration management system. Detected deviations automatically generate alerts or tickets.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A compliance scanner or the configuration management tool itself (in check mode) is used for the automated check. The results are visualized in a dashboard that shows the configuration drift. Remediation is carried out downstream by an administrator.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the automated scanner and the reports. It is verified that the alarms or tickets are processed promptly. The accuracy of the detection is tested by a targeted manual change to a system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A self-healing system is implemented. The automated system not only detects the configuration drift, but also corrects it immediately and fully automatically by restoring the centrally defined desired state.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration management tool (e.g., Puppet, Ansible) runs in enforcing mode at regular, short intervals. Any deviation from the state defined in the code is automatically reverted. The actions are logged and are traceable for the administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs an unauthorized, manual change on a system and observes how the system automatically corrects it within the defined time frame. The logs of this automatic correction are checked for completeness and correctness.

controls.title: Securing system management communication between the system management solution and the systems to be managed (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: System management communication between the system management solution and the systems to be managed SHOULD generally be encrypted. The strength of the cryptographic methods and keys used SHOULD be checked regularly and adjusted if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Protocols such as TLS 1.2 or SSHv2 are used for communication by default. The configuration ensures that encryption is enabled. The strength is checked manually on an annual basis based on best practice recommendations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the communication is encrypted by means of network analysis and configuration review. The documentation of the annual review of the cryptography strength is inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of strong, up-to-date encryption protocols and cipher suites (in accordance with, e.g., BSI TR-02102) is enforced for all communication. The cryptographic configuration is centrally managed and regularly and automatically checked for compliance with the requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration management tool distributes a hardened TLS/SSH configuration to all systems. A compliance scanner with a corresponding profile checks the configuration weekly and reports deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the centrally managed cryptography policy and the reports from the compliance scanner. It is verified that no outdated protocols or weak cipher suites are still active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to strong encryption, measures against traffic analysis (e.g., padding, constant data flow) are considered in high-security environments. The private keys of the system management solution that are critical for encryption are protected by a hardware security module (HSM).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An HSM is used for TLS termination on the central management server to protect the private key. Wherever possible, communication is tunneled through a VPN with a constant packet size to make traffic analysis more difficult.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration and operation of the HSM. The measures against traffic analysis are evaluated. It is verified that the private key of the management server cannot be extracted from the HSM.

controls.title: High-availability implementation of the system management solution (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system management solution is operated on a single server. Availability is ensured by regular backups that allow for recovery after a failure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The application runs on a single virtual or physical machine. Daily backups are created and there is a documented process for manual recovery.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the backup configuration and the recovery documentation. It is determined that it is a single-point-of-failure architecture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system management solution is operated in a configuration that offers increased availability, e.g., as an active-passive cluster or on a virtualized platform with automatic restart in the event of hardware failures (e.g., VMware HA).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The application is installed on a failover cluster or in a high-availability virtualization environment. In the event of a failure of the primary node or host, an automatic or semi-automatic switch to a secondary system occurs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the cluster or the virtualization HA function. A failover test is performed or its logs are reviewed to verify functionality.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central system management solution SHOULD be operated in a high-availability mode. To this end, the servers and tools used for the system management solution, including network connections, SHOULD be designed redundantly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The solution is operated as an active-active cluster with load balancing across multiple systems and locations. This includes redundant servers, databases, storage systems, and network connections. The failure of a single component does not lead to an interruption of service.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the entire high-availability design for remaining single points of failure. The configuration of the load balancer and clustering is analyzed. Tests are carried out in which individual components (server, switch, storage) are deliberately shut down to check the resilience of the overall system.

controls.title: Physical separation of the central system management networks (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management network is separated from other networks by logical separation using VLANs. Access control between the VLANs is regulated via a central firewall.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated VLAN for system management is configured on the switches. Routing between this and other VLANs is only possible via a firewall that controls the traffic.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the VLAN configuration on the switches and the firewall rules. It is checked whether direct communication bypassing the firewall is possible (e.g., due to incorrect switch configuration).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management network is isolated from the production networks using advanced logical separation mechanisms such as VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding). This ensures that there is no direct routing possibility between the networks, except via explicitly defined and secured gateways.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Separate VRF instances for the management and production networks are configured on the routers and Layer 3 switches. Communication between the VRFs is only possible via a dedicated firewall appliance that serves as a 'VRF leak' point.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the VRF configuration on the network devices and the configuration of the firewall that serves as a gateway between the VRFs. It is ensured that the separation at the routing level is effective.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management network for system management SHOULD be physically separated from the functional networks, especially production networks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A completely separate physical network infrastructure (own switches, own cabling, own network cards in the servers) is operated for the management network. There is no physical connection to other networks, except via a strictly controlled and monitored firewall.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a physical inspection of the data center cabling and network devices. It is verified that the management infrastructure is physically completely separated from all other networks. The documentation (cabling plans) is reviewed.

controls.title: Integration of system management into automated detection systems (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All security-relevant log data from system management (e.g., logins, configuration changes, actions performed) are forwarded to a central log management solution and stored there for a defined period of time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The system management application and the associated operating systems are configured to send their logs via syslog to a central server. There, the logs are archived but not systematically analyzed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the log forwarding and verifies on the central server that the logs are arriving. The retention periods are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The logging of security-relevant events from system management SHOULD be integrated into a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system. It SHOULD be documented in a traceable manner which events are forwarded to the SIEM. The required interfaces and transfer formats SHOULD be specified.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The logs are forwarded to a SIEM where they are parsed and normalized. Correlation rules are created to check for known attack patterns or policy violations related to system management (e.g., logins outside of business hours, changes by unauthorized users). Alerts from the SIEM are processed by the Security Operations Center (SOC).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the connection to the SIEM, the parsing rules, and the defined correlation rules. The documentation that specifies which events are relevant is reviewed. The processing of test alarms by the SOC is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to SIEM integration, the system management solution is automatically and continuously monitored by a system for detecting security-relevant vulnerabilities. The analysis in the SIEM is supplemented by User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) to detect unknown and anomalous activities of administrators.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated vulnerability scanner regularly checks the system management application and its components for known CVEs. The UEBA function of the SIEM creates behavioral profiles for each administrator and alerts on significant deviations from normal behavior, even if no explicit rule has been violated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the reports from the vulnerability scanner. The configuration and effectiveness of the UEBA system are analyzed, e.g., by reviewing the anomalies detected in recent weeks. It is tested whether an unusual but permitted action by an administrator triggers a UEBA alarm.

controls.title: Cross-site time synchronization for system management (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each site operates its own independent time synchronization. The systems within a site are synchronous, but there may be deviations between the sites.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At each site, there is a local NTP server that gets the time from public servers on the Internet. There is no coordination of time sources between the sites.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the time of systems at different sites and notes possible deviations. The NTP configurations at the various sites are identified as not being coordinated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All sites of the institution are configured to use a common, consistent time base. This is ensured by using a common set of primary, trusted time sources.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A cross-site, hierarchical NTP infrastructure is established. Central Stratum 1 or Stratum 2 servers supply the local NTP servers at the individual sites. All systems use the same time base.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the design of the cross-site time infrastructure. It is verified that all sites use the centrally defined reference time sources and that the times are consistent across all sites.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Time synchronization SHOULD be ensured for both the system management solution and the systems to be managed across all sites of the institution. A common reference time SHOULD be used for this purpose. The transmission of time information is cryptographically secured.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A common reference time is realized by operating our own, high-precision time sources (e.g., GPS or DCF77 receivers) at several geographically separate locations. The distribution of time between the sites and to the clients is secured using Network Time Security (NTS) or NTP with authentication.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the high-precision time sources and the implementation of the cryptographic protection of the NTP protocol. It is tested whether manipulated time packets are rejected by the clients. The cross-locational synchronicity is compared with an independent, precise time source.

controls.title: Automated verification of security-relevant configurations by suitable detection systems (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security-relevant configurations are checked manually or by simple scripts at regular intervals. This is done on the basis of checklists derived from the security policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator performs a quarterly manual check of the most important security settings (e.g. password policies, firewall rules) on a sample of systems. The results are logged in a table.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the checklists and the logs of the manual checks. The sample size and selection are assessed for their representativeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automated detection system (e.g. a compliance scanner or a vulnerability scanner with configuration checking) is used to regularly check configurations for deviations from defined security baselines (e.g. CIS Benchmarks). Deviations are presented in reports.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A tool such as Nessus (with compliance checks), OpenSCAP, or a commercial CSPM (Cloud Security Posture Management) scanner is used to perform weekly scans. The reports are evaluated manually and lead to the creation of tickets for remediation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the scanner, the baselines used, and the reports generated. It is checked how promptly the identified deviations are rectified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security-relevant configurations of the system management solution and the systems to be managed SHOULD be regularly checked for deviations from the target state and for potential vulnerabilities by suitable detection systems. The check is carried out continuously, and deviations trigger real-time alerts. The configuration policies are managed as code.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A compliance-as-code framework (e.g. InSpec) is used. The security policies are stored as code in the Git repository and are continuously executed on the systems via a CI/CD pipeline. Any deviation detected is immediately reported to the SIEM and a ticketing system. Optionally, automatic remediation can be triggered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration policies defined as code and the automation pipeline. An intentional misconfiguration is made to test for correct and timely detection and alerting. The completeness of the checks is assessed.

controls.title: Logging and regulation of system management sessions (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logon and logoff events of administrative sessions on the system management solution and on directly managed systems are centrally logged. The commands executed are not recorded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The standard login logging of the operating systems is activated and the corresponding events are sent to a central syslog server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the login events are collected centrally. It is determined that no information about the activities within the session is available.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All commands executed on the command line during an administrative session are logged. Certain commands classified as particularly critical are either blocked or require additional confirmation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools for session logging and control (e.g. `script`, `ttyrec`, extended shell logging, Sudo with I/O logging) are used. The logs are stored on a secure, read-only log server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the session logging. A test session is conducted to verify that all commands are captured. The secure storage of the logs is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The session content, in particular the activities of users on the system management solution and all direct access to systems to be managed, SHOULD be continuously logged and regulated by a technical solution. The activities SHOULD be controlled at the command level and, if necessary, prevented. During monitoring, an alert SHOULD be triggered not only for concrete rule violations, but also for anomalies in user behavior.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution with session recording functionality is used. All administrative sessions are forcibly routed through this solution. The solution records the sessions (e.g. as video), analyzes the executed commands in real time, and can automatically terminate the session in case of rule violations or anomalous behavior.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the PAM solution, including the policies for session control and recording. A test session is conducted with a forbidden command, which must be blocked. The quality of the session recordings and the effectiveness of the anomaly detection are evaluated.

controls.title: Decoupling of access to the system management solution (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Administrators access the system management solution directly from their workstations in the office network. Access is restricted by a network firewall to the IP addresses of the office networks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A firewall rule allows access to the management interface from any client in the internal network. This poses a risk, as the compromise of any client allows a direct attack on the management solution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall rules and determines that access is permitted very broadly. The increased risk due to the lack of decoupling is documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative access to the system management solution must be through a hardened bastion host (jump server) located in a secure, separate network segment (DMZ). Direct access from workstations is blocked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated server is set up as a jump host. It is minimally installed and hardened. Firewall rules allow access to the system management solution only from this jump host. Administrators first connect to the jump host via SSH or RDP and from there on.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall rules and the configuration of the jump host. It is verified that direct access to the management solution around the jump host is not possible. The hardening measures of the jump host are evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative access to the system management solution SHOULD be secured by using jump servers. Access to the jump server requires multi-factor authentication, and all sessions via the jump server are logged and monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Access to the jump server is secured by a PAM solution or by a combination of MFA and session recording (as described in A25). The jump server is a single-purpose system with no unnecessary software. The connection from the administrator to the jump server and from the jump server to the target system are both strongly encrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the entire access chain, including the MFA for the jump server and the session logging. The configuration of the jump server is checked for minimality and hardening. An attempt is made to bypass the decoupling, which must fail.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Reliable system management is a basic prerequisite for the secure and efficient operation of modern networked systems. For this, it is necessary that system management comprehensively integrates all relevant systems. In addition, appropriate measures must be implemented to protect the system management communication and infrastructure.
System management includes many important functions such as system monitoring, system configuration, event handling, and logging. Another important function is reporting, which can also be set up as a common platform for IT systems and network components. Alternatively, it can be implemented dedicatedly as a uniform platform or as part of the individual system management components.
The system management solution consists of various system management components, for example, agents, which are operated on an underlying system management infrastructure. This solution is used to control the integrated and managed systems via the corresponding interfaces of the information network. The combination of the solution, the underlying infrastructure, the systems to be managed, and the operation forms the entirety of system management.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of this module is to establish information security as an integral part of system management. The module describes, on the one hand, how system management can be structured and secured, and on the other hand, how the associated communication can be protected.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module OPS.1.1.7 System Management is to be applied to the system management solution used in the information domain.
To create an IT Baseline Protection model for a specific information domain, the entirety of all modules must generally be considered. As a rule, several modules apply to the topic or target object.
This module covers, for example:
• the necessary system management components,
• the conceptual tasks for system management,
• logging from the perspective of system management, and
• updating the system management solution.
The following contents are also important and are dealt with elsewhere:
• Requirements for network management (see NET.1.2 Network Management)
• Details regarding the security of the underlying infrastructure and of the IT systems to be managed, especially their management interfaces (see SYS.2 IT Systems)
• Logging and archiving concepts (see OPS.1.1.5 Logging, OPS.1.2.2 Archiving)
• Updating, e.g., through additional software, so-called agents (see OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management)
• User access to the system management solution (see ORP.4 Identity and Authorization Management, as well as OPS.1.2.5 Remote Maintenance and OPS.1.1.2 Proper IT Administration).

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Unauthorized access to the system management solution
parts.prose:
Due to its central position and the necessary access rights to all systems to be managed, system management is a primary target for attacks.
If attackers succeed in accessing system management solutions, e.g., through unpatched security vulnerabilities, they can control and reconfigure all systems managed by the system management. This allows them to, for example, access sensitive information or disrupt services or managed systems. For example, a company could provide central configuration servers for a system management solution. In this example, an unpatched vulnerability is used to modify the configuration files in such a way that the managed systems install ransomware. As a result, in this example, all systems managed by this system management solution are encrypted.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Errors in automation functions for system management
parts.prose:
All protection goals of the information systems to be managed can be compromised by faulty automated processes.
Errors in one or more automation functions, such as scripts, can render the managed systems inoperable or compromised. Due to the automated processes, a large number of IT systems can be compromised quickly. Even highly critical IT systems can be rapidly compromised in this way.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Unauthorized interference in system management communication
parts.prose:
Accidental interference with or targeted attacks on system management communication can violate the integrity of managed IT systems and limit the availability of services or IT systems.
If system management communication is intercepted and manipulated, active systems can be controlled in this way. Furthermore, the data transferred to and from the systems can be recorded and viewed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Insufficient time synchronization of system management components
parts.prose:
Errors in time synchronization can obscure problems and events, making it difficult to detect security incidents and data exfiltration, for example.
If the system time of the system management components is insufficiently synchronized, protocols that use timestamps to evaluate communication validity, for instance, can be disrupted by different system times on the system management components and the managed systems.
Additionally, the logging data for system management may not be able to be correlated with each other. The correlation may also lead to erroneous conclusions if timestamps only appear to match or differ due to faulty synchronization.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Incompatibility between the systems to be managed and the system management solution
parts.prose:
A only partially compatible system management solution can trigger malfunctions in the managed IT systems and limit their availability.
If the system management solution does not fully support the managed IT systems, certain actions cannot be performed as planned. This threat can also occur when updating the systems, where the management interfaces are changed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Loss of connection between users and system management solution
parts.prose:
Connection interruptions can limit the availability of the system management solution.
If the connection between the administrators and the system management solution is disrupted, IT systems can fail. In addition, troubleshooting and the management of IT systems can be made more difficult.
If a connection is dropped or disrupted, cost-intensive security-relevant as well as time-critical tasks cannot be carried out on time, for example, security updates can no longer be installed or security incidents cannot be responded to appropriately.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Loss of connection between system management solution and systems to be managed
parts.prose:
Connection interruptions to the managed systems can particularly impair the availability or integrity of services in the information network.
The scope and constellation of such a connection loss determine whether services are affected and what damage may occur. The resulting error patterns can be difficult to analyze and the occurring errors difficult to resolve.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.8. Insufficient coordination between system management and network management
parts.prose: Uncoordinated actions in network management can have a negative impact on system management. This can lead to configuration inconsistencies between IT systems and connecting networks. For example, connection losses in the network can trigger a large number of subsequent events in the system management area. These events can range up to misconfigurations.

controls.title: Determination of influencing factors for electronic archiving

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only a few technical or legal influencing factors for archiving are considered on an ad hoc basis and without a systematic process. The analysis is incomplete and undocumented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Typically, only the most obvious requirements, such as the statutory retention period from the Commercial Code, are observed, while technical aspects such as format stability or organizational responsibilities are ignored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds that there is no formal or documented analysis of the influencing factors. Random interviews with employees confirm that only a few, general requirements are known.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Although the essential technical, legal and organizational influencing factors are identified, the process is informal and the results are not documented centrally or completely.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For example, there is a checklist in a spreadsheet in which the most important points are recorded. However, this is not consistently maintained and is not integrated into an overall concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds evidence of a basic analysis, for example in the form of internal memos or simple checklists. However, it cannot be proven that the analysis was comprehensive or that the results were incorporated into further planning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before deciding which procedures and products are to be used for electronic archiving, the technical, legal, and organizational influencing factors MUST be identified and documented. The results MUST be incorporated into the archiving concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A defined process for determining the influencing factors is established. This process is documented and the results are recorded as an integral part of the archiving concept. This step is the basis for the selection of suitable archiving systems and strategies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of a documented process for determining the influencing factors. It is checked whether the results of this analysis (technical, legal, organizational factors) are fully documented in the current archiving concept.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process for determining the influencing factors is formalized and is reviewed regularly, for example annually or in the event of significant changes. External experts (e.g. lawyers, compliance officers) are systematically involved.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The results of the analysis are versioned and the review is logged. The analysis is integrated into the organization's overall risk management process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the regular reviews and the documentation of the involvement of subject matter experts. It is checked whether the analysis of the influencing factors is managed as a separate control point in the risk management system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process of determining influencing factors is largely automated. Changes in legislation or technical standards are continuously monitored by specialized services (e.g. legal tech solutions, standard monitoring). The results lead to automated notifications and initiate a review process of the archiving concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools are used that query compliance databases and, in the event of relevant changes (e.g. new EU regulation, outdated crypto algorithm), automatically trigger a workflow to adapt the risk profile and the archiving concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration and logs of the automated monitoring tools. It is checked whether relevant external events (e.g., a new BSI guideline) have been correctly detected and the corresponding internal adaptation processes have been demonstrably initiated.

controls.title: Development of an archiving concept

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A rudimentary archiving concept exists in the form of notes or drafts. It is incomplete, not approved, and only covers basic aspects, while important points such as responsibilities or regular adjustments are missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Often, the 'concept' is limited to the decision for a specific software product, without defining the strategic goals and long-term processes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During interviews, the auditor finds evidence of a planned approach but cannot identify a formal, let alone approved, concept document.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A documented archiving concept is available and describes the essential goals and regulations. However, it lacks formal approval by management and a process for regular review and adaptation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A project team created a concept that is no longer maintained after the project's end. It has the status of a one-time work product.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor receives a dated concept document. However, there is no evidence of formal approval (e.g., signature of the institution's head) or of subsequent updates.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be defined what objectives are to be achieved with archiving. In this context, it MUST be considered which regulations are to be complied with, which employees are responsible, and what functional and service scope is intended. The results MUST be documented in an archiving concept. The institution's management MUST be involved in this process. The archiving concept MUST be regularly adapted to the current circumstances of the institution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal archiving concept is created that covers all mentioned points. It is formally approved by the institution's management. A responsible person is appointed who is in charge of the regular review and adaptation of the concept. The adaptation process (e.g., annual review) is also defined in the concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of an approved archiving concept. It is checked whether all required contents (goals, regulations, responsibilities, etc.) are present, whether the institution's management has been demonstrably involved, and whether a process for regular adaptation is defined and implemented (e.g., by inspecting the minutes of the last review).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The archiving concept is formally versioned and the approval processes are documented. It is explicitly integrated into the higher-level Information Security Management System (ISMS) and its policy framework. Planned reviews are tracked in a central system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concept is managed in a document management system with versioning and an approval workflow. It refers to relevant higher-level and lower-level policies (e.g., IS policy, data backup concept) and vice versa.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the version history of the concept and the logs of the approval workflows. The integration into the ISMS is verified by checking the links to other relevant security documents.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The archiving concept is a living document linked to automated compliance checks. Significant changes to the IT landscape, business processes, or legal frameworks automatically trigger a review and adaptation workflow for the concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Changes in the CMDB (e.g., introduction of a new data store) or signals from legal tech monitoring (see A1-M5) automatically trigger a task in the ticket system to review the relevance for the archiving concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automation rules. Using examples (e.g., decommissioning of an old system), it is traced whether the workflow for concept adaptation was correctly triggered and processed.

controls.title: Suitable setup of archive systems and storage of archive media

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The components of the archive system are set up in a general office space or an inadequately secured server room. Archive media (e.g., tapes, external hard drives) are stored unsecured at the workplace or in an unlocked cabinet.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This situation often arises when archiving is misunderstood as a purely administrative task and the physical security requirements are ignored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through an inspection that the archive systems and media are freely accessible and not subject to any special physical protection measures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT components of the archive system are housed in a server room with general access control. Archive media are stored in a lockable office cabinet or a separate, locked room.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The server room offers basic protection, but there are no specific zones or racks for the high-protection-need archive system. The storage of the media is fundamentally secure, but without special environmental conditions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the systems are in a room with access control and that the media are stored separately and locked. However, it is noted that the access rights are very broad and there is no environmental monitoring.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT components of an archive system MUST be set up in secure rooms. It MUST be ensured that only authorized persons are allowed to enter the rooms. Archive storage media MUST be stored appropriately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The archive servers are set up in a data center or a dedicated server room with regulated access control (e.g., key, chip card). Access permissions are granted restrictively according to the need-to-know principle. A suitable storage location (e.g., fireproof data cabinet) is selected for the archive media according to the media manufacturers' specifications.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation of the access rights for the server room and compares it with the responsible roles. The suitability of the storage location for the archive media is verified through an inspection and comparison with the specifications of the media manufacturers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The secure rooms have documented and monitored environmental controls (temperature, humidity, fire protection). Access is logged, and the logs are regularly checked for unauthorized attempts. The storage conditions for the media are explicitly documented and actively monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Sensors for temperature and humidity are installed and connected to a monitoring system. Access logs from the electronic locking system are evaluated monthly by the security department. A thermometer/hygrometer in the data cabinet is checked regularly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the environmental monitoring and access control, as well as the evaluation reports. The documentation of the target storage conditions for the media is checked and compared with the recorded actual values.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The physical protection of the archive systems includes video surveillance and two-factor authentication for access (e.g., card and biometrics). The environmental monitoring is automated and triggers alarms directly in case of deviations. For emergency preparedness, archive media are stored at one or more geographically separate, equally high-security locations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Access control to the archive system's rack requires separate authentication. The monitoring system is coupled with the ticket system. An external service provider is used for the audit-proof storage of backup tapes at another location.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the two-factor access control and the monitoring's alarm chain. The contracts and audit reports of the external service provider for the off-site media storage are reviewed to ensure that an equivalent level of protection exists there.

controls.title: Consistent indexing of data during archiving

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The indexing of archive data is done manually, sporadically, and inconsistently. There are no guidelines for the metadata to be used, which means that retrieving documents depends on chance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each user names and tags archived files at their own discretion. There is no uniform folder structure or metadata.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines from a sample of archive data that no uniform indexing logic is discernible. File names, folder structures, and metadata are heterogeneous and not standardized.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic indexing scheme (e.g., a predefined folder structure and some mandatory metadata) is used. However, compliance with this scheme is not enforced or checked, leading to errors and inconsistencies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a written guide on how to store files, but the archive system does not check the entries for conformity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds a documented specification for indexing. However, when checking samples, numerous deviations from this specification are found.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data, documents, and records stored in an archive MUST be uniquely indexed. For this purpose, the structure and scope of the index entries for an archive MUST be defined during the conception phase.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A binding metadata schema is defined in the archiving concept. This defines which index information (e.g., date, document type, file number) must be recorded for which type of document to enable unique identification and research.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that a clear indexing scheme is defined in the archiving concept. Using samples, it is checked whether the metadata recorded in the archive system corresponds to this scheme and enables unique identification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The indexing scheme is formally documented and enforced during archiving by technical means (e.g., input masks with mandatory fields and validation rules). Regular, planned audits check the consistency and quality of the index data.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The archive system only allows a document to be saved if all mandatory metadata is validly filled out according to the schema. Once a quarter, a script is run that checks the index database for inconsistencies and creates a report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the validation rules in the archive system. In addition, the logs and results of the regular index audits are reviewed to assess the effectiveness of the control.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The indexing is fully automated. Metadata is extracted and adopted directly from the source systems (e.g., ERP, DMS) or through intelligent document analysis (e.g., OCR and semantic analysis). The integrity of the index is continuously secured by cryptographic chaining.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A middleware component reads the metadata from the source system when a document is submitted for archiving. For unstructured documents, an AI-based classification and keywording engine is used. Every index change is recorded in a tamper-proof log.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the automated metadata import and the AI engine. The effectiveness of the cryptographic protection of the index is verified through a technical audit. It is checked whether a `get-logentry -hash <hash>` command returns a valid response.

controls.title: Regular processing of archived data sets

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Curation or migration of archive data only occurs reactively when access fails or a medium is no longer readable. There is no proactive process for data preservation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The motto is 'out of sight, out of mind'. Only when a document is needed years later and cannot be opened is an attempt made to fix the problem, often without success.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During interviews, the auditor discovers that there are no planned activities for data curation. Past incident tickets could provide evidence of data loss due to outdated formats or defective media.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an awareness of the need for data maintenance. Occasional manual readability checks are performed, but there is no formally planned and regular process for data curation or migration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator checks random samples every few months to see if old files can still be opened. However, there is no fixed strategy on what to do in case of impending incompatibility.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds no formal planning or documentation for data curation. However, individual employees can report sporadic, manual checks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Throughout the entire archiving period, it MUST be ensured that the data format used can be processed by the applications in use, that the stored data will remain readable and reproducible in the future in such a way that semantics and evidentiary value are maintained, that the file system used on the storage medium can be processed by all components involved, and that the storage media can be read at any time without technical problems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A defined, repeatable process for data curation is established. This process includes regular checks of media readability (e.g., through refresh cycles for tapes), data integrity checks (e.g., using checksums), and monitoring of the file formats used. A plan for conversion to new formats or migration to new media is maintained.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and documentation of the data curation process. Logs are used to prove that the defined checks (e.g., annual media check, regular integrity checks) are actually carried out.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal data migration strategy is documented and embedded in the archiving concept. Planned, automated tasks regularly perform checks for format obsolescence, media integrity, and data integrity. Regular and documented test restorations ensure reproducibility.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script checks all archive data monthly against a database of known file formats and reports outdated formats. Annually, 1% of the archive data is randomly restored and checked for readability and correctness. The results are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documented migration strategy. The configuration of the automated checking scripts and the logs of the performed checks and test restorations are inspected and evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire preservation process is highly automated. The archive system continuously monitors data integrity (bit rot detection), format validity, and the health of the storage media (e.g., via SMART). When thresholds are reached, migration or refresh tasks are automatically initiated, logged in detail, and alarms are triggered in case of errors.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The storage system performs permanent background scans for integrity checking. The archive system is connected to a format registry (e.g., PRONOM) and triggers workflows upon changes. During migration, the successful conversion of each individual object is validated by a hash comparison.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automated monitoring and migration processes. The system logs are used to trace the complete monitoring and the correct execution of automated curation processes. A `get-archive-health-report` command is executed and the result is analyzed.

controls.title: Protection of the integrity of the index database of archive systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Backups of the index database are performed irregularly and without a fixed plan. No restore tests are carried out and the integrity of the database is not actively checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A backup is only created when major changes are pending. The usability of the backup files is not checked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds no backup plans or logs. The existing backup files are sporadic and their consistency cannot be verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Regular backups of the index database are planned and performed. Basic database integrity checks (e.g., using internal database commands) are occasionally performed manually.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A daily backup of the database is set up as a scheduled task. An administrator runs a `CHECKDB` command monthly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the regular backups and reviews the backup logs. However, no proof of regular and successful restore tests can be provided.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrity of the index database MUST be ensured and be verifiable. Furthermore, the index database MUST be backed up regularly. The data backups MUST be restorable.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data backup concept for the index database is created and implemented. This includes regular, automated backups. The restorability is tested and logged at planned intervals (e.g., semi-annually). The integrity of the database is verified through regular, planned execution of consistency checks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the data backup concept, the configuration of the backup jobs, and the logs of the regular integrity checks. The logs of the successful restore tests are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The index database is designed to be redundant (e.g., through replication or clustering) to increase availability and minimize the risk of data loss. Restore tests are performed regularly and the results are documented. Integrity checks are automated and performed daily.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The index database runs on an SQL cluster with synchronous replication to a second system. Restoration from backup is practiced quarterly in a test environment. The results of the daily, automated integrity checks are reported to a central monitoring system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the redundant database architecture. The logs of the quarterly restore tests and the log data of the daily integrity checks in the monitoring system are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The index database is operated as a highly available, geographically redundant cluster. The integrity of the index entries is additionally protected by cryptographic methods, such as a blockchain-like chaining of transaction logs. The verification of this cryptographic integrity is continuous and automated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The database is mirrored across two data centers. Every change to the index data is cryptographically signed and linked to the previous state. A separate monitoring service permanently verifies the integrity of this chain.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture of the geo-cluster. The functionality of the cryptographic chaining is verified through a technical audit. A `verify-index-chain` command is executed and the result is evaluated.

controls.title: Regular data backup of system and archive data

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data backups are performed ad hoc and incompletely. It is not ensured that all relevant data (system, index, AND archive data) are backed up.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Although the file system with the archive data is backed up, the corresponding index database or the configuration files of the archive system are forgotten.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the scope of the backed-up data with the system documentation and finds that critical components are missing from the backup jobs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic backup plan exists and is followed, so that all relevant data categories are covered. However, restore tests are performed rarely or not at all.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All necessary data are included in the backup jobs and the backups run regularly. However, there is a reliance that the backup will work in an emergency.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the completeness of the backup jobs and the regularity of their execution. However, upon request, no logs of successful restore tests can be provided.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All archive data, the associated index databases, and the system data MUST be backed up regularly (see CON.3 Data Backup Concept).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Based on the general data backup concept (CON.3), a specific plan for the archive system is created. This plan defines exactly which data is backed up how often and specifies that regular restore tests must be carried out.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether a specific, documented data backup scheme exists for the archive system that covers all three data categories (archive, index, system) and is in line with CON.3. The execution of backups and restore tests is verified using logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire data backup and restoration process is fully documented. Restore tests are carried out according to a fixed schedule (e.g., quarterly) and the results (success, duration, problems encountered) are formally logged and evaluated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are detailed instructions for restoring the entire system. The logs of the restore tests are stored centrally and reviewed by the CISO. Findings from the tests are used to improve the process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation and the logs of the planned restore tests from the last year. It is checked whether measures have been derived and implemented from the test results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The data backup is fully automated and includes an automatic integrity check of each backup. Restore tests are also automated and carried out at short intervals in an isolated test environment (recovery sandbox). Geographically separate storage locations are generally used for the backups.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After each backup job, a test restore to a virtual machine is automatically initiated, which boots up the system and checks the data consistency. The results are reported to the monitoring system. Backups are replicated daily to an external data center.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automated backup verification and the recovery sandbox. The logs of the daily automated tests and the configuration of the cross-site replication are checked. A `get-last-recovery-test-report` is executed.

controls.title: Logging of archive access

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logging is not activated on the archive system at all or only with minimal default settings. The captured logs do not contain enough information to trace access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For example, only logins and logouts are logged, but not which documents were accessed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: When reviewing the system configuration, the auditor determines that the logging level is insufficient or the logging function is deactivated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Detailed log data about archive access is generated. However, it is only evaluated reactively when a security incident is already suspected. There is no regular, proactive monitoring.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The logs exist, but they are not collected centrally and are overwritten after a short time. No one is responsible for regular review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that detailed logs are generated. However, when asked, no process or person responsible for regular evaluation can be named.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All access to electronic archives MUST be logged. It SHOULD be specified how long the log data is retained. The log data of archive access SHOULD be regularly evaluated. It SHOULD be defined which events are displayed to which employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A logging concept is established in the archiving concept. This defines WHICH events (date, time, user, client, actions, errors) are logged, HOW LONG the logs are kept, and WHO is responsible for the REGULAR evaluation. A process for escalating critical events is defined.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the logging concept and the technical configuration of the logging. The regular review of the logs is proven by means of evaluation reports or entries in the ticket system. It is checked whether the retention periods are being observed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The log data is transmitted to a central log management system to protect it from manipulation on the source system. The evaluation of the logs is supported by automated rules that check for typical attack patterns or policy violations (e.g., mass downloads) and trigger notifications when there is a match.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A log agent on the archive server sends all relevant events in real time to a central SIEM or a log server. There, rules are defined such as 'Alert when user X downloads more than 100 documents in one hour'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the log forwarding and the rules in the central log management system. The logs of the central system are checked to ensure the completeness of the captured data. An alarm is triggered on a test basis to check the notification chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The log data in the central SIEM system is correlated in real time with information from other sources (e.g., network logs, authentication servers) to detect complex attacks. In the event of critical events, automated responses (e.g., blocking a user account) are triggered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SIEM correlates a failed login to the archive system with a virus detection on the user's client and unusual network traffic from this client. This leads to a high-priority alert and the automatic move of the client to a quarantine network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the complex correlation rules in the SIEM and the configuration of the automated responses (SOAR). The effectiveness of the entire detection and response chain is reviewed using simulated attack scenarios.

controls.title: Selection of suitable data formats for archiving documents

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Proprietary, undocumented, or file formats known to be unsuitable for long-term archiving are used for archiving. The selection is made without considering long-term readability.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Documents are archived in the native format of an outdated software for which there will soon be no licenses or runnable systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: By analyzing the archived data, the auditor identifies the use of unstable or proprietary formats and determines that no strategy exists to ensure future readability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Common standard formats such as DOCX or JPEG are used. However, there is no conscious selection of formats specifically designed for long-term archiving (e.g. PDF/A).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users save files in the default formats of their Office applications, which works in the short to medium term, but poses long-term risks (e.g. due to embedded dynamic content).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor notes that although no highly problematic formats are used, the specific requirements of long-term archiving (e.g. stability, completeness) were not taken into account when choosing the format.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A suitable data format MUST be selected for archiving. It MUST ensure that archive data and selected features of the original document medium can be reproduced in the long term and true to the original. The document structure of the selected data format MUST be clearly interpretable and electronically processable.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A policy for file formats to be used is defined in the archiving concept. This policy lists recommended and permissible formats that are based on open standards and promise high stability for long-term archiving (e.g. PDF/A, TIFF, XML).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of the policy for file formats in the archiving concept. Random checks are used to verify whether the files stored in the archive comply with the provisions of this policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only open, well-documented data formats published by a standardization organization are used. For evidential and audit-proof archiving of image data, a lossless image compression method is used. Compliance with the format specifications is technically checked upon entry into the archive.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: It is specified that only PDF/A-2u and TIFF G4 are permissible for documents. The archive system checks during upload whether the file corresponds to the declared format (format validation) and rejects non-compliant files.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the policy for the explicit requirement of open standards and lossless compression. The configuration of the automatic format validation in the archive system is checked. An attempt is made to archive a file in an impermissible format as a test.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection and use of data formats is governed by a strict, technically enforced policy. The organization actively monitors the development of relevant standardization bodies to identify impending format obsolescence early and proactively develop migration strategies. All incoming files are automatically converted to the defined target format during archiving.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An ingest process in the archive system accepts various input formats, validates them, and mandatorily converts them to PDF/A-3b. A designated employee is responsible for 'format watching' and reports regularly on developments.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automatic conversion process. It is checked whether a process for 'format watching' has been established and whether reports on this are available. The conversion is verified by archiving a test file in a different format and then checking the result.

controls.title: Creation of a policy for the use of archive systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are only informal, orally transmitted rules for the administration and use of the archive system. There is no written documentation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: New administrators are trained by their predecessors. Knowledge of correct procedures is tied to individuals and is lost when they leave.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor cannot find any written policies or instructions. Interviews with employees confirm the lack of a formal regulation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are separate, basic instructions or manuals for administrators and users. However, these are not combined into a coherent, approved policy and do not cover all relevant aspects.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is an 'Admin Manual' and a 'Quick Start Guide for Users'. However, aspects such as data backup, rights assignment, or the handling of archive media are not described or are described inadequately.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds individual documents, but determines that they do not have the depth and breadth of a comprehensive policy and that important regulatory areas are missing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be ensured that employees use the archive system as intended in the archiving concept. For this purpose, an administration and a user policy SHOULD be created. The administration policy SHOULD regulate the responsibility for operation and administration, agreements on performance parameters, modalities of rights assignment, handling of data and media, monitoring, data backup, logging, and the separation of producers and consumers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A comprehensive policy (or set of policies) is created that clearly distinguishes between the tasks and rights of administrators and users. All points mentioned in the requirement text are addressed and regulated therein. The policy is made known to the relevant groups of people.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of a comprehensive administration and user policy. It is checked whether all required regulatory areas (responsibility, SLAs, rights assignment, etc.) are covered and whether the policy has been demonstrably made available to the employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The policy is formally approved by the institution's management, versioned, and reviewed regularly (e.g., annually) for currency. Employees must formally acknowledge receipt of the parts of the policy relevant to them.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is managed in the document management system with versioning and an approval workflow. New employees must complete training on the policy as part of their onboarding and confirm their participation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the version history and approval documentation of the policy. Evidence of regular reviews and confirmed acknowledgment by employees (e.g., signed forms, log entries in the LMS) is reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the policy is regularly checked through internal or external audits. This includes both manual controls and automated technical checks that can detect policy violations in the system configuration. The policy is integrated into the organization's central policy management framework.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A compliance management tool performs nightly checks of the archive system's configuration against the policy requirements (e.g., correct logging settings, no excessive admin rights). Annual audits review the organizational processes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the reports of the automated compliance checks and the results of the last internal audits. It is verified that identified deviations have been tracked and resolved. The integration into the organization's overall policy framework is checked.

controls.title: Instruction on the administration and operation of the archive system

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Induction takes place only informally on a 'learning by doing' basis. There are no structured training materials and attendance is not documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: New employees look over their colleagues' shoulders. The quality of the onboarding depends heavily on the available time and knowledge of the colleague providing the training.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds that no training materials or certificates of attendance exist. Interviews confirm the informal nature of the onboarding process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A one-time, basic training on the operation or administration of the archive system is offered to new employees. However, there are no regular refresher courses or content tailored to specific tasks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a standard PowerPoint presentation that is shown to all new employees. Specific admin topics or legal frameworks are only covered superficially.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds training materials for a basic training course. However, no concept for advanced or recurring training can be proven.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The responsible IT operations staff and users SHOULD be trained for their area of responsibility. The training for IT operations SHOULD cover system architecture, security mechanisms, installation, operation, media handling, documentation, and escalation procedures. The user training SHOULD cover system handling, operation, and legal frameworks. The execution of the training sessions and the attendance SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A training concept is created that defines different, role-based training modules for administrators and users. The content covers all mentioned topics. Attendance lists are kept for each training session and stored centrally.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the training concept and the associated documents. Based on the attendance lists, random checks are performed to see if the responsible employees have received the training intended for their role.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Participation in the role-based training is mandatory. Refresher courses are also mandatory at regular intervals (e.g., every two years) or in case of significant changes to the system or processes. Learning success is checked with a simple test or a practical exercise.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The HR system or a Learning Management System (LMS) manages the training obligations and reminds employees and supervisors of due training courses. At the end of a training course, a short multiple-choice test must be passed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks in the LMS or the personnel files whether the training and refresher courses have been completed by the employees in due time. The existence and results of the learning success checks are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive, multi-level training program is established. In addition to theoretical content, this includes practical exercises in a test environment (hands-on labs) and simulations of malfunctions or security incidents. The training records are managed centrally in a Learning Management System (LMS) and are linked to the authorization management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators must pass a practical exam in a sandbox environment before they receive admin rights for the production system. In annual exercises, for example, the restoration of data after a simulated failure is trained.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the curriculum of the comprehensive training program, including the practical exercises. A technical and organizational check is performed to determine whether the assignment of critical permissions is actually tied to the proof of successful training participation.

controls.title: Monitoring of storage resources of archive media

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The available storage capacity is only checked manually and irregularly, or only when errors already occur due to full storage.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The archiving fails. During the subsequent troubleshooting, an administrator determines that the hard disk is full.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds no configuration for storage monitoring. Incident tickets from the past show failures due to storage bottlenecks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The storage capacity is checked regularly and manually by an administrator. However, there is no automatic alerting when a critical level is reached.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator has a weekly calendar entry to check the fill levels of the archive drives.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds no automated monitoring. Interviews with administrators confirm the existence of regular manual checks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The available free storage capacity on the archive media SHOULD be continuously monitored. As soon as a defined threshold is fallen below, responsible staff MUST be automatically alerted. The alerting SHOULD be role-based. Sufficient empty archive media MUST always be available to quickly prevent storage bottlenecks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring system is configured to permanently monitor the fill level of the archive storage. When a threshold is reached (e.g., 80% full), an email is automatically sent to the distribution list of the storage administrators. A process is established to procure and provide new media in a timely manner.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the storage monitoring configuration in the monitoring tool, including the defined thresholds and alert recipients. It is checked whether a process for procuring and providing new media exists and whether sufficient empty media are in stock.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The monitoring includes a trend analysis and capacity planning to proactively predict future storage needs. Alerts are not only sent via email but are fed directly into a ticket system to ensure traceable processing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The monitoring system generates monthly reports on storage growth and predicts when the capacity limit will be reached. The alerts automatically create a high-priority ticket that is assigned to a storage admin.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the capacity reports and forecasts from recent months. The configuration of the interface to the ticket system is checked and it is verified how alerts were responded to.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Capacity management is largely automated. The system not only triggers alarms, but can also automatically assign new storage from a predefined pool if required (scale-out) or directly initiates a standardized procurement workflow via an interface.

parts.name: guidance
