parts.prose: After an APT incident, IT systems are often reinstalled or completely decommissioned. However, if no forensic copy of the IT systems was made beforehand, traces could be destroyed that would be necessary for further clarification of the incident or even for legal proceedings.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Premature alerting of attackers
parts.prose:
Typically, before an APT incident is remediated, the attack is observed and forensically analyzed over a longer period of time in order to identify all access routes as well as the tools and methods used. If the attackers notice during this phase that they have been discovered, they may resort to countermeasures. For example, they may try to cover their tracks or sabotage other IT systems. They could also abort the attack for the time being or set up additional backdoors to continue the attack later.
Since an APT attack must generally be assumed to have compromised the institution's entire IT infrastructure, there is a high risk that the attackers will discover the remediation activities. This is especially true if the compromised IT infrastructure is used to plan and coordinate the remediation. If the essential steps for remediation do not take place in the correct order or if critical measures are not carried out simultaneously and in a coordinated manner, the risk of alerting the attackers increases. For example, if those responsible isolate the network step by step instead of all at once, the attackers may be warned before their access is effectively terminated.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Data loss and failure of IT systems
parts.prose: During the remediation of an APT incident, various IT systems are reinstalled and networks are also temporarily isolated. This inevitably leads to IT system downtime, and services are then only available to a limited extent or not at all. If the remediation takes a very long time, this can lead to a loss of productivity for the institution. This in turn can result in significant economic losses, which can even be existential. This is particularly the case if no or insufficient documentation is available for a rebuild.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Lack of network redesign after an APT attack
parts.prose: In an APT attack, the attackers gain detailed knowledge of how the target environment is structured and configured. For example, they know the existing network segments, naming schemes for IT systems, accounts, and the software and services used. With this knowledge, the same attackers may be able to regain access to the target environment even after a remediation. They can move very specifically, efficiently, and inconspicuously within the network and quickly achieve a high level of infection again.

controls.title: Definition of Responsibilities (B) [Institution Management]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The responsibility for audits is informal and is only assigned to a person, often the CISO, on an as-needed basis. There is no formal appointment or a clear demarcation to avoid conflicts of interest.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The assignment is made verbally or by email when an audit is due. There is no systematic check to see if the assigned person (e.g., the CISO auditing their own ISMS) has a conflict of interest.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing the institution's management about who is responsible for planning audits. Reviewing emails or minutes of past audits to determine how responsibility was assigned.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is generally known who is responsible for audits, and this is stated in a general role description (e.g., of the CISO). However, there is no explicit appointment by the institution's management for each audit program.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The responsibility is mentioned in general terms in the CISO's job description or in the IS policy. The results of audits are collected but not systematically used to improve security measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the CISO's job description or the relevant policies. Checking if a general responsibility for audits is defined. Randomly checking whether audit results are archived.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution's management MUST formally designate a person or role responsible for planning and initiating audits or reviews. In doing so, the management MUST ensure that no conflicts of interest arise. The institution MUST use the results of audits and reviews to improve security measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is an official letter of appointment from the institution's management for the person in charge of audits (e.g., an audit manager or the CISO with a clear regulation on independence when auditing their own areas). The use of audit results is a fixed item in the ISMS management review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the official document for the appointment of the person in charge of audits. Analyzing the regulations for avoiding conflicts of interest. Reviewing the minutes of management reviews to verify the systematic use of audit results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The responsibilities for the entire audit process (planning, initiation, execution, follow-up) are detailed in a policy. There is a defined process to systematically identify and manage conflicts of interest. The improvement of security measures based on audit results is tracked via a ticketing system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated audit policy describes all roles and responsibilities. Before each audit, the audit team completes a declaration of independence. Measures from audits are recorded as tickets in a system like Jira or a GRC tool and their processing is monitored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the audit policy. Randomly checking the declarations of independence of audit teams. Verifying in the ticketing system that findings from audit reports are recorded as tasks and their status is tracked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The role of audit management is established as an independent staff unit reporting directly to the institution's management. The process for improving security measures is fully integrated into a GRC tool and automates the assignment, monitoring, and escalation of measures. The effectiveness of the improvement process is measured and reported using key performance indicators (KPIs).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution's organizational chart shows an independent Internal Audit department or a Chief Audit Executive. A GRC tool automatically creates tasks for the specialist departments based on the audit findings and escalates in case of deadline overruns. Regular KPI reports show, for example, the average time to resolve deficiencies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the organizational chart and the reporting lines. Live demonstration of the automated process in the GRC tool. Analysis of the KPI reports on the effectiveness of the measures tracking.

controls.title: Preparation of an audit or a review (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Audits are conducted with minimal preparation. The subject and objectives of the audit are often communicated orally only at the beginning of the audit. Affected personnel are informed at short notice and informally.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The preparation consists of a short email to arrange an appointment. There is no formal agenda or documentation of the audit objectives in advance. The staff council is usually not informed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing employees on how they were informed about past audits. Checking existing documentation (e.g., emails) for the audit announcement for completeness and deadlines.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before an audit, the subject of the audit is roughly defined and communicated to the affected area. However, a formal definition of detailed audit objectives is usually missing. The personnel is informed, but the staff council is not notified as a standard procedure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple agenda is sent out in advance by email. This lists the systems or departments to be audited. The decision on whether to inform the staff council is made on a case-by-case basis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the audit announcements for the definition of the audit scope. Interviewing the person in charge of the audit about the process for informing the staff council.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before an audit or a review, the institution MUST define the subject and the objectives of the audit. The affected personnel MUST be informed. Depending on the subject of the investigation, the staff council MUST be informed about the planned audit or review.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each audit, a standardized audit announcement document is used, which clearly names the subject, objectives, period, and the involved auditors and contact persons. There is a checklist that checks when the staff council must be informed (according to the Works Constitution Act or staff representation acts).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Randomly checking the audit announcement documents. Verifying that the audit objectives are clearly defined. Reviewing the checklist and the corresponding evidence of informing the staff council.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit preparation process is formalized in a policy. The audit objectives are derived from the audit program on a risk-based basis. Communication to the affected personnel and the staff council is done using standardized templates and with appropriate deadlines, which are also defined in the policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC tool or a dedicated audit management tool supports the preparation process by automating the creation of the announcement documents and adopting the risk-based objectives from the audit program. Informing the staff council is implemented as a fixed workflow step.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the audit policy. Analyzing the connection between the objectives in the audit program and the objectives in the audit announcement. Verifying the standardized information process, e.g., by inspecting system logs or email templates.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit preparation is a fully digitized and largely automated process. Based on the selected audit subject, relevant documents and contact persons are automatically compiled from a CMDB or GRC system. The staff council is informed via a dedicated portal and can directly view and comment on the planned scope there.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit management tool is integrated with the GRC system, the HR system, and the CMDB. When planning an audit, the system suggests the relevant stakeholders and the staff council to be informed based on the systems and processes. Approval and communication are done at the push of a button.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the automated audit preparation process. Checking the configuration of the interfaces to peripheral systems. Inspecting the staff council's portal and the documentation therein.

controls.title: Conducting an audit (B) [Audit team]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Audits are conducted unsystematically, often as a mere interview without document review or technical tests. The results are communicated orally and rarely recorded in writing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit consists of a conversation with the system administrator. No configuration files or log files are checked. An audit report is not created; the results are summarized in an email.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing employees about the process of past audits. Searching for any form of written audit results (e.g., emails, notes).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An audit fundamentally checks whether requirements are met, usually through a combination of document review and interviews. Care is taken not to actively intervene in systems. The results are summarized in a simple report.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit team uses a simple checklist to verify the requirements. The audit report lists the checked items and the identified deviations. The report is sent as a PDF document via email.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of past audit checklists and reports. Verification that both documents and interviews were part of the audit.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In an audit, the audit team MUST verify that the requirements from policies, norms, standards, and other relevant specifications are met. The audit team MUST conduct a document review and an on-site inspection, ensuring they never actively intervene in systems themselves. All findings MUST be documented in writing and summarized in an audit report, which is promptly submitted to the responsible body.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit team follows a defined audit process. Working papers are used to document the audit procedures and the evidence collected. The audit report follows a standardized template and is transmitted via a defined communication channel.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Random inspection of audit reports and related working papers. Verification of the traceability of the audit. Checking timestamps to confirm the timely submission of the report.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit is conducted according to a detailed, risk-based audit plan. In addition to document review and interviews, the audit methods include technical verifications in read-only mode and system walk-throughs. The findings are systematically evaluated and assigned a criticality level. The audit report contains concrete recommendations for action.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An audit management tool is used for planning and documenting the audit. Auditors use read-only scripts to automatically check configurations. Each finding in the report is classified by risk (e.g., high, medium, low).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the audit plans for risk-based focus areas. Analysis of the audit methods documented in the audit report. Verification of the consistency of the risk assessment of findings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit execution is supported by continuous auditing techniques, where controls are automatically and continuously monitored. The on-site inspection focuses on complex issues and a review of the effectiveness of the automated controls. The audit report is dynamically generated in a GRC tool and allows for an interactive analysis of the results.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC tool is connected to SIEM and configuration management systems to detect control deviations in real time. Auditors act more as analysts of the automated results. The audit report is an interactive dashboard with drill-down capabilities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the continuous auditing system. Check of the configuration of the automated control tests. Analysis of the interactivity and traceability of the audit dashboard.

controls.title: Conducting a Review (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Reviews are conducted ad hoc, usually in response to a problem. It is checked whether a single requirement has been implemented, without considering the overall context. Corrections are made spontaneously and are not documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator checks a firewall rule after an access problem has been reported. The rule is adjusted directly, but the change is not recorded in any logbook or ticket system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing administrators on how they ensure the correctness of configurations. Searching for evidence of corrections made, e.g., in change requests or system logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During a review, it is checked whether requirements have been implemented correctly in principle. Identified deviations are corrected. A simple change tracking system, e.g., through comments in configuration files, is in place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A development team conducts a code review before a release and checks for compliance with the basic coding guidelines. Changes are marked in the code with comments like `// Corrected on YYYY-MM-DD`.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of configuration files or code repositories. Searching for comments or simple notes that indicate reviews and corrections.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During a review, the review team MUST check whether the requirements are implemented completely, correctly, appropriately, and are up-to-date. The institution MUST correct any identified deviations as quickly as possible. The respective reviews MUST be documented with a change tracking system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Reviews are a planned part of the operational or development process (e.g., annual review of firewall rule sets, peer reviews in the software development cycle). All changes resulting from a review are handled via a formal change management process with a ticket system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the process documentation for operations or development for planned review activities. Random check of tickets in the change management system that relate to review findings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Reviews are systematically conducted using checklists tailored to the specific review subject. The correction of deviations is not only carried out, but a root cause analysis is also performed to prevent future errors. The results of the reviews are collected and used to improve standards and policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Detailed checklists and procedural instructions exist for recurring reviews (e.g., firewall rule review). After correcting a deficiency, a brief "post-mortem" is conducted and documented. The CISO analyzes the review results for trends on a quarterly basis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the review checklists used. Examination of documents on root cause analysis. Review of minutes of meetings in which review results were discussed to improve policy documents.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The review of configurations and documents is largely automated. Tools continuously check for deviations from the desired state (Policy as Code). Identified deviations automatically trigger a workflow for correction and approval. The effectiveness of the review process is measured by key performance indicators (e.g., number of deviations over time).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like Ansible, Puppet, or Terraform in combination with testing frameworks (e.g., InSpec) are used to continuously verify the conformity of systems. A GRC tool or SOAR platform orchestrates the process from deviation detection to documented correction.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check of the configuration of the automation tools (e.g., Ansible Playbooks, InSpec profiles). Live demonstration of the automated correction workflow. Analysis of the KPI reports on the effectiveness of the review process.

controls.title: Integration into the Information Security Process (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Audits and reviews take place in isolation from the rest of the ISMS. The results are noted, but there is no process to systematically feed them back into the ISMS or to manage corrective actions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An audit report is sent to the CISO and filed by them. No measures are derived or tracked. The reports are not considered in the annual management review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Comparison of the findings in audit reports with the action plan of the ISMS. Checking whether the findings have led to actions. Review of the management review documents for mention of audit results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The results of audits and reviews are manually incorporated into the security process. There is a simple list for tracking corrective actions. The results are mentioned in the report to management but are not analyzed in detail.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The CISO maintains an Excel spreadsheet with the findings from audits and the planned corrective actions. The annual report to management mentions the number of audits conducted and the number of deficiencies found.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the Excel spreadsheet for action tracking for currency and completeness. Analysis of the report to management to see the level of detail in which audit results are handled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD provide a policy for internal ISMS auditing and for the management of corrective actions. The results of audits and reviews SHOULD be fed back into the ISMS and improve it. The CISO SHOULD include the conducted audits, their results, and the status of remediation in the regular report to the institution's management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a formal ISMS audit policy and a documented procedure for corrective action management. The results are an integral part of the management review, in which the status of remediation and the improvement of quality are discussed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the policies for auditing and corrective action management. Analysis of the minutes of the management review for the required content regarding audits. Verification that the report to management contains the results and the status of remediation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit and corrective action process is fully integrated into the PDCA cycle of the ISMS. The results of audits flow directly into the risk analysis and the planning of security measures for the next cycle. A ticket system or GRC tool is systematically used for the management of corrective actions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution's GRC tool has dedicated modules for audit management and action tracking. Findings from audits can be directly linked to risks and transferred to the risk treatment plan. The status of all corrective actions can be viewed at any time via a dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the ISMS process description for the integration of the audit process into the PDCA cycle. Live demonstration in the GRC tool of how a finding becomes an action and influences the risk status. Analysis of the dashboards for action tracking.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integration of the audit process is so profound that the results of continuous audits and reviews feed into the risk assessment in real time, enabling dynamic adaptation of the ISMS. The effectiveness of the entire integrated process is measured and optimized using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC platform aggregates results from automated compliance checks (review) and manual audits. A deviation automatically increases the score of an associated risk (KRI). The report to management is an interactive dashboard that visualizes the correlation between audit results, risk status, and the effectiveness of measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Analysis of the GRC tool configuration to verify the automated linking of audit results and risk assessment. Review of the defined KPIs and KRIs for their significance. Inspection of the management dashboards and their historical data.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Audits and reviews are fundamental to any successful Information Security Management System (ISMS). The overall state of information security can only be assessed if established security measures and processes are regularly checked to see if they are still effective, complete, appropriate, and up-to-date. Audits and reviews are therefore a tool for establishing, achieving, and maintaining an appropriate level of security. Through audits and reviews, it is possible to identify security deficiencies and negative trends and to take appropriate countermeasures.
An audit (from Latin audire = to hear, to listen) is a systematic, independent examination of activities and their results. It checks whether defined requirements such as norms, standards, or guidelines are being met. A review (from Latin revidere = to check, to examine) examines whether documents, conditions, objects, or procedures are correct, effective, and appropriate. In contrast to an audit, a review does not necessarily have to be independent. In addition, in the sense of maintenance, a review can also include subsequent improvement.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The DER.3.1 Audits and Reviews module defines requirements for audits and reviews with the aim of improving information security in an institution, avoiding negative trends in this area, and optimizing security measures and processes.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module is to be applied to the entire information network. This concerns internal audits (first-party audits) and reviews as well as audits of the institution's service providers (second-party audits) or other institutions with which the institution has entered into a partnership. Certification audits (third-party audits) are not considered in this module.
Likewise, the IS audit, which is mandatory for federal authorities, is not considered. This is dealt with in module DER 3.2 Audits based on the IS Audit Guideline.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Insufficient or unscheduled implementation of security measures
parts.prose: The level of protection of an institution depends on security measures being implemented completely and correctly. Particularly in the critical phase of projects or under certain framework conditions, it can happen that security measures are temporarily suspended. If it is then forgotten to reactivate them, a security level that is too low can arise.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Ineffective or uneconomical implementation of security measures
parts.prose:
If security measures are implemented without considering certain practical aspects, the measures may be ineffective. For example, it is pointless to block the entrance area with turnstiles if employees can simply enter the building through an open side entrance.
Likewise, individual measures may be taken that are not economically viable. For example, to protect information with a normal level of confidentiality, a cleanly implemented rights and roles concept is more suitable and more economical than complex, certificate-based encryption of the file server.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Insufficient implementation of the ISMS
parts.prose: In many institutions, the Information Security Officer checks for themselves whether security measures have been implemented. However, the audit of the actual ISMS is often forgotten, especially as this should be carried out by independent third parties. As a result, an ISMS's processes may be implemented inefficiently or inappropriately. This can in turn compromise the institution's security level.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Insufficient qualification of the auditors
parts.prose: If the persons who are to carry out an audit or a review are not sufficiently qualified or do not prepare adequately for the audits, they may incorrectly assess the security status of an institution. This could lead to missing or even incorrect corrective measures in the audit report. In the worst-case scenario, this will result in the information being protected at a level that is too high and therefore uneconomical, or too low and therefore very risky.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Lack of long-term planning
parts.prose: If audits and reviews are not planned centrally and for the long term, it may happen that some areas are audited very frequently and others not at all. This makes it very difficult or even impossible to assess the security status of the information network.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Lack of planning and coordination in conducting an audit
parts.prose: If an audit is poorly planned and not sufficiently coordinated with the institution, not all the required persons may be present during the on-site inspection. This may make it impossible to audit individual areas at all. Even if the deadlines for the individual areas have been set too tightly, the investigation may only be carried out superficially because too little time has been scheduled.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Lack of coordination with the staff council
parts.prose: Audits and reviews can also examine aspects from which conclusions can be drawn about the performance of employees. Thus, these audits could be regarded as performance appraisals. If the staff council is not involved, this can lead to violations of the applicable right of co-determination.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.8. Deliberate concealment of deviations
parts.prose: Employees might fear that an audit will uncover their mistakes and therefore try to cover up security problems. This could convey a false picture of the actual status quo.

groups.title: Reviews based on the IS-Revision guideline

controls.title: Designation of persons responsible for the IS revision

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A person has been informally designated as the contact for IS audits, but the responsibilities are neither officially documented nor consistently fulfilled. The planning of audits is done on an ad hoc and reactive basis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The designation has often only been made verbally or recorded in an email. There is no formal job description or documented process for audit planning.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should determine through interviews whether a person is considered responsible. It should be checked whether there is any documentation on role definition or audit planning, although its absence is to be expected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A responsible person for the IS audit is officially designated and anchored in the organizational chart or a role description. The basic tasks such as planning and initiation are defined, but the follow-up on the results is not yet systematic.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The role of the person responsible for IS audits is documented in the security guideline or a separate role description. a simple annual plan for audits is created.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should check for the existence of official documentation on the designation and core tasks of the responsible person. It is to be verified whether a basic audit plan exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution MUST designate a responsible person for the IS audit. This person MUST plan, initiate, and follow up on the results of the IS audits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The designation is made by the institution's management. The tasks, powers, and responsibilities are clearly defined and documented. The follow-up on the results is recorded in a list or a simple tracking system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check whether a responsible person has been officially designated by the management level. It is to be verified whether a documented process for planning, initiating, and following up on IS audits exists and is implemented. This can be done by inspecting the letter of appointment and the follow-up documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The role of the person responsible for IS audit is integrated into the relevant organizational processes (e.g., change management). The person receives regular training and has an allocated budget. The follow-up of findings is systematically carried out in a ticket system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The follow-up on the remediation of deficiencies is managed via a central task or ticket management system (e.g., Jira, OTRS), which makes due dates and responsibilities transparent.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the integration of the role into other processes by reviewing process descriptions. It is to be verified whether a ticket system is used for follow-up. Automated check: A script could query the ticket system's API to generate reports on open and closed audit findings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The role of the person responsible for IS audit is supported by a team and/or specialized GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance) tools. The effectiveness of the audit process itself is measured, evaluated, and continuously improved based on KPIs. The planning and tracking are largely automated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC tool is used to manage the entire audit cycle, from planning and execution to follow-up and reporting. KPIs such as 'time-to-fix' for findings are automatically recorded and reported to management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the use of the GRC tool and the associated process descriptions. The existence and application of KPIs for measuring process effectiveness is to be verified. Automated check: Reports and dashboards from the GRC tool are used as evidence for automated control and monitoring.

controls.title: Creation of an IS audit manual

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An IS audit manual MUST be created for the IS audit, which contains the intended objectives, legal requirements to be complied with, information about the organization, the resources, and the framework conditions. Furthermore, the archiving of the documentation MUST be described therein. The manual MUST be approved by the management level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IS audit manual is maintained as a central document in the ISMS. A template, e.g., from the BSI, is used and adapted to the circumstances of the institution. The approval is given by a verifiable signature or a digital release by the institution's management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check for the existence of an IS audit manual. It is to be verified whether all required contents (objectives, specifications, organization, resources, framework conditions, archiving) are included and whether the manual has been verifiably approved by the management level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IS audit manual is reviewed and updated annually or in the event of significant changes. It also contains detailed process descriptions for various types of audits (e.g., short, cross-sectional audit) as well as templates for audit plans and reports.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The manual is managed in a document management system (DMS) with versioning and a regulated approval process. The annual review is scheduled and documented in the ISMS annual plan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the revision history of the manual. It is to be verified whether a defined process for updating exists and is adhered to. The quality of the included templates and process descriptions is evaluated. Automated check: Logs from the DMS can be used to prove the regular reviews and approvals.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IS audit manual is part of an integrated management framework (e.g., in a GRC tool) and is directly linked to the corresponding processes, roles, and controls. Changes to relevant parts of the ISMS (e.g., new policies) automatically trigger a review of the manual.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The manual is implemented as a digital, interactive guide in the GRC tool or intranet. Hyperlinks lead directly to the relevant policies, process diagrams, and systems. Workflows ensure that all relevant stakeholders are informed about changes and prompted for confirmation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the dynamic linking of the manual with other ISMS artifacts in the GRC tool. It is to be verified whether automated workflows for reviewing and communicating changes have been implemented and are functioning. The effectiveness is verified using examples (e.g., a recent policy change).

controls.title: Definition of the audit basis

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The BSI Standards 200-1 to 200-3 as well as the IT-Grundschutz Compendium MUST be the audit basis for the IS audit. The standard protection of IT-Grundschutz SHOULD be used. These audit bases MUST be known to all participants.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The binding audit bases are explicitly named in the IS audit manual. Before each audit, the participants (auditors and auditees) are demonstrably informed of the valid audit basis, for example in the engagement letter or in the kick-off meeting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check whether the BSI standards and the IT-Grundschutz Compendium are explicitly defined as the audit basis in the IS audit manual. Using random samples from past audits, it is to be verified whether the participants were informed about the audit basis and whether it is referenced in the audit report.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the BSI standards, other relevant regulations (e.g., industry-specific standards, internal guidelines, legal requirements such as the GDPR) are systematically identified and defined and documented as part of the audit basis for specific audits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central library of the relevant regulations is maintained. For each audit, the audit plan explicitly states which additional regulations apply. This selection is made based on the scope of the audit.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether a process for identifying and managing additional relevant regulations exists. It is verified using audit plans whether the selection of the audit basis is appropriate and comprehensible for the respective audit scope.

controls.title: Creation of a plan for the IS audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If the institution is not certified according to ISO 27001 on the basis of IT-Grundschutz, it MUST be ensured that an IS short or cross-sectional audit is carried out at least every three years. In addition, further audits SHOULD be planned if the information network is significantly changed. A multi-year rough plan for the audit projects SHOULD be created. This SHOULD then be specified by an annual detailed plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A multi-year audit plan is created that provides for an IS short or cross-sectional audit at least every three years. This rough plan is converted annually into a detailed audit plan for the coming year, which specifies concrete dates and resources. Significant changes in the information network lead to an ad-hoc review of the plan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check the existence of a multi-year audit plan and the annual detailed plans. It is to be verified that the three-year cycle for short/cross-sectional audits is being adhered to. On a random basis, it is to be checked whether significant changes (e.g., introduction of a new core procedure) have led to an adjustment of the plan.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit planning is risk-based. Areas with a higher need for protection or known vulnerabilities are audited more frequently and intensively. The planning is coordinated with the general audit planning (e.g., financial audit) to leverage synergies and minimize the burden on the audited areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The results from the structural analysis and protection needs assessment of the ISMS flow directly into the prioritization of the audit planning. The coordination with other audit bodies takes place in regular, recorded meetings.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the methodology of risk-based audit planning. It is to be understood how risk information influences the frequency and depth of the planned audits. Minutes of coordination meetings with other audit functions are used as evidence of coordination.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit planning is fully integrated into a GRC tool and is dynamically adjusted. Changes in the institution's risk profile, results from continuous monitoring, or new threat intelligence lead to an automated reassessment and potential adjustment of the audit plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The GRC tool manages the audit plan and adjusts it based on defined triggers. For example, a significant security incident can automatically schedule an ad-hoc audit for the affected area in the plan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the dynamic plan adjustment in the GRC tool. Using test cases or past events, it is verified whether the automated triggers function as intended and have led to a comprehensible adjustment of the audit plan.

controls.title: Selection of a suitable IS audit team

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An IS audit team consisting of at least two persons MUST be assembled or commissioned. The IS audit team MUST be granted an unrestricted right to information and inspection for its activities. For internal IS audit teams, the individual members MUST be impartial. The members of an IS audit team MUST NOT be or have been involved in the planning or implementation of the ISMS.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The selection of the audit team is documented. For internal teams, declarations of impartiality are obtained from the members. The right of inspection is explicitly stated in the engagement letter for the audit and authorized by the institution's management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check whether the audit team consists of at least two persons. The documentation on team selection and the declarations of impartiality are to be checked. Furthermore, it must be verified that the team was not involved in the planning or implementation of the ISMS to be audited. The engagement letter is checked for the granting of the unrestricted right to information.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The members of the IS audit team must have demonstrably the required qualifications and experience (e.g., relevant certifications, proven audit experience). For each audit, a competence matrix is created to ensure that the team covers the specific requirements of the audit subject.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Proof of qualification (certificates, training records) of the team members are collected and managed centrally. Before each audit, the suitability of the team is assessed and documented based on the scope.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the qualification certificates of the audit team members. It must be verified whether the competence of the team was appropriate for the audited matter. The existence and plausibility of the competence matrix is assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a pool of pre-qualified internal and external auditors. The team is assembled according to a formalized process, which also includes a rotation of team members to avoid operational blindness. The performance of the audit team is evaluated after each audit.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A directory of qualified auditors is maintained. The rules for team composition and rotation are defined in the IS audit manual. After completion of an audit, the audited entity and the client fill out a performance evaluation form for the team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the process for managing the auditor pool and the rules for team composition and rotation. It is to be verified whether the performance evaluation of the audit teams takes place and whether the results are used to improve the selection process.

controls.title: Preparation of an IS audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An IS audit team MUST be commissioned to conduct an IS audit. The IS audit team MUST determine which reference documents are required for an IS audit. The institution to be audited MUST provide the security concept and all other required documents to the IS audit team.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The commissioning takes place through a formal engagement letter. The audit team creates a list of requirements for the necessary documents, which is sent to the audited entity. The documents are transferred via a secure channel and this is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check for the existence of a formal audit engagement. It must be verified whether a requirements list for documents was created and whether the requested documents (especially the security concept) were handed over completely and on time. The handover protocol must be inspected.

controls.title: Conducting an IS audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As part of an IS audit, a document review and an on-site inspection MUST be carried out by the IS audit team. All results of these two checks MUST be documented and summarized in an IS audit report. Before an IS cross-sectional audit is carried out for the first time, an IS brief audit MUST be selected as the IS audit procedure. The IS brief audit MUST be completed with a positive vote before an IS cross-sectional audit is carried out.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit is carried out in two phases: first, a review of the submitted documents, followed by an on-site inspection (interviews, site visits, system checks). The findings from both phases are documented in working papers. The rule for the preceding brief audit is taken into account during planning.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check whether both a document review and an on-site inspection have taken place. The working papers and the final audit report are inspected to verify the documentation of the results. It is checked whether the prescribed sequence (brief audit before cross-sectional audit) was followed during the initial implementation.

controls.title: Retention of IS audit reports

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution MUST securely store the IS audit report and its underlying reference documents for at least ten years from the delivery of the report, unless other laws or regulations apply. The institution MUST ensure that only authorized persons can access the IS audit reports and the reference documents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A secure, access-protected archive (physical or digital) is set up for the storage of audit documents. The retention period of ten years is defined in the archiving concept. An authorization concept regulates access to the archive.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor MUST check whether a process for the secure archiving of audit documents exists. On a random basis, it is checked whether reports and reference documents from past audits are available and access-protected. It must be verified that the retention period is being observed. Automated check: Access logs of the digital archive system can be evaluated to identify unauthorized access attempts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audit reports and associated documents are archived in a document management system (DMS) with versioning, immutable storage (WORM principle), and detailed access logging. Deletion after the period expires follows a documented process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DMS with an audit-proof archiving function is used. The retention and deletion periods are configured in the system. A four-eyes principle is applied for the final deletion of documents.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the DMS with regard to audit-proofing and retention periods. The access logs are examined for anomalies. The process for documented deletion is checked. Automated check: A script can query the metadata in the DMS to verify the correct application of the retention rules.

controls.title: Integration into the information security process

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IS audits take place, but their integration into the ISMS process is manual and unstructured. Results are passed on to the ISO, but there is no formal process for feedback into the ISMS or systematic tracking of improvement measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Audit reports are sent to the ISO by email. The ISO decides on an ad hoc basis what information is incorporated into the ISMS documentation. There is no central tracking of measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks through interviews with the ISO how audit results are processed. It is to be investigated whether there is evidence of systematic processing of the results, whereby a lack of formalization is to be expected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be ensured that the results of IS audits are documented and forwarded to the IS management team. The results MUST be taken into account in the further development of the ISMS, and significant findings MUST be included in the ISO's report to the institution's management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a defined process for how audit results are analyzed and fed into the PDCA cycle of the ISMS. This is done, for example, through regular meetings of the IS management team in which audit reports are discussed. Inclusion in the ISO report is a fixed agenda item.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the process description for the processing of audit results. Based on minutes of IS management meetings and past ISO reports, it is verified whether the results are actually handled and reported.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD ensure that IS audits are part of the security process. Furthermore, the results of IS audits SHOULD flow back into the ISMS and contribute to its improvement. Furthermore, the results of the IS audits as well as the activities to remedy deficiencies and to improve quality SHOULD be included in the regular report of the ISO to the institution's management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The results from audits are systematically recorded in a measures tracking system. The effectiveness of the implemented measures is checked after an appropriate period of time. The ISO report contains a dedicated section on the status of audit findings and improvement measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the measures tracking system and the processes documented therein. On a random basis, it is to be verified whether the effectiveness of corrective measures is checked. The quality and completeness of the corresponding section in the ISO report is assessed. Automated check: Reports from the measures tracking system can be used for verification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The feedback of audit results into the ISMS is fully automated via a GRC tool. Findings from audit reports automatically generate tasks for correction and tickets for policy adjustments. The results are incorporated into the reassessment of risks and dynamically influence the ISMS strategy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC tool is used to manage the entire lifecycle of a finding, from identification in the audit to confirmation of effective remediation and adjustment of the risk assessment. Dashboards visualize the status and impact on the entire ISMS in real time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration and workflows in the GRC tool. Using an example, the entire automated process from the finding to the adjustment of the risk assessment is traced. The data integrity and the effectiveness of the automated links are assessed.

controls.title: Communication arrangement

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be clearly regulated how information is exchanged between the IS audit team and the institution to be audited. This SHOULD ensure that this information remains confidential and integer.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The communication channels and means (e.g. encrypted email, secure data rooms) are defined in the IS audit manual or in the audit plan. Fixed contact persons are named on both sides. Confidential documents are classified and treated accordingly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether regulations for secure communication are defined in the audit manual or audit plan. Compliance with these regulations is checked on a random basis, e.g. by inspecting the communication logs or the configuration of the data room used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated, secure collaboration platform or data room is used for information exchange. All communication processes and document transmissions are logged on this platform to ensure traceability.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A platform such as Nextcloud with end-to-end encryption or a commercial virtual data room is set up for each audit. Access is restricted to the involved persons and is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is granted read access to the collaboration platform to verify secure handling and logging. The access logs are checked for correctness and completeness. Automated check: A script can analyze the platform's audit logs to assess access and activity patterns.

controls.title: Conducting a kick-off meeting for an IS cross-sectional audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For an IS cross-sectional audit, a kick-off meeting SHOULD be held between the IS audit team and the institution to be audited. The following topics SHOULD be discussed: Explanation and presentation of the IS audit procedure, introduction of the institution, and handover of the reference documents to the IS audit team.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The kick-off meeting is firmly scheduled at the beginning of each cross-sectional audit. A standardized agenda is used and minutes of the meeting are taken, in which the handover of documents is specifically recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks calendar entries, agendas, and minutes to determine whether the kick-off meeting took place and whether the required topics were covered. In particular, the recorded handover of the reference documents is to be verified.

controls.title: Creation of an audit plan

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before an IS audit, the IS audit team SHOULD create an audit plan. If it becomes necessary during the IS audit to expand or otherwise adjust the planned procedures, the audit plan SHOULD be adjusted accordingly. The audit plan SHOULD also be included in the final IS audit report. For the IS short audit, the BSI's mandatory list of audit topics SHOULD replace the audit plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each audit (except for short audits), a documented audit plan is created that defines the scope, methodology, schedule, and areas to be audited. Changes to the plan during the audit are versioned. The final plan is attached to the audit report as an appendix.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks for the existence and completeness of the audit plans for past audits. It is to be verified whether the plan is included in the final report and whether the BSI audit topic list was used for short audits.

controls.title: Review and examination of documents

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During the document review, the IS audit team SHOULD check the requirements specified in the audit plan. The IS audit team SHOULD verify that all relevant documents are current and complete. It SHOULD be ensured that all essential aspects are covered and that appropriate roles have been assigned. Furthermore, it SHOULD be checked whether the available documents and the decisions made therein are comprehensible. The results of the document review SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The document review is carried out using a checklist derived from the audit plan. The results, including any identified gaps or inconsistencies, are recorded in working papers. These results serve as the basis for planning the on-site audit.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the working papers of the document review. It is verified whether the review was systematic and whether the results are comprehensibly documented. It is checked how the results of the document review were incorporated into the further audit planning (on-site audit).

controls.title: Selection of target objects and requirements to be audited

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In an IS cross-sectional audit or IS partial audit, the IS audit team SHOULD select the module target objects for the on-site audit based on the results of the document review. The ISMS.1 module SHOULD always be audited in its entirety. A further 30% of the modeled module target objects SHOULD be selected on a risk-oriented basis. The selection SHOULD be comprehensibly documented. Of the selected module target objects, 30% of the respective requirements SHOULD be audited. Requirements with deficiencies from previous audits SHOULD also be audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit team documents the selection process for the target objects and requirements in a working paper. The risk-oriented selection is based on the findings of the document review and the results of previous audits. The 30/30 rule is used as a guideline and compliance is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation of the selection process. It is to be verified whether the selection was comprehensible and risk-oriented. It is checked whether ISMS.1 was always audited, whether the 30/30 rule was applied appropriately, and whether previous findings were taken into account.

controls.title: Selection of suitable audit methods

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IS audit team SHOULD ensure that suitable audit methods are used to determine the facts to be audited. All audits SHOULD be proportionate.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the audit plan, the planned audit method (e.g., interview, document inspection, system configuration review, walk-through) is specified for each requirement to be audited. The choice of method is based on effectiveness and proportionality.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the audit plan and working papers to assess the selection and application of the audit methods. It is assessed whether the chosen methods were suitable for obtaining meaningful audit evidence and whether they were proportionate.

controls.title: Creation of a schedule for the on-site audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Together with the institution to be audited, the IS audit team SHOULD develop a schedule for the on-site audit. The results SHOULD be documented together with the IS audit plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed schedule and timetable for the on-site audit is created. It contains the planned interviews with the respective contact persons and the dates for walk-throughs or system checks. The plan is coordinated with the audited institution to ensure the availability of the individuals.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence of the schedule and evidence of coordination with the audited body (e.g., e-mail traffic, minutes). It is assessed whether the plan was realistic and contributed to the smooth execution of the audit.

controls.title: Conducting the on-site audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During the on-site audit, the IS audit team SHOULD investigate and determine whether the selected safeguards adequately and practically meet the requirements of IT baseline protection. The audit SHOULD begin with an opening meeting and end with a closing meeting. All essential facts SHOULD be recorded in writing. The IS audit team SHOULD never actively intervene in IT systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The on-site audit is carried out in a structured manner according to the schedule. Opening and closing meetings are held with the responsible persons and are minuted. All audit activities and findings are documented in working papers. The audit team acts exclusively in an observing and requesting capacity, but does not intervene in systems itself.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the opening and closing meetings and the working papers of the on-site audit. It is to be verified whether the audit was carried out systematically and all essential findings were documented. In particular, it must be ensured that there is no evidence of active intervention by the audit team in the IT systems.

controls.title: Conducting interviews

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Interviews by the IS audit team SHOULD be structured. Questions SHOULD be formulated concisely, precisely, and in an easily understandable manner. In addition, suitable questioning techniques SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit team prepares for interviews by developing questionnaires in advance. During the interview, open-ended questions are used to obtain detailed answers. The results of the interview are minuted and reviewed by the interviewee.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the interview minutes and, if available, the prepared questionnaires. It is assessed whether the interview was conducted professionally and in a structured manner and whether the results were documented in a comprehensible way.

controls.title: Review of the selected risk treatment options

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IS audit team SHOULD check whether the remaining residual risks for the information domain are appropriate and acceptable and whether they are formally accepted by the institution's management. The IS audit team SHOULD verify on a random basis whether and to what extent the selected risk treatment options have been implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the document review, the risk management documentation is analyzed. Special attention is paid to the management's risk acceptance statements. During the on-site audit, it is checked on a random basis whether the measures declared as 'implemented' for risk reduction are actually effective.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the audit working papers to determine whether a review of risk treatment has taken place. It is verified whether the appropriateness of the residual risks was assessed and the implementation of the risk treatment options was checked on a random basis.

controls.title: Follow-up of the on-site audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: After the on-site audit, the collected information SHOULD be further consolidated and evaluated by the IS audit team. After the possibly requested documents, documentation, and additional information have been evaluated, the audited requirements SHOULD be finally assessed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After the on-site phase, the audit team holds an internal meeting to consolidate the results and evaluate the findings. Any ambiguities are clarified by making inquiries with the audited body. Each requirement is finally assessed as 'fulfilled', 'partially fulfilled', or 'not fulfilled' and justified.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the working papers created after the on-site audit. It must be possible to trace how the information was consolidated and how the final assessments of the requirements were derived. The justifications for the assessments are checked for plausibility.

controls.title: Creation of an IS audit report

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IS audit team SHOULD transfer the findings into an IS audit report and document them there in a comprehensible manner. A draft version of the report SHOULD be sent to the audited institution in advance. It SHOULD be verified whether the facts identified by the IS audit team have been recorded correctly. Due to the sensitive information they contain, IS audit reports SHOULD be assigned an appropriate confidentiality classification.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The audit report is created according to a standardized template. The draft is sent to the audited body for comments (only regarding factual correctness). The final report is given a confidentiality classification and distributed to the client via a secure channel.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks past audit reports for completeness and traceability. It is verified whether a process exists for the audited body to comment on the draft and whether the final report has been appropriately classified and protected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be considered to have the IS audit team present the results of the IS audit to the institution's management in the form of a presentation. The audited institution SHOULD ensure that all affected departments within the institution receive the important and necessary passages of the IS audit report within a reasonable timeframe.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: By default, a results presentation for the institution's management is prepared and held after the audit is completed. There is a defined distribution process for the audit report that ensures relevant excerpts are communicated to the affected departments and system owners.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether results presentations for management have taken place (e.g., by reviewing presentation materials and minutes). It is verified whether a distribution process for the report exists and, on a random basis, whether affected parties have received the information relevant to them.

controls.title: Follow-up to an IS audit

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The deviations identified in the IS audit report SHOULD be corrected by the institution within a reasonable time. The corrective measures to be implemented SHOULD be documented with responsibilities, implementation date, and the respective status. The implementation SHOULD be continuously tracked and the implementation status updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution creates an action plan based on the findings of the audit report. This plan is maintained in a list or table and contains a description, a responsible person, a deadline, and a status for each measure. The status is updated at regular intervals (e.g., monthly).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existence and quality of the action plan. It is verified whether all findings from the report are addressed and whether the tracking of measures is actively pursued. The auditor checks on a random basis whether the documented status of the measures is correct.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The tracking of measures is supported by a central ticket or task management system. The effectiveness of the implemented measures is checked by an independent body (e.g., the ISO) before the measure is closed. In principle, it SHOULD be checked whether supplementary IS audits are necessary and the rough and detailed planning for the IS audit should be adjusted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Findings from the audit report are created as tickets in a system like Jira or OTRS. The workflow in the ticketing system includes an explicit step for an effectiveness check before a ticket can be closed. After completion of the measures, the central audit plan is reviewed and adjusted if necessary.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process of tracking measures in the ticketing system. It is verified whether an effectiveness check is implemented and performed. It is checked whether a reassessment of the audit planning takes place after completion of the measures. Automated check: Reports from the ticketing system can prove the lifecycle of measures.

controls.title: OBSOLETE

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: This requirement is obsolete and is no longer applied.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: No measures are required for this requirement, as it is marked as obsolete in current versions of the IT-Grundschutz Compendium. It must be ensured that no old checklists or procedures are used that refer to this requirement.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks that no resources are being spent or measures planned for this outdated requirement. There is no active audit of the requirement itself, but only a verification that it is being treated as obsolete.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
A special form of audit is the Information Security Audit (IS Audit) based on the document Information Security Auditing - A Guideline for IS Auditing based on IT-Grundschutz (short "IS Audit Guideline").

The "IS Audit Guideline" is a document published by the BSI that describes the procedure for IS auditing. Federal authorities are obliged to have their information security management system (ISMS) reviewed by IS audits. Other institutions can, instead of a regular IT audit, carry out an IS audit based on the guideline if they want to review the implementation of their ISMS.

The IS audit based on the guideline is characterized by a holistic approach. This means that all levels of an ISMS are audited, from the structure of an information security organization to personnel aspects to the configuration of IT systems and applications. The economic efficiency and regularity, which are the focus of classic IT audits, are only considered secondarily. Information security (including the appropriateness of the security measures) is thus the essential audit criterion of the IS audit.

The IS audit is an essential component of successful information security management. Only when the established measures and processes for information security are regularly reviewed can it be assessed whether they are effectively implemented, complete, up-to-date, and appropriate. The IS audit is thus a suitable tool to determine, achieve, maintain, and continuously improve an appropriate level of security in an institution.

The main task of the IS audit is to support and accompany the management of the institution, the IS management team, and in particular the ISO, so that they can achieve the highest possible level of information security in the institution.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The module defines requirements for an IS audit with the aim of improving information security in an institution, avoiding undesirable developments in this area, and optimising the security measures and processes.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
This module must always be applied when an institution is obliged to carry out reviews on the basis of the 'IS Review Guide' or wishes to do so voluntarily. The module is to be applied to the entire information network.

It does not take into account how the IS review can be integrated into an existing, higher-level audit organisation of an institution (e.g. internal audit). The DER.3.2 Reviews based on the IS Review Guide module is a concrete implementation of the requirements generally described in the DER.3.1 Audits and Reviews module. Institutions that implement the present module no longer need to implement the DER.3.1 Audits and Reviews module, as its requirements are fully contained in this module.

The IS review and the certification of an ISMS according to ISO 27001 on the basis of IT-Grundschutz are mutually complementary. IS reviews can accompany the path to certification and, in contrast to this, can already be carried out when the security process is initiated in the institution. They show the institution where there is an urgent need for action and which security deficiencies should be dealt with as a priority. If individual information networks of the institution are certified according to ISO 27001 on the basis of IT-Grundschutz, re-certification and IS review for these information networks should be carried out together if possible. Findings from surveillance audits or the certification procedures can be used for the IS review.

If an ISO 27001 certificate on the basis of IT-Grundschutz is available for the entire institution, the surveillance audits required in the certification procedure replace the IS reviews.

The provisions of the protection of classified information and the Federal Security Regulations for Classified Material (VSA) remain unaffected and apply irrespective of the requirements of this module.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Violation of the requirements of the UP Bund
parts.prose: The "Implementation Plan for Ensuring IT Security in the Federal Administration" (UP Bund 2017) is defined as a guideline for information security in the federal administration. Thus, federal authorities are part of a cross-departmental management system for information security in which each authority is responsible for creating and implementing its specific security concept. Not only federal authorities but also other institutions may be obliged by legal, contractual or other regulations to implement the UP Bund 2017. The UP Bund 2017 explicitly states that the BSI standards on information security and IT-Grundschutz as well as the standard protection procedure described therein must be implemented as a minimum requirement. Furthermore, the UP Bund 2017 makes it mandatory for all obligated institutions to regularly review the status of their own ISMS, e.g. by means of a suitable IS audit, and to apply the "Guideline for the Information Security Audit" in doing so. If this is not done, these institutions are in breach of the requirements of the UP Bund.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Suspension of security measures
parts.prose: The security level of institutions is influenced by whether security measures are implemented completely and correctly. Especially in the critical phase of projects or under certain framework conditions, security measures are often temporarily suspended. Sometimes, however, it is then forgotten to reactivate them, so that an insufficiently low security level remains.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Ineffective or uneconomical implementation of security measures
parts.prose:
If security measures are implemented without considering existing practical aspects, these measures may be ineffective. For example, it is pointless to block an entrance area with turnstiles if employees can instead enter the building through an open side entrance.

Similarly, it can happen that individual measures are taken that are not economically viable. For example, for the protection of information with a normal protection requirement regarding confidentiality, an appropriately implemented rights and roles concept is more sensible and economical than setting up a complex, certificate-based encryption on the file server.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Inadequate implementation of the Information Security Management System
parts.prose: In many institutions, the ISO themselves check whether security measures are being implemented. In this context, the audit of the actual ISMS is often forgotten, as the ISO, as part of the ISMS, is not impartial. Consequently, the processes of an ISMS may have been implemented inefficiently or inappropriately, which could have led to an unintentionally low security level for the institution.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Inadequate qualification of the audit team
parts.prose: If the audit team is not sufficiently qualified or does not prepare adequately for the audits, it may incorrectly assess the security status of an institution during an IS audit. In its audit report, it may then recommend unnecessary or even incorrect corrective measures. In this case, it may happen that the information is protected uneconomically or in a very risky manner.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Bias of internal IS audit teams
parts.prose: Within institutions, IS audit teams can be formed from internal staff. If these teams are not sufficiently separated from other processes, they could be influenced or biased. This is particularly the case if members of the IS audit team are or were involved in the planning or implementation of the ISMS.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Lack of long-term planning
parts.prose: If IS reviews are not planned for the long term and centrally, it can happen that individual organizational units of an institution are audited very frequently and others not at all. It is also possible that changes to the ISMS are not sufficiently examined if audits are only carried out irregularly. In this case, it is very difficult or even impossible to adequately assess the security status of the entire information network.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.8. Deficient planning and coordination in the execution of IS audits
parts.prose: If an IS audit is poorly planned and not coordinated with the responsible personnel of the institution, the right people may not be available during the on-site audit. Consequently, it may not be possible to audit individual areas at all. Also, if the deadlines for auditing the individual areas are set too tightly and not enough time is scheduled, the institution might only be audited superficially.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.9. Lack of coordination with the staff council
parts.prose: Within the scope of IS audits, aspects can be examined from which conclusions could be drawn about how individuals behave at work and how productive they are. Thus, these audits could be interpreted as monitoring of behavior and performance. If the staff council is not involved, the on-site audit may be delayed or even canceled.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.10. Intentional concealment of deviations or problems
parts.prose: Individuals might fear that their own mistakes will be uncovered during an IS audit. To avoid this, they might cover up security problems, thus conveying a false picture of the actual security situation. As a result, security deficiencies would remain undetected and could not be corrected. Furthermore, the institution's management could misjudge the risk associated with this security deficiency.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.11. Loss of confidentiality of sensitive information
parts.prose: During an IS audit, confidential information (e.g., vulnerabilities and attack vectors) is collected by the IS audit team. Deficiencies in the information security of the audited institution may also be identified. If these deficiencies become known to unauthorized third parties, they could be used to attack the institution or damage its reputation.

controls.title: Creation of an emergency manual

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are only isolated, unstructured documents for emergencies, such as a simple list of phone numbers. A coherent and complete emergency manual is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, emergency information often exists only in the minds of individual employees or is scattered as loose notes and file collections on personal drives. There is no central, accessible place for this information for everyone.

parts.name: assessment-method
