parts.prose: The auditor asks various employees where to find emergency information. If different, incomplete, or no sources are named, this maturity level is met.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic emergency manual has been created, but it is incomplete, outdated, or not known to all relevant persons. It only covers the most obvious scenarios.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document titled 'Emergency Manual' exists, but it has not been maintained since its initial creation. The contact lists or procedures it contains are no longer up-to-date. It was distributed once via email; new employees do not know about the document.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the emergency manual and checks the currency of its contents on a random basis (e.g., personnel, technical systems). If essential information is outdated or important plans are missing, this maturity level is met.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An emergency manual MUST be created that contains the most important information on roles, immediate measures, alerting and escalation, as well as communication, business continuity, restart, and recovery plans. Responsibilities and authorities MUST be assigned, communicated, and recorded in the emergency manual. It MUST be ensured that trained personnel are available in an emergency. The manual MUST be accessible in an emergency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency manual is maintained as a central document (e.g., in a wiki, on a network drive). Accessibility in an emergency is ensured by also storing it in printed form in secure locations (e.g., safe, home office of emergency team members) and/or on offline media (e.g., USB stick, laptop). The responsibility for updating is clearly regulated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the emergency manual presented to them and checks it for completeness according to the requirement. It is verified that the defined roles are filled and that the contents are known to all relevant persons. The auditor checks the mechanisms intended to ensure accessibility in an emergency (e.g., physical copies).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency manual SHOULD be formally reviewed regularly, at least annually, and updated as needed. The measures described therein SHOULD be regularly tested for functionality through tests and exercises. The manual SHOULD be supplemented with rules of conduct for special cases (e.g., fire, flood) and made known to all employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal review process for the emergency manual is established, which provides for a fixed annual review cycle. The results from emergency exercises are mandatorily incorporated into the updating of the manual. Specific rules of conduct are prepared as information sheets or checklists and published on the intranet, as well as being covered in security training.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the last emergency exercises and compares the resulting 'lessons learned' with the subsequent versions of the emergency manual. It is checked whether a documented process for the regular review of the manual exists and is adhered to.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency manual is integrated into a dynamic emergency management system (BCMS tool). Where possible, content is updated automatically, e.g., by connecting to the HR system for personnel changes. Access is provided via multiple, redundant channels (e.g., a mobile app with an offline cache). The displayed content is role-based and tailored to the user's current situation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Specialized software for business continuity management is used. Personnel data is synchronized via an interface to the Active Directory or HR system. Plans are structured modularly so that in the event of a system failure, the relevant sections are automatically compiled for the affected persons and distributed via an app.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of the BCMS tool with other systems by checking the configuration and testing an automated update. An emergency scenario is simulated to check whether a test user receives the correct, role-based instructions via the mobile app, even if the network connection is disconnected.

controls.title: Integration of Emergency Management and Information Security Management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The roles of the Information Security Officer (ISO) and the Emergency Officer operate in isolation from each other. Coordination only takes place reactively in the event of a serious incident, if at all.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: ISMS and emergency management are treated as completely separate topics. There are no joint meetings or defined information channels. Each area has its own, unsynchronized documents and plans.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews the ISO and the emergency officer separately. If both cannot clearly name the responsibilities of the other and cannot describe established communication channels, this maturity level is met.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Occasional, informal coordination takes place between emergency management and information security management. However, the interfaces and information flows are not formally defined or documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ISO and the emergency officer meet irregularly to exchange information. There is a mutual awareness of each other's tasks, but the escalation paths from a security incident to an emergency are not clearly regulated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for minutes of joint meetings or for documents describing the interface. If such are not available or only in the form of informal email exchanges, this maturity level is met.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The processes in security management MUST be coordinated with emergency management. In particular, the process for handling security incidents (see DER.2.1) must have a clear interface to emergency management to decide when a security incident escalates to an emergency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Regular coordination meetings between the ISO and the emergency officer are institutionalized. In the process for handling security incidents, a clear criterion (e.g., based on impact and urgency) is defined for when the emergency officer is to be involved and the emergency process activated. This interface is documented in writing.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the process documentation of the security incident management (Incident Response Plan) and verifies that it contains a defined interface and escalation criteria to emergency management. In addition, meeting minutes of the coordination meetings are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Joint exercises are conducted that explicitly test the interaction between the security incident team (CSIRT) and the emergency team. The results of these exercises are used to improve both process areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least once a year, an exercise is conducted that begins with the reporting of a security incident (e.g., ransomware) and escalates during the scenario to the declaration of an emergency, in which the emergency team takes the lead. The handover of responsibility and information flows are specifically trained in this process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the exercise plan and the minutes of the last joint exercise. It is checked whether the scenario addressed the interface between ISMS and emergency management and whether the 'lessons learned' were documented and implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The information security management and emergency management processes are mapped in a common management system tool (e.g., GRC tool). The escalation of a security incident to an emergency is an automated workflow in the tool. A common operational picture is provided in real time by an integrated dashboard.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) tool is linked to the BCMS tool. When an incident in the SOAR tool reaches a certain criticality level, an emergency ticket is automatically created in the BCMS tool and the emergency team is alerted. Status updates are synchronized between the systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the tool integration demonstrated. The manual triggering of a test security incident in the source system is used to verify that the automated workflow for creating an emergency in the target system functions correctly and that the operational picture is updated accordingly.

controls.title: Definition of scope and emergency management strategy

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The scope for the emergency management system MUST be clearly defined. The institution's management MUST define an emergency management strategy that outlines the intended goals and the risk acceptance level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal document is created that clearly defines the scope (e.g., which locations, processes, organizational units are included). Another document approved by management describes the strategy, e.g., 'We will restore the production of product X within 24 hours'. The risk acceptance level is described qualitatively (e.g., 'Outages of more than 3 days are not acceptable for critical processes').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documents on the scope and the emergency management strategy approved by the institution's management. It is checked whether these documents are clear and understandable and whether the risk acceptance level is defined.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency management strategy SHOULD be reviewed annually and adapted to the overarching business strategy. The risk acceptance level SHOULD be quantified. The scope SHOULD be regularly validated based on the business impact analysis (BIA).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The review of the strategy becomes a fixed item on the institution's management's annual agenda. The risk acceptance level is substantiated with concrete key figures such as maximum tolerable downtime (MTD) and maximum tolerable data loss (RPO) for process categories. After each update of the BIA, the defined scope of the emergency management system is cross-checked against the results and adjusted if necessary.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the management meetings to verify the annual review of the strategy. It is checked whether the results of the BIA were demonstrably used to validate the scope and whether the risk acceptance level is supported by quantitative values.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Scope and strategy are dynamically managed in a BCMS tool and are linked to the enterprise risk management process. The strategy includes quantitative RTO/RPO specifications derived from the BIA at the process level, which are regularly reviewed against changing threats and business requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BCMS tool visualizes the scope and the dependencies between processes, applications, and IT systems. Changes in the BIA lead to an automated review workflow for the affected strategy elements. Scenario analyses are used to simulate the effectiveness of the strategy under different assumptions (e.g., failure of a cloud provider).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown in the BCMS tool how a change in the criticality of a business process in the BIA triggers a process to review the associated continuity strategy. Reports from the tool are viewed that demonstrate compliance with the RTO/RPO specifications from exercises.

controls.title: Guideline on emergency management and assumption of overall responsibility by the institution's management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution's management MUST adopt a guideline on emergency management that contains the essential key points. This guideline MUST be communicated to all employees. The institution's management MUST assume overall responsibility for emergency management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution's management signs a formal policy document. This document is published on the intranet and communicated to the staff as part of a general announcement. The policy explicitly states the overall responsibility of the management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the emergency management guideline signed by management. It is checked whether and how this guideline was communicated (e.g., by inspecting the corresponding intranet page or circular email).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency management guideline SHOULD be reviewed regularly, e.g., annually, and revised if necessary. The communication SHOULD be supplemented by targeted training or information measures for different employee groups.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review date for the guideline is anchored in the calendar of the institution's management. The communication of the guideline is not only done passively via the intranet, but is also actively discussed in management meetings and team meetings. New employees are informed about the guideline as part of their onboarding.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the version history of the guideline and the minutes of the management reviews to verify the regular review. In addition, random checks are carried out on employees (especially managers) to determine the level of awareness of the guideline.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The guideline is embedded in the organization's integrated management system. The institution's management actively demonstrates its responsibility through visible participation in emergency exercises and through the regular, critical review of the performance of the emergency management system using key performance indicators.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency management guideline is part of a comprehensive policy framework that also covers information security, quality, etc. The management actively participates in a staff exercise at least once a year. The performance of the BCMS is a fixed agenda item in regular management reporting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews participant lists and minutes of emergency exercises for the participation of members of the institution's management. Management dashboards and reports are examined to verify that the performance of the emergency management system is regularly addressed at the management level.

controls.title: Establishment of a suitable organizational structure for emergency management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The roles for emergency management MUST be appropriately defined for the circumstances of the institution. This MUST be documented in writing with the tasks, duties, and competencies of the roles. Qualified employees MUST be appointed for all roles in emergency management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An organizational chart for the emergency organization is created and documented in the emergency manual. For each role (e.g., emergency officer, crisis team leader, recovery team), there is a written role description. The appointed persons are officially appointed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the emergency organization (organizational chart, role descriptions). It is checked on a random basis whether the appointed persons know their role and their tasks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The organizational structure in emergency management SHOULD be regularly checked to see if it is practical, effective, and efficient. Qualified deputies SHOULD be appointed and trained for all key roles.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After every major exercise or real emergency, the effectiveness of the organizational structure is evaluated in the 'lessons learned' session. For each key role in the emergency team, at least one deputy is appointed who undergoes the same training as the role holder.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documentation of the emergency organization for the appointment of deputies. The minutes of the 'lessons learned' sessions are reviewed to verify that the organizational structure is regularly evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency organization is tested for its resilience in realistic, large-scale exercises. The performance of the role holders is evaluated and flows into individual training plans. The structure is demonstrably scalable to handle different types and sizes of emergencies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency organization is modular (e.g., core crisis team, extended crisis team, specialist teams) so that it can be flexibly assembled depending on the emergency scenario. Performance in exercises is evaluated based on predefined criteria and is part of the personnel development for the employees concerned.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the exercise plan to check whether exercises with different scaling and complexity are carried out. Individual development plans of members of the emergency team are reviewed on an exemplary basis to check whether the results from exercise evaluations are taken into account there.

controls.title: Provision of adequate resources for emergency management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The financial, technical, and personnel resources for the intended goals of emergency management MUST be adequate. The emergency officer or the emergency management team MUST have sufficient time for the tasks in emergency management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the annual budgeting process, a separate budget for emergency management (e.g., for external consulting, training, tool licenses, emergency equipment) is requested and approved. The members of the emergency team are officially assigned a specific amount of time for their tasks in emergency management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the approved budget plan and checks whether a budget for emergency management is shown. The job descriptions or target agreements of the members of the emergency team are reviewed to verify the assigned time quotas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Resource planning SHOULD be a formal process based on the approved strategy and planned activities (e.g., BIAs, exercises). The adequacy of the resources SHOULD be reviewed annually by management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency officer prepares a detailed resource plan annually, which derives the requirements for the coming year based on the tasks to be performed (e.g., updating BIA, conducting 3 exercises, training 20 employees). This plan is submitted to management for approval as part of the management review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the resource planning for emergency management for the current and upcoming year and checks whether it is comprehensibly derived from the objectives and planned tasks. The minutes of the management review are inspected to verify the review and approval by management.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Resource allocation is based on a risk-based approach. Business cases for major investments in resilience are created and evaluated by management. The effectiveness of resource deployment is measured and reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For investment decisions (e.g., setting up a redundant data center), a formal business case calculation is created that compares the costs of the measure with the potentially avoided damage (based on the BIA). The performance of the BCMS is measured using key performance indicators (e.g., adherence to RTOs in exercises) to evaluate the effectiveness of the invested resources.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews a sample business case for a major resilience investment and checks whether it is based on the results of the risk analysis and BIA. The management reports are inspected to check whether the effectiveness of the resource deployment is evaluated and reported using key performance indicators.

controls.title: Creation of an emergency concept

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An emergency concept MUST be created. For this, all critical business processes and resources MUST be identified, for example with a Business Impact Analysis (BIA). The most important risks for these MUST be identified and assessed. Continuity strategies MUST be developed to enable a restart and recovery within the required time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A BIA is conducted and the results (critical processes, RTOs, RPOs) are documented. Based on this, a high-level emergency concept is written that defines the fundamental strategies (e.g., 'we use cold standby for IT systems', 'we qualify deputies for personnel shortages') and refers to the emergency plans to be created.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the BIA and the emergency concept derived from it presented. It is checked whether the concept addresses all critical processes and whether plausible continuity strategies have been defined for the identified risks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The BIA SHOULD be a recurring process that is updated regularly (e.g., annually). The emergency concept SHOULD take information security into account and corresponding security concepts SHOULD be developed for the emergency solutions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BIA is formally included in the annual plan for emergency management. For each emergency solution (e.g., alternate workspaces, emergency IT system), a separate, brief risk assessment is conducted and a security concept is created that addresses aspects such as access control, confidentiality, and data integrity in the emergency situation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the BIA has been updated in the last 12-18 months. It is checked on a sample basis for an emergency solution whether a corresponding security concept exists that addresses the specific risks in emergency operation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency concept is a living document that is continuously updated through an established BCMS process. It is closely interlinked with risk management and the security architecture. Continuity strategies are regularly tested and optimized for their effectiveness and cost-efficiency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Changes to critical systems or processes in the change management process automatically trigger a review workflow for the BIA and the emergency concept. The selected continuity strategies are not only documented but also validated in exercises to ensure that the RTO/RPO requirements can actually be met. Alternative strategies are periodically evaluated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor tracks a change request for a critical system and verifies that it has resulted in an update of the BIA and the emergency concept. Exercise logs are reviewed to check whether the selected strategies have achieved the goals (RTO/RPO) defined in the BIA.

controls.title: Integration of employees into the emergency management process

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All employees MUST be regularly made aware of the topic of emergency management. There MUST be a training and awareness concept. The employees in the emergency management team MUST be trained regularly to build up the necessary competencies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A training concept is created that distinguishes between general awareness for all employees (e.g., annual mandatory training in the e-learning system) and specific training for the emergency team (e.g., external crisis management training). A plan specifies who receives which training and when.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the training and awareness concept and the training plan. Training records (participant lists, certificates) for the members of the emergency team and records of the implementation of general awareness measures are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training concept SHOULD include different modules for different target groups (regular employees, managers, emergency team). The success of the training SHOULD be measured, e.g., through knowledge tests or active participation in exercises. The awareness measures SHOULD be varied.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the general training, there is a briefing for managers on their special tasks in an emergency. The e-learning modules end with a test that must be passed. Awareness is raised not only via email but also through posters, intranet articles, or short videos.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the different training materials for the various target groups. The results of the knowledge tests are evaluated. Participation in emergency exercises is used as proof of practical training.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Emergency management tasks are anchored in the job descriptions and target agreements for relevant roles. The training is practice-oriented and includes participation in realistic exercises. A culture of resilience is actively promoted throughout the entire organization.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For members of the crisis management team, successful participation in an annual staff exercise is part of their individual target agreement. Training focuses on practical skills through simulations and exercises rather than on purely theoretical knowledge transfer. Corporate communication regularly conveys messages that emphasize the importance of preparedness and resilience.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews samples of the job descriptions and target agreements of members of the emergency team. It is checked whether the training plan has a high proportion of practical exercises. The auditor evaluates internal communication (intranet, newsletter) for contributions promoting a culture of resilience.

controls.title: Integration of emergency management into organization-wide procedures and processes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be ensured that aspects of emergency management are considered in all business processes and specialist tasks of the institution. The processes, specifications, and responsibilities in emergency management MUST be coordinated with risk management and crisis management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Workshops are held with the owners of critical business processes to discuss emergency aspects and include them in the process documentation. There are defined interfaces and regular meetings with those responsible for risk management and crisis management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly inspects the documentation of critical business processes and checks whether aspects of emergency management (e.g., procedure in case of system failure) are described there. The minutes of the coordination meetings with risk and crisis management are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Emergency management SHOULD be a mandatory part of the change management process. New projects or systems SHOULD have an approved continuity concept before going live.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The change management process form is extended with a mandatory field or a checklist on the topic of 'Impact on Emergency Management'. The emergency officer is part of the Change Advisory Board (CAB) or must explicitly approve changes to critical systems. Project management guidelines require a 'Business Continuity' chapter in the project closure document.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documentation of the change management process. Several completed changes for critical systems are examined to see if an assessment of the emergency relevance has taken place. For a new project, it is checked whether a continuity concept has been created.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Requirements for fault tolerance and recoverability (Resilience Requirements) are firmly anchored in the corporate architecture. A 'Business Continuity by Design' principle is applied. The BCMS is fully integrated into the organization's Integrated Management System (IMS).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Enterprise Architects have standardized architecture patterns for different resilience levels (e.g., highly available, fast recovery), which must be used mandatorily when designing new applications. BCM aspects are part of the internal and external audits of the IMS.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the corporate architecture specification documents for resilience requirements. The IMS audit program is checked to see if BCM is a regular audit subject. It is checked whether the results of the BCM audits are addressed in the IMS management review.

controls.title: Tests and emergency drills

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All essential immediate measures and emergency plans MUST be tested and drilled in an appropriate manner, both regularly and on an ad-hoc basis. The time frame and the technical scope of all drills MUST be documented comprehensively in a drill plan. Sufficient resources MUST be provided in emergency management for the planning, conception, execution, and evaluation of the tests and drills.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual drill plan is created that specifies which emergency plan (e.g., 'Restart ERP system', 'Building evacuation') is tested, when, and in what form (e.g., as a tabletop exercise). Time and, if necessary, money are planned in the budget for its execution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the drill plan for the current and past year. It is checked whether the planned drills have taken place by inspecting logs or other evidence. It is checked whether essential plans are included in the plan.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The drill plan SHOULD cover a variety of drill types (e.g., plan review, technical test, simulation exercise) and scenarios that progressively increase in complexity. The results of the drills SHOULD be documented, and a process for tracking potential improvements (lessons learned) SHOULD be established.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The drill plan is designed for several years and provides for starting with simple drills (e.g., alert test) and progressing to more complex drills (e.g., functional exercise). For each drill, there is a formal log with a 'Lessons Learned' section, in which improvement measures with responsible persons and deadlines are recorded. Their implementation is tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the exercise plan and assesses whether it shows a meaningful increase in complexity and variety. Multiple exercise logs are examined to verify that a structured 'lessons learned' process exists and that the implementation of measures is tracked (e.g., via a ticketing system).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A multi-year exercise strategy is established, culminating in full-scale exercises that also involve external partners (e.g., critical service providers, authorities). The test results feed directly into the BCMS strategy and resource planning. Technical tests are automated where possible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A major crisis management team exercise is conducted every two to three years, which includes simulating the failure of a major cloud provider and involving their representative in the exercise. If an exercise shows that an RTO cannot be met, this leads to a re-evaluation of the continuity strategy and, if necessary, an investment proposal. The failover of cluster systems is tested nightly and logged using automated scripts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the exercise strategy and the logs of exercises in which external parties were involved. An example is tracked in which a negative exercise result led to a demonstrable change in strategy or budget. The logs of the automated failover tests are checked.

controls.title: Documentation in the Emergency Management Process

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The workflow of the emergency management process, the work results of the individual phases, and important decisions MUST be documented. An established procedure MUST ensure that these documents are updated regularly. Furthermore, access to the documentation MUST be restricted to authorized personnel.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All emergency management documents (BIA, concept, plans, etc.) are stored in a central, access-protected location (e.g., a network drive with a permission group). A document lists all emergency documents with their owner and the next planned review date.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the central document repository demonstrated and checks the access permissions. The directory of emergency documents is inspected to check whether a procedure for updating has been established.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A document management system (DMS) with version control, approval workflows, and detailed access control SHOULD be used. An annual review of all key documents SHOULD be mandatory.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Emergency documents are managed in a system such as SharePoint or a dedicated DMS. Changes to documents must go through a formal approval process (e.g., approval by the emergency officer). The system automatically archives old versions. The review process is supported by automatic reminders to the document owners.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the version history and the approval workflow of an emergency plan demonstrated in the DMS. It is checked whether the system configuration ensures that only authorized persons can make changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation is largely generated from a central BCMS tool to ensure consistency. An audit trail logs all changes and decisions completely. The documentation is available on a high-availability platform that is also accessible in an emergency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Instead of writing plans in Word, data (processes, systems, contacts, measures) is maintained in the BCMS tool. If required, the tool generates the current plans in PDF format from this data. The BCMS tool itself is implemented as a high-availability SaaS solution and offers a mobile app for offline access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the BCMS tool demonstrate how a change to a contact is automatically updated in all relevant plans. The tool's audit trail is checked for completeness. The availability and functionality of offline access is tested.

controls.title: Review and Control of the Emergency Management System

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution's management MUST regularly inform itself about the status of emergency management based on management reports. They MUST thus regularly review, evaluate, and, if necessary, correct the emergency management system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency officer prepares an annual or semi-annual status report that summarizes the activities of the last period (e.g., exercises conducted, plans updated). This report is submitted to and discussed with the institution's management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the management reports for the last two years and the minutes of the corresponding management meetings. It is checked whether the reports were prepared regularly and demonstrably addressed by the management.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management reviews SHOULD be conducted based on a formal agenda and predefined key performance indicators (KPIs). Decisions made SHOULD be documented and the resulting measures tracked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal management review for the BCMS is established. The agenda is standardized and includes items such as 'Performance Indicators', 'Results from Exercises and Audits', 'Resource Situation', and 'Improvement Measures'. Decisions and measures are recorded in a measure tracking system (e.g., a ticket system) and their status is reported in the next review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the agendas and minutes of the management reviews. It is checked whether the reviews are based on key performance indicators and whether a formal process for tracking measures has been established and is being used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management review is an integral part of the organization's governance cycle. It uses a dashboard with real-time data on the performance of the BCMS. The review process itself is subject to internal audit to ensure its effectiveness.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The management review is supported by a live dashboard in the BCMS tool, which displays the current status of plans, measures, and key performance indicators. The internal audit department checks every two years whether the management review is conducted effectively and whether management is fulfilling its management and control obligations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the management dashboard demonstrated live. The reports of the internal audit that dealt with the management review process are inspected.

controls.title: Regular review and improvement of emergency measures

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All emergency measures MUST be reviewed regularly or in the event of major changes to determine whether they are still being complied with and correctly implemented, and whether they are still suitable for achieving the defined objectives. In the event of deviations, the causes MUST be determined and improvement measures initiated. The reviews in the areas of audit, IT, security management, and emergency management MUST be coordinated with each other.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual audit plan is created that specifies which emergency measure will be audited and when. The audit is carried out by the emergency officer or by internal/external auditors. A coordination meeting between the auditing bodies takes place annually to avoid duplicate audits and to leverage synergies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the audit plan and the audit reports for the last period. It is checked whether a process for root cause analysis and measure tracking for identified deficiencies exists. The minutes of the coordination meetings of the auditing bodies are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For identified deficiencies, a structured root cause analysis SHOULD be performed. The improvement measures SHOULD be tracked centrally in a system. The overview of results SHOULD be approved by the institution's management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Identified deficiencies are not only rectified, but their actual cause is systematically investigated (e.g., using the 5 Whys method) to prevent recurrence. All deficiencies and the resulting improvement measures are recorded in a ticketing system and tracked until they are resolved. Management receives a quarterly report for their information on the most important deficiencies and the status of improvements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor selects an identified deficiency from an audit report and checks whether a documented root cause analysis has been performed. The ticketing system is inspected to verify the tracking of the measures. The management reports are checked for reporting on deficiencies.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A continuous improvement process (CIP, e.g., based on PDCA) is fully implemented for all emergency measures. The effectiveness of the measures is measured with quantitative metrics. Automated compliance checks are used to continuously verify the configuration of technical measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BCMS follows a documented PDCA cycle, which is evaluated in the management review. The effectiveness of a backup solution is not only assessed by test restores (planned), but also by the metric 'success rate of nightly backup jobs' (measured). A configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) automatically checks daily whether the configuration of the emergency systems complies with the specifications and reports deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the documentation of the CIP for the BCMS demonstrated. The reports of the quantitative metrics and the automated compliance checks are inspected. It is checked whether the results of these measurements demonstrably lead to improvement measures.

controls.title: Assessment of the performance of the business continuity management system

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be regularly assessed how powerful and effective the emergency management system is. As a basis, measurement and evaluation criteria such as key performance indicators MUST be defined. These metrics MUST be determined regularly and compared with suitable previous values. In the event of negative deviations, the causes MUST be determined and improvement measures defined. The results of the assessment MUST be reported to management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Some basic key performance indicators (KPIs) are defined, e.g., 'Number of exercises conducted per year', 'Update level of emergency plans in %', 'Number of trained employees'. These KPIs are manually recorded in an Excel spreadsheet and compared with the previous year's value in the annual management report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the definition of the key performance indicators and the data collection sheets or tables demonstrated. It is checked whether the data is plausible and whether the comparisons and evaluations are included in the management report.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive set of KPIs SHOULD be defined that covers all aspects of the BCMS (e.g., BIA timeliness, RTO compliance in tests, budget utilization). These SHOULD not only be compared with previous year's values, but also with defined target values. Based on the evaluation, management SHOULD decide on the measures with which the system will be further developed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A KPI catalog is developed that defines a target value, a threshold value, and the collection cycle for each key figure. Example: KPI 'RTO compliance in recovery tests', target value '> 95%'. The KPI evaluation is a fixed component of the management review. The management's decisions on further development are recorded in the minutes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the KPI catalog and checks whether it is meaningful and comprehensive. The reports on KPI achievement and the minutes of the management reviews are examined to verify that management makes controlling decisions based on the KPIs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Performance measurement is automated and presents the results in a real-time dashboard. The BCMS is externally benchmarked or certified according to a standard such as ISO 22301 to obtain an objective assessment of its performance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BCMS tool collects data from various sources (exercises, audits, change management) and calculates the KPIs automatically. The result is visualized in a management dashboard. The organization has its BCMS certified by an accredited body according to ISO 22301 and undergoes annual surveillance audits.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests a live demonstration of the KPI dashboard in the BCMS tool. The valid ISO 22301 certificate and the reports of the last external audits are used as proof of the system's performance.

controls.title: Emergency preparedness and response planning for outsourced components

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In emergency preparedness and response planning for outsourced components, the emergency management of the supplying or servicing institution MUST be regularly reviewed in the signed contracts. The procedures in emergency tests and exercises MUST be coordinated with the supplying or providing institution. The results and evaluations MUST be exchanged regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Clauses on emergency management are included in the contracts with critical service providers (e.g., obligation to submit the emergency concept, right to participate in exercises). Regular (e.g., annual) service management meetings are held, in which BCM topics are also discussed and exercise results are exchanged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the contracts with critical service providers for clauses on emergency management. The minutes of the service management meetings are reviewed to verify the regular exchange.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Procedures in emergency tests and exercises SHOULD, where appropriate, be carried out jointly with the supplying or providing institution. The organization SHOULD contractually secure the right to audit the BCM capabilities of the service provider.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least once a year, a joint exercise is conducted with the most critical service provider, during which the communication and escalation paths in an emergency are tested. An audit right is anchored in the contracts, which allows the organization to check the emergency plans and the infrastructure of the service provider (or its certifications).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the exercise plan and the minutes of a joint exercise with a service provider. It is checked whether use is made of the contractual audit rights by inspecting the corresponding audit reports or certificate checks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive supply chain continuity management program is established. This includes a risk assessment of the entire supply chain, not just the direct service providers (Tier-1). Exit strategies and alternative service providers are identified and pre-qualified for critical services.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An analysis of dependencies in the supply chain is carried out to identify concentration risks (e.g., several critical service providers use the same cloud hyperscaler). In the event of a critical SaaS provider failure, a plan for data extraction and migration to a predefined alternative provider is in place and has already been tested.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks to see the documentation of the supply chain risk analysis. For a critical service provider, the existence and plausibility of the exit strategy is checked, ideally by inspecting the records of a corresponding test.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
In emergencies, institutions must be able to continue accessing information in order to restore a business process, an IT system, or a specialist task. To maintain information security in an emergency, appropriate processes should therefore be planned, established, and reviewed.
Optimal emergency preparedness and response is only possible if a planned and organised approach is taken. A professional emergency management process reduces the impact of an emergency and thus secures the operation and continued existence of the institution. Suitable measures must be identified and implemented to make time-critical business processes and specialist tasks more robust and resilient. On the other hand, these measures should also make it possible to manage an emergency quickly and in a targeted manner.
Maintaining information security in an emergency must be integrated into an overarching emergency management system, ideally into an emergency management system. However, emergency management has its own process owner, the emergency officer, who coordinates with the IS officer.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The goal of this module is to describe requirements for ensuring information security in institutions even in critical situations. For this purpose, the corresponding measures must be embedded in a holistic emergency management system. In addition, all aspects that are necessary to maintain information security even in the event of damaging events or emergencies must be considered. This ranges from planning to the review of all processes.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module DER.4 Emergency Management must always be applied once for the entire information network.
If a damaging event occurs, the right information must be available completely and correctly. This module does not explain criteria or processes by which those responsible can decide whether an emergency exists or not. This decision is made while the security incident is being handled (see DER.2.1 Handling of Security Incidents).
Crises are considered within the framework of a separate crisis management and are only treated as an interface in this module, e.g. in the context of further escalation of emergencies. Further information on the individual phases of emergency management and the distinction between emergency management and crisis management can be found in BSI Standard 100-4 'Emergency Management'.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Staff absence
parts.prose: If personnel are absent, it can quickly mean that an institution can no longer perform its specialized tasks and business processes. The reasons for personnel absence can be varied. For example, many employees can be absent at the same time due to germs in the canteen or a strike. The death of an employee can also lead to failures or impairments of important business processes or specialized tasks. In addition, relevant information for restarting the business process or IT systems may no longer be accessible. Often, individuals have specific expert knowledge (knowledge monopolies), so that damage can also occur if the personnel absence is numerically very small.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Failure of IT systems
parts.prose: If components of an IT system fail, e.g., due to defective hardware or a power outage, the entire IT operation can be disrupted. This jeopardizes the availability of the respective information and thus also of the respective business process. In addition, important information needed for restart measures may not be available.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Failure of a wide area network (WAN)
parts.prose: The causes for the failure of a wide area network (WAN) can be diverse. Therefore, it is possible that a network outage only affects individual users, a provider, or a specific region. Often, such outages are only brief and then only affect the business processes and specialized tasks that require a correspondingly high availability of the WAN. However, there are also always longer outages that can lead to massive problems in communication and accessibility.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Failure of a building
parts.prose: Buildings can become unexpectedly unusable, e.g., because they have been partially or completely destroyed by fire, storm, flood, earthquake, or an explosion. However, a building can also fail because the police or fire department cordons off the area and the building can no longer be entered or must be evacuated, for example, because electricity, water, sewage, heating, or air conditioning no longer function for a certain period of time.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Failure of a delivery or service
parts.prose: If institutions are dependent on services, this can quickly lead to interruptions in their own business continuity if the service-providing or delivering institution fails partially or completely. For example, if the delivery of a specific material is required for production and this delivery fails, the entire production may be at risk. But the failure of an externally provided service, such as a cloud or even email, can also severely restrict or even completely interrupt one's own operations. This particularly endangers critical business processes and specialized tasks.

controls.title: Restricting Active Content (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an instruction or recommendation that users should disable the automatic execution of Active Content (macros) in Office applications. However, this setting is not centrally managed or monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Implementation is done through a one-time communication, e.g., via email, to the employees. No technical enforcement measures are taken. The responsibility lies entirely with the individual user.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews a sample of users to determine if they are aware of the instruction to disable Active Content and if they have implemented it. It is checked whether a corresponding written communication exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The automatic execution of Active Content is disabled by default on all systems in Office applications. Users are notified for documents with macros and must manually confirm the execution for each document. There is no distinction based on the origin of the sources.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default setting 'Disable all macros with notification' is set during client installation. However, there is not yet a central, mandatory policy (e.g., GPO) that prevents users from changing this setting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies on a sample of client systems that the default configuration for disabling macros is set. It is checked whether users receive a security warning when opening a document with macros. An automated check can read the corresponding registry keys on the clients.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The function that automatically executes embedded Active Content MUST be disabled centrally and in a way that users cannot change. If it is necessary to execute Active Content, care MUST be taken to ensure that it is only executed if it comes from defined trusted sources. All users MUST be instructed on the risks and the secure procedure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Deactivation is enforced for the entire organization using Group Policies (GPO). 'Trusted sources' are defined via 'Trusted Locations' (e.g., specific network drives) or through digitally signed macros from trusted publishers. User instruction is provided as part of regular security awareness training.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the relevant Group Policies. It is checked whether the list of trusted locations and publishers is documented and handled restrictively. The training materials and participant lists are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to central deactivation, all attempts to execute Active Content from untrusted sources are logged and reported to a central monitoring system. The list of trusted sources is regularly reviewed and reduced to the necessary minimum.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Windows Defender for Endpoint or a comparable EDR solution is used to monitor the execution of macros. SIEM rules are configured to trigger alarms for suspicious activities (e.g., frequent execution attempts by a user). The process for reviewing trusted sources is documented and is carried out quarterly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the SIEM configuration and the generated alarms. The logs of the reviews of the trusted sources are inspected. It is randomly checked whether log entries are generated for corresponding test actions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The execution of any Active Content is generally blocked, unless it is explicitly approved by a combination of a digital signature from an internal, strictly managed certificate service AND the origin from a trusted location. All other documents, especially from external sources, are automatically cleaned in a sandbox environment (Content Disarm and Reconstruction, CDR) before being delivered to the user.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A strict application whitelisting policy for macros is implemented. A CDR solution, integrated into the email gateway, proactively removes all active content from incoming documents and reconstructs the files. Only absolutely necessary exceptions are granted via a formal approval process with a four-eyes principle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the CDR solution and the application whitelisting rules. The process for signing and approving macros is checked. As a test, documents with unsigned macros are sent from external sources to check the effectiveness of the cleaning.

controls.title: Securely opening documents from external sources (B) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Antivirus software with a basic configuration is installed on the endpoints, which scans incoming files. There are no specific policies or instructions for handling external documents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The antivirus solution is rolled out as part of the standard client image. The manufacturer's default signatures are used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the installation and operation of the antivirus software on a sample of clients. It is checked whether the virus signatures are up to date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All documents obtained from external sources must be checked for malware before opening. This is ensured by a centrally managed antivirus solution on the endpoints and at the email gateway. Users are instructed not to open suspicious attachments.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A centrally managed endpoint protection solution is installed on all clients. In addition, an email security gateway scans all incoming attachments. Users are made aware of the dangers as part of security awareness.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the email gateway and the endpoint protection solution. It is checked whether all systems are connected to the central management. The content of the awareness campaign is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All documents obtained from external sources MUST be checked for malware before they are opened. All file formats classified as problematic and all those not needed within the institution MUST be prohibited. If possible, they SHOULD be blocked. Technical measures SHOULD be used to enforce that documents from external sources are checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A strict file type filtering based on a whitelist of allowed formats is enforced at the email gateway and/or proxy. Unnecessary or known high-risk file types (e.g., .js, .pif, .scr) are blocked. In addition to virus scanning, a sandboxing analysis is performed for unknown or potentially dangerous file types (e.g., Office documents, PDFs).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the file type filter at the gateway/proxy. The list of blocked/allowed file types is checked for appropriateness. The configuration of the sandbox analysis is checked. As a test, an attempt is made to receive blocked file types.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All documents from external sources are mandatorily opened in a protected mode (Protected View). This mode prevents editing and the execution of active content. Users can only disable the protection after a deliberate action. This setting is centrally configured and cannot be permanently disabled by users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The 'Enable Protected View for files from the Internet' setting is enforced via GPO for all Office applications. Disabling the protection is logged and forwarded to a SIEM system for analysis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the corresponding GPO setting. A test is performed to see if a document from the Internet (e.g., an email attachment) is opened in Protected View. The log entries in the SIEM are checked when the protection is disabled for a test.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All documents from external sources are proactively stripped of all potentially dangerous content (macros, scripts, external links) by a Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR) solution before delivery to the user. Alternatively or additionally, such documents are opened exclusively in a completely isolated container or virtualization environment (e.g., Microsoft Defender Application Guard) that has no access to the host system or the internal network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A CDR solution is placed upstream of the email gateway and the web proxy. For cases where original documents are needed, Application Guard for Office is enabled for all users via GPO. Users are trained to use this environment exclusively for documents from untrusted sources.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the CDR solution by sending test documents with active content from an external source and checks whether it is removed. The GPO configuration for Application Guard is checked and it is verified on a test client that an external document is opened in the container.

controls.title: Awareness of specific Office properties (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is some information, for example on the intranet, about the risks of handling Office documents, such as macro viruses.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: One or two articles containing general security advice are published on the intranet portal. There is no targeted campaign or training.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor searches the intranet for the relevant information pages and assesses their content and visibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All users are informed about the basic dangers of active content in Office files and how to handle documents from external sources as part of a general, annual security awareness training.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard e-learning module on information security is rolled out as mandatory for all employees. It includes a chapter on the topic of email security and malicious attachments.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the content of the awareness training and checks the attendance lists for completeness. It is verified whether the training is repeated regularly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All users MUST be appropriately sensitized to the dangers of active content and the handling of documents from external sources. Users SHOULD be informed about the possibilities and limitations of security features of the software and storage formats used. They SHOULD be taught how to protect documents from subsequent modification and how to use encryption functions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a dedicated, target-group-specific training campaign on secure Office practices. This includes e-learning, guides on the intranet, and regular phishing simulations with Office attachments. The training content covers macros, Protected View, document protection (e.g., read-only, restrict editing), and the use of integrated encryption.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses the training materials and the target group analysis. The results and the follow-up of the phishing simulations are reviewed. In interviews, the knowledge of a sample of users on the topics covered (e.g., 'How do you set read-only protection? When do you use encryption?') is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The awareness measures are embedded in a continuous improvement process. The effectiveness of the training is checked through regular, unannounced tests (e.g., targeted phishing campaigns). Users who perform poorly in tests receive automated follow-up training. The training content is dynamically adapted to current threat situations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A security awareness platform is used to manage campaigns, conduct tests, and individually control training needs. Current warnings from the BSI or manufacturers about vulnerabilities in Office products are promptly incorporated into communication measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the reports and statistics from the security awareness platform. The process for adapting training content based on test results and new threats is examined. Effectiveness is assessed based on the trend in click rates in phishing tests over time.

controls.title: Testing new versions of Office products (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before rolling out a new Office version, it is installed on a test system. The basic functions are informally checked by an IT employee to identify obvious problems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single PC in the IT department is used as a test system. The test is not formalized and focuses on basic functionality such as opening, editing, and saving documents.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the procedure for introducing new Office versions. It is checked whether tests are carried out at all, even if they are not documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: New versions of Office products SHOULD be tested for compatibility with established work tools such as macros, document templates, or forms of the institution before productive use. It SHOULD be ensured that important work tools also function perfectly with the new software version. If incompatibilities are discovered, suitable solutions for the affected work tools SHOULD be found.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a dedicated test environment that mirrors the production system. A formal test plan is created that includes all critical, institution-specific work tools (e.g., templates with macros for invoicing, Excel tools for controlling). Key users from the departments are involved in the tests. The test results and solutions found are documented before approval for rollout is granted (see OPS.1.1.6).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the test plan, the test documentation, and the release report for the last introduced Office version. It is checked whether the critical work tools were identified and whether key users were involved in the test process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The test process for new Office versions is largely automated. Test cases for critical macros and document templates are managed in a test automation framework and are automatically executed after each new version. The tests also include performance comparisons and checking compatibility with important third-party applications and add-ins.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A tool like Ranorex, Selenium (for web-based parts), or a specialized testing tool is used to script the interaction with Office applications. The test environment is set up automatically (Infrastructure as Code) to ensure consistent results. The test results are collected and evaluated in a central test management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the test automation framework and the test scripts. The automatically generated test reports are analyzed. It is checked how the test cases for new or changed work tools are updated.

controls.title: Regulation of software development by end users (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a fundamental decision on whether development by end users (e.g., creation of macros) is permitted. This decision is recorded in a general IT policy. If it is permitted, there are no further specific rules.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT user policy contains a sentence such as 'The creation of macros is only permitted after consultation with the IT department' or 'The creation of macros is generally not permitted'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the relevant IT policy and checks whether such a fundamental decision is documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For software development based on Office applications (e.g., macros), binding regulations SHOULD be established. A fundamental decision SHOULD be documented. If in-house developments are permitted, a procedure for handling these functions SHOULD be created. Responsibilities SHOULD be clearly defined. All necessary information about the created applications SHOULD be adequately documented and made accessible to all concerned.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a dedicated policy for 'End-User Computing' or 'Macro Development'. This defines who is allowed to develop macros (e.g., key users), what quality requirements apply (e.g., commenting the code, error handling), and how the macros must be tested, approved, and documented. A central directory (e.g., on the intranet or in a code repository) is maintained for approved macros and their documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the policy for end-user computing and checks its content. The directory of approved macros is reviewed. For a sample macro, it is checked whether documentation and an approval record exist.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All macros and scripts developed by end users that are used for business processes must undergo a formal code review by a second developer or the IT department before their productive use. All productive macros must be digitally signed to ensure their integrity and authenticity.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process for peer reviews is established. An internal certificate service is used to issue code signing certificates to authorized developers. The Office security settings are configured via GPO so that only digitally signed macros from trusted publishers can be executed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documented code review process and inspects review logs on a random basis. The configuration of the certificate authority and the GPO for the macro security settings is checked. It is checked whether a productively used macro has a valid digital signature.

controls.title: Regulated use of extensions for Office products (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation of extensions (add-ons, extensions) for Office products is only possible for users with administrative rights. There are no specific test or approval processes for these extensions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The principle of least privilege (standard users without admin rights) restricts the uncontrolled installation of add-ons. If an add-on is needed, it is manually installed by the IT department.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that standard users do not have local administrator rights and therefore cannot install system-wide add-ons. It is checked whether users can install add-ons from the Office Store themselves.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All extensions of Office products, such as add-ons and extensions, SHOULD be tested in the same way as new versions before productive use. The tests SHOULD take place exclusively on isolated test systems and check whether the extensions have negative effects. The tests SHOULD follow a defined, traceable test plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal process exists for the request, testing, approval, and deployment of Office add-ons. Each new add-on is tested in a dedicated test environment for functionality, compatibility with the existing Office installation, and security aspects (e.g., what data it accesses). The results are documented before approval is granted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the process for approving add-ons. For a recently introduced add-on, the test plan and test documentation are reviewed. It is checked whether a list of approved and blocked add-ons exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of Office extensions is technically restricted to an explicit whitelist of approved add-ons. Access to public add-on stores is blocked, and an internal, curated store with the approved extensions is provided instead.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Using Group Policies (GPO), the 'Office Store' is deactivated and a list of allowed add-ons is configured. Alternatively, the 'Centralized Deployment' service in the Microsoft 365 Admin Center is used to distribute only approved add-ons to specific user groups.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the corresponding GPO settings or the configuration in the M365 Admin Center. On a client system, an attempt is made to install an unapproved add-on to test the effectiveness of the block.

controls.title: Waiver of cloud storage (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a written directive in the IT user policy that prohibits the storage of business documents in private or unapproved public cloud storage. However, the integrated cloud functions in the Office applications are not technically deactivated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT user policy, which every employee receives upon joining, contains a corresponding clause. Compliance by the users is trusted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the IT user policy for the presence of the corresponding clause. In interviews, user awareness of this regulation is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cloud storage functions integrated in Office products SHOULD be disabled by default. All cloud drives SHOULD be disabled. All documents SHOULD be saved by users on centrally managed file servers. For sharing documents with third parties, specialized, approved applications SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Using Group Policies (GPO), the options for adding cloud storage locations (e.g., OneDrive, Dropbox) in the 'Save As' dialogs of Office applications are hidden and deactivated. Users are provided with an approved, in-house file-sharing solution as an alternative, which offers rights management and logging.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the relevant Group Policies. On a test client, it is checked whether the cloud storage options in Office applications are actually deactivated. The configuration and security features of the provided file-sharing solution are evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to deactivating the functions in Office, network traffic to known, unapproved cloud storage services is blocked at the central internet gateway (firewall, proxy). The use of the approved file-sharing solution is logged and monitored for anomalous activities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall or web proxy is updated with categorization feeds to identify the URLs and IP addresses of cloud storage services and block access to them. A Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) in discovery mode is used to detect shadow IT usage.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the rule sets of the firewall or proxy. An attempt is made to access a blocked cloud service from a client PC. The reports of the CASB system are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive Data Loss Prevention (DLP) solution is in use. It inspects outbound data traffic and actively blocks the upload of documents with sensitive content (based on classification or content analysis) to all unapproved destinations, including private cloud storage, webmail, and other channels.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A host-based and/or network-based DLP solution is implemented. Documents are classified automatically or manually (e.g., 'Internal', 'Confidential'). DLP policies prevent the transfer of documents classified as 'Confidential' to external destinations, with the exception of the approved file-sharing solution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the DLP policies and the classification schemes. An attempt is made to upload a document classified as sensitive to an external cloud storage to test the system. The DLP incidents and reports are analyzed.

controls.title: Use of viewer functions (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data from potentially insecure sources SHOULD be opened automatically in a protected mode that SHOULD NOT be deactivatable by users. A list of trusted sources SHOULD be defined. In protected mode, data SHOULD NOT be immediately editable and active content SHOULD NOT be executed automatically. If documents are only to be viewed, dedicated viewer applications SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The 'Protected View' in Microsoft Office is enforced via GPO for files from the internet, from email attachments, and from unsafe locations. The option to permanently disable this feature is blocked for users. A list of trusted locations (e.g., internal network drives) is maintained for which Protected View does not apply. For viewing PDF files, for example, a reader without editing functions is set as the default application.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the GPO settings for Protected View. It is tested whether a document from an email attachment opens in protected mode and whether editing functions are blocked. The list of trusted locations is checked for appropriateness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to protected mode, all documents from external sources are analyzed by a sandboxing solution before delivery to the user. The results of the analysis are displayed to the user to enable an informed decision about releasing the document.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Advanced Threat Protection (ATP) or sandboxing solution (e.g., Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Check Point SandBlast) is placed upstream of the email gateway and web proxy. It executes documents in an isolated environment to detect malicious behavior. Suspicious documents are blocked or delivered to the user with a clear warning.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the sandboxing solution. The reports and logs are analyzed. As a test, a (harmless but unknown) document is sent from an external source to verify the analysis process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All documents from untrusted sources are opened exclusively in a hardware-isolated container environment. This environment is completely separated from the host operating system and the internal network and is reset after each session.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Microsoft Defender Application Guard is mandatorily enabled via GPO for Office, Edge, and PDF Reader for all users. Policies prevent copying data from the container to the host system, unless explicitly allowed by a policy. Users are trained to use this feature for all external documents.

parts.name: assessment-method
