controls.title: Designation of Contact Persons (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A generic contact email address (e.g., info@) is available on the website. However, it is unclear who is responsible for handling security-related inquiries and how they are processed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The legal notice page contains a general email address. Incoming security notifications may not be recognized as such or may get lost in the general inbox.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the contact options on the website. Inquiring about the process for handling emails sent to the general address.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A person or team is internally designated as the contact for web-related issues, including security. A basic incident handling process exists, but may not be formally documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT operations team is known internally as being responsible for all web server issues. There is an unwritten rule that in the event of a security problem, the team leader must be informed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing employees to identify the known contact person and the informal incident process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For extensive web offerings, the institution SHOULD designate central contact persons. Processes, procedures, and responsible parties for problems or security incidents SHOULD be named. It SHOULD publish a contact option on its website (e.g., `security.txt`) through which security problems can be reported, and a process for handling such reports SHOULD be defined.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the operating concept of the web offering, the roles 'Technical Contact' and 'Functional Contact' are named. An incident response plan defines the responsibilities. A `/.well-known/security.txt` file is published on the web server, which specifies a `security@example.com` email address for security notifications. A ticketing system workflow is defined for processing incoming reports.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the operating concept for named contact persons. Checking the website for the presence and content of the `security.txt` file. Requesting and reviewing the defined process for handling external security reports.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The incident response plan for the web offering is detailed and includes communication plans. A formal Vulnerability Disclosure Policy (VDP) is published. It includes assurances on response times and a 'Safe Harbor' for security researchers who adhere to the policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The VDP is published on a dedicated '/security' page. It promises an initial response to reports within 2 business days and clarifies that research conducted within the policy will not lead to legal action.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the published VDP for completeness and clarity. Inspection of tickets from recent security reports to verify compliance with promised response times.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The incident response process is regularly tested through practical exercises. The vulnerability disclosure process is mature and possibly linked to a bug bounty program. Roles and responsibilities are integrated into the organization's overall crisis management framework.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Annual 'table-top' exercises simulate a security incident on the web service. The VDP directs researchers to a bug bounty platform where qualified reports are rewarded. The point of contact for the web service is part of the core team in the organization's crisis management unit.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the logs and results of the incident response exercises. Review of the integration with the bug bounty platform. Inspection of the crisis management framework documentation.

controls.title: Redundancy (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A single web server exists without any redundancy. Backups are made, but restoration is a manual and time-consuming process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single virtual server runs the website. Nightly backups are stored on a separate storage system. A failure requires manually provisioning a new server and restoring the data from the backup.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the system architecture. Analysis of the backup and recovery process and estimation of the recovery time objective (RTO).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A cold standby server is available. In the event of a failure, the DNS must be switched manually and the latest data restored from the backup, which leads to noticeable downtime.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A second, identically configured server is available, but normally switched off. In the event of a failure, it is started up, the data is restored, and the DNS A-record is manually changed to the new IP address.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the documentation and functionality of the cold standby server. Analysis of the failover process for manual steps and the associated downtime.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Web servers SHOULD be designed to be redundant. This is achieved by using at least two servers in a load balancer cluster (active-passive or active-active) to ensure basic high availability. Redundancy of other systems, such as the internet connection, has not yet been implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Two web servers are operated behind a single load balancer. The load balancer performs health checks and, in the event of a server failure, automatically directs traffic only to the remaining server. The content is kept synchronized via a shared, high-availability file system (e.g., NFS).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the load balancer configuration and the health checks. Simulation of a web server node failure and verification that the service remains available without manual intervention.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire delivery chain is designed to be redundant, as required. This includes redundant web servers, redundant load balancers, redundant internet connections from different providers, and a redundant backend (e.g., clustered application servers, replicated databases). The system can withstand the failure of any single component without service interruption.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A pair of high-availability load balancers (e.g., with VRRP) distributes traffic to the web servers. The server room has two separate internet uplinks routed via BGP. The web servers access a database cluster (e.g., Galera Cluster for MySQL).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the network and system architecture diagram for single points of failure. Performing failover tests for the various components (load balancer, database nodes, internet uplink).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The application is operated across multiple, geographically separate data centers or cloud availability zones in an active-active configuration with automatic failover. Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB) is used to direct traffic to the nearest or best-performing data center, ensuring maximum availability and disaster recovery capability.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The web application is operated in two different AWS regions (e.g., Frankfurt and Ireland). AWS Route 53 is configured with a latency-based or failover routing policy to distribute traffic. Data is kept synchronized between regions via asynchronous database replication.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the GSLB configuration (e.g., in AWS Route 53). Performing a regional failover test, in which a complete region is shut down, and measuring the time until all traffic is redirected to the remaining region.

controls.title: Protection against Denial-of-Service attacks (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Basic server performance metrics such as CPU and memory usage are monitored. There are no specific protective measures against DoS attacks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring tool like Nagios or Zabbix monitors the web server's CPU load and sends an alert if it exceeds 90%. The response to a DoS attack would be purely reactive.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the monitoring system's configuration. Inquiry about plans and measures for protection against DoS attacks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The web server and firewall are configured with basic rate limiting to mitigate simple DoS attacks. Server health and availability are monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The `limit_req_module` of Nginx is used to limit the number of requests per IP address. The firewall has rules to throttle the rate of new connections. A ping check monitors the server's reachability.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the rate-limiting configuration on the web server and firewall. Analysis of its effectiveness against simple DoS tools in a test environment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The web server SHOULD be constantly monitored for performance and availability. Measures SHOULD be defined and implemented to prevent or at least mitigate DDoS attacks. This is achieved through a combination of local hardening and a reactive (on-demand) DDoS protection service.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Comprehensive performance monitoring is established. A formal plan for defending against DDoS attacks exists. This plan includes a contract with a DDoS mitigation provider, who will redirect traffic through their scrubbing center in the event of an attack. This process is initiated manually when the attack is detected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the DDoS defense plan and the contract with the mitigation provider. Analysis of the defined thresholds and processes for activating the protection. Interviewing the team about the procedure in a real emergency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An 'always-on' DDoS protection service is used, which automatically detects and mitigates volumetric and protocol-based attacks at the network edge before they reach the organization's infrastructure. A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is used to protect against application-layer DoS attacks (Layer 7).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All traffic is permanently routed through a service like Cloudflare Spectrum or AWS Shield Advanced. A WAF is configured with rules against application-layer attacks like Slowloris, HTTP floods, or resource-intensive API calls (e.g., complex searches).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the DDoS protection service and WAF configuration. Analysis of reports on mitigated attacks. Performing simulated Layer 7 DoS attacks against a test interface.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A hybrid DDoS protection model is used, combining on-premise appliances for immediate mitigation of smaller attacks with a cloud-based scrubbing service for large-volume attacks. The system uses machine learning to create a baseline of normal traffic and can thus automatically detect and mitigate zero-day application-layer DoS attacks. The effectiveness of the mitigation measures is regularly tested through DDoS attack simulations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An on-premise DDoS appliance (e.g., from Radware or Arbor Networks) protects against smaller attacks. For larger attacks, traffic is automatically rerouted to a cloud scrubbing provider via BGP. The WAF uses behavioral analysis to detect anomalous request patterns. Planned annual DDoS tests are conducted with a specialized provider.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the hybrid protection model's architecture. Analysis of the behavioral analysis engine's configuration. Request and evaluation of the reports from the DDoS tests conducted and the resulting improvement measures.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
A web server is the core component of any website; it accepts requests from clients and returns the corresponding content. The data is usually transported via the Hypertext Transfer Protocol (HTTP) or its variant encrypted with Transport Layer Security (TLS), HTTP Secure (HTTPS). Since web servers offer a simple interface between server applications and clients, they are also frequently used for internal information and applications in institutional networks, such as the intranet.
Web servers are usually directly available on the Internet and thus offer an exposed attack surface. Therefore, they must be secured by suitable protective measures.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The goal of this module is to protect the web server and the information provided or processed by it.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module must be applied to all web servers in the information network.
The term web server is used for both the software that answers HTTP requests and the IT systems on which this software is executed. This module primarily considers the web server software. Security aspects of the IT system on which the web server software is installed are covered in the module SYS.1.1 General Server and the respective operating system-specific modules.
Recommendations on how to integrate web servers into the network architecture and secure them with firewalls can be found in the modules NET.1.1 Network Architecture and Design and NET.3.2 Firewall, respectively.
This module deals with fundamental aspects that are important for providing web content. Dynamic content provided by web applications is not the subject of this module. This is covered in module APP.3.1 Web Applications and Web Services. Likewise, web services are not considered here.
Web browsers are not considered in this module. Requirements for them can be found in module APP.1.2 Web Browsers.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Loss of reputation
parts.prose: If an attacker manages to access a web server with administrative rights, a manipulated website can be delivered (defacement). This can damage the institution's reputation. Likewise, the publication of false information, such as incorrect product descriptions, can lead to the institution's reputation suffering in the public eye. The institution can also receive a warning if content is published on its website that violates legal regulations. Damage can also occur if the website is unavailable and potential customers therefore switch to competitors.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Manipulation of the web server
parts.prose: In an attack, unauthorized persons could gain access to a web server and manipulate its files. For example, the web server software configuration could be changed, malware could be distributed, or web content could be modified.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Denial of Service (DoS)
parts.prose:
DoS attacks can be used to specifically impair the availability of a web service, for example by locking individual accounts through incorrect login attempts.
DDoS (Distributed Denial of Service) attacks can cause a web server to partially or completely fail. For clients, the web service is then only available very slowly or not at all. For many institutions, such a failure can quickly become business-critical, e.g., for online shops.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Loss of confidential data
parts.prose: Many web servers still use outdated cryptographic methods such as RC4 or SSL. Insufficient authentication or unsuitable encryption can lead to communication between clients and web servers being read or manipulated. The same applies to communication between the web server and other servers, such as load balancers.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Violation of laws or regulations
parts.prose: There are various regulatory requirements for publishing web content. In addition to the regulations of telemedia and data protection laws, the rules of copyright law must also be observed. Violations of these laws can have legal consequences.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Missing or inadequate error handling
parts.prose: If errors occur during the operation of a web server, this can affect its availability, for example. Content may also be displayed incompletely or security mechanisms may fail. If errors are not handled correctly, both the operation and the protection of the functions and data of a web server are no longer guaranteed.

controls.title: Use of RAID systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: RAID is only used sporadically for particularly important data volumes. There is no systematic approach to using RAID on all file servers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, RAID is typically only set up where data loss has already occurred in the past, rather than as a preventive measure. Often, simple RAID levels like RAID 1 are used on the server's system volume, but not necessarily on all data volumes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the disk configuration of all file servers in the information system. It is checked whether RAID systems are present and on which volumes they are active. The implementation is expected to be inconsistent.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic RAID system (e.g., RAID 1 or RAID 5) is implemented on all file servers. However, the decision for a specific RAID level is not formally documented, and no hot spare disks are maintained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All new file servers are set up with a RAID array by default. The configuration is usually based on a simple rule of thumb, without a detailed analysis of performance and availability requirements. There is no proactive plan for replacing failed hard drives.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should verify that all systems declared as file servers use a RAID system. A random check is made to see which RAID level is in use. The auditor should ask for the documentation for the selection decision and for the presence of hot spares, expecting both to be missing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations MUST determine whether a RAID system is to be used on the file server. A decision against such a system MUST be documented in a comprehensible manner. If a RAID system is used, IT operations MUST decide which RAID level to use, what the maximum time for a RAID rebuild process may be, and whether to use software or hardware RAID.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A policy is created that defines the process for deciding on RAID usage. For each file server, a documented decision is made that justifies the chosen RAID level (e.g., RAID 5 for a good balance, RAID 10 for high performance), the expected rebuild time, and the type of RAID (hardware RAID is preferred for better performance and reliability).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should check for the existence of a policy on RAID usage. For each file server, the documentation of the RAID decision should be requested and checked for completeness (RAID level, rebuild time, hardware/software). It is verified that the actual configuration corresponds to the documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the defined RAID strategy, hot spare disks are maintained in all RAID systems to automatically start the rebuild process in case of a failure. The status of the RAID system is actively monitored, and administrators are automatically notified in case of errors or the start of a rebuild.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least one hot spare disk of the same type and size is configured in all servers with RAID systems. The monitoring system (e.g., Nagios, Zabbix, or the manufacturer's own management software) is configured to query the RAID status and send emails or SMS messages to the IT operations team in case of status changes (e.g., 'degraded', 'rebuilding').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should review the configuration of the RAID controllers or RAID software on all file servers to verify the configuration of hot spares. The configuration of the monitoring system is checked and verified that corresponding alerting rules are defined and active for RAID failure events. An alarm can be triggered for testing purposes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection of the RAID level (e.g., RAID 6 or RAID 10) is based on a formal risk analysis that considers the probability of multiple disk failures during long rebuild times. The entire lifecycle of the hard drives, including preventive replacement procedures based on S.M.A.R.T. data and regular, automated tests of the rebuild process, is established and logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For large arrays with many hard drives and long rebuild times, RAID 6 or a comparable method with dual parity is used by default. Scripts and automation tools are used to continuously analyze S.M.A.R.T. values and predict impending failures. There is a defined process for planned 'fire drills' where a hard drive failure is simulated to test the reliability of the rebuild process and the alerting chain.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the risk analysis for the selection of the RAID level. Logs of the S.M.A.R.T. monitoring and automated rebuild tests are reviewed. The auditor verifies the existence and currency of the procedures for the preventive replacement of hard drives and the execution of 'fire drills'.

controls.title: Use of anti-virus programs

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An anti-virus program is installed on the file server, but it only performs periodic scans (e.g., nightly). An on-access scan, which checks files as they are written, is not activated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An anti-virus solution is considered 'installed', but the configuration is minimal for performance reasons. This leaves a window of opportunity where malware can be placed on the server and accessed by other clients before the next scheduled scan is executed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the configuration of the anti-virus program on the file server. It is specifically checked whether the on-access or real-time protection component for write operations is active. It is expected that this function is deactivated and only a scheduled scan is configured.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An on-access scan is activated on the file server and checks written files. However, the management of the software, especially the updating of virus signatures, is done manually or only irregularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Real-time scanning is active, which provides basic protection. Since the update process is not automated, the protection can quickly become outdated, making the server vulnerable to new threats. The configuration is otherwise standard and not optimized for the server role.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the on-access scan is active. Additionally, the date of the last signature update is checked. It is expected that this date is not current. The process for updating the signatures is queried, with a manual procedure being expected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data MUST be scanned for malware by an anti-virus program before it is stored on the file server. The anti-virus software is centrally managed, and the signatures are updated automatically and regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A server-side antivirus program with an on-access scan function for write access is installed and active. It is connected to a central management console that automatically distributes daily or multiple daily signature updates to all agents and reports the status (last scan, viruses found, signature version).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should be shown the configuration of the central management console for the antivirus protection. It is checked whether the file server is listed as a managed client, whether the on-access policy is active, and how the update policy is configured. A look at the server's logs shows that scans are taking place and signatures are up to date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the signature-based on-access scan, heuristic and behavior-based analysis methods are used to detect unknown malware (zero-day malware). Scan results and virus findings are centrally logged and actively monitored to enable a quick response to outbreaks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the antivirus solution, the modules for heuristic and behavior-based detection (often referred to as 'ransomware protection' or 'exploit protection') are activated. The logs from the virus scanner are forwarded to a central log management or SIEM system, where dashboards and alarms for virus findings are configured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration policy of the antivirus protection for the activation of heuristic and behavior-based protection mechanisms. The SIEM or log management system is inspected to verify that logs from the file server's antivirus are received, parsed, and processed in corresponding dashboards or alarms.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A multi-layered protection mechanism is implemented. Data is scanned at the network level by an ICAP (Internet Content Adaptation Protocol) server before it reaches the file server. In addition, on-server protection (as described in Level 4) is active. All events are integrated into a SIEM system that responds to threats using SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response) playbooks, e.g., by automatically isolating affected clients.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An ICAP-capable proxy or a service connected to the storage controller scans all SMB/NFS-uploads in real time. This offloads the file server and provides a first line of defense. Findings from the ICAP server and the on-server scanner are correlated in a SIEM. A SOAR playbook is created that automatically locks the accessing user account or isolates the source system from the network upon a confirmed malware finding on the share.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the network diagram and the configuration of the storage system or network proxy to verify the ICAP integration. In the SIEM, the correlation rule for virus findings is checked. In the SOAR tool, the playbook for automatic response to malware findings is demonstrated, and its execution logs are reviewed.

controls.title: Planning of File Servers

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: File servers are set up ad-hoc and reactively, usually when there is an acute need for storage space. No formal planning takes place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A department head requests storage space, and an administrator quickly sets up a server with default settings, without considering the type of data, access patterns, or future growth. Sometimes, powerful workstations are repurposed as unofficial file servers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor questions the administrators about the process of commissioning a new file server. It is expected that no formal planning or requirements document exists. An inspection of the server hardware could reveal that components not designed for continuous operation (e.g., desktop hard drives, workstations) are being used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Basic planning takes place, which mainly focuses on estimating the initial storage capacity. Security aspects and hardware selection are only considered superficially. The use of workstations as file servers is avoided, but there is no strict rule against it.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before setting up a file server, a rough estimate of the required storage space is made. Server hardware is procured, but not necessarily models that are optimized for the specific use case (e.g., high I/O load). The planning of storage reserves is unstructured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for planning documents for recently set up file servers. It is expected that these will be limited to capacity. The auditor verifies whether systems declared as file servers are actually server hardware and not devices classified as workstations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before an institution introduces one or more file servers, it SHOULD decide what the file servers will be used for and what information will be processed on them. The institution SHOULD plan every used function of a file server, including its security aspects. Workstations MUST NOT be used as file servers. The storage space of the file server MUST be sufficiently dimensioned, and sufficient storage reserves SHOULD be maintained. Only mass storage designed for continuous operation SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each new file server, a short concept document is created that describes the purpose (e.g., 'home directories', 'marketing project storage'), the type of data, the expected number of users, and the required services (e.g., SMB, NFS). Capacity planning considers the initial volume plus a 30% buffer for future growth. A rule is established and communicated that prohibits the use of non-server hardware for file server services. Only server-grade hard drives (e.g., SAS or Enterprise SATA) are procured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the planning documents for a selection of file servers and checks whether purpose, functions, and security aspects have been considered. The storage utilization is checked to assess the adequacy of the dimensioning and reserves. It is checked whether a binding rule prohibiting the use of workstations as file servers exists and whether the hardware used meets the specifications for continuous operation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning includes formal capacity and performance management with trend analyses based on historical data. A documented standard for the hardware and software configuration of file servers exists, which is applied to every new installation to ensure consistency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The utilization (storage space, CPU, I/O) of the file servers is continuously monitored, and the data is stored. Based on this data, future growth is forecasted to plan expansions in a timely manner. A 'golden image' or a configuration management script (e.g., with Ansible) is used to set up new file servers in a standardized and reproducible way.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the capacity and performance management reports and checks the forecast models. The document with the configuration standards for file servers is requested. The auditor compares the configuration of several file servers to verify compliance with the standard.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: File server planning is an integral part of the overall IT architecture and capacity management strategy. Decisions about new acquisitions, expansions, and technology selection are data-driven and based on long-term monitoring and forecasting models. The entire lifecycle of a file server, from procurement and operation to secure decommissioning, is fully planned and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: File server resources are listed as a service in the IT service catalog. Planning is linked to the budgeting process. The selection of new technologies (e.g., migrating to a different file system or a scale-out architecture) is supported by proof-of-concept tests and a formal evaluation against business and IT objectives. A standardized process exists for decommissioning, which includes data migration and certified deletion of data carriers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the IT strategy and architecture documents to verify the integration of file server planning. The records of technology evaluations and PoC tests are inspected. The decommissioning process is reviewed, including evidence of completed data deletions.

controls.title: Procurement of a file server and selection of a service

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The file server software SHOULD be selected appropriately. The file server service SHOULD support the intended use of the file server, e.g., mapping network drives on clients, streaming multimedia content, or exclusive file transfer via FTP. The performance, storage capacity, bandwidth, and the number of users using the file server SHOULD be considered when procuring the file server.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before procurement, a requirements profile is created that defines the primary purpose (e.g., 'SMB shares for 500 office users'). Based on this, the requirements for performance (IOPS), capacity (TB), bandwidth (GbE), and supported protocols (SMBv3, NFSv4) are specified. The selection of software and hardware is based on these defined criteria.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the requirements profile and procurement documents for a file server. It is checked whether the intended purpose, performance, capacity, and user requirements were documented and considered in the selection decision.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal requirements catalog is created and used as a basis for a structured market analysis and evaluation of various file server solutions (software and hardware). The decision is made and documented according to a comprehensible scheme.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed catalog of criteria is created in a table, containing functional (e.g., support for snapshots, deduplication) and non-functional requirements (e.g., scalability, support level, license costs). At least two to three different solutions are evaluated using this catalog. The results are recorded in an evaluation sheet that justifies the final decision.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the formal requirements catalog and the documented product comparison or evaluation sheet. The traceability of the evaluation process and the final selection decision is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before the final procurement decision, a Proof-of-Concept (PoC) is conducted in a test environment with the shortlisted solutions. This validates the performance, security, manageability, and compatibility with the existing IT infrastructure under realistic load scenarios.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A test environment that closely resembles the production environment is set up. Standardized load tests (e.g., with Iometer or fio) are performed to measure IOPS and throughput figures. Additionally, integration with Active Directory, connection to the backup system, and the management interface are practically tested by administrators. The PoC results are logged and are decisive for the final selection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the PoC planning documents, test logs, and the final results report. It is checked whether the tests covered relevant scenarios and whether the results support the procurement decision made.

controls.title: Selection of a file system

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD create a requirements list to evaluate the file server's file systems. The file system SHOULD meet the institution's requirements. The file system SHOULD offer a journaling function and have a protection mechanism that prevents multiple users or applications from writing to a file simultaneously.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A checklist is created that defines the minimum requirements for a file server file system: journaling (e.g., in NTFS, ext4, XFS) to protect against inconsistencies after a crash, and file locking support (standard in modern network protocols like SMB/NFS). The available file systems of the chosen operating system are evaluated against this list, and the selection is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the requirements list for file systems and the documentation of the selection decision. It is checked whether the file system in use (e.g., via `fsutil fsinfo volumeinfo` on Windows or `df -T` on Linux) supports the required properties, especially journaling.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the basic requirements, the selected file system supports advanced features such as snapshots for rapid data recovery and native data integrity checks using checksums (Copy-on-Write). The selection and configuration of the file system are justified and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Modern file systems like ZFS, Btrfs, or ReFS are specifically chosen to benefit from their advanced features. A snapshot schedule is configured (e.g., hourly) to allow users self-service recovery of previous file versions. The checksum function is active by default to detect and, if necessary, correct 'silent data corruption'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the selection documentation for the consideration of advanced features. The file system configuration on the server is checked to verify the activation of snapshots and checksumming (e.g., via `zfs get all` or `btrfs property get`). The auditor asks about the process for using snapshots for recovery.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection of the file system is part of an overall storage strategy. The decision is based on performance tests that simulate the organization's specific workload (e.g., many small files, large video streams). Integration with backup, disaster recovery, and security systems (e.g., native encryption, immutability options) is a crucial selection criterion.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a file system is rolled out company-wide, benchmark tests are conducted in a test environment with representative data and access patterns. The backup speed and the efficiency of replication mechanisms are measured. File systems that support immutable snapshots (immutability) as protection against ransomware are specifically evaluated. The results are incorporated into a formal technology decision.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the storage strategy as well as the logs and evaluations of the benchmark and integration tests. The configuration of the immutability features is verified. The auditor assesses whether the choice of file system demonstrably supports the strategic goals regarding performance, resilience, and security.

controls.title: Structured data storage

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A structure SHOULD be defined for storing data. Users SHOULD be regularly informed about the required structured data storage. Files SHOULD be stored exclusively in a structured manner on the file server. It SHOULD be specified in writing which data may be stored locally and which on the file server. Program and work data SHOULD be stored in separate directories. The institution SHOULD regularly check whether the specifications are being adhered to.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data storage policy is created and published on the intranet. It defines the top-level folder structure (e.g., /Departments, /Projects, /Archive) and specifies naming conventions. Employees are reminded to adhere to the structure in regular department meetings. Spot checks of the directory structures are carried out manually by IT staff.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the data storage policy. It is checked whether users have been demonstrably informed (e.g., through training logs or email distribution lists). The auditor performs a random visual inspection of the directory structure on the file server to assess compliance with the specifications and asks for the logs of internal reviews.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The defined data structure is supported and partially enforced by technical means where possible. For example, a sophisticated permissions concept guides users to the correct storage locations. Regular, automated reports identify data stored outside the intended structure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Permissions are set so that users can only write in their designated areas. Templates for project folders are automatically created with a predefined subfolder structure (e.g., /Quote, /Invoices, /Documentation). A script is run weekly that finds orphaned files or folders in the wrong place and reports them to the IT department.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the permission concept on the file server to determine the extent to which it supports the data structure. The automated reports on structure violations from recent months are requested and reviewed. The process for creating new project folders is checked for the use of templates.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal data classification policy is linked to the storage structure. Automated tools (e.g., File Server Resource Manager - FSRM, Data Loss Prevention - DLP) enforce the storage structure, classify data upon saving based on its content, and manage the data lifecycle, for example, by automatically moving outdated data to an archive.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DLP solution or FSRM with classification rules is implemented. Rules are created that automatically classify documents as 'internal' or 'confidential' based on keywords or patterns (e.g., 'confidential', IBANs). Another rule moves all files that have not been accessed for over two years to a special archive area with read-only access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the data classification policy and reviews the configuration of the automated tools (DLP/FSRM). It is tested using sample documents whether the classification and the derived actions (e.g., blocking, moving) function correctly. The logs of the lifecycle management tasks are inspected.

controls.title: Secure Storage Management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD regularly check whether the file server's mass storage devices are still functioning as intended. Suitable replacement storage SHOULD be kept on hand. If a storage hierarchy (primary, secondary, or tertiary storage) has been established, (semi-)automated storage management SHOULD be used and its function manually verified. At a minimum, unauthorized file access attempts and changes to access rights SHOULD be logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A weekly maintenance plan for file servers is created, which includes the manual check of hard disk S.M.A.R.T. values and free disk space. Spare hard disks for each model in use are kept in stock. Native Windows or Linux auditing for file access and permission changes is activated. The resulting logs are manually checked weekly for suspicious entries.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the maintenance plan and checks the logs of the performed reviews. An inventory list of the spare hard disks is inspected. The auditor verifies the configuration of the audit policies on the file server and requests to be shown the logs of the log reviews from the past few weeks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automated monitoring system is used to continuously monitor the state of the storage (S.M.A.R.T., RAID status), capacity, and performance. In the event of threshold breaches or errors, alarms are automatically sent to the administrators. The audit logs of access attempts and permission changes are forwarded to a central log management system and regularly analyzed there.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring tool such as Zabbix or Nagios is configured to query the relevant metrics of the file servers via SNMP or agent. Triggers are defined for 'free disk space < 15%' or 'S.M.A.R.T. error', which trigger email alarms. A log forwarder (e.g., Winlogbeat) sends the security event logs to a central Elasticsearch or Splunk cluster, where dashboards and search queries are available for analysis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the monitoring tool and the defined triggers and alerting rules. It is checked whether the file servers are set up as monitored hosts. In the central log management system, it is verified that logs from the file server are arriving and that dashboards for analysis exist. A test alarm can be triggered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Storage management is highly automated. Predictive analytics tools are used to forecast capacity requirements and potential hardware failures. Access logging is fully integrated into a SIEM system with UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) functions to automatically detect and alert on anomalous activities (e.g., mass deletions, access outside of business hours).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The monitoring tool is enhanced with machine learning functions to identify trends in storage utilization and predict when an expansion will be necessary. The file server logs in the SIEM are analyzed by UEBA rules that learn the normal access behavior of each user. In case of significant deviations (e.g., a user suddenly accesses 1000 files, although their average is 50), a high-priority security alert is triggered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the reports from the predictive analysis. In the SIEM, the configuration of the UEBA rules for file access and the resulting alarms from the last few months are reviewed. The effectiveness of the system is discussed and checked using example scenarios.

controls.title: Use of storage restrictions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If there are multiple users on the file server, IT operations SHOULD consider setting up storage space restrictions for individual users (quotas). Alternatively, mechanisms of the file or operating system used SHOULD be utilized to warn users when a certain disk fill level is reached or, in this case, to grant write permissions only to IT operations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A basic quota policy is defined. Either soft quotas (warnings only) or hard quotas (write operation is blocked) are set up for user home directories (e.g., via FSRM under Windows or `quota` under Linux). The decision and the level of the quotas are documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the quota policy. The configuration of the quota management on the file server is reviewed to check if and how quotas are set up for user directories. It is checked whether the configuration corresponds to the documented policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hard quotas are consistently implemented and enforced for all user or group directories. In addition, file screening is used to prevent the storage of unwanted or non-compliant file types (e.g., personal multimedia files, executable files) on the shares. The policies are documented and communicated to the users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Via the File Server Resource Manager (FSRM) or an equivalent tool, quota templates are created and assigned for different user groups (e.g., 'Standard User': 10 GB, 'Power User': 50 GB). File filters are defined that block the saving of file extensions such as .mp3, .avi, .exe and notify the user and the administrator of an attempt.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the quota templates and file filters in FSRM or the corresponding tool. It is tested whether saving a blocked file is actually prevented. The auditor verifies that the policies are available for users to view on the intranet or another central location.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Quota and file screening management is dynamic and automated. Quotas are automatically assigned based on the user's role or project affiliation in the identity management system. Users can request temporary quota increases via a formal, audited workflow in a self-service portal.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A provisioning script is developed that automatically creates the home directory with the correct quota template when a new user is created in Active Directory, based on the user's department. An IT self-service portal (e.g., based on ServiceNow or another ITSM tool) is enhanced with a workflow for quota requests that requires supervisor approval and automatically performs the increase after approval.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the provisioning script or the workflow in the IdM system. The workflow for quota requests in the self-service portal is demonstrated. The system's audit logs are reviewed to check the traceability of the approved quota changes.

controls.title: Use of error-correction codes

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD use an error-detecting or error-correcting file system. Sufficient storage space SHOULD be reserved for this purpose. IT operations SHOULD note that, depending on the method used, errors can only be detected with a certain probability and can also only be corrected to a limited extent.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When setting up the file server, a file system that supports data integrity (e.g., ZFS, Btrfs, ReFS) is deliberately chosen. The decision is documented. It is taken into account that storing checksums requires additional storage space. The administrators are aware of the system's limitations (e.g., that it does not detect bit flips in RAM if ECC RAM is not used).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation on the choice of file system. It is verified on the server which file system is in use and whether it is a system with error correction functions. The auditor questions the administrators about their known limits of the method used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A file system with strong data integrity functions (e.g., ZFS, ReFS) is used. Regular, automated 'scrubbing' operations are scheduled and performed to proactively check the entire dataset for latent data corruption (silent data corruption) and, if possible, correct it. In case of uncorrectable errors, alarms are automatically generated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On the ZFS or ReFS-based file server, a monthly 'scrub' job is set up via cron or Task Scheduler. The system monitoring is configured to evaluate the scrub reports and send a notification to the IT team in case of error messages. The status of the last scrub is displayed in the monitoring dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automated scrub job on the server. The logs of the last scrub operations are reviewed to confirm their regular and successful execution. The configuration of the alerting for scrub errors is checked in the monitoring system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire data path is protected by end-to-end checksums ('End-to-End Data Integrity'), from the application via the network protocol (if supported) to storage on the hard disk. The file system for error correction is combined with other fault-tolerant hardware such as ECC RAM and enterprise SSDs with power loss protection to ensure maximum data security.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A combination of ZFS/ReFS, ECC RAM, and an SMB dialect that supports integrity checking (SMB 3.1.1 with 'SMB Signing') is used. The hardware specifications for file servers mandate the use of ECC RAM and data carriers with protection against write losses in the event of a power failure (PLP). This architecture is enforced as the standard for all critical file servers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the hardware specifications of the server (e.g., via `dmidecode` for ECC RAM). The configuration of the network protocol (e.g., SMB settings via PowerShell `Get-SmbServerConfiguration`) is checked for the activation of integrity functions. The architecture document for file servers is reviewed to verify the holistic planning.

controls.title: Encryption of the data stock

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The mass storage of the file server SHOULD be encrypted at the file system or hardware level. If hardware encryption is used, products whose encryption function has been certified SHOULD be used. It SHOULD be ensured that the virus protection can scan the encrypted data for malware.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard solution for full disk encryption such as BitLocker under Windows Server or LUKS under Linux is implemented to encrypt all data volumes. When selecting self-encrypting drives (SEDs), attention is paid to a certification (e.g., FIPS 140-2). Since the decryption takes place transparently at the operating system level, compatibility with the virus protection is given and is verified on a random basis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the encryption status of the data volumes on the file server (e.g., with `manage-bde -status` or `cryptsetup status`). If SEDs are used, the manufacturer's certificates are requested. It is checked whether the virus scanner is active and functioning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management of encryption keys is separate from the file server and is handled by a dedicated Key Management Server (KMS) or a Hardware Security Module (HSM). The decision between file system-based and hardware-based encryption is based on a documented risk analysis that weighs aspects such as performance, cost, and security.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central KMS (e.g., a Key Management Interoperability Protocol (KMIP) compliant server) is set up to store and release the keys for BitLocker or LUKS encryption. The file server's access to the KMS is protected by certificates or other strong authentication methods. A risk analysis is created that highlights the pros and cons of software vs. hardware encryption in the specific context of the organization and serves as the basis for the decision made.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the encryption solution and verifies the connection to the external KMS. The security configuration of the KMS itself is checked. The risk analysis for the selection of the encryption technology is requested and checked for plausibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive data-at-rest encryption strategy is implemented. This includes the use of certified hardware encryption (e.g., FIPS 140-2 validated SEDs), robust key management with an HSM, and additionally, granular, file-based encryption (e.g., with Azure Information Protection or Vormetric) for data classified as particularly sensitive. Access to the keys is strictly controlled and audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default configuration for critical file servers provides for FIPS-validated SEDs whose keys are stored in a network-based HSM. In addition, a data-centric security solution is rolled out that automatically encrypts documents based on their classification (determined by a DLP solution). Only authorized users can decrypt these files, regardless of their storage location. All key accesses in the HSM are logged and sent to a SIEM for monitoring.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the SEDs and the HSM as well as the connection. The policies of the file-based encryption solution are checked. It is tested whether an unauthorized user can open a classified file. The audit logs of the HSM and the SIEM regarding key accesses are reviewed.

controls.title: Replication between sites

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For highly available file servers, data SHOULD be adequately replicated across multiple mass storage devices. Data SHOULD also be replicated between independent file servers located at independent sites. For this purpose, IT operations SHOULD select a suitable replication mechanism. To ensure that the replication can function as intended, sufficiently accurate time services SHOULD be used and operated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An asynchronous replication technology (e.g., DFS-R under Windows, rsync scripts, or ZFS send/receive under Linux) is set up to mirror data from a primary file server at one site to a secondary file server at another site. Both servers are configured with a reliable, synchronized time source (e.g., internal NTP servers).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the replication mechanism on the primary and secondary server. The status of the replication and the timestamp of the last replicated files are checked. The configuration of the time services on both servers is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Synchronous or quasi-synchronous replication is configured between two geographically separate data centers to ensure minimal data loss (RPO near zero). The state of replication and available bandwidth are continuously monitored. A documented disaster recovery plan that describes the failover process exists and is tested regularly (e.g., annually).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Storage-based synchronous replication or a solution like Storage Replica in Windows Server Datacenter Edition is used. The monitoring system supervises the replication status ('Healthy', 'Degraded') and replication latency. A detailed DR plan is stored in the emergency manual. A planned failover to the second site is performed once a year to validate the process and functionality.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the synchronous replication and the monitoring dashboards for the replication status. The disaster recovery plan is requested. The logs and result reports of the last DR tests are reviewed to verify the regular practice and the RTO/RPO values achieved.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A fully automated failover and failback solution (e.g., a geographically extended cluster or 'stretched cluster') is implemented across multiple sites. The solution provides continuous availability with no or minimal data loss (RPO=0) and a very fast recovery time (RTO in minutes). The entire solution, including redundant network paths and high-precision time services, is designed for high availability and is continuously monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Windows Server Failover Cluster or a comparable Linux cluster is extended across two or more sites. The underlying storage infrastructure supports synchronous replication and presents the storage actively at both sites. Failover in the event of a site failure occurs automatically and without manual intervention. The network connection between the sites is designed to be redundant (e.g., via two different carriers).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture of the stretched cluster and the configuration of the cluster services. The configuration of the automatic failover policies is checked. The network diagram is reviewed to verify the redundancy of the connections. Logs of past (real or simulated) failover events are evaluated to confirm the automatic functionality and compliance with RTO/RPO targets.

controls.title: Planning the use of a Samba server (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic plan for the use of Samba exists only for individual, isolated servers. Advanced functions such as Active Directory integration, cluster operation (CTDB), or the specific configuration of VFS modules are not considered. The planning is done ad-hoc and is not documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this maturity level, Samba is typically installed only as a simple file server in a workgroup, without deeper integration into existing directory services. The configuration is based on default settings and is adjusted as needed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines whether a planning document or concept for the use of Samba exists at all. It is checked whether the planning only covers basic file shares and ignores aspects such as authentication, high availability, or IPv6.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A documented plan for the use of Samba servers exists that covers all servers. This plan defines the basic tasks (e.g., file and print services) and the operating mode. Concepts for AD integration or CTDB are mentioned but not worked out in detail. The planning for IPv6 is rudimentary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central document describes the standard installation and configuration of Samba. It specifies which servers take on which roles. However, the configuration of advanced features is still largely manual and without detailed preliminary design.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the planning document for the use of Samba. It is checked whether all productive Samba servers are included in the plan and whether the basic tasks and operating modes are defined. The level of detail of the concepts for AD, CTDB, and IPv6 is assessed as superficial.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT operations department MUST carefully plan and regulate the introduction of a Samba server. It MUST be defined, depending on the deployment scenario, which tasks the server is to perform and in which operating mode it will be run. It MUST be specified which Samba components are required. If CTDB, AD services, specific authentication methods, or VFS modules are to be used, these MUST also be carefully designed. If IPv6 is used, this MUST be planned and checked for correct functionality in a test environment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A separate concept document is created for each deployment scenario (e.g., Domain Controller, member server). This document describes the exact configuration, the selection and order of VFS modules, the AD integration including authentication mechanisms, and the network configuration (IPv4/IPv6). The implementation SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the submission of the planning and concept documents for the various Samba deployment scenarios. It is verified whether the documents cover all MUST requirements, especially the detailed design for AD, CTDB, VFS, and IPv6. It is checked on a random basis whether the production systems have been implemented according to the concept.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning (Level 3) is extended to include documented test procedures for all essential components (AD, CTDB, VFS, IPv6) in a dedicated, production-like test environment. The implementation plan contains detailed rollout and rollback procedures. The implementation of all configurations is consistently documented, as required as SHOULD in Level 3.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before every major change or introduction, a test case catalog is processed. The results of the tests are logged. The implementation documentation is maintained in a central configuration management system or wiki and is versioned.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the test logs and the documentation of the test environment. It is checked whether the rollout and rollback plans exist and are plausible. The quality and completeness of the implementation documentation are assessed. As an automated check, a script can compare the configuration of the production system with the documented configuration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire planning and concept process is fully integrated into the organization's change management system. The planning includes capacity and performance modeling for various load scenarios. The security concept for Samba is reviewed regularly, at least annually, and on an ad-hoc basis (e.g., in case of new known vulnerabilities) and adapted to the current threat landscape.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Automated tools are used to check the concept before deployment (e.g., 'testparm' in CI/CD pipelines). Performance tests are conducted automatically. The security concept is validated through regular, automated configuration audits and penetration tests.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the integration of Samba management into the change management process. The existence and up-to-dateness of performance analyses and the proactively maintained security concept are checked. Audit logs from automated configuration checks and reports from penetration tests are used as evidence.

controls.title: Secure basic configuration of a Samba server (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The basic security settings are applied on all Samba servers. This includes configuring access controls for shares and restricting network access (e.g., via `hosts allow / deny`). The SWAT configuration tool is not installed on any server. Changes to the configuration are logged informally.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple text document or an entry in a ticket system serves as a logbook for configuration changes. The network restrictions are maintained directly in `smb.conf`. The configuration syntax is checked manually with `testparm` after each change.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks on all Samba servers whether the package for SWAT (samba-swat) is uninstalled. The `smb.conf` is checked for the use of `hosts allow / deny` or comparable mechanisms. The change log is spot-checked for completeness and traceability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations MUST configure the Samba server securely. For this, the access control settings MUST be adjusted. Samba MUST be configured to accept connections only from secure hosts and networks. Changes to the configuration SHOULD be carefully documented. After each change, the syntax of the configuration file MUST be checked. Additional software modules like SWAT MUST NOT be installed. Performance settings SHOULD also be adjusted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration (`smb.conf`) is created according to a documented security standard. Changes are recorded in a formal logbook (e.g., a wiki with a change history) specifying the reason, date, and person. The syntax check with `testparm` is a mandatory step after each change. Performance is influenced by adjusting parameters such as `socket options`.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the configuration (`smb.conf`) with the documented security standard. The change log is checked for completeness and compliance. It is verified that SWAT is not installed. It can be checked automatically via script whether `testparm` reports correct syntax on all servers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The Samba server's configuration files are managed in a version control system (e.g., Git). Changes require a review and approval process (e.g., pull request). The syntax check is performed automatically with every commit. The SHOULD requirement for performance optimization is systematically implemented, and the effects are measured and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A CI/CD pipeline is used to manage `smb.conf`. Every proposed change is automatically validated with `testparm`. The documentation of changes occurs automatically through the commit history in the version control system. Performance tuning is carried out based on load tests in the test environment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configured workflow in the version control system, including the review and approval steps. The logs of the CI/CD pipeline are inspected to verify the automatic syntax check. Documentation on performed performance measurements is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A configuration management system (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) is used to automatically enforce and monitor the secure baseline configuration on all Samba servers. Any deviation from this 'Golden Image' is automatically corrected or triggers an alarm. The configuration is regularly subjected to automated audits against recognized hardening guidelines (e.g., CIS Benchmarks).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ansible playbooks or Puppet modules define the desired state of the Samba configuration. A central server runs these regularly and ensures conformity. The results of the configuration audits are visualized in a central dashboard and used for continuous improvement.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is given read access to the configuration management system and analyzes the defined configuration templates and rules. The system's logs are checked to verify automatic enforcement and alerting. The reports of the compliance scans against the hardening guidelines are used as evidence. An automated audit command would be e.g. `ansible-playbook --check playbook.yml` to detect deviations.

controls.title: Secure configuration of a Samba server (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Databases in Trivial Database (TDB) format SHOULD NOT be stored on a partition that uses ReiserFS as the file system. If a netlogon share is configured, unauthorized users SHOULD NOT be able to modify files in this share. The operating system of a Samba server SHOULD support Access Control Lists (ACLs) in conjunction with the file system used. In addition, it SHOULD be ensured that the file system is mounted with the appropriate parameters. The default settings for SMB Message Signing SHOULD be retained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: It is ensured that TDB files are located on a stable file system such as ext4 or XFS. The permissions of the netlogon share are set so that only administrators have write access (`write list = @Administrators`). The file system is mounted with the `user_xattr,acl` options. The SMB signing (`server signing`) is left at `auto` or `mandatory`.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the type of file system on which the TDB files are located (typically under /var/lib/samba/). The configuration of the netlogon share in `smb.conf` is checked for restrictive write permissions. The `mount` command is executed to verify the mount options for ACLs. The setting for `server signing` in `smb.conf` is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All SHOULD recommendations from Level 3 are consistently implemented and this is documented. A script periodically checks the permissions of the netlogon share for deviations. The necessary file system options are enforced via `/etc/fstab` and a configuration management tool. The SMB signing policy is formally documented and actively enforced (e.g., `server signing = mandatory`).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A cron job runs a script nightly that compares the permissions of the netlogon directory with a desired state and sends an email to the administrators in case of deviations. In Ansible, the `mount` option is explicitly set to ensure correct mounting. SMB signing is set to 'mandatory' if all clients support this.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the permission checking script and its execution logs. The configuration management system (e.g., Ansible playbook) is checked to verify the enforcement of the mount options. The global configuration in `smb.conf` is checked for `server signing = mandatory`. The check script can be re-run by the auditor in an automated way to validate the correct permissions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The choice of file system and its configuration is part of an automated server build standard enforced by configuration management. A File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) system monitors the netlogon share and critical TDB files in real time for unauthorized changes. SMB signing is enforced via Group Policy (in AD environments) or an equivalent configuration management, and connection attempts without signing are logged and trigger a security alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'Golden Image' for Samba servers, managed by Packer and Ansible, ensures the correct baseline configuration. Tools like AIDE or Wazuh are used to monitor file integrity. The Samba configuration is adjusted so that rejected connections due to missing SMB signing are logged with a high log level and captured by a SIEM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the server build process. The configuration and alerting rules of the FIM and SIEM systems are checked. Test connections without SMB signing are initiated to verify that they are blocked and a corresponding alarm is generated.

controls.title: Avoiding NTFS properties on a Samba server (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a version of Samba is used that cannot map Alternate Data Streams (ADS) in the New Technology File System (NTFS), file system objects SHOULD NOT contain ADS with important information when they are copied or moved across system boundaries.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators and users are informed via a policy or a leaflet that storing critical data in ADS on shares managed by older Samba versions is not supported and can lead to data loss. It is recommended to refrain from using ADS.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether an appropriate policy or communication measure to avoid ADS exists and has been distributed to the relevant users. The Samba version in use is checked to determine if the problem is relevant at all (modern versions can usually map ADS).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A modern Samba version is used that is capable of correctly storing NTFS Alternate Data Streams in extended file attributes of the Unix file system using appropriate VFS modules (e.g., `vfs_streams_xattr`). The configuration is applied consistently on all servers. Alternatively, a script is used that regularly scans the file systems for files with ADS and reports them.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In `smb.conf`, the `streams_xattr` VFS module is activated globally or for the relevant shares. The functionality is tested by copying a file with ADS from a Windows client to the share, copying it back, and checking the integrity of the ADS.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks `smb.conf` for the activation of the `vfs_streams_xattr` module or a comparable module. The correct function is verified by a practical test. If a scan script is used, its configuration and logs are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Support for Alternate Data Streams is ensured on all systems by a modern Samba version and the correct VFS configuration and is enforced by configuration management. A Data Loss Prevention (DLP) system is used to prevent files containing sensitive information in ADS from being transferred to insecure systems or over insecure channels where the ADS could be lost.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The VFS configuration is part of the automated server build process. The DLP system is configured with rules that analyze the content and metadata of files, including ADS, and block the transfer in case of violations against the data classification policy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration in the configuration management system. The rules and logs of the DLP system are analyzed. A test case is performed in which an attempt is made to copy a file with an ADS classified as sensitive to a non-compliant storage location to verify the blocking function of the DLP system.

controls.title: Secure configuration of access control on a Samba server (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The parameters used by default by Samba to map DOS attributes to the Unix file system SHOULD NOT be used. Instead, Samba SHOULD be configured to store DOS attributes in Extended Attributes. Shares SHOULD be managed exclusively via the Samba registry. Furthermore, the effective access permissions on the Samba server's shares SHOULD be reviewed regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In `smb.conf`, parameters like `map archive = no`, `map hidden = no`, etc. are set, and `store dos attributes = yes` is used instead. The management of shares is moved from `smb.conf` to the registry database (`net conf setparm` and `net share add`). There is a defined, manual process for an annual permission review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks `smb.conf` for the correct parameters for attribute storage. `net conf list` and `net share list` are used to verify that the shares are managed in the registry. The logs of the annual permission reviews are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All SHOULD requirements from Level 3 are implemented. A documented process for the quarterly review of access permissions is established and demonstrably followed. Scripts are used to simplify the review of permissions, for example, by automatically reading the effective rights for critical directories and comparing them with a target state.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PowerShell or shell script is developed that uses `smbcacls` or similar tools to read the NTFS ACLs on the shares and present them in a clear report. This report serves as the basis for the quarterly review by the respective data owners.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation of the review process and the logs of the last four quarterly reviews. The permission analysis script is inspected and its results are compared with the actual permissions on the server on a random basis. The script can be executed again automatically to generate a current report.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The review of access permissions (Access Reviews) is fully automated by an Identity and Access Management (IAM) tool. This tool regularly (e.g., quarterly) prompts the data owners to re-certify existing access. Any deviation from the defined permission baseline detected by the IAM system leads to an immediate alarm and an automated correction or escalation process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An IAM tool like SailPoint, OneIdentity, or an open-source solution is connected to the Samba server (via AD integration). Workflows for access certification are set up. Alerting rules are configured in the IAM or SIEM system to react immediately to critical permission changes (e.g., 'Everyone' receives full access).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and workflows in the IAM system. The reports of completed certification campaigns are used as proof of performed reviews. It is checked whether alerting rules for permission deviations exist and whether test alarms can be successfully triggered.

controls.title: Secure configuration of Winbind under Samba (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a corresponding account does not exist in the server's operating system for every domain account, Winbind SHOULD be used to map domain accounts to Unix accounts. When using Winbind, it SHOULD be ensured that collisions between local users in Unix and users in the domain are prevented. Furthermore, PAM (Pluggable Authentication Modules) SHOULD be integrated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In `smb.conf`, defined and sufficiently large UID and GID ranges are set for the ID mapping of domain users and groups, which do not overlap with the local UIDs/GIDs. The PAM configuration (`/etc/pam.d/`) is adapted to use Winbind for authentication (`auth`), account management (`account`), session management (`session`), and password changes (`password`).

parts.name: assessment-method
