Custom software is usually developed as part of a project. A wide variety of procedural or project management models have been established for this. While classic, linear procedural models, such as the waterfall process, are very well suited to projects with fixed requirements at the beginning, agile procedural models, such as Scrum, allow custom software to be developed iteratively and incrementally. Agile procedural models can thus adapt better to changing conditions, especially if not all requirements are fixed at the beginning. However, they do not offer the same calculation certainty as linear procedural models and in some cases do not fit the classic structures of procurement processes that are geared towards a linear approach.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of this module is to show which fundamental security requirements must be taken into account during the planning and development of custom software.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module APP.7 Development of Custom Software must be applied once for each development of custom software.

Aspects for the planning, design, and use of custom software, such as defining necessary security functions or decommissioning custom software, are covered in the module APP.6 General Software. It must therefore always be applied together with this module.

When software is developed, there is very often a contractor and client relationship. In IT Baseline Protection, this situation is reflected by the fact that the module APP.7 Development of Custom Software deals with the client side and the module CON.8 Software Development deals with the contractor side.

The release and testing of custom software is covered in the module OPS.1.1.6 Software Tests and Releases.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Inadequate contractual arrangements with external service providers
parts.prose: Due to inadequate contractual arrangements with external service providers, a variety of serious security problems can arise. This is particularly true when applications are created, introduced, or maintained. If tasks, performance parameters, or the effort required are described inadequately or ambiguously, security measures may not be implemented due to lack of knowledge, insufficient qualifications, or a lack of resources. This can lead to many negative consequences, for example, if regulatory requirements and obligations are not met, disclosure obligations and laws are not complied with, or no responsibility is taken because control and steering options are missing.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Software design flaws
parts.prose: When applications, programs, and protocols are designed, security-relevant design flaws can arise. These often result from reusing application modules and protocols intended for a specific purpose in other usage scenarios. If different security requirements are then relevant, this can lead to massive security problems, for example, when application modules and protocols originally intended for isolated operational environments are connected to the internet.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Undocumented features
parts.prose: Many applications contain undocumented features built in by the manufacturer, often for development or support of the application. These are usually not known to the users. Undocumented features are problematic when they allow essential security mechanisms, e.g. for access control, to be bypassed. This can significantly compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the processed data.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Missing or insufficient security measures in applications
parts.prose: Security mechanisms or security functions in the application are intended to ensure that the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information can be guaranteed to the required extent during processing. However, when developing an application, the focus is often on the business functionality or the time and cost constraints. As a result, important security mechanisms may be too weak, so that they can be easily bypassed or may be missing altogether.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Poor governance of software development
parts.prose:
If software development is not sufficiently controlled by the client, a number of dangers arise, such as:
• Required security functions may be missing or inadequately implemented. This can lead to various risks that jeopardize the availability, confidentiality, and integrity of the data processed with the custom software.
• The development project may be delayed, so the custom software is not available on time.
• Priorities may be set incorrectly, for example, by extensively developing low-priority functions while urgently needed security functions are only implemented rudimentarily. This can also lead to project delays and various security risks.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Commissioning of unsuitable software developers
parts.prose:
If unsuitable software developers are commissioned, various threats can arise:
• Due to a lack of professional expertise, e.g., in the programming language used, in the frameworks employed, or the planned technical deployment environment, the software may contain many avoidable security vulnerabilities.
• A lack of knowledge in project management and requirements engineering can lead to friction in coordination processes and thus to significant delays. This can also lead to priorities being set incorrectly, so that essential security functions are not implemented with the required priority. Unsuitable software developers might be commissioned, for example, due to tight, unrealistic cost calculations. Errors, misleading requirements, and incorrect objectives in tenders can also lead to this.

controls.title: Access Protection and Use (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only individual servers considered critical are housed in lockable rooms. A general regulation for the physical protection or use of servers does not exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For example, the domain controller is in a locked rack, while a departmental file server is operated freely accessible in an office space.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts a site survey to identify the physical location of all servers and determines that no uniform protection measures are implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All physical servers are housed in dedicated, locked server rooms or cabinets. Access to virtualization platforms is restricted to administrators. There is an informal instruction not to use servers as workstations, but compliance is not checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All servers are consolidated in a central server room. A list of authorized persons is posted on the door. Access to the vSphere web interface is restricted to members of the IT department.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that all servers are physically secured. He checks the access list for plausibility and compares the permissions for the virtualization platform with the list of responsible administrators.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical servers MUST be operated in locations to which only authorized persons have access. For virtualized servers, access to the instance's resources and its configuration MUST also be limited to authorized persons. Servers MUST NOT be used as workstations. In particular, existing applications, such as web browsers, on the server MUST NOT be used to retrieve information from the Internet.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Access to server rooms is regulated by an electronic locking system with logging. Access to the management interfaces of virtualization environments is regulated via a dedicated administrator group in the central directory service. The usage policies are documented and known to the administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the log data of the electronic locking system. He checks the memberships of the administrative groups for the virtualization environment. On a random basis, servers are checked for the installation of unauthorized software (e.g., web browsers, office suites) or whether browser histories indicate private use.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical access to server rooms is additionally secured by video surveillance at the entrances. Administrative access to virtualization platforms is consistently protected using multi-factor authentication (MFA). Policies on the unauthorized use of servers are enforced through technical measures (e.g., Application Whitelisting).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A camera is installed at the entrance to the server room. MFA is enforced for logging into the vCenter or Hyper-V console. The execution of unauthorized software such as web browsers is blocked via AppLocker or an equivalent system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the video surveillance recordings. They check the MFA configuration for administrative access. They attempt to launch a web browser on a server to verify the effectiveness of the technical block.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical access is controlled by biometric features or a four-eyes principle. All administrative access to servers (physical and virtual) is exclusively via a Just-in-Time (JIT) Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. Compliance with usage policies is monitored in real time by an agent-based security solution (EDR/XDR), which automatically blocks and reports violations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM system is implemented for all administrative access to the server infrastructure. An EDR agent is rolled out to all servers, configured to prevent the execution of unwanted processes and report suspicious activities to the SIEM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration and logs of the PAM system to check the correct functioning of JIT privilege assignment. They analyze the alarms and reports of the EDR solution regarding attempted policy violations on the servers. Automated check: `Get-EDRPolicy -Server $server | Where-Object {$_.Rule -eq 'Block-WebBrowsers'} | Select-Object -ExpandProperty 'Enabled'` must return `true`.

controls.title: Authentication on servers (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication methods are used on some servers, but there is no uniform regulation. Weak, easy-to-guess passwords or shared accounts are often used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Some servers use local user accounts with simple passwords, while others have no password protection for certain services.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor identifies servers with weak or missing authentication mechanisms through port scans and manual checks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication methods are enforced for logging into all servers. Mostly, local user accounts with a simple password policy (e.g., minimum length) are used. Central authentication services are not yet used consistently.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A local security policy is activated on all servers that enforces a password length of 8 characters. Administrative accounts are individual but are managed separately on each server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the local security policies of the servers and finds that there is no central management of user accounts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication methods appropriate to the protection needs of the servers MUST be used for user and service logins to the server. This SHOULD be considered in particular for administrative access. Wherever possible, central, network-based authentication services SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All servers are integrated into a central directory service domain (e.g., Active Directory, LDAP). Login is via personalized domain accounts. Company-wide password policies that require complexity and regular changes apply.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the domain membership of the servers. They check the configuration of the central password policies. It is checked whether local accounts (except for emergency admins) are disabled. Automated check: `Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Server $server` must return `true`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enforced for all administrative access to servers. Strong, automatically rotated passwords (managed service accounts) are used for service accounts.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Logging into servers via RDP or SSH for administrators requires a one-time password (TOTP) or a smart card in addition to the password. Service accounts are configured as gMSA (group Managed Service Account) in Active Directory.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor attempts to log into a server as an administrator without a second factor and verifies that access is denied. They check the configuration of the service accounts in the directory service.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any authentication to servers, for both interactive logins and service-to-service communication, is passwordless using certificate-based or FIDO2-compliant methods. Access is controlled and logged via a central Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators authenticate using smart cards or YubiKeys (PIV/FIDO2). Windows login is implemented via 'Windows Hello for Business' with certificate trust. All logins are tunneled through a PAM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration of the PAM system and the Public Key Infrastructure (PKI). They verify that password-based logins are technically blocked on the servers and that all login events are recorded in the central logging system.

controls.title: Protection of interfaces (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On the servers, all physical and logical interfaces are active by default. There are no regulations for deactivation or for connecting devices.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: USB ports, serial interfaces, and unused network adapters are operational on all servers. Anyone can connect any USB stick.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor physically and in the operating system checks the active interfaces and determines that no hardening measures have been taken.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On servers, obviously unused physical interfaces such as USB ports are manually disabled in the BIOS/UEFI. The connection of removable storage is informally prohibited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: During the initial setup of the server, the USB ports are disabled in the BIOS/UEFI, unless they are needed for a keyboard/mouse.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the BIOS/UEFI settings of servers to verify the deactivation of ports.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be ensured that only designated removable storage and other devices can be connected to the servers. All interfaces that are not used MUST be deactivated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The deactivation of unused interfaces (e.g., USB, serial/parallel ports, FireWire) is centrally enforced via Group Policies (GPOs) or a Mobile Device Management (MDM) for servers. Exceptions are documented and approved.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the corresponding GPO or MDM settings. They try to connect an unauthorized USB device to a server and verify that access is blocked. Automated check: `Get-GPOReport -Name 'Server-Hardening-Policy' -ReportType Html | Select-String 'Deny all removable storage classes'`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The connection of devices to interfaces is not only blocked, but a whitelist of allowed devices (based on hardware ID or serial number) is also enforced. Any attempt to connect an unauthorized device is logged and triggers an alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A whitelist for USB devices is implemented using an endpoint security solution. Only encrypted USB sticks of a specific brand, which are required for maintenance work, are permitted. Connection attempts from other devices are reported to the SIEM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the whitelist in the endpoint security solution. They connect an unauthorized device and verify that an alarm is generated in the SIEM system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All physical interfaces on servers are sealed with physical port blockers (port locks) by default. Any activation must be requested via a formal change process. The system configuration is continuously monitored by a configuration management tool, and any deviation (e.g., a reactivated port in the operating system) is automatically reverted and reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Physical USB and RJ45 blockers are inserted into all unused ports. A configuration management tool such as Puppet, Ansible, or DSC is used to continuously enforce the desired state of the interface configuration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a physical inspection of the servers and checks the sealing of the ports. They audit the configuration and execution logs of the configuration management tool to verify continuous compliance with the policy.

controls.title: Deactivation of unnecessary services (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Servers are operated with the default installation of the operating system. All default installed roles, features, and services are active, regardless of whether they are needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Windows Server is installed with a graphical interface and all recommended features, although it only serves as a pure file server. The IIS web server is running, although no web application is hosted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a port scan of the server and identifies numerous open ports from services that are not required for the server's function.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Administrators manually disable obviously unnecessary services and uninstall unused software to the best of their knowledge. However, there is no systematic or documented process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After installing a server, an administrator goes through the list of services and disables services like 'Print Spooler' on a database server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the running services on two functionally identical servers and finds significant differences, which indicates a non-standardized hardening process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All unnecessary server roles, features and functions, other software and services MUST be deactivated or uninstalled, especially network services. All unnecessary functions in the firmware MUST also be deactivated. The decisions made SHOULD be documented in such a way that it is possible to understand which configuration and software equipment were selected for the servers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each server type (e.g., web server, database server), there is a documented base image or an installation script that installs only the minimally required components (e.g., Windows Server Core). The decisions about the installed components are recorded in the server operating manual.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the list of installed roles and features and the running services of a server with the corresponding, documented target state in the operating manual. Automated check: A script like `Get-WindowsFeature | Where-Object Installed -eq $true` is executed and the result is compared with a predefined baseline.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The server configuration is regularly and automatically compared with a recognized hardening benchmark (e.g., CIS Benchmarks). Deviations from the hardened configuration are reported. On servers, the storage space for individual users, but also for applications, SHOULD be appropriately limited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A security scanner (e.g., Nessus, OpenSCAP) is used to check the server configuration weekly against the CIS benchmark for the respective operating system. Reports on deviations are sent to the administrators. Filesystem quotas are set for user profiles and application logs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the reports from the security scanner and checks whether the reported deviations are resolved in a timely manner. They verify the configuration of the filesystem quotas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet, DSC) continuously enforces the hardened desired state of the server. Any manual change that deviates from the defined baseline is automatically detected and reverted within minutes (self-healing). Any drift is centrally reported and analyzed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ansible Playbooks or Puppet manifests, based on a hardening standard, are executed on the servers every 30 minutes. The 'Enforce' mode is activated, so that configuration changes are automatically corrected. The results are visualized in a central dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the code and configuration of the configuration management tool. They deliberately try to manually activate a service on a server and observe how the automation reverts this change within the defined time frame.

controls.title: Use of antivirus programs on servers (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Antivirus software is only installed on individual servers, typically on file servers, without central management or monitoring.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A free virus scanner is manually installed on the central file server. Other servers such as database or application servers have no protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Through an inventory check, the auditor determines that there is no comprehensive and uniform antivirus solution in use on the servers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Antivirus software is installed on all servers. However, management is decentralized on each server, and the configuration is not standardized. Signature updates are not centrally monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The same virus scanner is installed on every server, but the configuration (e.g., scan times, exceptions) is done individually by each administrator.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks several servers and finds that although the antivirus software is installed, the signature databases are outdated and the configurations differ from each other.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Depending on the installed operating system, the services provided, and other existing protection mechanisms of the server, it MUST be checked whether antivirus programs should and can be used. Where available, specific statements from the relevant operating system modules of the IT-Grundschutz Compendium MUST be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A centrally managed endpoint protection solution for servers is used. For each server type (e.g., file server, Exchange server, SQL server), specific scan exclusions recommended by the manufacturer are configured in a central policy to avoid performance issues. The update status and alerts are centrally monitored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the central management console of the endpoint protection solution. They verify that all servers are managed, have current signatures, and that the configured exceptions are documented and plausible. Automated check: `Get-MpComputerStatus` on a server must show `AMEngineVersion`, `AMProductVersion`, and `NISProductVersion` as current.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The protection solution used on the servers includes not only signature-based protection but also behavior-based detection (e.g., protection against ransomware) and a host-based intrusion prevention system (HIPS) component. The configuration is regularly reviewed for its effectiveness.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solution is used instead of a classic virus scanner. The anti-ransomware function is activated and tested. HIPS rules are implemented to block suspicious process calls.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the EDR console for the activation of behavior-based protection modules. In a safe test environment, they run an EICAR-like test script for ransomware to verify the system's response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The EDR solution on the servers is fully integrated into the SIEM and SOAR system. Critical alerts from servers lead to automated responses, such as the immediate network isolation of the affected server, without human intervention.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: EDR alerts are sent to the SIEM via API. A playbook is configured in the SOAR tool that, in the event of a high-criticality EDR alert (e.g., 'Mimikatz execution detected'), automatically triggers a script that deactivates the server's switch port or activates a host firewall rule for isolation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration of the API integration between EDR and SIEM/SOAR. They trigger a test alert and verify in the SOAR system and on the network switch/server that the automated isolation measure is successful and executed within seconds.

controls.title: Logging (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logging on servers is limited to the operating system's default settings. The logs are only stored locally on the servers and are overwritten after a short time. No analysis takes place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Windows Event Viewer is operated with the default size and settings. Important events are often overwritten within a few hours due to the small file size.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor opens the event viewer on a server and finds that the logs only go back a few hours or days and that no security-relevant events are specifically audited.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The size of the local log files on the servers is manually increased to ensure a longer retention period. Administrators look at the logs sporadically, especially after an incident.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The maximum size of the security event log is manually increased to 1 GB on all servers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the log file size and finds that although it has been increased, there is no process for central collection or regular analysis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In general, all security-relevant system events MUST be logged. This includes at least: system starts and reboots, successful and unsuccessful logins, failed permission checks, blocked data streams, setup or changes to users, groups, and permissions, security-relevant error messages, and warning messages from security systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The events to be logged are configured on all servers via central policies (e.g., GPOs). The log data from all servers is sent to a central log management system (e.g., Syslog-NG, Graylog, ELK stack), where it is stored in an audit-proof manner for a defined period.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the audit policies in the GPO. They select a server, generate a login event, and verify that this event arrives in the central log management system and is correctly interpreted. Automated check: `auditpol /get /category:*` is executed on a server and the result is compared with the defined policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The log data collected in the central log management system is automatically analyzed for suspicious activities and security incidents using predefined correlation rules. In case of detected patterns (e.g., brute-force attack), administrators are alerted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system, rules are configured that, for example, alert if more than 10 failed login attempts for the same user from different IPs are registered within one minute. The time of all systems is synchronized via NTP to ensure correct correlation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the correlation rules in the SIEM. They simulate an attack attempt (e.g., by repeatedly entering the wrong password) and verify that the SIEM generates and sends a corresponding alert.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The analysis of log data is enhanced by User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) algorithms that detect anomalies in the behavior of users and systems. The response to critical alerts is automated via a connected SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response) system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A UEBA module in the SIEM learns the normal behavior of administrators. If an admin account logs in at 3 a.m. from an unknown location and executes unusual commands, a high-criticality alert is triggered. A SOAR playbook then automatically locks the user account and isolates the affected server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the UEBA models and the SOAR playbooks. They discuss the effectiveness of the anomaly-based detection and the results of the automated responses from recent months with the analysts.

controls.title: Defining a security policy for servers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the institution's general security policy, the requirements for servers SHOULD be specified in a separate security policy. This policy SHOULD be known to all administrators and other persons involved in the procurement and operation of the servers and SHOULD be the basis for their work. The implementation of the content required in the policy SHOULD be checked regularly. The results SHOULD be documented appropriately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document 'Security Policy for Server Systems' is created, which regulates topics such as hardening, patch management, access control, logging, and data backup for servers in a binding manner. The document is published on the intranet and is part of the training materials for new administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the security policy for servers and checks its content for completeness and timeliness. They interview administrators to ensure that they are familiar with the policy and that it serves as a basis for their work. The results of the last internal review of the policy implementation are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The server security policy is supplemented by specific, technical baselines and configuration specifications for each type of server operating system used. Compliance with the policy is regularly checked through automated configuration scans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the general policy, there are detailed hardening guides for 'Windows Server 2022' and 'Ubuntu 22.04 LTS'. A scanner checks the server configurations against these specifications weekly. The results are displayed in a compliance dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the technical baselines for conformity with the parent policy and recognized standards (e.g., CIS). They review the configuration and reports of the compliance scanner to assess the effectiveness of the monitoring.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The technical specifications from the security policy are implemented as 'Policy as Code'. A configuration management tool continuously and automatically enforces these specifications on all servers. Any deviation is automatically corrected and reported, ensuring permanent policy compliance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The hardening specifications are codified in Ansible playbooks or Puppet manifests, which are versioned in Git and rolled out to the servers via a CI/CD pipeline. Every change to the 'Policy as Code' undergoes a formal review and approval process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the 'Policy as Code' inventory in the Git repository and the CI/CD pipeline. They review the logs of the configuration management tool to verify the complete and correct enforcement of policies across the entire server fleet.

controls.title: Planning of server deployment (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each server system SHOULD be planned appropriately. At a minimum, the following points SHOULD be considered: platform selection, hardware sizing, communication interfaces, power consumption, administrative access, user access, logging, updating, and integration into management and protection systems. All decisions SHOULD be documented in such a way that they can be traced at a later date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a new server is deployed, a standardized planning document is completed. This document captures all relevant aspects, from hardware requirements and network integration to the backup concept. The completed document is archived and becomes part of the server documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor selects recently commissioned servers on a sample basis and requests the associated planning documents. They check whether the documents are complete and whether the actual implementation corresponds to the plan.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning of server deployment is integrated into a formal requirements and architecture process. Hardware sizing is based on systematic load forecasts and performance tests. The security aspects of the planning, especially the integration into protection systems, are reviewed and approved by the Information Security Officer (ISO).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For new services, a load test scenario is defined and executed before server planning to precisely determine resource requirements. The planning document includes a dedicated section on security architecture, which must be countersigned by the ISO before the server is ordered or set up.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation for server planning. Using the planning documents and signatures, they verify that the ISO was systematically involved for security-relevant servers. They ask for the results of load tests for capacity-critical systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire server planning and provisioning process is part of an automated 'Infrastructure as Code' (IaC) workflow. Requirements are captured in a central system, which automatically defines the necessary resources (virtual machines, network segments, firewall rules, backup jobs) and provisions them via IaC tools. The documentation is automatically generated from the code definitions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A user requests a new web server via a service portal. This starts a CI/CD pipeline that executes Terraform code to create a VM in the cloud or on-premise, uses Ansible for configuration, registers the server in monitoring, and adjusts the firewall rules in the central management tool. The configuration is versioned in Git.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the IaC code in the repository and the associated CI/CD pipeline. They trace a deployment workflow from the request to the finished system and check whether all planning steps (security, network, backup) have been implemented correctly and automatically and whether the generated documentation is complete.

controls.title: Procurement of servers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before one or more servers are procured, a list of requirements SHOULD be created, against which the products available on the market are evaluated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standardized checklist is used for the procurement of server hardware. This includes functional requirements (CPU, RAM, storage) and non-functional requirements (e.g., management interface, power consumption, warranty conditions). The offers from various manufacturers are compared using this checklist, and the decision is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the procurement documents for recently acquired servers. They check the existence and completeness of the requirements list and verify that the product evaluation is documented in a traceable manner.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirements list for procurement contains explicit and detailed security requirements. These include requirements for the manufacturer's trustworthiness, supply chain security, and specific hardware security features such as TPM 2.0, Secure Boot, and a secure management interface (e.g., without outdated protocols).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The tender for new servers explicitly requires that the devices support TPM 2.0, that the manufacturer's firmware updates are signed, and that the management engine (e.g., iDRAC, iLO) supports modern encryption standards and does not rely on Java applets. Only manufacturers who provide transparent information about their Secure Development Lifecycle are considered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the tender documents and requirements lists for the explicit mention of security features. They compare the ordered models with the security requirements and check whether the required features are actually present and usable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution maintains a catalog of standardized and security-vetted server models (Golden Hardware). New procurements may only be made from this catalog. Supply chain security is actively verified, e.g., by checking seals or by initial commissioning in a quarantine environment to rule out tampering (interdiction).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is an internal website with 3-4 approved server models for different use cases, whose security configurations are fully documented. Newly delivered servers are started up in an isolated network, their firmware is flashed to a known good version, and the hardware configuration is checked against the order before the server is moved to the production environment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the process for adding new models to the hardware catalog and reviews the associated security assessments. They check the logs of the onboarding process for newly delivered hardware in the quarantine environment.

controls.title: Uninterruptible and stable power supply (S) [Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each server SHOULD be connected to an uninterruptible power supply (UPS).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All servers in a rack are connected to a rack UPS. The UPS is sized to provide enough time for a controlled shutdown of all connected servers in the event of a power outage. A shutdown agent is installed on the servers, which initiates the shutdown when the UPS battery level is low.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the server cabling in the rack and verifies that all power supplies are connected to a UPS. They check the configuration of the shutdown agent on the servers. They review the documentation of the last UPS maintenance and the last battery test.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Servers with redundant power supplies are connected to two separate power circuits (A/B supply). Each power circuit is protected by its own independent UPS. The status of the UPSs (battery charge, load, error messages) is centrally monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The first power supply of each server is connected to a PDU (Power Distribution Unit) powered by UPS-A. The second power supply is connected to a PDU powered by UPS-B. Both UPSs are connected to the central monitoring system (e.g., via SNMP), which alerts in case of failure or low battery.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor traces the power cabling from the server power supplies back to the PDUs and UPSs to confirm the redundant A/B supply. They check the configuration of the UPS monitoring and the alarm history in the monitoring system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The redundant UPS infrastructure is additionally secured by an emergency power system (EPS), e.g., a diesel generator, which can bridge a longer power outage. Regular, automated tests of the entire power supply chain, including switching to the EPS, are performed and logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The data center's power supply is designed with redundant UPS systems and an EPS with an automatic transfer switch (ATS). A monthly test run of the generator under load is performed. The results, including switchover times, are automatically logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the maintenance and test logs of the EPS and the UPS systems. If possible, they attend a scheduled test run to verify the correct functioning of the automatic transfer switch.

controls.title: Secure installation and basic configuration of servers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The complete installation and configuration process SHOULD be carried out as far as possible within a separate installation environment. The operating system configuration SHOULD be completed before the server is put into production. Several essential functions and roles SHOULD NOT be fulfilled by a single server but should be appropriately divided. All security-relevant settings SHOULD be configured, tested, and regularly reviewed according to the security policy. Configuration options SHOULD always be set, even if this does not change the preset default behavior. If the server requires an internet connection, it SHOULD only be connected after the installation and configuration are complete.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: New servers are installed and configured in a staging or quarantine network separate from the production network. Standardized installation images and configuration scripts (baselining) are used. The basic configuration includes hardening measures according to the internal policy. Only after completion and testing of the configuration is the server moved to the production network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the installation process for new servers described and demonstrated to them. They check the network configuration of the installation environment to verify the separation from the production network. They compare the configuration of a newly installed server with the specifications from the security policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation and basic configuration of servers is largely automated. Hardened operating system images (Golden Images) are used, which are regularly updated and checked for compliance with hardening benchmarks (e.g., CIS). The separation of functions is consistently enforced, e.g., through dedicated servers for databases, web applications, and authentication.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An image management solution (e.g., Packer) is used to create 'Golden Images' for Windows and Linux monthly. These images already contain all current patches and a hardened basic configuration. Deployment is automated via a deployment tool. The separation of roles is specified by clear server architecture documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the process and scripts for creating the golden images. They review the version history of the images and the results of the compliance scans. They analyze the server inventory to verify the enforcement of separation of duties.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Server installations are treated entirely as 'Infrastructure as Code' (IaC). The entire configuration, from operating system installation to application deployment, is defined in versioned code (e.g., Ansible, Terraform) and automated through a CI/CD pipeline. There are no more manual installation or configuration steps. Every configuration change is made exclusively through a code change with review and approval.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A new server is triggered by a Git commit in an IaC repository. A Jenkins or GitLab pipeline starts, runs Terraform to create the VM, and then applies an Ansible playbook to fully configure the system. The configuration is continuously monitored and deviations are automatically corrected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the IaC repository, the CI/CD pipeline configuration, and the commit history. They perform a 'dry run' of the pipeline to check the planned changes. They verify that manual configuration changes on the server are blocked or automatically rolled back.

controls.title: Setup of local packet filters (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Existing local packet filters SHOULD be configured with a ruleset to restrict incoming and outgoing communication to the required communication partners, communication protocols, as well as ports and interfaces. The identity of remote systems and the integrity of the connections with them SHOULD be cryptographically secured.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The host-based firewall (e.g., Windows Defender Firewall, iptables) is enabled on all servers. Configuration is done centrally via Group Policies or a configuration management tool. The ruleset follows a 'default deny' approach, where only explicitly defined communication is allowed (e.g., inbound TCP port 443 for a web server). Connections are secured using TLS/IPsec wherever possible.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the central policies for the host firewall. On a server, they check the active firewall rules and compare them with the documented function of the server. They perform a port scan to ensure that no unexpected ports are open. Automated check: `Get-NetFirewallRule -PolicyStore ActiveStore -Enabled True` is executed and compared with a baseline.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The ruleset of the local packet filter is dynamic and application-specific. It filters not only by port and protocol, but also by which process initiates the communication. The firewall rules are proactively monitored and unused rules are regularly removed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Windows Defender Firewall is configured with application-specific rules that, for example, only allow the 'httpd.exe' process to listen on port 80. A script is used that monthly checks the firewall rules for 'hit counts' and reports rules that were never used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules and verifies that they are tied to specific applications and services, rather than just opening ports. They review the logs of the script for identifying unused rules and the cleanup process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The host firewall is part of a comprehensive micro-segmentation strategy. The firewall rules are automatically generated and enforced based on application communication patterns. Any blocked communication is centrally logged, analyzed, and triggers alarms for suspicious patterns.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A micro-segmentation solution (e.g., VMware NSX, Illumio) is used. The solution learns the normal communication flows between servers in observation mode and then suggests a tailored, detailed set of rules. This is then switched to enforcement mode. All blocked connection attempts are forwarded to the SIEM for analysis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the console of the micro-segmentation solution. They analyze the visualized communication flows and the automatically generated rules for their correctness. They check the analysis of the blocked connection attempts and the resulting alarms in the SIEM.

controls.title: Operational documentation for servers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Operational tasks performed on a server SHOULD be documented in a traceable manner (Who?, When?, What?). In particular, configuration changes SHOULD be traceable from the documentation. Security-relevant tasks, e.g., who is authorized to install new hard drives, SHOULD be documented. Everything that can be documented automatically SHOULD also be documented automatically. The documentation SHOULD be protected against unauthorized access and loss.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An operations manual is maintained for each server in a central wiki (e.g., Confluence) or a CMDB. All manual configuration changes are recorded in a ticket system that is linked to the operations manual. Important changes are approved by a Change Advisory Board (CAB). The documentation is access-protected and regularly backed up.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor selects a server and requests the corresponding operations manual and the change history from the ticket system. They compare the documented state with the live system to assess the timeliness and correctness of the documentation. They check the access permissions to the documentation system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational documentation is largely automatically generated and kept up-to-date through the use of configuration management tools and automation scripts. Manual changes to the system that do not go through the defined process are detected and reported by configuration auditing tools.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script daily reads important configuration parameters of the servers (e.g., installed software, network configuration, disk usage) and automatically updates the corresponding pages in the wiki/CMDB. A configuration scanner compares the state of the servers with an approved baseline and reports deviations (configuration drift).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the scripts for automatic documentation creation. They review the reports of the configuration auditing tool and investigate how reported configuration drifts are responded to.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational documentation is fully realized as code ('Documentation as Code') and is an integral part of the 'Infrastructure as Code' (IaC) approach. The entire server configuration is declared in a versioned repository (e.g., Git). Changes to the configuration are made exclusively through code changes that go through a review and approval process. The readable documentation is automatically regenerated from the IaC files with every code change.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration of a server is described in Ansible playbooks and Terraform files. Comments in the code and separate Markdown files in the same Git repository form the documentation source. A CI/CD pipeline generates an HTML website with the current documentation upon every commit and deploys the configuration to the server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the IaC repository. They review the commit history, pull requests, and review comments to understand the change process. They compare the declared state in the code with the live system, where it is expected that these are identical. The audit focuses on the security and robustness of the code management and deployment process.

controls.title: Integration into contingency planning (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The server SHOULD be considered in the emergency management process. For this purpose, the emergency requirements for the server SHOULD be determined and suitable emergency measures SHOULD be implemented, e.g., by creating recovery plans or securely storing passwords and cryptographic keys.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each server, the required recovery time objective (RTO) and the maximum data loss (RPO) are determined as part of a Business Impact Analysis (BIA). Based on this, a recovery plan is created that describes the steps to restore the server (e.g., from a backup). Critical information such as passwords for local emergency accounts are stored in a central, secure password safe.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the BIA results and the recovery plans for a selection of servers. They check the plans for completeness, plausibility, and timeliness. They verify that the passwords and keys referenced in the plan are present in the password safe and accessible to the emergency team.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The recovery plans for critical servers are practically exercised regularly, at least once a year. The recovery is carried out in an isolated test environment to verify the functionality of the plans and the technical measures (e.g., backups). The results of the tests are documented and used to improve the plans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Once a year, a contingency drill is conducted in which the recovery of a critical database server from backup is simulated in a test environment separated from the production network. The time required is measured and compared with the RTO. Findings from the test (e.g., 'backup medium was faulty') are incorporated into an improvement plan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs and result reports of the last contingency drills. They check whether the identified deficiencies and potential for improvement have been tracked and implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the most important servers, high-availability, redundant architectures (e.g., failover clusters) are implemented that allow for automatic switching in case of failure. The recovery processes are largely automated (Disaster Recovery as Code). The functionality of the failover is continuously or at very short intervals automatically tested (Chaos Engineering).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Critical servers run as a failover cluster across two fire compartments or locations. The recovery of the entire application environment is mapped in automation scripts (e.g., Ansible, PowerShell DSC). A tool regularly introduces small, controlled disruptions (e.g., intentionally stopping a service) to test whether the automatic fault detection and correction works as expected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the architecture of the high-availability solution and the automation scripts for disaster recovery. They analyze the logs of the automated tests and the chaos engineering experiments to assess the resilience of the system.

controls.title: System supervision and monitoring of servers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The server system SHOULD be integrated into a suitable system supervision or monitoring concept. The system status as well as the functionality of the server and the services operated on it SHOULD be continuously monitored. Error states as well as the exceeding of defined limit values SHOULD be reported to the operating personnel.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All servers are integrated into a central monitoring system (e.g., Nagios, Zabbix, Prometheus). Standard metrics such as CPU load, memory consumption, disk space, and service availability (via port checks) are monitored. If defined thresholds are exceeded (e.g., > 90% disk usage), an email is automatically sent to the administrator team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the monitoring system. They select a server and verify which metrics are being monitored and whether the thresholds and alerting rules are defined sensibly. They simulate a failure (e.g., by stopping a service) and check if an alert is triggered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The monitoring not only supervises system metrics, but also application performance and end-user experience (Application Performance Monitoring, APM). Trends and anomalies in the performance data are analyzed to proactively indicate emerging problems before they lead to an outage.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An APM tool is used that instruments the application code to measure the duration of database queries and web requests. The monitoring system uses anomaly detection algorithms to alert, for example, when the average response time of an application suddenly increases for no apparent reason.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the dashboards of the APM tool and analyzes the collected performance data. They discuss with the administrators how proactive warnings and detected anomalies are handled. They check the configuration of the anomaly detection algorithms.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The monitoring is fully integrated into AIOps (AI for IT Operations) processes. The system automatically correlates metrics, logs, and traces from various sources to identify the root cause of problems (Root Cause Analysis). Simple problems are solved through self-healing by connecting to an automation system (SOAR/RPA), e.g., by restarting a service or scaling resources.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An AIOps platform is used. If the system correlates a high CPU load, an increase in errors in the application log, and a slow response time for a specific service, it identifies a faulty process as the cause. It then automatically triggers an Ansible playbook that restarts the service and creates a ticket for tracking.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration of the AIOps platform and the automation workflows built on it. They analyze the logs of detected incidents and the corresponding automated remediation actions to assess their effectiveness and reliability.

controls.title: Security checks for servers (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Servers SHOULD undergo regular security tests that verify compliance with all security requirements and identify any existing vulnerabilities. These security tests SHOULD be performed in particular on servers with external interfaces. To avoid indirect attacks via infected IT systems on the internal network, internal servers SHOULD also be tested accordingly in defined cycles. It SHOULD be checked whether the security tests can be implemented in an automated manner, e.g., using suitable scripts.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A vulnerability scanner (e.g., Nessus, OpenVAS) is used to scan all servers on the network monthly for known vulnerabilities (CVEs) and common misconfigurations. The scans are performed authenticated to obtain a detailed view of the installed software and configuration. The reports are forwarded to the administrators for processing.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and scheduling of the vulnerability scanner. They analyze the scan reports from the last few months and check whether the identified vulnerabilities (especially critical ones) have been remediated in a timely manner. This can be done by comparing reports over time or by checking the patch management system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to automated vulnerability scans, manual penetration tests are conducted by external or internal specialists at regular intervals or after major changes for particularly critical or exposed servers (e.g., web servers in the DMZ). The results are fed into the risk management process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An external penetration test is commissioned annually for the online shop server. The test report is analyzed by the ISO and the system owners. The vulnerabilities found are evaluated in the risk management system and assigned remediation measures, the implementation of which is tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the reports of the last penetration tests. They check whether the findings and recommendations contained therein have been systematically assessed and processed and whether the corrective actions have been implemented and their effectiveness reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security tests are part of a continuous and proactive program. This includes 'Red Teaming' exercises, which attempt to penetrate systems undetected and achieve objectives, as well as the use of 'Breach and Attack Simulation' (BAS) platforms, which continuously and automatically test attack paths against the servers and validate the effectiveness of the defensive measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A BAS platform is implemented that executes hundreds of simulated attack techniques (according to the MITRE ATT&CK Framework) against the servers daily. The system checks which attacks would be successful and which are detected and blocked by existing security solutions (EDR, firewall). The results are visualized in a dashboard to show security gaps in real time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration and reports of the BAS platform. They analyze the results of the simulations and assess how the company prioritizes and remediates the identified weaknesses in the defense mechanisms. They discuss the results of the last red teaming exercise with management.

controls.title: Controlled decommissioning of a server (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When decommissioning a server, it SHOULD be ensured that no important data is lost and that no sensitive data remains. There SHOULD be an overview of what data is stored where on the server. It SHOULD be ensured in a timely manner that services offered by the server are taken over by another server. A checklist SHOULD be created that can be worked through when decommissioning a server. This checklist SHOULD include at least aspects of data backup, migration of services, and the subsequent secure deletion of all data.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a standardized process for decommissioning servers, supported by a checklist. The process includes: 1. Identification and migration of all services and data. 2. Creation of a final backup. 3. Secure deletion of data on the hard drives according to a recognized method (e.g., with a tool like `shred` or `DBAN`). 4. Removal of the server from all management systems (Monitoring, DNS, CMDB). The completed protocol is archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the decommissioning protocols for recently decommissioned servers. They check the completeness of the completed checklists and, in particular, the proof of secure data erasure. They check in the management systems whether the server objects have actually been removed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The decommissioning process is largely automated. The checklist is processed by an automation script or a workflow in a service management tool. The secure deletion of data is carried out by certified erasure software that creates a tamper-proof report.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the service management tool (e.g., ServiceNow), a decommissioning workflow is started. This executes scripts to automatically remove the server from DNS, Active Directory, and monitoring. For data erasure, a commercial solution like Blancco is used, which generates a detailed, signed erasure report that is automatically attached to the ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the decommissioning workflow in the service management tool. They check the configuration of the automation steps and analyze the generated erasure certificates for their authenticity and completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data carriers in servers are encrypted by default (Full Disk Encryption). During decommissioning, instead of time-consuming data erasure, the 'Crypto Shredding' method is used, where only the cryptographic key is securely and verifiably destroyed, making the data on the data carrier irretrievably unreadable. For physical disposal, the data carriers are additionally mechanically destroyed (shredded).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All servers use Self-Encrypting Drives (SEDs) or software-based full-disk encryption. The decommissioning process includes the command to securely destroy the key in the Key Management System (KMS). The physical data carrier is then removed and destroyed in a certified shredder on-site. The entire process is recorded on video and logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the crypto shredding process by reviewing the KMS logs for key destruction. They review the logs and video recordings of the mechanical destruction of the data carriers.

controls.title: Creation and maintenance of an operations manual (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An operations manual SHOULD be created. It SHOULD document all necessary regulations, requirements, and settings required to operate servers. There SHOULD be a specific operations manual for each type of server. The operations manual SHOULD be updated regularly. The operations manual SHOULD be protected from unauthorized access and be available in emergencies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each server role (web server, database server, etc.), a template for an operations manual is created in a central wiki (e.g., Confluence). When commissioning a new server, a copy of this template is created and filled with the specific details of the server (IP addresses, installed applications, configuration details, backup job, etc.). The manuals are subject to access control and are regularly reviewed by the team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly selects servers and requests the corresponding operations manuals. They check them for completeness, up-to-dateness (comparison with the live system), and clarity. They verify that the documentation is access-protected and would also be available in an emergency (e.g., offline).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Large parts of the operations manual are automatically generated from configuration management databases (CMDB), monitoring systems, and automation scripts. The manual is dynamic and reflects the current configuration state. There is a formal review process for all manual changes to the documentation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The operations manual in the wiki is dynamically enriched with data from the CMDB (e.g., for master data), monitoring (e.g., for current performance data), and the backup system (e.g., for the status of the last backup) via APIs. A script generates a daily report on discrepancies between the documentation and reality.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the automation workflows for documentation generation. They check the accuracy of the automatically inserted data. They analyze the review process for manual entries to ensure its effectiveness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no longer a separate, text-based operations manual. The entire configuration and operational state are represented as code in an 'Infrastructure as Code' (IaC) and 'Configuration as Code' framework. The documentation is the code itself, supplemented by comments and automatically generated diagrams and reports. 'What needs to be done' is defined directly in the executable code.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The answer to the question 'How is the web server configured?' is a reference to a specific Ansible playbook in a Git repository. The answer to 'What to do if the service fails?' is a reference to a SOAR playbook that automates the recovery. The documentation is always in sync with the implementation because it is the same source.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor directly audits the code (Terraform, Ansible, etc.) in the repository. The audit focuses on the readability, commenting, and inherent logic of the code. They check whether the automation workflows completely and reliably replace the traditional instructions of an operations manual.

controls.title: Encapsulation of security-critical applications and operating system components (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To prevent both unauthorized access to the operating system or other applications during attacks and access from the operating system to particularly sensitive files, applications and operating system components SHOULD be specially encapsulated or isolated from other applications and operating system components according to their protection needs. In this context, special consideration SHOULD be given to security-critical applications that handle data from untrusted sources (e.g., web browsers and office communication applications).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Applications are run with dedicated service accounts with minimal permissions. Sensitive services, such as a Public Key Infrastructure (PKI), are operated on dedicated, hardened servers that are strictly isolated from the rest of the network. Administrative tasks are performed via dedicated jump hosts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the service accounts and their permissions. They analyze the network firewall rules for particularly sensitive servers to verify isolation. They check the configuration and access logs of the jump host.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Applications, especially high-risk ones, are isolated from the host operating system using virtualization or containerization. A separate, minimal container with only the absolutely necessary libraries and dependencies is created for each application.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Web applications are no longer installed directly on the host operating system but are run as Docker containers. The container images are based on hardened, minimal base images (e.g., 'distroless' or Alpine Linux). Communication between containers is controlled via a container network with its own firewall rules.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the Dockerfiles and the configuration of the container orchestration platform (e.g., Kubernetes). They scan the container images for vulnerabilities. They review the network policies that govern traffic between containers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Advanced technologies for runtime isolation and application protection are used, such as OS-level sandboxing or hardware-assisted virtualization (e.g., Intel SGX, AMD SEV) for processing particularly sensitive data. Each application runs in a highly restricted environment that only allows explicitly permitted system calls (Seccomp, AppArmor).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Critical cryptographic operations are performed in a Secure Enclave (Intel SGX), so that not even the host operating system has access to the keys. Detailed Seccomp and AppArmor profiles are defined for containers, restricting access to kernel functions to an absolute minimum. Any violation of these profiles is alerted and blocked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the code running in the Secure Enclaves, as well as the configuration of the Seccomp and AppArmor profiles. They analyze the system logs for alarms triggered by attempted policy violations. They perform tests to verify that disallowed system calls from within a container are blocked.

controls.title: Central management of server security policies (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All server settings SHOULD be managed using a central management system and configured according to the determined protection requirements and internal policies. Configuration parameters that cannot be technically implemented SHOULD be documented, justified, and coordinated with security management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Security-relevant settings for Windows servers are centrally managed via Group Policies (GPOs) in Active Directory. For Linux servers, a configuration management tool like Ansible or Puppet is used in 'push' mode to regularly apply configuration baselines. Deviations necessary for compatibility reasons are recorded in an exception document with justification and risk assessment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the GPOs and the configuration of the configuration management tool. They compare the central specifications with the local configuration of a server to verify correct application. They check the document with the approved exceptions for completeness and plausibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central management system not only checks the configuration but also actively enforces it. Manual changes to security-relevant settings are automatically detected and reported. The compliance of all servers with the central policies is visualized in a dashboard.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) runs in 'daemon' mode or is called by a regular cron job. It not only configures but also monitors the state. A configuration drift is displayed as 'non-compliant' in the central dashboard and triggers a ticket for the admin team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor intentionally changes a security-relevant setting on a test server. They verify that this deviation is displayed in the compliance dashboard and that a notification is sent. They check the historical compliance data to assess response times to deviations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central management system is set to a 'self-healing' mode. Any unauthorized configuration change on a server is not only reported but also automatically reverted to the target state defined in the policy within minutes. The policies themselves are managed as code ('Policy as Code') in a versioned repository.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The server security policies are codified in Puppet manifests or Ansible playbooks, which are stored in a Git repository. The configuration management tool is configured to actively enforce the declared state. If an administrator manually changes a firewall rule, it is automatically reset to the state defined in the code on the next run of the tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the 'Policy as Code' repository and the associated review process for changes. They deliberately change a configuration on a server and verify that the change is automatically and promptly reverted. They check the system's logs for reports of such automatic corrections.

controls.title: Host-based Intrusion Detection (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Host-based intrusion detection systems (IDS) or intrusion prevention systems (IPS) are deployed on critical servers. The systems are operated with standard rule sets to detect known attack patterns. Alarms are forwarded to the administrators.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A host-based IDS (e.g., OSSEC) is installed on the web servers in the DMZ. It monitors the integrity of system files and alerts on suspicious log entries. The alerts are sent by email to a central mailbox.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the installation and configuration of the HIDS on the critical servers. They check the alarm chain and analyze the alarms received in the central mailbox over the past few weeks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Host-based Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Intrusion Prevention Systems (IPS) SHOULD be used to monitor system behavior for anomalies and misuse. The IDS/IPS mechanisms used SHOULD be appropriately selected, configured, and thoroughly tested. In the event of an attack detection, the operating personnel SHOULD be alerted in an appropriate manner. Changes to system files and configuration settings SHOULD be checked, restricted, and reported via operating system mechanisms or suitable additional products.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A modern Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solution is rolled out on all servers. This monitors not only signatures but also process behavior, system calls, and network connections. The alarms are reported to a central console and enriched with context information. A File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) is activated to report changes to critical configuration files.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the central EDR console. They check the configuration of the detection rules and the FIM. They simulate a suspicious action (e.g., running a PowerShell command for privilege escalation) and verify that a detailed alarm is generated in the console.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The host-based intrusion detection is fully integrated into a SIEM and SOAR system. The EDR solution operates in prevention mode (IPS) and proactively blocks suspicious activities. Critical alarms trigger automated responses, such as network isolation of the server, creation of a memory dump for forensics, and deactivation of the compromised user account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The EDR solution is configured to immediately block the execution of processes classified as malicious (e.g., Mimikatz). At the same time, a SOAR playbook is triggered via an API, which moves the server to a quarantine VLAN and locks the associated user account in Active Directory.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration of the IPS rules in the EDR solution and the associated SOAR playbooks. They conduct a controlled test to trigger a malicious action and verify that the entire chain of automated blocking and response measures is executed correctly and within the expected time.

controls.title: Increasing availability through redundancy (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Servers with high availability requirements are equipped with redundant hardware components such as power supplies and network cards. Recovery in the event of a failure is performed manually according to the specifications of the recovery plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Critical servers are ordered and operated with two power supplies and two network cards (in bonding mode). If a component fails, a warning is triggered by the monitoring system, and a technician manually replaces the defective component.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the hardware inventory list and the physical servers for the presence of redundant components. They check the monitoring system logs for alarms regarding hardware failures and the associated remediation tickets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Servers with high availability requirements SHOULD be appropriately protected against failures. For this purpose, at least suitable redundancies SHOULD be available and maintenance contracts SHOULD be concluded with suppliers. It SHOULD be checked whether high-availability architectures with automatic failover are required for very high requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For critical services, active/passive or active/active failover clusters (e.g., Windows Server Failover Clustering, Pacemaker for Linux) are implemented. If the active server node fails, the passive node automatically takes over the services. Maintenance contracts with a guaranteed response time (e.g., 4 hours) are in place for the hardware.

parts.name: assessment-method
