Based on the intended use and the underlying protection requirements, it SHOULD be evaluated which of the functions 'Lock Screen', 'Unified Communication', 'Siri', 'Wallpaper', 'Connection to Host Systems', and 'Diagnostics & Usage Data' are to be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented decision is made as to which iOS functions are disabled for business use based on a risk assessment. These decisions are technically implemented via the 'Restrictions' payload in the MDM configuration profile.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the risk assessment and the resulting configuration decisions. The MDM configuration is checked to ensure that the defined restrictions have been correctly implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of restrictions is granular and adapted to different user groups and protection requirement scenarios. For example, users with access to sensitive data have stricter restrictions than others. The configurations are regularly reviewed and adapted for new iOS features.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the MDM, several configuration profiles for restrictions are stored, which are assigned to different groups (e.g., via LDAP/AD groups). There is a defined process to evaluate new available restrictions for new iOS versions and to update the profiles.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the different restriction profiles and their assignment to user groups in the MDM. It is checked whether a process exists for adapting the profiles to new iOS versions and whether this is demonstrably carried out (e.g., through change documentation).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the restrictions is permanently monitored by an automated compliance engine in the MDM. Any manual change to a setting by the user that contradicts a policy (if technically possible) is detected and automatically corrected or reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM continuously performs compliance checks on the endpoints. If the state of a setting deviates from the specification in the profile, this is reported in the compliance dashboard. For critical settings, automatic correction (auto-remediation) is configured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the compliance engine and the auto-remediation rules in the MDM. The compliance reports and logs are analyzed. As a test, an attempt is made to use a restricted function to verify the effectiveness of the monitoring.

controls.title: Use of the iCloud infrastructure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of iCloud is not explicitly regulated and is left to the users. There is no formal assessment of the risks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users activate iCloud services at their own discretion, often with their private Apple ID. Business data such as contacts, calendars, or even documents can end up uncontrolled in the user's private iCloud.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly questions users about whether and for what purpose they use iCloud on their company device. In the device settings, it is checked which iCloud services are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a general policy that prohibits the use of iCloud for business data. However, this is only communicated organizationally and not enforced by technical measures in the MDM.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A clause in the user agreement for mobile devices prohibits the storage of company data in iCloud. However, there are no MDM profiles that technically disable iCloud services.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the user agreement and checks the corresponding clause. On sample devices, it is verified whether users could technically activate iCloud services despite the organizational rule, or have already activated them.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before the extensive or selective use of the iCloud infrastructure is approved for business use, it SHOULD be assessed whether the general terms and conditions of Apple Inc. are compatible with internal policies regarding availability, confidentiality, integrity, and data protection. Based on this assessment, a clear policy for the use or prohibition of iCloud functions is created and implemented via MDM.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal risk assessment for the use of iCloud is conducted and documented. Based on the result, a policy is created and implemented via an MDM profile that disables the use of iCloud in general or specific functions (e.g., iCloud Drive, Backup).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the risk assessment and the iCloud policy. The configuration of the corresponding MDM profile is checked to ensure that the policy's requirements are technically implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: iCloud usage is granularly controlled via MDM. This allows non-critical functions (e.g., synchronization of contacts via a managed Apple ID) to be permitted, while critical functions (e.g., iCloud Backup, iCloud Drive) are blocked for business data. If usage is permitted, identity at the iCloud web service SHOULD be verified by two-factor authentication.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM profile is configured to allow differentiated control of iCloud services. For all managed Apple IDs that are allowed to use iCloud, two-factor authentication (2FA) is enforced. Use for purely business purposes is reduced to a minimum or completely excluded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the MDM profile for the granular configuration of iCloud services. It is checked in Apple Business Manager or the MDM whether 2FA is enforced for the managed Apple IDs used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data flows to iCloud services are actively monitored by a Cloud Access Security Broker (CASB) or comparable technology to ensure policy compliance. Only those iCloud features are used that are explicitly designed for businesses and offer contractual guarantees regarding data protection and security.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All network traffic from mobile devices is routed through a CASB solution. This detects and blocks attempts to upload sensitive company data to unapproved iCloud services or private accounts. Contracts such as Apple's 'Advanced Data Protection for iCloud' feature are evaluated and used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and policies in the CASB. The CASB logs are analyzed for blocked or reported incidents. The contractual agreements with Apple regarding the used business features are reviewed.

controls.title: Use of Continuity features

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The Continuity features (e.g., Handoff, Universal Clipboard) are enabled by default, and there are no regulations or assessments regarding their security implications.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users can answer calls from their iPhone on their Mac or copy text from one device to another without an assessment of the associated risks of data flow between potentially differently secured devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor tests on a company iPhone and a connected computer (Mac) whether Continuity features like Handoff or Universal Clipboard are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an organizational recommendation not to transfer sensitive data via Continuity features. However, there is no technical deactivation or restriction.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A security policy or user guide points out the risks of the Continuity features. The responsibility for secure use lies with the user.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the relevant policies and checks whether users are informed about the risks. It is verified that no technical controls are implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If the use of the iCloud infrastructure has not been fundamentally prohibited by the institution's security management, the compatibility of the Continuity features with internal policies SHOULD be assessed, taking into account confidentiality and integrity aspects. Based on the assessment results, it SHOULD be regulated to what extent these features are to be technically or organizationally restricted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A risk assessment is conducted that analyzes the dangers of data leaks through Continuity features. Based on the result, it is decided whether features like Handoff or Universal Clipboard must be disabled via an MDM profile.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the risk assessment. The MDM profile is checked to see if the 'Allow Handoff' feature has been disabled, if the assessment deemed it necessary.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The Continuity features are disabled by default via the MDM profile. Users can only get them enabled after a justified request and a new risk assessment. The policies apply across devices, especially in conjunction with also-managed macOS systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default MDM profile for all iOS and macOS devices disables Continuity. A separate profile that enables the feature is only assigned upon request and after approval by a supervisor and the information security officer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that Continuity is disabled in the default profile. The process for requesting and approving an exception is checked for its traceability and documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of Continuity features is not only configured via MDM, but their activity is also monitored (as far as technically possible) on the endpoints and in the network to detect unauthorized data transfers between devices in different security zones (e.g., private and business).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Endpoint protection solutions (EDR/MTD) on the iOS and macOS devices monitor processes and data flows. Rules are configured to detect and alert on the transfer of data with specific classifications via the Universal Clipboard. Network firewalls monitor the peer-to-peer traffic used for Continuity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the monitoring rules in the EDR/MTD solution. A test is conducted by attempting to copy data marked as 'confidential' to see if an alarm is triggered. The logs of the SIEM system are checked for corresponding events.

controls.title: Use of the device passcode history

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The complexity of the device passcode is defined, but there is no restriction on reusing old codes. Users can switch back and forth between two codes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Although a minimum length for the code is set in the MDM profile, the 'Number of previous passwords that cannot be reused' (Passcode History) option is not configured or is set to 0.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the MDM passcode profile and determines that the code history is not enforced. A user is asked to change their code and immediately change it back to the old one to verify this.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Reuse of the immediately preceding device code is prevented (history of 1). A longer history is not enforced.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The passcode history in the MDM profile is set to 1. This prevents switching back directly but allows alternating between three different codes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the value for the passcode history in the MDM profile and verifies that it is set to 1. It is checked whether this is considered sufficient for the organization's protection needs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the configuration profile, the number of unique codes until the first repetition SHOULD be set to an appropriate value to prevent the reuse of old device codes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the passcode profile of the MDM, the option to enforce a passcode history is activated and set to an appropriate value, e.g., 5. This forces users to actually use new codes when changing them.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies in the MDM configuration that the passcode history is enabled and set to a value of at least 5 (or another value defined as appropriate). Compliance is ensured through the MDM's compliance reports.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The device code history is set to a high value (e.g., 10 or more). This setting is combined with other passcode policies, such as a maximum passcode age, to enforce regular renewal of the code.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the MDM profile, both the passcode history (e.g., to 10) and a maximum passcode age (e.g., 90 days) are configured. This ensures that codes are changed regularly and cannot be reverted to recently used ones.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the MDM passcode profile and verifies that both a high history count and a maximum passcode age are configured. It is checked whether the combination of values is reasonable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the device code history policy is checked by automated compliance checks of the MDM. Additionally, the policy is supplemented by enforcing biometric authentication (Face ID/Touch ID), so that the complex code needs to be entered less frequently, but unfolds its full protective effect when needed (e.g., after a restart).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The passcode policy (incl. history, complexity, age) is combined with the policy for using Face ID/Touch ID. The MDM continuously monitors compliance with these combined policies. A non-compliant device (e.g., because the user disables biometrics) is automatically excluded from accessing corporate resources until compliance is restored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the combined passcode and biometrics policies in the MDM as well as the associated automated compliance actions. A test is conducted by attempting to disable biometrics on a device to check the system's correct response (e.g., revocation of certificates or network access).

controls.title: Use of the configuration option for the Safari browser

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Safari is used without specific security configurations. Reliance is placed on Apple's default settings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: No MDM profile is distributed to configure Safari. All settings such as cookie management, pop-up blocker, or fraud warnings remain in the user's hands.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies in the MDM that no configuration for Safari is distributed. On a device, it is checked which default settings are active and whether they can be changed by the user.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Some basic security features of Safari are enabled via MDM, but there is no full adoption and adaptation of the existing institutional browser policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An MDM profile enforces a few settings, e.g., enabling the pop-up blocker and the fraud warning. A detailed adaptation to the desktop browser policy does not take place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the distributed MDM profile and compares the configured Safari settings with the institution's general browser policy to identify gaps.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The browser policies already established in the institution SHOULD also be implemented for Safari through technical and organizational measures. In doing so, the already established requirements for browsers on stationary and portable PCs, as well as the use case scenarios, SHOULD serve as the basis for securing the iOS-based devices. The operational environment of the devices SHOULD be considered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The existing policy for secure browser configuration is analyzed and the applicable points are transferred to an MDM configuration profile for Safari. This typically includes settings for blocking pop-ups, enforcing fraud warnings, managing cookies, and disabling AutoFill.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the institutional browser policy with the MDM configuration profile for Safari. They check whether all relevant and technically feasible settings have been configured for Safari. The effectiveness of the settings is verified on an endpoint device.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the basic configuration, advanced security measures are implemented. This includes configuring a web content filter to block access to malicious or unwanted websites, as well as centrally managing bookmarks for trusted corporate applications.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A web content filter payload is distributed via MDM, which either blocks categories of websites (e.g., gambling, malware) or only allows a whitelist of permitted domains. Additionally, important internal links are provided to users as 'Managed Web Clips' or bookmarks on the home screen.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the web content filter in the MDM. They attempt to access a blocked website to test the effectiveness of the filter. They check whether the managed bookmarks appear correctly on the device.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All web traffic from Safari is routed through a Secure Web Gateway (SWG) or an MTD solution, which provides real-time phishing and malware protection and enables in-depth content analysis (DLP). All security-relevant browser settings are continuously checked for compliance via MDM and automatically corrected in case of deviations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A global HTTP proxy profile or a VPN configuration in MDM routes all device traffic through an SWG cloud solution. This solution scans the traffic for threats and checks for data leaks. The compliance of the Safari settings is continuously monitored by the MDM and restored if necessary.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the global proxy or VPN in the MDM. The policies in the SWG are analyzed. A test is conducted with a known phishing test page or by downloading a test malware file (EICAR) to verify detection by the SWG.

controls.title: App Installation and Apple App Store Integration

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users can freely install apps from the App Store. There is only an informal list of recommended or forbidden apps.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The installation of apps is not restricted in the MDM profile. Compliance with app guidelines is not monitored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks on a sample device whether the App Store is accessible and whether unauthorized apps are installed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation of new apps by the user is blocked via an MDM profile. All required apps must be pre-installed on the device by IT operations. Apple Business Manager is not yet used for flexible app assignment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM profile prohibits the use of the App Store. If a user needs a new app, they must create a ticket, and an administrator installs the app manually or assigns it via MDM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the App Store is blocked on the devices. The process for installing new apps is checked for its feasibility and efficiency.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To ensure that authorized users have sufficient access to the necessary apps at the right time, integrating Apple Business Manager into the MDM infrastructure SHOULD be considered. The use of the public App Store is restricted or blocked, and apps are instead procured centrally and installed on devices in a targeted manner via MDM.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Apple App Store is blocked for users. Apps are licensed through the Apple Business Manager's volume licensing program and managed via MDM. They can either be automatically installed (pushed) to devices or made available to users in a controlled catalog.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of Apple Business Manager with the MDM. It is checked whether the public App Store is blocked and whether app distribution is handled via MDM. The inventory of licensed apps is reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A corporate app catalog (self-service portal) is provided via MDM, from which users can independently install a selection of approved and vetted apps. Payments in the App Store SHOULD NOT be confirmed using biometric methods, as app distribution is managed centrally and at no cost to the user.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM provides a self-service app or web portal where users can see all apps approved for their role and install them as needed. Since all apps are provided through volume licensing, no payments or password entries are required in the App Store. The option to make in-app purchases or confirm payments biometrically is disabled via MDM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the self-service catalog and tests the installation of an app. It is verified in the MDM profile that in-app purchases and biometric confirmation for payments are disabled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire app lifecycle (installation, update, uninstallation) is fully automated and controlled by the MDM. A Mobile Application Management (MAM) solution checks apps for security vulnerabilities and unwanted behavior before they are approved. App-specific configurations (Managed App Config) are also centrally specified.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before a new app or an update is released in the self-service catalog, it undergoes an automated scan (e.g., through integration of an app reputation database). Critical updates for apps are rolled out automatically to all devices without user interaction. For apps like email clients or browsers, the server settings and security configurations are centrally distributed via 'Managed App Config'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the process for approving new apps and checks the integration of the security scan. The configuration for automatic app updating is verified in the MDM. The 'Managed App Config' for a key application (e.g., email) is analyzed to ensure that no sensitive configuration data needs to be entered by the user.

controls.title: Use of the automatic configuration profile deletion feature

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The automatic deletion feature is known but not used. The company relies on the manual decommissioning of lost or long-unused devices by IT operations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is no automated rule. IT operations sporadically check the list of devices and manually delete those that have not been online for a long time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the process for handling inactive devices and determines that it is manual and not systematic. It is verified in the MDM configuration that no automatic deletion function is configured.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automatic deletion of the configuration profile is configured, but with a very long period (e.g., > 90 days). There is no proactive notification to the user before the deletion occurs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In MDM, a rule for automatic deletion after 120 days of inactivity is set up. This serves as a final security measure, but not as a proactive management tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the setting for automatic deletion in the MDM configuration and assesses whether the configured period is appropriate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An MDM feature is configured to automatically delete the configuration profile and its associated corporate data from the device if it has not connected to the MDM server for a defined period. As a result, offline devices lose access to internal resources after a certain time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A compliance policy is created in the MDM console that specifies that devices that have not checked in for, e.g., 60 days, automatically receive a command to delete the corporate profile.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of this compliance policy in the MDM, including the time period and the associated action (e.g., 'Remove MDM Profile' or 'Corporate Wipe').

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The period for automatic deletion is adapted to the data protection requirements (e.g., 30 days). Users SHOULD be automatically notified before the deadline and prompted to connect the device. If a device connects before the deadline, the counter SHOULD be reset automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tiered rules are configured: After 20 days of inactivity, the user receives an email notification. After 25 days, the supervisor receives a notification. After 30 days, the profile is automatically deleted. If the device checks in, the process is reset.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the multi-level compliance policy and the configured notifications in the MDM. It is checked whether the time periods are appropriate for the organization's protection needs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process is fully automated and integrated into the asset management and IAM processes. A device whose profile has been deleted is automatically marked in asset management as 'inactive' or 'potentially lost'. In addition, the deletion of the profile triggers further actions, such as blocking the associated user account for mobile access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM is connected to the IT Asset Management system (ITAM) and Identity and Access Management (IAM) via APIs. The deletion of the profile by the inactivity rule triggers a webhook or API call that updates the device status in ITAM and blocks the user account in IAM for mobile access (e.g., via Conditional Access Policies).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the API integrations between MDM, ITAM, and IAM. A past case is traced using logs. The configuration of the automated actions (webhooks, API calls) is analyzed to ensure correct functionality.

controls.title: Use of the configuration option for AirPrint

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: AirPrint is enabled, and users can connect to any AirPrint printer visible on the network without any central management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: No MDM configuration for AirPrint is distributed. Users may accidentally send sensitive information to a wrong or unsecured printer on the same Wi-Fi network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor connects a test device to the Wi-Fi and checks which printers are visible via AirPrint. It is verified that no restrictions are configured.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The AirPrint function is disabled by default via an MDM profile to generally prevent printing from mobile devices. There is no configuration for approved printers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the MDM profile, the use of AirPrint is generally prohibited ('Allow AirPrint' is set to 'No'). This is a simple but restrictive measure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the MDM profile and verifies that AirPrint is disabled. It is checked whether this restrictive stance meets the business requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Shared AirPrint printers SHOULD be provided to users via a configuration profile. To prevent users from printing information on untrusted printers, all communication connections SHOULD always be routed through the institution's infrastructure systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An MDM profile distributes a list of approved AirPrint printers (based on their IP address and resource path) to the devices. This ensures that users only see these printers in their print dialog and cannot use other, unsecured printers on the network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner analyzes the AirPrint configuration profile in the MDM and compares the list of printers with the official list of company printers. It is verified on a test device that only the configured printers are available for selection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to assigning shared printers, it is ensured that all print communication is encrypted (IPPS) and routed through the institution's secure infrastructure, such as a dedicated and hardened print server.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The printers configured in the MDM profile use the IPPS (IPP over TLS) protocol. The printers are located in a separate, protected network segment (VLAN), and communication from the mobile devices is routed through a central print server that controls access rights.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner checks the AirPrint configuration for the use of IPPS. The network architecture and the configuration of the print server are analyzed to verify the secure forwarding of print jobs. A network analysis can confirm the encryption of the print data.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A 'Secure Pull Printing' solution is integrated. Jobs sent from iOS devices are sent to a virtual printer queue and are cached on a server. They are only physically printed after the user authenticates directly at the printer (e.g., with a smart card or PIN).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A print management solution such as PaperCut or YSoft is implemented. The MDM profile for AirPrint points to the virtual queue of this solution. The printers are equipped with card readers or PIN pads. This solution prevents confidential printouts from being forgotten in the output tray and enables accurate billing and logging.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner is shown a demonstration of the pull-printing solution's architecture. A print job is sent from an iOS device, and the process of authentication at the printer and the release of the printout is tested live. The configuration of the virtual queue in the MDM and on the print server is checked.

controls.title: No connection with host systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are no restrictions. Users can connect their work iOS devices via USB to any computer, including private ones, create backups, or synchronize data.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The function for pairing with host systems is not restricted by MDM. This poses a high risk of data leakage and malware injection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner connects a corporate iOS device to an unauthorized laptop and checks if a connection (e.g., in Finder or iTunes) and data exchange are possible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an organizational directive that prohibits users from connecting corporate iOS devices to private or untrusted computers. However, there is no technical enforcement.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The usage policy for mobile devices contains a clause that prohibits connecting to non-company-managed computers. Compliance is based on user trust.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner requests the usage policy and checks the corresponding clause. It is verified that no technical control is configured in the MDM profile.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To prevent iOS-based devices from being connected to other IT systems without authorization, users SHOULD only be able to connect iOS-based devices to the MDM. The ability to connect iOS devices to a host system via USB is technically prevented via an MDM profile.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the MDM configuration profile for restrictions, the 'Allow pairing with non-Supervising host' option is disabled. This prevents the device from establishing a trust relationship with a computer, which blocks data exchange.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner verifies in the MDM profile that pairing with hosts is disabled. An attempt is made to connect a device to a computer. The 'Trust This Computer?' prompt should not appear, or the connection should fail.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Pairing with hosts is generally prohibited. For legitimate use cases (e.g., support by IT operations), a special configuration profile can be temporarily assigned that allows pairing with a certificate-based authenticated host system of the support team. After the support case, the restriction is reactivated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default for all devices is to prohibit pairing. The IT support team has a special Mac with Apple Configurator whose supervision certificate is stored in the MDM. Pairing is only possible with this host. Alternatively, the support team can temporarily assign a different profile to a device that allows pairing.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner is shown a demonstration of the support process. The configuration of the default profile (pairing prohibited) and the support profile (pairing allowed) in the MDM is analyzed. The process for assigning and revoking the support profile is checked for documentation and traceability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any attempt to pair a device with an unauthorized host is detected and blocked by a Mobile Threat Defense (MTD) solution on the endpoint. The incident is logged centrally and triggers an alert. The only allowed connection is the wireless one to the MDM system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the MDM restriction, an MTD app is installed on all devices. This app monitors low-level system events. If a USB enumeration process is detected that indicates a pairing attempt, the MTD app blocks the process and sends a high-priority alarm to the SIEM and the MDM console.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The examiner analyzes the configuration of the MTD solution and the associated alerting rules. An attempt is made to connect a device to a host to test whether the alarm is triggered correctly and recorded in the central logging system. The SIEM logs are checked for corresponding events.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Due to their modern, simple operating concepts and high performance, smartphones and tablets are widespread today. This includes the mobile devices iPhone and iPad produced by Apple, with the operating systems iOS and iPadOS. Since iPadOS is based on iOS, both are summarized as "iOS" in this module for readability. The two operating systems currently have mainly functional differences that account for the different form factor of the devices.
Originally, these devices were designed for private use. However, due to the redesign of infrastructures and the way information is collected and processed, they are increasingly being used in a professional context and are even partially replacing notebooks.
Through the integration of business functions, iOS has been gradually expanded for use in companies and public authorities since version 4, and functions for administration from an institutional perspective have been integrated. This includes the possibility of centralized device registration (Apple Business Manager) as well as options like Single Sign-On (SSO).

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The goal of this module is to show how devices running iOS (for Enterprise) can be used securely in institutions. To this end, requirements are established for the settings of iOS-based devices, which can be distributed to the devices in the form of configuration profiles. iOS configuration profiles contain uniformly defined settings, e.g., for security policies or individual system aspects, to manage and automatically configure iOS-based devices uniformly and centrally.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module SYS.3.2.3 iOS (for Enterprise) is to be applied to all smartphones and tablets used for business purposes with the Apple iOS operating system.
This module contains fundamental requirements that must be observed and fulfilled when operating iOS-based devices that are integrated into the institution's processes. Requirements for integration into the institution's security or collaboration infrastructure are not the focus of this module. With a so-called "Mobile Device Management" (MDM), it is possible to centrally manage the devices and roll out configuration profiles per group of users or purpose. Security measures can also be implemented uniformly via an MDM. This module assumes that the iOS devices to be managed are integrated into an MDM infrastructure. If a small number of devices are managed, they can exceptionally be used without MDM for economic reasons. Requirements for the operation of MDM can be found in the module SYS.3.2.2 Mobile Device Management (MDM). For smaller environments, the Apple Configurator can be used to uniformly implement the requirements listed in this module on multiple end devices. General and overarching aspects of operating smartphones and tablets, regardless of the operating system used on them, can be found in the module SYS.3.2.1 General Smartphones and Tablets and must also be implemented when using iOS-based devices.
For the use of biometric authentication mechanisms, the module SYS.3.2.1 General Smartphones and Tablets contains corresponding requirements.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Risk concentration through one account (Apple ID) for all Apple services
parts.prose: The Apple ID provides central access to all services provided by Apple (e.g., "iMessage", "FaceTime", "iCloud", "App Store", "iTunes", "iBook Store", "Find My iPhone", or synchronization services). If unauthorized persons can access an insufficiently secured Apple ID, they may be able to use these Apple services, disrupt the availability of the Apple ID-based services, remotely locate or reset iOS-based devices to factory settings, and access information from the iCloud cloud service. In particular, with iCloud backups enabled, it is possible for attackers to clone the stored data to their own iOS device.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Tight integration of pre-installed apps and their functions
parts.prose: With iOS, Apple already delivers tightly integrated and pre-installed apps (e.g., "Mail" and "Safari"). These apps are sometimes executed with higher privileges than apps downloadable from the App Store, which increases the attack surface of the iOS-based device.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Abusive access to offloaded data
parts.prose: For a number of iOS-specific functions, the infrastructure operated by Apple must be used. If the functions "iCloud Keychain", "iMessage", "FaceTime", "Siri", "Continuity", "Spotlight Suggestions", as well as iCloud functions for creating backups or for collaborating on documents are used, the data is always synchronized between different devices or users via Apple's infrastructure. Push notifications for iOS-based devices are also routed through this infrastructure. There is therefore a fundamental risk that Apple servers will be accessed and the data stored or transmitted there will be misused for other purposes.

controls.title: Deactivate developer mode (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Developer mode is only deactivated on some of the Android devices. There is no consistent policy or check for deactivation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Deactivation, if it occurs at all, is done manually by individual users or administrators on an ad-hoc basis. No central management solution (MDM) is used to monitor or enforce the setting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: A sample of devices is manually checked to determine if developer mode is active. It is expected that a significant portion of the devices will show a deviation from the target requirement (deactivation).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Developer mode is deactivated by default on all Android devices during initial setup. However, there is no regular check or active prevention of reactivation by users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Deactivating developer mode is a documented step in the initial setup process for new devices. However, users with the appropriate knowledge can reactivate the mode later without it being noticed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The documentation of the setup process is reviewed to ensure that the deactivation of developer mode is included as a fixed step. In addition, a manual check of a sample of devices in operation is performed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is established by a policy that developer mode must be deactivated on all corporately used Android devices. Compliance with this policy is checked regularly, for example, as part of audits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Deactivation is ensured during the onboarding process. A formal device usage policy explicitly prohibits users from activating developer mode. Periodic manual or semi-automated checks verify the status on all devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The corresponding security policy is checked. A manual or script-based check of all managed devices is performed to ensure that developer mode is consistently deactivated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The deactivation of developer mode is technically enforced via a Mobile Device Management (MDM) solution, so users cannot activate it. Regular, automated compliance checks take place, which actively report deviations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An MDM policy that technically prevents the activation of developer mode is rolled out to all Android devices. The MDM system generates a compliance report at least monthly, which is sent to the responsible administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The configuration of the MDM policy is checked. The automated compliance reports from the MDM are analyzed to verify consistent deactivation. An attempt is made on a test device to activate it to check the effectiveness of the block.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The deactivation of developer mode is strictly enforced by an MDM policy. Any attempt to activate developer mode is blocked in real time and triggers an immediate, high-priority security warning. Devices on which unauthorized activation is detected are automatically isolated from the corporate network (quarantine).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A restrictive MDM policy is in use and coupled with a SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system. In the event of a blocked activation attempt, an alert is sent to the Security Operations Center (SOC) and the device is disconnected from the corporate network and critical services through an automated response.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The configurations of MDM, SIEM, and Network Access Control (NAC) are checked for the correct implementation of real-time blocking, alerting, and automatic quarantine. An attempt is made to bypass the protective measure as part of a penetration test.

controls.title: Use of multi-user and guest mode (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no regulation for the use of multi-user or guest modes. Users can activate and use these functions at their own discretion, which can lead to uncontrolled access to device resources.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default Android settings regarding user management remain unchanged on all devices. No configuration or restriction is applied.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Users are interviewed and a sample of devices is manually checked for the existence of multiple or unauthorized user accounts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In a general usage policy, users are recommended to use only the guest mode for sharing devices. However, there is no technical implementation or regular check of this recommendation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A corresponding clause is included in the general IT usage policy, which is made available to employees. Implementation is the responsibility of the users themselves.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The IT usage policy is checked for the corresponding clause. Manual spot checks of devices are carried out to assess compliance with the recommendation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is clearly regulated whether a device may be shared with other people. It is specified whether the multi-user or guest mode must be used for this purpose. It must be ensured that all created user accounts are assigned to natural persons and that no anonymous or generic permanent accounts exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal policy defines the exact conditions for the use of devices by multiple people. For temporary use by third parties, for example, the exclusive use of the ephemeral guest mode is prescribed, which deletes all data after the session.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The applicable device usage policy is reviewed. The user accounts configured on the devices are checked on a random basis to ensure their compliance with the policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of multi-user and guest modes is actively configured and restricted via an MDM solution. For example, only the use of guest mode is permitted, while the creation of new, permanent user accounts by the user is blocked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An MDM policy implements the requirements technically, e.g. by setting the Android restriction `DISALLOW_ADD_USER`. Compliance with the policy is continuously monitored by the MDM system and documented in reports.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The configuration of the corresponding MDM policy is checked. The MDM's compliance reports are analyzed. An attempt is made on a test device to create a new user contrary to the policy in order to verify the block.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: User management is completely and restrictively controlled via MDM. Only explicitly permitted modes (e.g. ephemeral guest mode) are available. The rights of guest or secondary users are severely restricted by granular policies (e.g. no access to company data, separate and filtered network access, no app installation). Any deviation from the policy is blocked and reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Granular MDM policies are used that enforce specific restrictions for secondary user profiles (e.g. `DISALLOW_INSTALL_APPS`, `DISALLOW_CONFIG_VPN`). Network traffic from guest profiles is routed through a separate, restrictive gateway. Attempts to bypass the restrictions lead to an alert.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The detailed MDM configuration for user and rights management is analyzed. The permissions of a guest user are technically checked on a test device to confirm the effective data separation and functional restriction.

controls.title: Advanced security settings (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Permissions for device administration, trust agents, or access to usage data are granted by users as needed and without a central approval process. There is no overview of granted permissions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users grant permissions when an app asks for them during installation or use, often without fully understanding the implications. There is no central control or policy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: A sample of devices is manually checked to determine which apps have extended permissions. The results are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an informal list of known and trusted apps (e.g., the MDM client) that may be granted extended permissions. Compliance checking is done manually and irregularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A recommendation or a simple list is stored in the internal IT documentation or a wiki. Administrators and users are encouraged to follow it.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The recommendation list is reviewed. A manual spot check of devices is carried out to compare the permissions granted with the list.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is defined by a policy that only explicitly approved apps may receive device administration rights, act as "Trust Agents", or access usage and notification data. Compliance with these requirements is checked regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Allowlists are maintained for apps that are permitted to receive these sensitive permissions. The check can be carried out by a script that reads the installed apps and their permissions and compares them with the approved list.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The formal policy and the maintained allowlists are checked. The results of the periodic reviews are analyzed to verify compliance with the policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The granting of rights for device administration, as a Trust Agent, and for access to sensitive data is actively managed by an MDM solution. Only apps on a central allowlist can request and receive these permissions. The MDM performs regular, automated compliance checks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM solution is configured to block or at least report the granting of these permissions for unapproved apps. Compliance reports are regularly generated and evaluated by administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The MDM configuration regarding permission management and the allowlist is checked. The compliance reports are analyzed. On a test device, an attempt is made to grant corresponding rights to an unapproved app to check the system's reaction.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A zero-trust model is applied. The granting of any extended permissions is blocked by default by the MDM (Deny by Default). Only absolutely necessary, audited apps receive the required rights via explicit assignment. Any attempt at unauthorized rights escalation is blocked in real time, logged, and triggers an alarm in the SIEM.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The MDM is configured in the most restrictive mode. The assignment of permissions is a formalized process that requires a security review of the app. Real-time alerting is integrated with a SIEM system that can trigger automated responses, e.g. deactivating the app.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The MDM configuration in 'Deny by Default' mode and the SIEM integration rules are checked. As part of a test, an attempt is made to grant extended rights to a specially prepared app in order to verify the effectiveness of the blocking and the alerting chain.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose: A frequently used operating system for smartphones and tablets is Android by Google. Since version 4, Android has been gradually expanded for enterprise use. For example, functions have been integrated that make it easier for institutions to manage Android devices. The number of management policies supported by Android also increases with each version. In addition, specific extensions from the manufacturing institutions enable additional policies.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of the module is to provide information on typical threats in connection with Android and to show how Android-based devices can be used securely in institutions. Security policies can also be created on the basis of the requirements listed in the module.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module SYS.3.2.4 Android is to be applied to all business-use smartphones and tablets with the Google Android operating system.

The module contains fundamental requirements to be observed and met when operating Android-based devices. General and overarching requirements for the operation of smartphones and tablets are not covered in this module, but in SYS.3.2.1 General Smartphones and Tablets, and must also be implemented when using Android-based devices. Also not part of this module are requirements for the case of central administration of Android devices via an MDM. These are listed in module SYS.3.2.2 Mobile Device Management (MDM).

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Deactivation of security functions
parts.prose:
The boot process of Android-based devices is secured with the help of a manufacturer certificate. The next execution step is checked before it is executed. This ensures that the Android operating system starts unchanged.
Unlocking the bootloader interrupts this chain of trust, so that a modified operating system can start. Such changes to the boot process are sometimes supported by the manufacturing institution, and sometimes bootloaders are also unlocked via vulnerabilities.
The Android security concept is bypassed or disabled, and new threats arise that must be secured in other ways.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Malware for the Android operating system
parts.prose: Due to their high prevalence and open architecture, devices with the Android operating system are a popular target for malware, which is often installed by users themselves. On Android, it is relatively easy to install apps not only from Google's Play Store, but also from alternative sources or via direct download. In addition to the monitored app stores from Google, device manufacturers, and other providers, apps are also offered for installation from rather dubious sources. Since it is not mandatory on Android to install apps from the official Google Play Store, attackers could, for example, infect a popular app with malware and then make it available for download again.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Missing updates for the Android operating system
parts.prose: Some manufacturing institutions ship smartphones and tablets with outdated versions of Android or provide no regular or even no updates at all. Since vulnerabilities are regularly discovered in Android, such devices are particularly at risk. As a consequence, known vulnerabilities of these devices cannot be eliminated and are therefore easily exploited by attackers.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Risk from accounts (Google ID) for Google services
parts.prose:
With the Google ID, users can centrally access all Google services, e.g., device management, recorded geographical positions, chat software, cloud storage, the Play Store, music, book and film offers, data backup, bookmarks or password storage for websites and synchronization services. Many other providers of services on the Internet also use the Google ID to authenticate users.
If attackers can authenticate via the Google ID, all associated services can be used under the stolen identity. It is also possible, for example, to access all data stored there and to locate or reset devices remotely, i.e., to delete all data on the device.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Pre-installed apps and integrated functions on Android-based devices
parts.prose: Along with the operating system, the manufacturers of Android devices often deliver already tightly integrated and pre-installed apps as well as a connection to third-party services (Twitter, Facebook, etc.). Users often cannot remove these apps themselves. This increases the attack surface of the Android operating system. The direct connection to third-party services is also often not desired in institutions.

controls.title: Security policies and regulations for the use of mobile phones (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is only a draft of a security policy for mobile phones, which has been neither officially approved nor distributed to the employees. The policy is incomplete and only covers basic aspects such as private use, while critical points such as how to handle losses are missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In this phase, a first draft is typically created in a word processing document, often in response to a specific incident. There is no formal review or approval by management or information security.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines whether a policy exists by interviewing the Information Security Officer (ISO). The auditor reviews the document for its status (e.g., "Draft") and its content to confirm its incompleteness and the lack of a distribution process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic security policy has been created and made available to all employees when a mobile phone is issued. It covers the most important rules of use, but it is not regularly checked for compliance or updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is published as a standard document on the intranet or handed out as a printout when the device is handed over. Acknowledgment may be confirmed by a signature, but no further measures are taken to ensure understanding.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether an official version of the policy exists and whether a process for distribution to all mobile phone users has been established. Spot checks with users are used to verify whether they have received the policy. The lack of review and update processes is noted in the audit report.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A security policy MUST be created for the use and control of the devices. Every person using a mobile phone MUST be given a copy of the security policy. It MUST be checked regularly whether the security policy is being complied with.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The security policy is an official, management-approved document. The handover is documented. Regular checks can take the form of annual surveys or random technical inspections, the results of which are recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence, approval status, and up-to-dateness of the security policy. They verify the evidence of distribution to users (e.g., receipts of acknowledgment). In addition, the logs of the regular checks are reviewed to confirm compliance with the process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is an integral part of security training. Its compliance is actively monitored through regular, documented spot checks. The policy is reviewed at least annually or in the event of significant changes in the threat landscape or technology and updated if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The content of the policy is integrated into the annual security awareness campaigns and onboarding processes. Compliance is checked by IT operations. A formal process for updating the policy, including a review by the ISO, is established.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the training materials for content related to the mobile phone policy. They review the logs of the spot checks and the documentation of the policy review process to assess its regularity and thoroughness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is mapped in a GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance) tool and its compliance is, as far as technically possible, automatically enforced and monitored by a central management solution (e.g. MDM/UEM for smartphones). Exceptions to the policy require a formal, documented risk assessment and approval process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Policy compliance is ensured by technical profiles that are deployed to the devices. Violations of the policy (e.g., installation of unapproved apps, if applicable) lead to automatic alarms or sanctions. The process for exception requests is implemented in the GRC tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration in the GRC and MDM/UEM system to verify the automated enforcement of the policy. They check the logs of the automated monitoring and the documentation of approved exceptions for completeness and traceability. An automated audit can check the MDM system's configuration files against a predefined 'golden standard'.

controls.title: Locking measures in case of loss of a mobile phone (B) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users are aware that a lost phone should be reported, but there is no documented process. The contact information for blocking the SIM card is not easily available and must be researched on a case-by-case basis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In case of loss, users must find out for themselves who to contact, which leads to significant delays in blocking the SIM card. There is no central point of contact.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews with users whether they know how to react in the event of a device loss. The lack of a documented process and centrally provided contact information is documented as a finding.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A simple process for reporting a lost device is documented and available on the intranet. Users know who to contact to have the SIM card blocked. However, the response only occurs during regular business hours.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A page on the intranet lists the phone number of the internal IT helpdesk as the point of contact. The helpdesk has the necessary information to initiate the blocking with the mobile network operator.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation of the reporting process on the intranet. They verify through a test request to the helpdesk (outside of a real emergency) whether it is prepared for the process. The limited availability is noted in the audit report.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In case of loss of a mobile phone, the SIM card used in it MUST be blocked promptly. All necessary information for blocking the SIM card and mobile phone MUST be immediately available to the responsible bodies and users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central emergency hotline or a clearly defined reporting channel is established and known to users. The necessary data (e.g., phone number, SIM card number, customer number with the provider) is kept centrally to enable quick blocking. The information is stored, for example, on an emergency card or in a secure online portal.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the defined reporting channel exists and is known to the users (e.g., by checking onboarding material). They verify on a random basis whether the information necessary for blocking is available centrally and readily accessible to the responsible body (e.g., IT helpdesk).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process of blocking SIM cards and devices is ensured by a 24/7 service desk. If the devices support it, anti-theft mechanisms such as remote wipe or lock are actively used. The entire process is tested regularly, at least once a year.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An on-call service from the IT helpdesk or an external service provider is commissioned to carry out blocking around the clock. Users are trained on how to initiate a remote lock themselves, if necessary. The tests of the process are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the contracts and service level agreements (SLAs) of the 24/7 service desk. They review the logs of the process tests conducted. In addition, training materials are checked to see if the use of remote wipe functions is covered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process for responding to a device loss is largely automated. As soon as a user reports a device as lost via a self-service portal, the blocking of the SIM card with the mobile provider is automatically initiated via API and, if technically possible, the device is remotely locked and wiped.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Mobile Device Management (MDM/UEM) solution is integrated via an API with the mobile provider's system and a self-service portal for users. The process runs without manual intervention to minimize response time. The status of the process (reporting, blocking, deletion) is transparently visible to the user and IT security.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the MDM/UEM solution, the API interfaces, and the self-service portal. An end-to-end test of the automated process is performed to verify correct functionality. The system's logs are checked for successful and failed automation runs. An automated audit can monitor the availability and correct configuration of the API endpoints.

controls.title: Awareness and training of employees in handling mobile phones (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The topic of mobile phone security is only mentioned peripherally in general IT guidelines. There is no specific awareness or training for the associated dangers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A short paragraph in the general IT usage policy is the only source of information. No proactive measures are taken to raise employee awareness.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing policies and notes the lack of dedicated training or awareness measures. Interviews with employees confirm the low level of knowledge about specific risks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: New employees receive a one-time, basic briefing on the secure handling of their company mobile phone as part of their onboarding. This covers the most important rules of conduct.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard presentation is shown during the induction event for new employees. The content is not regularly updated, and there are no refresher courses.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the onboarding documents for the existence of the briefing. They assess the content for its timeliness and completeness. It is noted that there are no recurring training sessions for existing employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Employees MUST be made aware of the special information security risks posed by mobile phones. They MUST be instructed on the security features of the mobile phones. Users MUST be familiar with the process by which mobile phones can be locked. Users MUST be advised on how mobile phones should be stored safely and correctly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated training on mobile phone security is conducted, with mandatory and documented participation for all users. The training content includes the use of PIN/device code, the reporting process in case of loss, and protection against eavesdropping (e.g., during conversations in public).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the training materials for completeness regarding the required content. They verify the participant lists to confirm compliance with the training obligation. Random interviews with users are conducted to check their understanding of the content taught.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the basic training, regular refresher courses are conducted at least annually. These also cover current threats such as SMiShing (SMS phishing). The training content is tailored to the specific risks of the organization.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The refresher courses are offered as e-learning courses or in short in-person sessions. Simulated SMiShing campaigns are conducted to test and raise awareness. The results are used to adapt the training content.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the plan for the annual refresher courses and the associated materials. They review the anonymized results of the SMiShing simulations and the improvement measures derived from them. Participation in the refresher courses is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training program is role-based and managed via a Learning Management System (LMS). Training success is measured and proven through mandatory tests. Gamification elements are used to increase employee engagement and learning success.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees with special security requirements (e.g., travelers to high-risk countries) receive advanced training modules. The LMS tracks progress and automatically sends reminders for due trainings. Successfully passed tests are a prerequisite for continued access to certain services.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and content in the LMS, including the role-based assignments and test questions. They analyze the LMS reports on training success and completion rates. The effectiveness of the program is evaluated by a measurable reduction in security incidents related to mobile phones.

controls.title: Decommissioning and proper disposal of mobile phones and memory cards used in them (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Decommissioned mobile phones are collected and stored unsorted in a box. There is no defined process for deleting data or for secure disposal.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The collected devices are unsecured and potentially accessible to anyone in the storage area. Data, especially on memory cards, remains intact.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the storage location of the old devices and notes the lack of physical security and the absence of a deletion and disposal process. A device is switched on at random to check if data is still present.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users are instructed to reset their devices to factory settings before returning them. The returned devices are stored in a locked cabinet until they are disposed of.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The instruction to reset is part of the offboarding process. However, there is no verification of whether the deletion was actually and completely carried out. Disposal is done via general electronic waste without special security measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the offboarding checklist for the instruction to reset. They inspect the storage location and determine that there is no verification of data deletion. The disposal route is assessed as not secure for devices that potentially contain data.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Mobile phones MUST be reset to factory settings before disposal. It MUST be verified that all data, including on memory cards, has been deleted. Collected mobile phones and memory cards MUST be stored protected from unauthorized access until disposal.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An IT employee is responsible for the decommissioning process. Each returned device is manually reset to factory settings, and the successful deletion is documented on a checklist. Memory cards are removed and stored separately and securely. The devices are stored in a dedicated, access-protected area.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation and the completed data deletion checklists. They inspect the secure storage location. Devices are randomly taken from storage and an attempt is made to recover data to check the effectiveness of the deletion.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is ensured that the mobile phones and any memory cards used in them are disposed of properly and verifiably. For this purpose, a certified service provider for data destruction is commissioned. The entire process is documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a contract with a disposal company certified according to ISO 21964 (formerly DIN 66399). The devices are handed over in sealed containers. The service provider issues a certificate of destruction, which is archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the contract with the disposal service provider and its certification. They review the handover protocols and the received certificates of destruction to ensure a complete chain of custody.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire lifecycle of the mobile phones is tracked in an asset management system. The decommissioning process is initiated in the system, whereby data erasure is verified by a second person (four-eyes principle) and confirmed in the system before the device is released for physical destruction. Memory cards are always physically destroyed (e.g., shredded).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The asset management system enforces compliance with the process. The status of each device (e.g., 'in use', 'returned', 'deletion verified', 'destroyed') can be tracked transparently. The physical destruction of memory cards is carried out internally with a suitable shredder.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the workflow in the asset management system and the corresponding log entries. They verify the records of the four-eyes principle and check the process of internal destruction of memory cards. An automatic audit can regularly generate reports from the asset management system to identify devices whose decommissioning process is overdue.

controls.title: Use of mobile phone security mechanisms (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of a SIM card PIN is mandatory for all users. The use of a device lock code is recommended, but not enforced or checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When the device is issued, the user is instructed to change the default SIM card PIN. There are no further configurations or checks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly questions users to see if they use a SIM PIN. It is noted that no measures exist to enforce a device lock code.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The available security mechanisms SHOULD be used and preconfigured on the mobile phones. The SIM card SHOULD be protected by a secure PIN. The mobile phone SHOULD be protected by a device code. The Super-PIN/PUK SHOULD only be used by the responsible persons within the defined processes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before being issued, mobile phones are configured to enforce the use of a SIM PIN and a device lock code. During handover, users are guided to set secure, non-trivial codes. The PUK is managed centrally and securely by IT operations and is only issued after the user's identity has been verified.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the device issuance process to ensure that the security mechanisms are configured. They review the process for managing and issuing the PUK for security and traceability. During the physical inspection of devices, it is checked whether lock codes are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the mandatory PIN and device code, if technically possible, the device is permanently linked to the issued SIM card (SIM lock). A policy for the complexity of device codes (minimum length) is enforced, and the screen is configured to lock automatically after a short period of inactivity.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SIM lock function is configured either directly with the mobile operator or, if supported by the device, manually. Users are instructed to use a device code of at least 6 digits and to set the automatic lock to a maximum of 1 minute. This is checked upon issuance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the configuration of the devices for the activation of SIM lock, compliance with the code length, and the automatic lock setting. The process documentation for the configuration is reviewed.

controls.title: Mobile phone updates (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a policy stating that users should install available software updates for their mobile phones. The IT department occasionally sends out email reminders when important updates become known.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The responsibility for performing updates lies entirely with the user. There is no verification of whether the updates have actually been installed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and the email reminders sent. By questioning users, it is determined that the update status of the devices is inconsistent and not traceable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be checked regularly whether software updates are available for the mobile phones. The handling of updates SHOULD be regulated. When new software updates are available, it SHOULD be specified how users are informed and whether they are allowed to install the updates themselves or whether the mobile phones should be handed in at a central location for this purpose.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: IT operations maintains a list of the mobile phone models used and checks the manufacturers' websites for a vailability of updates on a quarterly basis. A process is defined: either users are informed by email with instructions for self-installation, or an appointment for a central update by IT is offered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the list of mobile phone models and the logs of the regular update checks. They verify the existence of the defined process for carrying out updates (e.g., by inspecting the instructions sent or the appointment announcements).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT department proactively and promptly monitors security announcements from manufacturers for the device models in use. An accelerated update process is initiated for critical security updates. The successful installation is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: IT operations subscribes to the security advisories of the relevant manufacturers. In the case of critical vulnerabilities, users are promptly requested to install the update. The check is carried out when the devices are with IT for other support requests.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the processes for monitoring security announcements. They review the communication and the measures taken in the event of the last critical security vulnerability. The logs of the random checks are reviewed.

controls.title: Procurement of mobile phones (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the procurement of mobile phones, there is a simple requirements list that focuses primarily on functional properties such as battery life, camera quality, and price. Security aspects are not systematically evaluated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The procurement department selects devices based on a simple market analysis that meets the basic functional requirements and is cost-effective.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the requirements list and finds that security criteria are missing. The latest procurement decisions are analyzed for their primary decision criteria.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before mobile phones are procured, a requirements list SHOULD be created. Based on the requirements list, the products available on the market SHOULD be evaluated. The product SHOULD be selected based on whether the manufacturers offer updates for the planned period of use. It SHOULD be ensured that spare parts such as batteries and chargers can be procured in sufficient quality.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements list is created by IT operations and, in addition to functional criteria, also contains basic security and support criteria. Before a procurement, research is conducted on how long the manufacturer is expected to provide updates and whether common spare parts are available. The decision is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
