parts.prose: The auditor checks the requirements lists and the corresponding evaluation documentation for recently procured device models. They verify that the criteria for updates and spare parts availability were part of the evaluation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirements list for procurement is formalized and contains specific security criteria (e.g., support for device encryption, remote wipe, SIM lock). The manufacturer's past reliability in providing security updates is a key selection criterion. A limited number of standard models is defined to simplify administration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Information Security Officer (ISO) is involved in creating the requirements list. A product catalog with 2-3 approved standard models is maintained. The selection of these models is based on a thorough evaluation that also includes the manufacturer's reputation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the formalized procurement process and the involvement of the ISO. They review the product catalog of standard models and the corresponding evaluation documentation to confirm that the extended security criteria have been taken into account.

controls.title: Use of wireless interfaces on mobile phones (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users are advised in a policy to deactivate unused wireless interfaces such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. Compliance is not checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A corresponding clause is part of the general security policy for mobile phones. No further measures are taken to remind or train users about this rule.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the policy for the corresponding note. During a random inspection of devices, it is found that the interfaces are often permanently activated, which indicates the low effectiveness of the measure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Wireless interfaces of mobile phones such as IrDA, Wi-Fi, or Bluetooth SHOULD be deactivated as long as they are not needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This rule is actively communicated to users as part of security training. It is explained why this is important (reducing the attack surface, saving power). Users are instructed to activate the interfaces only when needed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the training materials for corresponding content. In interviews and random device checks, it is verified whether users know the rule, understand its purpose, and implement it for the most part in their daily routine.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The policy to deactivate unused interfaces is reinforced by regular reminders as part of awareness campaigns. Users are explicitly trained on the risks of connecting to insecure public Wi-Fi or pairing with unknown Bluetooth devices.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The topic is regularly addressed in newsletters or on "Security Awareness Day". The training sessions contain concrete examples of attacks via wireless interfaces. Compliance is randomly checked during support requests and the user is kindly reminded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the materials of the awareness campaigns and the extended training content. They interview employees to determine if they are aware of the specific risks (e.g., "Man-in-the-Middle" attacks on Wi-Fi).

controls.title: Secure data transmission via mobile phones (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a general rule that confidential information should not be processed or transmitted via mobile phones. However, there is no precise definition of what is considered confidential and what exceptions exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The rule is part of the IT usage policy, but it is difficult for users to implement in everyday life because it is too unspecific.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: When reviewing the policy and in interviews with users, the auditor finds that the rule leads to uncertainty and inconsistent application due to its lack of specificity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be regulated which data may be transmitted via mobile phones. The interfaces permitted for this purpose SHOULD be specified. Furthermore, it SHOULD be decided how the data is to be encrypted if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple data classification (e.g., "public," "internal," "confidential") is defined. A policy specifies which data classes may be transmitted over which channels (e.g., email, SMS). For the transmission of data classified as "confidential," a method of encryption (e.g., password-protected ZIP archives) is mandated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks for the existence of the data classification and the associated transmission policy. They verify that a method for encryption is defined and known to the users.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The data transmission rules are detailed and linked to a multi-level data classification policy. Specific, approved applications and procedures are defined for the transmission of sensitive data (e.g., use of a secure messenger, if available on the device). Users are trained in the application of these procedures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is practical and provides clear instructions for various scenarios. For example, the HR department may process certain data on mobile devices, but only via a secure channel. The training includes practical exercises on encryption.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the detailed policy and training materials. Interviews are conducted to verify users' understanding of the correct handling of different data classes on their mobile phones.

controls.title: Contingency planning for mobile phones (S) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users are instructed to manually back up important contact data to their SIM card. A small pool of unconfigured replacement devices is maintained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The responsibility for data backup lies entirely with the user. In the event of a defect, the user receives an empty replacement device and must insert their SIM card. Recovery of data that was not on the SIM card is not possible.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews that data backup is inconsistent and often incomplete. They check the existence of the replacement device pool and the exchange process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data stored on a mobile phone SHOULD be backed up to an external medium at regular intervals. If a defective mobile phone needs to be repaired, all data SHOULD be deleted beforehand and the device reset to its factory state. Spare devices SHOULD always be available to be able to replace a failed mobile phone at short notice.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process for regular backups is defined, e.g., by instructing to synchronize the phone monthly with PC software. A pool of pre-configured replacement devices is available. There is a checklist that ensures that devices are reset before being passed on for repair.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation for backups and for handling repair cases. They inspect the replacement device pool. Compliance with the backup procedure is verified by questioning the users.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Where technically possible, contact data and calendars are centrally synchronized with an organization's server (e.g., Exchange ActiveSync). The replacement of a defective device is guaranteed within a defined, short period (e.g., one working day).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For feature phones that support synchronization, this is configured upon issuance. This reduces the dependency on manual backups. The device exchange process is optimized to minimize downtime.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the synchronization services. They verify the defined Service Level Agreement (SLA) for the exchange and check whether it was met by reviewing tickets from past exchange processes.

controls.title: Setting up a mobile phone pool (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A pool of mobile phones is managed in a simple list (e.g., Excel). Issuance and return are noted manually. After return, each device is reset to factory settings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The responsibility lies with a person in IT support. The devices are not pre-configured but are fitted with a SIM card upon issuance. The charge level is not guaranteed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the inventory list and the log entries for issuance and return. They note that the preparation of the devices for the next user (charging, configuration) is not part of the process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For frequently changing users of company mobile phones, a pool SHOULD be set up. The issuance and return of mobile phones and accessories SHOULD be documented. Before issuance, it SHOULD be ensured that the mobile phones are charged and equipped with the necessary data for the new owners. In addition, users SHOULD be reminded to comply with the security policy. After the devices have been returned, they SHOULD be reset to their factory state.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal process for the device pool is defined. A checklist for issuance and return ensures that all steps (documentation, charging, configuration, policy reminder, deletion after return) are followed. The devices are stored in a lockable cabinet with charging facilities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation and the checklists used. They inspect the storage location. They accompany (or simulate) an issuance and return process to verify compliance with the defined steps.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The rental process is managed via an IT ticketing system that automates the documentation. Upon issuance, each user must sign a form confirming receipt and acknowledgment of the security policies. Each device has a standard configuration profile that is installed before issuance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Requests for loan devices are recorded as tickets. Issuance and return are documented in the ticket. The signed forms are digitally archived. The standard configuration includes, e.g., stored emergency numbers or basic settings.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the workflow in the ticketing system. They randomly inspect the archived acknowledgments of receipt. They review the defined standard configuration profiles.

controls.title: Ensuring the power supply of mobile phones (H) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each user is responsible for keeping their mobile phone sufficiently charged for the workday. Each user is provided with a standard charger.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirement is part of the general usage policy. No further measures are taken, other than providing one charger per device.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the provision of chargers is complete. It is noted that no provisions are made for special requirements (e.g., long field assignments).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Appropriate measures SHOULD be taken to ensure the continuous power supply of mobile phones. Depending on the need, spare batteries or power banks SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For users with special availability requirements, such as on-call services or frequent travelers, additional spare batteries, power banks, or car chargers are issued based on a needs analysis. This equipment is part of the standard package for these user groups.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the needs analysis and the definition of user groups with increased energy requirements. They verify on a random basis whether the defined user groups have received the additional equipment.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For critical roles, a redundant power supply is ensured, consisting of spare batteries, a high-capacity power bank, and a car charger. The condition of the batteries is checked regularly, and they are proactively replaced after a certain period of use or when performance degrades.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A lifecycle management for batteries is established. For example, batteries are replaced across the board every two years to prevent age-related failures. The issuance and replacement are documented in asset management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the definition of critical roles and the corresponding equipment. They verify the process of proactive battery replacement using the records in the asset management system.

controls.title: Protection against the creation of movement profiles during mobile phone use (H) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policies and training highlight the risks of location tracking by the mobile network and GPS. For devices with a GPS function, it is stipulated that this must be deactivated by default.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Users are instructed to deactivate the GPS function in the device settings and only activate it when needed for navigation purposes. This is covered in the security training.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policies and training materials. The GPS setting is checked during random device inspections.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be clarified whether the creation of movement profiles by third parties can have a negative impact or is considered a problem. To prevent tracking via GPS, this function SHOULD be switched off.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specific risk analysis is conducted for certain user groups (e.g., executives, secret keepers) to assess the threat posed by movement profiles. Based on the result, binding instructions for deactivating GPS and, if necessary, further rules of conduct are issued.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the risk analysis performed and the protective measures derived from it. Through interviews and technical checks, they verify that the measures are implemented for the affected user group.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If tracking via the mobile network is to be reliably prevented in certain situations or at certain locations, the mobile phone SHOULD be switched off completely and the battery removed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For stays in high-security areas or during confidential meetings, a mandatory instruction has been issued to switch off mobile phones and remove the battery. Special, shielded bags or lockers are provided for storage. The rule applies to all participants.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the corresponding policy and the physical precautions (e.g., lockers). They observe compliance with the rule at the beginning of a meeting classified as confidential.

controls.title: Protection against phone number identification when using mobile phones (H) [Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is clearly stated in a policy that company mobile phone numbers must NOT be published or passed on to unauthorized third parties.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees are instructed not to state their mobile phone number in public directories, on business cards, or in email signatures, unless explicitly approved for their role. Compliance is promoted by raising employee awareness.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the corresponding policy. They conduct random checks of business cards and email signatures to verify compliance.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To prevent the phone numbers used from being assigned to specific individuals, phone numbers for outgoing calls SHOULD be suppressed by default (CLIR).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For user groups with increased protection needs, Calling Line Identification Restriction is configured on the network side by the mobile provider or, if possible, on the device as a default setting. Users are trained on how to disable the restriction for a single call if necessary.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration instructions for the provider or the configuration of the devices for the affected user groups. They have the function demonstrated to them via a test call.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For roles with the highest protection needs, SMS and MMS messages SHOULD NOT be sent from the business mobile phone to minimize the creation of metadata profiles and vulnerability to SMiShing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This strict rule is enforced as a mandatory directive for defined high-security roles. Alternative, secure channels are provided for necessary communication. If necessary, the provider will deactivate SMS/MMS for these connections on the network side.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and the instruction to the provider to deactivate the services. They conduct interviews with the affected individuals to verify compliance and understanding of the measure.

controls.title: Protection against eavesdropping on conversations in a room via mobile phones (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To prevent confidential information from being eavesdropped on, it SHOULD be ensured that no mobile phones are taken into the respective rooms for confidential meetings and conversations. This is established as a formal policy for designated security areas and meeting rooms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The affected rooms are clearly marked. The rule is part of the invitation to confidential meetings. The organizer reminds the participants of the rule at the beginning of the meeting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the policy and the marking of the rooms. They participate as a silent observer in a confidential meeting to see if the rule is communicated and followed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The ban on taking mobile phones into security areas is enforced by organizational measures. Lockers are provided in front of the respective rooms for the secure storage of the devices. Compliance with the rule is actively monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Pictograms and signs are posted at the entrances to the security areas. The lockers are accessible to all employees and guests. The organizer of a meeting or a security officer is responsible for ensuring compliance before the meeting begins.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the physical controls (signs, lockers). They review the process instructions for meeting organizers. Consistent implementation of the control is verified through observation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If necessary, the carrying ban SHOULD be technically enforced by using mobile phone detectors at the entrances to high-security areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At the entrances to the defined high-security zones, fixed or mobile detectors are used that react to active or passive mobile phones. Their use has been legally reviewed and is monitored by security personnel. Persons in whom a device is detected are denied access until the device has been put away.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the legal basis and the process documentation for the use of the detectors. They check the functionality of the detectors and observe the procedure of the security personnel in the event of an alarm. An automatic audit can regularly check the functionality and operational readiness of the detectors.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
The mobile phones considered in this module, also called "feature phones" or "dumbphones," have fewer features than a smartphone, but offer more functions than just pure telephony. For example, these mobile phones can also be equipped with a camera for videos and photos, a scheduler, e-mail programs, games, an MP3 player, or a radio receiver. "Classic" mobile phones usually do not have a touchscreen and an operating system on which additional apps can be installed. These missing functions distinguish the mobile phone from a smartphone.
Mobile phones are identified by an internationally unique serial number (International Mobile Equipment Identity, IMEI). The user of the mobile phone is identified by the SIM card, which is assigned by the mobile network provider upon conclusion of the contract.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of the module is to highlight typical threats that can arise from the use of mobile phones, and to secure information that is stored on or transmitted via mobile phones.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module SYS.3.3 Mobile Phone is to be applied to all mobile phones used for business purposes.
This module deals with general aspects of typical mobile phones, with security aspects of telephony and messaging via the mobile network, and with security aspects of handling the devices. This module thus covers a wide range of different devices that can be connected to mobile networks. Supplementary aspects that go beyond communication via a mobile network and the handling of the devices can be found in other modules of the IT-Grundschutz Compendium. For example, security requirements for smartphones and the operating systems used on them can be found in the modules of the SYS.3.2 Tablet and Smartphone layer. Aspects of data-based telephony are dealt with in the module NET.4.2 VoIP. If the mobile phone in question uses VPNs, the module NET.3.3 VPN should also be considered. For smartphones or tablets, the module SYS.3.2.1 General Smartphones and Tablets is to be applied.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Inadequate planning when procuring mobile phones
parts.prose: If relevant features of the mobile phones to be procured are not identified in the planning phase, urgently needed functions may not be available. If certain mobile communication standards are not supported, the devices cannot be used in certain countries. In the worst-case scenario, the range of functions does not correspond to the intended purpose, so these devices cannot be used at all. Often, there are also other constraints that must be met for the devices to be used. These include, for example, security functions that are often not apparent at first glance but can lead to problems regarding availability and confidentiality when used.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Loss of the mobile phone
parts.prose: Since mobile phones are generally small and constantly carried around, they can easily be lost, forgotten, or stolen. In addition to the financial damage, the loss of confidentiality and integrity of the data they contain is particularly serious. This is because attackers could access institution-critical information via a stolen mobile phone. Furthermore, costs and efforts are incurred to restore a workable state.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Carelessness in handling information during mobile telephony
parts.prose: Through inattention and carelessness of employees during mobile telephony, third parties can gain access to information worthy of protection. For example, information can be eavesdropped on or recorded during telephone conversations, and messages can be read while they are being composed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Unauthorized private use of the company mobile phone
parts.prose: Company-owned mobile phones can be used for private purposes without authorization. Through inattention and careless handling, this can lead to information security problems for the institution, for example if private and business content are mixed. In this way, unauthorized persons could gain knowledge of the institution's internal affairs. If company mobile phones are used privately, this can also result in additional costs for the institution.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Mobile phone failure
parts.prose: A mobile phone failure can have several causes. For example, users may have failed to charge the device's battery, or the battery may have lost its ability to store energy. It is also possible that users have forgotten the access password or PIN and can no longer use the device. The device can lock itself after multiple incorrect entries of the access code. If the phone is not handled carefully, it can be damaged, for example, by being dropped. In all these cases, the users are then unreachable and, in turn, cannot reach anyone via the mobile phone themselves.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Analysis of connection data when using mobile phones
parts.prose: Due to the characteristics of mobile communication, it cannot be prevented that the transmitted signals are eavesdropped on and recorded without authorization with appropriate effort. For most radio services, mobile communication devices must also be located for technical reasons in order to be reachable. Thus, location information can be used by network operators or service providers to create movement profiles.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Eavesdropping on room conversations via mobile phones
parts.prose: Mobile phones can be used to secretly record or eavesdrop on conversations. In meetings, connections to unauthorized eavesdroppers can be established via mobile phones brought along. Many mobile phones are equipped with a hands-free device, so conversations throughout the room can be easily captured. On many devices, it is not visible whether they are turned on or not. Thus, it cannot be directly detected whether conversations are being recorded or eavesdropped on.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Use of outdated mobile phones
parts.prose:
Because smartphones can be used in more diverse ways than mobile phones, many manufacturing institutions now exclusively offer smartphones. As a result, the supply of smartphones significantly exceeds the supply of mobile phones, and hardly any mobile phones are still produced. Due to the limited supply, many mobile phones from old stock are used. Worn-out components like batteries are often replaced with third-party replicas, allowing these mobile phones to continue being used for decades after their production.
Often, these outdated mobile phones have operating systems installed that are no longer being developed or supported. Software vulnerabilities can therefore no longer be fixed through updates. Frequently, the manufacturing institutions of the mobile phones no longer exist, or they have shifted their business to other markets. Original accessories and spare parts can often no longer be purchased. Third-party manufacturers also often no longer offer corresponding products for very old mobile phones. If third-party manufacturers do offer spare parts, it is not guaranteed that these components have the same quality as the original parts. For example, replica batteries are often less powerful than the originals. As a rule, these devices can also often no longer be repaired, and in case of problems, there are hardly any suitable contact persons who can help.

controls.title: Planning the use of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning for the use of printers is limited to the selection of devices based on cost and basic functions. Security aspects are only considered on an ad hoc basis for individual devices classified as particularly critical.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, there is no formal planning process. Devices are often procured departmentally and decentrally, without a central security assessment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through random checks that there is no documented security planning for most of the printers procured. Interviews are conducted with those responsible for procurement to confirm the lack of a systematic process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before new printers, copiers, or multifunction devices are procured, a basic checklist is used that queries some security features such as the availability of device passwords and network protocols. However, the results are not systematically documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple checklist is provided on the intranet. The IT department checks during procurement whether the most basic points are met.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests and compares the checklists used during procurement. It is found that although the checklists exist, they are not consistently used or archived for all devices.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before printers, copiers, and multifunction devices are procured, their secure use MUST be planned. Criteria such as support for secure protocols, encryption, on-device authentication, physical protection mechanisms, secure deletion, and the availability of updates and maintenance contracts SHOULD be considered. It MUST be determined where the devices may be set up and who may access them. The results SHOULD be documented in a baseline concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal document, the "Baseline Concept for Print Security," is created and is part of the procurement process. This concept lists all relevant security requirements and is used as a requirements catalog for every new procurement. The installation locations are defined in a room plan with security zones.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and content of the baseline concept for print security. It is checked whether this concept was demonstrably applied in recent procurements (e.g., through notes in the procurement files). In addition, the documentation of the defined installation locations and access authorizations is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning process for printer deployment is formalized and integrated into the overarching security and procurement policies. The requirement criteria are reviewed and updated annually or when new threats become known. The planning explicitly considers different protection requirement classes of information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The baseline concept is versioned and subject to formal change management. The procurement department is trained to check and enforce the security requirements. For areas with high protection needs, specialized devices with advanced security features are evaluated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the change management of the baseline concept and checks whether the criteria are up to date. It is verified that the procurement process provides for mandatory security approval by the ISO or IT security.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning is part of a dynamic IT asset lifecycle management process. The security requirements for printers are continuously aligned with current threat analyses and technological developments. The selection of devices is supported by automated conformity checks against the internal security catalog.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance) tool manages the security requirements for the printer fleet. Before procurement, potential devices are validated in a test environment for compliance with security policies. The planning also includes a strategy for secure decommissioning and disposal.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of the planning process into the asset management system. Logs of the automated conformity checks are reviewed. In addition, the existence and implementation of a comprehensive lifecycle strategy for the printer fleet is checked, including the secure disposal records.

controls.title: Suitable placement and access to printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only a few central printers, which are known to be used for confidential printouts, are located in lockable rooms. For most devices, there are no specific placement or access rules.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The placement is based on practical considerations such as proximity to workgroups. Physical security and access control are not systematically considered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts a walk-through and finds that many printers are located in freely accessible areas. There are no documented rules for physical access to the devices.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All printers are located in areas controlled by the institution, so that unauthorized persons from outside do not have direct access. Standard device passwords are set for administration, but they are often uniform and rarely changed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Printers are placed in general office areas. The manufacturers' default passwords are replaced by a uniform institutional password.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the printers are not located in public areas. On a random basis, attempts are made to log into the devices with known default passwords to check if they have been changed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations MUST set up and secure printers, copiers, and multifunction devices in such a way that only authorized persons can use the devices and access processed information. It MUST be ensured that only authorized persons can administer, maintain, and repair the devices. Written confidentiality agreements MUST be concluded with service providers. The devices MUST be provided with passwords that comply with the specifications of identity and access management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a placement concept that places printers according to the protection needs of the location (e.g., no central printers in entrance halls). Administrative access is restricted to a defined group in Active Directory. Signed confidentiality agreements are available for all external service providers. The device passwords are individual, sufficiently complex, and documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the actual installation locations with the concept. The access rights for administration are checked in the management system (e.g., Active Directory). The confidentiality agreements with service providers are reviewed. The configuration of the device passwords is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical access to devices is further restricted by organizational measures (e.g., placement in non-freely accessible offices) and, for high protection needs, by technical measures (e.g., housing locks). The device passwords are centrally managed and regularly rotated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Central departmental printers are set up in separate, lockable printer rooms. A password manager is used to manage the device passwords. The passwords are changed semi-annually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the printer rooms and checks the access controls. The password management and rotation processes are verified using the documentation in the password manager and the device configuration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physical and administrative access to printers is controlled and monitored by a central IAM system. Every access attempt is logged, and anomalies (e.g., repeated failed login attempts) automatically trigger an alarm. Physical security measures are supplemented by video surveillance at critical locations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: RADIUS or TACACS+ is used for authenticating administrative access. The printer logs are sent to a central SIEM system and correlated there. The installation locations are part of the institution's physical security concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the central authentication (e.g., RADIUS server settings). In the SIEM system, the printer logs and the configured alerting rules are checked. Conformity with the overall physical security concept is confirmed.

controls.title: Proper disposal of printed documents (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Printed documents are mostly disposed of in the normal paper waste. Only in individual departments with high protection needs (e.g., human resources) is there a shredder.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is no institution-wide regulation. Disposal is at the discretion of individual employees or departments.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly inspects the wastepaper baskets in various office areas and finds that they regularly contain documents with potentially sensitive information.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Shredders or lockable collection containers for secure disposal are available at central printer locations. Employees are instructed to use them for confidential documents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A shredder is placed next to each departmental printer. An email is sent to all employees pointing out the correct usage.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether secure disposal options are available at all central printer locations. The level of knowledge about the disposal rules is determined through interviews with employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Documents that are no longer needed but have been printed and contain confidential information MUST be destroyed in an appropriate manner. If home workstations are equipped with printers, it SHOULD be ensured that the printed information can also be appropriately destroyed on site if it is no longer needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A written data disposal policy is established and communicated. This policy mandates the use of shredders (with a defined security level, e.g., P-4 according to DIN 66399) or certified disposal service providers. For home workstations, either a shredder is provided, or employees are required to bring documents to the institution for secure destruction.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence and content of the disposal policy. The security level of the shredders used is verified. Contracts with external disposal service providers are reviewed. The regulations for home workstations are checked on the basis of policies and random checks on employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the disposal policy is actively promoted through regular awareness campaigns and unannounced inspections ("Clean Desk Audits"). The shredders used consistently meet a high security level that corresponds to the general protection needs of the institution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Annual e-learning courses on information security are conducted, which cover the topic of data disposal. The results of Clean Desk Audits are published anonymously to raise awareness.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the materials of the awareness campaigns and the reports of the Clean Desk Audits. It is verified that the security level of the shredders corresponds to the class defined in the policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire document destruction process, including disposal at home workstations, is handled by a certified service provider with a complete chain of custody (destruction certificate). The policy covers all types of data media that could be generated or processed by the multifunction devices.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A framework agreement is concluded with a service provider certified according to ISO 21964 (Destruction of data carriers). The service provider provides locked security containers and collects them regularly, including at decentralized locations or by arrangement with employees working from home.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the contract and certifications of the disposal service provider. The destruction logs are reviewed on a random basis to confirm the completeness of the process.

controls.title: Creation of a security policy for the use of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD develop a security policy for printers, copiers, and multifunction devices. It SHOULD regulate what requirements and specifications are placed on the information security of the devices and how these are to be met. It SHOULD also be specified which functions may be administered or used by which users under which conditions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An official policy document is created by the CISO in cooperation with IT operations. It defines topics such as: required security protocols (e.g., IPPS, HTTPS, SNMPv3), specifications for data encryption on the device, configuration hardening (deactivation of insecure services), rules for the use of scan-to-email and fax, and the assignment of administrator and user rights.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the security policy for printers and checks its content for completeness in accordance with the requirement. It is verified that the policy has been officially adopted and communicated to the relevant target groups (IT operations, administrators).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is reviewed and updated annually or on an ad-hoc basis (e.g., after security incidents or when new technologies are introduced). The implementation of the policy is monitored through technical configuration baselines and regular compliance checks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is part of the ISMS and is subject to a formal review process. Hardened configuration templates exist for the most common device models, which are automatically distributed and checked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the policy reviews. It is checked whether configuration templates exist and whether their compliance is periodically checked by technical means (e.g., scripts, central management software). Compliance check reports are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is integrated into a GRC tool that directly links the requirements with technical controls. Compliance is continuously monitored, and deviations lead to automated notifications or corrective actions. The policy is dynamically adapted based on risk analyses and threat intelligence.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Security Configuration Management (SCM) solution monitors the printer fleet in real time. The policy requirements are managed as "Policy as Code". In case of deviations, a ticket is automatically created in the ITSM system or a self-healing routine is triggered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration in the GRC and SCM tool. The policies defined as code and the logs of the automated monitoring and correction measures are checked. The process for adapting the policy based on new risks is analyzed.

controls.title: Creation of usage guidelines for handling printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (S) [Information Security Officer (ISO)]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the institution, the ISO SHOULD create a usage policy that summarizes all security requirements for handling the devices in a clear and understandable way. The usage policy SHOULD be known to all users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ISO creates a one- to two-page handout or an intranet page that summarizes the most important rules of conduct for users. These include: not leaving confidential documents unattended in the output tray, using Secure Print (if available), correctly disposing of misprints, and reporting malfunctions. The policy is distributed to all employees via email and published on the intranet.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the usage policy and assesses its clarity and completeness. It is checked how the policy was communicated to the users (e.g., based on email distribution lists or intranet statistics).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Acknowledgment of the usage policy is mandatory for all employees and is documented. The content is repeated and reinforced through regular awareness measures, such as training or topic-related emails.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The usage policy is part of the annual, mandatory IT security training for all employees. Participation and passing a short test are recorded in the HR system. Additionally, posters with the most important rules are hung up near printers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the training materials and the proofs of participation. It is checked whether the awareness measures take place regularly and whether the content of the usage policy is correctly reproduced.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the usage policy is supported and monitored by technical means. For example, print jobs that are not collected after a certain time are automatically deleted and the user is notified. Suspicious behavior (e.g., printing extremely large volumes of documents) is logged and can be reviewed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The print management software is configured to automatically delete uncollected Secure Print jobs after 24 hours. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) systems are used to monitor and, if necessary, block the printing of highly sensitive documents.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the print management software (e.g., the deletion deadlines). The rules and logs of the DLP system regarding printing processes are analyzed. The notifications to users for deleted jobs are checked on a random basis.

controls.title: Restriction of administrative remote access to printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD ensure that administrative remote access to printers, copiers, and multifunction devices is only possible for a clearly defined group of administrative and service personnel. This SHOULD also be guaranteed when a central device management software is used. It SHOULD be specified whether the control panel may be viewed via a data network, and if so, this should be restricted to IT operations and coordinated with the users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated "Printer Admins" group is created in Active Directory. Only members of this group have administrative rights via the central management software or direct device access. The use of the remote control panel function is disabled by default and only temporarily enabled for support cases when needed. This rule is documented in the security policy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the membership of the "Printer Admins" group in Active Directory. The configuration of the management software is verified to ensure that rights are assigned via this group. A random sample of devices is checked to determine if the remote control panel function is deactivated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Remote administrative access is further secured via a dedicated management network or a bastion host solution. All administrative sessions are logged to track who made which changes and when. Separate, non-personalized admin accounts are used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators must first log into a separate management VLAN via VPN, from which access to the printer interfaces is then possible. The devices and the central management software are configured to store all administrative actions on a central log server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network configuration (firewall rules, VLANs) for the management network. The configuration of log forwarding is checked on the devices and in the management software. The central logs are checked for completeness and content on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All remote administrative access is exclusively via a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. This enforces multi-factor authentication, records the entire session (video and command logging), and enables just-in-time rights assignment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution is implemented. Administrators authenticate to the PAM solution, which then establishes a secure and recorded connection to the printer or management software. The direct device passwords are not known to the administrators, as they are managed and rotated by the PAM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the architecture and configuration of the PAM solution. It is checked whether all administrative access paths lead exclusively through the PAM solution. Session recordings and access logs in the PAM system are reviewed on a random basis.

controls.title: Restricting the connection of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: IT operations SHOULD ensure that network-capable printers, copiers, and multifunction devices are not accessible from external networks. If multifunction devices are connected to the telephone network, it SHOULD be ensured that no uncontrolled data connections can be established between the data network and the telephone network. Network printers and multifunction devices SHOULD be operated in their own network segment, separate from the institution's clients and servers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A separate VLAN is set up for all printers and multifunction devices. The firewall rules are configured to block incoming connections from the internet to this VLAN. Connections from the client VLAN to the printer VLAN are only allowed for the required printing protocols (e.g., IPP, LPD). If possible, the fax function is connected via a central fax server instead of connecting the devices directly to the telephone network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network topology and the VLAN configuration. The firewall rules between the internet, the client network, and the printer network are checked. It is verified that no direct connections exist from multifunction devices between the data and telephone network.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall rules for the printer segment are configured according to the principle of least privilege. It is explicitly defined which clients are allowed to communicate with which printers. Any outbound internet traffic from the printer VLAN is blocked by default and only allowed for explicitly approved services (e.g., retrieving firmware updates from manufacturer servers).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Granular rules are created on the firewall that, for example, only allow the print servers or specific client subnets to access the printer VLAN. A "Default Deny" rule for outbound traffic from the printer VLAN is implemented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a detailed analysis of the firewall rule sets and checks their specificity. Penetration tests or port scans are conducted from the printer VLAN to verify the effectiveness of the outbound traffic blockade.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Network Access Control (NAC) according to IEEE 802.1X is used in the printer segment. Only authenticated and authorized printers are allowed to access the network. All network traffic to and from the printer segment is monitored for anomalies. Micro-segmentation is used to prevent communication between the printers themselves.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A NAC system is implemented that authenticates printers based on their certificate or MAC address. Unauthorized devices are denied network access. The firewall rules are configured so that printers cannot communicate with each other (Client Isolation). An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) monitors the traffic of the printer VLAN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the NAC system (e.g., RADIUS server and switch configuration). An attempt is made to connect an unauthorized device in the printer VLAN to test the effectiveness of the NAC solution. The IDS rules and logs for the printer segment are analyzed.

controls.title: Encryption of information on printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If possible, all information stored on internal, non-volatile storage media (e.g., hard drives) SHOULD be encrypted. Print jobs SHOULD also be transmitted in encrypted form if possible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For all devices with an integrated hard drive, the disk encryption function is activated in the device settings. For the transmission of print jobs, the printer drivers on the clients are configured to use the IPPS (IPP over TLS) protocol, if supported by the device.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the configuration of devices with a hard drive to verify the activation of encryption. The configuration of the printer queues on the client systems or the print server is checked to determine the use of IPPS. A network sniffer can be used to verify the encrypted transmission.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encryption of the internal storage is a mandatory requirement when procuring new devices. Encryption of print data transmission using IPPS is enforced by policy for all compatible devices and configured centrally. The encryption algorithms used comply with current recommendations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirement for storage encryption is anchored in the procurement policy. The configuration of print servers and clients to use IPPS is automated via group policies or scripts. TLS 1.2 or higher is configured in the device settings as the minimum standard for communication.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the procurement policy. The configuration in the group policies is checked. The TLS configuration of the devices is checked on a random basis to ensure that no outdated and insecure protocols or algorithms are used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only devices with hardware-based storage encryption (e.g., FIPS 140-2 certified Self-Encrypting Drives) are used. End-to-end encryption of print jobs from the client to the printer is fully implemented. The certificates used for encryption are managed via an internal PKI.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: During procurement, attention is paid to the certification of the encryption module. The print servers and clients are configured so that the print data is already encrypted before sending. The printers receive device certificates from the internal PKI to ensure secure TLS communication with the clients and servers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the technical data sheets and certifications of the devices used. The configuration of the end-to-end encryption is analyzed. The management of device certificates in the PKI is verified. The validity and trustworthiness of the certificates installed on the printers are checked.

controls.title: Protection of user and metadata (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: User and metadata such as print jobs and scan files SHOULD be stored on the devices for as short a time as possible. The data SHOULD be automatically deleted after a predefined time. File servers in the devices and functions such as "Scan to device memory" SHOULD be disabled by IT operations. In general, IT operations SHOULD ensure that all metadata is not visible to unauthorized persons.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On all devices, the automatic deletion of job data on the hard drive is configured after a short period (e.g., 24 hours). Functions such as "Save to Mailbox" or "Scan-to-HDD" are deactivated in the administration menu. The display of job lists on the device display is configured so that only the user's own username or anonymized job names are visible.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the device settings regarding automatic data deletion and the deactivation of storage functions. It is checked on the device display which metadata from other users' jobs are visible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The automatic deletion of data on the device is carried out by a function that securely overwrites the data (e.g., according to DoD 5220.22-M). The visibility of metadata is controlled by role-based access control. The institution has assessed the issue of tracking watermarks (e.g., Yellow Dots) and has issued a policy for handling them.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the security settings of the devices, the option for secure overwriting of data upon deletion is activated. Access to job lists is restricted to administrators. An official statement on the use of printouts with potential watermarks for external communication is published.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the secure deletion function in the device settings. The permissions for accessing job lists are checked. The existence and content of the policy on handling tracking watermarks are controlled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The secure deletion of all temporary data after each individual job is enforced. All access to stored jobs and metadata is logged and sent to a SIEM for monitoring. The institution uses technical means to prevent or neutralize the application of tracking watermarks where possible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Devices are configured to securely overwrite temporary data immediately after job completion. The audit logs of the printers are collected centrally and analyzed for suspicious access (e.g., repeated viewing of job lists). Special drivers or filters are used that attempt to remove known watermark patterns.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration for immediate data deletion. The log forwarding to the SIEM and the analysis rules set up there are checked. The effectiveness of the measures against tracking watermarks is verified by test printouts and subsequent analysis.

controls.title: Configuration of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All printers and multifunction devices SHOULD only be configurable by IT operations. Unneeded device functions and data interfaces SHOULD be disabled. The devices SHOULD be managed exclusively via encrypted protocols such as HTTPS and SNMPv3. All protocols used for unencrypted access (especially for configuration changes such as SNMP, Telnet, PJL) SHOULD be replaced or disabled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A hardened configuration profile is defined. This includes deactivating all unneeded functions (e.g., FTP server, Apple AirPrint, Wi-Fi Direct) and physical interfaces (e.g., USB ports). In the network settings, insecure management protocols such as Telnet, HTTP, and SNMPv1/v2c are deactivated and replaced with HTTPS and SNMPv3 (with authentication and encryption).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the configuration of several devices and compares it with the defined hardening profile. They check whether insecure management protocols are active, e.g., by a port scan of the device or by checking the web interface.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The hardened configuration baseline is centrally rolled out to all devices via management software. The configuration of the device fleet is regularly and automatically checked for deviations from this baseline.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The central device management software from the manufacturer or a third-party provider is used to create configuration templates and apply them to all devices. A script is created that reads the configuration of all printers weekly and compares it with the baseline. Deviations are logged and reported to the administrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration templates in the management software. The compliance check scripts and the logs of the last runs are analyzed to assess the effectiveness of the monitoring.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration baseline is managed as 'Infrastructure as Code' (IaC) in a version control system. A Security Configuration Management (SCM) solution continuously monitors compliance in real-time and is able to automatically correct deviations (self-healing).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration files or scripts (e.g., with Ansible or PowerShell) are managed in a Git repository. An SCM tool like Ansible Tower, Puppet, or a specialized printer management software with this capability ensures that all devices permanently comply with the desired state. Any manual change to a device is automatically detected and reverted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration files managed as code in the repository. The configuration of the SCM tool and its logs are checked to verify continuous monitoring and automatic correction. An attempt is made to manually change the configuration on a test device to test the self-healing function.

controls.title: Authentication and Authorization for Printers, Copiers, and Multifunction Devices (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only authorized persons SHOULD be able to access the printed or copied documents. If possible, only central printers, copiers, and multifunction devices SHOULD be used where users authenticate themselves at the device before the print job starts ('Secure-Print'). After users have authenticated, only their own print jobs SHOULD be visible. Only the functions necessary for the respective users SHOULD be enabled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A follow-me printing solution is implemented. Users send their print jobs to a central queue. To print the job, they must go to any printer and authenticate there with a username and password or a PIN. After logging in, they only see their own job list and can release the required documents. The devices are configured so that functions such as copying or scanning are also only available after a login.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the follow-me printing solution. It is tested whether user A can log in and accidentally see or print jobs from user B. It is checked whether access to functions such as copying effectively requires authentication.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Authentication at the printer is integrated into the central directory service system (e.g., Active Directory) and is performed conveniently and securely via employee ID cards with RFID/NFC or smartcards. Authorization (i.e., the release of functions such as color printing, scanning, faxing) is controlled on a role-based basis via groups in the directory service.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All printers are equipped with card readers. The print management software is linked to the Active Directory. Based on membership in AD groups (e.g., 'Print-Color-Allowed', 'Scan-Allowed'), the corresponding functions are enabled for users after logging in at the printer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the connection to the directory service. It is tested whether authentication via card works. The role-based function release is checked by creating test users with different group memberships and testing their permissions on the printer.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the release of particularly sensitive print jobs or access to critical functions, multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enforced on the device. All authentication and authorization events are centrally logged and monitored for anomalies. The authorization model is dynamic and can be based on the classification of the document.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The printing solution is configured so that users must also enter a PIN or provide a confirmation on their smartphone (via MFA app) after scanning their card. If a document in the ERP system is classified as 'strictly confidential', it can only be released by a manager with extended rights. All login attempts (successful and failed) are forwarded to the SIEM system for analysis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of MFA on the printing system. The process for releasing classified documents is tested. In the SIEM, the incoming printer logs and the configured correlation rules for suspicious behavior (e.g., brute-force attacks on PINs) are checked.

controls.title: Reducing Downtime for Printers, Copiers, and Multifunction Devices (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To keep the downtime of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices as low as possible, spare devices SHOULD be available, maintenance contracts SHOULD ensure an appropriate response time, a list of specialist dealers SHOULD be kept to quickly procure spare devices or parts, and if necessary, frequently needed spare parts SHOULD be stored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A pool of pre-configured spare devices is maintained. Maintenance contracts with the service provider define a maximum response time of 8 working hours. A list of standard consumables (toner, drums) and frequently needed spare parts is kept, and a minimum stock is maintained in the warehouse.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the warehouse to verify the existence of spare devices and parts. The maintenance contracts are reviewed and the agreed response times (SLAs) are checked. The list of specialist dealers and warehouse stocks is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A detailed emergency plan for the failure of printing services is part of the general Business Continuity Management (BCM). The maintenance contracts include guaranteed recovery times. A proactive monitoring system monitors the status of the devices (e.g., toner level, error codes, component wear) and reports potential problems before they lead to a failure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BCM manual contains a specific chapter for the failure of the central printing infrastructure. The SLAs in the maintenance contracts guarantee recovery within 24 hours. The central management software is used to collect status messages from the printers and to automatically create a ticket in the service desk system at critical values (e.g., toner < 10%).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the BCM manual. The SLAs in the contracts are checked for guaranteed recovery times. The configuration of the monitoring system and the automatic ticket creation is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: High availability of printing services is ensured through technical redundancy, such as clustered print servers and a sufficient number of devices per location. The entire process from fault reporting to resolution is automated in the ITSM tool, including escalation mechanisms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The central print servers are configured as a failover cluster. At critical locations, it is ensured that if one device fails, the print load can be seamlessly taken over by other devices (load balancing). The ITSM tool automates the assignment of fault tickets to technicians and escalates to management if the SLA is exceeded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the server cluster. The site concepts are checked for sufficient device redundancy. The workflows and escalation rules in the ITSM tool are analyzed. A controlled failure test of a print server or device can be performed to test the functionality of the failover.

controls.title: Extended Protection of Information on Printers, Copiers, and Multifunction Devices (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On the print server, the names of print jobs SHOULD only be displayed anonymously. All interfaces for external storage media SHOULD be blocked. On-device address books SHOULD be disabled and alternative addressing methods (e.g., LDAP) SHOULD be offered. For the e-mail function, it SHOULD be ensured that e-mails can only be sent with the address of the authenticated user and only to internal addresses. Incoming fax documents and transmission reports SHOULD only be accessible to authorized persons.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The print server is configured so that job names are not displayed. The USB and SD card interfaces on the devices are disabled in the admin menu. The function for local address books is switched off and instead a connection to the central LDAP/Active Directory is configured for address search. The scan-to-email function is set so that the 'From' field is not freely editable and emails are only delivered to internal domains (@institution.de). Faxes are routed to a central mailbox to which only a few authorized employees have access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the print server configuration. The deactivation of external interfaces and local address books on the devices is checked. It is tested whether the scan-to-email function can send emails to external addresses. Access to incoming faxes is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The 'Scan-to-Email' function is integrated into a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) solution, which checks the content of scanned documents for sensitive information and can block sending in case of rule violations. All fax communications (incoming and outgoing) are centrally logged. The LDAP queries for address search are exclusively made via an encrypted connection (LDAPS).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The email traffic from the multifunction devices is routed through a central email gateway equipped with a DLP solution. This checks attachments for keywords or patterns (e.g., credit card numbers). The fax server logs all activities in a log file. The LDAP connection in the device settings is switched to LDAPS (Port 636) with certificate validation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and rules of the DLP solution. The logs of the fax server are analyzed. The configuration of the LDAPS connection on the devices is verified, including the trustworthiness of the used certificate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data flows (printing, scanning, copying, faxing) are subject to content inspection by a comprehensive DLP solution that also applies OCR (text recognition) to image files. The use of the fax function is severely restricted and requires approval. Attempts to use blocked interfaces are logged and trigger a security alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A host- and network-based DLP solution analyzes print jobs and scanned documents. The fax function is disabled by default and is only enabled for specific users following an approval workflow. The device logs, which record access attempts to locked USB ports, are sent to the SIEM and configured with alarms there.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor tests the DLP solution by attempting to scan and send a document containing test-sensitive data. The approval workflow for the fax function is reviewed. The SIEM is checked to see if alarms are generated for attempted use of locked interfaces.

controls.title: Advanced hardening of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The IT operations SHOULD regularly check and correct the security settings of printers, if necessary through an automated system. It SHOULD be restricted that the devices can be reset to factory settings via the boot menu. It SHOULD be ensured that no firmware or additional software that has not been verified and approved by the manufacturer can be installed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least once per quarter, the security settings of important printers are manually checked against a checklist. Access to the advanced boot or service menu is protected by a separate password. Firmware updates are sourced and installed exclusively from the official manufacturer's website. The ability to install apps or third-party add-on software is disabled in the admin menu.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the manual configuration checks. An attempt is made to access the boot menu without a password. The installed firmware version is compared with the version released by the manufacturer. It is checked whether the installation function for additional software is disabled.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A Security Configuration Management (SCM) tool continuously monitors all devices for compliance with a hardened baseline and automatically reports deviations. All firmware updates are tested for security and compatibility in a test environment before rollout. The integrity of the firmware is verified by digital signatures during the update process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The central management software is used for continuous compliance monitoring. A dedicated test environment with representative device models is operated. When uploading firmware, it is ensured that the option to verify the digital signature is activated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and reports of the SCM tool. The process for firmware tests is reviewed based on the test documentation. It is verified that the devices are configured to only accept signed firmware.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrity of the devices is ensured by Secure Boot and continuous Runtime Integrity Monitoring, which triggers an alarm for any manipulation of the firmware or critical configuration files. Any attempt to install unsigned firmware or software is not only blocked but also triggers a high-priority security incident. All configuration changes are correlated in a central SIEM with the records from the change management system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Only devices that support Secure Boot and runtime integrity monitoring are procured. These functions are activated and their log outputs are sent to the SIEM. A rule is created in the SIEM that triggers an alarm if a configuration change is detected on the printer for which no approved change ticket exists in the ITSM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the activation of Secure Boot and integrity monitoring in the device settings. In the SIEM, the correlation rules between printer logs and the change management system are checked. A test change request is created and the entire process up to the alarm (or non-alarm in case of a correct process) is tracked.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Modern printers, copiers, and multifunction devices are complex devices that, in addition to mechanical components, contain their own operating systems and provide server services and functions. Since the devices often process confidential information, they, or the entire printing and scanning infrastructure, must be protected.
Multifunction devices are devices that offer multiple paper-processing functions, such as printing, copying, scanning, as well as sending and receiving fax documents.
Even today, paper is still used as an information carrier for many business processes and specialized tasks. Thus, printers, copiers, or multifunction devices are important components in the IT infrastructure. If the devices fail or print falsified documents, this can sometimes affect critical processes and lead to considerable economic damage.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: This module describes how to operate printers, copiers, and multifunction devices securely, so that neither can information flow out through these devices, nor can they compromise the security of the rest of the internal IT infrastructure.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The SYS.4.1 Printers, Copiers, and Multifunction Devices module is to be applied to every printer, copier, or multifunction device in the information network.
The module deals with the security of printers, copiers, and multifunction devices. Networked or locally connected document scanners are not explicitly considered. However, the risks and requirements can be derived from those for multifunction devices. Similarly, networked fax machines are not considered separately. The risks and requirements for the fax function listed in this module therefore also apply to this type of device. In addition, the requirements of the NET.4.3 Fax Devices and Fax Servers module must be taken into account.
Printers, copiers, and multifunction devices are often connected to data networks. In addition to wired connections, some devices can also be connected directly to a WLAN. Recommendations for this can be found in the modules of the NET Networks and Communication sub-layer, such as in the NET.2.2 WLAN Usage module.
Printers, copiers, and multifunction devices often have confidential information stored on them, which remains on the devices after decommissioning. Leased devices are often exchanged after a predetermined period or frequency of use, depending on the contract. They are returned at the latest after the lease contract expires. Paper and other consumables can also contain confidential information. Before these devices and consumables are disposed of, exchanged, repaired, or returned, all sensitive information must be deleted from them. Recommendations for this are not the subject of this module, but can be found in the CON.6 Deletion and Destruction module.
Print servers are IT systems with print queues, print job management, and other possible functions, e.g. driver distribution or secure printing. For every print server, the general and operating system-specific security requirements for servers must be met. These are not described in this module, but in the SYS.1.1 General Server module and the respective operating system-specific server modules.
An essential focus when securing printers, copiers, and multifunction devices is to regularly update the software installed on the devices and thus close software vulnerabilities. However, this module does not cover this aspect. Requirements for this can be found in the OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management module.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Unauthorized viewing of printed documents
parts.prose:
Printed documents often remain in the output tray of central printers and multifunction devices for a longer period of time, for example, because several files are printed first and then all are collected together later. It can also be that the wrong printer was selected at the client and the documents are not in the expected location. Since floor or departmental printers are used by many users, unauthorized persons can also view or take away information worthy of protection.
Left-behind printouts in the output trays of decentralized workplace printers, which are located in the immediate vicinity in the office rooms, are also a risk. Persons who have access to these rooms could also view or remove the printouts.
Another danger is fax documents and printed transmission protocols in the output tray, on which, in addition to the fax number, date, time and page number, a reduced image of the first page is sometimes visible.
