parts.prose: A hardened, isolated PC is operated as a sluice. The deactivation of Autorun/Autoplay is enforced via Group Policies (GPO). The scan station may use a virus scanner from a different manufacturer than the clients to increase the detection rate.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and correct configuration of the scan station, including its network isolation. The GPO settings for deactivating Autorun/Autoplay are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data from external removable media is analyzed for malicious behavior in an automated sandbox environment before internal use. This supplements signature-based detection with behavioral analysis. Data transfer from the data sluice to the internal network is only possible via a controlled, unidirectional mechanism.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The data sluice is equipped with a sandboxing solution (e.g., Cuckoo Sandbox) and a system for Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR). CDR removes potentially active content from files before they are forwarded. The transfer is carried out, for example, via a 'diode' system or a manual process by an administrator.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the architecture and configuration of the data sluice, including the sandboxing and CDR components. The effectiveness of the analysis and the controlled transfer is demonstrated using log files and test cases.

controls.title: Creation of a policy for the secure handling of removable media

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A short, informal document exists that lays down basic rules for the use of removable media, such as the prohibition of private devices. However, the policy is not comprehensive and is not actively communicated or reviewed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple memo or a page on the internal wiki lists a few rules of conduct.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor notes the existence of the document, but finds that it does not cover all relevant aspects and is hardly known to the employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A policy for the correct handling of removable media MUST be created. It regulates which removable media may be used, what data may be stored on them, how they must be protected (access, manipulation, loss), and how the spread of malware is prevented. In addition, the use of private removable media is generally prohibited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formally adopted policy is published on the intranet. It covers key aspects such as permitted device types, encryption requirements, procedures in case of loss, and malware scans. The policy is demonstrably brought to the attention of all employees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the official policy and checks whether the essential regulatory points are included. The proof of acknowledgement by the employees is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The policy on handling removable media is comprehensive and takes into account all aspects from requirement SYS.4.5.A4. This includes regulations on secure deletion, exchange with external parties, connection to third-party systems, shipping, and storage. The policy is reviewed regularly, at least once a year, for its up-to-dateness and adjusted if necessary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is a detailed document that contains specific instructions for various scenarios (e.g. business trip, home office, shipping by post). The review process is documented and the results are recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the policy for its completeness based on the BSI specifications. The logs of the annual reviews and the resulting adjustments are inspected and evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the policy for removable media is enforced by technical measures and continuously monitored. Deviations from the policy are automatically detected and trigger an alarm or an immediate countermeasure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An endpoint protection solution enforces the policy requirements (e.g., blocking unauthorized USB devices, enforcing encryption) directly on the client. All events related to removable media (connecting, writing, blocked attempts) are logged to a SIEM system and correlated and analyzed there.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the endpoint protection solution and the SIEM correlation rules. Test cases are used to prove that violations of the policy (e.g., connecting a private USB stick) are reliably detected and blocked and that corresponding alarms are generated.

controls.title: Regulation for taking removable media off-site

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There MUST be clear written rules on whether, how, and on what occasions removable media may be taken off-site. In particular, it MUST be specified which removable media may be transported off-site by whom and what basic security measures must be observed (e.g., mandatory encryption).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The regulation for taking media off-site is part of the general policy for removable media. It defines which employee groups (e.g. field staff) are generally authorized to take media off-site. For other employees, an approval process may be required.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the written regulation and checks its clarity. The approval process for exceptional cases is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Taking removable media off-site must be approved and documented by a supervisor. The approval is tied to the purpose and duration of the off-site use. Stricter requirements apply to taking media with highly sensitive data off-site, e.g., the obligation to transport it in a locked container.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A workflow-based form on the intranet is used for the approval process. The granted approvals are logged centrally. The additional protective measures for highly sensitive data are clearly described in the policy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the logs of the granted approvals and compares them with the actual off-site transports (e.g., by questioning or by inspecting travel documents). It is checked whether the stricter requirements for highly sensitive data have been met.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Taking removable media off-site is technically monitored and is only possible after explicit release in the management system. The release can be limited in time and geographically (geofencing). Any attempt to use an unreleased data carrier outside the company premises is blocked and reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central management console for the hardware-encrypted data carriers is used to technically enforce the off-site rules. Policies can be pushed to the devices remotely. The release is carried out through a multi-stage process that is mapped in the system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the management console and the defined release workflows. A test case is used to verify that an unreleased data carrier is not functional outside the defined area and that a corresponding message is generated.

controls.title: Media management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There MUST be a management system for removable media. The removable media SHOULD be uniformly labeled. The management system for removable media SHOULD ensure that removable media are handled and stored properly, as well as used and transported correctly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An inventory list (e.g., in a spreadsheet) is maintained in which all issued removable media are recorded with a unique ID, the type, and the assigned user. The media themselves are labeled with a label containing the ID.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the inventory list and compares it on a random basis with the physically existing or issued media. It is checked whether the labeling is uniform and the list is kept up-to-date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management of removable media is carried out via a dedicated asset management system. In addition to the basic information, the life cycle status (in use, stored, decommissioned), the assigned protection requirement, and the history (e.g. repairs, data deletions) of each data carrier are documented. The labeling of the data carriers is tamper-proof.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT asset management tool is extended to include fields for removable media. Labeling is done using engraved or sealed labels. Regular inventories ensure the correctness of the data.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the data quality in the asset management system and checks the logs of the inventories carried out. The tamper-proof nature of the labeling is physically assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The media management is fully automated and integrated with other security systems. The unique identifier (e.g., serial number) of each removable media is stored in the endpoint protection system. Only registered and authorized media can be used on the institution's IT systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The endpoint protection solution has a device control module. A whitelist of all official removable media is maintained here. Inventorying is done automatically when a new, approved data carrier is connected for the first time. The attempt to use an unregistered device is blocked and reported.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the whitelist in the endpoint protection solution. Connecting an unregistered test device verifies that access is blocked as expected and the incident is logged.

controls.title: Secure erasure of removable media before and after use

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before removable media are passed on, reused, or decommissioned, they MUST be securely erased in an appropriate manner. A procedure is defined which specifies which erasure method (e.g., overwriting with special software) is to be used for which type of data carrier.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented work instruction describes the process of secure erasure. Specified software (e.g., `shred` under Linux, DBAN or manufacturer-specific tools) is used. The successful erasure process is logged for each data carrier.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the work instruction for secure erasure and the logs of the erasure processes carried out. The conformity of the procedure with recognized standards (e.g. BSI, NIST) is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process of secure erasure is verified by a second person (four-eyes principle) or by a technical system that automatically validates the erasure process and creates a certificate-like erasure log. For final decommissioning, data carriers are also physically destroyed (e.g., by shredding).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Professional erasure tools are used that generate detailed, audit-proof reports. For physical destruction, a certified service provider is commissioned or a suitable in-house shredder is used. The certificates of destruction are archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the generated erasure reports and certificates of destruction. The process of physical destruction is inspected or the contracts and certifications of the external service provider are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For removable media, where technically possible, cryptographic erasure (Crypto-Erase) is used as the primary method. This involves securely destroying the key used for data encryption, which makes the data on the medium irretrievably unreadable. This is supplemented by secure overwriting or physical destruction as a secondary measure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The erasure process is integrated into the asset management system. When a data carrier is marked as 'to be decommissioned', the command for cryptographic erasure is automatically sent to the data carrier's management console. The successful execution is recorded in the asset lifecycle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the technical implementation of the crypto-erase function and the security of the key management. It is verified that the process is automated, logged, and secured by a secondary destruction measure.

controls.title: Labeling of removable media for shipment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Removable media to be shipped MUST be labeled in such a way that the senders and recipients can identify them immediately. The label MUST be unambiguous for the recipients. The labeling of removable media containing information requiring protection MUST NOT allow outsiders to draw conclusions about the type and content of the information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The labeling is done using a neutral, unique reference number on the data carrier or the inner packaging. The sender and recipient communicate this reference number via a separate, secure channel (e.g., telephone or encrypted email) to be able to assign the shipment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the shipping policy and checks shipping logs or samples to see if the labeling procedure is being followed. It is checked that the label itself does not disclose any confidential information.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Labeling for shipment is part of a comprehensive shipping process. For each shipment, a transmittal slip is created that contains the reference number, sender, recipient, and a description of the contents for internal use. The packaging is sealed to make it difficult to open undetected during transport.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Security seals or tamper-evident shipping bags are used. The serial numbers of the seals are noted on the transmittal slip. The recipient checks the integrity of the seal upon receipt.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the shipping materials used (e.g., security bags) and checks the transmittal slips for completeness. It is verified that the process for checking seal integrity is established at the recipient's end.

controls.title: Ensuring integrity and availability for long-term storage

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If removable media are used to store data for long periods, the institution MUST ensure that the removable media used are suitable for this purpose. The integrity of the data SHOULD be checked regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For long-term archiving, only media specified by the manufacturer for this purpose are used (e.g., special LTO tapes, M-DISC DVDs). A plan for regular integrity checks (e.g., annual reading and comparison of checksums) is created and implemented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the long-term archiving policy, the specifications of the media used, and the logs of the integrity checks performed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A data migration strategy is implemented for long-term archiving. This involves copying the data to new media generations or technologies at regular intervals (e.g., every 5-7 years) to prevent media aging and technical obsolescence. At least two copies of the archive data are stored on different media in separate, secure locations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal migration plan is part of the archiving concept. The storage locations meet defined requirements for fire protection, climate control, and access control. Integrity checks also include regular tests of recoverability.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the migration plan and the documentation of the storage locations. The logs of the migrations and recovery tests performed are checked.

controls.title: Integrity protection through checksums or digital signatures

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For confidential information on removable media, a procedure to protect its integrity MUST be used. For this purpose, checksums (e.g., SHA-256) are created for the files or containers to be protected. The checksums are transmitted to the recipient via a separate, secure channel.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A work instruction describes how users can create checksums for their data with a standard tool and how these are to be transmitted (e.g., by phone or separate email). The recipient is instructed to verify the checksum after receiving the data.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the work instruction and checks by asking users whether the procedure is known and applied. The process is traced using examples.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Digital signatures are used to protect the integrity and authenticity of the data. The files or data containers on the removable media are signed with a personal or departmental certificate. The procedures for protection against changes SHOULD be state-of-the-art.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution operates its own public key infrastructure (PKI) or uses a trusted external provider to issue certificates for users. Signature creation and verification is integrated into the applications used (e.g., archiving programs, document software).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the PKI and the policies for certificate issuance. It is checked on a random basis whether exchanged data is correctly digitally signed and whether the signature verification works properly at the recipient's end.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process of signature creation and verification is fully automated. A central system automatically signs all data written to official removable media with an organization-wide certificate. When reading the data on another system of the institution, the signature is automatically checked and if the integrity is violated, access is denied and an alarm is triggered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An endpoint protection solution with device control handles the automatic signing and verification. The private keys for the signature are securely stored in a Hardware Security Module (HSM). Integrity violations are reported to a central SIEM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the endpoint solution and the HSM. A test, in which a file on a removable disk is manipulated after signing, is used to verify that access is blocked on re-reading and the incident is reported.

controls.title: Secure shipping method and packaging

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When shipping removable media with confidential information, a shipping method MUST be chosen that allows tracking of the shipment. The packaging MUST be robust to avoid physical damage.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: It is specified in a policy that only parcel services with shipment tracking may be used for shipping such data carriers. Padded shipping bags or boxes are used. The tracking number is communicated to the recipient.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the shipping policy and uses shipping receipts to verify that traceable shipping methods were used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution MUST verify how confidential information can be adequately protected during shipment. A secure shipping package for removable media MUST be used, where tampering is immediately apparent. The institution MUST inform all parties involved about necessary shipping and packaging methods.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tamper-evident shipping bags or boxes with security seals are used. The unique numbers of the seals are recorded before shipment and communicated to the recipient via a separate channel. The recipient is instructed to check the integrity of the seal upon receipt and to report any irregularities immediately.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the packaging materials and seals used. The process of seal number communication and acknowledgment of receipt, including seal inspection, is checked using shipping logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the shipment of removable media with data requiring very high protection, a valuable cargo transport or courier service with a continuous, documented, and insured chain of custody is used. Alternatively, the transport is carried out by personally known and vetted messengers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are contracts with specialized security logistics companies. The entire transport route is fully documented, and each handover is acknowledged. The choice of service provider and procedure is based on a prior risk assessment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the contracts with the courier services and the chain-of-custody documentation created for a shipment. It is checked whether the choice of shipping method corresponds to the data's protection requirement assessment.

controls.title: Use of certified removable media

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For use with data requiring protection, only removable media from established and trusted manufacturers are procured. Models that offer integrated hardware encryption are selected.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the procurement process, there is a positive list of manufacturers and models that are approved for use. This list is regularly maintained based on market research and security recommendations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the procurement policy and the positive list. Based on purchase receipts and inventory lists, random checks are carried out to ensure that only approved models are procured and used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD only use removable media that are certified. The certification SHOULD particularly cover the integrity of data preservation as well as any existing encryption methods. Data carriers with a certification according to recognized standards such as FIPS 140-2/-3 or Common Criteria (CC) are preferably used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The procurement policy explicitly requires certification according to FIPS 140-2 Level 2 (or higher) or a comparable CC certification for all newly acquired hardware-encrypted removable media. The products' certificates are checked before purchase.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies, based on the procurement documents, that the purchased products have the required certificates. The validity of the certificates is checked on the websites of the certifying bodies (e.g., NIST, BSI).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only removable media are used that have a BSI approval for use with classified information or an equivalent, recognized national certification. The conformity of the delivered devices with the certified model is checked upon receipt of goods.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Procurement is limited to a small selection of models with BSI approval. The supply chain is secured to prevent tampering (supply chain attacks). Upon receipt, the exact model and firmware version is checked against the approval documents.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the approval documents and the processes for securing the supply chain and goods receipt. It is physically verified that the devices in use correspond exactly to the approved models.

controls.title: Use of dedicated IT systems for data verification

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated IT system (scan station), separate from the production network, is set up. All removable media from unknown or untrusted sources MUST be scanned for malware at this station before their data is used further.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard PC is used as a scan station. It is not a member of the domain and is located in a separate VLAN with no routing to the production network. It is equipped with up-to-date antivirus software. A work instruction regulates its mandatory use.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and network isolation of the scan station. The up-to-dateness of the antivirus software and the employees' awareness of the work instruction are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD use dedicated IT systems as a data sluice, where data is transferred from one removable medium to another and scanned for malware in the process. The data sluice is a hardened system and uses several different scan engines (multi-scanner) to increase the detection rate. Data transfer to the internal network is only possible via a controlled path.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The data sluice is a physically or logically (air gap) separated system. It is equipped with special kiosk software that enforces a guided process for scanning and controlled transfer of data. The transfer takes place, for example, to an internal, approved removable medium or via a read-only network share.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture and hardening of the data sluice. The configuration of the multi-scanner solution and the controlled transfer mechanism is checked. The effectiveness is demonstrated by a test with various malware samples.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The data sluice is a fully automated system that, in addition to virus scans, performs dynamic analysis in a sandbox and Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR). Any active or potentially malicious content is removed or neutralized before transfer to the internal network. The transfer is only possible via a data diode or a comparable, strictly unidirectional mechanism.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A commercial or open-source based kiosk solution with integrated sandbox and CDR technology is used. The logs of all scan, analysis, and transfer processes are stored and monitored centrally in a SIEM. The data diode ensures the physical separation of the networks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the detailed configuration of the sandbox and CDR components as well as the data diode. The system's ability to detect and block even unknown (zero-day) malware through behavioral analysis is verified. The log analysis in the SIEM is checked.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Removable media are often used to transport, store, or provide mobile access to data. Removable media include external hard drives, CD-ROMs, DVDs, memory cards, magnetic tapes, and USB drives.
Removable media can be classified by whether they are read-only, write-once, or rewritable. There are also differences in the type of data storage (analog or digital) or their form factor. For example, there are interchangeable storage media (e.g., installed hard drives) or external data storage devices (e.g., USB drives).

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: This module shows how removable media can be used securely. It also describes how to prevent unintentional disclosure of information via removable media.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The SYS.4.5 Removable Media module must be applied to every removable media device in the information network.
This module deals with the security properties of removable media. The protection of the IT systems to which the removable media can be connected is not considered in this module. Recommendations for this can be found in the SYS.1.1 General Server and SYS.2.1 General Client modules, as well as in the operating system-specific modules.
Removable media store data electronically, magnetically, or in other, not directly perceptible ways. They do not process data themselves. The requirements for such devices, e.g., smartphones and tablets, are listed in the SYS.3.2.1 General Smartphones and Tablets module. Cloud storage is also not considered removable media. Requirements for cloud environments can be found in the OPS.2.2 Cloud Usage module.
Removable media can be exchanged during in-person meetings or by mail. The secure exchange of the actual information is not covered in this module. For this, the requirements of the CON.9 Information Exchange module must be met.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Carelessness in handling information
parts.prose: Although institutions often have organizational regulations and technical security procedures for removable media, these are often bypassed through careless handling of the removable media. For example, it happens that removable media are left unattended in a meeting room during a break or left behind in a train compartment.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Insufficient knowledge of regulations
parts.prose: If the regulations for the correct handling of removable media are not sufficiently known, they cannot be followed. This can lead to numerous information security risks, for example, if unchecked USB drives are connected to the institution's IT systems.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Theft or loss of removable media
parts.prose: With removable media, the risk of data loss is higher than with stationary IT systems. Causes of data loss include theft or lost devices. The information stored on the removable media is often irretrievably lost in these cases. Furthermore, the information can fall into the hands of third parties.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Defective data carriers
parts.prose: Due to their size and areas of application, removable media are susceptible to damage, errors, or failures. The causes include constantly changing operating environments or mechanical impacts.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Impairment due to changing operating environment
parts.prose: Removable media are used in very different environments and are therefore exposed to many threats. These include, for example, damaging environmental influences such as excessively high or low temperatures and dust or moisture. In addition, there is, for example, transport damage. Another important aspect is that removable media are often used in areas with different security levels.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. Spread of malware
parts.prose: Removable media are often used to exchange data between different devices and the workstation computer. Malware could compromise data on the removable media and thus be transferred to the workstation computers.

controls.title: Integration into the security organization

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are initial approaches to organizing OT security. A responsible person has been named, but their role and tasks are not formally defined or communicated, and a formal ISMS exists only in fragments.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At this stage, the IT security officer is typically also entrusted with responsibility for OT, without dedicated resources or processes being provided for this purpose. Implementation is ad-hoc and reactive.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether a person has been appointed for OT security. It is determined whether there are initial documents or e-mails that prove a basic intention to establish an ISMS for OT.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic ISMS exists for the OT area, often as a simple document describing the most important responsibilities. A person is named as the main person responsible for OT security and is known within the relevant departments.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A basic ISMS document is created that describes the most important security goals and the role of the OT security officer. The announcement is made, for example, via a circular e-mail to the heads of the production departments.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existence of an ISMS document for OT. By interviewing employees in the OT environment, it is verified whether the person responsible for OT security is known.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An Information Security Management System (ISMS) for the operation of the OT infrastructure MUST exist, either as a standalone ISMS or as part of an overall ISMS. A person with overall responsibility for information security in the OT area MUST be appointed. He or she MUST be announced within the institution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ISMS for OT is formally documented, either as a standalone system or as a specific scope within the parent ISMS. The role of the OT security officer, including tasks, powers, and responsibilities, is clearly defined and published on the intranet or in the organizational handbook.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the formal documentation of the OT ISMS and its anchoring in the organization. It is verified that the role of the OT security officer is clearly defined and the person has been officially appointed and announced. This can be done by checking organizational charts, letters of appointment, and internal publications.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT ISMS is fully integrated into the institution's overall ISMS. There are clearly defined interface processes between OT and IT security teams (e.g., for incident response and change management). The effectiveness of the security organization is regularly evaluated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Joint workshops between IT and OT security teams are held to coordinate processes. The results are recorded in process descriptions and service level agreements (SLAs). Regular meetings between those responsible take place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documentation of the interface processes between IT and OT. Based on meeting minutes and examples from the ticket system, the practiced cooperation and information exchange between the areas is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrated ISMS for IT and OT is subject to a continuous improvement process (CIP), which is controlled by measurable key performance indicators (KPIs). The roles and responsibilities are so deeply embedded in the corporate processes that security aspects are automatically considered in all decisions in the OT environment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: KPIs such as 'time-to-patch' for OT systems, 'number of detected security incidents in OT', or 'maturity level of security measure implementation' are defined and visualized via a dashboard. The results feed directly into the management review. OT security is a fixed component of the target agreements for relevant managers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the defined KPIs and their development over time. It is checked whether the KPI results have demonstrably led to improvement measures in the OT ISMS. Through interviews with managers, it is verified that OT security is an integral part of their strategic planning.

controls.title: Protection against malicious programs

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Antivirus software is installed on some OT components considered particularly critical, such as engineering workstations. However, the configuration and checking of the manufacturer's approval are only carried out sporadically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Standard antivirus software from the office environment is installed on some Windows-based OT systems. Signature updates are often carried out manually and irregularly, sometimes directly from the internet.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks some OT systems for the existence of antivirus software. It is checked whether there is a comprehensible reason why some systems are protected and others are not.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On all OT components for which an antivirus solution is available and approved by the manufacturer, such a solution is installed. The signature updates are managed centrally to avoid direct internet connections for the OT systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central update server (e.g., WSUS or a manufacturer-specific tool) is placed in a DMZ between the office and OT network. The OT systems retrieve the signatures exclusively from this server. A list of systems with and without antivirus protection is maintained.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the central update server and verifies on a random basis on OT systems that it is configured as the sole update source. The list of systems without antivirus protection is checked for plausibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When using antivirus software on OT components, it MUST be considered whether and in which configuration the operation of antivirus software is supported by the manufacturing company. If this is not the case, the need for alternative protection methods MUST be checked. The virus signatures MUST NOT be obtained by OT systems directly from the internet.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented process is established. For each OT component, the manufacturer's approval for antivirus is checked and documented. If no approval is available, alternative protection measures such as application whitelisting, host-based intrusion detection, or enhanced network segmentation are evaluated and their selection is justified. The distribution of signatures is carried out exclusively via a dedicated, internal system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the documentation and evaluation procedure. Based on the system documentation, it is verified that for each component, either a manufacturer's approval for the antivirus protection is available or a justified decision for an alternative protection measure has been made. The technical implementation of the signature distribution is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For systems without classic antivirus protection, alternative protection measures such as application whitelisting are consistently implemented and in use. The configuration of the antivirus protection is hardened and optimized for the specific requirements of the OT applications (e.g., through exception rules for process communication). Alerts from the protection systems are collected centrally and analyzed promptly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Application whitelisting is introduced in monitoring mode to create a baseline of allowed applications, and is then switched to blocking mode. Antivirus configurations are optimized together with the plant manufacturers to avoid performance problems. Logs are sent to a central SIEM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the application whitelisting system and the defined rules. It is verified that the antivirus configurations contain specific exceptions for OT processes. In the SIEM, the prompt processing of alerts is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A multi-layered endpoint protection (Defense-in-Depth) is implemented on all OT systems, combining antivirus protection, application whitelisting, host-based intrusion detection/prevention systems (HIDS/HIPS), and behavioral analysis. The management and monitoring of these systems is highly automated, including automatic responses to defined threats.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solution is used that is specifically designed for OT environments. This solution integrates various protection mechanisms. Predefined SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) playbooks are used to automatically initiate countermeasures, e.g., isolating an affected system in the network, when attack patterns are detected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture of the endpoint protection solution and the configuration of its integrated modules. The effectiveness is verified by analyzing logs from past security incidents or through controlled tests (e.g., with the EICAR test virus). The configuration and functionality of the automated response mechanisms are checked.

controls.title: Logging

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On individual, particularly critical ICS components, logging of access and changes is enabled. However, the logs are only stored locally and not regularly analyzed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default logging functions of Windows or the respective ICS system are activated on the engineering workstation and the central server. A systematic analysis only takes place in the event of an error.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks on a random basis whether logging is activated on critical systems and whether log files are present.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Logging of access and changes is enabled on all ICS components where this is technically possible. There is an instruction on how to handle the log data, but central collection does not yet take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A policy specifies that logging must be enabled on all systems. The logs are stored locally and manually copied to a central storage at regular intervals (e.g. monthly).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logging policy and verifies on a sample of systems that logging is active. A check is made to see whether the manual archiving of the log files is carried out in a traceable manner.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every change to ICS components MUST be logged. In addition, all access to ICS components MUST be logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A logging policy for the OT environment is defined, which specifies which events (e.g. login, logout, configuration change, start/stop of processes) are to be logged on which systems. The logs are recorded in a standardized format.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the logging policy for completeness and appropriateness. Using test cases (e.g., carrying out a configuration change), it is verified whether the corresponding events are logged on the target systems as required.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All relevant log data from ICS components are collected centrally on a dedicated log server or in a SIEM system. Basic correlation rules are defined to detect security-relevant events (e.g., a large number of failed logins) and trigger alarms. The integrity of the log data is ensured.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A log server is set up in a secure network zone. The ICS components are configured to send their logs to this server via syslog or via agents. Dashboards and rules for monitoring critical OT events are created in the SIEM. After transmission, log files are provided with hash values to detect manipulation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture of the central log collection. A check is performed to ensure that all systems defined in the concept are sending their logs to the central server. The effectiveness of the correlation rules is tested by simulating attack or failure scenarios. The mechanisms for protecting log integrity are verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central log analysis is highly automated and uses User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) to detect anomalies and complex attack patterns in the OT environment in real time. The response to critical alarms is automated via SOAR playbooks. The log data is archived for the long term in an audit-proof manner for forensic analysis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A SIEM system with a UEBA module is used to learn normal behavior and report deviations. A SOAR tool is connected to the SIEM to automatically trigger reactions such as blocking a user account or isolating a device on the network in the event of highly critical alarms. The logs are archived on WORM (Write Once, Read Many) storage.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration and effectiveness of the UEBA module. The function of the SOAR playbooks is verified on the basis of test runs. The audit-proof archiving of the log data over the required period is checked.

controls.title: Creation of data backups

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data backups of programs and data are created irregularly and only for the most important OT systems. A backup after system changes does not take place systematically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators manually create copies of project files or system images and save them on external hard drives or network drives. There is no fixed schedule.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether data backups exist at all and how up-to-date they are. The ad-hoc nature of the process is determined through interviews.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic backup plan that provides for regular backups for all OT components. The backups are carried out according to a fixed schedule. A backup after changes is carried out manually, but usually promptly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple backup plan (e.g. in an Excel spreadsheet) lists all systems and the backup frequency. Scripts are used to automate the backups. After changes, a checklist reminds the administrator of the necessary data backup.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the backup plan and compares it with the existing backup files to verify compliance with the schedule. The checklists or logs for backups after changes are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Programs and data MUST be backed up regularly. A backup MUST also be created after every system change to OT components.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed data backup concept for the OT environment has been created and approved. It defines the backup type (full, incremental), frequency, and retention periods for each system category. The process for creating a backup after a system change is clearly defined and linked to the change management process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the data backup concept for completeness. Based on the change management log, random checks are carried out to verify whether a corresponding data backup was also created and logged after each documented change. Compliance with the regular backup schedules is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data backups are performed and monitored automatically. The backup data is stored in a physically separate and secure location (e.g. different fire compartment, external location). Recovery tests are carried out and documented regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central backup software is used, which controls the backup process and notifies about success or failure. The backup media are stored in a fireproof safe or with an external service provider. A test recovery of a selected system is carried out quarterly in a test environment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the backup software and the alerting system. The logs of the recovery tests are reviewed. The secure storage of the backup media is verified by an inspection or by certificates from the service provider.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire backup and recovery management is a highly automated and validated process. The backup data is encrypted before it leaves the system. Recovery tests are part of the regular, comprehensive emergency drills, and the recovery time objectives (RTO) and recovery point objectives (RPO) are measured and optimized.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The backup software encrypts the data client-side with a strong algorithm. The key is managed securely. As part of annual emergency drills, the complete failure of a plant section is simulated and the recovery from backups is practiced under time pressure. The measured RTO/RPO values are compared with the target values defined in the concept and, in case of deviations, measures for optimization are taken.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the encryption configuration and the key management concept. The logs of the emergency drills are analyzed, in particular the sections on data recovery and the measured RTO/RPO values. It is checked whether a process for continuous improvement of the backup and recovery process exists and is practiced.

controls.title: Documentation of the OT infrastructure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are basic inventory lists of OT components and a simple network diagram. However, these are not updated regularly and may not be complete.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The inventory lists are maintained in spreadsheet programs. The network diagram is a simple drawing showing the most important components and connections. Updates are only made for major projects.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the existing lists and plans with the real environment on a random basis to determine the degree of obsolescence and incompleteness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All security-relevant parameters of the OT infrastructure SHOULD be documented. An inventory SHOULD list all software and system components. In addition, an up-to-date network diagram SHOULD document zones, zone transitions, communication protocols used, and external interfaces.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A system inventory (e.g. in a CMDB or specialized OT management software) is being built and maintained. It contains at least the type, version, and responsible person for each component. A detailed network diagram is created and versioned with a suitable tool. The documentation is updated after every relevant change.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence and level of detail of the system inventory and the network diagram. Based on current change logs, it is verified whether the documentation was updated promptly. The consistency between the network diagram and the actual configuration (e.g., firewall rules at zone transitions) is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation is managed and detailed in a central management system or a CMDB. It includes product and protocol versions used, responsibilities, and any restrictions imposed by manufacturers or regulatory authorities. The network diagram also documents manual data transfer procedures, e.g., via removable media.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The CMDB is expanded with specific attributes for OT components (e.g. 'manufacturer approval for patch X'). Processes for manual data transfers are analyzed and documented in the network diagram as logical connections with corresponding risk notices. The documentation is linked to the change and incident management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the completeness of the extended documentation attributes in the CMDB. It is verified that the documentation is actively used in the planning of changes and the processing of incidents by checking corresponding links in the ticket systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT infrastructure documentation is kept up-to-date wherever technically possible by automated discovery tools. The data integrity of the CMDB is regularly checked. The documentation is so detailed that it enables automated compliance checks against security policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Passive network scanners suitable for OT protocols are used to automatically capture inventory and communication relationships and reconcile them with the CMDB. Scripts are developed to read system configurations, compare them with the target values stored in the CMDB, and report deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration and coverage of the automated discovery tools. The reports from automated compliance checks are analyzed, and the handling of reported deviations is tracked. The effectiveness of the process is verified by intentionally misconfiguring a test system.

controls.title: Development of a suitable zoning concept

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT network is fundamentally separated from the office network, for example, by a firewall. However, there is no further segmentation within the OT network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single firewall is installed between the IT and OT network. The rules are often kept very general (e.g., 'allow all traffic from the engineering workstation to the OT network').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall configuration that separates the IT and OT network and verifies that there are no unsecured bypass routes. It is determined that the OT network is internally a flat, unsegmented network.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT infrastructure SHOULD also be segmented horizontally into independent functional areas, such as plants. The individual zones SHOULD be independent of each other in operation as far as possible. The network SHOULD be designed to be resistant to tampering and faults.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A zoning concept, based for example on the Purdue model, is developed and documented. The OT network is divided into several zones (e.g., control level, supervision level, field level) using VLANs or physical firewalls. The communication rules between the zones are restrictively defined according to the 'need-to-know' principle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documented zoning concept and compares it with the actual implementation (VLAN configuration, firewall rules). It is verified that the defined rules restrict data traffic between the zones as intended. Penetration tests can verify the effectiveness of the segmentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In particular, the zones in which the technical process is controlled SHOULD remain functional for a certain period of time in the event of a failure of the other zones. The decoupling after an attack SHOULD also continue to function. This period SHOULD be suitably defined and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each critical zone, a risk analysis is performed to determine the maximum tolerable downtime of supporting systems from other zones. Based on this, measures for self-sufficiency are implemented (e.g., local data storage, redundant control components). The time periods and emergency procedures are documented and tested.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the risk analysis and the requirements for zone autonomy derived from it. Controlled tests (e.g., disconnecting the connection to a higher-level zone) are used to verify that the critical zone continues to function for the defined period. The emergency procedures are checked for their practicality.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The zoning concept is further refined by using micro-segmentation within the zones to prevent the lateral movement of attacks. All data traffic between the zones and segments is monitored by OT-specific Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) that detect anomalies in communication behavior.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Technologies such as Software-Defined Networking (SDN) or specific security gateways are used to dynamically enforce communication rules down to the individual device level. An OT IDS is implemented at strategic points in the network (e.g., on the mirror ports of core switches). It learns the normal communication behavior ('baseline') and alerts on deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture and rules of the micro-segmentation. The configuration of the OT IDS is checked and its ability to detect attacks is verified by simulating attacks in a test environment. The response to IDS alarms is tracked in the SIEM and incident response process.

controls.title: Change management in OT operations

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Changes to OT systems are recorded in a logbook or a list. There is an informal agreement on major changes, but no formal approval process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A shared network drive contains a text or spreadsheet document where administrators enter their changes. Important changes are discussed in the team meeting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the content of the logbook with the actual configurations and log files of the systems to assess the completeness and accuracy of the manual recording.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated change process SHOULD be defined, documented, and practiced for changes to the OT.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal change management process is described in a process document. It includes the steps 'Request for Change', 'Assessment', 'Approval', 'Implementation', and 'Review'. Standard forms are used for requesting changes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation. Using a sample of recently implemented changes, the entire process from request to review is tracked to ensure that all defined steps have been followed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT change process is supported by a ticketing system. Every change requires a risk assessment and the creation of a rollback plan. There is a Change Advisory Board (CAB) with representatives from OT operations and security, which decides on high-risk changes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT ticketing system is extended with a workflow for OT changes, or a separate system is used. The fields for risk assessment and rollback plan are mandatory fields in the change request form. The CAB meets on a regular basis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the workflow in the ticketing system. The quality of the risk assessments and rollback plans is evaluated on a sample basis. The minutes of the CAB meetings are reviewed to understand the decision-making processes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The change process is largely automated. Before productive implementation, all changes, especially to the control logic, are validated in a realistic test and simulation environment. Automated configuration monitoring detects and reports unauthorized changes in real time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'digital twin' or a Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) test environment is used for validating changes. File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) or configuration monitoring tools are rolled out on all critical OT systems and report any deviation from the approved target state to the SIEM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation and use of the test environment. The configuration of the FIM solution is verified. To test its effectiveness, an unauthorized change is made to a test system and it is checked whether this is correctly detected and reported.

controls.title: Establishment of comprehensive access management between OT and office IT

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a list of people who have access to OT systems. The granting of permissions is done on request, but without a formal approval process or regular review. Group accounts are often used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Excel list is maintained that contains users and their basic access rights (e.g., 'Admin', 'User'). New users are created by the local administrator on demand.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the list of authorized persons with the accounts actually configured on the systems. The widespread use of shared administrator accounts is noted.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD establish a process for managing access and assigned permissions for accessing the OT. The access management SHOULD include the process, execution, and documentation for requesting, setting up, and revoking permissions. Permissions SHOULD be granted according to the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented process for user access management in OT is established. It uses forms for requesting, changing, and revoking permissions, which must be approved by the user's supervisor and the system owner. Personalized accounts are used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation. Based on personnel changes (new hires, departmental changes, departures), it is verified whether the process for setting up or revoking permissions is consistently followed. The permissions of individual users are checked for compliance with the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A role and authorization concept for the OT is defined. Permissions are reviewed regularly (e.g., annually) as part of a recertification campaign. Access to IT systems for employees, administrators, and third parties is also regulated. All participants are regularly made aware of compliance with the regulations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Typical roles (e.g., 'plant operator', 'maintenance technician', 'PLC programmer') are defined and the necessary permissions are permanently assigned to them. Every year, supervisors receive a list of their employees and their OT permissions for review and confirmation. The security policies are taught in regular training sessions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the role and authorization concept. The logs of the last recertification campaign are reviewed and it is checked whether identified deviations have been corrected. Participation in the awareness measures is verified using participant lists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management of users and permissions in OT is fully integrated into a central Identity and Access Management (IAM) solution. The entire lifecycle of an identity (Joiner, Mover, Leaver) is automated. The recertification campaigns are controlled and monitored by the IAM system. Misconduct is sanctioned.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An IAM system is connected to the OT systems (e.g., control systems, PLCs) via connectors. The HR process is linked to the IAM system so that when an employee joins, the basic accounts are automatically created and when they leave, all accounts are blocked. Escalation rules for recertifications not completed on time are configured in the IAM system. A catalog of sanctions is part of the works agreements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture and configuration of the IAM system and its connectors. The automated Joiner-Mover-Leaver process is validated through test cases. It is checked whether the measures defined in the sanctions catalog were demonstrably applied in cases of identified misconduct.

controls.title: Secure administration

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For administration, the protocols and tools provided by the system manufacturer are used, even if they are known to be insecure (e.g., Telnet, VNC). Access is protected by simple passwords.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators connect directly from their workstations to the OT systems via native protocols. There are no separate administration networks or special protective measures.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network traffic and detects the use of insecure administration protocols. The password policies are assessed as insufficient.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For initial configuration, administration, and remote maintenance in OT, either secure protocols or separate administration networks with appropriate protection requirements SHOULD be used. Access to these interfaces SHOULD be restricted to authorized personnel. Access SHOULD only be granted to the systems and functions required for the respective administrative task.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Wherever possible, insecure protocols are deactivated and replaced with secure alternatives (e.g., SSH instead of Telnet, RDP with NLA). For systems that only support insecure protocols, administrative access is restricted to a separate, highly secured administration VLAN. Access to this VLAN is strictly regulated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the OT systems for deactivated insecure services. The configuration of the administration VLAN and the associated firewall rules are reviewed. It is verified that only authorized persons have access to this network.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative access is performed via a central Bastion Host or Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. This solution enforces the principle of least privilege by restricting access to specific systems and commands per user. All administrative sessions are recorded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A jump server (Bastion Host) is set up in a secure DMZ. Administrators must first authenticate to this server before they can establish a connection to the target systems in the OT. A PAM solution is used to securely manage passwords (credential vaulting) and to record administrative sessions (e.g., as video).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture and configuration of the PAM solution. It is verified that no direct administrative access is possible past the PAM solution. The session recordings are reviewed on a random basis to understand the administrators' activities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Secure administration is fully automated. Configuration changes are no longer performed manually on the systems, but are declared and rolled out via 'Infrastructure as Code' (IaC) tools and central configuration management systems. The systems and communication channels for administration have the same high level of protection as the managed OT components themselves.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like Ansible, Puppet, or SaltStack are used for the configuration management of OT systems (where applicable). The configuration files are versioned in a Git repository, and the rollout process is coupled with the change management process. The administration infrastructure (e.g., PAM system, Ansible server) is designed redundantly and is hardened.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the IaC workflow, including code reviews and access permissions to the Git repository. It is verified that the configuration of the administration infrastructure complies with the highest security standards and is regularly audited. Manual, unlogged changes to the configuration must not be possible.

controls.title: Restrictive use of removable media and mobile devices in ICS environments

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an informal rule not to use private USB sticks in the OT environment. However, all USB ports on the OT systems are active and unprotected.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees are verbally instructed to be careful. There are no technical controls to prevent the use of removable media.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through an on-site inspection and technical check that USB ports are freely accessible and active. Interviews with employees confirm the absence of a formal regulation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the use of removable media and mobile devices, regulations SHOULD be established and communicated. Their use SHOULD be restricted. All unnecessary interfaces SHOULD be deactivated. At the active interfaces, usage SHOULD be restricted to specific devices or media.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A written policy governs the handling of removable media. Unnecessary USB ports are deactivated via BIOS/UEFI or group policy. For necessary data exchange, dedicated, company-owned USB sticks are used, which may only be used at a secured kiosk station (virus scanner airlock).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and verifies on a random basis on OT systems that unnecessary interfaces are actually deactivated. The function of the kiosk station is tested. It is checked whether the use of dedicated devices is technically enforced (e.g., via device control software).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For media and devices from service providers, there SHOULD be an approval process and a list of requirements. The requirements SHOULD be known to all service providers and confirmed by them in writing. The use of removable media is logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal process is established whereby service providers must apply to use their own devices or media. The application is reviewed and approved by the system owner. The service provider's devices are checked at the kiosk station before use. Service providers must sign a security agreement. The device control software logs every connection of a removable storage device.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the approval process and the signed security agreements from service providers. The logs of the device control software are analyzed for unauthorized usage attempts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data exchange via removable media is, wherever possible, replaced by secure network transmissions via a DMZ (data lock). For the remaining use cases, only encrypted removable media with a hardware-based device ID are used, a practice that is centrally managed and monitored in real time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data diode or a Content Disarm and Reconstruction (CDR) solution is implemented as a secure data lock. Only specially approved, hardware-encrypted USB sticks whose serial number is stored in the device control software can be used. Any attempt to use an unauthorized stick triggers an immediate alarm in the SIEM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture and configuration of the data lock. The configuration of the device control software is checked to ensure it only allows the authorized, encrypted sticks. The alarm chain is tested by attempting to connect a foreign USB stick.

controls.title: Monitoring, logging and detection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Log and event data are stored locally on the OT systems. Analysis only takes place reactively when a problem or a malfunction has occurred. There is no formal incident response plan.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default event viewers of the operating systems are manually checked by the administrators in case of an error. A contact list for emergencies is available.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor finds that log data exists but is not used proactively. The absence of an incident response plan is documented as a major weakness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Operational and security-relevant events SHOULD be identified promptly. For this purpose, a suitable log and event management system SHOULD be developed and implemented. The log and event management SHOULD include appropriate measures to detect and collect security-relevant events. It SHOULD also include a response plan (Security Incident Response).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A concept for log and event management is created. It defines which events are considered security-relevant. Logs are centrally collected on a log server. A basic incident response plan is written that defines roles (e.g., Incident Manager), reporting channels, and basic response steps (e.g., isolating the system).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the log management concept and the incident response plan. It is verified that the defined security-relevant logs are collected centrally. The knowledge of the response plan among the responsible employees is checked through interviews.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The response plan SHOULD define procedures for handling security incidents. It SHOULD cover the classification of events, reporting channels and definition of the organizational units to be involved, response plans for damage limitation, analysis and recovery of systems and services, as well as the documentation and follow-up of incidents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The log data is fed into a SIEM system, which uses correlation rules to identify and classify incidents from individual events. The incident response plan is expanded into a detailed playbook that contains specific instructions for different incident types (e.g., malware, unauthorized access). A 'lessons learned' workshop is held after each incident.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the SIEM and the effectiveness of the correlation rules. The incident response playbooks are evaluated for completeness and practicality. The minutes of the 'lessons learned' workshops and the resulting improvement measures are analyzed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated OT monitoring system that masters network traffic analysis (NTA) and protocol deep packet inspection (DPI) is used to detect threats. The response to incidents is largely automated by SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response). Regular exercises (table-top, simulations) keep the incident response team ready for action.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specialized OT security platform (e.g., from Nozomi, Dragos, Claroty) is implemented. It learns the normal network traffic and detects anomalies, such as the use of unusual PLC function codes. Critical alarms from this platform automatically trigger responses via the SOAR system, e.g., blocking an IP address on the firewall. Emergency drills are conducted quarterly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture and configuration of the OT monitoring platform. The effectiveness of the anomaly detection is evaluated by analyzing logs or through targeted tests. The protocols and results of the emergency drills are reviewed to assess the maturity of the incident response process.

controls.title: Secure procurement and system development

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When procuring OT systems, security aspects are considered informally, but there are no fixed requirements or criteria. The decision is mainly based on functional and price aspects.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In discussions with the vendor, questions are asked about security features. The answers are included in the general assessment but are rarely decisive.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the tender documents of past procurement projects and finds that no formal security requirements were included.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When OT systems are to be procured, planned, or developed, information security regulations SHOULD be established and documented. The documents SHOULD be part of the tender. For ICS components, uniform information security requirements appropriate to the protection needs SHOULD be defined.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standardized requirements catalog for OT security is being developed. This catalog will become a fixed component of every tender for new OT systems. It contains requirements such as 'support for secure protocols', 'option to deactivate ports', or 'vendor commitment to provide security patches'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the standardized security requirements catalog. Based on current tenders, it is verified that this catalog is actually used and the providers' responses are evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During procurement, planning, or development, information security SHOULD be considered throughout the entire lifecycle. Prerequisites and implementation instructions for secure operation from the manufacturing companies SHOULD be planned and implemented at an early stage. The institution SHOULD document how the system fits into the existing security concepts (zone, authorization, antivirus protection).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The procurement process requires the provider to supply a 'security manual' or a 'hardening guide' for their product. Before commissioning, the integrator or supplier must prove that the system has been hardened and securely configured according to the specifications. The system owner must create an integration concept that describes the integration into the existing security architecture.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the required security manuals and configuration certificates are available. The integration concept is checked for plausibility and completeness. It is verified that the systems were accepted before going live.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution requires contractual assurances from its suppliers regarding the secure development process of the products (Secure Software Development Lifecycle). Products undergo an independent security test (penetration test, vulnerability scan) before commissioning. In the event that a cooperation partner fails, it is regulated how operations can be maintained (e.g., through source code escrow).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Contracts with suppliers include clauses that require compliance with standards such as IEC 62443-4-1. An independent team conducts vulnerability scans and penetration tests before go-live. For critical, individually developed software components, the source code is deposited with a trustee (escrow agent).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the supplier contracts for corresponding security clauses. The reports of the independent security tests are reviewed and it is checked whether the identified vulnerabilities were remedied before commissioning. The existence of escrow agreements is verified.

controls.title: Establishing a vulnerability management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Information about vulnerabilities is handled reactively when it becomes known by chance, e.g., through trade press or vendor emails. There is no systematic process for identification or assessment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When an administrator learns of a critical vulnerability, they check if their own systems are affected and, if necessary, apply a patch. This is done in an uncoordinated manner.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares a list of known vulnerabilities for the products in use with the patch level of the systems and identifies significant gaps.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the secure operation of an OT environment, the institution SHOULD establish a vulnerability management. The vulnerability management SHOULD identify gaps in software, components, protocols, and external interfaces of the environment. Furthermore, it SHOULD be possible to derive, evaluate, and implement necessary actions from this.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented process for vulnerability management is established. Responsibilities are assigned. Information sources are actively subscribed to (e.g., vendor advisories, CERT notifications). Incoming reports are compared with the system inventory. Each relevant vulnerability is assessed (e.g., using CVSS) and a decision on treatment (patching, mitigating, accepting) is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
