parts.prose: The handling of security incidents SHOULD be documented in an Incident Response Plan. This SHOULD define the roles and responsibilities and contain the measures to be taken.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specific Incident Response Plan for the SIS is created, which differs from the general IT emergency plan. It defines what constitutes an SIS security incident, who is on the emergency team (incl. OT personnel), and contains basic instructions (e.g., disconnecting the Engineering Station from the network).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence and content of the SIS-specific incident response plan. It is verified that the roles are clearly defined and the contact information is up to date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The incident response plan contains detailed instructions (playbooks) for specific SIS threat scenarios. The plan is tested regularly, at least once a year, through exercises (e.g., tabletop exercises) and improved as needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Playbooks are developed for scenarios such as 'Malware on Engineering Station', 'Unauthorized logic change detected', or 'Denial-of-Service attack on SIS network'. The exercises are logged, and the results are incorporated into the revision of the plan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence of the specific playbooks. The logs and 'lessons learned' documents from the last emergency drills are reviewed to verify that the plan is tested and improved.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The response to security incidents is largely automated and supported by a SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) platform suitable for OT use. The recovery procedures have been tested and enable a quick and secure return to normal operation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A SOAR solution collects alarms from various security tools (e.g., IDS, FIM). Upon detecting a known attack pattern, predefined actions are automatically executed, such as isolating a system or notifying the on-call team with specific recommendations for action. Current, tested backups of the SIS logic and configuration exist for restoration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the SOAR platform and the defined automation workflows. The existence and test status of the recovery backups are verified. Reports on past incidents are analyzed to assess the effectiveness of the automated process.

controls.title: Secure Planning and Specification of the SIS

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Accidental or unauthorized changes to the specification, implementation, and engineering data SHOULD be prevented by defined processes and access controls.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All relevant documents and data files are stored in a central, access-protected directory. Only a defined group of people has write access. Changes must be requested via a change request process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the access permissions for the central directory. Random checks are used to verify that changes to the data are covered by a documented change request.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All specifications and engineering data are managed in a version control system with strict access controls and a complete audit trail. Changes require approval according to the four-eyes principle.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A system like Git or Subversion is used to manage the engineering data (e.g., PLC programs, configuration files). Every change (commit) must be approved (reviewed) by a second, authorized person before it is merged into the production branch.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the version control system, especially the access controls and the configuration of the branch protection rules that enforce the four-eyes principle. The commit history is checked for compliance with the process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Changes to specifications and engineering data are cryptographically signed. The integrity and authenticity of the data are automatically checked each time it is used. Any attempt at unauthorized modification is blocked and reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Commits in the version control system must be signed with developers' GPG keys. The build and deployment system automatically checks these signatures. The final engineering files are also signed, and the logic system verifies this signature before loading the program.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the signature verification in the versioning and deployment system. It is verified that unsigned or invalidly signed changes are automatically rejected. The secure management of the cryptographic keys is also checked.

controls.title: Separation and Independence of the SIS from the Environment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The SIS SHOULD be operated without interference from its environment to ensure its safety functions. Processes that could potentially impact the SIS SHOULD be subject to the change management process of Functional Safety Management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SIS is operated in its own, dedicated network segment (VLAN). Data traffic between the SIS network and other networks (e.g., the process control system network) is controlled by a firewall that only allows the absolutely necessary communication.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the network architecture plans and the configuration of the firewalls and switches. It is verified that the SIS network is logically separated and the firewall rules follow the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The SIS is located in its own, strictly controlled security zone, which is separated from both the IT and the rest of the process network (BPCS) by dedicated firewalls. All data flows are explicitly defined, enforced, and monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) is set up between the SIS network and other networks. All data traffic is logged and monitored for anomalies by an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) specialized in OT protocols.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall rule sets for their restrictiveness and the configuration of the IDS. The logs of the firewall and the IDS are analyzed on a sample basis to evaluate the effectiveness of the monitoring.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The separation of the SIS is enforced by the use of unidirectional gateways (Data Diodes) for all outgoing data flows. This guarantees that any feedback to the SIS is prevented at the hardware level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data diode is used to transfer data from the SIS to the process control system or to a historian system. Any communication into the SIS network, e.g., for programming, is done via a highly secured bastion host solution with terminated connections.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor physically inspects the installation of the data diode and checks its configuration. It is verified that no alternative, bidirectional paths into the SIS network exist that could bypass the data diode.

controls.title: Secure Transfer of Engineering Data to SIS

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrity of the engineering data SHOULD be ensured during transmission to the SIS. This is typically done by checking checksums.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After transferring a new configuration or program file to the logic system, a hash value (e.g., SHA-256) of the source file is compared with the hash value of the target file. This process is described in a work instruction and is performed manually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the work instruction for the data transfer. Based on change logs, it is verified that the hash comparison has been documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The engineering data is transferred via a cryptographically secured (encrypted) channel. The integrity of the data is automatically verified by the protocol used or by the engineering tool.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The connection from the engineering station to the logic system is established using a secure protocol such as TLS or SSH. Many vendor-specific engineering tools offer such secure connections and automatically perform an integrity check after the transfer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the engineering software and the logic system to ensure that secure communication protocols are configured and enforced. A network analysis can be used to verify the encryption.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The engineering data is digitally signed by the creator or the engineering system before transfer. The target system (logic system) verifies the cryptographic signature before the data is accepted and loaded. This ensures both the integrity and authenticity of the data.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The engineering software uses a code-signing certificate to sign each new program version. The firmware of the logic system is configured to only accept signed programs from trusted sources. The public keys of the trusted sources are securely stored in the logic system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the process for managing code-signing certificates and the configuration of the logic system with regard to signature verification. It is tested whether the system correctly rejects an unsigned program or a program signed with an untrusted key.

controls.title: Securing data and signal connections

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If freedom from interference (unidirectionality) of data and signal connections cannot be demonstrated, these connections SHOULD be appropriately secured, typically by a firewall.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All network connections between the SIS and other systems (e.g., the process control system for displaying values) are routed through a firewall. The firewall rules are configured to only allow explicitly required communication (e.g., only read access from the control system to specific variables in the SIS).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the network documentation and the firewall configuration. The firewall rules are analyzed for their necessity and restrictiveness. It is checked whether a 'deny all' rule is at the end of the rule set.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All bidirectional connections to the SIS are routed through a dedicated firewall with a 'Deny-all-by-default' policy. The firewall logs are actively monitored for suspicious activities and rule violations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall logs are sent to a central SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system. In the SIEM, correlation rules are defined that trigger an alarm in case of unusual patterns (e.g., connection attempts to blocked ports).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks not only the firewall rules but also the configuration of log forwarding to the SIEM. In the SIEM, it is verified that corresponding alarming rules are implemented and that alarms are demonstrably processed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all connections where this is possible, unidirectional gateways (Data Diodes) are used to enforce a read-only data flow out of the SIS. Necessary bidirectional connections are secured via an application-layer proxy with Deep Packet Inspection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A data diode is used for the transfer of SIS data to the control system and the historian system. For the rare need for remote maintenance, a proxy solution is used in a DMZ that understands the specific protocol and only allows permitted commands, instead of just opening ports.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the physical installation and configuration of the data diode. The configuration of the application-layer proxy is checked in detail to ensure that the filter rules at the application level are correctly implemented and do not allow unsafe functions.

controls.title: Display and alarming of simulated or bypassed variables

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: SIS variables that are set to substitute values (simulated) or are externally bypassed SHOULD be monitored appropriately. The values SHOULD be continuously displayed to the users. Limits SHOULD be defined. When these limits are reached, the responsible personnel SHOULD be alerted appropriately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On the HMI of the control system, bypassed or simulated SIS variables are specially marked (e.g., by a different color or a symbol). There is a defined procedure on how to handle active bypasses (e.g., entry in the shift log).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the display of bypassed variables on the HMI demonstrated. The operating instructions and shift logs are checked to verify that the handling of bypasses is regulated and documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Each bypassed or simulated variable is prominently highlighted on all relevant HMI screens. An alarm is automatically generated if a bypass is active for longer than a predefined, risk-based period (e.g., one shift length).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the alarm system of the control system, a timer is configured for each possible SIS bypass. If this timer expires, an alarm with medium or high priority is triggered, which must be actively acknowledged by the operator. A list of all active bypasses can be viewed on the HMI at any time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the alarm system regarding the monitoring timers for bypasses. It is tested whether an alarm is correctly triggered if a variable remains bypassed beyond the defined time.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system requires formal approval and periodic re-authorization for each bypass. All activities related to bypasses (setting, resetting, authorizing) are logged in a tamper-proof audit trail. The system actively prevents bypasses from being forgotten.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A bypass can only be activated after entering a password or with confirmation from a second person (four-eyes principle). Each bypass has a maximum validity period. After expiry, the bypass is either automatically removed (if safe) or a highest-priority alarm is escalated to the shift supervisor and management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the bypass management system, including the workflows for approval and escalation. The audit trail for bypasses is checked for completeness and tamper-proofing.

controls.title: Handling of integrated systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For integrated systems that perform both safety and non-safety functions, a suitable strategy SHOULD be developed that regulates the handling of components affecting functional safety (Safety).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document is created that clearly defines which software modules, hardware components, and communication paths of the integrated system are safety-relevant (Safety) and which are not. The system is configured to implement this separation as best as possible.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the strategy document for clarity and completeness. The system configuration is spot-checked to verify that the defined separation between safety and non-safety functions has been implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documented strategy contains specific configuration guidelines and test procedures to verify that non-safety functions cannot negatively impact safety functions (non-interference).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Resource management functions of the integrated system are used to assign guaranteed CPU time and memory to safety-relevant processes. As part of system tests, faults are deliberately provoked in non-safety functions to demonstrate that the safety functions remain unaffected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the test reports of the non-interference tests. The configuration of the resource management in the system is analyzed to verify the correct prioritization of the safety functions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrated system uses certified hardware and software partitioning mechanisms (e.g., according to IEC 61508) to ensure a rigorous separation of safety and non-safety functions. The manufacturer provides a formal proof of non-interference.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A system is used that has been explicitly developed for mixed-criticality applications. Communication between the partitions takes place exclusively via a certified, strictly controlled, and monitored communication channel (e.g., a secure hypervisor or an RTOS with partitioning).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the manufacturer's certificates regarding partitioning and the non-interference properties. The configuration of the partitions and the secure communication channel is verified. It is checked whether changes to the configuration of the non-safety partition require a new safety acceptance.

controls.title: Ensuring the integrity and authenticity of application programs and configuration data

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a defined process to ensure the integrity of application programs and configuration data. This is done by manually checking hash values before installation or transfer.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Software downloads provided by the manufacturer are verified using the SHA256 hashes published on the website. Before transferring logic to a controller, the hash of the file is calculated and compared with a reference value from the change management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation and the logs from the change management system to verify that the hash value check is performed and documented as part of the process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The SIS or the engineering station automatically checks the integrity (e.g., via hash value or CRC checksum) of application programs and configuration data when loading or transferring. Integrity violations are reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The system's own functions for integrity checking are activated. The engineering software automatically performs a hash comparison after the transfer and displays the result. The controller's firmware checks the integrity of the stored program at every system start.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the system configuration to ensure that the automatic integrity checks are enabled. A test could be performed in which a deliberately corrupted file is transferred to see if the system correctly detects and rejects it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be ensured that manufacturing companies develop and integrate appropriate mechanisms that guarantee the integrity and authenticity of configuration data and application programs on the logic system or on the associated sensors and actuators. Any software offered as a download SHOULD be protected against manipulation. Integrity violations SHOULD be automatically detected and reported.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Only SIS components and software from manufacturers that consistently use digital signatures to ensure authenticity and integrity (code signing) are used. The systems (controllers, sensors, actuators) are configured to accept only signed firmware, configurations, and programs from authorized sources. The public keys of the authorized sources are securely stored on the device. Any integrity or authenticity violation triggers an immediate alarm.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the manufacturer's specifications and the system configuration regarding the enforcement of digital signatures. The process for secure management and distribution of public keys is audited. It is tested whether the system correctly blocks an unsigned update or an update signed with an invalid key and triggers an alarm. The automated verification of integrity and authenticity can also be performed via a script through an API, which queries the status of signatures on all devices and compares it with a central database.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS) form a subgroup of Industrial Control Systems (ICS). SIS are used to avert dangers to technical plants, the environment, and people. The basic structure of SIS hardly differs from conventional automation systems. The main difference lies in the increased reliability requirements with which the safety instrumented functions (SIF) to be executed by an SIS are performed. The level of reliability is expressed using the four-level Safety Integrity Level (SIL), which are defined in IEC 61508. SIL1 is the lowest and SIL4 the highest reliability requirement. Depending on the SIL level, different requirements apply to the permissible failure rate of components, the hardware fault tolerance of the architecture, the independence of testers, and other safety-relevant points. The entire lifecycle of an SIS is organizationally embedded in a Functional Safety Management (FSM).
This module is to be implemented regardless of the respective SIL level of an SIS. Information security must be considered in every phase of the lifecycle, from the development of the components to their application, operation, and decommissioning. It should be noted that ensuring the integrity of the SIS has the highest priority.
Another key feature of SIS is the independence and separation from surrounding IT systems and from Operational Technology (OT). This means that the availability and integrity of the SIS must not be influenced by them.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose:
The objective of this module is to formulate suitable requirements for SIS that must be met when establishing an Information Security Management System (ISMS).
For the purposes of this module, the term 'SIS' includes the components sensor, actuator, the safety-related programmable logic controller (SPLC), also referred to as a logic system, the application program, and especially the associated programming devices (Engineering Station, handhelds for sensor/actuator configuration) and visualization equipment.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module IND.2.7 Safety Instrumented Systems is to be applied once to each SIS component.
This module supplements the higher-level modules IND.1 Process Control and Automation Technology and IND.2.1 General ICS Component and requires their implementation.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Manipulation of the logic system
parts.prose:
The manipulation of the application program on the logic system, which can violate the integrity of an SIS, represents the greatest risk. Unlike with "simple" OT components, this can potentially have the most severe effects on the safety of people, the environment, and technical systems. In worksheet NA 163 of the international user association of automation technology in the process industries, NAMUR, the following three categories for risk assessment are defined:

• Category 1 covers manipulations that trigger the safety instrumented function (SIF) without a demand occurring. In terms of functional safety, the effects are not dangerous, as the SIS has initiated the safe state. However, the manipulations lead to an operational interruption. The cause can be, for example, malware or human error.

• Category 2 describes a case where the safety function is deactivated, and thus no longer provides protection. An unacceptable result is only reached when the demand occurs. The effects are classified as dangerous because the SIS cannot fulfill its primary task. Attack scenarios are classified as complex because the manipulation of the logic system alone is not sufficient to cause damage.

• The third category deals with the most serious scenario, in which one or more safety functions are deactivated and the demand is intentionally brought about. Here, too, the effects are classified as dangerous and the attack scenarios as very complex. This is because to bring about the demand, attackers must have not only knowledge of manipulating the SIS but also in-depth knowledge of the physical processes.

In December 2017, malware that specifically manipulated SIS was reported for the first time. The attack path led through the engineering station, which contained the special software for programming and parameterization. The malware installed there specifically searched for connected logic systems from a particular manufacturer and loaded executable code onto them that manipulated the application program (the logic). Due to an error in this code, the validity check failed. As a result, the safety function was triggered and shut down the attacked plant to a safe state. Although the attack was not successful, it could have been assigned to category 2 or 3 due to both its impact and its complexity.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Insufficient monitoring and detection methods
parts.prose:
A key function of automation systems is to monitor the operating states of the process to be automated. For example, warnings relating to the process (e.g., when fill levels are exceeded) and technical parameters (e.g., temperature, valve position) are usually taken into account. In contrast, the supporting IT infrastructure is often not monitored.
If unusual or security-relevant events are not monitored or are monitored inadequately, attempted attacks, network bottlenecks, or foreseeable failures cannot be detected at an early stage.

groups.title: Remote maintenance in the industrial environment

controls.title: Planning the use of remote maintenance in OT (B) [Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Planning for the use of remote maintenance is done on an ad-hoc basis and is incomplete. A rudimentary concept exists only for individual, particularly critical remote maintenance accesses. A central overview or a uniform approach for the entire OT is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In this phase, often only the standard remote maintenance solutions provided by the manufacturer are used without further adaptation or conceptualization. The documentation, if it exists, is distributed across individual departments or teams and is not consolidated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews and review of documentation fragments that no uniform, central remote maintenance concept exists. It is checked whether any planning documents for remote maintenance exist for randomly selected systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic remote maintenance concept has been created that covers the most important systems. However, it does not take into account all specific requirements, such as those of decentralized infrastructures or legacy systems. The documentation of the accesses exists, but it is not maintained centrally or consistently.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A first concept is drafted as a Word or a wiki document. It lists the known remote maintenance accesses and defines rough rules. Coordination with suppliers is reactive and not part of a standardized process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of a remote maintenance concept. Through random checks, the coverage of different system types (new, old, decentralized) is examined to determine whether the concept has gaps. The completeness of the recorded remote maintenance accesses is checked against an inventory list.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the industrial environment, a uniform, central remote maintenance concept MUST be created for all remote maintenance facilities for the entire OT of the institution. The OT remote maintenance concept MUST take into account specific legal requirements, specifications from plant manufacturers, requirements from decentralized infrastructures, connections, availability, environmental conditions, and existing systems. All aspects MUST be coordinated with all involved internal and external parties. All remote maintenance accesses MUST be recorded in a central documentation. For newly acquired machines that can be remotely maintained, the requirements MUST be coordinated with the suppliers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concept is created as a formal, versioned, and approved document. Workshops are held with OT operations, IT operations, planners, and, if necessary, external service providers to coordinate all aspects. The central documentation of the accesses is done in a dedicated database or a CMDB module. For the procurement of new machines, a checklist is developed that contains the requirements for remote maintenance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the central OT remote maintenance concept and checks whether all required aspects (legal requirements, manufacturer requirements, etc.) are covered. It is verified that coordination processes with internal and external parties have taken place (e.g., through minutes). The central documentation of the accesses is inspected and checked for completeness and timeliness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Building on the defined concept, standardization of the remote maintenance solutions used is actively pursued. As soon as standardized solutions for remote maintenance are planned, OT and office and building IT MUST coordinate with each other. The concept is reviewed regularly, at least annually, and updated as needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A project to standardize remote maintenance is initiated with the goal of reducing the variety of solutions. Preferred standard solutions are evaluated and defined. Regular coordination meetings are held between OT and office IT to leverage synergies and develop common standards.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether there is a documented strategy for standardizing remote maintenance solutions. Evidence is requested for the regular review and updating of the concept. In addition, the existence of minutes of joint meetings of OT and office IT for the coordination of remote maintenance solutions is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The remote maintenance concept is fully integrated into the entire lifecycle of the OT systems, from procurement to operation and decommissioning. The standardization of remote maintenance solutions is largely implemented. The central documentation of accesses is automated and dynamically kept up-to-date and validated through regular network scans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements from the remote maintenance concept are an integral part of the procurement process and are technically verified before a new system is put into operation. An asset management system is coupled with discovery tools to automatically inventory remote maintenance accesses and report deviations from the target state.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of remote maintenance requirements into the formal procurement policies. The functionality of the automated inventory and deviation scans is demonstrated. The auditor can initiate a test scan to check the detection rate.

controls.title: Consistent documentation of remote maintenance by OT as well as office and building IT (B) [IT operations, maintenance personnel]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only the most obvious remote maintenance accesses are documented. The documentation is maintained separately by OT and IT in different lists and formats. Accesses integrated in package units are systematically overlooked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each team (OT, IT) maintains its own Excel list of the accesses it knows. There is no reconciliation and no consolidated view.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation from both departments and determines through comparison that they are inconsistent and incomplete. A random check of a package unit on site reveals undocumented accesses.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a first joint effort to record all remote maintenance accesses. The resulting documentation is stored in a common location, but the process for updating it is manual and not performed regularly. Deactivated accesses are not consistently tracked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A shared wiki or a network drive is used to store a central list. Updates are only made on request and not as part of a defined process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of the shared documentation. Based on change logs from recent months, it is checked whether new systems or changes to existing systems have led to a timely update of the documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the industrial environment, OT and office and building IT MUST jointly record and document all OT remote maintenance accesses. Especially for remote maintenance components integrated in package units, all deactivated accesses MUST also be documented. The documentation is maintained centrally and is accessible to both areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A defined, joint process is established to record and document remote maintenance accesses. This process is part of plant onboarding and change management. A CMDB or a dedicated database serves as the storage location. It is explicitly recorded which accesses are active and which have been deliberately deactivated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the defined process for recording and documenting remote maintenance accesses explained to them. Access to the central documentation is checked. Random samples of systems (especially package units) are selected and it is verified whether all their remote maintenance accesses (active and deactivated) are correctly documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The manual documentation is supplemented by regular, semi-automated scans of the OT network to identify undocumented remote maintenance accesses. The results of the scans are compared with the CMDB and deviations are tracked in a defined process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Port scanners or specialized OT discovery tools are used to periodically (e.g., monthly) search for open ports that indicate remote maintenance services (RDP, VNC, SSH, manufacturer-specific ports). A script compares the scan results with the entries in the CMDB and generates a report on deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and logs of the discovery tools. The reports from the last deviation scans are analyzed, and it is tracked how the identified deviations were processed (e.g., subsequent documentation or deactivation of the access).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation of remote maintenance accesses is fully automated. Passive and active network discovery tools update the CMDB continuously and in real-time. Any newly detected or changed remote maintenance interface that does not comply with the target state automatically triggers a security alarm and an incident response process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A professional OT security platform is used that offers continuous asset and vulnerability management. The platform is configured to monitor a 'golden' baseline of allowed remote maintenance accesses. Any deviation triggers an automated ticket in the incident response system and can optionally trigger an automatic network quarantine of the affected device.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the OT security platform demonstrated to them. An unauthorized remote maintenance service is activated live on a test system to verify that the alarm and the incident response process are triggered as defined.

controls.title: Regular checks and exception approvals of existing OT remote maintenance accesses (B) [IT operations]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Checks of remote maintenance accesses only take place reactively, e.g., after a security incident. There is no established process for approving exceptions to the (possibly non-existent) concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When a problem occurs, the configuration of the affected system is manually investigated. Exceptions are approved informally by word of mouth and are not documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the process for configuration checks and exception approvals and finds that none exists. The analysis of past incidents shows that checks only took place retrospectively.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Manual, periodic checks (e.g., annually) are carried out using checklists to verify that remote maintenance access conforms to the concept. An informal approval process for exceptions exists but is not consistently documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Once a year, an employee goes through a checklist and randomly checks some systems. Exceptions are approved by email and filed in a folder.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the checklists and audit logs from the last audit. The consistency of the audit is assessed. The documentation of the exception approvals is checked for completeness and traceability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All systems MUST be checked regularly to ensure that all their remote maintenance access points comply with the target state, i.e., the current remote maintenance concept for OT. An approval process MUST be established within OT for necessary deviations from the concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An audit plan is created that specifies which systems are to be audited at which interval. The approval process for exceptions is formally described, including the responsible roles, the necessary justification, and a maximum validity period. All audits and approvals are centrally documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and implementation of the audit plan. The formally defined approval process for exceptions is audited. Existing exceptions are randomly selected and checked to see if the process was followed (e.g., presence of an approved application, compliance with the validity period).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The audits are carried out at shorter intervals and are partially automated through the use of configuration management or scanning tools. The approval process for exceptions is formally documented, time-limited, and requires a documented risk assessment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Scripts or configuration compliance tools are used to automatically check the configuration of remote maintenance interfaces (e.g., firewall rules, service status) against a defined baseline. Each exception request must include a risk assessment form that describes the necessity and the compensating controls.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the functionality of the automated audit tools demonstrated. He checks the quality of the risk assessments for approved exceptions and ensures that compensating controls are plausible and implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance checks are performed continuously and fully automatically using configuration baselining and drift detection tools. Any deviation from the approved configuration (including approved exceptions) automatically triggers an alert. The exception management process is integrated into a GRC (Governance, Risk, Compliance) tool.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A system integrity monitoring system (e.g., Tripwire, OSSEC) or an OT security platform continuously monitors the relevant configuration files and system settings. The workflow for exception approvals, including risk assessment and release, is fully mapped and audited in the GRC tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the drift detection tool. In the GRC tool, they check the end-to-end process of an exception approval. To test the functionality, an unauthorized change is made to a test system to check whether the alarm is triggered correctly and promptly.

controls.title: Binding regulation of OT remote maintenance by third parties (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Contracts with the most important suppliers contain only general, non-specific clauses on remote maintenance. Smaller service providers or integrators often have no contractual regulations regarding remote maintenance at all.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The standard purchasing conditions are used without specific adjustments for IT/OT security. Remote maintenance is considered a self-evident service that does not require further regulation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews contracts with several external service providers and finds that specific, enforceable regulations on OT remote maintenance are missing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Standard contract templates contain basic clauses on remote maintenance. However, these are not tailored to the specific risks of the system to be maintained. Internal responsibilities for authorizing access are named, but compliance is not consistently monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The legal department has created a standard clause on remote maintenance, which is included in all new contracts. This clause requires, for example, that the service provider must adhere to the 'operational regulations' without further specifying them.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the standard contract templates and assesses the effectiveness of the clauses. Through interviews, it is determined that while the internal responsibilities are known, there is no process to verify the service provider's compliance with the agreed-upon rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Appropriately restrictive regulations for OT remote maintenance MUST be contractually agreed upon with all external users, ensuring controlled and coordinated access at all times. Internally, it MUST be defined which activities by external parties are permissible via which access points, and which internal employees authorize, monitor, and support these accesses. It MUST be ensured that persons on or in plants cannot be endangered, either directly or indirectly, by active remote maintenance. Especially for safety-critical machines, remote access without the explicit consent of internal OT staff MUST be contractually excluded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A contract addendum (information security annex) is developed that details the technical and organizational requirements for remote maintenance. This annex becomes part of all relevant contracts. Internally, a matrix is created that defines for each service provider and system who (internal role) may authorize what (activity). For safety systems, an explicit clause is formulated that prohibits unannounced access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the standard contract addendum and randomly selected concluded contracts to verify the implementation. The internal responsibility matrix is checked. For contracts concerning safety systems, the clause on the reservation of consent is explicitly checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The contracts specify detailed technical and organizational requirements, such as the mandatory use of defined security gateways, the required logging depths, and the strict application of the principle of least privilege. The process for authorizing and monitoring external access is formally documented and regularly audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The contract addendum is expanded to include specific technical requirements, e.g., 'Access must be exclusively via the central PAM system of the institution on host xyz.ot.corp'. The requirements for logging are specified (e.g., 'all CLI commands are to be logged'). The internal authorization process is mapped in a workflow tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the technical conditions (e.g., gateway configuration) with the contractual requirements. Logs from past remote maintenance sessions are reviewed to check whether the required logging depth is being achieved. The audit logs of the authorization process are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All contracts with third parties are managed as part of a central vendor risk management program. Compliance with security requirements is regularly checked (e.g., annually) through audits at the service provider. Access rights are granted dynamically according to the 'just-in-time' principle. All third-party sessions are recorded and their activities are automatically analyzed for anomalies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC tool is used to manage supplier risks. The process includes an initial assessment, contract design, and regular re-assessments. The technical access solution (e.g., PAM) is configured to grant time-limited access only after successful approval in the workflow tool. The session logs are automatically sent to a SIEM system, which checks for suspicious behavior patterns.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the processes and documentation in the vendor risk management program. They have the configuration of the just-in-time access control and the automated analysis in the SIEM demonstrated. Reports from supplier audits are reviewed.

controls.title: Internal coordination for OT remote maintenance with office and building IT (B) [Planner]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are informal, irregular discussions between individual employees of OT and IT. There are no formal, documented agreements. Responsibilities are unclear, which leads to control gaps or conflicts of responsibility, especially with shared infrastructure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In case of problems, communication between technicians is by phone or email. There are no overarching regulations or committees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Through interviews with employees from OT and IT, the auditor determines that there are no formalized coordination processes or regulations. Contradictory statements on responsibilities are identified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic policy document describes the overarching responsibilities for OT remote maintenance. However, detailed regulations for specific processes, permissions, and shared interfaces are missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a high-level policy that states, for example, 'OT is responsible for the security of the production facilities, IT for the central network infrastructure'. How changes to the shared firewall are handled is not regulated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy document and assesses its level of detail. By analyzing an exemplary change process (e.g., enabling a new remote maintenance access), it is determined that the practical procedures are not regulated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT, the office and building IT, and all other involved organizational units MUST establish appropriately restrictive regulations for all components and interfaces that directly or indirectly enable OT remote maintenance. These internal regulations MUST ensure controlled and coordinated use at all times. The following aspects MUST be regulated: processes, responsibilities, and permissions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A joint, detailed policy or a Service Level Agreement (SLA) is created between OT and IT. This document clearly regulates the responsibilities (e.g., using a RACI matrix) for shared systems such as firewalls or VPN gateways. Change management processes are defined that require the consent of both parties.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the joint policy or SLA and checks whether processes, responsibilities, and permissions are clearly and completely regulated. Using examples (e.g., 'Who approves a firewall rule for an OT remote maintenance access?'), the practical suitability of the regulation is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive, joint policy for OT remote maintenance, signed by all stakeholders, is established. It includes detailed RACI charts for responsibilities and clear rules for the shared infrastructure. The policy is regularly reviewed and updated in a joint committee (e.g., OT-IT Security Board).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A regular meeting is established between OT and IT managers to discuss operational topics, upcoming changes, and the further development of joint regulations. The minutes of these meetings are archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the signed policy and the minutes of the joint committee. It is checked whether the policy is up-to-date and whether the discussed topics reflect operational reality.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The joint policy is enforced through technical controls. The shared infrastructure is managed using a 'Security-as-Code' approach, where configuration changes require approval from both OT and IT managers before their automated deployment (e.g., via a pull request in a Git repository).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration of firewalls and VPN gateways is stored in a version control system (e.g., Git). Changes can only be submitted via a defined workflow (e.g., merge request), which requires a technical review (linting, syntax check) and formal approval by representatives of both areas before a CI/CD pipeline rolls out the change to the systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the 'Security-as-Code' workflow. They analyze the commit history in the repository to verify that the four-eyes principle approval process by OT and IT is consistently followed. A test change is submitted to demonstrate the entire workflow live.

controls.title: Securing every remote maintenance access to the OT (B) [IT Operations]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only the main access points to the OT network are secured by a general firewall. Individual remote maintenance solutions integrated by manufacturers, e.g., in package units, can bypass these controls (e.g., via an integrated cellular modem).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central firewall separates the office network from the OT network. However, there is no inspection to determine if individual machines in the OT have their own paths to the internet or other networks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor identifies uncontrolled external connections that bypass the central firewall through physical inspection of a package unit and network analysis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central VPN gateway or firewall is used for all known remote maintenance access. However, this component is managed by the office IT without specific OT security knowledge. There is no additional security component to secure decentralized, manufacturer-specific access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The OT uses the central VPN service of the IT. The firewall rules are often too broad ('allow service provider X access to the entire production network').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules for OT remote maintenance access and finds that they do not follow the principle of least privilege. The responsibilities for maintaining the rules are identified as unclear.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In an industrial environment, the OT MUST be able to control every access to an IT system that provides a remote maintenance service for the OT. For this purpose, the access MUST be secured by at least one security component under the responsibility of the OT. If components of OT remote maintenance access are located decentrally or are integrated into package units, then these accesses MUST be secured by an additional security component that is centrally located and not integrated into a package unit.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated firewall or gateway is placed in an OT DMZ, managed by OT operations. All remote maintenance access, including that from package units (e.g., by redirecting traffic), is technically forced to pass through this central component. The rules on this component are maintained restrictively according to the 'need-to-know' principle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and configuration of the central OT security component. Network topology plans and routing tables are analyzed to ensure that no bypass possibilities exist. The responsibility of the OT for managing the component is proven by checking the access permissions on the system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access for remote maintenance SHOULD be standardized for all access types. Every access SHOULD be controlled and explicitly authorized using central authentication components. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) is enforced for all remote maintenance access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central Remote Access Gateway (e.g., based on SSL-VPN or a PAM system) is implemented. This gateway is connected to a central authentication service (e.g., OT-Active Directory with RADIUS) that enforces MFA. All manufacturer-specific authentication methods are disabled or replaced by this central mechanism.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the configuration of the central Remote Access Gateway and the authentication service. An attempt is made to establish a remote maintenance access without MFA to test the effectiveness of the control. It is checked whether all access runs through this unified solution.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All remote maintenance access is handled via a dedicated Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution in an OT DMZ. Access is granted per session and 'just-in-time' with strong MFA. All native remote maintenance functions of package units are either technically rerouted through the central PAM solution or completely disabled and replaced by access via the PAM system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution is used that not only controls access but also securely manages passwords (credential vaulting) and can record sessions. Network Access Controls (NAC) are implemented in the OT network to ensure that only authorized connections initiated via the PAM system can be established to the target systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the end-to-end architecture of the PAM solution, including its integration with NAC. They have a complete 'just-in-time' access workflow demonstrated. It is checked whether a direct connection to the target system bypassing the PAM system is effectively prevented by the NAC solution.

controls.title: Technical decoupling of access (S) [Planner]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The concept of a jump server is known, but it is only used for the most critical systems. In many cases, direct connections (e.g., RDP, VNC) from the outside to the target systems in the OT are routed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a jump server for controlling the main process, but for the maintenance of auxiliary units, a direct VPN access to the target system is allowed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules and finds that direct connections are allowed for numerous targets. Interviews confirm the inconsistent use of jump servers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A jump server exists, but it may be a simple system without specific hardening or located in the wrong network segment (e.g., in the office network instead of a DMZ). The required maintenance tools are installed locally on the service providers' client PCs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard Windows Server is used as a jump server without system hardening according to recognized standards. It is located in the server network of the office IT, from which a routed connection to the OT exists.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the network topology and the configuration of the jump server and finds that it is not in a DMZ and no specific hardening measures have been implemented. A port scan of the jump server shows unnecessarily open services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every remote access to any component in an OT zone SHOULD be decoupled. In every remote maintenance access to the OT, an IT system (jump server or application layer gateway) SHOULD be positioned to terminate the connection before it enters the OT target zone and to establish a new, monitored communication. All tools and programs required for remote maintenance SHOULD be installed on this IT system. The system SHOULD be positioned in a dedicated security segment (e.g., OT DMZ) and ideally be under the responsibility of the OT.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated server (physical or virtual) is installed as a jump server in a specially created OT DMZ. The operating system is hardened. All necessary maintenance software clients are installed directly on the jump server. Access to the jump server is realized via a separate protocol (e.g., RDP, SSH), while the jump server itself then speaks the system-specific protocols to the target system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the network architecture and the positioning of the jump server in the OT DMZ. The configuration of the firewall rules is checked to ensure that all remote maintenance connections are terminated via the jump server. The list of software installed on the jump server is checked for necessity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The jump server solution is consistently implemented for all remote maintenance access. It is a hardened multi-user system that is the responsibility of the OT. The access policies on the gateway are granular and restrictive. Data and file transfer between the external network and the jump server, as well as between the jump server and the target network, is strictly controlled and monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A terminal server (e.g., based on Windows Server or Linux with X2Go) is used, which allows simultaneous, isolated sessions for multiple users. The user profiles on the terminal server are configured so that they can only access the tools and connection targets relevant to them. File transfer is restricted to a dedicated, monitored folder.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the terminal server, especially the user and rights management. It is tested whether one user can access the tools or connection targets of another user. The logs of the file transfer monitoring are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A highly sophisticated Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution is used, which not only acts as a jump server but also offers session recording, keystroke logging, and command filtering. The required maintenance tools are provided in isolated containers on the jump server to prevent cross-contamination.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A commercial PAM solution is implemented. For each use case (e.g., maintenance of a PLC from manufacturer A, maintenance of a database from manufacturer B), a separate, minimal container with the exact required software version is provided. Access to this container is granted 'just-in-time' and the session is fully logged and filtered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the PAM solution and the container technology demonstrated. The function of the command filtering is tested by attempting to execute a forbidden command. The immutability and isolation of the container images are checked.

controls.title: Explicit approval of each OT remote maintenance session (S) [Employees]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Approval is given verbally and is not documented. The remote maintenance access is often permanently open, and the reliance is on the service provider connecting only when needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The service provider calls the plant operator and says, "I'll just take a quick look." The firewall rule for this service provider is permanently active.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews and analysis of firewall rules that access is permanently open and no formal approval process exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A ticket system or email is used for requesting and approving access. The access path is manually activated and deactivated by OT personnel. The 'inside-out' connection model is not implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The service provider sends an email, the OT manager replies with 'OK' and then manually enables a firewall rule. After the work is done, the rule is (hopefully) deactivated again.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews email threads or tickets to understand the approval process. They check the firewall logs to see how long the rules were active and if they were deactivated promptly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every remote maintenance session SHOULD be approved in advance by a responsible OT employee. Only then SHOULD the remote maintenance access be enabled. The explicit approval SHOULD be adhered to both on-demand and during coordinated maintenance windows and should only be valid for a limited period. Furthermore, external remote maintenance access SHOULD exclusively be established from the inside out, i.e., initiated from the OT network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal process is defined: The external service provider requests access via a portal or a ticket system. The responsible OT employee approves the access and then enables it for a defined period. Technically, this is implemented by establishing the connection from the target network to the service provider (e.g., via a reverse tunnel or a web session provided by the service provider).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the defined approval process and the associated tickets or requests. The technical configuration of the access solution is analyzed to ensure that connections can only be established from the inside out. The validity period of the approvals is compared with the technical activation times.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated remote maintenance portal is used. The OT employee can approve a request, which then automatically opens the specific firewall rules for a predefined, limited time. All connections are technically forced to be initiated from the OT network outwards.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A remote support solution is implemented that provides a workflow for requests and approvals. After approval by the OT employee in the portal, the required rule is activated for a defined time (e.g., 2 hours) and for specific IP addresses via an API call to the firewall and is then automatically deactivated again.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the entire workflow in the remote maintenance portal demonstrated, from the request to the automatic deactivation. The logs of the firewall and the portal are cross-referenced to verify correct functionality.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A Privileged Access Management (PAM) system automates the entire workflow. A request triggers an approval workflow. After approval, the PAM system provides passwordless, just-in-time access to the target system for the specified duration. The connection is automatically terminated when the time expires.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The PAM system is integrated with the ticketing system and the identity management system. An approved ticket triggers the provisioning of a temporary account or the release of access in the PAM system. The user authenticates at the PAM portal and receives a direct connection to the target system without ever seeing a password. After the session expires, the account is locked or deleted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the PAM system and its integrations. The entire automated just-in-time access process is demonstrated. It is verified that after the session expires, access is actually and irrevocably terminated.

controls.title: Secure file exchange accompanying OT remote maintenance (S) [Planners, IT Operations]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: File exchange occurs uncontrolled via email attachments or insecure methods like FTP. No virus scan takes place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The service provider sends an update as a ZIP file via email to the OT employee, who then copies it to the target system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor identifies through interviews and analysis of email traffic that no secure processes for file exchange are established.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated network drive is used for file exchange, but the access controls are lax. A check for malicious software is performed manually and inconsistently.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a share '\\fileserver\upload' where all service providers can write. An OT employee is supposed to manually check the files with a virus scanner before further use.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the permissions of the upload directory and finds them to be too broad. There are no logs to prove consistent virus scanning.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For file exchange within the scope of OT remote maintenance, a secure procedure SHOULD be established. This MUST include at least a check for malicious software. The connection establishment between a data exchange system and the file source SHOULD not be automated but should be initiated and authenticated by the institution's OT before each file exchange. File exchange SHOULD generally be logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated server (e.g., an SFTP server) is set up in the DMZ as a 'data airlock'. The external service provider uploads files to this server. An OT employee then manually initiates the transfer from the airlock server to the internal network. During this transfer, the file is automatically checked by a virus scanner. All uploads and downloads are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the architecture and configuration of the data airlock. The file transfer process is demonstrated, including the virus scan. The logs of the file exchange are checked for completeness and correctness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A hardened file transfer server in the DMZ is used. All uploaded files are not only automatically scanned for viruses but also analyzed for suspicious behavior in a sandbox environment before being released to the internal network. The entire process is logged and coupled with an approval workflow.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The data airlock is extended with a sandboxing solution (e.g., Cuckoo Sandbox or a commercial product). An uploaded file is moved to the download area only after a 'green' result from the virus scan and sandbox analysis. The OT employee is informed about the release.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the sandbox environment. A test file with harmless but potentially suspicious macros is uploaded to test the detection and analysis function. The analysis reports from the sandbox are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A data diode or a similar unidirectional transfer mechanism is used for file uploads to the OT network. All files undergo a deep content inspection and cleaning (Content Disarm and Reconstruction - CDR), in addition to sandboxed malware analysis. The process is fully automated, and the logs are correlated in a SIEM system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A CDR solution is placed upstream, which removes active content (e.g., macros, scripts) from files and rebuilds the file from harmless components. Only the sanitized file then undergoes further analysis. This process is transparent to the user. All logs (upload, CDR, sandbox, download) are sent to the SIEM to trace the entire lifecycle of a file.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the CDR solution. A file with an active macro is uploaded to verify that the macro has been removed in the target file, but the file is otherwise intact. The correlated log entry for this process is checked in the SIEM.

controls.title: Observation and control of OT remote maintenance sessions (S) [Employees]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Remote maintenance sessions are not actively monitored. There is complete trust in the competence and good conduct of the external technician. There is no easy way to interrupt an ongoing session.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The service provider connects and works independently. The OT employee is busy with other tasks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews that no monitoring takes place. No process or technical means to interrupt a session can be named.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An OT employee is present on-site at the plant during critical remote maintenance work. However, they are not necessarily able to technically follow all the technician's actions on the screen. There is a way to physically disconnect the connection (e.g., pulling the network plug).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For important updates, the shift supervisor stands next to the machine. However, he cannot interpret the actual commands on the console. His instruction is to pull the plug in case of 'strange noises'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor questions the employees about their monitoring procedures. It is determined that the monitoring is based purely on a duty of presence and no technical tracking of the actions takes place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In an industrial environment, it MUST be ensured that neither people nor plants are endangered by active remote maintenance and that the production process is not impaired. If personal injury or property damage is possible, it MUST be ensured that OT employees can monitor the remote maintenance activities on-site (four-eyes principle). OT employees SHOULD be able to intervene if necessary and interrupt a remote maintenance session.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The technical capability is created for an OT employee to follow the external technician's session live on their own screen (screen sharing, session mirroring). The remote maintenance solution must offer a function that allows the observing employee to terminate the session at any time with a single click. This procedure is made mandatory for all security-critical interventions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the function for monitoring and interrupting the session demonstrated. It is checked whether the work instructions for critical maintenance prescribe the four-eyes principle using session mirroring. Logs of past sessions are reviewed to check who participated as an observer.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All remote maintenance sessions are actively mirrored on the screen of a monitoring OT employee. The employee has the technical capability to take over or terminate the session at any time with a single click. This process is documented, and its execution is logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The remote maintenance or PAM solution used offers a 'Join' and 'Terminate' function for supervisors. The participation of a supervisor is automatically recorded in the session log. The training of employees for this task is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the supervisor functions in the remote maintenance solution. They review session protocols and compare them with the supervisors' schedules. A test session with supervisor participation is conducted.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All remote maintenance sessions are fully recorded (video and keystroke logging). The session is routed through a real-time monitoring system that can automatically flag or terminate the session if potentially dangerous commands are entered or unauthorized actions are attempted. Live monitoring by an employee is additionally performed for particularly critical systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution with integrated session recording and threat analysis is used. Policies are defined that detect and block dangerous commands (e.g., 'reboot', 'rm *') or actions (e.g., access to specific system files) in real time or require supervisor approval (Just-in-Time Approval).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the session monitoring policies in the PAM system. A test session is conducted in which an attempt is made to execute a blocked command to verify the correct functioning of the control. The quality and completeness of the session recordings are checked on a random basis.

controls.title: Centralized management of all accounts for OT remote maintenance (S) [IT Operations]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Shared accounts (e.g., 'maintenance', 'vendor') with static, rarely changed passwords are used on many systems. There is no central account management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Passwords for shared accounts are stored in unsecured Excel lists or text files and passed on when needed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the user accounts on several target systems and discovers the existence of generic, shared accounts. They inquire about the password management process and uncover the insecure storage.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Individual, local accounts are created on the target systems as needed. An attempt is made to manage them via a central list (e.g., a spreadsheet), but there is no central directory service.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A local account is created on the system to be maintained for each external technician. A central Excel spreadsheet is intended to keep track of who has an account where. Deactivating the accounts after the project ends is often forgotten.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the central list with the accounts actually present on the systems and finds discrepancies (e.g., orphaned accounts of former employees of the service provider).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For remote maintenance access in OT, only accounts managed in a central directory service of the OT or the institution SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated directory service (e.g., Active Directory or LDAP) for the OT is established. All systems used for remote maintenance that technically support this are connected to this directory service. Personalized accounts are created for external technicians in this directory, which are deactivated again after use.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of the central OT directory service. It is checked which systems are connected. The lifecycle of an external user account (creation, use, deactivation) in the directory service is traced on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The dedicated OT directory service is used to manage all user and service accounts for remote maintenance. Group policies or equivalent mechanisms are used to centrally enforce password complexity, expiration periods, and other security settings. Regular reviews of accounts and permissions are conducted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the OT-AD, specific organizational units (OUs) and groups are set up for external service providers. Group Policy Objects (GPOs) are used to enforce restrictive settings such as logon hours or the computers allowed for logon. An identity access management process for the regular recertification of accounts is established.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the Group Policy Objects in the OT directory service. They review the logs of the last permission recertification campaign.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central OT directory service is integrated with a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. Users authenticate to the PAM system, which then uses dynamically created one-time credentials or performs a direct, passwordless login to the target system. No user ever knows the actual password of the account on the target system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The PAM system manages the passwords of local administrator accounts or service accounts on the end systems and rotates them automatically after each use. The external technician logs into the PAM web portal with their personal, central account, selects the shared session, and the PAM system logs them into the target system in the background with the privileged account.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the passwordless login process via the PAM system demonstrated. They check the configuration of the password rotation and the secure storage of the credentials (Credential Vault) in the PAM system.

controls.title: Dedicated remote maintenance solution in the OT (H) [Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For remote maintenance in an industrial environment, a dedicated OT remote maintenance solution SHOULD be used that is independent of the office and building IT. All other functions on the IT systems for OT remote maintenance, especially functions for the administration of IT systems and networks outside the OT, SHOULD be deactivated or prevented. If maximum independence is to be realized, a dedicated internet connection for OT remote maintenance SHOULD also be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A separate infrastructure for OT remote maintenance is built. This includes its own VPN gateway and its own jump servers, which are located in an OT-DMZ. These systems are hardened, and all unnecessary services and software are removed. The administration of these systems is the sole responsibility of the OT personnel. Optionally, a separate, physical internet connection is procured just for this purpose.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and the logical/physical separation of the dedicated OT remote maintenance solution based on network diagrams, configurations, and physical inspection. They check the hardening configurations of the systems and the access permissions to ensure independence from office IT.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The OT remote maintenance solution is completely physically separated from the office IT infrastructure. It uses its own hardened jump servers, its own authentication system, and its own firewall. The entire solution is operated as a self-contained, high-availability system.

parts.name: guidance
