parts.prose: Logging is only enabled on a few critical network components. Mainly only error conditions are logged, while login attempts or configuration changes are not recorded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Logging is enabled on the core router to detect interface failures. Logging is disabled on the access switches to avoid affecting performance. The logs remain local on the devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor logs into a sample of network devices and checks with commands like `show logging` whether and what is being logged. It is determined that no uniform configuration exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All events required in the control text are logged on the network components. However, the log data is stored locally on the devices and not centrally consolidated. A correlation of events is therefore not possible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard configuration for all switches and routers ensures that login attempts, configuration changes, and errors are logged. If necessary, however, an administrator must log into each device individually to view the log files.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the standard configuration for network devices for the correct logging settings. It is verified that no central log server is configured, which prevents central analysis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: At a minimum, the following events MUST be logged: unauthorized access or access attempts, network performance or availability fluctuations, errors in automated processes (e.g., during configuration distribution), and limited reachability of network components.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All network components are configured to send their log data in a uniform format (e.g., Syslog) to a central log management server. This server collects the events, stores them, and provides basic search and filter functions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of a representative sample of network components to ensure they point to the central log server. On the log server, it is verified that the logs from the components are arriving and that the event types required in the control text are being captured.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The log data is transmitted in near real-time to the central, hardened log server. Basic correlation rules and alarms are defined to notify operations staff of security-relevant patterns (e.g., repeated failed logins).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The log management server (e.g., Graylog, ELK stack) has a rule that triggers an alarm if more than ten failed login attempts from the same IP address are registered on different network devices within one minute. The server itself is configured according to a hardening standard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the log management system and analyzes the implemented alerting and correlation rules. The configuration of the log server's operating system is checked for compliance with hardening guidelines.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All relevant log data from network management is fed into a SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system. There, an advanced, automated correlation with data from other sources (e.g., servers, clients) takes place to detect complex attacks. The integrity of the log data is cryptographically secured.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Syslog-ng is used on the log aggregators to sign the log messages before forwarding them to the SIEM. A rule is implemented in the SIEM that correlates a configuration change alarm on a switch with an unauthorized login event on the admin PC to detect a possible compromise.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the data flow from the network component to the SIEM. The configuration of log signing and verification is checked. The complex correlation rules implemented in the SIEM that involve network management events are reviewed.

controls.title: Time Synchronization

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only the central network management servers are synchronized with a time server. The managed network components have no or incorrectly configured time synchronization, leading to widely diverging timestamps in the logs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Windows server running the management software synchronizes itself via the standard domain hierarchy. The Cisco and Juniper devices in the network have no NTP configuration, and their system time often deviates by hours or days after a restart.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the system time of the central management server with the time on a sample of network devices (`show clock`). Large discrepancies indicate this maturity level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All network management components and managed devices are configured for time synchronization. However, they use different, potentially unreliable public NTP servers from the internet.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each administrator has entered a different NTP server from an internet search when configuring a device. This leads to slight but noticeable time differences between devices, which complicates the correlation of events.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the NTP configuration (`show ntp status`, `show ntp associations`) on several devices from different manufacturers and finds that different and unauthorized external time sources are being used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All components of the network management, including the integrated network components, MUST use a synchronous time. The time SHOULD be synchronized at each location within the local network using an NTP service. If a separate management network is set up, an NTP instance SHOULD be positioned in this management network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: One or two central, internal NTP servers (Stratum 2 or 3) are established in the network. These synchronize with reliable public sources (e.g., from PTB). All internal components (servers, clients, network devices) are configured exclusively with these internal NTP servers. If a dedicated management network exists, its own NTP server is operated there, which in turn synchronizes with the central NTP servers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of a sample of devices to ensure they point to the defined, internal NTP servers. The status of the central NTP servers is checked to ensure they are correctly synchronized. Commands like `ntpq -p` on the servers and `show ntp status` on the network devices are used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: NTP communication is secured against spoofing attacks through authentication (e.g., symmetric keys in NTPv4). The time synchronization status of all components is actively monitored, and an alarm is triggered in case of deviations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: NTP keys are configured on the NTP servers and clients. The NTP configuration on the network devices is supplemented with `ntp authenticate` and `ntp trusted-key`. The monitoring system regularly checks the NTP status of the devices (e.g., via SNMP) and alerts if a device loses sync or the deviation becomes too large.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of NTP authentication on the servers and a sample of clients. The configuration of the monitoring system is checked to ensure that NTP monitoring and alerting are correctly implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A hierarchical, highly available NTP infrastructure with its own physical time sources (Stratum 1, e.g., GPS or DCF77 receivers) is operated. For securing the communication, the modern standard NTS (Network Time Security) is used across the board.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Two servers at different locations are equipped with GPS receivers and serve as Stratum 1 time sources. These form a high-availability cluster. All clients in the network use NTS for cryptographically secured time synchronization. The NTP configuration is centrally rolled out to all devices via automation (e.g., Ansible) and checked for compliance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the physical time sources and the configuration of the Stratum 1 servers. The configuration of the NTS keys and certificates is checked. The configuration management software is analyzed to verify the automated and compliant distribution of NTP settings.

controls.title: Securing network management communication and access to network management tools

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A mix of secure (SSH) and insecure (Telnet, HTTP) protocols are used for accessing network management tools. Management traffic is not separated from production traffic.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators use SSH to access new routers, but Telnet for older switches. The web interface of some devices is only accessible via HTTP. Access is made directly from the office VLAN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a port scan on a sample of network devices to identify open, insecure management ports (e.g., 23, 80). The network configuration is checked to determine that no segmentation of management traffic exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Management traffic is separated from other data traffic in its own VLAN (in-band management). However, within this VLAN, some insecure protocols are still used. Access from outside is via VPN, but without multi-factor authentication.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A management VLAN (e.g., VLAN 100) is set up, and all management interfaces of the network devices are assigned to this VLAN. Access to this VLAN is restricted to admin workstations. However, Telnet is still active on the devices themselves.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and correct assignment of the management VLAN. However, a port scan within the management VLAN still shows open insecure services. The VPN configuration is checked for the absence of MFA.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If network management communication takes place over the production infrastructure, secure protocols MUST be used. If this is not possible, a dedicated administration network (out-of-band management) MUST be used. If network management tools are accessed from a network outside the management networks, secure authentication and encryption methods MUST be implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: One of the two main options is consistently implemented: Either only secure protocols such as SSHv2, HTTPS (TLS 1.2+), and SNMPv3 are used in the production network (in-band), OR a separate management network (out-of-band) with its own switches is built, in which the traffic is isolated. Any access from outside (e.g., home office) MUST be via a VPN with strong authentication (e.g., certificates or MFA).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the chosen strategy. In the case of in-band management, the device configurations are checked for the exclusive use of secure protocols. In the case of out-of-band management, the physical or logical separation of the networks is checked. The configuration of remote access (VPN) is checked for the use of strong authentication methods.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated out-of-band (OOB) management network is used by default. Access to this network is only possible via a hardened bastion host (jump server), which enforces multi-factor authentication (MFA) and performs detailed session logging.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A physically separate OOB network is implemented. Administrators must first log in to a jump server via SSH with MFA. Only from this server can the actual network components be accessed. The jump server records all keystrokes of the sessions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the network architecture to confirm the OOB implementation. The jump server's configuration is checked for MFA enforcement, hardening, and logging functions. Session logs are spot-checked for completeness and meaningfulness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative access is controlled via a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. The PAM solution enforces hardware-based MFA, automatically manages and rotates the credentials of network devices, and performs video recording and real-time analysis of administrative sessions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution like CyberArk or Thycotic is in use. Administrators authenticate to the PAM solution with a smart card certificate. The PAM solution then establishes the connection to the target device without the administrator knowing the device's password. Anomalous commands during a session can automatically terminate it.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture and configuration of the PAM solution. The configuration of credential rotation, session recording, and threat detection is reviewed. The process for requesting and approving privileged access is audited.

controls.title: Restriction of SNMP communication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: SNMPv1 or SNMPv2c is used with the default community strings "public" and "private". There is no restriction on which systems are allowed to send SNMP requests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: SNMP is enabled on all network devices with default settings, as this is the easiest way to integrate them into the monitoring tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor scans the network with an SNMP scanner (e.g., `snmp-check`) and the default community strings to find devices that respond to these requests. A device's configuration is checked for the use of default strings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: SNMPv1 or SNMPv2c is used with non-default community strings. Access is restricted to the IP address of the central management server using Access Control Lists (ACLs).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On all devices, the community strings are changed to a company-specific value. An ACL on the devices' SNMP configuration allows SNMP packets only from the IP address 192.168.1.10 (the management server).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies on a sample of devices that no default community strings are used. The configuration of the SNMP ACLs is checked to ensure that access is correctly restricted to the authorized management servers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As a general rule, insecure versions of the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) MUST NOT be used in network management. If insecure protocols are nevertheless used and not secured via other secure network protocols (e.g., VPN or TLS), a separate management network MUST be used. As a general rule, SNMP SHOULD only be accessed with the minimum necessary access rights. Access authorization SHOULD be restricted to dedicated management servers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Wherever possible, SNMPv3 is configured with the `authPriv` security level (authentication and encryption). A different user with higher privileges is used for write access than for read access. If a legacy device only supports SNMPv1/v2c, it is moved to a separate, highly isolated management VLAN. SNMP access is restricted to the dedicated management servers via ACL.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the SNMP configuration on a representative sample of devices. It is verified that SNMPv3 `authPriv` is the default. For exceptions, the existence and correct configuration of the separate management network is checked. The configured access rights (read-only vs. read-write) are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of SNMPv3 is mandatory. Strong authentication and encryption algorithms (e.g., SHA-256, AES-128) are used. Using SNMP views, access for different management roles is restricted to the required MIB subtrees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SNMPv3 configuration is standardized to allow only strong algorithms. An SNMP view called "Interface-Monitoring" is created that only allows access to the `ifTable` MIB. A user for performance monitoring is only granted access to this view.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the SNMPv3 configuration for the use of strong crypto algorithms. The configuration of the SNMP views and their assignment to user groups is analyzed to verify the correct implementation of the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of insecure SNMP versions is actively monitored throughout the network and blocked by firewall rules. The SNMPv3 credentials (users, passwords, keys) are rotated regularly and automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The network firewall has a rule that blocks any traffic on port 161/162 that is not SNMPv3-encrypted. An Ansible playbook is run monthly to change the SNMPv3 keys on all devices and store the new configuration in the management tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules that block insecure SNMP. The automation scripts for key rotation are reviewed. It is checked whether the rotation process is successful and traceable.

controls.title: Definition of a security policy for network management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are informal, unwritten rules for network management that are followed by the administrators. There is no formal, adopted policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The team knows that SSH should be used instead of Telnet for new devices. However, this rule is not written down anywhere and its compliance depends on the knowledge of individual employees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: In interviews, the auditor determines that while there is a common understanding of certain security aspects, there is no document that can be described as an official policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a document that is referred to as a security policy for network management. However, it is incomplete, outdated, or not known to the responsible employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a three-year-old policy that prescribes the use of SNMPv1 and does not address modern topics such as out-of-band management or secure protocols. The current administrators are not familiar with the document.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the policy and finds that its content is outdated and does not cover important topics required in the module (e.g., network separation, access control). Interviews confirm that the policy plays no role in practice.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A security policy SHOULD be created and sustainably maintained for network management. The security policy SHOULD be known to all persons involved in network management. It SHOULD be regularly and traceably checked that the content required in the security policy is implemented. The policy SHOULD specify which areas are realized via central tools, which tasks are automated, and make provisions for network separation, access control, logging, and communication protection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal security policy for network management is created, approved by management, and published on the intranet. It contains clear specifications on all points mentioned in the control text. New employees are made aware of the policy as part of their induction. Compliance with the policy is checked as part of internal reviews.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the current, approved security policy for network management. It is checked whether the policy covers the required topics (automation, network separation, access control, etc.) and is known to all relevant employees (e.g., through spot-check interviews). Evidence of the regular review of the implementation is requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is reviewed and updated at least annually or in the event of significant changes to the infrastructure or threat landscape. There is a formal process for reviewing compliance, the results of which are documented and reported to management. The policy defines clear roles and responsibilities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ISMS annual plan includes a fixed item for reviewing the network management policy. The results of the internal audits on policy compliance are summarized in a report and submitted to the CISO. The policy clearly defines who is responsible for configuration, monitoring, and auditing.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the revision history of the policy to understand the annual review process. The audit reports from the last review cycles are requested. The roles defined in the policy are compared with the actual tasks assigned to the employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is fully integrated into the overarching ISMS. Compliance with the policy requirements is continuously monitored with automated tools (compliance scanners). Deviations from the policy lead to automated alarms and are visualized in a central dashboard for management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy requirements (e.g., 'only SSHv2 allowed', 'SNMPv3 authPriv required') are stored in machine-readable form in a compliance tool. This tool continuously scans the configurations of all network devices and immediately reports any deviation to the SIEM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the automated compliance tool and the policy rules stored in it. The tool's reports and dashboards are viewed to assess the effectiveness of the continuous monitoring. The process for handling reported deviations is reviewed.

controls.title: Actual state assessment and documentation of network management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Documentation SHOULD be created that describes how the management infrastructure of the network is structured. It SHOULD contain the initial actual state assessment as well as all changes made in network management. In particular, it SHOULD be documented which network components are managed with which management tools. Furthermore, all relevant IT systems, information assets, and interfaces SHOULD be recorded. The documentation SHOULD be complete and always up-to-date and should be aligned with the documentation of the network infrastructure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Documentation, typically in a wiki or a structured document, is created and maintained. It contains an overview of the management servers, the software used (e.g., Nagios, Zabbix), a list of the managed network components with their management IPs, the protocols used, and the interfaces to other systems such as the ticket system. Changes to the management infrastructure must be recorded in the document.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the management infrastructure and compares it with reality on a random basis. For example, it is checked whether a newly added switch is listed in the documentation and whether the documented interfaces (e.g., to the log server) are correct. The timeliness is assessed by comparing the last modification date with recently made changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation is managed in a central CMDB or a versioned document management system. The process for updating the documentation is formalized and linked to the change management process. The accuracy of the documentation is regularly audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Any change to the management infrastructure requires a change request ticket. A mandatory step in the ticket's workflow is to update the CMDB and the associated documentation. Once a quarter, an internal audit is conducted that compares the CMDB entries with a network scan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the change management process to verify the link to the documentation obligation. The logs of the regular audits of the documentation are inspected. The version history of the documentation is checked to assess the traceability of changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation of the network management infrastructure is largely created and kept up-to-date automatically by network discovery and inventory tools. The data obtained in this way is automatically synchronized with the CMDB, monitoring, and configuration management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A tool like NetBox or a commercial NMS solution scans the network daily, identifies new devices, reads their configuration, and automatically updates the CMDB entries. When a new device is added to monitoring, the corresponding entry in the documentation is automatically generated or updated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and logs of the automatic discovery tools. The synchronization between the discovery tool, CMDB, and monitoring system is checked. It is verified how manually added information is merged with the automatically collected data to ensure consistent documentation.

controls.title: Creation of a network management concept

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the security policy, a network management concept SHOULD be created and maintained sustainably. At a minimum, the following aspects SHOULD be considered as needed: methods, techniques, and tools; securing access and communication; network separation; scope of monitoring and alerting; logging; automation; reporting chains; provision of information for other areas; integration into emergency planning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed concept document is created that builds on the higher-level policy. It specifically describes which tools (e.g., Zabbix for monitoring, Ansible for automation) are used, how the management network is segmented (e.g., VLANs for servers, security, external connection), which parameters are monitored per device type, who is notified for which alarms (reporting chain), and how the logs are delivered to a central system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the network management concept and checks it for completeness based on the points mentioned in the control text. It is verified whether the concept provides a comprehensible and detailed guide for the implementation and operation of network management and is consistent with the security policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The network management concept contains detailed process descriptions for the core tasks of network management (e.g., change, incident, problem management) based on established frameworks such as ITIL. Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are defined to measure the effectiveness and efficiency of network management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concept describes the exact procedure for how a configuration change on a switch is requested, tested, approved, and implemented. As a KPI, for example, the "average time to resolve a critical network outage" is defined and measured regularly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process descriptions and KPIs defined in the concept. It is checked whether the processes are put into practice (e.g., by inspecting change tickets) and whether the KPIs are regularly recorded and evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The network management concept is a living document that is integrated into enterprise architecture management. It includes a roadmap for the future development of network management, which is oriented towards technology trends, the threat landscape, and business requirements. The automation of management tasks is a central component of the concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concept is managed in an EA tool. The roadmap plans for the introduction of Network-as-Code principles next year and the evaluation of AI-based analysis tools the year after. The concept describes in detail which manual activities are to be replaced by automation scripts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the concept in the context of the overarching enterprise architecture management. The existence and plausibility of the roadmap are assessed. The progress in implementing the automation goals is checked based on implemented scripts and processes.

controls.title: Detailed and implementation planning

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A detailed and implementation plan for the network management infrastructure SHOULD be created. All points addressed in the security policy and the network management concept SHOULD be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Based on the concept, a detailed project plan is created. This plan contains specific work packages (e.g., "Installation of the Zabbix server," "Configuration of SNMPv3 on all core switches"), time estimates, and assigned responsibilities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the implementation plan and checks whether it is logically derived from the concept and whether it has the necessary level of detail for a structured implementation. It is checked whether essential points from the concept have been translated into concrete planning items.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The implementation planning is carried out using professional project management methods. The plan includes resource planning, a risk analysis for the project, and a detailed rollback plan in case of problems during implementation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The plan is managed in a project management tool like MS Project or Jira. For the transition to a new monitoring system, the risk "false alarms after transition" is identified, and a multi-week parallel operation is planned as a countermeasure. A detailed plan describes how the old solution can be reactivated in case of an error.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the project plan in the tool used. Particular attention is paid to the existence and quality of the risk analysis and the rollback plan. The status of milestone completion is tracked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The implementation is managed not as a one-time project, but as a continuous improvement process with agile methods (e.g., Scrum, Kanban). The planning is adapted in short cycles to be able to react to new requirements or findings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The network management team works with a Kanban board. The introduction of a new automation script is formulated as a user story and goes through the phases "Backlog," "In Progress," "Testing," and "Done." The prioritization of tasks in the backlog is regularly re-evaluated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the agile framework used and the associated artifacts (e.g., Kanban board, sprint backlogs, burndown charts). It is assessed whether the process enables a flexible yet structured further development of the network management infrastructure.

controls.title: Concept for the secure operation of the network management infrastructure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the security policy and the network management concept, a concept for the secure operation of the network management infrastructure SHOULD be created. The application and system operation for the network management tools SHOULD be considered. It SHOULD also be examined how the services of other operational units can be integrated and controlled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An operations manual is created. This document describes the daily, weekly, and monthly tasks of the administrators. It specifies how patches for the management servers are applied, how new users for the tools are created, and how to respond to failures of the management infrastructure itself. It also defines how the server team is supported in the maintenance of the underlying operating systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the operating concept or operations manual. It is checked whether the essential operating aspects (patching, user management, incident response for the management tools) are regulated therein and whether the interfaces to other teams (e.g., server operations) are clearly defined.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operating concept contains detailed and tested procedures (Standard Operating Procedures, SOPs) for all regular and unforeseen operational activities. The authorizations for operating the management infrastructure are role-based and designed according to the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a step-by-step guide for applying a security patch to the monitoring server, including pre-tests and a rollback plan. There is a "Monitoring Operator" role, which can only view and acknowledge alarms, and a "Monitoring Admin" role, which can also change the configuration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing SOPs and compares them with the activities carried out (e.g., based on change logs). The authorization concept for the management tools is analyzed and checked for the correct implementation of the role concept and the principle of least privilege.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A large part of the activities described in the operating concept is automated. This includes automated patching, automated system hardening, self-healing mechanisms for the management tools, and the automatic enforcement of security configurations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An automation tool like Ansible is used to regularly check the management servers for the desired configuration state and automatically correct deviations (configuration drift). If a service on a management server fails, it is automatically restarted by a watchdog process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and scripts of the automation tools. The logs of the automation runs are checked to assess the effectiveness of the self-healing and configuration management processes. It is verified how the automated processes are monitored.

controls.title: Setup and configuration of network management solutions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Solutions for network management SHOULD be set up, securely configured, and put into operation based on the security policy, the specified requirements, and the detailed and implementation plan. Afterward, the specific processes for network management SHOULD be established.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The installation and configuration of the network management solution follows a documented plan. After technical commissioning, the processes defined in the concept, such as the reporting chain for alarms or the process for adding new devices, are configured in the system and employees are trained on them.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the actual configuration of the management solution with the specifications from the concept and planning documents. It is checked whether the defined processes (e.g., alerting, reporting) are technically implemented and ready for operation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the network management solutions is based on established hardening guides (e.g., from CIS, DISA, or the manufacturer). Before productive commissioning, a formal acceptance test is carried out to check for correct functionality and security.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The operating system of the management server is hardened according to the CIS benchmark. The application itself is configured according to the manufacturer's security best practices (e.g., deactivating insecure cipher suites, configuring access restrictions). The results of the acceptance test are recorded in a protocol.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the system based on a relevant hardening guide. The protocol of the acceptance test is requested and checked for completeness and positive results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire setup and configuration of the network management solution is automated using Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC) tools. This ensures consistent, repeatable, and documented deployments. The security configuration is automatically verified against the policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ansible playbooks or Terraform scripts are used to provision the virtual servers for management, harden the operating system, install the management software, and perform the basic configuration. Every change to the scripts is versioned (e.g., in Git) and goes through a review process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the IaC scripts and the associated version control. The process for changes to the scripts (e.g., pull requests, reviews) is audited. How the automated deployments are monitored and logged is examined.

controls.title: Regular target-actual comparison as part of network management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be checked regularly and traceably to what extent the network management solution corresponds to the target state. It SHOULD be checked whether the existing solution still meets the security policy and requirements specification. It SHOULD also be checked to what extent the implemented management structure and the processes used are up-to-date and whether the management infrastructure is current.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A manual target-actual comparison is performed semi-annually. The current configuration of the management tools and processes is compared with the specifications from the concept and the policy. It is checked whether all devices are managed correctly and whether the software used is still up-to-date. The results are recorded in a report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the reports from the last target-actual comparisons. The methodology of the comparison is evaluated and random checks are performed to see if the identified deviations have been tracked and rectified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The target-actual comparison is carried out at planned intervals (e.g., quarterly). The process is formalized, and the results are documented, evaluated, and incorporated into an action plan to rectify deviations. The process is partially automated by scripts.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script is executed quarterly that reads the configurations of all network devices and compares them with a “Golden Configuration” template. The deviations are output in a report. A ticket is created for each deviation to be rectified.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the formalized process of the target-actual comparison. The scripts and the generated reports are reviewed. The tracking of deviations in the ticket system is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The target-actual comparison is carried out continuously using automated configuration and compliance management tools. Any deviation from the defined target state (configuration drift) is detected and reported in real time. Optionally, an automatic correction can be made.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A configuration management tool such as Ansible or Puppet is used in enforce mode. It ensures that the configuration of the management infrastructure and the managed devices corresponds to the target state defined in code at all times. Any manual change that deviates from the target state is either immediately reverted or a high-priority alarm is triggered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and logs of the configuration management tool. It is checked how deviations are handled (alarming vs. automatic correction). The target configuration defined in code is compared with the specifications from the policy and the concept.

controls.title: Training for management solutions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the network management solutions used, training and education measures SHOULD be designed and implemented. The measures SHOULD cover the individual circumstances in configuration, availability, and capacity management, as well as typical situations in fault management. The training and education SHOULD be repeated regularly, but at least when major technical or organizational changes occur.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A training concept for the network management solutions is created. New employees receive basic training. When a new software version or a new module is introduced, specific training is provided for the affected personnel. Participation in the training courses is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the training concept and evidence of completed training courses (e.g., attendance lists). It is checked whether the training content covers the relevant aspects of network management and whether training courses are held on an ad-hoc basis (e.g., for updates).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a formal, annual training plan that provides for different training modules tailored to the respective role (e.g., for operators, administrators, architects). The success of the training measures is evaluated by subsequent knowledge tests or practical exercises.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The training plan includes an “Operator Course” that deals with handling alarms, and an “Admin Course” that teaches system configuration. After each course, there is a short online test. The results are used to improve the training content.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the annual training plan and the various training materials. Evidence of the performance reviews carried out (e.g., anonymized test results) is requested. It is checked whether the training courses are role-specific.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training sessions include practical exercises in a dedicated laboratory environment where typical fault and attack scenarios are simulated. A continuous learning platform (e.g., with e-learning modules, videos, knowledge base) is available to employees to keep their knowledge up-to-date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Once a quarter, a “Game Day” takes place in which a network failure is simulated in a test environment and the team has to analyze and resolve it using the management tools. The intranet has a section with short video tutorials on specific functions of the management software.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the laboratory environment and the scenarios for the practical exercises demonstrated. The content and use of the learning platform are analyzed. The extent to which the training measures go beyond pure knowledge transfer and promote practical skills is assessed.

controls.title: Decoupling of network management communication

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Direct management access by administrators from an IT system outside the management networks to a network component SHOULD be avoided. If such access is necessary without a central management tool, the communication SHOULD be decoupled. Such jump servers SHOULD be integrated into the management network and positioned in a separate access segment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated jump server is set up for administrative access. Administrators first connect to this server and from there initiate the connection to the actual network devices. The jump server itself is located in a specially secured network segment (DMZ) that strictly controls access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network architecture and firewall rules to verify the correct placement and securing of the jump server. It is checked whether all administrative access is routed through this jump server and direct access from the admin workstations to the network devices is prevented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The jump server is hardened, enforces multi-factor authentication (MFA) for all logins, and performs detailed logging of all sessions and commands entered. Direct access to the target systems is blocked at the network level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: To log in to the jump server, a password and a one-time password (TOTP) are required. The server is hardened according to CIS benchmarks. All SSH sessions are recorded using `script` or `ttyrec` and the log files are sent to the central log server. Firewall rules allow SSH access to the network devices only from the IP address of the jump server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the jump server for MFA enforcement, hardening, and session logging. The firewall rules are analyzed to ensure that they effectively block direct access. Session recordings are randomly checked for completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The jump server is part of a comprehensive Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. This solution centrally manages credentials, rotates them automatically, records sessions as video, and can analyze and terminate sessions in real time in case of suspicious activities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A PAM solution is used. Administrators no longer know the passwords of the target systems. The PAM solution establishes the connection and injects the credentials. The sessions are recorded and an AI-based analysis checks for anomalous commands. If a critical command (e.g., `reload`) is detected, the session is automatically terminated and an alarm is triggered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration of the PAM solution, in particular the credential management, session recording, and the rules for real-time analysis. The process for accessing privileged sessions is checked. The logs of terminated sessions are analyzed.

controls.title: Restriction of management functions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ONLY the required management functions SHOULD be activated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the commissioning of a network device, its configuration is reviewed and all services and functions not explicitly required for operation or management are deactivated. This includes, for example, unused protocols, test and diagnostic functions, or outdated web interfaces.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of a sample of network devices. It is checked which services and functions are active and whether an operational necessity can be plausibly demonstrated for each activated function. Commands like `show running-config` and `show ip services` are used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Configuration templates (“Golden Templates”) are used, which, according to the “Default Deny” principle, only activate the explicitly permitted and required management functions. Any deviation from this template is detected and reported by a configuration management tool.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each device type (e.g., access switch, core router), there is a basic configuration in which all unnecessary services such as CDP/LLDP on user ports, HTTP server, etc. are explicitly deactivated. a nightly job compares the running configuration of all devices with these templates and reports deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration templates and compares them with hardening recommendations. The reports of the configuration management tool are analyzed to evaluate the effectiveness of the monitoring for deviations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automated system continuously scans all devices for active services and functions. Any function that is not on a centrally maintained whitelist for the respective device type and the role of the device is automatically deactivated and an alarm is triggered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) is operated in "enforce" mode. It ensures that the device configuration corresponds to the desired state at all times. If an administrator manually activates an unapproved service, it is automatically deactivated again during the next run of the tool (e.g., every 30 minutes).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the automation tool, especially the whitelists of permitted functions and the "enforce" mode. The tool's logs are reviewed to determine how often and which unauthorized changes were detected and corrected.

controls.title: Centralized configuration management for network components

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Software or firmware and configuration data for network components SHOULD be able to be automatically distributed over the network and installed and activated without interrupting operations. The information required for this SHOULD be securely available at a central location and integrated into version control and data backup. The central configuration management SHOULD be sustainably maintained and regularly audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central system (e.g., an NMS or a TFTP/SCP server in conjunction with scripts) is used to distribute new firmware versions and configuration changes to the network devices. The configuration files are stored in a versioned repository (e.g., Git, Subversion) before being distributed. The entire inventory of configurations and firmware images is regularly backed up.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the process for distributing configuration and firmware updates demonstrated. The versioned repository for configurations is inspected and it is checked whether the versions there match the backed-up data. The traceability of changes through version control is assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration management system uses a template-based approach to generate configurations from a central data source (source of truth). All changes are tested in a lab environment before distribution. There are automated rollback procedures for failed updates.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Jinja2 templates are used to generate the complete configuration for a device from variables (e.g., hostname, IP address from a CMDB). Before a large-scale firmware update, it is first installed on devices in a test environment. If an update attempt in the production network fails, the automation script automatically tries to restore the previous configuration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration templates used and the connection to the central data source. Logs of tests in the lab environment and of (successful or failed) rollbacks are inspected. The reliability of the process is assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire configuration lifecycle is managed according to a GitOps workflow. Configuration changes are treated as code and go through a formal review and approval process (e.g., pull requests). Distribution is fully automated after approval. The system continuously enforces the state defined in Git on the devices.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator proposes a configuration change by creating a pull request in GitLab. This is automatically checked for syntax errors (linting). Another administrator must review and approve the change. After approval, the change is automatically merged and a CI/CD pipeline job (e.g., with Ansible) rolls out the change to the affected devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the GitOps process, including the configuration of the CI/CD pipeline, the branching strategy, and the review process in Git. The history of pull requests is analyzed to verify compliance with the four-eyes principle and the testing procedures.

controls.title: Status monitoring of network components

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The basic performance and availability parameters of the central network components SHOULD be continuously monitored. For this purpose, the respective threshold values SHOULD be determined in advance (baselining).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A monitoring system (e.g., Zabbix, Nagios, PRTG) is used to continuously query parameters such as CPU utilization, memory usage, interface status, and bandwidth utilization of the network components via SNMP. Before activating alerts, the normal operating values are determined over a period of several weeks (baselining) to set meaningful thresholds (e.g., alert at >80% CPU load for more than 5 minutes).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the monitoring system demonstrated. It is checked whether the essential performance and availability parameters for critical network components are being monitored. The documentation of the baselining process and the derivation of the defined thresholds is requested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The monitoring also includes advanced metrics for quality of service such as latency, jitter, and packet loss (e.g., using IP SLA). The collected historical performance data is used for proactive trend analysis and capacity planning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cisco IP SLA or comparable mechanisms are configured on core routers to continuously measure the round-trip time to important servers. The monitoring system stores the performance data over long periods (e.g., > 1 year) and can create graphs that show the growth of bandwidth usage on a WAN link in order to plan an expansion in a timely manner.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the advanced monitoring mechanisms (e.g., IP SLA). Reports and graphs from the capacity and trend analysis are requested to assess whether the data is being used proactively.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An AIOps platform is used to correlate the collected metrics from various sources, to automatically detect anomalies in network behavior (Anomaly Detection), to predict future bottlenecks or failures (Predictive Analytics), and to support root cause analysis (Root Cause Analysis).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The monitoring data is fed into an AIOps solution along with log data and application metrics. This learns the normal behavior of the network and alerts on significant deviations, even if no fixed threshold has been exceeded. In the event of a malfunction, the system automatically suggests a probable cause, e.g., "Latency anomaly correlates with high CPU load on switch X and configuration change Y".

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the AIOps platform demonstrated. The configuration of the data sources and the analysis models is analyzed. The effectiveness of the automatic anomaly detection and root cause analysis is assessed using examples of past incidents.

controls.title: Alerting and Logging

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Important events on network components and on the network management tools SHOULD be automatically transmitted to and logged in a central management system. The responsible personnel SHOULD also be automatically notified. The alerting and logging SHOULD include at least the following points: failure or unavailability of components, hardware malfunctions, failed login attempts, and critical states or overload of IT systems. Alert messages SHOULD be transmitted immediately, logging data continuously or in batches.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The central monitoring system is configured to send a notification to a defined email distribution list or a chat tool of the network team when one of the specified events is detected (e.g., failure of a switch, three failed SSH logins). All alerts are also logged in the system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the alerting rules in the monitoring system. It is checked whether all required event types are covered and whether the notification is sent to the correct recipients. An alert is triggered on a test basis to verify the functionality of the notification chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A detailed alerting matrix is defined, which specifies different notification channels (e.g., email, SMS, phone call) and recipient groups (e.g., on-call service) for different event types and criticalities. The system can suppress irrelevant follow-up messages in the event of major outages (Dependency-based Alerting).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The alerting matrix specifies: "Critical error (e.g., core router down) -> SMS to on-call service", "Warning (e.g., CPU load > 80%) -> Email to team mailbox". If a core router fails, the alerts about the unavailability of the access switches behind it are automatically suppressed to avoid an alert flood.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the alerting matrix and compares it with the configuration in the monitoring system. The implementation of the dependencies and the suppression rules is analyzed. It is checked whether the on-call schedules match the configured notification paths.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The alerting system is fully integrated into an incident management system (e.g., a ticketing system) and a SOAR platform (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response). Critical alerts lead to the automatic creation of incidents. Security-related alerts can trigger automated responses.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An alert about the failure of a WAN link automatically creates an incident ticket in ServiceNow and assigns it to the correct group. A security alert from the SIEM about a suspicious connection from an internal IP can automatically send a command to the firewall via a SOAR solution to temporarily block this IP.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the interface configuration between the monitoring, incident management, and SOAR systems. The workflow from alert detection to ticket creation or automated response is traced. The configuration of the automated playbooks in the SOAR platform is audited.

controls.title: Integration of network management into emergency planning

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The network management solutions SHOULD be integrated into the institution's emergency planning. For this purpose, the network management tools and the configurations of the network components SHOULD be backed up and integrated into the recovery plans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution's central emergency manual contains a chapter dedicated to network recovery. This chapter refers to the backed-up configurations of the network devices and describes the steps to restore the central network management software (monitoring, logging) on a replacement system. The backups (see A6) are the basis for this.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the emergency manual and checks whether network management and its components are taken into account. It is checked whether the described recovery plans are consistent with the actually existing backups.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The recovery of the network management infrastructure is regularly tested in practice (e.g., annually) as part of the general emergency drills. The lessons learned from the tests are used to improve the recovery plans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: During the annual emergency drill, one scenario is the recovery of the central monitoring system in a test environment. The team must restore the system from backup according to the instructions in the recovery plan. The time required and any problems encountered are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the logs and evaluations of the last emergency drills that concerned network management. It is checked whether the drills take place regularly and whether the results have led to an update of the plans.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A standby system exists for the critical parts of the network management infrastructure in a separate (fire) section or location (hot/warm site). The failover process is largely automated and is tested regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The database of the central management system is continuously replicated to a server in a second data center. In an emergency, it is possible to switch to this system with a few scripted steps. This switchover process is tested semi-annually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture of the standby solution and the configuration of the replication. The automation scripts for the failover process are checked. The logs of the regular failover tests are reviewed to verify the Recovery Time Objective (RTO).

controls.title: Placement of management clients for in-band management

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dedicated management clients SHOULD be used for the administration of both internal and external IT systems. For this purpose, at least one management client SHOULD be placed in the external network area (for the administration of IT systems adjacent to the internet) and another in the internal area (for the administration of internal IT systems).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Two dedicated admin workstations (or VMs) are set up. One is located in the DMZ to manage the systems there (e.g., web servers, firewalls). The second is located in a secured internal management VLAN to manage the internal servers and switches. Administrators use the appropriate client depending on the task, typically via RDP.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network architecture and the firewall rules to verify the placement of and access paths to the dedicated management clients. It is checked whether the separation between the administration of external and internal systems is maintained.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The dedicated management clients are hardened systems (Privileged Access Workstations, PAWs). Only the software necessary for administration is installed on them, and internet access is severely restricted or blocked. Access to the PAWs requires multi-factor authentication.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The PAWs are virtual machines that are cloned from a hardened template. They have no browsers or email clients. Outgoing network traffic is restricted to the management ports of the target systems. A smart card certificate is required for RDP login to the PAW.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of a PAW to verify the hardening, the installed software, and the network restrictions. The login process is checked for the enforcement of MFA.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The Privileged Access Workstations are non-persistent (stateless). After each administrative session, the PAW is reset to a clean, known initial state. All activities on the PAW are centrally logged and monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The PAWs are operated in a VDI environment that is configured to delete the VM after the user logs off and recreate it from a 'golden image' template. System and application logs from the PAW are sent to a central syslog server before the VM is destroyed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the VDI environment to verify the non-persistent operation of the PAWs. The process of log collection before the destruction of the VM is audited. The centrally collected logs of the PAW sessions are checked for completeness.

controls.title: Use of VLANs in the management network

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If management networks are separated by VLANs, it SHOULD be ensured that the external packet filter and the devices connected to it are in their own subnet. In addition, it SHOULD be ensured that the ALG is not bypassed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The management VLAN is further subdivided. For example, there is a separate VLAN for managing the internet firewall and the DMZ systems. Communication between the management VLANs is regulated by a central firewall. Application Layer Gateways (ALGs), which could potentially create insecure dynamic port openings, are deactivated on the firewall for management traffic.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the VLAN structure and the firewall rules between the management VLANs. In particular, the configuration of the internet firewall is checked to ensure that its management interface is in a dedicated, isolated VLAN. The global and interface-specific configuration of the firewall is examined for active, potentially dangerous ALGs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall rules between the management VLANs are configured according to the default-deny principle and only allow explicitly necessary communication. Measures against VLAN hopping attacks are implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall rule base contains an explicit 'Deny All' rule at the end. Only specific connections, e.g., from the central monitoring server to the SNMP port of the devices in the firewall management VLAN, are allowed. On all switch ports, the unused VLAN 1 is removed from the trunk and the native VLAN is set to an unused ID to make VLAN hopping more difficult.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the complete rule base of the firewall that separates the management VLANs. The configuration of the switch ports (trunks and access ports) is checked for measures against VLAN hopping, e.g., with `show interface trunk`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Micro-segmentation is used within the management VLANs to further restrict communication between the management interfaces. This is achieved through technologies such as Private VLANs (PVLAN) or a distributed firewall based on VXLAN.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The VLAN for server management is configured as a Private VLAN. All management interfaces of the servers are connected to 'isolated' ports. This means the servers can only communicate with the 'promiscuous' port (e.g., the gateway or the management server), but not with each other. This prevents the spread of an attack should a server be compromised.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the micro-segmentation solution (e.g., PVLAN configuration on the switches, policies of the distributed firewall). It is verified through targeted connection tests (e.g., ping between two servers in the same management VLAN) that the unwanted communication is effectively prevented.

controls.title: High-availability implementation of the management solution

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A concept has been created for the high-availability implementation of the central management solutions. The concept describes how servers, tools, and network connections are to be made redundant.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A concept document describes that the central monitoring server is to be implemented as an active/passive cluster and that the database must be located on shared storage. It is also planned that the servers will be connected via two different switches.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the concept for high availability and assesses whether the planned measures are suitable for increasing the availability of the management solution. It is checked whether all critical components have been considered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Central management solutions SHOULD be operated with high availability. For this, the servers or tools, including the network connections, SHOULD be designed to be redundant. The individual components SHOULD also be provided with high availability. The failover process is automated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The central monitoring server and the log server are implemented as an active/passive cluster with a cluster manager (e.g., Pacemaker, Windows Failover Clustering). If the active node fails, the cluster manager automatically switches the services and the virtual IP address to the passive node. The servers are each connected to two different switches (NIC teaming).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the cluster manager and the redundant network connection. Logs of past failover events (planned or unplanned) are reviewed. Optionally, a planned failover is performed as part of the audit to verify the function.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management solution is geographically redundant across two or more locations. The failover process between the locations is fully automated and is tested regularly. This ensures the function of the network management even in the event of a complete failure of a data center.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A complete stack of the management solution runs in each of two data centers. The data (e.g., monitoring configuration, log data) is replicated in real-time between the locations. A Global Server Load Balancing (GSLB) or DNS-based failover system automatically redirects requests and incoming data streams to the remaining location in the event of a failure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the cross-site architecture, the configuration of the data replication, and the automatic failover mechanism. The logs of the regular tests of the cross-site failover are reviewed to verify RTO (Recovery Time Objective) and RPO (Recovery Point Objective).

controls.title: Fundamental use of secure protocols

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It is stipulated in a policy that secure protocols must be used for network management as a matter of principle. The implementation is checked as part of manual reviews.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT security policy contains a clause that prescribes the use of SSH, HTTPS, and SNMPv3 for management and prohibits Telnet, HTTP, and SNMPv1/v2c. Compliance with this requirement is manually checked when commissioning new devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the policy and compares it with the configuration of a sample of devices. It is checked whether the requirements of the policy are known and implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only secure protocols SHOULD be used for network management. All security features of these protocols SHOULD be used. The configurations of the protocols use strong, current cryptographic algorithms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The use of insecure protocols for management is technically prevented wherever possible. For SSH, only secure key exchange algorithms and ciphers are allowed. For TLS, only versions 1.2 and 1.3 with strong cipher suites are permitted. For SNMPv3, `authPriv` with AES encryption is enforced. The configuration is distributed via central templates.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration templates for network devices. Tools such as `sslscan` or `nmap` with appropriate scripts are used to check the configuration of the protocols on the devices for the use of strong algorithms and the absence of vulnerabilities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The use of insecure management protocols and weak cryptographic algorithms is actively blocked at the network level by a firewall or an Intrusion Prevention System (IPS). The conformity of the configurations is continuously monitored by automated tools.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A firewall between the management clients and the target devices has rules that explicitly only allow SSH and TLS traffic with strong ciphers and block all Telnet or HTTP traffic on management ports. A compliance scanner checks the configuration of all devices daily and alerts on any deviation from the secure baseline configuration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall or IPS rules that block insecure traffic. The configuration and reports of the compliance scanner are reviewed to verify the continuous monitoring of protocol security.

controls.title: Physical separation of the management network

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management network is logically separated from the production networks by VLANs. The separation is enforced by ACLs or firewall rules.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A separate VLAN is configured for all management traffic. An Access Control List (ACL) on the core switch or a rule on an internal firewall restricts traffic between the management VLAN and other VLANs to the bare essentials.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the VLAN architecture and the configured ACLs or firewall rules to verify the logical separation and its enforcement.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The management network SHOULD be physically separated from the production networks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Dedicated, separate switches and cabling are used for the management network (out-of-band network). There is no direct physical connection between the switches of the management network and the switches of the production network. Any necessary data exchange takes place via a firewall that connects both networks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the physical cabling and the network devices in the racks. It is checked whether dedicated hardware is used for the management network and whether the separation is consistently implemented. The configuration of the connecting firewall is audited.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The physical separation between the management and production network is complete and implemented as an "air gap" wherever possible. Necessary data transfers (e.g., log data) are carried out exclusively via highly secure gateways such as data diodes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The management network is completely self-sufficient and has no routed connection to the production network. To send log data from the management network to the central SIEM in the production network, a data diode is used. This physically allows data to flow in only one direction, thus preventing any attack attempt from the production network on the management network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the physical separation by inspecting the network diagrams and infrastructure. The implementation and configuration of the data diode or other highly secure gateways is analyzed. Penetration tests are conducted to attempt to bypass the separation.

controls.title: Physical separation of management segments

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Within the (logically separated) management network, different zones are separated from each other by VLANs and firewall rules (e.g., a zone for LAN components, one for security components).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The management VLAN is subdivided into sub-VLANs: VLAN 101 for internal switches, VLAN 102 for firewalls and security systems, VLAN 103 for servers. A firewall strictly controls the traffic between these VLANs.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the VLAN structure within the management network and the firewall rules that control traffic between these zones.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Physically separate zones SHOULD be established at least for the management of LAN components, security components, and components for external connectivity.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Within the physically separated out-of-band network, separate switches are used for different zones. There is a switch stack for managing the internal LAN infrastructure, a separate, highly secured switch for managing the firewalls, and another for managing the routers and systems in the DMZ. These zones are only connected to each other via a dedicated management firewall.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the physical infrastructure of the management network to verify the separation of zones by dedicated hardware. The cabling plans and the configuration of the management firewall are audited to confirm the consistent implementation of zone separation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to each physically separated management zone is controlled by its own dedicated bastion host or PAM gateway instance. Data traffic between the zones is inspected by a highly secure firewall with intrusion prevention.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: To manage the firewalls, an administrator must authenticate to a specific bastion host for the security zone. To manage the LAN switches, to another one. A next-generation firewall with IPS functionality inspects all traffic flowing between these management zones and blocks suspicious activity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the configuration of the dedicated bastion hosts for each zone as well as the configuration of the management firewall including the IPS signatures. It is checked whether a compromise of one zone (e.g., LAN management) would allow access to a more privileged zone (e.g., security management).

controls.title: Provisions for securing evidence

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Policies and procedures are defined for the long-term archiving of log data to meet compliance requirements. The data is stored in a way that protects it from unauthorized modification.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After a retention period on the central log server (e.g., 90 days), log data is moved to a separate archive system. Access to the archive is highly restricted. The archived files are protected with restrictive file permissions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the archiving policy and the configuration of the archiving process. The access permissions on the archive system are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The collected logging data SHOULD be archived in a legally compliant and audit-proof manner for forensic analysis. This is achieved by using WORM (Write Once, Read Many) storage media and ensuring a tamper-proof chain of custody.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The log data is archived on a WORM-capable storage system or in a cloud storage solution with object lock enabled. Each archived log file is given a cryptographic hash, which is stored separately and securely to prove its integrity. The process of archiving and access is meticulously logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the WORM storage. The process for creating, storing, and verifying the hashes is audited. The logs of access to the archive are examined for unauthorized activities.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire log pipeline, from collection and transmission to archiving, is designed according to forensic best practices. The integrity and authenticity of the log data is ensured by digital signatures and qualified timestamps. The process is certified by an external third party (e.g., public accountant).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each log message is already signed on the collecting log aggregator with a private key and provided with a timestamp from a trusted timestamping service before it is forwarded to the central system.
