The security policy SHOULD describe understandable requirements and specifications on how to operate routers and switches securely. The policy SHOULD be known to all administrators and be fundamental to their work.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal document 'Security Policy for Network Components' is created, approved, and published. It defines binding rules for topics such as hardening, logging, access control, patch management, and the use of protocols. The policy is presented to all network administrators as part of a training session.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the specific security policy for routers and switches and checks its content for completeness and comprehensibility. Interviews with the administrators are conducted to determine whether they know the policy and use it as a basis for their work.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If the policy is changed or if there are deviations from the specified requirements, this SHOULD be coordinated with the Information Security Officer and documented. It SHOULD be checked regularly whether the policy is still being implemented correctly. The results SHOULD be documented appropriately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review process for the policy is established. Deviations from the policy must be approved and documented via a formal exception request (exception handling). The implementation of the policy is checked through regular internal audits or configuration reviews.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the last policy reviews and the documentation of approved exceptions. The reports of the internal audits on the implementation of the policy are analyzed and their results evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The rules defined in the security policy are translated into machine-readable configuration and compliance checks. Compliance with the policy is continuously and automatically checked against the live configurations of all routers and switches. Deviations lead to automatic alerts or are prevented as part of a GitOps workflow.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy requirements are mapped in a compliance tool (e.g., Ansible with compliance roles, Batfish) or an NCM tool with a compliance module. Every configuration change that is deployed via the automation pipeline is validated against these rules before deployment. A daily scan checks all devices for conformity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the implemented compliance rules in the automation tool and compares them with the security policy. The compliance dashboards and reports are evaluated. A non-compliant change is checked into a test branch of a configuration repository to check whether the CI/CD pipeline correctly prevents the rollout.

controls.title: Procurement of a router or switch (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before routers or switches are procured, a requirements list SHOULD be created based on the security policy, against which the products available on the market are evaluated. The basis for procurement SHOULD therefore be the requirements from the security policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal procurement process is established. Part of this process is a requirements catalog that, in addition to functional criteria (number of ports, speed), also contains mandatory security requirements from the policy (e.g., 'Must support SSHv2', 'Must support Syslog over TLS').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the procurement documents for recently acquired network components. It is checked whether a documented requirements catalog exists and whether it takes into account the relevant security requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be ensured that the security level targeted by the institution can be achieved with the devices to be procured. The evaluation of the products also includes an analysis of the manufacturer's security track record, such as the average time to provide security patches.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the market analysis, not only the data sheets of the products are evaluated, but also the security advisory pages of the manufacturers (e.g. Cisco PSIRT). A list of preferred manufacturers known for their good security practices is maintained.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the product selection process and asks those responsible how the manufacturers' security practices are incorporated into the decision. It is checked whether there are documented analyses or justifications for the selection of a particular manufacturer.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before a purchase decision is made for a new product line, the favored devices are tested in a lab environment. The implementation of the security functions and the stability under load are verified. For strategically important components, products with a formal security certification (e.g., according to Common Criteria) are preferred.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated test lab is set up. Test plans are created to validate the security functions defined in the requirements list. The results of the lab tests are a major factor in the purchase decision. The requirement for a CC certification is included in the tender documents.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the test plans and result reports from the lab tests. It is checked whether the test procedures are suitable for verifying the security requirements. It is checked whether the procured products actually have the certifications required in the tender.

controls.title: Creation of a configuration checklist for routers and switches (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A configuration checklist SHOULD be created, which can be used to check the most important security-relevant settings on routers and switches.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: One or more hardening checklists (e.g., as a Word or Excel document) are created based on the security policy and vendor best practices. This checklist is processed and checked off during the commissioning of each new device.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the configuration checklist(s). It is checked whether the checklist covers all essential security aspects (access, logging, hardening, etc.). Based on the commissioning records, it is verified whether the checklist is actually used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Since the secure configuration depends heavily on the intended use, the different requirements of the devices SHOULD be taken into account in the configuration checklist. There are specific checklists or configuration templates for different device classes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Separate checklists or sections are created for different roles, e.g., 'Edge Router', 'Core Switch', 'Access Switch', 'DMZ Switch'. A checklist for an access switch, for example, would contain detailed points on port security, which are less relevant for a core switch.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the checklists for the different device classes and assesses whether the differentiation is meaningful. The configuration of an access switch is compared with the checklist provided for it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration checklist exists in the form of an automated compliance script. This script can read the configuration of a device and automatically compare it with the specifications. The result is a detailed compliance report that shows deviations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script (e.g., Python with Nornir/NAPALM, Ansible with appropriate roles) is developed that logs into the devices, reads relevant configuration sections, and validates them against a 'Golden Configuration' template. The script is run regularly and the reports are stored centrally.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the source code of the compliance script and the configuration templates used. It is demonstrated live how the script is run on a device. The auditor manually introduces a non-compliant change and checks whether the script correctly detects and reports it on the next run. An automated audit can run the script with `ansible-playbook compliance_check.yml --limit <test-device>`.

controls.title: Administration via a separate management network (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers and switches SHOULD be administered exclusively via a separate management network (out-of-band management). The available security mechanisms of the management protocols used for authentication, integrity protection, and encryption SHOULD be activated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A dedicated management VLAN is set up throughout the network. Each network device receives an IP address in this VLAN, which is used exclusively for administration. Access to this VLAN is heavily restricted by ACLs. Only secure protocols such as SSHv2 and HTTPS are allowed for administration on the devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network configuration to verify the existence and correct segmentation of the management VLAN. It is checked whether the ACLs effectively restrict access to the management VLAN. Port scans are performed on the management IPs of the devices to ensure that only encrypted administration services are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Any existing administration interface via the actual data network (in-band) SHOULD be deactivated. All insecure management protocols SHOULD be deactivated. The out-of-band network is not only logically (VLAN) but also physically separated from the production networks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A completely separate physical infrastructure with its own switches is set up for management. The management ports of the production devices are connected exclusively to this OOB network. In-band management is prevented by removing the IP address from production SVIs or by strict ACLs that block all management access. Protocols such as Telnet, SNMPv1/v2c, or HTTP are completely uninstalled or deactivated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a physical inspection of the cabling in the data center to verify the physical separation of the OOB network. An attempt is made to access the management interface of a device via a production VLAN. The configuration is inspected for remnants of insecure protocols.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative traffic in the out-of-band network is additionally protected by end-to-end encryption at the transport layer, for example, by implementing MACsec (IEEE 802.1AE). Access to the OOB network is only possible from dedicated, hardened bastion hosts that require MFA.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: MACsec is configured on all switches in the OOB network to encrypt and authenticate all data traffic at Layer 2. This prevents attacks such as ARP spoofing within the management network. The only permitted access to the OOB network is via a PAM gateway, which is the only host allowed to communicate through the OOB firewall.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the MACsec configuration on the OOB switches. The firewall rules governing access to the OOB network are analyzed to ensure that only the bastion host is permitted. The auditor attempts to access the OOB network from an unauthorized system. A `show macsec summary` command can display the status of the MACsec connections.

controls.title: Protection against misuse of ICMP messages (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The ICMP and ICMPv6 protocols SHOULD be restrictively filtered. At the network boundaries, ACLs are used to permit only the strictly necessary ICMP types and to discard all others.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An ACL is created on the edge router that typically allows ICMP Echo-Reply, Echo-Request, Time-Exceeded, and Destination Unreachable (with sub-types for Path MTU Discovery). All other ICMP types such as Redirect, Router Advertisement (incoming), or Mask Request are explicitly blocked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the ACLs applied to the border routers and assesses the list of permitted and blocked ICMP types. Using a tool like `hping3`, an attempt is made to send disallowed ICMP messages from externally into the network to test the filter's effectiveness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ICMP filtering is supplemented by rate limiting to mitigate ICMP-based flooding attacks. This applies in particular to permitted but potentially abusable types such as Echo-Request.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'Control Plane Policing' (CoPP) policy is configured on the router, which limits the rate of ICMP packets directed to the router's CPU itself. Alternatively, a Quality of Service (QoS) policy is applied to the external interface, which throttles ICMP traffic to a reasonable bandwidth.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration for rate limiting mechanisms (CoPP, QoS). Using a tool like `hping3 --flood`, an ICMP flood is simulated against a router IP to observe whether the rate limiting takes effect and the router's CPU load remains stable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An IPS/IDS system analyzes ICMP traffic for anomalous patterns that indicate covert channels or tunneling attempts (e.g., ICMP tunnel). Such connections are detected and blocked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In a next-generation firewall or a dedicated IPS system, signatures and behavioral analysis rules are activated that specialize in the misuse of ICMP for data exfiltration or for C2 communication. The payload of ICMP packets is inspected for unusual content.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the IPS configuration for activated ICMP tunneling signatures. As part of a penetration test, an attempt is made to establish a covert channel via ICMP using a tool like `ptunnel` or `icmpsh` and to check whether it is detected and blocked by the IPS.

controls.title: Bogon and spoofing filtering (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be prevented that attackers can penetrate routers and switches using forged, reserved, or not-yet-assigned IP addresses. This is implemented through ingress and egress filtering at the network perimeter.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An ingress ACL is configured on the external interface of the border router, which discards packets with private (RFC 1918) or other non-routable source IP addresses ('bogons'). On the internal interface, an egress ACL is configured to ensure that only packets with source IP addresses from one's own assigned network block can leave the network. Additionally, Unicast Reverse Path Forwarding (uRPF) is used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the ACLs at the network boundaries and the uRPF configuration (`ip verify unicast source reachable-via rx`). It is checked whether the bogon lists are up to date. Using a packet generator, an attempt is made to send packets with spoofed source IPs from outside and inside to test the filter effectiveness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The bogon filter lists are updated automatically and at regular intervals (e.g., daily) from trusted sources to also correctly handle newly assigned or returned IP address ranges.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script is implemented that regularly downloads bogon lists (e.g., from Team Cymru), converts them into the router's ACL format, and updates the ACL on the router. This process is monitored to detect update errors.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the automation script and the sources of the bogon lists. It is checked when the last update took place and whether the process functions reliably. The logs of the update script are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Spoofing filtering is implemented not only at the perimeter, but also at internal network boundaries between different security zones or VLANs to prevent the spread of attacks within the network. The implementation of BCP38 / BCP84 (Ingress Filtering) is consistently enforced throughout the network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On the Layer 3 interfaces (SVIs) of distribution switches, ACLs are applied that ensure that only packets with the source IP addresses intended for this VLAN originate from a specific VLAN. uRPF is operated in 'strict mode' wherever possible, also in the internal network.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configurations of the internal L3 switches for anti-spoofing mechanisms. As part of an internal penetration test, an attempt is made to send packets from one VLAN with a source IP of another VLAN to test the effectiveness of the internal segmentation filters.

controls.title: Protection against 'IPv6 Routing Header Type 0' attacks (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When using IPv6, mechanisms SHOULD be used that detect and prevent attacks on the Routing Header Type 0. On the border router, the receipt of packets with this outdated and dangerous header type is blocked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An IPv6 ACL is configured on the border router that explicitly discards packets with 'Routing Header Type 0' (Next Header value 43 with Routing Type 0). For many modern operating systems, this is already the default setting, but it should be explicitly verified.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the IPv6 ACLs on the border router. It is checked whether a rule exists that blocks 'Routing Header Type 0', or whether the router's operating system discards it by default (`show ipv6 cef`). Using a packet generator like Scapy, a test packet with RH0 is created and sent from the outside to check if it is blocked.

controls.title: Protection against DoS and DDoS attacks (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Mechanisms SHOULD be used that detect and defend against high-volume attacks as well as TCP state-exhaustion attacks. This includes rate limits and the configuration of TCP Intercept or SYN cookies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: DoS protection profiles are activated on the border router or an upstream firewall. These typically include thresholds for SYN floods, UDP floods, and ICMP floods. TCP SYN cookies or a TCP intercept mechanism are configured to protect the device's state table from overload. Control Plane Policing (CoPP) is used to prioritize legitimate management traffic.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the DoS protection configuration on the perimeter device, including the thresholds and activated protection mechanisms (e.g., `ip tcp intercept mode watch`). The CoPP configuration is evaluated for its effectiveness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The DoS protection mechanisms are able to not only detect attacks, but also to initiate targeted countermeasures, such as automatically null-routing the attack targets (Remotely Triggered Black Holing, RTBH) or notifying an external DDoS mitigation service provider.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The router is configured to send a BGP message to the upstream provider when it detects a massive attack on a specific target IP, in order to discard traffic to this target already in the provider's network (RTBH). Alternatively, the traffic flow is permanently monitored via NetFlow or sFlow, and in case of anomalies, an external scrubbing service is automatically activated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the BGP and NetFlow configurations as well as the contracts and activation procedures with the external DDoS protection provider. As part of a planned exercise, the process for activating the external mitigation is tested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A hybrid DDoS protection is used, which combines an on-premise solution for fending off low-volume, application-layer attacks with a cloud-based scrubbing service for high-volume attacks. The switchover occurs automatically and in seconds based on traffic analysis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specialized on-premise DDoS appliance (e.g., from Arbor, Radware) is installed. This analyzes the traffic and mitigates attacks up to a certain threshold. If the attack exceeds the capacity of the appliance or the internet connection, the traffic is automatically redirected to the cloud scrubbing service via BGP or DNS. The solution uses machine learning to learn normal traffic patterns and to accurately detect anomalies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the architecture of the hybrid DDoS solution and the configuration of the on-premise appliance. The thresholds and procedures for the automatic switchover to the cloud are checked. The logs of past attacks are analyzed to assess the effectiveness and response time of the solution.

controls.title: Setting up Access Control Lists (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to routers and switches SHOULD be defined using Access Control Lists (ACLs). The ACL SHOULD define, based on the institution's security policy, via which IT systems or networks and with which method a router or switch may be accessed. In the event that no specific rules exist, the more restrictive allowlist approach SHOULD generally be preferred.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: ACLs are used to filter traffic between different network segments (VLANs) according to the security policy. The principle is 'deny by default', meaning only explicitly permitted traffic is allowed through. Every ACL ends with an implicit or explicit `deny any` statement. Every rule in an ACL is documented to explain its purpose.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the ACLs configured on the routers and L3 switches. It is checked whether they follow the 'deny by default' principle and whether the permitted rules comply with the security policy's requirements. The documentation of the ACL rules is checked for its clarity and up-to-dateness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ACLs are reviewed regularly to identify and remove outdated or no longer needed rules. Tools are used to simulate the effects of ACL changes before they are put into production. Blocked packets are logged to detect misconfigurations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A quarterly review process for all important ACLs is established. Tools like `object-groups` are used to make ACLs clearer and more maintainable. The `log` option is appended to `deny` statements to make dropped packets visible and analyzable on the syslog server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the last ACL reviews. He analyzes the syslog servers for logged 'deny' events and asks how they are analyzed. It is checked whether the ACLs are well-structured (e.g., through the use of `object-groups` and comments).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: ACLs are managed centrally via a 'Single Source of Truth' and rolled out to devices automatically. The policies are not defined based on IP addresses, but on identities or tags (Policy as Code). A central tool analyzes and visualizes the resulting data flows and can automatically detect redundant or shadowed rules.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A system like Cisco ACI or a vendor-independent solution is used to define network policies centrally. The policies are maintained in a human-readable language (e.g., YAML) in a Git repository and rolled out via a CI/CD pipeline. Formal verification tools like Batfish are used to prove the correctness and impact of changes before deployment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the policy definitions in the central management solution or in the Git repository. The process of automated rollout and validation is checked. The reports from the analysis tools on shadowed or redundant rules are evaluated. The audit is performed automatically by comparing the policy definitions with the security requirements.

controls.title: Securing Switch Ports (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The ports of a switch SHOULD be protected against unauthorized access. This is achieved by implementing port security, which limits the number of allowed MAC addresses per port and reacts to violations with a defined action.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Port security is configured on all access ports to which end devices are connected. Typically, the maximum number of MAC addresses is set to 1 or 2. In case of a violation, the port is put into `shutdown` or `restrict` mode. The MAC addresses are learned dynamically and stored in the configuration (sticky MAC).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the configuration of access ports for the activation and correct configuration of port security. A test device is used to try to connect a second device to a secured port to test the switch's reaction. The command `show port-security interface <interface-id>` shows the status.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to port security, other Layer 2 protection mechanisms are implemented to prevent attacks such as DHCP spoofing and ARP spoofing. These include DHCP Snooping and Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: DHCP Snooping is enabled on all access switches. The ports leading to legitimate DHCP servers are configured as 'trusted'. Based on the binding table built by DHCP Snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection (DAI) is enabled to discard ARP packets with inconsistent IP-MAC mappings.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the global and interface-specific configuration of DHCP Snooping and DAI. It is checked whether the trust settings are correct. As part of a test, an attempt is made to operate a malicious DHCP server or to forge ARP packets. A `show ip dhcp snooping binding` can be used to check the learned mappings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All Layer 2 protection mechanisms are supplemented by the implementation of port-based network access control (IEEE 802.1X). A device is only granted access to the network after successful authentication (e.g., via a certificate). Unauthenticated devices are moved to a quarantine VLAN.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A RADIUS server (e.g., FreeRADIUS, Cisco ISE) is set up as an authentication server. On the switches, 802.1X is enabled for all access ports. The end devices are equipped with client certificates and configured for authentication via EAP-TLS. The RADIUS policies define which device is placed in which VLAN upon successful authentication.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the RADIUS server and the switches. It is checked whether an unconfigured device can connect to the network and whether it is correctly moved to the quarantine VLAN. The authentication process of a legitimate client is captured and analyzed. A `show authentication sessions` on the switch provides information about the status.

controls.title: Security Aspects of Routing Protocols (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers SHOULD authenticate each other when exchanging routing information or sending updates for routing tables. Only routing protocols that support this SHOULD be used. Dynamic routing protocols MUST NOT be used in demilitarized zones (DMZs). In DMZs, static routes SHOULD be used instead.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For internal routing protocols such as OSPF or EIGRP, neighbor authentication is configured using a pre-shared key and a hashing algorithm (e.g., MD5, ideally SHA). Passive interfaces are defined to prevent the sending of routing updates into end-user VLANs. In the DMZ, only static routes to the required systems and a default route to the internet gateway are configured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the routing protocol configurations on all routers. It is checked whether authentication is enabled for all neighborhoods (`show ip ospf interface`). The configuration of the DMZ routers is checked for the exclusive use of static routes (`show ip route`).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The distribution of routes is strictly controlled by route filters (distribute lists, prefix lists, route maps). Only explicitly needed routes are accepted from a routing neighbor and passed on. This prevents the injection of unwanted routes and the uncontrolled spread of routing information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each BGP or OSPF neighborhood, prefix lists are defined that contain exactly the expected subnets. These lists are integrated into route maps and applied to incoming and outgoing route updates. This is particularly important at the boundaries between different routing domains or security zones.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configured route filters and assesses their strictness and correctness. It is checked whether a router would learn an unexpected, more specific route from a neighbor, or whether the filter prevents this.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the external routing protocol BGP, advanced security mechanisms such as RPKI (Resource Public Key Infrastructure) for validating route origin and BGPsec for securing the path are used to prevent route hijacking. The authentication keys for internal routing protocols are rotated regularly and automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The border router is configured to check the routes received from BGP neighbors against an RPKI validation database and to discard invalid routes. The keys for OSPF/EIGRP authentication are managed in a central key management system and regularly updated on all routers via automation scripts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the BGP configuration for the activation of RPKI validation (`show bgp rpki summary`). The key rotation process is analyzed. It is checked how the organization reacts to RPKI 'invalid' routes announced by their upstream providers.

controls.title: Identity and Authorization Management in the Network Infrastructure (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers and switches SHOULD be connected to a central identity and authorization management system. A personal account is used for each administrator. Group or functional accounts are avoided.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central authentication server (e.g., TACACS+ or RADIUS) is implemented. All routers and switches are configured to send authentication requests to this server (AAA configuration). An individual user account is created for each administrator on the central server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the AAA configuration on the network devices and the user accounts on the central authentication server. It is checked whether the use of local databases on the devices is restricted to an emergency account. It is checked whether shared accounts exist.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central system is used not only for authentication, but also for authorization and accounting. Different authorization levels (roles) are defined and assigned to users. This allows the permitted commands per user or group to be restricted (Command Authorization).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On the TACACS+ server, roles such as 'Network Operator' (only `show` commands) and 'Network Administrator' (full rights) are defined. These roles are assigned to the user accounts. The network devices are configured to send every executed command to the TACACS+ server for authorization and logging (accounting).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the role and permission configuration on the TACACS+ server. With a test account assigned to the operator role, an attempt is made to execute a configuration command. The accounting logs on the server are checked for completeness and level of detail.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central identity and authorization management for the network infrastructure is fully integrated into the organization's overall Identity and Access Management (IAM) process. Logging into the central authentication server (e.g., TACACS+) requires Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The TACACS+ server is connected to the central directory service (e.g., Active Directory) and the organization's MFA solution. A joiner-mover-leaver process ensures that user accounts and permissions are automatically created, modified, and immediately deactivated when an employee leaves.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of the TACACS+ system with AD and the MFA solution. It is tested whether a login is possible without a second factor. The process for deactivating a user account is verified by deactivating a test account in AD and immediately checking access to a network device.

controls.title: Emergency preparedness for routers and switches (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be planned and prepared which failures on routers or switches could be diagnosed in an emergency. Furthermore, it SHOULD be planned and prepared how the identified failures can be resolved. Corresponding action plans SHOULD be defined for typical failure scenarios. The emergency plans SHOULD be based on the general emergency preparedness concept and be coordinated with the overall incident and emergency preparedness.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An emergency manual specifically for the network infrastructure is created. It describes typical scenarios (e.g. 'switch fails', 'routing problem', 'configuration error') and contains detailed, step-by-step instructions for diagnosis and remediation. It also includes contact lists and escalation paths.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the emergency manual for network components and checks it for completeness, clarity, and plausibility of the described scenarios and instructions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The action plans SHOULD be updated at regular intervals. It SHOULD be ensured that the emergency preparedness documentation and the action plans contained therein are available in paper form. The procedure described in the context of emergency preparedness SHOULD be practiced regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency manual is reviewed and updated at least annually. A printed version is kept in a secure and accessible location (e.g., in the data center). An emergency drill (tabletop or simulation exercise) is conducted at least once a year to test the action plans and train the team's responsiveness.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the printed version of the emergency manual for currency. The logs and 'lessons learned' reports from the last emergency drills are reviewed and evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cold or hot spare devices are kept available for critical routers and switches (Cold/Hot Spare). The process for replacing a device and applying the last known good configuration is largely automated and is regularly practiced as part of live tests (e.g., failover tests in a maintenance window).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each critical device class, at least one identical spare device is procured, pre-configured, and stored. The recovery process is supported by automation scripts (e.g., Ansible playbooks) that fetch the current configuration from the NCM tool and apply it to the new device. In high-availability setups (e.g., switch stacks, router clusters), failover is tested regularly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and condition of the spare devices. The automation scripts for the recovery process are analyzed. The logs of the last failover tests are checked to assess the reliability of the process.

controls.title: Audits and Penetration Tests (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers and switches SHOULD be regularly checked for known security issues. Revisions SHOULD also be carried out regularly. Among other things, it SHOULD be checked whether the actual state corresponds to the defined secure basic configuration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An internal audit is conducted regularly (e.g., quarterly). This includes a comparison of the running configurations with the hardening guidelines and checklists. In addition, the manufacturers' security advisories are subscribed to and regularly checked to see if the products in use are affected by new vulnerabilities.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the reports from the last internal audits. They check the process for monitoring manufacturer vulnerability announcements and how they are responded to.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The results of the audits SHOULD be documented in a comprehensible manner and compared with the target state. Deviations SHOULD be investigated. The check is supported by automated configuration compliance scanners.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The results of each audit are recorded in a formal report. Identified deviations are recorded as findings in a ticket system, prioritized, and their remediation is tracked. An NCM tool or an automation script is used to automatically check the configurations against a 'Golden Configuration' and generate a compliance report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the audit reports and the handling of the deficiencies identified therein. The configuration and reports of the compliance scanner are evaluated. It is checked whether a remediation plan exists and is being implemented for all identified deviations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to internal audits, external penetration tests are carried out regularly (e.g. annually), specifically targeting the security of the network infrastructure. The findings from these tests are used to improve security policies and configurations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specialized external service provider is commissioned to conduct a penetration test. The test scope includes attack attempts on the management interfaces, attempts to bypass ACLs and Layer 2 protection mechanisms, and verification of network segmentation. The results are evaluated by management and lead to concrete improvement projects.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the management summary and the technical report of the last external penetration test. It is analyzed how the identified vulnerabilities were assessed and remediated. It is checked whether the 'lessons learned' have led to an adjustment of the security policies.

controls.title: Use of Network Access Controls (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Port-based Access Control SHOULD be implemented according to IEEE 802.1x. A secure authentication protocol such as EAP-TLS should be used. There SHOULD be NO implementation according to the outdated and insecure standards IEEE 802.1x-2001 and IEEE 802.1x-2004.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Network Access Control (NAC) solution is implemented. This consists of a RADIUS server (Policy Server), the switches as supplicants, and the endpoints as clients. 802.1X is enabled per port on the switches. Authentication is done via EAP-TLS, for which both the RADIUS server and the clients require certificates issued by an internal PKI.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the RADIUS server, the switches, and a sample client. It is verified that EAP-TLS is enforced as the authentication method. It is checked whether the switches support and have configured the modern 802.1X versions. A `show authentication sessions` on the switch displays the details of the active sessions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The NAC solution is used for the dynamic assignment of network resources. Based on the identity of the user and/or device, authenticated clients are automatically assigned to the correct VLAN. Separate VLANs with restricted access are provided for guests or non-compliant devices.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Policies are created on the RADIUS server that dynamically return VLAN IDs or downloadable ACLs (dACLs) to the switch based on attributes (e.g., AD group membership of the user). A guest VLAN (with a captive portal) and a quarantine VLAN (with no external access) are configured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the policies on the RADIUS server. It is tested whether a user from the marketing department is correctly placed in the marketing VLAN and a user from development is placed in the development VLAN. The behavior when connecting a non-authenticatable device is tested.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before granting network access, the NAC solution performs a comprehensive security posture assessment of the endpoint. It checks whether the operating system is up to date, an antivirus program is running, and disk encryption is active. Devices that fail the check only receive limited access to a remediation VLAN.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An agent of the NAC solution is installed on all endpoints. This agent collects the information necessary for the posture check and transmits it to the Policy Server. Detailed posture rules are defined in the Policy Server. The remediation VLAN only allows access to update servers and the helpdesk so that the user can rectify the deficiencies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the posture rules in the NAC system. An attempt is made to connect with a test device that is intentionally missing security updates. It is checked whether the device is correctly identified as non-compliant and moved to the remediation VLAN.

controls.title: Advanced integrity protection for configuration files (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a router or switch crashes, it SHOULD be ensured that no old or faulty configurations (including ACLs) are used during recovery or restart. The 'startup-config' is defined and protected as the sole source of truth after a reboot.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The process of saving configuration changes (`copy running-config startup-config`) is strictly enforced and is part of the change management process. The 'startup-config' is backed up regularly (see A8) and the backups are checked for integrity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the 'running-config' with the 'startup-config' on several devices. Large discrepancies indicate a flawed process. The backup procedures for the 'startup-config' are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrity of the configuration file that is loaded at boot time is protected by a hash value or a digital signature. The device's bootloader verifies this signature before loading the configuration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Modern network operating systems offer features for signing configuration files. This feature is enabled. The private key for signing is securely managed in a Hardware Security Module (HSM) or a Key Management System.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the device's configuration to verify that the configuration file protection feature is enabled. The process for managing the signing key is reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A comprehensive 'Secure Boot' chain is implemented. This ensures that from the hardware through the bootloader to the operating system and the configuration file, each component is cryptographically verified before it is loaded. Tampering at any point in the boot process is detected and prevents the device from starting.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Only devices that have a hardware 'Root of Trust' (e.g., a TPM chip) and a complete Secure Boot implementation are procured. This feature is enabled and configured. The state of the Secure Boot chain is regularly checked via remote attestation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the device documentation and configuration to verify the activation of Secure Boot. It is checked how the organization responds to a failed Secure Boot process. The results of the remote attestation checks are analyzed. The `show platform integrity` command or an equivalent can display the status.

controls.title: High Availability (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers and switches SHOULD be designed redundantly. Care SHOULD be taken to ensure that the institution's security policy is adhered to. The implementation of a high-availability solution SHOULD NOT impede the operation of the routers and switches or their security functions, nor lower the security level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Critical network components (core switches, border routers) are implemented as redundant pairs (cluster, stack). Protocols such as HSRP/VRRP for router redundancy and LACP for redundant switch uplinks are used. The configuration of the redundant pair is kept synchronized.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network topology and the configuration of the critical components to verify the redundant design. It is checked whether the configurations of the redundant devices are consistent and whether the failover protocols are configured correctly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The redundant design includes not only the devices themselves, but also their power supply and network connections. Each device in a redundant pair is connected to separate power circuits (ideally UPS A/B). Uplinks are distributed across different line cards or modules.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Switches with redundant power supplies are procured. One power supply is connected to the A-feed, the other to the B-feed. Uplink ports are physically distributed across different modules of the chassis. The redundant devices are placed in different fire compartments or at least in different racks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a physical inspection in the data center to check the cabling of the power supply and the uplinks. It is checked whether the placement of the devices corresponds to the concept of physical redundancy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The high-availability architecture is designed to be fully site-redundant. Critical network functions are operated in parallel in two geographically separate data centers. The failover process between the sites is tested regularly and automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An active/active or active/passive data center architecture is implemented. Routing protocols are configured so that in the event of a site failure, traffic is automatically rerouted via the second site. Techniques such as OTV (Overlay Transport Virtualization) or VXLAN are used to enable Layer 2 connectivity between the sites.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the cross-site network architecture and the configuration of the routing protocols. The logs of the last disaster recovery tests, in which a complete site failure was simulated, are evaluated.

controls.title: Bandwidth management for critical applications and services (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers and switches SHOULD include and use features that allow applications to be identified and bandwidth to be prioritized. Critical traffic is given preferential treatment over less important traffic.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Quality of Service (QoS) policy is defined and implemented. Traffic is classified based on Layer 3 (IP addresses) and Layer 4 information (port numbers). Critical traffic (e.g., VoIP, important business applications) is assigned a higher priority (e.g., by setting DSCP values) and a guaranteed bandwidth. Unimportant traffic (e.g., social media) is assigned a lower priority.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the QoS configuration on the routers and switches. It is checked whether the classification and prioritization correspond to the defined policy. Under simulated load, it is checked whether the critical traffic is actually preferred and receives the guaranteed bandwidth.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Application detection is not only based on ports, but also through Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) at Layer 7. This allows for more precise classification of applications that use dynamic ports or are encrypted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Routers or switches with advanced QoS features (e.g., Cisco NBAR2) are used. The classification is based on application signatures that are updated regularly. This allows, for example, to distinguish 'Microsoft Teams Call' traffic from 'Microsoft Teams File-Transfer' traffic and prioritize them differently.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the Layer 7 application detection. It is tested whether the QoS policy is correctly applied to traffic that runs over standard ports like 443 but belongs to different applications. The router's statistics functions (`show policy-map interface`) are used to verify the classification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central, SD-WAN-capable (Software-Defined WAN) bandwidth management system is used. This dynamically controls traffic across various paths (e.g., MPLS, Internet), based on the application, the real-time performance of the paths (latency, jitter, packet loss), and the centrally defined business policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An SD-WAN solution (e.g., from Cisco, Fortinet, VMware) is rolled out. Application policies are defined in the central controller (e.g., 'VoIP traffic must always use the path with the lowest latency'). The edge routers at the sites implement these policies and continuously measure the quality of all available WAN paths.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the policies in the central SD-WAN controller. The monitoring dashboards are evaluated to understand the path quality measurements and the dynamic routing decisions. As part of a test, the quality of a WAN path is artificially degraded to observe whether the SD-WAN solution correctly switches the critical traffic to a better path.

controls.title: Use of certified products (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When procuring routers and switches, care is taken to ensure that the products come from reputable manufacturers who have a transparent process for managing security vulnerabilities (e.g., a PSIRT).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the procurement process, the existence and quality of the manufacturer's Product Security Incident Response Team (PSIRT) is used as an evaluation criterion. It is checked whether the manufacturer publishes security advisories regularly and promptly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the procurement policies and processes. It is checked if and how the security practices of the manufacturers are included in the purchasing decision.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Routers and switches with a security evaluation according to Common Criteria (CC) SHOULD be used, at least with level EAL2 or an equivalent evaluation proven by a protection profile.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A certification according to Common Criteria is formulated as a requirement in the tender and procurement documents. Products that have a valid CC certificate are specifically selected. The certificates are checked for their validity and the exact target of evaluation (TOE).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the procurement documents for the requirement of a CC certification. It is verified whether the products used actually have the required certificates by inspecting the certification reports (e.g., on the website of the BSI or the CC portal).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For use in high-security environments, routers and switches with a security evaluation according to Common Criteria (CC) of level EAL4 or higher are used. The configuration of the devices is carried out exactly as described in the associated guide for certified operation (guidance documentation).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirement 'CC EAL4+' is specified as a mandatory criterion in the tender. After procurement, the device is configured strictly according to the specifications of the administrator guidance in the certification report to ensure that the evaluated state of security is also achieved in operation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the live configuration of the device in detail with the specifications from the guidance documentation of the CC certificate. Any deviation is documented and evaluated, as it can lead to the certified state no longer being met.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Routers and switches form the backbone of today's data networks. A failure of one or more of these devices can lead to a complete standstill of the entire IT infrastructure. They must therefore be specially secured.
Routers operate at OSI Layer 3 (Network Layer) and forward data packets based on the destination IP address in the IP header. Routers are able to connect networks with different topologies. They are used to segment local networks or to connect local networks via wide area networks. A router identifies a suitable connection between the source system or source network and the destination system or destination network. In most cases, this is done by forwarding the data packets to the next router.
Switches originally operated on OSI Layer 2, but are now available with different functions. Companies usually label the devices with the OSI layer that is supported. This gave rise to the terms Layer 2, Layer 3, and Layer 4 switch, whereby Layer 3 and Layer 4 switches are in fact already routers in terms of functionality. The originally different functions of switches and routers are thus often combined on a single device today.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: This module describes how routers and switches can be used securely.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The NET.3.1 Routers and Switches module must be applied to every router and switch used in the information system.
A wide range of different routers and switches from various companies is available on the market. This module does not describe specific requirements for particular products. It is kept as product-independent as possible.
Due to the merging of router and switch functions, most of the requirements can be applied to both routers and switches. This module largely does not differentiate between these device types.
Today, almost all server and client operating systems also offer routing functionality. This module does not specify requirements for activated routing functions in server and client operating systems.
Furthermore, aspects of infrastructural security are not listed in this module, such as suitable placement, power supply, or cabling. Security requirements for these topics can be found in the respective modules of the INF Infrastructure layer.
This module does not describe requirements for securing virtual routers and switches. Nor does it address any firewall functions of routers and switches. For this, the NET.3.2 Firewall module must also be implemented. Some aspects of network design and management are also relevant for the use of routers and switches and are mentioned in the context of the corresponding requirements. Further information on the structure, design, and management of a network can be found in the NET.1.1 Network Architecture and Design and NET.1.2 Network Management modules.
Routers and switches should generally be taken into account when implementing the ORP.4 Identity and Access Management, OPS.1.1.3 Patch and Change Management, CON.3 Data Backup Concept, and OPS.1.1.2 Proper IT Administration modules.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
parts.prose: In the event of a DDoS attack on a protected network, for example via TCP SYN Flooding or UDP Packet Storm, the router may fail due to the large number of network connections that need to be processed. This can result in certain services in the Local Area Network (LAN) no longer being available or the entire LAN failing.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Manipulation
parts.prose: If attackers manage to gain unauthorized access to a router or switch, they can reconfigure the devices or start additional services. For example, the configuration can be changed in such a way that services, clients, or entire network segments are blocked. At the same time, network traffic on the switch can be intercepted, read, or manipulated.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Incorrect configuration of a router or switch
parts.prose: Routers and switches are delivered with a default configuration in which many services are activated. Login banners, for example, reveal the model and version number of the device. If routers and switches are used in production with insecure factory settings, it is easier to gain unauthorized access to them. In the worst case, this makes internal services accessible to attackers.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Incorrect planning and design
parts.prose: Many institutions plan and design the use of routers and switches incorrectly. For example, devices are procured that are not sufficiently dimensioned, e.g. in terms of the number of ports or performance. As a result, a router or switch may already be overloaded when it is used for the first time. This may result in services or entire networks being unreachable and the error having to be corrected at great expense.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Incompatible active network components
parts.prose: Compatibility problems can arise in particular when existing networks are supplemented with active network components from other companies or when networks are operated with network components from different companies. If active network components with different implementations of the same communication method are operated together in a network, individual sub-areas of the network, certain services, or even the entire network may fail.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.6. MAC Flooding
parts.prose: In MAC flooding, attackers send many requests with changing source MAC addresses to a switch. As soon as the switch has reached the limits of the MAC addresses it can store, it starts sending all requests to all IT systems in the network. This allows attackers to view the network traffic.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.7. Spanning Tree Attacks
parts.prose: In Spanning Tree attacks, attackers send so-called Bridge Protocol Data Units (BPDUs) with the aim of getting the switches to see their own (malicious) switch as the root bridge. This redirects the network traffic via the attackers' switch, so that they can intercept all information sent via it. As a result, they can initiate DDoS attacks and, by using false BPDUs, force the network to rebuild the Spanning Tree topology, which can cause the network to fail.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.8. GARP attacks
parts.prose: In Gratuitous ARP (GARP) attacks, attackers send unsolicited ARP replies to specific victims or to all IT systems in the same subnet. In this forged ARP reply, the attackers enter their MAC address as the mapping for a foreign IP address and cause the victim to change its ARP table in such a way that the network traffic is now sent to the attackers instead of to the valid destination. This allows them to intercept or manipulate the communication between the victims.

controls.title: Creation of a security policy

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are only isolated, informal guidelines or drafts for firewall operation. A formal security policy, approved and communicated by management, is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In this state, firewall rules are often created ad-hoc by individual administrators based on verbal agreements or immediate needs, without an overarching strategy.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Through interviews with IT staff and management, the auditor determines whether a formal, written security policy for firewalls exists and whether it has been officially approved.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic security policy for firewalls exists as a document. However, it is not known to all responsible employees or is not consistently applied. Regular reviews of the policy do not take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy was created once and stored in a file system, but there is no process to train new employees or ensure compliance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the firewall security policy and checks through random interviews with firewall administrators whether they know the content of the policy and use it as a basis for their work.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the general security policy of the institution, a specific security policy MUST be created. This MUST describe traceable requirements and specifications on how firewalls can be operated securely. The policy MUST be known to all employees responsible for firewalls and be fundamental to their work. If the policy is changed or if there are deviations from the requirements, this MUST be coordinated with the ISO and documented. It MUST be regularly checked whether the policy is still being implemented correctly. The results MUST be appropriately documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is published on the intranet or a comparable system accessible to all relevant employees. Changes are managed through a defined change management process, which includes coordination with the ISO. The review (e.g., annually) is scheduled and the results are recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and content of the security policy. He checks the minutes of the last reviews and the documentation of changes, including the proof of coordination with the ISO.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is reviewed and adapted at least annually and on an ad-hoc basis (e.g., after security incidents or major infrastructure changes). Compliance with the policy is verified through regular, random, manual checks of the firewall configurations. All changes to the policy are versioned and traceable.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An internal audit team or the ISO conducts quarterly or semi-annual manual checks, during which the live firewall configuration is checked against the policy specifications. The results are documented and deviations are tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the audit reports of the internal controls, the version history of the security policy, and the logs of ad-hoc reviews.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is integrated into a higher-level Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) framework. Its compliance is continuously monitored through automated configuration and compliance checks. Detected deviations from the policy trigger automatic alerts to the security team, and a defined and partially automated process exists for handling these deviations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Specialized software for Security Policy Management or Network Configuration Management is used, which continuously compares firewall configurations with the policy. Rule sets for these tools are derived from the central GRC platform.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and reports of the automated compliance management tool. He checks the configuration of the automated alerting and the processing logs of occurred deviations to assess the effectiveness of the process.

controls.title: Defining firewall rules

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Firewall rules are created ad-hoc and without formal documentation. An 'allow-any' approach is often pursued, where non-specific traffic is permitted to quickly establish functionality.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A typical example is a rule like `allow any any from internal to internet`, configured without specific port or destination restrictions. Documentation, if any, exists only as a comment in the rule itself.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the firewall rule set for the presence of broad, non-specific 'allow' rules and questions the administrators about the process for creating and documenting new rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An allowlist approach (default-deny) is generally followed, but the rules are not always sufficiently documented. Responsibilities for rule changes are informally known but not formally defined.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a 'deny all' rule at the end of the rule set. Although new rules are formulated more specifically, the reason for their creation or the requester is not systematically recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of a 'default-deny' rule at the end of the rule set and requests the documentation for a sample of recently added rules to assess their completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Unique rules MUST be defined for the firewall that specify which communication links and data streams are permitted. All other connections MUST be blocked by the firewall (allowlist approach). Responsible persons MUST be named to design, implement, and test filter rules. Furthermore, it MUST be clarified who is allowed to change filter rules. The decisions made, as well as the relevant information and reasons for the decisions, MUST be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A ticketing system or a standardized request form is used to request new firewall rules. Each rule is provided with a ticket number, the requester, the reason, and an expiration date. Changes to the rule set are carried out according to the four-eyes principle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the rule set and compares a sample of rules with the associated documentation (e.g., tickets). He checks the process documentation for rule changes and verifies compliance with the four-eyes principle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall rule set is regularly reviewed, at least semi-annually, for rules that are no longer needed, too broad, or redundant. An 'owner' (responsible person) and an expiration date are defined for each rule. Before expiration, the owner is automatically notified to extend or delete the rule.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Scripts or specialized tools (e.g., Firewall Policy Analyzer) are used to analyze the rule set and generate reports on unused or 'shadowed' rules. The management of owners and expiration dates is handled in a central database or the ticketing system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the reports from the last rule set reviews and checks whether the identified issues have been resolved. He randomly checks whether rules with expired validity dates have been deactivated or removed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The process for requesting, approving, and implementing firewall rules is largely automated. Based on application and risk information, a rule proposal is automatically generated, which is automatically rolled out to the firewall after approval. Continuous analyses check the rule set for optimization potential and conformity with the security policy in real time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A firewall orchestration and automation platform is used. This is integrated with the CMDB and the ticketing system. Requests are made via a self-service portal, and the platform automatically validates the request against security policies before forwarding it for approval.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configured workflow in the automation platform, including the approval steps and the automatic validation rules. He checks the audit logs of the platform to trace the lifecycle of some rules from request to implementation.

controls.title: Setting up suitable filter rules on the packet filter

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The packet filter is configured statelessly. Rules for TCP connections are created without considering flags like SYN or ACK. ICMP is either completely blocked or completely allowed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This corresponds to a classic Access Control List (ACL) on a router that does not track the state of a connection. Each packet is considered in isolation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the configuration of the packet filter and determines whether stateful inspection functions are activated. He checks the ICMP rules for their specificity.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A packet filter MUST be set to discard all invalid TCP flag combinations. Stateful filtering MUST always be used. Stateful filter rules MUST also be configured for the connectionless protocols UDP and ICMP. The firewall MUST filter the ICMP and ICMPv6 protocols restrictively.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall's stateful inspection engine must be activated. For TCP, it is ensured that only packets with the SYN flag set can initiate a new connection. For UDP, a pseudo-state table is maintained, which only allows response packets if a packet was recently sent in the opposite direction. For ICMP, only the explicitly required types (e.g., Echo-Request/Reply, Time-Exceeded) are allowed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the activation of the stateful inspection function. He checks the configuration for rules that block invalid TCP flags and the specific handling of UDP and ICMP traffic according to the stateful principle.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the defined filters, anti-spoofing filters (according to BCP 38 / RFC 2827) are consistently enforced on all interfaces. Rules are implemented to prevent filter evasion through IP fragmentation. The packet filter is configured to also check or discard IPv6 extension headers that can be misused for attacks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At the external interface, all packets whose source IP address is from the internal address range are discarded. At internal interfaces, it is ensured that only packets with source IPs from the respective network segment are accepted. The firewall is configured to reassemble fragmented packets before the filter rules are applied.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the configuration of the firewall interfaces for active anti-spoofing filters. He verifies the settings for handling IP fragments and IPv6 extension headers.

controls.title: Secure configuration of the firewall

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall is operated with the manufacturer's default settings. Unnecessary services may be active. Configuration changes are not systematically documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is not further hardened after initial setup. Default passwords are changed, but further configurations such as disabling Telnet access or unused web interfaces are omitted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the list of active services on the firewall with a list of a actually needed services. He asks for the documentation of the last configuration changes.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before a firewall is deployed, it MUST be securely configured. All configuration changes MUST be traceably documented. The integrity of the configuration files MUST be appropriately protected. Access passwords MUST be secured using a modern cryptographic method. A firewall MUST be configured so that only strictly necessary services are available. Unnecessary (information) services and unnecessary functional extensions MUST be deactivated or completely uninstalled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented hardening process is followed, based on manufacturer recommendations or CIS benchmarks. All unnecessary management interfaces (e.g., Telnet, HTTP) and services (e.g., SNMP with public community) are deactivated. Configuration changes are controlled and logged via a change management process. Backups of the configuration are created regularly and stored securely.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the documentation of the hardening process and compares it with the active configuration of the firewall. He checks the change management logs and verifies the configuration of the password storage and the active services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrity of the configuration files and the firewall software is regularly checked by verifying cryptographic checksums. The configuration is automatically monitored for deviations from a defined secure baseline.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A configuration management tool (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) or a specialized Network Configuration Management (NCM) tool is used to define and enforce a configuration baseline. Daily or weekly jobs check the live configuration against the baseline and report deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the monitoring tool, the defined baseline, and the reports on configuration deviations. He checks how reported deviations are responded to. An automated check could be `sudo debsums -c` on a Debian-based firewall system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Every configuration change is automatically checked for compliance with the security policy and potential negative security impacts (e.g., creation of overly permissive rules) before it is applied. Changes that violate the policy are automatically blocked or require an escalation approval. In case of an unauthorized change, the system can automatically revert to the last approved configuration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A firewall automation or orchestration platform is used that enables a 'policy-as-code' approach. Security policies are defined in a machine-readable format. A CI/CD pipeline approach is used for rolling out configuration changes, including automatic pre-deployment checks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the security policies defined in code and the configuration of the CI/CD pipeline. They trigger a test change that violates the policy to verify that the process correctly blocks or reports the change.

controls.title: Protection of the administration interfaces

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall is administered over the production network. Insecure protocols such as Telnet or HTTP are used for management. Access is not restricted to specific source IP addresses.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Administrators connect to the firewall from their normal workstations via Telnet or an unencrypted web interface to make configuration changes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall configuration for active insecure administration protocols. They check the access rules for the management interfaces for restrictions on source IP addresses.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative and management access to the firewall MUST be restricted to individual source IP addresses or address ranges. It MUST be ensured that administrative interfaces cannot be accessed from untrusted networks. To administer or monitor the firewall, ONLY secure protocols (e.g., SSH, HTTPS) MUST be used. Appropriate time limits MUST be set for the user interfaces.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A management zone or a dedicated VLAN is set up for administration. Access to the firewall's management interfaces is only permitted from dedicated admin workstations or jump hosts from this network. The firewall rules are configured accordingly. Insecure protocols are disabled. Inactive sessions are automatically terminated after a short period (e.g., 15 minutes).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the firewall rules that protect the management ports (e.g., TCP/22, TCP/443). They check the list of allowed source IPs and the session timeout configuration. An automated check can be performed by a port scan of the management interface from an unauthorized network.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall is administered exclusively via a dedicated, physically or logically separate administration network (out-of-band management). Two-factor authentication (2FA) is required for administrative access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall has a dedicated management interface connected to a separate switch. Access to this network is highly restricted. Authentication to the firewall is coupled with a central AAA system (e.g., RADIUS, TACACS+) that enforces 2FA.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the physical network setup and the configuration of the management interface. They check the configuration of the connection to the AAA system and verify the enforcement of 2FA through a test login.

controls.title: Emergency access to the firewall

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST always be possible to access the firewall directly so that it can be administered locally in an emergency, even if the entire network fails.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A serial console access (e.g., via RS-232) is set up for the firewall. A laptop with the appropriate cable and the necessary terminal software is kept in a secure location for emergencies. The password for console access is stored securely and is available to the responsible administrators in an emergency.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the physical access to the firewall's serial console. They check the availability of the emergency laptop and the console cable. They verify the process for accessing the emergency password.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The serial console access is connected to a secure terminal or console server. This allows remote access to the console via an independent communication path (out-of-band), even if the firewall's primary network connections are disrupted. Access to the console server is protected by strong authentication.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A console server with its own modem for a dial-up connection or a separate internet connection is installed in the data center. Access to it requires multi-factor authentication. All access via the console server is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the console server, the protective measures for its remote access, and the logging of accesses. They have the process of an emergency access via the console server demonstrated.

controls.title: Prevention of dynamic routing

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dynamic routing MUST be disabled in the firewall settings, unless the packet filter is used as a perimeter router in accordance with module NET.3.1 Routers and Switches.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: During the basic configuration of the firewall, it is explicitly checked that no dynamic routing protocols such as OSPF, BGP, or RIP are activated. Routes are configured statically.
