If dynamic routing is absolutely necessary, this is documented, approved, and configured according to the specifications for secure routing in NET.3.1 (e.g., with authentication of routing updates).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor examines the global configuration and the process list of the firewall to ensure that no routing daemons are active. They compare the configuration with the documentation if dynamic routing is exceptionally permitted.

controls.title: Logging

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall logs events only locally. The log files are not regularly backed up or evaluated and are overwritten after a short time. The system time is not synchronized.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The default logging configuration is retained. This often causes the local hard drive or memory to fill up quickly, and older logs are lost. Analysis only takes place reactively after an incident, provided the data is still available.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall's logging configuration, the fill level of the log storage, and the retention period. They compare the firewall's system time with a reference time.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall MUST be configured to log at least the following security-relevant events: rejected network connections, failed access to system resources, error messages from firewall services, general system error messages, and configuration changes. If security proxies are used, security breaches and violations of access control lists MUST also be logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is configured to send its log data in real time to a central, secured syslog server. This ensures that the logs are preserved even after a compromise of the firewall itself. The firewall's system time is synchronized with an internal NTP server. The retention period for the logs is determined in accordance with legal and operational requirements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the firewall's logging configuration and checks on the central log server whether the data is arriving. They check the NTP configuration and the settings for log rotation and archiving on the log server. Automated check: `grep 'sshd' /var/log/auth.log` on the syslog server to see if the logs are arriving.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The centrally collected log data from the firewall is regularly, at least weekly, checked manually or with simple scripts for conspicuous patterns and security-relevant events. There are defined thresholds for certain events (e.g., high number of rejected packets), and a notification is sent if they are exceeded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The log data is fed into a central log management system. Simple correlation rules and dashboards are created to provide an overview. An administrator is responsible for reviewing the reports weekly and investigating anomalies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the reports and dashboards of the log management system. They check the protocols of the weekly evaluations and inquire about the process for investigating anomalies.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall's log data is integrated into a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system. Complex correlation rules analyze the data in real time and in correlation with events from other systems (e.g., IDS, server logs) to automatically detect attacks and anomalies. In case of critical events, an incident response process is automatically triggered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SIEM system is enriched with threat intelligence feeds. Use cases such as 'detection of brute-force attacks', 'communication with known C2 servers', or 'anomalies in data traffic' are implemented. The alerting is integrated into a SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation and Response) tool to automate initial response steps.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the correlation rules in the SIEM. They have the functionality of an important use case demonstrated and trace the path of an alarm from detection to response, including the automated steps.

controls.title: Defense against fragmentation attacks on the packet filter

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Protective mechanisms MUST be activated on the packet filter to defend against IPv4 and IPv6 fragmentation attacks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is configured to reassemble fragmented IP packets before further processing (IP Reassembly). This ensures that the filter rules are applied to the complete packet and prevents attacks that work by overlapping fragments or hiding information in fragments. Limits are set for the number of fragments to be processed simultaneously to mitigate resource exhaustion attacks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies in the firewall configuration that the IP fragment reassembly feature is enabled. They check the configured limits and protection mechanisms against fragment flooding.

controls.title: Operational documentation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational tasks of a firewall MUST be documented in a comprehensible manner. All configuration changes and security-relevant tasks MUST be documented, especially changes to the system services and the firewall's rule set. The documentation MUST be protected from unauthorized access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An operations manual is created for the firewall. This document describes recurring tasks such as backup and restore, installing updates, checking log files, and the process for rule changes. All changes to the configuration are recorded in a change log or ticketing system. The documentation is stored in a system with access restrictions (e.g., a protected network drive or a wiki with an authorization concept).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the operations manual and the change logs. They compare a sample of the most recent changes with the corresponding documentation. They check the access permissions for the documentation repository.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operational documentation is reviewed regularly, at least annually, for currency and completeness and revised as needed. The documentation also includes a network topology that illustrates the integration of the firewall and data flows.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The review of the operating manual is part of the annual review cycle. A dedicated network diagramming tool is used to keep the topology up to date. The documentation is versioned.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the last reviews of the operational documentation. They compare the documented network topology with the actual configuration.

controls.title: Procurement of a firewall

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before a firewall is procured, a list of requirements MUST be created, against which the products available on the market are evaluated. Care MUST be taken to ensure that the security level targeted by the institution can be achieved with the firewall. The basis for procurement MUST therefore be the requirements from the security policy. If IPv6 is used, the packet filter MUST inspect the IPv6 extension headers. In addition, IPv6 MUST be configurable in a manner adequate to IPv4.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed requirements catalog is created, containing functional (e.g., throughput, number of interfaces, VPN capability) and non-functional requirements (e.g., management interface, logging capabilities, IPv6 capabilities, manufacturer support). The requirements from the firewall security policy are decisive here. Various products are evaluated based on this catalog (Proof of Concept).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the requirements catalog and the product selection documentation. They check whether the requirements from the security policy have been taken into account and whether the capabilities of the selected product (especially regarding IPv6) meet the requirements.

controls.title: Building a "P-A-P" structure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A single firewall component is used that combines both packet filtering and proxy functions on the same system. There is no architectural separation between the filter and application layers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single Unified Threat Management (UTM) or Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) device is placed at the perimeter and performs all security functions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network architecture and determines whether a single component is responsible for all firewall tasks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A "Packet Filter - Application-Level Gateway - Packet Filter" (P-A-P) structure SHOULD be used. It MUST consist of multiple components with appropriate hardware and software for each. For the most important protocols used, security proxies SHOULD be available at the application layer.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The architecture consists of an outer packet filter, an Application-Level Gateway (ALG) in a Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), and an inner packet filter. The outer filter only allows traffic to the proxies in the DMZ. The inner filter only allows traffic from the proxies to the internal network. Direct traffic from outside to inside is not possible.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network diagram and the configurations of the outer and inner packet filters as well as the Application-Level Gateway to verify the correct implementation of the P-A-P architecture and data flows.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the P-A-P structure, at least generic security proxies are used for all essential services (TCP/UDP). The security proxies SHOULD also run within a secured operating system runtime environment (e.g., container, hardened OS).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to specific proxies (e.g., for HTTP, SMTP), generic SOCKS or TCP/UDP proxies are used for other protocols. The proxy services run on a hardened Linux system where all unnecessary services are disabled and the operating system is protected by security mechanisms such as AppArmor or SELinux.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the Application-Level Gateways and ensures that proxies are used for a wide range of services. They analyze the hardening measures of the operating system on which the proxies are running.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The components of the P-A-P structure (outer packet filter, ALG, inner packet filter) are sourced from different manufacturers (vendor diversity) to make it more difficult to exploit a single vendor-specific vulnerability. The components are also designed for high availability.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The outer packet filter is from vendor A, the Application-Level Gateways are open-source solutions on hardened systems, and the inner packet filter is from vendor B. Each of these layers is implemented as a cluster (e.g., Active/Passive or Active/Active).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the manufacturers and models of the firewall components used. They check the configuration of the high-availability clusters at each layer of the P-A-P architecture.

controls.title: Disabling IPv4 or IPv6

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If the IPv4 or IPv6 protocol is not needed in a network segment, it SHOULD be disabled at the respective firewall network access point (e.g., at the corresponding firewall interface). If the IPv4 or IPv6 protocol is not needed or used, it SHOULD be completely disabled on the firewall.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In pure IPv6 networks, IPv4 processing is disabled on the corresponding firewall interface. In pure IPv4 networks, IPv6 processing is disabled to prevent attacks via the unused protocol (e.g., via tunnels or unintended configurations). This is done through explicit configuration commands on the firewall.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the firewall interfaces. Using the network documentation, they determine which protocols are needed in the connected segments and compare this with the configuration. An automated check can be performed by sending packets of the unwanted protocol (e.g., ICMPv6 Ping) to the interface to see if a response is received.

controls.title: Administration via a separate management network

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Firewalls SHOULD be administered exclusively via a separate management network (out-of-band management). Any existing administration interface via the actual data network (in-band) SHOULD be disabled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is connected to a separate management switch via its dedicated management interface. Administrative access to the data interfaces is blocked by firewall rules. Access to the management network is restricted to a few dedicated administrator workstations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network diagram and the physical cabling of the firewall. They check the firewall configuration to ensure that management services (SSH, HTTPS) are listening only on the management interface and that access via the data interfaces is blocked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Communication in the management network SHOULD be restricted by management firewalls to a few management protocols with precisely defined sources and destinations. The available security mechanisms of the management protocols used for authentication, integrity protection, and encryption SHOULD be activated. All insecure management protocols SHOULD be disabled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The management network itself is protected by its own, smaller firewall. This allows, for example, only SSH connections from the jump hosts to the management interfaces of the network components. Insecure protocols like SNMPv1/v2c are blocked; only SNMPv3 with authentication and encryption is permitted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the management firewall and checks the rule set for compliance with the principle of least privilege. They verify that only secure protocol variants are used.

controls.title: Protection against TCP SYN Flooding, UDP Packet Storm and Sequence Number Guessing at the packet filter

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: On the packet filter that protects server services, a suitable limit for half-open and open connections SHOULD be set (protection against TCP SYN flooding). Rate limits SHOULD be set for UDP data streams. On the outer packet filter, random generation of Initial Sequence Numbers (ISN) SHOULD be enabled for outgoing TCP connections.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is configured with SYN proxy or SYN cookie mechanisms to protect the servers behind it from SYN floods. Rate limits for UDP packets are configured per source IP or globally to mitigate UDP floods. The ISN randomization feature is enabled to make TCP session hijacking more difficult.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the activation and parameters of the protection mechanisms against SYN flooding, the UDP rate limits, and the ISN randomization in the firewall configuration.

controls.title: Securing fundamental Internet protocols

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The HTTP, SMTP, and DNS protocols, including their encrypted versions, SHOULD be routed through protocol-specific security proxies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All web traffic (HTTP/HTTPS) is routed through an explicit forward proxy or a transparent web proxy. Emails (SMTP) are routed through a mail gateway (SMTP proxy). DNS requests are handled by a DNS proxy or forwarder on the firewall. These proxies can validate protocols and filter content.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall rules to ensure that direct HTTP, SMTP, and DNS traffic from the internal network is blocked and that the traffic is instead redirected to the corresponding proxy systems.

controls.title: Temporary decryption of data traffic

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encrypted connections to untrusted networks SHOULD be temporarily decrypted to verify the protocol and inspect the data for malware. The legal framework SHOULD be observed in this process. The component that decrypts the data traffic SHOULD prevent the use of outdated encryption options and cryptographic algorithms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A TLS inspection function (also known as SSL inspection) is activated on the firewall or a dedicated web proxy. It acts as a man-in-the-middle by terminating the TLS connection from the client and establishing a new one to the server. The unencrypted data stream in between can then be examined by other security functions (e.g., antivirus, IPS). Whitelists are maintained for trusted sites (e.g., online banking), whose traffic is not decrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the TLS inspection configuration, including the configured cipher suites and the exception lists. They check the documentation for compliance with legal requirements (e.g., employee consent, works agreement).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TLS proxy used SHOULD be able to check whether certificates are trustworthy. If a certificate is not trustworthy, it SHOULD be possible to reject the connection. It SHOULD be possible to add custom certificates to configure and check "internal" root certificates as well. Pre-configured certificates SHOULD be reviewed and removed if they are not needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The TLS proxy is configured to validate the target server's certificate chain and block connections to servers with invalid, expired, or self-signed certificates. The proxy's trust store is maintained; unneeded or untrusted root CA certificates are removed, and the organization's internal root CAs are added.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the TLS proxy's trust store and the certificate validation configuration. They test access to a website with an invalid certificate to verify that the connection is blocked.

controls.title: Secure Time Synchronization

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall's time SHOULD be synchronized with a Network Time Protocol (NTP) server. The firewall SHOULD NOT allow external time synchronization.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is configured to obtain its time exclusively from trusted, internal NTP servers (e.g., Stratum 2 or 3). Incoming NTP requests from the internet to the firewall are blocked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall's NTP configuration and ensures that only internal NTP servers are listed. They check the firewall rules for blocking incoming NTP traffic. An automated check can be performed via `ntpq -p` on the firewall CLI to see the synchronized peers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The NTP communication between the firewall and the internal NTP servers is protected against manipulation by authentication mechanisms (e.g., NTP Authentication with symmetric keys).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Matching keys for NTP authentication are configured on the NTP servers and the firewall. The firewall is instructed to only accept authenticated NTP responses.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the NTP authentication configuration on both the firewall and the configured NTP servers.

controls.title: System Monitoring and Evaluation

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Firewalls SHOULD be integrated into a suitable system monitoring or monitoring concept. It SHOULD be constantly monitored whether the firewall itself and the services running on it are functioning correctly. In the event of errors or if limit values are exceeded, the operating personnel SHOULD be alerted. Log data or status messages SHOULD ONLY be transmitted via secure communication channels.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall is added to the central monitoring system (e.g., Nagios, Zabbix, Prometheus). Important metrics such as CPU load, memory usage, number of connections, and interface utilization are queried via SNMPv3 or an agent. Thresholds for warnings and critical alerts are defined.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration in the monitoring system that relates to the firewall. They check the defined metrics, the thresholds, and the configured alert paths.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to basic monitoring, automatic alerts are generated that are triggered by specified security-relevant events. This includes, for example, alerts for failed administrative login attempts, configuration changes, or the failure of a cluster component.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The monitoring system is coupled with the log management system or SIEM. Specific log events (e.g., 'configuration changed' or 'login failed') are configured as triggers for alerts in the monitoring system. For cluster systems, the failover process is actively monitored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the event-based alerting. They trigger a test alert (e.g., through an intentionally incorrect login attempt) to check the functionality of the chain.

controls.title: Review and Penetration Testing

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall structure SHOULD be regularly checked for known security problems. Regular penetration tests and reviews SHOULD be carried out.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least once a year, a comprehensive review of the firewall architecture, configuration, and rule set is carried out. In addition, external or internal penetration tests are commissioned at regular intervals (e.g., every one to two years) to check the effectiveness of the firewall security measures from an attacker's perspective.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the reports of the last firewall reviews and penetration tests. They check whether the identified vulnerabilities have been tracked and remediated.

controls.title: Emergency Preparedness for the Firewall

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Diagnostics and troubleshooting SHOULD be planned and prepared in advance. Corresponding instructions for typical failure scenarios SHOULD be defined and updated at regular intervals. The emergency plans SHOULD be coordinated with the overall incident and emergency preparedness. It SHOULD be ensured that the documentation for emergency preparedness is available in paper form.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specific emergency plan for the firewall is created, covering scenarios such as hardware failure, software errors, or incorrect configuration. The plan contains clear instructions, contact lists, and escalation paths. A printed copy of the plan and the last working configuration is kept in a secure location (e.g., in the emergency cabinet).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the emergency plan for the firewall and checks its content and timeliness. They verify the existence and storage location of the printed emergency documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The procedure described in the context of emergency preparedness SHOULD be practiced regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An emergency drill is conducted at least once a year. This can be a purely tabletop exercise where a scenario is discussed, or a functional exercise where, for example, the restoration of a configuration to a test system or the failover of a cluster is tested. The results and lessons learned are documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs and the documentation of the lessons learned from the last emergency drills. They check whether the identified potential for improvement has been implemented.

controls.title: Enhanced Integrity Protection for Configuration Files

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To restore a crashed firewall, it SHOULD be ensured that no old or faulty configurations (including access lists) are used. This SHOULD also apply if an attacker succeeds in restarting the firewall.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A defined process for restoring the firewall configuration is established. After a crash or restart, the running configuration is manually compared with a known, good reference configuration ('Golden Image'). The configuration backups are versioned and marked as 'good' or 'last known working'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the restoration process described to them and reviews the associated documentation. They check the backup management, especially the marking and versioning of the configuration files.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The integrity of the active configuration and system files on the firewall is monitored by a File Integrity Monitoring (FIM) system. An alarm is triggered for any unauthorized change.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A FIM tool (e.g., AIDE, Tripwire) is installed on the firewall. A baseline of the files to be monitored is created. The tool regularly checks (e.g., hourly) whether the checksums of the files have changed and sends an alarm to the central monitoring or SIEM system in case of deviations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the FIM tool, the list of monitored files, and the defined baseline. They trigger a test change to verify the alerting.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall uses a hardware-based root of trust (e.g., Trusted Platform Module, TPM) and a Secure Boot process. This ensures that only a signed, unmodified version of the operating system and configuration can be loaded. Any manipulation causes the system to fail to start or to switch to a secure, isolated state.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A firewall appliance that has a TPM and Secure Boot is procured. The Secure Boot process is configured and activated. The startup configuration is cryptographically bound to the state of the system (TPM sealing), so that it can only be loaded on an unmodified system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the activation of Secure Boot and the use of the TPM in the firewall's BIOS/UEFI and operating system. They check the signatures of the system and configuration files.

controls.title: Outsourcing of Functional Enhancements to Dedicated Hardware

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Functional enhancements of the firewall, such as virus protection, Intrusion Prevention System (IPS), or Web Application Firewall (WAF), are activated as software modules on the central firewall appliance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: On a Unified Threat Management (UTM) or Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW), the licenses for the required additional functions are purchased and the corresponding software blades are activated. All traffic is processed on this single system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration and active modules on the firewall appliance. They assess the system's resource utilization to ensure that the core firewall function is not impaired by the additional services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Functional enhancements of the firewall SHOULD be outsourced to dedicated hardware and software.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Instead of combining all functions on one box, a defense-in-depth architecture with specialized systems is built. Behind the actual firewall, dedicated appliances for a web proxy with virus scan, a separate intrusion prevention system, and a web application firewall for the web servers in the DMZ are operated. This reduces the complexity of the individual components and avoids a single point of failure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network architecture diagram and the configuration of the individual dedicated security systems. They verify the data flows between the components to ensure that traffic is correctly routed through the various security zones and appliances.

controls.title: Use of different firewall operating systems and products in a multi-tiered firewall architecture

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In a multi-tiered firewall architecture (e.g., P-A-P), products from the same manufacturer are used for all components (outer filter, inner filter).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: This is often done for reasons of simpler administration and more favorable licensing. The administrators only have to familiarize themselves with one system and can possibly use a central management tool.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor identifies the manufacturers and models of the firewall components used in the multi-tiered architecture.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In a multi-tiered firewall architecture, different operating systems and products SHOULD be used for the outer and inner firewalls.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Vendor diversity is deliberately implemented. For example, a product from manufacturer A is used as the outer packet filter and a product from manufacturer B is used as the inner packet filter. This increases resilience, as a vendor-specific vulnerability (e.g., a 0-day exploit) cannot compromise the entire firewall architecture.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the manufacturers and models of the firewall components at the different levels of the architecture and confirms that they are products from different manufacturers.

controls.title: Central filtering of active content

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The filtering of active content (e.g., JavaScript, ActiveX) is performed decentrally on the client, for example, through browser settings or endpoint security software.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The responsibility for content filtering lies with the end user or endpoint administration. The firewall allows the content to pass through untouched.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the firewall configuration and determines that no central content filtering is taking place. They consult the endpoint managers about the configurations in place there.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Active content SHOULD be filtered centrally in accordance with the institution's security objectives. For this purpose, encrypted data traffic SHOULD also be decrypted. The required security proxies SHOULD support the filtering of active content.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central web proxy with TLS decryption is used. It analyzes data traffic and removes or blocks potentially malicious active content such as certain JavaScript libraries, Java applets, or ActiveX controls based on a central policy. This complements the protective measures at the endpoint.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the web proxy's configuration, particularly the rules for filtering active content and the TLS decryption function. They test access to a website with blocked content to verify the effectiveness of the filtering.

controls.title: Use of high-availability solutions

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall components are not designed to be redundant. A failure of one component leads to a failure of network connectivity. There is a manual restart process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Individual firewall appliances are in use. In the event of a failure, an administrator must manually configure and install a replacement device (cold standby).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the network diagram and the physical installation to determine that there is no redundancy. They review the disaster recovery plan for the manual replacement.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Packet filters and application-level gateways SHOULD be designed for high availability. In addition, there SHOULD be two independent access options to the external network. Internal and external routers, as well as all other active components involved, SHOULD also be designed for high availability. Even after an automatic failover, the firewall structure SHOULD meet the requirements of the security policy. The function SHOULD be monitored using numerous parameters.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All firewall components are implemented as a cluster (Active/Passive or Active/Active). Two separate internet connections from different providers are used. The upstream routers and downstream core switches are also designed to be redundant (e.g., with VRRP/HSRP). The monitoring system checks the cluster status, the synchronization of configuration and sessions, and the reachability of both internet uplinks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the cluster systems and the redundant routing protocols. They have a controlled failover test demonstrated to them to verify the automatic switchover and the maintenance of connectivity. They check the monitoring configuration for the HA components.

controls.title: Bandwidth management for critical applications and services

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no explicit bandwidth management. All data traffic is treated equally (best-effort principle).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: High load from non-critical applications (e.g., large downloads, video streaming) can impair the performance of business-critical applications (e.g., VoIP, ERP system).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the firewall configuration for the absence of Quality of Service (QoS) or traffic shaping rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To ensure bandwidth management for critical applications and services, packet filters with a corresponding bandwidth management function SHOULD be used at network gateways and at the transition between different security zones.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Quality of Service (QoS) rules are configured on the firewall. Data traffic is classified (e.g., by application, source/destination IP, port). Critical traffic (e.g., VoIP) is assigned a high priority and a guaranteed bandwidth, while non-critical traffic (e.g., peer-to-peer) is limited or treated with lower priority.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the classification rules and the configured QoS policies on the firewall. They compare the configuration with the documentation of the critical applications and their bandwidth requirements.

controls.title: Use of certified products

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When procuring the firewall, products are selected that are established in the market and have a good reputation for security and stability. A formal certification is not a selection criterion.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The selection is based on analyst reports (e.g., Gartner), test results from trade magazines, and the administrators' experience.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the documentation of the procurement process and the basis for the decision.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Firewalls with a security evaluation according to Common Criteria SHOULD be used, at least with level EAL4.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the requirements catalog for procurement, a valid Common Criteria certification (at least EAL4 or a comparable protection profile-based approach) is defined as a mandatory requirement (must-have criterion). Only products that meet this requirement are shortlisted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests proof of the Common Criteria certification for the firewall product used. They verify the validity of the certificate and the evaluation assurance level (EAL) achieved on the website of the responsible certification body (e.g., the BSI).

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
A firewall is a system of software and hardware components that is used to securely connect IP-based data networks. For this purpose, a firewall structure is used to restrict the technically possible information flow to the communication previously defined as secure in a security policy. Secure in this context means that only the desired access or data streams are permitted between different networks.
To secure network perimeters, a single component is often no longer used, but a whole series of IT systems that perform different tasks, e.g. exclusively filtering packets or strictly separating network connections using proxy functions. The term "Application Level Gateway" (ALG) used in this module refers to a firewall component that regulates data streams on the basis of security proxies.
A firewall is used at the transition between networks with different levels of trustworthiness. Networks with different levels of trustworthiness do not necessarily only represent the combination of the Internet and an intranet. Rather, two internal networks of an institution can also have different levels of protection requirements. For example, the office communication network usually has a lower protection requirement than the network of the HR department, in which particularly sensitive personal data is transmitted.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The aim of this module is to be able to use a firewall or a firewall structure securely with the help of the requirements described in the following chapters in order to securely connect networks with different protection requirements.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The NET.3.2 Firewall module must be applied to every firewall used in the information network.
A typical application is securing an external connection, e.g. at the transition from an internal network to the Internet or for connections to networks of partner institutions. However, the module must also be applied when coupling two internal networks of an institution with different levels of protection requirements, e.g. when separating the office communication network from the network of the development department, if particularly confidential data is processed there.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS)
parts.prose: In the event of a DDoS attack on a protected network (e.g. TCP SYN Flooding, UDP Packet Storm), the firewall may fail due to the large number of network connections that need to be processed. This can result in certain services in the Local Area Network (LAN) no longer being available or the entire LAN failing.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Manipulation
parts.prose: If attackers manage to gain unauthorized access to a firewall or a corresponding management interface, they can manipulate files there at will. For example, they can change the configuration, start additional services or install malware. They can also intercept the communication connections on the manipulated IT system. It is also possible, for example, to change the firewall rules in such a way that the firewall and the institution's intranet can be accessed from the Internet. Furthermore, attackers can launch a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack by preventing access to individual server services in the rule set.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Bypassing firewall rules
parts.prose: Attackers can use fundamental mechanisms in the network protocols to bypass the firewall rules (e.g. through fragmentation attacks) in order to penetrate an area protected by the firewall. In the protected area, they can then cause further damage, e.g. read, manipulate, or delete sensitive data.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Incorrect configuration and operational errors of a firewall
parts.prose: An incorrectly configured or operated firewall can have a serious impact on the availability of services. If, for example, firewall rules are set incorrectly, network access can be blocked. Furthermore, incorrect configurations can result in IT systems no longer being fully protected or not being protected at all. In the worst case, this makes internal services accessible to attackers.

controls.title: Planning of VPN usage (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning for VPN use is ad-hoc and limited to individual, urgent use cases. There is no formal or documented planning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A team member quickly sets up VPN access for an external partner without anchoring it in an overall concept. The configuration is communicated via email.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews that there are no planning documents for VPN use and that setup is done on demand.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic, informal plan for VPN use. Responsibilities and user groups are roughly outlined but not formally defined or documented. The process for assigning rights is not standardized.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a wiki page that describes the basic idea of VPN use. New access is created on request in the IT team, but there is no formal approval process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the informal planning documents (e.g., wiki pages) and compares them with the actually configured VPN accesses to identify inconsistencies in the implementation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The introduction of a VPN MUST be planned carefully. The responsibilities for VPN operation MUST be defined. User groups and their permissions for the VPN MUST also be planned. Likewise, it MUST be defined how granted, modified, or revoked access permissions are to be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal VPN concept is created and approved. It names the VPN responsible person, defines user groups (e.g., 'Employees', 'External Developers') with associated access rights, and describes the process for requesting, changing, and revoking rights via a ticket system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the VPN planning document and checks whether the responsibilities, user groups, and processes defined in it have been established. Tickets for rights allocation are checked on a random basis to verify compliance with the documentation process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VPN plan is reviewed regularly, at least annually, and updated as needed. The process for managing access rights is formalized, handled via a central system (e.g., a ticket system with an approval workflow), and compliance is monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review process for the VPN concept is established in the ISMS. All access changes require approval from the supervisor in the ticket system. Regular reports on granted permissions are generated and reviewed by the VPN responsible person.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the protocols of the annual reviews of the VPN concept. In the ticket system, they check whether approval workflows for granting permissions are enforced. An automated comparison of the configuration with the approved rights could be performed using `diff vpn-config approved-rights.yml`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire planning and access management process for the VPN is integrated into an Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) system. The granting and revocation of permissions, as well as regular recertifications, are fully automated and based on the roles and status of users in the HR system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IGA tool is connected to the HR system and the VPN gateway. If an employee leaves the company, their VPN access is automatically blocked within hours. Managers must recertify their team members' VPN rights quarterly via an automated dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the IGA system and the connectors to the HR system and VPN gateway. They have the automated logs of rights recertifications and user deactivations shown to them to confirm the seamless automation.

controls.title: Selection of VPN service providers (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A VPN service provider is used on the basis of standard contractual terms and without formal Service Level Agreements (SLAs). There is no review of the provider's performance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For a short-term project, a cloud VPN provider is used by simply signing up for their standard subscription online. The terms and conditions are accepted without being read.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the contracts with the VPN service provider and finds that there are no specific SLAs, only standard terms and conditions, and that no performance monitoring is carried out.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If VPN service providers are used, Service Level Agreements (SLAs) MUST be negotiated and documented in writing with them. It MUST be regularly checked whether the VPN service providers are complying with the agreed SLAs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before signing the contract, specific SLAs on availability (e.g., 99.9%), maximum recovery time, and support response times are negotiated with the service provider. Compliance is monitored through monthly reports from the provider and our own random checks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the written, negotiated SLAs. They request the logs of the regular checks (e.g., monthly evaluation of the service provider reports, own measurement logs) for the last 12 months.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: SLA compliance is continuously monitored using automated tools. A formal process for escalating violations exists, including defined penalties.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An external monitoring tool pings the service provider's VPN endpoints every minute and measures latency. If the SLA thresholds are exceeded, a ticket is automatically created and the service provider is notified. The contract specifies financial credits for non-compliance with availability.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and logs of the automated monitoring tool. They check the contract for penalty clauses and compare the monitoring data with the service provider's invoices to determine if penalties have been correctly applied.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The SLA monitoring is fully integrated into the central SIEM system and correlates technical performance data with security-relevant events. The service provider audit process includes regular on-site inspections or the obligation to present recognized certifications (e.g., ISO 27001).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Failures in SLA monitoring trigger not only a technical but also a security ticket in the SIEM to investigate a possible attack. The contract obliges the service provider to provide an annual audit report by an independent third party.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the correlation rules in the SIEM that process SLA data. They review the audit reports and certificates of the service provider and check whether they meet the contractual requirements and are currently valid.

controls.title: Secure installation of VPN endpoints (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VPN components are installed by available personnel without specific qualifications. No formal acceptance tests or security checks are performed before commissioning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An intern installs the VPN software on a server following a short online guide. As soon as a connection can be established, the service is declared 'ready for operation'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interviews the personnel responsible for the installation and finds that there are no specific training courses or certifications for the VPN product. No records of acceptance tests can be provided.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If an appliance requiring maintenance is used, there MUST be a valid maintenance contract for it. It MUST be ensured that only qualified personnel install VPN components. The functionality and the selected security mechanisms of the VPN MUST be tested before commissioning. The installation of the VPN components and any deviations from the planning specifications SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 3-year maintenance contract is signed for the VPN appliance at the time of purchase. The installation is carried out by a certified technician from the manufacturer or a partner. Before release, a checklist is processed which checks, among other things, the correct function of two-factor authentication and the encryption strength. The technician creates an installation report.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the valid maintenance contract and the installation records (e.g., personnel certificates, installation report). They ask to see the completed commissioning checklist and randomly compare the settings documented there with the live configuration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Documentation of the installation and all deviations from the plan is mandatory. An independent team (e.g., the IT security team) verifies the performed commissioning tests before the system goes live (four-eyes principle).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each installation is documented in a standardized form, which is stored in the configuration management system (CMDB). After completion of the installation and tests by the administration team, an IT security officer checks the configuration and the test results and gives formal approval for operation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether standardized installation documents for all VPN components are available in the CMDB. They review the approval records and verify that they have been signed by a second, independent person.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation and configuration of VPN components are fully automated using Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and configuration management tools. All commissioning tests, including security scans, are integrated as automated tests into the deployment pipeline.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Ansible playbook or Terraform script is used to deploy a new VPN instance in the cloud or on a virtual machine. The script installs the software, loads the hardened configuration, and then automatically runs a port scan and a configuration compliance check. Only if all tests are successful is the instance added to the production cluster.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a code review of the IaC script (e.g., Ansible playbook) to assess the correctness of the installation and configuration steps. They analyze the logs of the CI/CD pipeline to verify that the automated security and functional tests have been successfully passed with each deployment.

controls.title: Secure configuration of a VPN (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VPN components are operated with the manufacturer's default settings. There is no defined or documented security configuration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After installing the VPN software, the 'Quick Start' wizard is run through without changing security-relevant presets such as weak encryption algorithms or default passwords.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the current configuration of a VPN component with the default configuration from the manufacturer's manual and determines that no hardening measures have been taken. Default passwords can be tested, for example, with `ssh admin@vpn-gateway` and the password 'admin'.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A secure configuration MUST be defined for all VPN components. This SHOULD be appropriately documented. The person responsible for administration MUST also regularly check whether the configuration is still secure and, if necessary, adapt it for all IT systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A configuration standard is created for the VPN, which specifies, among other things, strong ciphers (e.g., AES-256-GCM), secure key exchange methods, and the deactivation of insecure protocols. This standard is documented. The VPN administrator manually checks the configuration for deviations quarterly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the document with the configuration standard. They ask to see the logs of the regular manual checks and randomly compare the live configuration of a component with the standard.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration standards are mandatory and are managed in a versioning system (e.g., Git). The configuration is automatically checked for conformity using scripts or compliance tools, with deviations triggering a notification.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration templates are stored in a Git repository. A script that runs nightly connects to the VPN components, exports their configuration, and compares it with the approved template from the repository. Differences are reported to the security team via email.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration compliance script. They ask to see the alert logs from the last few months and check how reported deviations were responded to. An automated test could be: `run-compliance-check.sh --target vpn-gateway-01`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the VPN components is managed entirely via a configuration management system (e.g., Ansible, Puppet) (Configuration as Code). Any deviation from the defined target state is automatically detected and immediately corrected (self-healing).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Ansible server is responsible for enforcing the state of all VPN components. If an administrator manually changes a setting on a gateway, this change is automatically reverted to the value defined in the Git repository during the next run of the Ansible playbook (e.g., every 15 minutes).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the configuration management tool and its associated code repositories. They can make an intentional, unauthorized change to a test component and observe whether it is automatically corrected as expected by monitoring the tool's logs in real time.

controls.title: Deactivation of unneeded VPN access (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VPN access is only deactivated upon manual request. There are no regular reviews or time limits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A VPN account for an external service provider remains active even after the project ends, until someone notices that it is no longer needed and asks IT to delete it.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests a list of all active VPN accounts and compares it with the current employee and service provider list. They identify accounts of former employees that are still active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be checked regularly whether only authorized IT systems and users can access the VPN. VPN access that is no longer needed MUST be deactivated promptly. VPN access MUST be restricted to the required usage times.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Semiannually, a list of all VPN accounts is sent to the department heads for review and confirmation. Accounts of former employees are immediately blocked as part of the offboarding process. For administrative access, access is restricted to core working hours (Mon-Fri, 8 a.m. - 6 p.m.).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks to see the logs of the last two semi-annual access reviews, including the confirmations from the departments. They check the VPN configuration for the implementation of the time-based access restrictions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The access rights review process is semi-automated by automatically generating reports on inactive accounts (e.g., no login in 90 days) and proposing them for deactivation. The time restrictions are defined granularly per user group or role.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A script analyzes the VPN logs weekly and creates a list of accounts that have not been used for over 90 days. This list is automatically created as a ticket for review and, if necessary, deactivation. In the VPN profile of the 'Developer' group, access is set to 7 a.m. - 10 p.m., while the 'Accounting' group only has access from 8 a.m. - 5 p.m.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the script for detecting inactive accounts and the resulting tickets. They check the configuration of the VPN user groups for the correct implementation of the granular time restrictions. A test could be: `vpn-log-parser --inactive-days 90`.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The lifecycle of VPN access is fully automated and linked to the central HR system and IGA system. Accounts are automatically and immediately disabled when an employee leaves. Access rights are granted dynamically and just-in-time based on attributes (ABAC) for the duration of the required session.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When the HR department sets an employee's status to 'terminated' in the HR system, the corresponding VPN account is immediately disabled via an API interface of the IGA tool. External service providers only receive access if an active ticket exists for them in the system, and only to the resource specified in the ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the configuration of the automated workflows between HR, IGA, and VPN systems. They can simulate the offboarding process of a test user and check in real time whether the VPN account is disabled as expected by monitoring the system logs.

controls.title: Conducting a VPN requirements analysis (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A requirements analysis MUST be performed to determine the use cases for the respective VPN and to derive the requirements for the necessary hardware and software components. The following points MUST be considered in the requirements analysis: business processes or tasks, access paths, identification and authentication procedures, users and their permissions, responsibilities, and reporting channels.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before selecting a VPN solution, workshops are held with the relevant business departments (e.g., sales, development) to gather their requirements. The results are recorded in a requirements document that details the use cases (e.g., 'field sales representative accesses CRM', 'developer needs access to test systems'), the required bandwidth, and the security requirements (e.g., 'two-factor authentication is mandatory').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the requirements document for the VPN and checks whether all required aspects (business processes, access paths, etc.) are covered. They conduct interviews with stakeholders to verify that their requirements are correctly reflected in the document.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirements analysis is a formal, documented process that is repeated with every significant change to the network or business processes. The results are formally approved and signed by the process owners and IT security.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements document is versioned and, after finalization, signed by the heads of the participating departments and the CISO. When a new ERP system is introduced, the requirements analysis process is repeated to assess the impact on the VPN and adapt the concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the versioned requirements documents and the corresponding signed approval records. They check the change management logs for significant changes and verify whether an update of the VPN requirements analysis has subsequently taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirements analysis is part of a continuous service design process and is integrated into Enterprise Architecture Management (EAM). The gathered requirements dynamically inform the configuration of the VPN via policy engines to ensure continuous alignment with business requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The business processes and their remote access requirements are modeled in the EAM tool. a change in the model (e.g., a new process requires access to a specific application) triggers an automated workflow that proposes a corresponding adjustment to the VPN policy, which is automatically rolled out after approval.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the models in the EAM tool and the configuration of the policy engine. They trace a requirements change process from modeling in the EAM tool to the automated adjustment of the VPN configuration to verify end-to-end integration.

controls.title: Planning the technical VPN implementation (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The technical aspects of a VPN MUST be carefully planned. Thus, the encryption methods, VPN endpoints, permitted access protocols, services, and resources MUST be defined for the VPN. In addition, the subnets that are reachable via the VPN MUST be defined.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A technical concept is created based on the requirements analysis (A6). It specifies: encryption with IPsec (IKEv2), VPN gateway on the central firewall, permitted protocols are HTTPS and RDP, access only to the server VLAN, but not to the client VLAN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the technical VPN concept. They review the configuration of the VPN gateway and the firewall rules and compare them with the specifications in the concept to verify the correct implementation of the defined protocols, resources, and subnets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The technical plan includes redundancy and failover scenarios as well as performance considerations. The selection of cryptographic methods is mandatorily based on the institution's central crypto concept (in accordance with CON.1).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The technical concept describes a high-availability VPN cluster with two gateways at different locations. The selection of ciphers and key lengths is directly derived from and justified by the overarching crypto concept. It includes capacity planning for 500 concurrent users.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the technical concept for the description of redundancy and capacity planning. They compare the cryptographic methods specified in the concept with the requirements of the central crypto concept and check their correct implementation on the gateways.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The technical planning is implemented as an automated deployment blueprint (Infrastructure as Code). Network segmentation is performed dynamically (micro-segmentation) based on the identity and context of the user and endpoint device (Zero Trust approach).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Instead of a text document, the technical plan consists of a set of Terraform scripts and Ansible playbooks. Depending on the user role and the state of the endpoint device (e.g., patch level, enabled disk encryption), only the firewall rules for the exactly required applications are dynamically enabled upon connection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts a review of the IaC code. They test the dynamic segmentation by logging in with different user roles and from endpoints with different security statuses (e.g., a compliant and a non-compliant device) and check whether network access is dynamically restricted as expected.

controls.title: Creation of a security policy for VPN usage (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a simple user guide for the VPN that mentions basic security-related aspects (e.g., 'keep password secret'), but it does not constitute a formal, mandatory policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT department provides a PDF document 'VPN Guide' that explains the client installation and includes a sentence at the end such as 'Please handle your access credentials with care'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the provided guides and determines that no formal security policy exists that must be acknowledged by users.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A security policy for VPN use MUST be created. This MUST be communicated to all employees. The security measures described in the security policy MUST be explained in training sessions. When a VPN access is set up for employees, a leaflet with the most important VPN security mechanisms MUST be handed out to them. All VPN users MUST be required to comply with the security policies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'Policy for Secure VPN Use' is created, covering topics such as the obligation to use on secure devices and in trusted networks. Every new VPN user must attend a short training session and sign the policy. In addition, a one-page leaflet ('VPN Rules at a Glance') is issued.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the VPN security policy, the leaflet, and the training materials. They ask to be shown the signed commitment declarations from a sample of users.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the policy is promoted through regular awareness measures (e.g., phishing tests, short online quizzes). The policy is reviewed at least annually and, if necessary, updated and re-communicated to all users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A security awareness campaign is conducted annually, which also includes a module on secure VPN use. The results are evaluated to identify training needs. The policy is reviewed and updated as part of the annual ISMS review.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the materials and result reports of the awareness campaigns. They check the revision history of the VPN policy and the logs for a communication of the last update to the employees.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training sessions on the policy are interactive and role-based. Acknowledgment of receipt is recorded digitally and in an audit-proof manner. Key requirements of the policy, such as the prohibition of use on insecure devices, are enforced by technical measures (endpoint security check) upon connection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before the first VPN use, every employee must complete an e-learning module that concludes with a test. The confirmation is stored in the training management system. The VPN client checks for an up-to-date antivirus scanner and an activated firewall on the endpoint before establishing a connection. If this is not the case, the connection is denied.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the e-learning system and the digital proofs of employee training. They test the connection setup from a non-compliant test device and verify that the connection is blocked as expected. This can be done by evaluating the VPN gateway logs and the endpoint check configuration.

controls.title: Suitable selection of VPN products (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The product selection is based on a few basic functional requirements such as 'supports mobile clients' or 'can do site-to-site'.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT team selects a well-known open-source VPN solution because it is considered flexible and supports mobile clients, without conducting a detailed comparison with other commercial or open-source products.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines in interviews that the product selection was based on general assumptions and not on a structured analysis of the specific institutional requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When selecting VPN products, the institutions' requirements for networking different sites and connecting mobile employees or teleworking stations MUST be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Based on the requirements analysis (A6), a catalog of requirements for the VPN product is created. This includes criteria such as the maximum number of concurrent tunnels, support for site-to-site and remote access scenarios, and compatibility with the authentication systems in use. Three products are evaluated against this catalog.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the requirements catalog and the product evaluation documentation. They check whether the selection decision is traceably based on the results of the evaluation and the requirements from the requirements analysis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As part of the product selection, a formal evaluation (Proof of Concept, PoC) of the top candidates is conducted in a test environment. Product security certifications (e.g., according to Common Criteria) are a key selection criterion.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The two best products from the pre-selection are installed for a four-week PoC in an isolated test environment. A group of test users checks the functionality and usability. IT security checks the configuration options and hardenability. Only products with a valid BSI certification or comparable are shortlisted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the PoC documentation, including the test plan, test results, and final report. They check whether the requirement for security certificates was considered and proven in the selection process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The product selection is part of a strategic technology roadmap and is based on modern security architectures. The selected solution supports native concepts for Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA), is highly scalable, and can be fully automated via APIs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The choice falls on a modern ZTNA/SASE solution as it strategically aligns better with the planned cloud migration and the 'Work-from-Anywhere' approach than a classic VPN appliance. A crucial criterion is the existence of a well-documented REST API for complete integration into existing automation tools.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the selection decision with the documented IT strategy and technology roadmap. They ask to see the API documentation and perform spot checks to see whether the automation scenarios (e.g., user provisioning via API) have been implemented as planned or are implementable.

controls.title: Secure operation of a VPN (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a simple operating manual or checklist that focuses on basic tasks such as applying patches and checking system availability.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a wiki page for VPN operation that says: 'Check for and install updates monthly' and 'Check daily if the gateway is online'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the operating manual and compares it with the system logs to determine whether the few defined tasks (e.g., patching) are performed regularly.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An operating concept MUST be created for VPNs. The aspects of quality management, monitoring, maintenance, training, and authorization MUST be considered therein.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal VPN operating concept is created. It describes: How performance is monitored (quality management), which events are logged and analyzed (monitoring), the process for patch and change management (maintenance), how new administrators are onboarded (training), and the process for approving configuration changes (authorization).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the operating concept and checks whether all required aspects are covered in it. Using system logs, tickets, and training records, they perform spot checks to verify that the processes described in the concept are being followed in practice.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operating concept contains defined Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for security and availability. The monitoring is proactive and generates alerts for anomalies in user behavior or performance bottlenecks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The operating concept defines KPIs such as 'maximum CPU load < 80%' and 'no successful logins from blocked IP addresses'. The monitoring system alerts the team if the CPU load exceeds 80% or if a user attempts to log in from two different continents within 30 minutes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the operating concept for the definition of KPIs. They analyze the configuration of the monitoring system for the implementation of proactive alerting rules and check the handling of the generated alerts in the ticket system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The operation is highly automated, including automated patching and configuration management. A dedicated team or role is responsible for the continuous improvement of the VPN service (CSI). The operating concept is reviewed and adapted at least quarterly based on operational data and new threat information.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Security patches for the VPN system are automatically rolled out and tested in a test environment. If successful, the rollout in production occurs automatically in the next maintenance window. The VPN team meets monthly to discuss operational KPIs, user feedback, and current security warnings and to derive improvement measures from them.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the automation tools for patching and configuration management. They review the minutes of the CSI meetings and check whether the measures decided there have been tracked and implemented. They verify the revision history of the operating concept for regular updates.

controls.title: Secure connection of an external network (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VPN connections from external networks are restricted to a specific subnet, but without further restriction to specific services or ports.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An external service provider is granted VPN access to the entire development network (10.1.2.0/24) so that they can 'reach all necessary servers'. There is no restriction to, e.g., only the RDP port of the specific server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules for external VPN access and finds that access is granted to an entire subnet with 'any' as the service/port, instead of restricting access to the actually needed systems and services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be ensured that VPN connections are established ONLY between the intended IT systems and services. The tunnel protocols used MUST be suitable for the purpose.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The firewall rules for an external service provider's VPN access are configured according to the least-privilege principle. Only access from their fixed source IP to the IP address of the server to be maintained on TCP port 3389 (RDP) is permitted. IPsec with IKEv2 and strong, current algorithms is used as the tunnel protocol.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the firewall rules and verifies that they restrict access to the specifically approved systems and services. They check the configuration of the VPN tunnel for the use of protocols and algorithms classified as secure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The firewall rules for VPN connections are regularly reviewed for their necessity and correctness, at least semi-annually. The selection of tunnel protocols is enforced by the central crypto concept and their configuration is automatically checked for compliance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A firewall rule review takes place every six months, during which the responsible technician must confirm in writing the necessity of each rule for external VPN access. A compliance script checks weekly whether all active VPN tunnels use the ciphers prescribed in the crypto concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the minutes of the semi-annual firewall rule reviews. They analyze the compliance script for the tunnel protocols and its execution logs to verify the continuous verification.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Micro-segmentation is implemented. Access from external networks is dynamically granted per session and per application based on user and device context (Zero Trust Network Access). The security of the tunnel protocols is continuously monitored for new vulnerabilities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A ZTNA solution is used. When an external user requests a connection, their device is checked for compliance. Then, a direct, encrypted tunnel to the specifically requested application is established only for the duration of the session, without granting the user access to the rest of the network. A subscription-based threat intelligence feed informs about new vulnerabilities in the used VPN protocols.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the ZTNA solution and the dynamic access policies. They test access with different user contexts and from different device states to verify the correct functioning of the micro-segmentation. They check the process for processing threat intelligence information.

controls.title: Account and access management for remote access VPNs (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VPN user accounts are managed locally on the VPN appliance. There is no central directory, and shared accounts are used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Local users 'developer', 'sales', and 'guest' are created on the VPN gateway, with passwords shared with the respective teams.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the user database on the VPN gateway and finds that local, non-personalized accounts are used, which makes traceability of actions impossible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Central and consistent account and access management MUST be guaranteed for remote access VPNs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The VPN gateway is connected to the central Active Directory (AD). Authentication is done via the users' personalized AD accounts. Access is controlled by membership in specific AD groups (e.g., 'VPN-Users').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the VPN gateway configuration to ensure that it is connected to a central directory for authentication. They check the configuration of the access groups in the directory service and ensure that no local users are configured on the gateway.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) model is implemented for VPN access. Different roles get access to different resources. The permissions are reviewed regularly as part of a recertification process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In Active Directory, there are the groups 'VPN-Sales' and 'VPN-Dev'. Members of 'VPN-Sales' get VPN access only to the CRM system, while members of 'VPN-Dev' can access the development environment. The membership in these groups is reviewed and confirmed semi-annually by the department heads.
