parts.prose: The principle of least privilege (need-to-know) is applied. By default, all functions not explicitly requested are deactivated. Critical functions such as 'baby monitor', 'call intrusion' or external call forwarding are specifically switched off or only enabled for authorized users.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the PBX system shown to them and compares the list of active features with the needs defined in the requirements analysis. In particular, it is checked whether known critical functions are deactivated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal positive and negative list of features is maintained, based on a documented risk assessment. The PBX system configuration is regularly audited (e.g., semi-annually) against this list to identify and correct deviations. The configuration is documented in a hardened baseline.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A table lists all available features, assesses their risk, and documents the decision (allowed, prohibited, only for certain roles). Regular configuration reviews are carried out and documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the list of evaluated features and the corresponding risk assessment. The logs of the regular configuration audits are inspected and the live configuration is compared with the baseline on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the features is managed via an automated configuration management tool. This continuously monitors the configuration of the PBX system and automatically resets any unauthorized change or activation of a non-approved feature to the defined, hardened state. Any deviation triggers an alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A tool like Ansible or a manufacturer's own management system is used to define the configuration as 'code'. A monitoring script runs at short intervals to compare the live configuration with the target state and to intervene correctively if necessary.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration templates and the scripts of the automation tool. A test case is generated (e.g., manual activation of a blocked feature) to verify that the system automatically detects and resets the change. The alerting is also checked.

controls.title: Training on the secure use of PBX systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: New employees receive a brief, verbal instruction on how to operate their telephone. A printed quick start guide from the manufacturer is available.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the onboarding process, a colleague shows the new employee the basic functions of the telephone. There are no specific training sessions on security aspects.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks new employees about the instruction they received and checks whether basic manuals are available.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The users of the PBX system SHOULD be instructed in the correct use of services and devices. The users of the PBX system SHOULD be provided with all necessary documents for operating the corresponding end devices. All conspicuous features and irregularities of the PBX system SHOULD be reported to the responsible persons.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standardized briefing is carried out for all employees, which is also available online as a reference. The briefing includes a reference to the reporting channel for problems or suspicious incidents (e.g. helpdesk ticket).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of standardized training materials and the availability of operating instructions. It is checked whether the reporting channel for incidents is clearly communicated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training is mandatory for all employees and is documented. It explicitly covers security-relevant aspects, such as handling confidential information on the phone, recognizing social engineering attacks (vishing), and the risks of functions such as call forwarding or conference calls. The training content is updated regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The training is part of the annual, mandatory security awareness program. Attendance is tracked. Concrete examples of vishing calls are discussed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the training materials and checks their content for the aforementioned security aspects. The attendance lists are checked to verify mandatory participation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The training sessions are role-based and are supplemented by regular awareness campaigns, including simulated vishing attacks. The results of these simulations feed directly into the improvement of the training content. An easily searchable knowledge base with instructions and security tips is available to all users.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees in the secretariat receive a different, more intensive training than employees in development. Test calls are regularly carried out by an external service provider. The click or success rates are evaluated anonymously.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is shown the concept of the role-based training and the plans for the awareness campaigns. The anonymized evaluations of the simulated vishing attacks and the resulting adjustments to the training content are reviewed.

controls.title: Documentation and revision of the PBX system configuration

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The initial configuration of the PBX system is documented during commissioning. However, this document is not systematically updated when subsequent changes are made.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The technician who installed the system left a handover protocol with the basic settings. Minor changes during operation are not subsequently documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the configuration documentation and compares it with the current configuration of the system. If significant deviations are found, this indicates that the documentation is outdated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The PBX system configuration SHOULD be suitably documented and updated. The PBX system configuration SHOULD be reviewed at regular intervals. The result of the review SHOULD be presented at least to the information security officer, the subject matter expert, and other responsible employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central configuration documentation is maintained, which is updated after every change. A review of the configuration is carried out at least once a year, during which the documentation is compared with the live system and checked for compliance with the guidelines. The result is logged and distributed to the mentioned roles.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the configuration documentation and the logs of the last configuration reviews. It is checked whether the reviews take place regularly and whether the results have been presented to the responsible persons.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration documentation is managed in a versioning system (e.g. Git, SVN) so that all changes are traceable. Every change to the configuration must follow a formal change management process that requires approval. The results of the reviews are tracked in a ticket system to ensure that identified deficiencies are rectified.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The configuration files are stored in a Git repository. Changes require a pull request that must be approved by a second person. Deviations found during the review lead to the creation of a JIRA ticket, which is assigned to the responsible administrator.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the history in the versioning system and the corresponding tickets in the change management system to trace the process on a sample basis. The handling of findings resulting from the revisions is checked in the ticketing system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the PBX system is treated entirely as 'Configuration as Code'. The documentation is the code itself. Automated tools continuously check the live configuration against the target state defined in the code. Any deviation (configuration drift) is reported in real time and can optionally be corrected automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ansible playbooks or similar declarative configuration tools define the entire state of the PBX system. A CI/CD system deploys the changes. A monitoring system like Prometheus with a specialized exporter reads the configuration and compares it with the baseline.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor audits the 'Configuration as Code' workflow, including code reviews and the CI/CD pipeline. The configuration and functionality of the automated monitoring and alerting system are analyzed. It is checked how reported configuration drifts are responded to.

controls.title: Decommissioning of PBX systems and devices

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before disposing of PBX systems or terminal devices, an attempt is made to reset the devices to factory settings in order to delete stored data such as phone books or call lists.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The administrator executes the 'Factory Reset' function in the device's menu before handing it over to the disposal company. Verification of successful deletion does not take place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor questions the responsible parties about the decommissioning process and checks whether resetting to factory settings is a known and implemented step.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The decommissioning of PBX systems and connected PBX devices SHOULD be considered in the security policy. All data stored on PBX systems or terminal devices SHOULD be securely deleted before decommissioning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a documented decommissioning process. This stipulates that all configuration data, answering machine messages, phone books, and other stored information must be removed using a secure deletion method (e.g., multiple overwriting or cryptographic erasure).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that the security policy or a process document mandates the secure deletion of data upon decommissioning. It is checked whether the responsible parties are familiar with this process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The decommissioning process is formalized and documented for each device. Secure data deletion is carried out according to a recognized standard (e.g., BSI TL-03420, NIST SP 800-88). Proof of deletion or destruction (deletion certificate, certificate of destruction) is created and archived by an internal responsible person or an external service provider.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A decommissioning form is completed for each retired device, documenting the deletion method used and the result. For external disposal, a certified service provider is commissioned who issues a certificate of destruction.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly requests the decommissioning documentation and the corresponding deletion or destruction certificates for recently decommissioned devices and checks them for completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The decommissioning process is fully integrated into the asset management system. For devices that have processed highly sensitive data, physical destruction of the non-volatile storage media (e.g., by a shredder) is mandatory. The entire process, from the decision to decommission to the confirmed destruction, is tracked seamlessly in the asset management system and is a regular subject of internal audits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When a device is set to 'retired' in asset management, a workflow for secure deletion or destruction is automatically triggered. An internal or external service provider shreds the hard drives or flash storage of the devices on-site. The successful completion of the workflow is noted in the asset record.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor tracks the lifecycle of a device in the asset management system from operation to certified destruction. It is checked whether the classification of the device correctly led to the prescribed disposal method (deletion vs. destruction) and whether the process is audited.

controls.title: Backup of configuration files

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Regular, automated backups of the PBX system's configuration files are performed. The backups are stored locally or on a network drive, but recovery tests do not take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A weekly cron job or scheduled task exports the system's configuration to a file on an internal file server. The success of the backup job is not systematically monitored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration of the backup job shown to them and checks the existence and age of the backup files. Evidence of performed recovery tests is requested; its absence indicates this level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration and application data of the PBX system used SHOULD be backed up during initial setup and regularly thereafter, especially after changes have been made. It SHOULD be regularly checked and documented whether the backups of the PBX systems can actually be used as a basis for a system recovery. A data backup concept for PBX systems SHOULD be created and coordinated with the general concepts of data backup.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specific data backup concept for the PBX system is created. It defines backup frequency, retention periods, and the process for recovery tests. A test is conducted at least annually, in which the configuration from the backup is restored to a test system or the production system. The test is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the data backup concept for the PBX system. The logs of the performed recovery tests are reviewed and checked for their regularity and completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The backups of the configuration files are automated, encrypted, and stored according to the 3-2-1 rule (three copies, two different media, one copy off-site/offline). The recovery tests are conducted at least semi-annually, and the results are used to optimize the recovery process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The backup software encrypts the backup files before transferring them to an external storage location (e.g., cloud storage or another data center). The recovery test is a fixed item in the IT department's annual plan, and the time measured (RTO) is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the encryption of the backups and compliance with the 3-2-1 rule by inspecting the configuration of the backup solution and the storage locations. The logs of the semi-annual recovery tests are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The backup and recovery processes are fully automated and integrated into the organization's central emergency management. Recovery Point Objectives (RPO) and Recovery Time Objectives (RTO) are clearly defined, and their compliance is verified through regular, automated tests. The integrity of the backups is continuously ensured through automated checksum checks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A disaster recovery tool orchestrates the entire recovery process. A script checks the integrity of the last backup daily. The RTO/RPO values are stored in the emergency manual and are measured and compared with the specifications during tests.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the emergency manual and the RTO/RPO values defined therein. The configuration and logs of the automated recovery and integrity tests are checked. It is verified whether the measured values comply with the specifications.

controls.title: Procurement of PBX systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The procurement of the PBX system is based on a basic list of functional requirements, such as the number of ports and support for standard telephony functions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple list of bullet points ('need 50 phones', 'must support conference calls') serves as the basis for the inquiry with a provider.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks to see the procurement documents and checks whether they are based on a basic, documented list of requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When procuring PBX systems, the results of the requirements analysis and planning (according to NET.4.1.A1) SHOULD be included. When procuring a PBX system, it SHOULD be noted that it should offer analog subscriber lines in addition to digital ones. Furthermore, existing communication systems and components SHOULD be taken into account during procurement.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The procurement process starts with the formal requirements document. In this document, the need for analog connections (e.g., for fax machines or emergency phones) and compatibility with existing systems (e.g., DECT base stations) is explicitly checked and recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the ordered hardware/software with the specifications recorded in the requirements document (NET.4.1.A1). It is checked whether the aspects 'analog connections' and 'compatibility' were demonstrably assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The procurement process includes a mandatory checklist of security requirements that a potential product must meet. These include, for example, support for specific encryption protocols (SRTP, TLS 1.2+), role-based access control, and hardened factory settings. Bids that do not meet these requirements are excluded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'Request for Proposal' (RFP) contains a mandatory appendix 'Security Requirements'. The providers' responses are systematically evaluated based on these criteria.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the tender documents and checks the appendix with the security requirements. It is checked whether the evaluation of the bids was demonstrably based on these criteria.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The procurement decision is based on a comprehensive risk assessment of the product and the manufacturer (Supply Chain Risk). The manufacturer must prove that they practice a secure software development lifecycle (Secure SDLC). Proof can be provided through recognized certifications (e.g., Common Criteria, BSZ certification) or audits.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the tender, providers must complete a self-assessment on the Secure SDLC or submit corresponding certificates. The results are incorporated into the purchase decision with a high weighting. The long-term patch supply by the manufacturer is contractually guaranteed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the risk assessment conducted for the provider/product. Submitted certificates and evidence of the development process are checked for their validity and relevance. It is verified that this assessment significantly influenced the procurement decision.

controls.title: Emergency preparedness for PBX systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The contact details of the manufacturer's support or the responsible service provider are documented and accessible to the administrators. Basic spare parts for known failure components (e.g., power supplies) could be kept on hand.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A note with the support hotline number is taped to the server cabinet. A spare power supply unit for the PBX system is stored in the warehouse.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the documented support contact details and inquires about the availability of basic spare parts.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An emergency plan for the PBX system SHOULD be created. This SHOULD be integrated into the institution's overall emergency concept. Emergency drills related to the PBX systems SHOULD be conducted regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A specific recovery plan for the PBX system is created. It is part of the overarching IT emergency manual. A recovery exercise is conducted once a year (which can be combined with the backup test NET.4.1.A12) to test the plan. The exercise and its results are documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the emergency plan for the PBX system and checks its integration into the overall concept. The logs of the emergency drills conducted are inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency plan contains detailed step-by-step instructions for various failure scenarios (e.g., power outage, hardware defect, software error). It defines clear roles and responsibilities as well as a communication plan. Theoretical emergency drills (tabletop exercises) are conducted with all involved persons at least once a year.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The plan includes checklists for the restart. In the annual exercise, a scenario is simulated and the reactions of the participants according to the plan are logged and subsequently discussed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the level of detail of the emergency plan and checks whether roles and communication channels are clearly defined. The logs of the tabletop exercises are inspected to verify the participation and the discussion of the results.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Emergency preparedness is based on a Business Impact Analysis (BIA) that defines clear recovery time and recovery point objectives (RTO/RPO) for the PBX services. A redundant system (e.g., hot/warm standby) exists to which a switchover can be made in an emergency. The functionality of the switchover and compliance with the RTO/RPO specifications are validated by regular practical failover tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A second, identical PBX system is available at another location and the configuration is continuously synchronized. Twice a year, the entire telephony operation is switched to the redundant system for a few hours to test the process under real conditions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the BIA and compares the RTO/RPO values defined therein with the technical capabilities of the redundant system. The logs of the practical failover tests are analyzed to verify compliance with the time specifications and the success of the tests.

controls.title: Emergency calls in the event of a PBX system failure

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an awareness of the problem that no emergency calls can be made in the event of a (VoIP) PBX system failure. It is trusted that employees will use their private mobile phones. Notices with emergency numbers are posted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: During security briefings, it is pointed out that in an emergency, one's own mobile phone should be used. There is no technical backup solution.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks those responsible about the solution for emergency calls in the event of a system failure. If private mobile phones are referred to and there is no technical provision, this level has been reached.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be ensured that emergency calls can be made from the institution even if the PBX system fails. The emergency call facilities SHOULD be reachable from all rooms within a sufficiently short distance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A concept is developed to ensure emergency call capability. This can be done by providing dedicated emergency phones or by maintaining a few analog telephone lines (POTS) that are independent of the main PBX system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the concept for ensuring emergency call capability. It is checked whether the solution described therein is plausible and guarantees accessibility from all relevant areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A technical backup solution is implemented. Emergency phones independent of the main PBX system are installed at strategically important points (e.g., per floor, in entrance areas). These are clearly marked as such. Their functionality is checked regularly, e.g., monthly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A red telephone connected directly to an analog trunk line is installed on each floor next to the elevator. Once a month, an employee picks up the receiver to check for a dial tone. The test is documented in a checklist.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly inspects the installed emergency phones and checks their labeling. The checklists of the regular functional tests are reviewed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The PBX system has a fully automatic and redundant emergency call functionality. If the primary connection (e.g., IP connection) fails, it automatically and seamlessly switches to an alternative path (e.g., PSTN gateway, cellular gateway). The functionality of this failover mechanism is regularly tested and monitored automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The VoIP system is equipped with a PSTN and a GSM gateway. The system continuously monitors the availability of the SIP trunk. In the event of a failure, it automatically routes emergency calls (911/112) via one of the alternative paths. A nightly test call to a control number verifies the function.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the failover routing for emergency calls in the PBX system. The logs of the automated tests are checked. If possible, a manual test is performed by simulating a connection failure.

controls.title: Securing of end devices in freely accessible rooms

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In freely accessible areas, only simple telephone models without advanced functions such as large displays or extended memory are deliberately used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For the reception area or the parking garage, the cheapest and simplest telephone model from the manufacturer's portfolio is procured and installed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the telephones in public areas and compares the model with the standard office telephones. A significantly simpler model indicates this level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The range of functions of the end devices to be installed in freely accessible rooms SHOULD be restricted. If this is not possible, the end device SHOULD be protected against unauthorized access in a suitable manner.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A special configuration profile is created on the central PBX system for telephones in public areas. This profile deactivates functions such as call lists, phone books, call forwarding, and the ability to call external or premium-rate numbers. Alternatively, the telephone is physically secured with a steel cable.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the configuration profile for public telephones shown to them or checks the configuration directly on the device. It is checked whether critical functions are deactivated or whether alternative protective measures (physical security) have been taken.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For telephones in public areas, a centrally managed, hardened configuration template is used that cannot be changed locally on the device. This template only allows calls to a predefined, restricted selection of internal numbers and to emergency numbers. Physical access to the connection cable and the network port is prevented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The telephone receives a locked profile via provisioning. Outgoing calls are restricted to the bare essentials by a Class of Service (CoS) on the PBX system. The connection socket is housed in a lockable enclosure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the central configuration of the hardened template and the Class of Service. An attempt is made to call a non-permitted number. The physical security of the cabling is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the measures from level 4, the telephone is mounted in a physically robust, lockable housing. The network port to which the telephone is connected is assigned to a highly segmented VLAN that blocks all communication at the network level except for the permitted telephony (e.g., to the provisioning server and SIP server). Any manipulation attempts on the device or the network connection are monitored and trigger an alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The telephone is mounted in a sheet steel wall housing. The firewall rules for the associated VLAN are extremely restrictive (Default Deny). The switch port security reports if another device is connected to the port.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the VLAN configuration and the associated firewall rules. The physical robustness of the housing is assessed. The configuration of the port security and the alerting in case of violations are checked.

controls.title: Maintenance of PBX systems

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The default password for administrative access to the PBX system has been changed. A single, shared password is used for all administrators.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A new administrator password was set during commissioning. This password is known to all members of the IT team.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the password management process for the PBX system. If it is confirmed that the default password has been changed, but a shared password is used, this level is reached.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The devices for maintenance and configuration of the PBX system SHOULD be secured with passwords or PINs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each administrator receives a personal account with an individual, complex password for access to the management interface of the PBX system. Shared accounts are not used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the user management of the PBX system shown to them and verifies that a personal account exists for each administrator and that no obviously shared accounts (e.g., 'admin', 'support') are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Administrative access to the PBX system is protected by multi-factor authentication (MFA). Role-based access control (RBAC) is used to restrict administrators' permissions to the minimum necessary for their tasks. Remote maintenance access is only permitted via a secure connection, e.g., a VPN with MFA.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the password, a one-time password (TOTP) is required for logging into the system's web interface. There are different administrator roles, e.g., 'User-Admin' (can only create users) and 'System-Admin' (can do everything). Remote access is only possible from the IT department's management VPN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of MFA and RBAC in the PBX system. The network firewall rules are checked to ensure that remote access is restricted to the VPN.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All administrative access is via a Privileged Access Management (PAM) solution. Administrators do not have permanent passwords; access is granted just-in-time for a specific task. All administrative sessions are recorded (Session Recording) and all commands executed are logged and audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An administrator requests access to the PBX system via a PAM solution (e.g., CyberArk, Teleport). After approval, a temporary session is established via a proxy. The PAM solution records a video of the session and saves all entered commands in an audit-proof log.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the PAM solution and the workflow for privileged access. Samples of session recordings and command logs are reviewed to verify complete monitoring.

controls.title: Increased access protection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The PBX system is housed in a separate, lockable room. Access is restricted to a named group of IT staff. External persons, such as maintenance technicians, are only granted access when accompanied by an authorized person.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A small technical room is used exclusively for the PBX system. Only the PBX administrators have a key. For maintenance work, the technician is accompanied by the administrator on duty.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the list of authorized persons and checks the regulation for external access. The installation site is inspected to verify that it is housed separately and can be locked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The room in which the PBX system is housed meets the requirements of a certified security room (e.g., according to a specific resistance class). Access is controlled and logged via an electronic access control system (ACS). The obligation to accompany external persons is formally defined in a policy and its compliance is checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The room has a class RC2 security door. Access requires a chip card. The ACS logs are checked monthly for anomalies. There is a visitor logbook in which the external technician and their escort must sign.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the specifications of the security room and the configuration of the ACS. The access logs and the visitor logbook are checked on a random basis to verify compliance with the escort obligation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The PBX system SHOULD be housed in a separate and suitably secured room. Access to the PBX system SHOULD only be possible for a restricted group of people. External persons SHOULD only be granted supervised access to the system. Access to the room requires multi-factor authentication (e.g., chip card + PIN or biometrics). Video surveillance is installed at the entrance. The access logs are automatically analyzed, and an alarm is triggered in case of anomalies (e.g., access outside of business hours).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: To gain access, a chip card must be held up to the reader and a PIN must also be entered. A camera records all persons entering the room. The ACS is coupled with the SIEM system, which generates alarms if an access attempt is made at night or on the weekend.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the implementation of MFA on the access system. The configuration of the video surveillance and the alerting rules in the SIEM are analyzed. It is checked how triggered alarms were responded to.

controls.title: Redundant Connection

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A second, independent connection for the PBX system is ordered and provided to create basic redundancy. For an IP-based system, a PSTN connection is also established. The switchover in the event of a failure is carried out manually by an administrator.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In addition to the primary SIP trunk, a basic rate ISDN (PSTN) connection is ordered and connected to the corresponding gateway of the PBX system. The emergency plan describes how an administrator manually reconfigures the system to the ISDN connection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of the second physical connection by inspecting the contracts and the physical cabling. The documentation for the manual switchover in the emergency plan is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The connection of the PBX system SHOULD be designed to be redundant. For IP-based PBX systems, an additional PSTN connection SHOULD be available. The switchover between the primary and the redundant connection is carried out automatically by the PBX system upon detection of a fault. The functionality of the automatic failover is tested regularly (e.g., quarterly) and the result is logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The PBX system is configured to monitor the primary SIP trunk. If it is no longer reachable, it automatically routes all outgoing calls via the PSTN gateway. Once a quarter, the primary connection is briefly deactivated for a test to verify the automatic switchover.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the failover routing in the PBX system. The logs of the regular failover tests are reviewed to verify their execution and success.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Full path and provider redundancy is ensured. The primary and secondary connections are provided by different carriers and are routed into the building via physically separate cable paths. The PBX system continuously monitors the quality of both connections (e.g., latency, jitter, packet loss) and can dynamically select the path suitable for the best call quality or switch over without interruption in the event of quality loss (Session Border Controller functionality).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The primary connection is a fiber optic connection from carrier A, which enters the building on the north side. The secondary connection is a fiber optic connection from carrier B, which enters on the south side. A Session Border Controller (SBC) in front of the PBX system manages both connections and can move calls from one trunk to the other without interruption.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of contracts with two different carriers and checks the plans of the building entries for physical separation. The configuration and real-time monitoring data of the SBC are analyzed to confirm the dynamic control and monitoring of the line quality.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
A telecommunications system, or TC system for short, allows an institution's telephones to be connected internally and externally to a public telephone network. Due to the increasing integration of IT and telecommunications, TC systems can be either analog or IP-based. Hybrid systems are a combination of a classic telecommunications solution and a VoIP system. With a hybrid system, classic digital and analog telephony as well as VoIP can be operated simultaneously.
In addition to voice telephony, other services can be used depending on the connected endpoints. It is thus possible to transmit data, texts, graphics, and moving images via TC systems. The information can be forwarded in analog or digital form via wired or wireless transmission media. Depending on the connection and the data networks used, a wide variety of telecommunications systems can be used in an institution.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: This module addresses the specific threats and requirements for TC systems and the corresponding parts of hybrid systems. The goal of the module is to protect the information transmitted via TC systems and to protect the system from unauthorized access and manipulation.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module NET.4.1 TC Systems is to be applied to every TC system.
This module deals with the threats and requirements that are specific to a TC system and the corresponding parts of a hybrid system. Topics that go beyond the TC system, such as threats and requirements for individual VoIP implementations, as well as externally provided services, are dealt with separately in the corresponding modules of the IT-Grundschutz Compendium.
The security aspects of VoIP components and voice transmission via VoIP are examined in more detail in the module NET.4.2 VoIP.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Eavesdropping on PBX systems
parts.prose:
If telephone calls or data are transmitted unencrypted via a TC system, there is always a risk that attackers can eavesdrop on or read the information. For example, they could directly tap the telephone cables or listen in on a TC system that mediates between the call participants.
In many TC systems, callers can leave messages for recipients if they are not available by phone at the time of the call. Some answering machines, especially on VoIP systems, send this information as an audio file in an email. The content of this email could be directly intercepted and listened to by attackers.
Furthermore, conversations could be listened to by third parties by activating blocked features, some of which are illegal in Germany. An example of this is call intrusion (Zeugenschaltung). Although such activation requires more detailed system knowledge, it is often not a major obstacle due to the large amount of freely available information on the internet.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Eavesdropping on rooms via PBX systems
parts.prose:
In principle, rooms can also be eavesdropped on using the microphones in endpoints. Two variants are distinguished here:
In the first variant, if corresponding functions are implemented, endpoints can be prompted to activate their built-in microphones from the public network or via the LAN. A well-known example of this is the so-called "baby watch function" of telephones or answering machines.
In the second variant, the "direct paging" feature can be misused in combination with the "hands-free" option. The intercom function that can be realized in this way can also be exploited under certain circumstances to eavesdrop on a room.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Toll fraud
parts.prose:
Toll fraud in connection with data or telecommunications services aims to transfer the costs of phone calls or data transfers to third parties. A TC system can be manipulated from the outside in various ways. On the one hand, attackers can try to misuse existing features for toll fraud. These features include, for example, remotely programmable call forwarding or dial-in options. On the other hand, permissions can be assigned in such a way that incoming "trunk lines" can seize outgoing "trunk lines." In this way, when a specific number is dialed, callers can be automatically reconnected to an outside line at the expense of the TC system operator.
Furthermore, not only external attackers but also employees within an institution can commit toll fraud. For example, they can try to make calls at the expense of the institution or other employees by, for instance, making calls from other people's phones, reading out other people's authorization codes (passwords), or changing personal permissions.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Misuse of freely accessible telephone lines
parts.prose: Often, telephones are operated that are not personally assigned to any user. Some of these telephones, such as those in printer rooms, are only accessible to a limited group of people. On the other hand, telephones are often found in areas that are freely accessible to visitors. These include, for example, parking garages or areas in front of access control systems. If these telephones have an electronic phone book in which internal telephone numbers are stored, these numbers could unintentionally leak to the outside.

controls.title: Planning of VoIP deployment

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The decision to use VoIP is made on an ad hoc and project-specific basis, without any overall planning or strategy. Only the most immediate functional requirements are considered, without a formal selection of protocols or an assessment of network capacities.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In this phase, VoIP is often introduced for a small pilot group or a new branch office. The configuration is mostly based on the provider's default settings. Documentation of the decision or configuration is largely missing.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines whether there are any written planning documents for the VoIP deployment. By interviewing the IT managers, it is determined whether the selection of the VoIP solution was based on a systematic decision or was an ad-hoc decision.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic plan that decides whether a full or partial migration to VoIP should take place. The basic signaling and transport protocols are selected, but without a in-depth analysis of security aspects or the exact network load.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple planning document is created. The selection of protocols (e.g., SIP) is based on manufacturer recommendations. A basic estimation of bandwidth requirements is made, but no detailed capacity planning.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the planning document and checks whether the basic decisions (partial/full, protocol selection) are documented. It is checked whether a basic assessment of the network requirements has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The conditions under which VoIP is to be used MUST be defined. Among other things, it MUST be decided whether to switch to VoIP completely or partially. Suitable signaling and media transport protocols MUST be selected before deployment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal planning document is created that defines the migration strategy, the selection and justification of protocols (e.g., SIP for signaling, RTP for media), and the basic framework conditions. This plan is approved by the responsible committee.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies, on the basis of the planning document, that the specifications required in the control have been made. It is checked whether the selection of protocols is documented and comprehensible. It is checked whether the decision on a full or partial switchover has been formally made.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the basic planning, special requirements for the availability of VoIP as well as for the confidentiality and integrity of telephone calls and signaling information SHOULD be determined and documented in advance. It SHOULD be decided whether and how the VoIP infrastructure is connected to public (data) networks. The capacities and design of existing data networks SHOULD be taken into account in detail during planning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The planning includes a requirements analysis regarding protection needs (availability, confidentiality, integrity). The connection to external networks is planned conceptually, e.g., through the use of a Session Border Controller (SBC). A capacity planning of the network is carried out to avoid bottlenecks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the planning documents contain an explicit analysis of the protection requirement requirements. It is checked whether a concept for the connection to public networks exists. The existence and adequacy of the network capacity planning is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VoIP planning is fully integrated into the overall IT security strategy and the ISMS. It includes a detailed risk analysis for the specific VoIP implementation. The capacity planning is validated by load tests. The plan is a living document that is reviewed and adapted regularly, at least annually, and whenever there are significant changes in the threat landscape.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal risk analysis according to, e.g., BSI Standard 200-3 is carried out for the VoIP infrastructure. Before the rollout, load tests are carried out in the network to verify the results of the capacity planning. A process for the regular review and updating of the VoIP concept is established and anchored in the ISMS.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and results of the specific VoIP risk analysis and load tests. It is checked whether the planning process includes a documented revision cycle and whether updates have taken place in the past. The integration into the ISMS is proven by checking the corresponding documents and processes.

controls.title: Secure administration and configuration of VoIP endpoints

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only a few, obviously unneeded functions are deactivated on some VoIP endpoints. There is no standardized configuration or a uniform approach to hardening the endpoints.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Typically, only web interfaces on endpoints are disabled if they cause problems. The configuration is done manually and inconsistently per device.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor selects a sample of VoIP endpoints and compares their configurations. Significant inconsistencies and active but known insecure or unnecessary services (e.g., Telnet, HTTP) are looked for.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic hardening is performed for all VoIP endpoints according to a simple checklist. This includes changing default passwords and deactivating known, unneeded services. Access to the configuration is protected by a changed password.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple hardening guide is created and followed during the commissioning of each device. The default administrator password is replaced with a uniform but non-trivial password.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the hardening checklist. Using a sample of devices, it is checked whether default passwords have been changed and whether the services mentioned in the checklist are deactivated. This can be done by a port scan of the devices or by inspecting the configuration.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Unneeded functions of the endpoints MUST be deactivated. It MUST NOT be possible for the configuration settings to be changed without authorization, for example, through password protection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A mandatory basic configuration is defined and documented for each type of VoIP endpoint. This configuration deactivates all functions not explicitly required for operation (e.g., web server, Bluetooth, WLAN, if not used). Access to the configuration menu is protected by an individual or role-based, secure password.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the configuration of a sample of endpoints with the documented basic configuration. It is checked whether unneeded services are deactivated and whether configuration access is effectively password-protected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All security functions of the endpoints, such as encryption options, SHOULD be tested before productive use. The security mechanisms used and the parameters used SHOULD be documented as part of the mandatory basic configuration.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The defined security configurations are tested for their function and compatibility in a test environment before they are rolled out. The configuration, including the parameters for encryption and authentication, is versioned and documented centrally.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the test documentation and the detailed configuration documentation. It is verified that the security functions were tested before deployment and that the productive configuration corresponds to the documented and tested version.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the VoIP endpoints is automatically rolled out and managed via a central provisioning server. The integrity of the configuration on the endpoints is monitored regularly and automatically. Any unauthorized configuration change triggers an alarm. All administrative access and changes are logged and evaluated centrally.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A provisioning server (e.g., via TFTP/HTTPS) is used to assign a signed configuration file to all endpoints. Configuration management tools or scripts are used to regularly compare the running configuration of the devices with the desired state. The results are sent to a central SIEM system for monitoring and alerting.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the provisioning server and the automated rollout process. The logs of the integrity monitoring and the SIEM system are reviewed to verify the effectiveness of the monitoring and alerting. An automated test could modify a configuration file on an endpoint and check if an alarm is triggered: `sudo sed -i 's/secure_mode=on/secure_mode=off/g' /etc/voip_phone/config.cfg && journalctl -f | grep 'ConfigDriftDetected'`.

controls.title: Restricting VoIP reachability

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no clear policy on how external participants access the VoIP infrastructure. Access is granted on a case-by-case basis and often with very broad firewall rules (e.g., ANY-ANY to the VoIP server) to avoid functional problems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Firewall rules are often created reactively when an external user cannot connect. This often leads to overly permissive rules.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules governing traffic to the VoIP infrastructure. It looks for overly broad rules (e.g., any/any) or rules without explicit source or destination restrictions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic policy for external access is defined. Direct access from insecure networks to internal VoIP components is prevented by basic network segmentation and firewall rules that only allow the necessary ports (e.g., UDP/5060).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The VoIP system is located in its own DMZ or a protected VLAN. The firewall rules explicitly allow only SIP and RTP traffic from known external IP addresses or gateways.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the network plan and the firewall configuration to ensure that the VoIP components are segmented and the access rules are restricted to the necessary protocols and ports.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be decided and documented how external parties can access the VoIP architecture. It MUST be prevented by technical measures, such as a firewall, that IT systems from insecure networks can establish direct, uncontrolled data connections to internal VoIP components.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal access policy for external VoIP communication is created. The VoIP infrastructure is placed in a DMZ. The firewall rules are configured restrictively (Default-Deny) and only allow the necessary traffic to defined VoIP components.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the access policy and compares it with the implemented firewall configuration. It is checked whether the rules effectively prevent direct access to internal VoIP clients or servers and only allow traffic to the defined gateway (e.g., in the DMZ).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If all incoming and outgoing connections are handled via a central IT system, it SHOULD be ensured that all signaling and voice information between the public and private data network is exchanged only via this authorized IT system. This system is typically a Session Border Controller (SBC).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Session Border Controller (SBC) is implemented as a central, authorized transition point between the internal and external network. All firewall rules enforce that all VoIP traffic is routed through the SBC. Direct connections from external to internal VoIP components are prohibited.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the network topology and the firewall rules to ensure that the SBC is the only allowed communication path for VoIP traffic across the network boundary. The SBC's configuration is checked for correct function (e.g., Topology Hiding).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A high-availability cluster of Session Border Controllers (SBCs) is deployed. All VoIP traffic is deeply inspected at the application layer (Deep Packet Inspection) to detect and block attacks such as SIP fuzzing or SQL injection in SIP headers. The SBCs use current threat intelligence feeds and Geo-IP filtering to proactively defend against known malicious actors.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A redundant pair of SBCs is operated in failover mode. The SBC's Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) functions for VoIP are activated and maintained with custom rules and vendor updates. The SBCs are connected to a SIEM system for central logging and correlation of security events.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the configuration of the SBC cluster for high availability and the activation of the DPI/IPS functions. The connection to threat intelligence feeds and the SIEM is verified. As a test, known attack patterns (e.g., from `sipp` with manipulated headers) can be run against the infrastructure to observe the SBC's reaction: `sudo sipp -sf custom_attack.xml -d 10000 -s service <SBC_IP>`.

controls.title: Secure configuration of the VoIP middleware

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VoIP middleware is operated with the manufacturer's default settings. Only the parameters absolutely necessary for basic functionality and the administrator passwords are changed. Many unneeded services continue to run.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The installation is done according to the 'Next-Next-Finish' principle. No systematic hardening takes place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the running configuration of the VoIP middleware with the manufacturer's known default settings. A port scan of the server shows which services are active and can be compared with a list of necessary services.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic hardening of the VoIP middleware is performed. All default passwords are changed and a checklist is used to deactivate common, unneeded services (e.g., unencrypted administration interfaces).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An internal checklist for the basic configuration is created and applied to every installation. This checklist is based on general best practices and manufacturer recommendations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the configuration checklist and checks on a random basis whether the points have been implemented in the productive environment. It is checked whether all default accounts have been deactivated or their passwords changed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VoIP components (middleware) MUST be configured to adequately meet the protection requirements. The default configurations of the VoIP middleware MUST be adapted before productive commissioning. All unneeded services of the VoIP middleware MUST be deactivated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal, documented security configuration for the VoIP middleware is created. This is based on an analysis of the required functions and the defined protection requirements. A standard hardening process is established, which includes the deactivation of all non-essential services and the configuration of security features.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the running configuration of the VoIP middleware with the documented security configuration. By means of a port scan and checking the process list (`ps aux` or `netstat -tulpen`), it is verified that no unneeded services are active.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All installation and configuration steps SHOULD be documented in such a way that the installation and configuration can be understood and repeated by knowledgeable third parties based on the documentation. The configuration documentation is versioned.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Detailed installation and configuration guides ('runbooks') are created. These guides are versioned and maintained in a central knowledge management system (e.g., a wiki). Changes to the configuration follow a change management process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the installation and configuration documentation and checks it for completeness, clarity, and currency. It is checked whether a change management process for configuration changes exists and is followed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The configuration of the VoIP middleware is managed using Infrastructure as Code (IaC), e.g., with Ansible, Puppet, or SaltStack. All configuration changes are tracked in a version control system (e.g., Git), automatically tested in a staging environment, and then rolled out to the production systems. System integrity and configuration compliance are continuously monitored, and deviations lead to automated corrections or alarms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Ansible playbooks or equivalent scripts are developed to fully automate the installation and configuration of the VoIP middleware. A CI/CD pipeline is used for testing and rolling out configuration changes. Tools like AIDE or Wazuh are used to monitor the configuration files on the server.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the IaC repository and the CI/CD pipeline. The logs of the automated tests and the configuration monitoring tools are reviewed. A test could consist of manually changing a configuration file and checking whether the system detects and corrects the change or raises an alert: `sudo echo '# Injected comment' >> /etc/asterisk/sip.conf; sleep 60; sudo cat /etc/asterisk/sip.conf | grep '# Injected comment'`.

controls.title: Creation of a security policy for VoIP

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: No specific VoIP security policy exists. Individual aspects of VoIP usage may be mentioned sporadically in other, general IT policies (e.g., password policy), but there is no coherent regulatory framework.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are no dedicated efforts to create a VoIP policy. The reliance is that general IT rules also apply to VoIP.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the VoIP security policy. If one does not exist, other IT policies are searched for specific regulations for VoIP to confirm the lack of a dedicated policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic, standalone usage policy for VoIP exists. It mainly covers rules of conduct for users, such as private use and securing voicemails. However, the policy is not fully integrated into the overarching information security policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A short document with 'Do's and Don'ts' for VoIP usage is created and distributed to users. It focuses on end-user aspects.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the VoIP usage policy and assesses whether it covers the basic user aspects. It is checked whether references to the central security policy are missing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central security requirements for VoIP and the security level to be achieved SHOULD be included in the institution-wide security policy or a dedicated subordinate policy. In this security policy, all general security specifications SHOULD be concretized. Furthermore, the policy SHOULD regulate the specifications for the operation and use of VoIP components.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal VoIP security policy is created as part of the ISMS policy framework. This policy defines the desired security level and contains clear rules for administrators and users. It is approved by the management level.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the VoIP security policy and checks whether it covers the aspects mentioned in the Control (security level, operational and usage specifications) and whether it has been formally approved and integrated into the institution's policy framework.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VoIP security policy SHOULD also consider and regulate specific VoIP functions, such as voicemails, conference calls, and the use of softphones, in detail. The VoIP security policy SHOULD be demonstrably made accessible and known to all involved persons and groups (administrators, users).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is expanded to include specific chapters on voicemail security, secure use of softphones (especially in home office), and rules for conference calls. The policy is published on the intranet, and employees are demonstrably informed about the policy through training or by email.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the content of the policy for the specific treatment of functions such as voicemail and softphones. Evidence (e.g., training materials, email distribution lists, intranet page) is requested to prove that the policy has been communicated to the relevant target groups.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The VoIP security policy is reviewed and updated at least annually and in the event of significant technological changes or new threats. Compliance with the policy is regularly audited through technical checks and interviews. The policy defines clear roles and responsibilities (e.g., VoIP administrator, user) and establishes a process for requesting and approving exceptions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A review process for the policy is established in the ISMS. Technical audits (e.g., configuration checks) and awareness checks (e.g., surveying users on voicemail security) are conducted regularly. A formal application process for exceptions (e.g., the use of an unapproved softphone) is established.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the review and update process of the policy based on logs and previous versions. The results of the internal audits on policy compliance are reviewed. It is checked whether a documented exception process exists and is applied.

controls.title: Encryption of VoIP

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Encryption is only active where it is a default setting of the clients or middleware used. There is no clear policy or uniform configuration for encrypting VoIP traffic. Often, in case of compatibility problems, there is a fallback to unencrypted communication.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The encryption options in the end devices and the telephone system are left in the default setting. If an end device does not support encryption, communication takes place unencrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor uses a network sniffer (e.g., Wireshark) to record the traffic of a sample of calls and checks whether the signaling (SIP) and the media stream (RTP) are transmitted unencrypted. In Wireshark, you can filter for `sip` and `rtp` to check this.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a policy that requires all VoIP traffic leaving the trusted network boundary to be encrypted. This is implemented by a Session Border Controller (SBC) or a VPN gateway. However, internal communication in the LAN is still unencrypted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The SBC at the network perimeter is configured to enforce TLS for SIP and SRTP for media data for all external connections. Internal clients communicate with the telephone system unencrypted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the SBC or VPN gateway for the enforcement of encryption for external connections. Additionally, the internal network traffic is captured to confirm that it is unencrypted.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be decided and documented whether and which voice and signaling information should be encrypted. In general, all VoIP data packets that leave the secured LAN SHOULD be protected by suitable security mechanisms (e.g., TLS for signaling and SRTP for media data).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal decision on the scope of encryption is made and documented. As a minimum standard, it is established that all communication that runs over insecure networks (such as the Internet) is encrypted. This is technically configured via an SBC or the telephone system itself.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the document that records the decision on the scope of encryption. The configuration of the relevant systems (SBC, PBX) is checked to ensure that encryption for external communication is active as defined. A network capture at the network boundary verifies this.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to encrypting external traffic, internal VoIP communication (both signaling via TLS and media data via SRTP) is also encrypted by default to protect against internal attackers. Users SHOULD be informed about the use and limitations of VoIP encryption (e.g., end-to-end vs. transport).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The telephone system and all end devices are configured to request and use encryption for all calls by default. Users are informed via the intranet or as part of security awareness training.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor captures traffic in the internal LAN and verifies that calls between two internal participants are also encrypted (SIP over TLS, SRTP). It is checked whether there is information material for users on VoIP encryption.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Wherever technically possible, end-to-end encryption (E2EE) for VoIP calls is enforced. Only strong, centrally managed cryptographic parameters are used. The system is configured to strictly reject unencrypted connections (Encrypt-or-Drop-Policy). The management of certificates for TLS is automated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Protocols such as ZRTP or a PKI-based solution for E2EE are implemented. The telephone system is configured to only accept secure crypto suites and to reject calls if a secure SRTP connection cannot be negotiated. An ACME client or an internal certificate management system is used for the automatic issuance and renewal of TLS certificates.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the telephone system and the end devices for the enforcement of E2EE and the configuration of the 'Encrypt-or-Drop' policy. It is checked whether a call attempt with a client that only supports unencrypted RTP fails. The process for automated certificate management is audited.

controls.title: Appropriate Selection of VoIP Components

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: VoIP components are selected mainly based on price, brand awareness, or recommendation. There is no formal list of requirements that serves as a basis for the selection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Procurement is often reactive, when an old system fails, and is based on what the preferred supplier is currently offering.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the documentation of the selection process for the current VoIP components. If this is missing or consists only of offers, this is an indicator for this maturity level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before procurement, a basic list of functional requirements is created. Products on the market are compared based on this list and the manufacturer's specifications. Security features play a subordinate role.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple feature table is created in a spreadsheet to compare the offers of different manufacturers. The decision is based on fulfilling the most functional requirements at the best price.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the requirements list and the comparison documentation. It is assessed whether the selection was based on a documented comparison, even if security aspects were not the focus.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before VoIP components are procured, a formal list of requirements SHOULD be created. Based on this list of requirements, the products available on the market SHOULD be evaluated and the selection decision documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal requirements catalog is created that includes functional and non-functional requirements (e.g., scalability). A standardized process for market analysis and product evaluation is carried out. The final decision is justified in writing and archived.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the requirements catalog and the documentation of the evaluation process and the selection decision. It is checked whether a systematic and comprehensible process has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The list of requirements SHOULD explicitly include all features for achieving the desired security level. This includes, for example, the support of specific encryption protocols or hardening measures. A formal process SHOULD be established for evaluating the products according to the list of requirements, including the weighting of security features.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements catalog contains a dedicated chapter on security requirements (e.g., 'Must support TLS 1.2+', 'Must support SRTP', 'Must have a role-based admin concept'). During the evaluation, a high weight is given to security features.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the requirements catalog for the existence and adequacy of the security requirements. It is checked whether the evaluation matrix appropriately weights the security criteria and whether the final product selection is consistent with these criteria.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection process includes a mandatory Proof-of-Concept (PoC) phase in which the favored products are validated against the defined security requirements in a test environment. The manufacturer's security reputation, its Software Development Lifecycle, and its patch policy (e.g., response time to vulnerabilities) are decisive criteria in the selection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The top 2 candidates from the paper evaluation are installed in a lab setup. A test plan is executed that specifically scrutinizes the security functions. At the same time, research is conducted on the manufacturer's security history and its handling of reported vulnerabilities is assessed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the PoC test plans and result reports. The documentation for evaluating the manufacturer and its security processes is reviewed. It is verified that the final decision is demonstrably based on the results of the PoC and the manufacturer evaluation.

controls.title: Secure handling of VoIP end devices

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users receive their VoIP phones without specific security instructions. The PINs for voicemails are often left at the default value or set to trivial values like '1234'.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There are no training or awareness measures for VoIP security. The responsibility for security is left entirely to the user.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor questions a sample of users about the security instructions they have received. An attempt can be made to log into test voicemail boxes with default PINs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When the phone is issued, users receive brief written instructions or an email explaining how to set a secure password (PIN) for their voicemail box.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A short leaflet on voicemail security is created and issued to all new users by default. The system forces the default PIN to be changed on first login.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the leaflet or the email template. It is checked whether the system forces the change of the initial PIN by creating a new test account.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Users who use VoIP end devices SHOULD be informed about the basic VoIP threats (e.g., eavesdropping, fraud) and the established security measures. Furthermore, they SHOULD be encouraged to select appropriate, secure passwords (PINs) to secure voicemails.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the general security awareness campaign, users are educated about specific VoIP risks. There are clear guidelines in the password policy that also apply to voicemail PINs, and users are made aware of them.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the security awareness training materials for content on VoIP security. It is checked whether the password policy covers voicemail PINs and whether users have been demonstrably informed of this.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Regular and mandatory security awareness training sessions are held, which include specific modules on VoIP threats such as Vishing (Voice Phishing). The VoIP system enforces technical password policies for voicemail PINs (minimum length, complexity, lockout after failed attempts).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The annual e-learning on information security contains a chapter on vishing. The telephone system is configured so that PINs must have at least 6 digits, must not be trivial, and the account is locked after 5 failed attempts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the training materials for vishing content. The configuration of the telephone system is analyzed to verify the enforcement of the PIN policy. A test could be to enter 6 incorrect PINs for a test account to check for account lockout.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Simulated vishing attacks are conducted regularly to test and improve employee awareness. Users are trained to report suspicious calls through a defined process. Access to voicemails, especially remotely or via email, is protected by multi-factor authentication (MFA) where technically possible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An external service provider or an internal team conducts quarterly vishing campaigns. There is a clear reporting channel for security incidents, which also includes suspicious calls. The voicemail-to-email function is configured so that the email only contains a link to a web-based, MFA-protected portal, instead of attaching the audio file directly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the reports of the vishing campaigns and the statistics of reported incidents. The process for securing voicemail access with MFA is checked. It is tested whether a voicemail notification email contains the audio file or links to a secure portal.

controls.title: Secure decommissioning of VoIP components

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Decommissioned VoIP devices are simply taken off the network and stored or disposed of without deleting the configuration or data. Labels indicating the institution or user are not removed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is no process for decommissioning. Devices are stacked in storage or sent directly to electronic waste.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the storage for decommissioned IT equipment and checks a sample of VoIP phones to see if they still contain configuration data (e.g., SIP credentials, phone books) or have labels.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A 'factory reset' is performed on all VoIP components before disposal or transfer. This is done according to a simple checklist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple process is established: 'Before disposal, press button X for 10 seconds'. The execution is not separately documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
