parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The load and condition of the electrical circuits are continuously monitored by an intelligent power monitoring system. Deviations from the normal state and impending overloads are reported automatically to enable proactive maintenance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Intelligent Power Distribution Units (PDUs) and smart fuses are used, which send their data to a central building management system or a DCIM (Data Center Infrastructure Management). Thresholds for alarms are defined and linked to the incident management process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the logs and alarm messages of the power monitoring system. It is checked whether the thresholds are configured meaningfully and whether alarms are responded to appropriately. Automated check: A script queries the API of the DCIM system and compares the measured load with the documented limits: `check_pdu_load --all --threshold 80%`.

controls.title: Compliance with fire safety regulations (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Fire safety regulations are only implemented reactively, often only after complaints from authorities. Escape routes are occasionally blocked by stored objects.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Awareness of fire safety is low among employees. There is no designated person who actively deals with the topic. Fire extinguishers are available, but not everyone knows their locations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts an unannounced inspection and checks whether escape and rescue routes are clear. Random checks are carried out to see whether fire doors are wedged open.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The basic fire safety regulations are complied with. Escape routes are signposted and are generally kept clear. There is a person who is also responsible for fire protection in addition to other tasks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A person from facility management is designated as a fire warden. Regular checks take place, but are not always documented. Unnecessary fire loads are removed when they are obviously detected.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the signposting and clearance of the escape routes. The appointment of the person responsible for fire protection and their basic qualification (e.g., fire warden training) is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The existing fire safety regulations and the requirements of the building authorities MUST be complied with. The escape routes MUST be signposted and kept clear in accordance with regulations. It MUST be checked regularly that the escape routes are usable and free of obstacles. Unnecessary fire loads MUST be avoided. There MUST be a fire safety officer or a person entrusted with this task. This person MUST be suitably trained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A fire safety officer is formally appointed. Regular, documented inspections (e.g., monthly) are carried out to check compliance with the regulations. Employees are instructed annually on the correct behavior in the event of a fire and the importance of clear escape routes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the certificate of appointment and the training certificates of the fire safety officer. The logs of the regular inspections are reviewed. It is checked whether identified deficiencies are tracked and rectified. The escape and rescue plans are checked for up-to-dateness and correctness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The local fire department SHOULD be consulted during fire protection planning to ensure that the building can be evacuated quickly in a hazardous situation. All fire protection measures are documented in a fire protection concept that is reviewed regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Regular coordination meetings are held with the local fire department to, for example, coordinate access routes and the locations of fire hydrants. The fire protection concept is part of the overall building security concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the minutes of the coordination meetings with the fire department. The fire protection concept is checked to ensure that it is comprehensive and up-to-date and that it takes into account the specific conditions of the building and its use. It is checked whether the fire department route cards are up to date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with fire safety regulations is supported by technical systems, such as camera systems linked to the building management system to monitor escape routes. Deviations, such as blocked doors, automatically trigger an alarm at the security service. Regular, unannounced evacuation drills are carried out and their results are used to optimize the plans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Video analysis software automatically detects objects placed in escape routes. The results of evacuation drills are systematically evaluated (e.g., time measurement, employee surveys) and feed into the continuous improvement of the fire protection concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and alarm logs of the technical monitoring system. The documentation and evaluation of the evacuation drills are checked. It is assessed whether a genuine continuous improvement process has been established in fire protection. Automated check: `check_cctv_rules --zone 'escape_route' --verify 'obstruction_detection_active'`.

controls.title: Fire detection in buildings (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are only individual, battery-operated smoke detectors installed in a few rooms, which do not meet the legal minimum requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Often, only smoke detectors from the hardware store are used. There is no regular check of the function or the batteries.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor determines in which areas smoke detectors are present and whether there is a lack of systematic equipment. The function of a detector is randomly checked by pressing the test button.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Buildings are equipped with smoke detectors in accordance with the legal minimum requirements. However, they only sound a local alarm and are not networked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Smoke detectors are installed in all required areas. Regular maintenance (e.g., battery replacement) is carried out by the facility management, but is not always fully documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the equipment with the legal requirements (e.g., state building code). It is checked whether a maintenance plan exists and whether it is generally adhered to.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Buildings MUST be equipped with a sufficient number of smoke detectors in accordance with the requirements in the building permit and the fire protection concept. If a local alarm at the detector's location is not sufficient, all detectors MUST be connected to a fire alarm control panel (FACP). In case of smoke detection, an alarm MUST be triggered in the building. It MUST be ensured that all persons present in the building can perceive it. The functionality of all smoke detectors and all other components of a fire alarm system (FAS) MUST be checked regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A certified fire alarm system (FAS) with a fire alarm control panel (FACP) is installed. Regular maintenance is carried out by a specialist company and documented in a logbook. The alarm is given acoustically (sirens) and, if necessary, optically (strobe lights).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the fire protection concept, the building permit, and the logbook of the FAS. It is verified that the maintenance intervals are adhered to and that the system complies with the standards. During a test alarm, it is checked whether the alarm is perceptible throughout the entire building.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire alarm system is connected to a permanently staffed location (e.g., gatehouse, security service) or directly to the fire department. In areas requiring protection, such as server rooms, aspirating smoke detection (ASD) systems are used for early detection instead of simple smoke detectors.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The connection to the fire department is contractually regulated. The installation of aspirating smoke detection systems allows the detection of smoldering fires before open flames and smoke are generated. The sensitivity of the systems is adapted to the protection requirements.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the contract for the connection of the FAS. The configuration and functionality of the early detection systems (e.g., ASD) are checked. It is verified that the personnel at the staffed location are trained to handle fire alarms.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire alarm system is fully integrated into the building management system. In the event of an alarm, measures are automatically initiated, such as shutting down the ventilation, opening smoke and heat extraction systems (SHEVS), and activating the escape route control system to ensure a safe evacuation. The detector types are specifically designed for the environmental risks (e.g., thermal detectors in kitchens, multi-sensor detectors in IT rooms).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Complex fire control matrices are defined that regulate the interaction of the various technical systems in the event of a fire. These matrices are tested regularly (full functional test). The selection of detectors was based on a detailed fire risk analysis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the fire control matrix for logic and completeness. The logs of the regular full functional tests are checked. It is verified that the automated controls (ventilation, SHEVS, doors) functioned correctly in the test case. Automated check: `check_bms_integration --trigger 'fire_alarm_zone_5' --verify 'hvac_shutdown,rwa_open'`.

controls.title: Hand-held fire extinguishers (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are a few hand-held fire extinguishers in the building, but some of their inspection deadlines have expired. The selection of fire classes is not adapted to the specific risks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Often, only water extinguishers are available, even in areas with electrical systems. Regular inspection is forgotten or ignored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks the inspection tags of the existing fire extinguishers. It is assessed whether the number and type of extinguishers are obviously insufficient.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hand-held fire extinguishers are available in sufficient numbers and are regularly inspected. However, employees are not trained in their use.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An external service provider maintains the fire extinguishers every two years. The locations are marked. However, there is no practical training for the staff.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the maintenance contracts and logs for the hand-held fire extinguishers. By interviewing employees, it is determined whether they know where the nearest fire extinguisher is and whether they would feel confident using it.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For immediate fire fighting, hand-held fire extinguishers of the appropriate fire class (DIN EN 3 Portable fire extinguishers) MUST be available in sufficient number and size in the building. The hand-held fire extinguishers MUST be regularly inspected and maintained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The number, type, and locations of the fire extinguishers are based on ASR A2.2 'Measures against fires'. The inspection is carried out at least every two years by a competent person. The locations are marked in the escape and rescue plans.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the equipment with the specifications of ASR A2.2. The maintenance logs are checked for completeness and timely execution. The marking of the locations and the entry in the plans are verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Employees SHOULD be instructed in the use of hand-held fire extinguishers. The instructions SHOULD be repeated at appropriate intervals. In particular, fire wardens receive regular practical exercises.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: As part of the annual safety briefing, a theoretical instruction on the operation of fire extinguishers takes place. For fire wardens (approx. 5% of the workforce), practical extinguishing exercises with a fire extinguisher trainer are carried out every two years.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the training materials and certificates of attendance for the instructions and practical exercises. It is checked whether the number of trained fire wardens complies with legal requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The hand-held fire extinguishers are equipped with sensors (e.g., pressure sensors or NFC tags) that report their status (pressure, location, next inspection date) to a central management system. The selection of extinguishing agents is optimally tailored to the respective fire risks, e.g., by using special grease fire or metal fire extinguishers in corresponding areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A CAFM system (Computer-Aided Facility Management) manages all fire extinguishers. Tampering with or removing an extinguisher triggers an alert. The fire risk analysis determines the exact type of extinguishing agent for each location.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the data in the CAFM system and compares it with a random physical check. It is checked whether the system functions reliably and whether the selection of extinguishing agents is based on a comprehensible risk analysis. Automated check: `check_cafm_asset --type 'fire_extinguisher' --verify 'status_ok,location_correct'`.

controls.title: Closed windows and doors (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no regulation for closing windows and doors after business hours. This is left to the discretion of individual employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Windows are often left tilted overnight or on weekends. Office doors are left open, even when no one is present.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts a walk-through outside of business hours and documents open windows and doors. It is determined whether a regulation is entirely missing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is an informal or verbal instruction to close windows and doors after leaving the office. There is no control.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: New employees are advised to close the window when they leave. There is no written instruction or regular reminders.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks employees if they are aware of a regulation for closing windows and doors. The effectiveness is checked by a walk-through after business hours.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Windows and externally accessible doors MUST be closed at times when a room is not occupied. Rooms MUST be locked if confidential information is left there. There MUST be a corresponding instruction for this. All employees SHOULD be obliged to comply with the instruction. Fire and smoke protection doors MAY ONLY be kept open permanently if this is done by approved hold-open systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A written instruction is part of the house rules or a service instruction. This is demonstrably brought to the attention of all employees. Warning signs are placed on fire and smoke protection doors prohibiting wedging or blocking.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the written instruction and the proof of acknowledgement by the employees. It is checked whether there are improperly wedged fire doors. It is checked whether approved hold-open systems are regularly maintained.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be checked regularly whether the windows and interior and exterior doors are locked after leaving the building. This check is carried out and logged by a locking service or security service.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A security officer conducts a daily inspection tour of all floors after business hours and closes any open windows found. Findings are documented in a logbook. In the event of repeated violations, the respective department head is informed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs (logbook) of the locking service over a longer period. It is analyzed whether the checks take place regularly and whether repeated violations are addressed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Windows and doors are equipped with sensors that report their status (open/closed/locked) to a central building management system. When arming the intruder alarm system, it is automatically checked whether all windows and exterior doors are closed. If this is not the case, arming is prevented and a message is sent to the security service.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Magnetic contacts on all windows and exterior doors are connected to the intruder alarm system (EMA) and the building management system. The logic for forced locking is configured in the EMA and is tested regularly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the EMA and the building management system. Through a practical test (opening a window and attempting to arm the EMA), the correct functioning of the forced locking and alarming is verified. Automated check: `check_bms_config --asset 'EMA' --verify 'window_check_on_arming_enabled'`.

controls.title: Access regulation and control (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no formal access regulation. Doors to areas requiring protection are often unlocked. Unauthorized persons can move largely uncontrolled within the building.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Everyone has a key to the entrance door. Doors to server rooms or archives are not consistently locked. Visitors are not registered or accompanied.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor conducts a walk-through and checks whether he can gain access to sensitive areas without authorization. It is determined whether there is a regulation for handling visitors.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a simple access regulation which states that doors to areas requiring protection must be locked. There is no differentiated granting of access rights.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Most employees have keys to almost all areas. Key management is decentralized and undocumented. The number of authorized persons is not reduced to a minimum.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor questions those responsible about the access regulation and key management. It is checked whether the 'need-to-know' principle is applied when issuing keys.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to protected parts of buildings and rooms MUST be regulated and controlled. An access control concept SHOULD exist. The number of persons with access rights SHOULD be reduced to a minimum for each area. All granted access rights SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An access control concept is in place that defines various security zones and the corresponding authorization groups. The granting of authorizations is based on a documented approval process. The authorizations are managed in a list or a system (e.g., in an electronic access control system).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the access control concept. The documentation of the granted authorizations is checked. It is checked on a random basis whether the granting of authorizations follows the 'need-to-know' principle and whether the corresponding approvals are available.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Other persons MAY only be granted access after it has been checked whether this is necessary. The access control measures MUST be regularly checked for their effectiveness. Access controls SHOULD also be in place as far as possible during relocations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process for granting temporary authorizations for visitors and service providers has been established. At least once a year, a 'recertification' process is carried out, in which all existing access rights must be reviewed and confirmed by the respective supervisors. Mobile or temporary access control solutions are used during relocations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the 'recertification' process. It is checked whether the process for external personnel is being followed (e.g., by reviewing visitor lists and temporary authorizations). It is verified that there are plans for maintaining access control during special events such as relocations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An electronic access control system (EACS) is in use that logs all access attempts (authorized and unauthorized). The logs are automatically monitored for anomalies (e.g., access attempts outside business hours). In high-security areas, two-factor authentication (e.g., card and PIN or biometrics) is required for access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The EACS is linked to the human resources management system, so that permissions are automatically revoked when an employee leaves. A SIEM (Security Information and Event Management) system analyzes the EACS logs and correlates them with other events. For server rooms, for example, entering a PIN is required in addition to the RFID card.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and logs of the EACS. The rules in the SIEM system for detecting anomalies are checked. The effectiveness of the two-factor authentication is tested on-site. Automated check: `check_access_control_system --verify 'auto_revocation_enabled' --zone 'high_security' --check '2fa_required'`.

controls.title: No-smoking policy (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no explicit smoking ban near IT systems or archives. Smoking is tolerated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees smoke at their workplaces, even if there are computers there. Ashtrays are available in office rooms.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through an inspection and observation whether smoking occurs in areas requiring protection or if there are signs of it (e.g., ashtrays, smell of cigarettes).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a general smoking ban in the building, but without a specific focus on IT areas. Designated smoking zones are available, but their location is not assessed from a security perspective.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A smoking area is located directly next to the open window of the server room, allowing smoke to enter. Compliance with the smoking ban is not actively monitored.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence of the general smoking ban and the location of designated smoking zones in relation to areas requiring protection. It is checked whether the setup of smoking zones leads to bypassing access controls (e.g., emergency exits being kept open).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For rooms with IT equipment or data media where fires or contamination can lead to high damages, such as server rooms, data media archives, or document archives, a smoking ban MUST be enacted. It MUST be regularly checked that access protection is not circumvented when setting up or tolerating smoking zones.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The house rules stipulate an explicit smoking ban for all technical operating rooms, server rooms, and archives. Corresponding pictograms are placed on the doors of these rooms. The locations of smoking zones are chosen so that no security objectives are compromised (e.g., by bypassing access control or smoke ingress).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the house rules and checks the signage of the affected rooms. During an inspection, the location of the smoking zones is assessed and it is checked whether security measures (especially access control) are thereby undermined.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The smoking ban extends to the entire building and also applies to e-cigarettes. Smoking zones are set up exclusively outside the building in defined locations equipped with safe ashtrays.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is clearly communicated to all employees. Compliance is checked during regular security inspections. The ashtrays in the outdoor area are emptied regularly to minimize fire hazards.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the comprehensive policy and its communication. It is checked whether the external smoking zones are designed securely and do not pose a new hazard (e.g., fire risk from full ashtrays).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In high-security areas (e.g., data centers), smoke detectors are installed that also react to the particles from e-cigarettes and trigger a silent alarm to the security service in case of a smoking ban violation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Special multi-sensor detectors or particle counters are used. The procedure for the security service in the event of such an alarm is clearly defined.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the technical specifications of the installed detectors and the alarm configuration. The effectiveness can be verified by a test with a test aerosol. The directive for the security service is checked.

controls.title: Compliance with relevant standards and regulations (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Standards and regulations are only considered when external bodies (e.g., building authorities) explicitly point them out. There is no process to identify relevant standards.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For construction measures, reliance is placed solely on the executing companies without checking their work for standards compliance or contractually requiring it.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks how it is ensured that, for example, electrical installations or fire protection measures comply with current regulations. The absence of a process is documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When commissioning external companies, reference is made to compliance with the 'generally accepted rules of technology' without specifying them. An acceptance test is only carried out superficially.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Contracts with craft businesses contain a standard clause on compliance with regulations. However, it is not checked whether, for example, the materials used or the type of installation comply with specific standards (e.g., VDE standards).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews sample contracts with installation companies and asks for the acceptance protocols. It is assessed whether the check for standards compliance is part of the acceptance.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the planning, construction, and modification of buildings, as well as in the installation of technical facilities, all relevant standards and regulations MUST be taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Planners and installation companies are explicitly contractually obliged to comply with specific, relevant standards (e.g., DIN, VDE, VdS). Upon acceptance of services, compliance with these standards is proven by presenting certificates, measurement protocols, and declarations of conformity.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the tender documents and contracts and checks whether relevant standards are specifically named. Acceptance protocols and the associated verification documents (e.g., VDE measurement protocol for an electrical installation) are checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a defined process to identify and evaluate relevant standards and regulations and their changes. The results are incorporated into internal planning and procurement guidelines.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution subscribes to standards information services (e.g., from Beuth or VDE). Once a quarter, a committee (e.g., consisting of construction management, IT, and ISB) assesses the relevance of new standards. Internal checklists for the awarding and acceptance of construction services are updated accordingly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the process for standards research and assessment explained. The minutes of the assessment meetings and the resulting adjustments in the internal guidelines and checklists are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with standards and regulations is documented and tracked in a compliance management system. The acceptance of critical technical facilities is generally carried out by an independent third party (e.g., an expert).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A GRC software is used to assign the relevant standards to each technical trade and to track the status of conformity. Before commissioning a new data center, for example, it is inspected and certified by a TÜV expert according to relevant standards (e.g., EN 50600).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the entries in the compliance management system. The reports and certificates of the independent experts are checked. It is verified that identified deviations are systematically tracked and rectified. Automated check: `check_grc_compliance --asset_type 'building_infrastructure' --verify 'all_norms_covered'`.

controls.title: Security concept for building use (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are only individual, disconnected instructions for building use, such as a separate fire safety regulation. An overarching concept is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a fire safety regulation and a separate instruction for key return, but no documentation on how these aspects interact.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor collects all existing regulatory documents for building use and determines that no integrated, overarching concept exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic document referred to as a security concept for building use. However, it is not aligned with the institution's overall security concept and is not regularly updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document was created when moving into the building that sets out basic rules. However, it does not take into account the specific protection needs of the departments that have since moved in or the general IT security guidelines.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing concept and compares it with the overall security concept (if available). The creation date is checked and it is determined whether updates have taken place since then.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There SHOULD be a security concept for building use. The security concept for the building SHOULD be aligned with the institution's overall security concept. It SHOULD be documented and regularly updated. An IT-related fire protection concept MUST be created and implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal security concept for building use is created and maintained. It references the higher-level ISMS framework and contains specific regulations for physical security. A separate, detailed IT fire protection concept that addresses the specific risks in server rooms is part of this concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence, completeness, and alignment of the building security concept with the overall security concept. In particular, the IT fire protection concept is checked for its appropriateness and implementation. The revision history of the document is checked for regular updates.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rooms or parts of buildings requiring protection SHOULD not be located in exposed or particularly vulnerable areas. The building security concept is reviewed and adapted at least annually or in the event of significant changes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In space planning, active care is taken not to place server rooms on the ground floor with large windows or in the basement (flood risk). A formal review process for the security concept is established and documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses the location of the rooms requiring protection based on building plans and an inspection with regard to known hazards (e.g., burglary, water, unauthorized viewing). The minutes of the annual review of the security concept are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security concept for building use is based on a detailed, quantitative risk analysis. It is fully integrated into a GRC tool that maps the dependencies between physical zones, IT assets, and business processes. Changes to one element automatically trigger a reassessment of the risks for dependent elements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The choice of location and the positioning of areas requiring protection are based on a formal site risk analysis that includes hazards such as floods, earthquakes, or crime rates. The GRC tool visualizes the impact of a physical zone failure (e.g., server room) on business processes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the risk analyses and dependency models stored in the GRC tool. It is checked whether the decisions on spatial planning are comprehensibly based on these analyses. The automatic reassessment of risks is tested by simulated changes in the tool. Automated check: `check_grc_config --asset-type 'building_zone' --verify 'risk_assessment_quantitative,bcm_linkage_complete'`.

controls.title: Key management (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no central key management. Keys are duplicated as needed and their issuance is not documented. It is unclear who has which keys.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees pass keys directly to colleagues. If a key is lost, no report is made or action taken.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through interviews that there is no overview of the keys issued and no process for issuing and returning them.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a simple list where the issuance of keys is noted. However, there is no key plan and spare keys are stored insecurely.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An Excel list is maintained, but not always consistently. A spare key for the server room hangs unsecured on the key board in the secretary's office.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the key list and compares it with the keys actually issued on a random basis. The storage of spare keys is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A key plan SHOULD be available for all keys in the building. The production, storage, management, and issuance of keys SHOULD be centrally regulated. Every key issuance SHOULD be documented. Unissued keys SHOULD be stored securely.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An up-to-date key plan exists that maps the hierarchy of the locking system. A central body (e.g., facility management, administration) is responsible for key management. Keys are issued only against a signature and are documented in key management software or a meticulously maintained list. Unused keys are stored in a safe.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the key plan and the key management documentation. It is checked whether the processes for issuance and return are being followed. The secure storage of unissued keys is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Spare keys SHOULD be kept available and secured, but readily accessible for emergencies. The documentation of key issuance is reviewed regularly, at least annually, to check whether the recipients still need the keys.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Emergency keys (e.g., for the fire department) are stored in a sealed fire department key depot (FSD). Once a year, the key issuance list is reviewed, during which supervisors must confirm the necessity of the keys for their employees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the secure and compliant storage of the emergency keys. The logs of the annual key review are inspected for completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Instead of a mechanical locking system, an electronic access control system (ACS) with programmable keys (e.g., RFID cards) is used. Key management is fully automated and linked to the human resources management system. If a key is lost, it can be electronically blocked immediately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Key management is a module of the ACS. Authorizations are assigned on a role-based basis. When an employee leaves, their transponder is automatically blocked by the HR system. The issuance of transponders is logged in the system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the ACS and its connection to the HR system. It is tested whether a transponder reported as lost actually no longer grants access. The logs of authorization assignments are checked. Automated check: `check_access_control_system --verify 'hr_integration_active' --test_revocation 'user_xyz'`.

controls.title: Regulations for access to distribution cabinets (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Distribution cabinets (power, network) are often unlocked and accessible to everyone. There is no regulation for access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Network distribution cabinets are located in freely accessible corridors. The doors of the cabinets are not locked. Any employee can repatch patch cables.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor checks the physical condition and accessibility of distribution cabinets. It is determined whether they are unsecured.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Most distribution cabinets are locked. However, the group of people with keys is very large and not clearly defined or documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The facility management and the IT department have keys for the distribution cabinets, but it is not documented which employee has which key. Quick access in case of need is not always guaranteed, as it is unclear who is currently available.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the regulation for access to distribution cabinets and who has keys. It is assessed whether the group of authorized persons is too large.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to the distribution cabinets of all supply facilities in a building SHOULD be restricted to a small group of authorized persons. Access SHOULD be possible quickly in case of need.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Access to distribution rooms and cabinets is regulated. Only defined roles (e.g., network administrators, electricians) receive the corresponding keys or authorizations. The list of authorized persons is documented and kept up to date. It is ensured (e.g., through key deposit) that quick access is also possible outside of normal working hours.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the list of persons authorized to access distribution cabinets and checks whether it is restricted to the necessary minimum. The process for emergency access is checked (e.g., by reviewing the key deposit regulation).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to distribution cabinets is logged. With electronic locking systems, this is done automatically; with mechanical keys, by entry in a logbook.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Distribution rooms are connected to the electronic access control system. Every access is recorded with a timestamp and person. For cabinets with mechanical keys, a logbook is available in which everyone must sign in.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the access control system or the logbooks. It is checked whether the logging is complete and whether the entries are plausible.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to critical distribution cabinets is additionally monitored by video surveillance. Unauthorized attempts to open the cabinets (e.g., by drilling) are detected by sensors and trigger an alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Cameras are installed in the main distribution rooms, and their recordings are marked when an access event occurs. The doors of the distribution cabinets are equipped with opening and vibration sensors that are linked to the intruder alarm system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the video surveillance and the alarm sensors. The alarm chain for an unauthorized opening attempt is tested. Automated check: `check_alarm_system --asset 'distributor_cabinet_1' --verify 'vibration_sensor_active,alarm_to_soc_enabled'`.

controls.title: Lightning protection systems (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are no or only rudimentary lightning protection measures in place. A lightning protection concept is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The building may have an old lightning rod on the roof, but there is no internal lightning protection (surge protection).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines that a comprehensive lightning protection system is missing through a visual inspection of the building and the electrical distribution, as well as by interviewing the responsible persons.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An external lightning protection system (air terminals, down conductors) is in place. However, internal lightning protection is only incomplete or not implemented at all.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The lightning protection system on the roof is maintained, but in the sub-distribution boards for the IT, there is no fine protection against surges.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the maintenance logs for the external lightning protection and checks the electrical distribution boards for the presence of surge protection devices (SPDs) of types 1, 2, and 3.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A lightning protection system SHOULD be installed in accordance with the applicable standard. A comprehensive lightning and surge protection concept SHOULD be in place. The lightning protection system SHOULD be regularly inspected and maintained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A lightning protection system, consisting of external lightning protection (air terminals, down conductors) and internal lightning protection (surge protection on all lines leading into the building), is installed in accordance with the DIN EN 62305 (VDE 0185-305) series of standards. A lightning protection concept documents the selected protection class and the implemented measures. The system is regularly inspected by a lightning protection specialist.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the lightning protection concept and the inspection reports of the lightning protection system. It is verified whether the inspections are carried out on time and by qualified personnel and whether the system complies with the standard specifications.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The air terminals for buildings with extensive IT equipment SHOULD at least comply with protection class II according to DIN EN 62305 lightning protection. All incoming metallic lines (power, data, water) are included in the equipotential bonding.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A risk analysis according to DIN EN 62305-2 was carried out for the building, which led to the decision for the higher protection class II. The implementation of the equipotential bonding was planned in detail and checked by measurement during acceptance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the risk analysis and checks whether the protection class derived from it has been correctly implemented. The measurement protocols of the equipotential bonding are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The condition of the lightning and surge protection components is continuously monitored. Sensors report the tripping or aging of surge protection devices (SPDs) to a central management system to enable immediate replacement.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Remotely reportable SPDs are used, which report their status to the building management system or a DCIM system. This ensures that an unnoticed failure of the protection is prevented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the monitoring in the management system. The alarm chain in case of a status change of an SPD is checked. A test can be triggered by simulating a failure at the SPD. Automated check: `check_bms_device --type 'spd' --verify 'status_ok,remote_monitoring_active'`.

controls.title: Layout plans of supply lines (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are no or only very old, incomplete layout plans of the supply lines (power, water, gas).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In an emergency (e.g., a burst water pipe), the main shut-off valve has to be searched for a long time because nobody knows its exact location.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the plans of the supply lines. The absence or the obviously outdated state is documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Layout plans from the time the building was constructed exist. However, subsequent changes have not been entered into the plans.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The original construction plans are archived in paper form. Renovations from the last 20 years are not documented. The plans are only available at one central location and are not quickly at hand in an emergency.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly compares the existing plans with the visible installations and determines that they are no longer up-to-date. It is checked how quickly the plans would be available in case of need.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There SHOULD be up-to-date site plans of all utility lines. It SHOULD be regulated who maintains and updates the site plans of all utility lines. The plans SHOULD be stored in such a way that they are quickly available in case of need.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a defined process that stipulates that after every change to the utility lines, the corresponding plans (e.g., CAD plans) must be updated. The building services department is responsible for maintaining the plans. The plans are stored both digitally and as printouts in a defined, accessible location (e.g., in the building services office).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor has the process for updating the site plans explained. It is checked whether the plans were actually updated after recent modifications. The availability of the plans in an emergency is assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The plans SHOULD be stored in such a way that only authorized persons can access them. The plans are versioned and changes are documented in a traceable manner.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The digital site plans are managed in a document management system (DMS) with access restrictions. Each change creates a new version. The main shut-off devices for all utilities are clearly and permanently marked on site.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the access permissions for the plans in the DMS. The version history is checked for traceability. During an inspection, the labeling of the shut-off devices is verified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The site plans are part of a digital twin (Building Information Model, BIM) of the building. In an emergency, emergency services can access the plans via a mobile device and have the location of shut-off valves or switches displayed directly on site.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BIM model is continuously maintained. The fire department has secure digital access to the plan sections relevant to them. Sensors on the shut-off devices report their status (open/closed) to the system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the currency and level of detail of the BIM model. The process for access by external emergency services is checked. It is tested whether the statuses reported by the sensors match reality. Automated check: `check_bim_model --verify 'all_utilities_mapped,fire_dept_access_configured'`.

controls.title: Avoidance of location indicators for sensitive building parts (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Large signs revealing their function (e.g., 'Server Room', 'Archive') are posted on the doors of sensitive areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A sign 'Server Room - Access for IT personnel only' is on the server room door, providing a clear target for attackers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor determines whether sensitive areas are conspicuously marked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An attempt is made to avoid direct location indicators, but the function of the rooms is easy to guess from other features (e.g., loud fan noises, special doors).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The 'Server Room' sign has been removed, but the massive steel door and the loud air conditioning units still give the room away. The room is easily visible from the outside.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses whether sensitive areas are easy to identify by structural or operational features even without direct signage. The visibility from the outside is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Location indicators for sensitive areas SHOULD be avoided. Sensitive building areas SHOULD not be easily visible from the outside.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Sensitive rooms are labeled neutrally or with code designations (e.g., 'Technical Room T.01'). Windows of sensitive rooms on the ground floor are fitted with privacy film.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the labeling of sensitive areas for neutrality. The effectiveness of privacy protection measures is checked during an external inspection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When planning buildings or conversions, active care is taken to position sensitive areas without exterior windows and not along publicly accessible corridors.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Server rooms are preferably planned in the core of the building. Visitor routing is designed so that it does not lead past the doors to sensitive areas.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the building plans and the planned routing. It is assessed whether the 'Security by Design' principle has been applied with regard to the positioning of sensitive areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sensitive areas are structurally designed so that they do not differ from normal office spaces. Sound insulation measures are taken to prevent acoustic location (e.g., through fan noise).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Server rooms have the same doors as office rooms. The air conditioning is designed and soundproofed so that it cannot be heard outside the room. The waste heat is dissipated inconspicuously.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor tries to identify sensitive areas based on external characteristics (appearance, acoustics). The effectiveness of the camouflage and insulation measures is assessed.

controls.title: Structural smoke protection (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Fire doors are present, but are systematically wedged open or their closing mechanisms are defective. Fire barriers are missing or have not been resealed after subsequent cable installations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A fire door is propped open with a wooden wedge to facilitate passage. New network cables are simply run through a hole in the wall next to the existing firestop.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor checks the condition of fire doors and fire barriers. Obvious defects such as wedged doors or open penetrations are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The structural smoke protection components (doors, barriers) were correctly installed when the building was constructed. However, there is no process to ensure their functionality after modifications or over time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An electrician drills a new hole for a cable but does not seal it smoke-tight. The self-closers on smoke protection doors become weaker over the years and are not readjusted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks about the process for ensuring smoke protection during and after construction work. The closing function of smoke protection doors is tested on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Structural smoke protection SHOULD be checked after installation and conversion work. It SHOULD be regularly checked whether the smoke protection components are still functioning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process is established that requires that after any construction measure that penetrates walls or ceilings, an acceptance by the fire safety officer must take place. As part of the annual maintenance, all smoke protection doors and fire barriers are checked for their correct function and integrity. The results are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the acceptance reports after recent modifications. The logs of the annual maintenance of the smoke protection components are checked for completeness and the rectification of identified defects.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A firestop register is maintained, in which all fire barriers are documented with their exact location, type, and the cables run through them. Changes to fire barriers may only be carried out by trained personnel.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A register (e.g., in a CAFM software) lists all barriers and contains photos and manufacturer information. Only certified employees or specialist companies are allowed to make subsequent installations on barriers. Every change is documented in the register.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the firestop register and compares it with reality on a random basis. It is checked whether the qualification certificates of the persons who carry out changes to barriers are available. The traceability of the documentation is assessed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In highly sensitive areas, smoke pressure systems (SPS) are used, which create overpressure in the event of a fire to actively prevent smoke from entering protected areas (e.g., escape routes, server rooms). The functionality of the SPS is permanently monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: SPSs are installed in the stairwells and the anterooms to the data centers. These are controlled by the fire alarm system. The system status is reported to the building management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the planning and acceptance documents for the SPS. The maintenance logs and the records of the status monitoring are checked. The correct triggering in the event of a fire is verified as part of a full-scale test of the fire control system. Automated check: `check_bms_device --type 'rda' --verify 'status_ok,bma_linkage_active'`.

controls.title: Fire safety inspections (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Fire safety inspections do not take place, or only reactively after an incident or an official order.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The topic of fire protection only becomes relevant when the fire department comes for an inspection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for logs of fire safety inspections and finds that no regular inspections are carried out.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Fire safety inspections are carried out irregularly and without a fixed checklist. Identified defects are not systematically followed up.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The facility management occasionally walks through the building and checks things. If a defect is noticed (e.g., a blocked fire extinguisher), it is rectified, but there is no documentation or follow-up.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for evidence of inspections carried out. It is assessed whether the inspections are systematic and comprehensive and whether a process for defect rectification exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Fire safety inspections SHOULD take place regularly, i.e., at least once or twice a year. Defects identified during fire safety inspections SHOULD be rectified immediately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The fire safety officer conducts a formal fire safety inspection at least semi-annually using a standardized checklist. The results, including identified defects, are logged. A responsible person and a deadline for rectification are assigned for each defect.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the logs of the fire safety inspections for the last two years. It is checked whether the inspections take place regularly, whether they are systematic, and whether the identified defects have been demonstrably rectified in a timely manner.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In addition to the fire safety officer, representatives from IT, administration, and the works council participate in the fire safety inspections. The results are reported to the management.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The inspection is carried out as an interdisciplinary team to incorporate different perspectives. The results are summarized in a management report that assesses the status of fire protection and highlights necessary investments.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the attendance lists of the inspections and the management reports. It is assessed whether the inspection is used as an effective tool for controlling and improving fire protection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire safety inspections are carried out with a mobile app that enables a guided inspection based on checklists and transfers the results (incl. photos) directly to a central defect management system. The rectification of defects is automatically tracked and escalated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The fire safety officer uses a tablet with special software. Identified defects are created as a ticket in the defect management system and assigned to the responsible department. The system monitors the processing deadlines and sends reminders.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the workflow in the defect management system. The entire lifecycle of several defects is traced from logging to resolution. The effectiveness of automated tracking and escalation is assessed. Automated check: `check_ticket_system --category 'fire_safety' --verify 'all_tickets_closed_or_in_progress'`.

controls.title: Information for the Fire Safety Officer (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no fire safety officer, or this person is not informed about construction measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT department lays new cables through walls without asking or informing someone knowledgeable about fire protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks the IT and facility management departments how the fire safety officer is involved in their processes and finds that there is no involvement.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire safety officer is informed about major construction measures, but often only after they have already begun.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The janitor tells the fire safety officer over coffee that a wall will be breached next week. There is no formal, early involvement.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks the fire safety officer when and how they are informed about planned work. It is assessed whether the information is provided in a timely manner to still be able to have an influence.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The Fire Safety Officer SHOULD be informed about work on cable routes, corridors, and escape and rescue routes. This person SHOULD control the proper execution of fire protection measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a process (e.g., a work permit form) that ensures the fire safety officer is informed about all relevant work before it begins and must give their approval. The fire safety officer conducts on-site inspections during and after the work.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the process documentation and the completed permit forms for recently performed work. It is checked whether the fire safety officer's approval was obtained and whether inspections are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire safety officer is firmly involved as early as the planning phase of construction and renovation measures, and their requirements are incorporated into the tender.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The fire safety officer is part of the project team for construction measures. The fire protection requirements (e.g., for firestops, doors) are specified by them and are a binding part of the specifications for the executing companies.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the planning and tender documents for a construction project. It is verified that the fire safety officer was demonstrably involved and that their requirements were taken into account.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All work orders involving structural changes are managed via a central CAFM or ticketing system. A workflow ensures that orders affecting fire protection-relevant areas are automatically routed to the fire safety officer for review and approval. The order cannot be executed without this approval.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An employee requests a new network socket. The ticketing system recognizes, based on the location, that a wall penetration in a firewall is necessary and forwards the request to the fire safety officer. The officer can add requirements (e.g., 'Use of firestop XYZ, acceptance test required') to the ticket.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configured workflow in the ticketing system. It is tested whether a test ticket for fire protection-relevant work is correctly routed to the fire safety officer and whether the process is blocked without their approval. Automated check: `check_workflow_engine --ticket_type 'construction' --verify 'fire_safety_approval_gate_active'`.

controls.title: Alarm plan and fire drills (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no alarm plan. Fire drills do not take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In case of a fire, no one knows what to do exactly, except to leave the building. The emergency number is not known to everyone.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for the alarm plan and records of drills and notes their absence.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A simple alarm plan (e.g., as part of the fire safety regulations) is posted but is not actively communicated or practiced.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The 'Behavior in case of fire' notice is present, but outdated. The employees are informed about it once when they are hired, but there are no regular drills.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the posted plan and assesses its timeliness and completeness. By interviewing employees, it is determined whether the contents are known.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An alarm plan for the measures to be taken in the event of a fire SHOULD be created. The alarm plan SHOULD be reviewed and updated at regular intervals. Fire drills SHOULD be conducted regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A detailed alarm plan has been created, is known to all employees, and is posted in central locations. It is checked for timeliness annually. An unannounced evacuation drill is conducted at least once a year. Participation and results are recorded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the alarm plan and the records of its annual review. The records of the evacuation drills are checked, especially with regard to evacuation times and identified problems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire drills are systematically evaluated. The results of the evaluation, such as evacuation times that are too long or unclear instructions, are used to improve the alarm plan and the organization.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After each drill, a debriefing is held with the fire safety and evacuation assistants. An action plan to address the identified weaknesses is created and its implementation is tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes not only the records of the drills but also the documentation of the debriefings and the resulting action plans. It is assessed whether a genuine continuous improvement process has been established.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Different scenarios for fire drills are practiced (e.g., fire in the underground garage, smoke-filled escape route, failure of the fire alarm system). The drills are sometimes conducted in cooperation with the local fire department.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The annual plan for drills includes various realistic scenarios to test the flexibility of the emergency organization. At least every three years, a large-scale drill is held, in which the fire department and rescue services also participate, to practice coordination.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the drill plan and the scenario descriptions. The records and evaluations of the joint drills with external emergency services are analyzed.

controls.title: Burglary protection (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are no specific measures for burglary protection, except for the standard locks on doors and windows.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The ground floor windows do not have mushroom head locks. The entrance door has a simple lock with no special protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor assesses the existing mechanical security devices at potential entry points (doors, windows, basement windows) and finds them to be inadequate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sporadic burglary protection measures have been implemented, e.g., on the main entrance door. However, a consistent concept for the entire building is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The front door has been retrofitted with a security lock, but the easily accessible ground floor windows remain unsecured. There is no intruder alarm system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses whether the burglary protection at different points of the building shows a highly varied and overall incomplete level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Sufficient burglary protection measures adapted to the local conditions SHOULD be implemented. In planning, implementation, and operation, care SHOULD be taken to ensure that burglary protection is equivalent and consistent.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Based on a simple risk analysis, mechanical security devices are retrofitted on all easily accessible openings (doors, windows) (e.g., according to resistance class RC 2). Care is taken to ensure that no simple vulnerabilities (e.g., unsecured basement windows) remain.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies whether a consistent level of protection has been implemented at all potential points of entry. It is checked whether the implemented measures comply with recognized standards (e.g., RC classes).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The burglary protection SHOULD be regularly assessed by a competent person. The regulations for burglary protection SHOULD be known to the employees. In addition to mechanical security devices, an intruder alarm system (IAS) is installed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Every two years, an assessment of the burglary protection is carried out by an external security expert or the police crime prevention unit. An IAS secures the building's perimeter and is activated during absence. Employees are informed about the rules of conduct (close windows, activate IAS).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the reports of the external assessments and checks whether the recommendations have been implemented. The functionality of the IAS is checked. It is verified that the employees are informed about the regulations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An integrated security concept combines mechanical security devices (e.g., RC 3), a VdS-certified intruder alarm system with connection to a security service, and video surveillance at critical points. Burglary attempts are not only reported but also recorded on video.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IAS is linked to the video surveillance system, so that in the event of an alarm, the relevant camera images are automatically recorded and transmitted to the security service. This allows for a quick situation assessment and perpetrator identification. The IAS is serviced annually by a certified specialist company.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the VdS certificate of the intruder alarm system and the contract with the security service. The maintenance logs are checked. A test is run to check if the correct video images are recorded and transmitted in the event of an alarm. Automated check: `check_alarm_system --asset 'EMA' --verify 'vds_certified,video_integration_active'`.

controls.title: Regular updates of documentation (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Building documentation such as blueprints or escape route plans are severely outdated or cannot be found at all. No updates are made.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Only the original plans from 1980 are available. All renovations of the last decades are not documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor asks for relevant plans and finds that they obviously do not correspond to the current state of the building.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Plans are only updated for major, official construction measures. Minor changes made by the in-house facility management are not documented. A regular review does not take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After a major renovation, the blueprints are updated by the architect. If the facility management later installs a new line, this is not recorded in the plan.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the plans with reality and identifies discrepancies attributable to undocumented minor changes. It is checked whether there is a process for regular review.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The documentation of a building, e.g., blueprints, route plans, riser diagrams, escape route plans, and fire brigade route cards, SHOULD always be kept up to date. It SHOULD be checked at least once every three years whether all relevant plans are still current and correct.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A process is established that requires all changes to the building or to technical systems to be incorporated into the respective plans. A responsible body (e.g., building services or facility management) conducts and documents a formal review of all plans for currency at least every three years.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the records of the regular documentation review. It is checked on a random basis whether recent changes have been updated in the plans.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Employees SHOULD be informed about changes to the documentation, especially to escape and rescue plans. The documentation is managed digitally in a central system with version control.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All plans are managed in a CAFM or DMS system. Changes result in a new version. If escape and rescue plans are changed, all employees receive an e-mail notification and the new plans are posted immediately.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the information distribution process for plan changes. The version history in the central system is checked for traceability. It is checked whether the posted plans correspond to the current version in the system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire building documentation is integrated into a Building Information Model (BIM). Changes are made directly in the model, from which all derived plans (e.g., escape route plans) can be automatically regenerated. This ensures end-to-end consistency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central BIM team is responsible for maintaining the digital twin. All specialist planners and craftsmen are obliged to record their changes directly in the model (as-built documentation).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the process for maintaining the BIM model. It is verified whether the process for the automatic generation of plans is established and delivers consistent results. The maturity level of the as-built documentation is assessed.

controls.title: Secure doors and windows (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Doors and windows have no certified resistance class and offer only minimal protection against burglary.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Standard residential doors and windows without special security features are installed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines by visual inspection and review of the construction documents that no classified security components were used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In some particularly critical areas, such as the main entrance door, components with a basic resistance class (e.g., RC 2) were used. A comprehensive concept is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The door to the server room is an RC 2 door, but it is located next to an unsecured standard window, which represents an alternative point of attack.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses the equivalence of the security measures in an area and determines that weaknesses nullify the effect of individual good measures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Doors and windows SHOULD be selected in the appropriate classification according to the relevant standards, based on the protection goals of the area to be secured and the protection needs of the institution. All room-enclosing security measures involving windows, doors, and walls SHOULD be equivalent and appropriate with regard to burglary, fire, and smoke.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each security zone, a required resistance class (e.g., RC 2 for offices, RC 3 for server rooms) and fire resistance class (e.g., T30) is defined based on a risk analysis. During procurement, attention is paid to certified products and it is ensured that all enclosing surfaces (wall, door, window) offer an equivalent level of protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the risk analysis and the requirements for doors and windows derived from it. It is checked whether the installed components have the required certifications and whether the principle of equivalent resistance has been observed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be checked regularly that the security doors and windows are functional. This includes checking the locks, closers, and seals.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A maintenance plan provides for the annual inspection of all classified doors and windows by a specialist company. The inspection includes mechanical parts, locking functions and, in the case of fire doors, the hold-open systems. The maintenance is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the maintenance contracts and logs. The function of a security door (e.g., correct fit, closing behavior) is checked on-site on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security doors are equipped with sensors that report the status (open, closed, locked, blocked) to a central management console (IDS or building management system). Any deviation from the target state (e.g., a fire door left open for too long) triggers an alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Bolt contacts, magnetic contacts, and door closers are networked with the IDS. Rules are defined in the IDS, e.g., 'Trigger alarm if server room door is open for more than 60 seconds.' The status of all security doors is visualized on a dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the door monitoring in the IDS (Intrusion Detection System). The function is verified by practical tests (e.g., intentionally keeping a door open). The system logs are checked for relevant events and the subsequent reactions. Automated check: `check_ema_config --asset_type 'security_door' --verify 'state_monitoring_active,alarm_on_tamper_enabled'`.

controls.title: Formation of security zones (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no defined zone structure. Rooms with high and low protection needs are mixed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The server room is located directly next to the public reception area. Confidential files are stored in a freely accessible office space.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines through analysis of the floor plan and an on-site inspection that there is no logical structure based on protection needs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a rough division into a public and a non-public area. Within the non-public area, however, there is no further subdivision.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Visitors only have access to the reception area. Behind it, however, all employees have access to all areas, regardless of the individual protection needs of the rooms (e.g., HR office, server room).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the access control concept and determines that it lacks sufficient granularity to represent different protection needs within the internal area.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Rooms with similar protection needs SHOULD be grouped into zones in order to treat comparable risks uniformly and to reduce costs for necessary security measures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A zone concept (e.g., based on the onion model) is created and documented. It typically defines zones such as 'Public Area', 'Internal Area', 'Protected Zone', and 'High-Security Zone'. Uniform security requirements (e.g., access control, intrusion protection) are defined for each zone.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the zone concept and checks whether the grouping of rooms into zones is logical and traceable. It is checked whether the security measures defined for a zone are consistently applied to all rooms in that zone.

parts.name: statement
