Data transmission capabilities are technically limited to the operational minimum wherever possible or actively monitored to enforce compliance with policies. Security requirements are dynamically updated based on threat analyses.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution commissions specialized service providers to conduct technical security analyses of vehicle types before fleet procurement. Technical measures (e.g., via gateways or configuration changes) are implemented to prevent unwanted data transmission. The results are incorporated into an internal knowledge base.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the reports of technical security audits and verifies how their results were implemented in the procurement process. It is checked whether technical controls to limit data flows are implemented and whether a process for updating security requirements based on new threat intelligence exists and is actively followed. An automated scan of the vehicles for active data services can verify conformity.

controls.title: Maintenance, Inspection and Updates (B) [Subject Matter Experts, IT Operations]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintenance is performed purely reactively when a defect occurs. Updates for IT components are installed sporadically or not at all. There are no clear rules about who performs maintenance or installs updates.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is no maintenance plan. Drivers are instructed to go to any workshop in case of problems. OTA update requests on the display are either ignored or confirmed by the drivers at their own discretion.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the vehicle history for planned vs. unplanned workshop visits. A lack of maintenance plans and records is an indicator of this maturity level. Software versions of IT components are checked on a random basis and compared with the currently available versions; large discrepancies confirm the inadequate provision of updates.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Vehicle maintenance follows the basic manufacturer's specifications. Updates are installed when the system prompts for them, but without a defined process or environmental controls. After maintenance, basic functional tests are performed, but not systematically using a checklist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Vehicles are taken to the workshop at the intervals specified by the manufacturer. OTA updates are usually initiated by the driver. After maintenance, the driver checks whether the vehicle drives and the essential systems are functioning.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the maintenance records and compares them with the manufacturer's specifications. It is checked whether a process for the release and installation of updates exists. The absence of standardized checklists for acceptance after maintenance indicates this maturity level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The vehicles and the associated IT components MUST be maintained according to the manufacturer's specifications. It MUST be clearly regulated who is allowed to install updates and in which environment. Over-the-Air (OTA) updates MUST also be installed in a regulated manner. Maintenance and repair work MUST be carried out by authorized personnel in a secure environment. It SHOULD be clarified before maintenance how to deal with third-party companies. Upon return to service, a checklist MUST be used to check whether all defects have been rectified and the IT components are operational.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A maintenance and update plan exists. It is defined that updates may only be installed by authorized personnel (e.g., IT operations) and in a trusted environment (e.g., in the corporate network). A standardized checklist is used for acceptance after maintenance, which also includes the checking of IT security functions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and adherence to maintenance and update plans. It is checked whether regulations for update installation and dealing with third-party companies exist. The completed acceptance checklists are checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dealing with third-party companies during maintenance work is regulated by binding contractual agreements (e.g., confidentiality agreements, security requirements for the workshop). OTA updates are managed via a central policy and ideally centrally approved before drivers can install them. The checklist used after maintenance is detailed, archived in a revision-proof manner, and contains specific IT security checkpoints.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before awarding maintenance work to a workshop, a data processing agreement or a comparable security agreement is concluded. A fleet management tool is used to monitor the update status of the vehicles and to control OTA updates centrally. The checklist is digitally stored as part of the maintenance record.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor inspects the contracts with external workshops for security clauses. The procedure for managing OTA updates is checked, ideally by inspecting the configuration of the fleet management tool. The completeness and quality of the digitally archived acceptance protocols are audited.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central, automated system manages maintenance schedules and the distribution of updates. Any third-party access to the vehicle IT during maintenance is strictly controlled and logged. The post-maintenance check is automated where possible (e.g., via scripts that check the configuration and functionality of IT systems) and generates compliance reports.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An advanced fleet management system is used that proactively reports maintenance needs (predictive maintenance) and enables fully automated patch management for the vehicle IT. For maintenance by third parties, a special, read-only "workshop mode" is activated, which prevents access to sensitive data and functions. Automated health checks after each workshop visit check the integrity of the systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and logs of the central management system. It is checked whether technical protective measures such as a "workshop mode" are implemented and used. The reports of the automated verification runs after maintenance are evaluated to assess the effectiveness of the process. An automated scan of the vehicle configuration can be used to verify correctness.

controls.title: Regulations for vehicle use (B) [IT Operations, Subject Matter Experts, Users, Data Protection Officers]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all activities that may affect the security of the information processed in the vehicles, it MUST be regulated beforehand whether they may be carried out in the vehicles. It MUST be clearly regulated which information may be transported and processed and what protective measures must be taken. It MUST be regulated to what extent infotainment systems, applications, and other vehicle services may be used. Business or service instructions MUST describe how carried IT may be used and stored in the vehicles.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal vehicle usage policy is created and communicated to all users. This policy contains clear chapters on information classification and the resulting protective measures (e.g., 'confidential documents must not be left in the vehicle'), on the use of the infotainment system (e.g., 'private smartphones must not be paired with the vehicle'), and on the storage of mobile devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence, completeness, and awareness of the vehicle usage policy. Knowledge of the regulations is verified on a random basis through interviews with users. During a vehicle inspection, it is checked whether the regulations are being complied with (e.g., no unsecured laptops, no unauthorized paired devices in the infotainment system).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The usage policy is detailed, regularly reviewed, and its acknowledgment by employees is ensured through mandatory training. It contains specific rules for different data classification levels and provides clear instructions for the secure configuration of infotainment systems (e.g., deactivating automatic contact synchronization).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Annual, mandatory security awareness training sessions are held, which include a module on secure vehicle use. The policy contains illustrated instructions on how to disable certain insecure functions in the infotainment system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies participation in the training courses on the basis of training records. It is checked whether the policy is reviewed regularly (e.g., annually) and updated as necessary. During the technical inspection of vehicles, it is checked whether the recommended secure configurations on the infotainment system are actually implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the usage policy is enforced by technical measures wherever possible. The use of vehicle systems is logged and checked for compliance with the policies. Regular, scenario-based security training sessions are conducted to test the awareness and correct response of employees.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Mobile Device Management (MDM) policies are enforced on carried devices to prevent insecure connections to the vehicle. Certain functions of the infotainment system (e.g., app installation, WLAN hotspot) are centrally deactivated by the IT department. Unannounced inspections (spot checks) of the vehicles are carried out.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the technical control mechanisms (e.g., MDM, vehicle configuration). Log data of vehicle use is evaluated to identify policy violations. The execution and results of the scenario-based training and spot checks are reviewed.

controls.title: Creation of a security policy (S) [Subject Matter Experts, IT Operations]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All relevant security requirements for the IT within the vehicles SHOULD be documented in a security policy that is mandatory for employees. The policy SHOULD be known to all relevant employees of the institution and form the basis for their handling of vehicles. The policy SHOULD clearly regulate the responsibilities for individual tasks. The security policy SHOULD be reviewed regularly and updated on an ad-hoc basis.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central document 'Vehicle Use Security Policy' will be created, summarizing all relevant aspects (usage, maintenance, information security, emergency procedures). The document will be published on the intranet, and employees will be informed via email. A person responsible for maintaining the policy will be designated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the security policy and checks its existence and completeness. It is verified whether responsibilities are clearly defined and whether a date of the last review is present. Through interviews with employees, it is checked on a random basis whether the policy is known.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is a formal document approved by management and mandatory for all employees. It is integrated into the onboarding process for new employees. The policy is reviewed at least annually or in the event of significant changes (e.g., new vehicle types, new threats). A clear process for policy exceptions is defined and documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Acknowledgement of the policy must be confirmed in writing or digitally by each employee upon hiring and in the event of significant changes. A formal review meeting for the policy is held annually, attended by subject matter experts, IT operations, and the ISO. Exception requests must be justified in writing and approved by the ISO.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the formal approval of the policy and the documented evidence of acknowledgement by the employees. The minutes of the annual review meetings and the documented exception requests are checked. The timeliness of the policy is assessed with regard to the technology used and known risks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security policy is an integral part of the institution's ISMS. Its effectiveness is measured by defined metrics (e.g., number of reported security incidents in the vehicle environment) and regular audits. The policy is dynamically updated based on risk analyses and current threat information. The employees' understanding of the policy is tested regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The policy is linked to other ISMS documents (e.g., Risk Management, Incident Response Plan). Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) on policy compliance are collected and reported to management. As part of awareness campaigns, short tests or quizzes on the content of the policy are conducted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor assesses the integration of the policy into the ISMS. The defined metrics and the associated reports are analyzed. The minutes of risk analyses are checked to see if the results have led to an adjustment of the policy. The results of the employees' comprehension tests are reviewed.

controls.title: Creation of an inventory list (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An inventory list SHOULD be maintained for each vehicle, covering permanently installed or associated IT components, the specialized applications running on them, operating instructions, and mobile devices paired with the infotainment system. The inventory list SHOULD be updated regularly and on an ad-hoc basis. It SHOULD be verified that all inventoried IT components are present and that no unauthorized mobile devices have been paired.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each vehicle, an inventory list is kept as a table (e.g., in a spreadsheet). This is stored in a central location. The list is checked and updated during every major maintenance or when a user changes. In particular, the list of paired Bluetooth devices is manually checked in the infotainment system and compared with the inventory list.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests inventory lists for several vehicles on a random basis. It is checked whether the lists are complete and kept up-to-date (identifiable by the modification date). During a vehicle inspection, the list is compared with reality, especially the list of paired devices in the infotainment system. An `ls /dev/` on a Linux-based infotainment system can help identify connected devices.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The inventory is managed in a central asset management system. The process for updating the inventory list is formalized and subject to periodic checks. The process for checking for unauthorized paired devices is documented and carried out regularly (e.g., at every vehicle return).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The vehicle IT is created as a separate asset category in the central IT asset management system. When a pool vehicle is returned, a checklist is followed that explicitly requires checking and clearing the paired devices. The execution is logged by the fleet manager.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor is granted read access to the asset management system and verifies the completeness and timeliness of the entries for the vehicle fleet. The logs of vehicle returns are checked on a random basis to verify the consistent execution of the device check.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Inventory management is largely automated. Agent-based or network scan tools detect and track IT assets in the vehicle. Attempts to pair unauthorized devices are automatically detected and blocked, or an alarm is triggered. The vehicle inventory list is fully integrated into the central Configuration Management Database (CMDB).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A fleet management system with a telematics connection is used, which reports the status and configuration of the vehicle IT to Asset Management in real time. Security policies on the infotainment system prevent the pairing of unapproved devices. Corresponding events are forwarded to a SIEM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and data flows between the telematics system and the CMDB. The configuration of the security policies on the infotainment systems is checked. The SIEM logs are searched for alarms regarding unauthorized pairing attempts to verify the effectiveness of the control.

controls.title: Definition of operating instructions (S) [Subject Matter Experts, Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all essential situations affecting the information security of vehicles, operating instructions SHOULD be available in the form of checklists. These SHOULD be integrated into the security policy and be available in a suitable form in the vehicle. In particular, the scenarios of IT component failure, emergency situations such as accidents, unauthorized entry, and theft SHOULD be covered. Responsibilities SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Short, concise checklists for the most important emergencies (accident, theft, IT failure) are created. These are deposited as part of the vehicle folder in the glove compartment. The checklists contain clear instructions and the telephone numbers of the responsible internal departments (e.g. IT helpdesk, ISO).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor randomly checks vehicles for the presence of the emergency checklists. The content of the checklists is checked for completeness and correctness (especially of the contact persons and telephone numbers). Employees are asked whether they know about the existence and location of the checklists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The checklists are detailed, laminated, and physically present in every vehicle. Employees receive training on these procedures. A clear 24/7 contact point for reporting security incidents is established and noted on the checklists. The procedures include, where applicable, steps for remote data erasure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The emergency checklists are designed as robust, laminated cards. Training on the procedures is part of the annual security briefing. The 24/7 contact point is the company's own Security Operations Center (SOC). The checklist for theft includes the instruction to immediately inform the SOC in order to initiate tracking and, if necessary, remote wiping of devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and accessibility of the 24/7 contact point. Training materials and records are checked to ensure that employees have been instructed. The content of the checklists is checked for further measures such as remote wiping.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The checklists are digital and context-dependent, e.g., available via an app on the company smartphone. The completion of the checklist items is logged digitally. The response to incidents is fully integrated into the central incident response process of the SOC/CERT, and the procedures are regularly tested through exercises.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An emergency app on the company smartphones guides the user through the necessary steps and simultaneously transmits relevant data (e.g. location) to the SOC. The app allows for the direct creation of an incident ticket. Emergency drills, e.g. simulating a vehicle theft, are held annually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the functionality of the emergency app and the process integration with the incident management system. Logs from the digital checklists and the associated incident tickets are analyzed. The planning documents and result reports of the emergency drills are audited.

controls.title: Proper handling of vehicles and sensitive information (S) [Subject Matter Experts, Users]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution SHOULD supplement regulations on when, how, and where vehicles are to be properly parked to protect them from unauthorized access or damage. It SHOULD be considered what information and IT systems may be stored in the vehicles. Sufficient access protection measures SHOULD be taken. Sensitive information SHOULD not be visible or audible from the outside. Employees SHOULD be familiarized with the basic functioning of the vehicles and IT components and informed about security risks.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The vehicle security policy defines clear rules for parking (e.g., 'preferably in well-lit areas'), locking the vehicle, and handling information (e.g., 'do not leave documents in plain sight', 'store laptop in the trunk'). As part of the vehicle briefing, users are made aware of these rules and general risks (e.g., relay attacks on keyless systems).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the policy for corresponding regulations. Compliance with the rules is checked on a random basis through observation in the company car park or through unannounced inspections (e.g., are vehicles locked, are laptops visible in the car?). Employees are asked about the risks known to them.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The policy defines secure parking locations (e.g., company garage, guarded parking lots) and prohibits parking in known high-risk areas. It specifies exactly which types of documents and devices must be removed from the vehicle when absent. Technical measures such as privacy screens for laptops or permanently installed, lockable cassettes are required for certain scenarios. The topic is covered in the annual security briefing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution provides lockable document cases for the transport of confidential documents. Laptops that remain in the vehicle must be locked in a permanently installed safe in the trunk. The training content includes concrete demonstrations of attacks (e.g., videos of relay attacks).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks whether the required additional equipment (safes, cases, privacy screens) is present and used in the relevant vehicles. Training materials are checked for specific content. Compliance with parking rules is verified, if necessary, by evaluating GPS tracking data.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The vehicle's location is actively monitored. Alarms are triggered when parking in unauthorized or areas classified as unsafe. All data on carried devices is fully encrypted by default. The effectiveness of the policy and protective measures is verified through regular, unannounced inspections (spot checks).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A geofencing system in the fleet management triggers an alarm in the SOC if a vehicle is parked for an extended period in an area classified as critical. All laptops and smartphones are secured with BitLocker or equivalent encryption, enforced via MDM. Security personnel conduct regular checks on the company premises and document violations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the geofencing system and the associated alarm logs in the SIEM. The MDM configuration for encryption is checked. The logs of the conducted spot checks are evaluated to assess practical compliance. The encryption status can be automatically checked on Windows laptops using `manage-bde -status`.

controls.title: Protection against weather-related influences (S) [Users, Subject Matter Experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Vehicles and the IT components installed in them SHOULD be adequately protected from weather-related influences. Depending on the vehicle type, location, and operating environment, additional protective measures SHOULD be taken. Appropriate protective measures SHOULD be taken for short-term extreme weather events. These protective measures SHOULD be documented in the operating instructions for vehicle use in the form of checklists.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The vehicle usage policy includes a chapter on protection against weather influences. It instructs drivers to park vehicles in the shade during strong sunlight and not to expose mobile electronic devices to direct sunlight. There is a special checklist for operations in extreme conditions (e.g., winter use in the mountains).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the usage policy and the existence of checklists for extreme weather conditions. The drivers' knowledge of the protective measures is verified by interviewing them. Failure statistics of IT components in vehicles can be analyzed for possible correlations with weather events.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Clear policies exist that, for example, mandate the use of covered parking spaces under certain weather conditions (hail, extreme heat). The operating temperature ranges for carried IT are specified, and equipment such as sun visors or additional ventilation is provided for mission-critical IT. Checklists for use in extreme weather are consistently used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution rents covered parking spaces for its vehicle fleet. For vehicles with permanently installed, temperature-sensitive IT, additional fans or air conditioning systems for the electronics cabinet are retrofitted. The checklist for winter use prescribes, for example, carrying and checking snow chains and using antifreeze.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the vehicle equipment (e.g., sun visors, fans). It is checked whether the parking policies are being followed (e.g., by inspecting the parking lots). The completed checklists from operations in extreme weather conditions are randomly checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Vehicles used in extreme environments are specially hardened (e.g., through specialized heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems for electronics bays). The environmental conditions inside the vehicle are remotely monitored, and alarms are triggered if the operating parameters for critical IT systems are exceeded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For operations in desert regions, vehicles with special insulation and active cooling for the IT systems are procured. Temperature sensors in the vehicle report their data in real-time to the fleet management system. If the limit values are exceeded or fallen below, the driver and the control center are automatically alerted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the specifications of the hardened vehicles and the configuration of the monitoring system. The alarm logs are evaluated to verify the monitoring function. The recorded temperature data is compared with the specifications of the installed IT components. The status of the sensors can be queried via `snmpwalk` or the monitoring system's API.

controls.title: Ensuring Supply (S) [Subject Matter Experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Before vehicles are deployed, it SHOULD be planned how they will be supplied with operating fluids during the mission. The vehicles SHOULD always be adequately supplied with operating fluids during the mission.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A policy stipulates that pool vehicles must be refueled to at least a certain level (e.g., half full) upon return. For longer or critical missions, the supply of operating fluids (fuel, AdBlue, etc.) is roughly planned in advance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the existence of the refueling policy. Compliance with the supply plan is verified on a random basis by checking logbooks and fuel receipts. The fuel level is checked during vehicle inspections.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal logistics plan is created for long or critical missions. Fuel levels are remotely monitored via telematics. Drivers are automatically reminded to refuel when the fuel level is low. Framework agreements exist with certain gas station chains to simplify payment and ensure supply.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The fleet management system is configured to send an email to the driver and the fleet manager if the fuel level drops below 25%. All vehicles are equipped with fuel cards that work at partner gas stations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the fleet management system and the alerting rules. The framework agreements with gas station chains are reviewed. The recorded telematics data on fuel levels are evaluated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire supply chain is managed and optimized based on planned routes and real-time vehicle data. Mobile refueling capacities are available for critical missions. The supply status is a key metric in the control center's operational dashboard.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A logistics software calculates the optimal time and location for refueling stops based on the planned route and current fuel prices. For large-scale operations (e.g., during disasters), a fuel tanker is included as part of the convoy. The central dashboard displays the current fuel level and remaining range for each operational vehicle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the functionality of the logistics software and the integration of real-time vehicle data. The planning documents for critical missions are checked for the consideration of mobile refueling. The view of the operational dashboard is audited.

controls.title: Decommissioning (S) [IT Operations, Subject Matter Experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When vehicles are decommissioned, no information worthy of protection SHOULD remain in the vehicles. Before vehicles are finally decommissioned, the inventory list SHOULD be used to check that no inventoried items and, in addition, no other relevant items have been left behind.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a checklist for vehicle decommissioning. It requires removing all personal items, resetting the IT systems (navigation device, infotainment) to factory settings, and checking the inventory list to ensure all institution-owned devices (e.g., handheld radios, SIM cards) have been removed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor requests the decommissioning checklist and checks it for completeness. For an upcoming decommissioning, the process is monitored and the completion of the checklist is verified. For vehicles that have already been decommissioned, the records are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal, documented decommissioning process is established. This includes the secure deletion of data on all IT systems according to recognized standards. The implementation of the measures is confirmed in a decommissioning record, which is attached to the vehicle file.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The process is carried out by trained personnel (IT Operations). In addition to resetting to factory settings, secure deletion methods (e.g., multiple overwriting) are used if technically possible. The decommissioning record is signed by the IT manager and the fleet manager.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the formal decommissioning process documentation and the signed records. It is checked whether the applied deletion methods correspond to the state of the art. The training records of the personnel are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Decommissioning is carried out exclusively by specially trained personnel. Wherever available, the 'Cryptographic Erase' function is used to make data unreadable by destroying the cryptographic key. Data carriers that cannot be securely erased (e.g., certain solid-state drives) are physically removed and verifiably destroyed. The entire process is audited, and a complete record is kept for the entire lifecycle of the vehicle.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The institution has detailed instructions for each vehicle type on how to securely erase or remove the IT systems. A certified service provider is commissioned for the physical destruction of data carriers, which issues a certificate of destruction. The decommissioning is documented by video or carried out according to the four-eyes principle.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the detailed technical instructions and the service provider's certificates of destruction. It is checked whether a complete record is kept for each vehicle from procurement to the certified destruction of the data. The records (video, logs) of the decommissioning are checked on a random basis.

controls.title: Contingency measures for failures (H) [Subject Matter Experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the event that vehicles or drivers fail, preparatory measures SHOULD be taken within the institution. Depending on the importance of the vehicles, replacement vehicles SHOULD be available, or alternatively, a framework agreement SHOULD be concluded with a suitable external institution. In addition, replacement drivers SHOULD be available.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For critical vehicle types, at least one replacement vehicle is kept in the own fleet. In addition, there is a framework agreement with a car rental company that guarantees the short-term provision of additional vehicles. There is a list of qualified employees who can step in as replacement drivers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of the replacement vehicle in the vehicle fleet. The framework agreement with the car rental company is inspected and checked for its validity and the guaranteed response times. The list of substitute drivers is checked for up-to-dateness and the qualifications of the individuals.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A formal Business Continuity Plan (BCP) for vehicle operations is documented. This plan ensures the guaranteed availability of replacement vehicles and drivers through contracts with defined Service Level Agreements (SLAs). The plan is tested regularly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BCP specifies exactly within what timeframe (e.g., within 4 hours) a fully equipped replacement vehicle must be available. This is contractually regulated with a service provider. The availability of substitute drivers is ensured via an on-call schedule. A BCP exercise simulating a vehicle failure is conducted annually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the BCP for completeness and plausibility. The contracts with service providers are checked for compliance with the defined SLAs. The planning and results documentation of the BCP exercises is audited.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The BCP for vehicle operations is fully integrated into the institution's overall Business Continuity Management (BCM). A 'hot standby' fleet of fully equipped and immediately ready-to-use vehicles is maintained. Driver availability is tracked in real time. The switchover process to replacement resources is automated as much as possible and can be executed within a very short time.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The replacement vehicles are ready in a garage, fully fueled and with all IT systems charged. A personnel deployment planning system shows at all times which qualified drivers are immediately available. In the event of a failure, the dispatcher in the fleet management system can assign and alert a replacement vehicle and driver with just a few clicks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the integration of the vehicle BCP into the ISMS/BCMS. The condition and operational readiness of the hot standby fleet are checked on site. The functionality of the personnel deployment planning system and the alerting process is demonstrated or proven by logs.

controls.title: Anti-theft protection or guarding (H) [Subject matter experts, employees]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An alarm system SHOULD be present. For ground vehicles, an immobilizer SHOULD also be present. When the vehicle is left unattended, the alarm system and immobilizer SHOULD be activated. Alternatively, the vehicles SHOULD be guarded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All vehicles are equipped with at least the standard factory-installed alarm system and immobilizer. During their orientation and in the usage policy, vehicle users are obliged to always lock the vehicle, which activates these systems. In particularly critical situations, the vehicle is guarded by personnel.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the equipment of the vehicles based on the vehicle specifications. The usage policy is checked for the obligation to activate the security systems. Compliance with this rule is checked on a random basis through observation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A certified alarm system with GPS tracking and the ability to remotely shut down the engine is installed. The policy strictly requires activation every time the vehicle is left. In high-risk areas, identified through a risk assessment, additional guarding is deployed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All vehicles are equipped with a telematics system that, in addition to GPS tracking, also allows the immobilizer to be controlled. Fleet management is instructed to activate the remote shutdown after a theft report and in consultation with the police. A list of high-risk areas is maintained and communicated to the drivers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the specification of the alarm system and the functionality of the remote control options in the telematics system. The risk assessment for identifying high-risk areas is reviewed. The process instruction for the event of a theft is audited.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The vehicle is protected by a multi-layered system: a certified alarm system, GPS tracking, remote shutdown, and geofencing that triggers an alarm if the vehicle is moved without authorization. For critical goods or in high-risk situations, constant surveillance (either by physical personnel or by remote video surveillance) is maintained.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The geofencing is configured to send a silent alarm to the SOC if a vehicle leaves a defined area (e.g., the parking lot) outside of operating hours. For the transport of highly critical goods, an escort vehicle or permanent video surveillance via 4G/5G is used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the geofencing system and the associated alarm logs in the SIEM. The plans and logs of the surveillance measures for critical transports are checked. The functionality of the overall system can be verified by a simulated theft test.

controls.title: Damaging external influence (H) [Subject matter experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Depending on the type of vehicles, appropriate measures SHOULD be taken to protect the vehicles from potential external influences in the planned operating environment, such as interfering radio emissions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is an awareness of risks such as GPS jamming. The driver briefing points out the possible behavior of the navigation system in case of interference and alternative navigation methods (e.g., map, app on the smartphone) are recommended as a backup.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the training materials for information on external influences. It is inquired whether a risk assessment for such scenarios has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A risk assessment is conducted to identify likely external threats (e.g., GPS jamming, strong RF interference). Based on this, countermeasures such as shielded cables, filtered antennas, or redundant navigation systems (e.g., inertial navigation as a supplement to GPS) are implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For vehicles used in critical areas, navigation systems are procured that use other satellite systems (Galileo, GLONASS) in addition to GPS and have inertial navigation. The cabling of critical systems is specially shielded.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the risk assessment and the protective measures derived from it. The technical specifications of the installed components (navigation systems, cables) are checked to verify the implementation of the measures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The vehicle is equipped with active countermeasures and detection systems for external threats. For example, a GPS anti-jamming system is used and the radio spectrum is monitored for anomalies. Where required, the vehicle is hardened against electromagnetic pulses (EMP).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Special vehicles are equipped with military or industrial anti-jamming and anti-spoofing GPS receivers. An on-board spectrum analyzer warns the driver and the SOC of unusual radio signals. The electronics are housed in an EMP-protected enclosure.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the certifications and specifications of the active protection systems. The configuration of the monitoring systems and the alarm logs are analyzed. Evidence of EMP hardening (e.g., test certificates) is reviewed.

controls.title: Protection of sensitive information from unauthorized access and disclosure (H) [IT operations, Subject matter experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Vehicles and their associated IT components SHOULD be secured in such a way that sensitive information cannot be read, manipulated, or deleted by unauthorized persons. The existing protective measures of the manufacturing companies SHOULD be checked and, if necessary, adjusted.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Basic security functions of the vehicle IT are activated. This includes setting a PIN code for the infotainment system and deactivating unnecessary wireless interfaces such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi when not in use. The manufacturer's documentation is checked for security recommendations.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During a vehicle inspection, the auditor checks whether the basic security mechanisms (e.g., PIN protection) are active. The configuration settings of the infotainment system are checked. It is checked whether a documented review of the manufacturer's security notices has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data storage within the vehicle, both in the on-board systems and on added devices, is encrypted. Access controls to the systems are hardened according to the principle of least privilege. A security assessment of the vehicle IT systems is conducted and identified vulnerabilities are remediated or accepted based on a risk assessment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Hard drives in retrofitted industrial PCs are encrypted with BitLocker or a comparable solution. Access to administrative functions of the vehicle IT requires two-factor authentication. An external company is commissioned to conduct a penetration test of the vehicle IT.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the encryption status of the data carriers. The configuration of the access controls is analyzed. The penetration test report and the follow-up on its findings are reviewed. The encryption of data carriers can be verified using `manage-bde -status` (Windows) or `lsblk -f` (Linux).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hardware Security Modules (HSM) or Trusted Platform Modules (TPM) are used for the secure storage of cryptographic keys and for cryptographic operations. Data transmission is protected by strong, mutually authenticated protocols (e.g., mTLS). The vehicle's IT is continuously monitored for unauthorized access attempts or configuration changes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The hard drive encryption uses keys that are protected in the on-board computer's TPM. The communication between the vehicle and the headquarters is secured by a VPN with certificate authentication. A Host-based Intrusion Detection System (HIDS) on the on-board computer reports integrity violations to the SIEM.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the key management (TPM, HSM) and the HIDS configuration. The VPN configuration is checked for strong algorithms and mTLS. The SIEM logs are analyzed for relevant alarms from the vehicles. Automated scripts can check the TPM configuration (e.g., via `tpm_version` on Linux) and the HIDS rules.

controls.title: Physical securing of interfaces (H) [IT operations, Subject matter experts]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All physical internal and external interfaces of the vehicles SHOULD be physically secured against unauthorized use and external influences.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Easily accessible USB ports in the passenger compartment are sealed with simple plastic plugs when not in use. Drivers are instructed not to connect any unknown USB devices.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor performs a visual inspection of the accessible interfaces in the vehicle. The usage policy is checked for corresponding instructions to the drivers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Unused physical interfaces (USB, Ethernet, etc.) are disabled in the software or physically blocked with lockable mechanisms. The OBD-II interface is secured with a lock or moved to a location that is difficult to access.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: USB ports are disabled via BIOS/UEFI settings or by Group Policy. A special lock (OBD saver) is used for the OBD-II interface. The installation is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor physically checks the security of the interfaces, especially the OBD-II port. An attempt is made to connect a device to a disabled USB port to test the effectiveness of the measure. The configuration of the software deactivation is checked, e.g., by reading the BIOS settings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A combination of physical and logical controls is used. Access to physical interfaces requires authentication (e.g., port-based network access control according to IEEE 802.1X). Critical interfaces are located in tamper-proof, sealed, and locked enclosures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The Ethernet port of the on-board computer is configured with 802.1X and only allows connections from devices with a valid certificate. The computer itself is housed in an enclosure with seals, the integrity of which is checked regularly.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the port-based access control (e.g., on the switch or the end device). The integrity of the seals is physically checked. An attempt is made to connect an unauthorized device in order to provoke a rejection by the access control and to verify this in the logs.

controls.title: Fire extinguishing system (H) [Specialist responsible]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The vehicles SHOULD have a fire extinguishing system that can extinguish a fire from the outside and inside. Alternatively, suitable means of firefighting SHOULD be carried.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard, serviced portable fire extinguisher is carried in each vehicle. The drivers are instructed in its use.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the presence and maintenance date of the fire extinguisher in each vehicle. The drivers' training records for firefighting are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automatic fire extinguishing system is installed in high-risk areas such as the engine compartment or the electronics cabinet. Users are effectively trained in handling the portable manual extinguishing agents.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In vehicles with extensive IT equipment, an automatic extinguishing system (e.g., with gas as the extinguishing agent) is installed in the IT systems rack. The drivers' training includes practical exercises with a fire extinguisher trainer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence and the maintenance log of the automatic extinguishing system. The documentation of the practical fire protection exercises is inspected.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A highly developed, integrated fire detection and extinguishing system is installed, covering all critical vehicle compartments. It uses extinguishing agents that are harmless to electronics and automatically triggers alarms to a monitoring center.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The system combines smoke and heat detectors in different zones of the vehicle. In the event of an alarm, not only is the extinguishing system activated, but the power supply to the affected components is also automatically cut off and an emergency call with GPS coordinates is sent to the SOC.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the planning documents and the configuration of the integrated fire detection and extinguishing system. The alarm chain to the SOC is tested (e.g., by a test alarm). The system's logs are checked for past events and false alarms.

controls.title: Network separation of the in-vehicle network with a special vehicle network via gateways (H)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In general, the institution SHOULD ensure that no information is exchanged between the In-Vehicle-Network (IVN), which is connected to the vehicle manufacturer's networks, and the mission-specific IT components in an unauthorized and undefined manner. For this purpose, gateways with standardized protocols SHOULD be used. The gateways SHOULD be approved by the vehicle manufacturing company.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A gateway recommended by the manufacturer is used to connect special IT (e.g., a diagnostic laptop) to the vehicle bus. The gateway's configuration only allows the communication that is absolutely necessary for the application. Direct, uncontrolled connections are avoided.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the vehicle's network plan and the specifications of the gateway used. It is checked whether there is an approval from the manufacturer for the gateway. The gateway's configuration is checked for plausibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A certified, manufacturer-approved gateway is used. It is configured with a strict default-deny rule set that only allows explicitly defined messages between the IVN and the special network. The gateway's configuration is centrally managed and audited.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The gateway is configured to function as a pure firewall. Only specific CAN IDs or Ethernet frames that are necessary for the function of the special IT are allowed through. Any change to the gateway configuration requires an approved change request and is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the firewall rules of the gateway in detail. It is checked whether the 'default-deny' principle has been implemented. The change management logs for configuration changes to the gateway are audited. Network traffic can be captured and verified against the rule list.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A high-assurance gateway with intrusion detection capabilities is used. It not only filters traffic but also monitors it for anomalies and attacks on the vehicle bus. All traffic between the segments is logged and analyzed. The gateway itself is a hardened device with Secure Boot and remote attestation functions.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The gateway uses Deep Packet Inspection for the vehicle bus traffic and compares it with a learned normal profile. In case of deviations (e.g., unknown CAN IDs, unusual frequencies), an alarm is sent to the SIEM and the suspicious traffic can be blocked. The gateway is regularly checked for integrity (Remote Attestation).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration of the Intrusion Detection System on the gateway. The SIEM logs are examined for alarms from the gateway to assess its effectiveness. The logs of the remote attestation checks are controlled to ensure the integrity of the gateway itself. A penetration test can attempt to cross the network boundary.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Institutions use a wide variety of vehicles for short and long-distance travel in many situations. In the context of this module, a vehicle is defined as a motorized means of transport that typically moves on land and air routes, seaways, and waterways and has a vehicle cabin or similar. Examples include cars, trucks, airplanes, or ships. In the following text, only the generic term vehicle is used, unless a specific type of vehicle is meant.
Almost all modern vehicles have integrated IT components, such as infotainment systems or internal analysis systems, which must be considered holistically within the framework of information security. In addition, official tasks are often carried out not only in the rooms and buildings of an institution, but also within vehicles, which can be located at changing locations and in different environments. A vehicle is therefore also an independent mobile working environment that must be adequately secured by the institution.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The module describes specific threats that must be considered when institutions use vehicles with IT components or use vehicles in general as IT workstations. Building on this, the module specifies which requirements must be met by vehicle users and operators to ensure the optimal operation of a vehicle from an information security perspective.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The module INF.11 General vehicle must generally be applied once to every land, air, and water vehicle used by the institution.
The target audience for the module is users and operators of vehicles. Autonomous or remote-controlled vehicles, rail vehicles, and spacecraft are excluded from this module.
The type, equipment, location, and field of application of vehicles may differ from one institution to another. The INF.11 General vehicle module only considers typical use scenarios for vehicles, so special purposes, such as rescue operations by rescue helicopters or combat missions by military vehicles, must be considered individually on a supplementary basis.
Therefore, retrofitted, application-specific IT systems or vehicle-specific specialized applications, as are common in emergency vehicles or command vehicles, for example, are not conclusively dealt with. The equipment and the associated specialized applications of these vehicles must be dealt with individually on a supplementary basis.
In addition, the vehicle's own networks via communication buses such as CAN, LIN, or Flexray, also known as IVN (In-Vehicle-Network), are not considered, as these are generally not modified by the users.
To secure the carried and retrofitted IT components, all relevant modules, such as SYS.3.1 Laptops, SYS.3.2 General smartphones and tablets, NET.3.3 VPN and the module layers NET.4 Telecommunications and NET.2 Wireless networks must be considered separately.
Furthermore, before the vehicle is disposed of or decommissioned, the CON.6 Deletion and destruction module must be applied to ensure that no sensitive information remains in the vehicle.
This module deals with all infrastructural aspects, so that INF.9 Mobile workplace does not need to be modeled additionally.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Missing or inadequate regulations for vehicles
parts.prose:
If it is not or only inadequately regulated which information may be transmitted and processed via the networks provided by vehicles for users, such as WLAN or Bluetooth, and which protective measures are to be taken, confidential information may be disclosed. If it is not sufficiently regulated how these are to be secured and used, sensitive information such as personal data could be disclosed.
If vehicles are stolen or integrated IT components fail and there are no regulations and defined procedures for this, this can have serious consequences. There is a risk that sensitive information remains in the vehicle and that unauthorized third parties gain access to it.
If vehicles or the IT components installed in them are improperly commissioned, this can lead to extensive threats to information security. Relevant settings, such as the automatic synchronization of phone books, could be incorrectly configured, or function tests on aircraft could be skipped or improperly performed. This, in turn, can lead to the aircraft's systems not functioning as intended during operation and, in the worst case, to a total loss of the aircraft.
Similarly, the function of the integrated IT components and the entire vehicle can be endangered if the vehicle is improperly switched off or temporarily decommissioned. An example of this is emergency vehicles. If these are switched off for a longer period of time, there is a risk that the vehicle battery will be completely discharged due to the extensive equipment. As a result, the vehicle can no longer start and data could be lost in the integrated IT components.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Lack of security awareness and carelessness when handling the vehicle
parts.prose:
A lack of security awareness and carelessness when handling vehicles and their components represent a serious threat. If employees are not sufficiently trained in how to handle vehicles and their IT components and are not aware of the potential risks, vehicles and their built-in IT components could be used incorrectly or carelessly. For example, IT systems on the bridges of ships are used by different people. If essential settings are changed by one user without informing the others, malfunctions could occur that the other users cannot comprehend.
A further danger can be that vehicles are not reliably locked. This could allow unauthorized third parties to easily enter the vehicle cabin and view or steal all IT components and stored information located there.
Furthermore, poorly trained employees could react inappropriately to malfunctions and worsen the situation with an incorrect response. If, for example, in the event of a malfunction of the vehicle's integrated IT systems, the responsible department within the institution is not contacted, but the user attempts to fix the problem themselves, this can have unforeseeable consequences. For instance, relevant security or data protection settings could be altered.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Unregulated data transmission to third parties and insecure communication interfaces
parts.prose:
Many modern vehicles have not only the wireless communication interfaces that are relevant or directly visible to the user, such as Bluetooth or Wi-Fi. Many of the vehicle's internal systems communicate directly with the manufacturers' IT systems via integrated cellular interfaces, and this information exchange can usually not be influenced by the users. This does not just mean legally required and user-transparent systems like eCall, but especially those that are not directly visible to the user. For example, many vehicle manufacturers transmit data to collect detailed information about the vehicle's location and mileage or about the driver's behavior. This could lead to the extensive collection of personal data about the vehicle users without their knowledge or explicit consent to this data collection and processing.
Another danger is insecure communication interfaces on vehicles. A lack of protective mechanisms can allow sensitive data to be read. For example, if the infotainment system allows Bluetooth pairing without security mechanisms, unauthorized third parties could covertly pair their smartphone with it and synchronize address books.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Improper modifications to the vehicle
parts.prose:
While conventional passenger cars are very rarely modified by the vehicle operator, vehicles for specialized purposes very often have to be subsequently adapted by the operators or specialized companies. Examples of this are emergency vehicles or ships that have been subsequently modernized or repurposed. If a vehicle is improperly modified in these cases, for example by laying additional cables in an unsuitable manner, this can lead to considerable damage, up to and including the total loss of the vehicle.
Other changes can also impair the operational capability of the vehicles. For example, if the infotainment system is manipulated to unlock new or blocked functions, the manufacturer's updates may no longer be installed and associated potential security vulnerabilities may no longer be closed.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Manipulation, unauthorized access, and theft of vehicles
parts.prose:
Information left openly in vehicles can often be seen from outside the vehicles if there is no or insufficient visual protection. This can create desires that lead to attacks.
Vehicles are often parked in publicly accessible parking lots or moored at boat docks that are not protected by the institution's central protective measures, such as security services or locked garages. They are therefore inherently exposed to an increased risk of being entered by unauthorized persons. Insecure locking systems can be a vulnerability here. For example, so-called keyless entry systems on vehicles can sometimes be easily bypassed by relay attacks.
Thus, IT systems, accessories, information, and software can often be more easily manipulated, destroyed, or stolen when left unattended in vehicles rather than in the institution's premises. If IT systems, accessories, information, or software are manipulated or destroyed, employees in vehicles are often only able to work to a limited extent. The affected IT systems could even be manipulated in such a way that, for example, the data processed on them is forwarded to unauthorized third parties by malware. Furthermore, destroyed IT components may need to be replaced, which requires both financial and personnel resources.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Dangers related to maintenance, repair, and updates
parts.prose:
If vehicles and the IT components used are not maintained or are insufficiently maintained and cared for, or if their functionality is not regularly checked, they may not be operational or only to a limited extent when needed.
A major challenge here is that updates for the IT systems integrated in the vehicles are not necessarily available at the regular maintenance cycles of the vehicles. This could mean, for example, that updates are only installed irregularly and with delays.
In the institution's own workshops, the vehicles and the installed IT components can generally not be fully maintained or repaired, which is why vehicles are often handed over to third-party companies. In the premises of the third-party companies, the vehicles are usually unobserved and third parties can have comprehensive access to the vehicle and the IT components used. This creates an increased risk that the IT components will be misused or that sensitive information will be stolen.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Dangers during decommissioning
parts.prose: When vehicles are decommissioned, they can be sold with all or some of the installed IT components. This can allow third parties to access the IT components and thus deduce internal information or personal data, such as stored phone numbers. In addition, institution-specific components such as SIM cards or crypto modules may remain in the vehicles. Thus, the subsequent owners would unintentionally gain access to them and could, for example, read information from these components (such as phone numbers from the SIM card) and use it unlawfully.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Impermissible temperature and humidity in vehicles
parts.prose: Every device has a temperature range within which it functions properly. If the ambient temperature exceeds or falls below the limits of this range, devices and IT components can fail and operation can be disrupted. The same applies to humidity. In vehicles, there are different conditions that can lead to precisely such situations. For example, the interior of vehicles parked in the sun can reach up to 70 degrees and thus exceed the usual temperature range of, for example, lithium-ion batteries.

controls.title: Selection of suitable cable types (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection of cable types is done ad-hoc and depends on the decision of the respective installer. There is no standardized approach, which leads to inconsistent quality and performance of the cabling in the institution.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In practice, this means that a cheap, unshielded cable might be used for an office area, while a higher-quality cable is used in another, similarly used area on the recommendation of a different service provider. A central overview or justification for the selection does not exist.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor determines by interviewing employees and reviewing various, unrelated project documentations that there is no uniform process for cable selection. A random visual inspection at different locations confirms the use of different cable qualities without any comprehensible reason.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic requirement to use a certain minimum standard for cables (e.g., Cat. 6). This requirement is generally observed for new installations. However, specific environmental conditions such as electromagnetic interference sources or special fire protection requirements are not systematically considered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The IT department has issued instructions to use at least Cat. 6 for all data cables. This is implemented in orders and by the installers. However, it is not checked whether shielding would be necessary in the vicinity of high-voltage power lines.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies the existence of the internal specification for the minimum standard. During an inspection, the labeling of the cables is checked on a random basis. In addition, it is assessed whether there are areas with obviously special requirements where the minimum standard is potentially insufficient.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: When selecting cable types, it MUST be checked which transmission properties are necessary. The relevant standards and regulations MUST be observed. The environmental conditions during operation and installation (e.g., temperatures, cable routes, tensile forces, type of installation, and distance to sources of interference) MUST also be systematically assessed and taken into account in the selection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An internal document defines the requirements for different application areas (e.g., office, server room, production hall). Based on these requirements, specific cable types are selected from an approved product catalog. The decision is recorded as part of the planning documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the planning documentation for recently completed cabling projects. It is checked whether an analysis of the environmental conditions has taken place and the selection of the cable type is comprehensibly documented. Compliance with relevant standards such as DIN EN 50173 is verified using the product data sheets of the cables used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The defined process for cable selection is supplemented by a regular re-evaluation and a life cycle perspective. Cables with improved properties (e.g., higher bandwidth reserves, better fire protection according to higher CPR classes) are proactively selected to prevent future requirements and risks. The selection is specifically optimized for each installation environment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For all new cabling, low-smoke, halogen-free (LSZH) cables are used as standard, even if this is not explicitly required. S/FTP cables are always used near potential sources of interference. The selection criteria are reviewed annually and adapted to the state of the art.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that a process for regular review of the selection criteria is established. It is checked whether the cable types used exceed the minimum requirements of the standards and whether the selection decisions demonstrably increase the resilience and future-proofing of the infrastructure. The documentation of the risk and environmental analyses is checked for its level of detail and quality.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The selection of cable types is fully integrated into an automated planning and procurement process. Only cable types with the best available security and performance characteristics are used. A central cable management system automatically validates the selection based on the stored environmental data of the installation site and the current standards situation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A tool for infrastructure planning (DCIM/CAFM) contains a catalog of approved cable types. When planning a new route, the system suggests the optimal cable type based on the planned path and the known sources of interference (e.g., from the electrical installation plans). Deviations require a formal approval process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the configuration of the management system and the selection rules defined therein. Test cases are used to verify the correct functioning of the automated validation. It is verified that the process is enforced and that all orders and installations comply with the system specifications. Logs of manual exception approvals are reviewed and assessed.

controls.title: Cable Routing Planning (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cable routing is determined ad-hoc during installation, often taking the shortest path, without forward-looking capacity planning or systematic separation of data and power cables.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A new server is installed, and the data cable is simply placed in an existing, already full cable duct along with the power cables. Future extensions are not considered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During an inspection, the auditor finds that cable trays are overcrowded and data and power cables are run in parallel without the required separation. There are no planning documents to justify the cable routing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cable trays are planned to be sufficient for current needs. A basic separation of power and data cables is intended but not always consistently implemented according to normative specifications. Reserve capacity is not systematically planned.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When setting up a new office, separate cable ducts are provided for power and data. However, the dimensions of the ducts are tight, so that no more cables can be run after just one year.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor checks the planning documents for the intended separation of the cable paths. During a visual inspection, the fill level of the cable trays is assessed and it is measured whether the normative separation distances are maintained at critical points.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Cables, cable pathways, and cable trays MUST be sufficiently dimensioned from a functional and physical perspective. Future requirements, such as space for extensions, MUST be taken into account. When routing IT and power cabling together, crosstalk MUST be prevented by maintaining the standard-compliant separation distance. Identifiable sources of danger MUST be bypassed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The cable trays are planned according to standards (e.g., DIN EN 50174-2) and include a reserve capacity of at least 30%. Separate trays are used for power and data cables or, if not possible, separation barriers are used in the cable ducts. The planning is documented and is part of the building documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor compares the installed cable trays with the planning documents. It is checked whether the dimensioning has sufficient reserve capacity and whether the separation distances between power and information cables have been implemented in accordance with standards. This can be done through measurements and visual inspections.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cable routing is planned redundantly. For critical areas, separate and independent cable paths (e.g., different riser shafts or fire compartments) are deliberately planned to ensure availability in the event of faults or physical damage to a route. The planning includes a capacity reserve of over 50%.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The main distributors in the data center are connected to the floor distributors via two separate, physically diverse paths. The route planning is visualized and managed in a CAFM or DCIM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies, using the planning documentation in the management system (e.g., DCIM), that redundant and physically separate cable paths exist for critical connections. An inspection confirms the implementation of the planned redundancy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The cable routing planning is fully automated and dynamic. A central system models the entire building infrastructure and optimizes cable routing not only according to technical criteria, but also taking into account physical risks (e.g., flood risk, fire load) and security aspects (e.g., avoiding publicly accessible areas).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DCIM tool, coupled with the building technology and security systems, plans the routing paths. It automatically warns if a planned route passes through a high-risk area or if the standard-compliant distances to new sources of interference (e.g., a newly installed machine) are not met. Capacity planning is continuously monitored and forecasted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor analyzes the configuration and algorithms of the planning system. It is checked whether the risk modeling is comprehensive and functions correctly. The resilience of the planning is validated using simulation scenarios (e.g., "what-if analysis" for water damage in riser zone A).

controls.title: Professional Installation (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation of the cabling is carried out without formal acceptance or inspection by a qualified person. The quality of the work depends solely on the executing service provider. Standards are not explicitly required or checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An electrician is hired to install new outlets. After the work is completed, the invoice is paid without measuring the connections or checking the installation for compliance with bending radii or tensile forces.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: During a visual inspection, the auditor finds obvious installation defects such as kinked cables, overly tightened cable ties, or improperly connected outlets. There are no measurement reports to prove the functionality of the cabling.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation work is carried out by service providers considered to be competent. A basic functional test is performed after installation (e.g., link test), but a detailed check of all normative requirements or a formal acceptance does not take place.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After the installation of new network connections, the installer hands over a simple handover protocol with the results of a simple connection test. A check of the cable paths for possible damage or compliance with standards during laying is not carried out.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor reviews the existing handover protocols. It is checked whether they are sufficiently meaningful. During an inspection, random checks are made to ensure compliance with basic installation rules, e.g., neat laying and strain relief.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation of the cabling MUST be carried out professionally and carefully, observing all relevant standards. The professional execution MUST be checked by a qualified person in all phases. This includes checking the material upon delivery, monitoring the assembly for damage, and ensuring that the cable paths are chosen so that damage from the normal use of the building is excluded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An external service provider is commissioned with the installation. The contract requires compliance with DIN EN 50174 and the handover of qualified measurement reports (certification measurement) for each connection. An internal responsible person (e.g., from facility management) accompanies the work and carries out a visual inspection and a plausibility check of the reports.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor verifies that contracts exist for all new installations that require compliance with standards. The acceptance protocols and the corresponding detailed measurement reports (e.g., for Permanent Link or Channel) are reviewed. The quality of the visible installation (e.g., at patch panels and outlets) is checked on a random basis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The installation quality is ensured by a multi-stage, formalized acceptance process. In addition to the inspection by an internal expert, the acceptance is randomly accompanied and verified by an independent third party (expert assessor). All installation steps are documented with photographs.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before cable trays, ceilings, or walls are closed, the condition of the installation is photographed and archived. For larger projects, an external expert carries out quality control during construction and prepares their own report on the conformity of the installation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: In addition to the internal acceptance protocols and measurements, the auditor also reviews the external expert reports and the photo documentation. It is checked whether the formalized, multi-stage acceptance process is consistently followed.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire cabling infrastructure is equipped with intelligent components (e.g., automated infrastructure management systems, AIM), which enable continuous physical monitoring of the connections. Installation errors or subsequent unauthorized changes to the patching are automatically detected and reported immediately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Patch panels and cabling components of an AIM system are used. The installation work is documented and approved directly in the AIM system. Each connection is permanently monitored; if a patch cable is removed, the system immediately generates an alarm.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor interacts directly with the AIM system. It is checked whether the state documented in the system corresponds to reality (e.g., by deliberately pulling a patch cable and observing the system's reaction). The configuration of the alerting and the system's logs are checked for completeness and correct function.

controls.title: EMC-compliant power supply (B)
