parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should randomly check the consistency between the BIM model, the data in the CAFM system, and the physical reality. It is verified whether the process for updating the digital twin is functional and documented.

controls.title: Creation of a security policy for TFM (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are unwritten security rules and practices that are followed by experienced employees. A formal, documented security policy for TFM does not exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Security awareness is based on oral tradition and individual experience. New employees are trained by observing and imitating.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should interview several TGM employees on a specific security topic (e.g., handling external service providers) and assess the consistency and appropriateness of the answers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The institution's general IT security policy is also declared valid for the TGM. However, there are no specific additions or adjustments that take into account the special features of TGM (e.g. OT components, real-time requirements).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the TGM department, the existence of the general IT security policy is pointed out. However, the practical implementation of the requirements (e.g. patch management) often fails due to the technical conditions of the TGA.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the general IT security policy and assess the extent to which its requirements are applicable to TGM systems. Interviews are conducted to understand the challenges in implementation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the institution's general security guideline, an overarching security policy for TGM SHOULD be created and traceably implemented. The security policy SHOULD traceably describe requirements and specifications for how the TGM is implemented. It SHOULD be known to all employees responsible for the TGM area and be fundamental to their work.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document is created that defines specific security rules for the TGM, e.g. for handling passwords for controllers, for segmenting TGM networks and for the use of remote maintenance access.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should request the TGM security policy and check it for completeness and traceability. It is verified that the policy is known to the employees, e.g. through interviews or proof of training.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Specific, detailed security policies for the various subject areas of the TGM are derived from the overarching TGM security policy (e.g. a policy for remote maintenance, one for network security). The policies are reviewed and updated regularly and as needed to reflect the current state of the art.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Topic-specific detailed documents are created that contain concrete configuration specifications. An annual review process for the policy family is established and documented. The results of audits or security incidents are incorporated into the update.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the derived, specific policies. The process for regularly updating the policies is checked, including the corresponding logs. It is checked whether the policies are up to date with the current state of the art.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM security policies are fully integrated into the institution's ISMS. Compliance with the policies is enforced by technical measures and continuously monitored. The effectiveness of the policies is measured and regularly assessed using Key Performance Indicators (KPIs).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration management tools are used to ensure compliance with policy requirements on the systems (Policy as Code). A SIEM system monitors policy violations in real time. KPIs, such as 'number of open security-relevant configuration deviations', are recorded and reported.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should analyze the configuration of the monitoring tools (configuration management, SIEM). The defined KPIs and the corresponding reports are checked. It is verified that detected deviations are systematically tracked and resolved.

controls.title: Planning of the TGM (S) [Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM, the underlying infrastructure, and the associated processes SHOULD be planned appropriately. The planning SHOULD include at least a detailed requirements analysis, a sufficient high-level design, and a detailed and implementation plan. For the requirements specification, the interfaces of the systems to be managed SHOULD also be documented. A requirements specification document SHOULD be created before commissioning.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A structured planning procedure is introduced. In the requirements analysis, functional and non-functional (including security) requirements are collected from all stakeholders. The high-level concept outlines the solution architecture, the detailed concept describes the implementation details. The requirements specification for tenders contains all specified requirements, including those for tests to be performed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the planning documents (requirements analysis, high-level/detailed concept, requirements specification) for a current TGM project. It is checked whether the security policy was taken into account and whether the interfaces are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning process for the TGM is formalized, e.g. according to a recognized procedural model. The planning phases (analysis, high-level, detailed concept) are concluded with formal reviews and approvals by defined committees (incl. information security). If Artificial Intelligence (AI) functions are used, the manufacturer is asked how information security is taken into account.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The V-Modell XT or an agile approach with a defined 'Definition of Done' for security requirements is used for planning. A 'Change Control Board' is established to approve planning changes. Inquiries about AI security are integrated into the procurement process by default.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the minutes of the formal reviews and approval meetings. It is checked whether the Information Security Officer (ISO) was involved in the planning process and whether their approval is documented. The documentation on inquiries regarding AI security is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM planning is fully integrated into a 'Security by Design' approach. Systematic threat analyses and risk analyses for the planned architecture are carried out in the early planning phase. The planning is model-based (e.g. using BIM), whereby security requirements are specified and validated directly in the model.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Methods like STRIDE are applied for the threat analysis of the TGM architecture. The results are directly incorporated into the security requirements. In the BIM model, security zones and protection mechanisms are visualized and their consistency is checked. Compliance with universal planning, if the demanding organization is not yet determined, is rigorously implemented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the documentation of the threat and risk analyses performed. It is checked how the identified risks were addressed in the planning. The consistency between the security concept and the implementation in the BIM model is verified.

controls.title: Creation of a TGM concept (S) [Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the security policy, a TGM concept SHOULD be created and maintained. At least aspects such as methods and tools, access and communication security, network segmentation, monitoring, logging, reporting chains, processes and integration into emergency planning SHOULD be considered.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central concept document is created that describes the technical and organizational security measures for the TGM. For example, it specifies which network areas should exist, which events must be logged, and who is notified in the event of a fault. This concept serves as the basis for detailed planning and configuration.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should request the TGM concept and check whether all aspects mentioned in the requirement are covered. It is checked whether the concept is consistent with the overarching TGM security policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM concept is reviewed regularly and also when needed and updated. In addition, a target-actual comparison between the specifications of the concept and the current state is carried out regularly. The results SHOULD be documented in a traceable manner and deviations SHOULD be rectified.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review process for the TGM concept is established. The target-actual comparison is implemented through technical configuration checks and organizational audits. A catalog of measures to rectify deviations is created and tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the logs of the annual concept review and the documentation of the target-actual comparisons. It is checked whether identified deviations were tracked and resolved promptly. This can be done by an automated check of configuration files against a baseline defined in the TGM concept.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM concept is integrated as a 'living' document into a configuration management system. Parts of the concept, such as firewall rules or logging configurations, are managed as code (Policy as Code) and automatically rolled out to the systems. The target-actual comparison is carried out continuously and automatically, and deviations lead to immediate alarms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Tools like Ansible or Puppet are used to manage system configurations according to the concept. A SIEM system is used to continuously check compliance with logging requirements. The TGM concept itself is versioned in a Git repository.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should analyze the 'Policy as Code' process and the tools used. The configuration of the continuous monitoring in the SIEM is checked. The response processes to automatically generated alarms in case of deviations are verified.

controls.title: Creation of a radio frequency register (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: To be able to use radio frequencies as interference-free as possible, a radio frequency register SHOULD be created that lists the systems and users of the frequency spectrum at the institution's locations. This SHOULD involve coordination between IT, TGM, and, if applicable, OT. The register SHOULD be regularly reviewed and updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A central list (e.g. in a database or a wiki) is created in which all used frequencies (WLAN, DECT, radio sensors, company radio, etc.) are documented with details of the system, location, person in charge and primary user. The register is consulted before new radio systems are put into operation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the radio frequency register and check it for completeness and up-to-dateness. It is verified whether a process for coordination between IT, TGM and OT has been established, e.g. by inspecting minutes of coordination meetings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The radio frequency register is supplemented by regular measurements of frequency utilization (spectrum scans) at critical locations. The results are used to verify the register and to identify potential sources of interference or unauthorized transmitters.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Portable or permanently installed spectrum analyzers are used to periodically monitor the frequency spectrum. The results of the scans are documented and compared with the entries in the register. Anomalies are investigated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the logs of the spectrum scans performed. It is checked whether the results were analyzed and compared with the register and whether measures were taken in case of deviations.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Dynamic frequency management is implemented. The frequency spectrum is continuously monitored by a distributed sensor system. The system detects and locates sources of interference or unauthorized transmitters in real time and can dynamically adjust frequency assignments to avoid interference.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'Wireless Intrusion Prevention System' (WIPS) or a dedicated frequency management system with distributed sensors is used. The management of the radio frequency register is integrated into this system and is largely automated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should analyze the configuration of the dynamic frequency management system and the reports from continuous monitoring. Its effectiveness in detecting and responding to simulated interference events is tested.

controls.title: Creation and maintenance of an inventory for the TGM (S) [Planner]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the documentation of systems managed by the TGM, an inventory SHOULD be created and maintained. The inventory SHOULD be kept complete and up-to-date. The inventory SHOULD clearly show the roles and responsibilities for all systems. The elements of the TGM infrastructure itself SHOULD also be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An inventory list is maintained in a database or a CAFM system. For each system (e.g., heating control, ventilation system, access control server), at least information such as designation, location, manufacturer, model, serial number, responsible person/department, and status is recorded. There is a process for updating the inventory when changes occur.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the TGM inventory and check its completeness and currency on a random basis through physical inspection of selected systems. It is checked whether a responsibility has been assigned for each system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM inventory is supported by automated discovery tools and regularly compared with their results. The inventory also contains security-relevant information such as firmware version, patch level, and network port assignments.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Network scanners are used to find active devices in the TGM network. The results are compared with the manually maintained entries in the inventory to find gaps or unauthorized devices. The additional information is used to support vulnerability management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should compare the reports of the discovery tools with the official inventory and analyze the process for handling discrepancies. It is checked whether security-relevant information such as firmware versions is kept up-to-date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The TGM inventory is fully automated and maintained in real time. It is the central, trusted data source ('Single Source of Truth') for all other TGM processes such as monitoring, patch management, and configuration management. The integrity of the inventory is continuously monitored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 'Configuration Management Database' (CMDB) is used as the central inventory. It is fed from various sources (discovery tools, asset management, manual entries). Other systems (e.g., SIEM, ticketing system) access the CMDB via API to obtain consistent and up-to-date information.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should analyze the architecture of the CMDB and its data sources and sinks. The correctness of the data in the CMDB is checked by queries and comparisons with reality. The process for ensuring data quality and integrity is verified.

controls.title: Regulation of the use of Computer-Aided Facility Management (S) [Planner]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If a Computer-Aided Facility Management system (CAFM system) is used, its use SHOULD be comprehensively planned and designed. If processes are mapped and supported in the CAFM, corresponding roles and permissions SHOULD be defined, especially if external service providers are involved in the processes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Before the introduction of a CAFM system, a concept is created that defines the purpose, the processes to be mapped (e.g., fault management, maintenance planning), and the required modules. A detailed role and authorization concept is developed that specifies which user (internal/external) may see which data and perform which actions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the CAFM concept and the associated role and authorization concept. It is checked whether the defined roles follow the 'need-to-know' principle and whether the involvement of external service providers has been adequately considered.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CAFM system is hardened and securely configured in accordance with the general requirements for IT systems. The data stored in the CAFM system is classified and secured according to its protection requirements, e.g., through encryption. Access to the system is logged.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The manufacturer's hardening recommendations for the CAFM system are implemented. Sensitive data, such as key management data, is encrypted in the database. All administrative access and security-relevant changes in the system are recorded and regularly evaluated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should check the configuration of the CAFM system for the implementation of hardening measures. The logging configuration is inspected and the log files are evaluated on a random basis. It is checked whether data classification has taken place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The CAFM system is fully integrated into the TGM and IT security architecture. It is connected to a central Identity and Access Management (IAM) system, and its log data is sent in real time to a central SIEM system for correlation and analysis. The security of the CAFM system is regularly checked by penetration tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Single-Sign-On (SSO) via the institution's central IAM is implemented for access to the CAFM system. Specific application logs of the CAFM are forwarded to the SIEM to detect anomalies (e.g., mass data exports). Penetration tests are performed at least every two years or after major changes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should verify the connection of the CAFM system to the IAM and the SIEM. The reports of the last penetration tests are inspected and it is checked whether the vulnerabilities found have been remediated.

controls.title: Regulation of the use of Building Information Modeling (S) [Planner]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: As far as possible, Building Information Modeling (BIM) SHOULD be used for the digital modeling of all relevant building data. When using BIM, the BIM project execution plan SHOULD be specified. Furthermore, the BIM architecture SHOULD be comprehensively planned and designed. Information security for the BIM tools SHOULD also be adequately ensured.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A BIM Execution Plan (BEP) is created that defines the goals, use cases, processes, roles, and responsibilities for the use of BIM. The IT infrastructure for BIM (e.g., Common Data Environment - CDE) is planned and fundamentally secured, e.g., through access controls.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should inspect the BIM execution plan and check whether it contains the necessary regulations. The design of the BIM architecture and the basic security measures (e.g., the authorization concept for the CDE) are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A protection requirement is determined for the BIM data and models and a data classification is carried out. Based on this, detailed security requirements for the BIM platform (CDE) and the collaboration processes are defined and implemented. This includes secure data exchange formats and paths.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A security concept is created specifically for the BIM application. Data exchange with external partners takes place exclusively via encrypted channels. A fine-grained authorization concept is implemented in the CDE, which controls access to models and data depending on the role and project phase.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should check the BIM security concept. It is verified whether the data classification has been correctly mapped to the permissions in the CDE. The configuration of the secure data exchange paths is checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Security is deeply integrated into the BIM process (Secure BIM Lifecycle). All access to BIM data is logged without gaps and monitored for anomalies. Models are checked for malicious or unwanted content before import. The entire BIM platform is regularly subjected to security reviews and penetration tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The logs of the CDE are forwarded to a central SIEM for analysis. Automated 'Model Checkers' are used to check the models for consistency and compliance with specifications (including security specifications). Digital signatures are used to ensure the authenticity and integrity of models.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: The auditor should verify the SIEM integration and the configured use cases for monitoring the BIM platform. The configuration and reports of the 'Model Checkers' are analyzed. The reports of the last penetration tests for the BIM platform are inspected.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Facility management (FM) is responsible for all services that arise during the planning and use phase of buildings, building complexes, properties or property portfolios. In the following, the term building will be used uniformly for this purpose. Exceptions to this will be explicitly mentioned.
FM is location- and property-specific. It can be subdivided into technical, infrastructural and commercial FM.
Technical facility management (TFM) comprises all services that maintain the technical function and availability of a building in accordance with DIN 32736. These services include, among others:

• Operating
• Documenting
• Energy and environmental management
• Information management
• Modernizing
• Refurbishing
• Converting
• Tracking of technical warranty

Essential technical functions of a building are provided by the technical building equipment (TBE), which is operated, maintained and further developed by the TFM. According to VDI 4700 Part 1, the TBE comprises all technical and use-specific equipment installed in and connected to the building, as well as technical equipment in outdoor facilities and furnishings (see also Chapter 4.1 TFM-specific technical terms used). If the TBE is to be operated in an automated and cross-trade manner, additional technical infrastructure for building automation (BA, Building Automation and Control Systems, BACS) is used. Thus, BA is a central tool of TFM. A building can be operated by TFM even without BA, whereas BA is always accompanied by TFM. Certain components of the BA are also to be assigned to the TBE, such as real-time capable Industrial Ethernet switches.
While in the past the TBE was usually operated independently of IT and operational technology (OT), network transitions to these areas are increasingly being established today. In addition, parts of the TBE are used around the clock. Therefore, changes often have to be carried out in parallel with productive use.
The basic values of information security must also be taken into account in TFM, because the loss of availability, confidentiality and integrity of systems can have far-reaching consequences in TFM, including endangering life and limb.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The goal of this building block is to establish information security as an integral part of planning, implementation, and operation within the framework of TFM.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The INF.13 Technical Facility Management module is to be applied to the TFM of an institution as soon as buildings with TBE are planned, built or operated.
This module deals with TFM, i.e. the tasks and processes required for the planning and operation of TBE systems (see Chapter 4.1 TFM-specific technical terms used) of a building. The technical infrastructure for the automated operation of buildings is dealt with in the INF.14 Building Automation module. The latter must be applied in addition to the INF.13 Technical Facility Management module if the TBE to be operated is automated and controlled across systems. In this sense, TFM also includes the processes of GA.
It is also possible that the systems to be managed also include those that are modeled by modules from the layers IND Industrial IT and SYS IT Systems, e.g. IND.2.1 General ICS Component or SYS.4.4 General IoT Device. In addition, the aspects of the ORP and OPS layers relevant to TFM must be observed, in particular the sub-layers OPS.1 In-house Operation and OPS.2 Third-Party Operation as well as the modules ORP.2 Personnel and ORP.4 Identity and Authorization Management. If cloud services are used for TFM, the OPS.2.2 Cloud Use module must be taken into account for the selection of these services.
To secure remote access in TFM, the modules OPS.1.2.5 Remote Maintenance and IND.3.2 Remote Maintenance in an Industrial Environment must be applied.
The INF.13 Technical Facility Management module does not deal with the physical security of buildings; this is dealt with in the INF.1 General Building module. Likewise, the aspect of safety does not play a prominent role in this module, but is dealt with in the IND.2.7 Safety Instrumented Systems module.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.1. Lack of fundamentals for planning TFM
parts.prose: If the demanding organizations (see Chapter 4.1 TFM-specific technical terms used) are not yet determined when a building is constructed, there is a lack of contact persons, objectives, and requirements for the TFM. This can lead to the TFM in operation not corresponding to the actual needs, because these could not be requested at the time of planning and implementation.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.2. Insufficient documentation in TFM
parts.prose:
A variety of service providers are often involved in technical building management (TBM). If the documentation of responsibilities with contact persons and associated SLAs is incomplete or inaccessible, this leads to avoidable delays in an emergency when important systems fail, which can even result in personal injury.
A lack of documentation of security certifications for the technical building equipment, including dates for necessary renewals, can lead to expired certifications not being renewed in time. This can result in violations of laws, danger to life and limb depending on the building equipment, and an inability to settle any resulting damage through the relevant insurance policies.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.3. Compromise of interfaces with TFM
parts.prose:
The TBM has technical interfaces to areas requiring special protection, e.g., Safety Instrumented Systems (SIS), security services, and fire alarm systems. If these interfaces are compromised, either intentionally or unintentionally, through errors in the TBM, this can result in a violation of laws and pose a danger to life and limb.
For example, if the visual or audible warning is disabled during a fire alarm in a data center, people in the room may not be able to leave in time before the room is flooded with extinguishing gas. Likewise, a fake fire alarm can cause escape doors to open, allowing unauthorized access, or cause doors to close, potentially trapping people inside.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.4. Insufficient monitoring of the TBE
parts.prose:
If the technical building equipment is inadequately monitored, security-relevant events, such as relevant malfunctions in the equipment, may not be detected or may be detected too late. Depending on the event, this can lead to further damage or pose a danger to life and limb.
For example, if a heating failure at sub-zero outside temperatures is not reported, the rooms will cool down significantly before the failure is noticed and a remedy can be initiated.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: 2.5. Insufficient role and authorization management
parts.prose: If the TFM or individual parts of it are physically separated from the rest of the institution's IT, a dedicated identity and authorization management system is usually set up. If this is inadequately designed and implemented, it cannot be ruled out that several people use the same account or that authorizations of former internal or external employees or service providers have not been deleted. As a result, unauthorized access to the TFM may occur.

controls.title: Planning of building automation (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The security aspects of building automation (BA) are only considered for individual, particularly critical trades. A comprehensive, consistent planning is missing and not documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The planning is limited to selective measures, e.g., securing the access control, while other areas such as air conditioning or lighting are disregarded. The specifications are made on an ad hoc basis and are not summarized in a comprehensive document.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check whether any planning documents or concepts for the BA exist at all and whether they address security aspects, even if only for sub-areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic planning document for the security of the BA that covers the most important trades. However, this is not consistently taken into account in all construction and conversion measures or regularly updated.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An initial security concept for the BA was created, but its integration into the ongoing planning and construction processes (e.g., via Building Information Modeling, BIM) is incomplete. The documentation is only updated for major projects, but not for minor changes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check for the existence of a BA security planning document. Random checks on current conversion measures to see if the document is used as a basis and if the documentation is up-to-date.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all trades controlled by building automation (BA), it MUST be defined and documented how the BA is to be designed securely. The BA MUST be systematically considered in the planning of new construction, conversion, extension, and renovation of a building. As part of the BA planning, the BA systems to be set up and the scope of automation of the technical building systems MUST be specified. The planning MUST be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal process is established that ensures that the planning department includes the BA security requirements in all relevant construction projects (new construction, conversion, etc.) from the very beginning. The use of BIM to document the security requirements is defined as standard procedure. The specifications are maintained in a central documentation system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the planning documentation for the building automation (BA). Verification of whether security aspects have been defined for all controlled trades. Check whether the BA planning is integrated into the general building planning process and whether the specifications of the BA systems are documented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the defined plan, secure and standardized communication protocols and interfaces are specifically selected to minimize the number of different systems. The plan is updated regularly and as needed, and adapted to the state of the art. A regular target-actual comparison of the plan with the current configuration is carried out to identify deviations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A positive list of approved, secure protocols (e.g. BACnet/SC) and systems is maintained. The target-actual comparison is carried out at least annually by the building services engineering department and the results are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the documentation on protocol and system selection. Inspection of the logs of the regular planning updates and the target-actual comparisons. Interview with the planners to verify the technology adaptation process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The entire planning and configuration process of the BA is integrated into the institution's overarching ISMS. The planning is supported by automated tools that continuously perform the target-actual comparison and report deviations to a central management system in real time. The selection of systems and protocols is based on a formal risk assessment between functionality and security effort.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Configuration and asset management tools (e.g., from the OT security sector) are used to monitor the BA systems. The results of the target-actual comparison are automatically fed into the change and incident management process. The risk assessment is an integral part of every procurement process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Verification of the integration of the BA planning process into the ISMS. Live demonstration of the automated target-actual monitoring. Review of the documentation of risk assessments for system selection. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/check-ga-config --compare-to-plan --report-diffs`

controls.title: Definition of a commissioning and interface management for the BA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A commissioning process only exists for individual, new BA systems. There is no overarching interface management between different trades or organizations.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Commissioning is carried out on a project-by-project basis and is uncoordinated. Interfaces are defined ad hoc as needed, which often leads to compatibility problems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing those responsible to determine whether a standardized process for commissioning exists. Checking project documentation for information on interface definitions.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a basic, documented procedure for commissioning BA systems. Clear interface definitions between the participating organizations exist, but are not consistently documented or checked.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Checklists are used for commissioning. Interfaces are defined, but changes to them are not systematically tracked, and the documentation is often not up to date.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the documentation of the commissioning process. Random checks to see whether the interfaces have been documented for recently commissioned systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The commissioning process for the involved technical building equipment (TBE) systems and BA-relevant components MUST be coordinated and defined comprehensively. Likewise, clear interfaces MUST be defined between the operating organizations of the BA and the BA-relevant components, as well as the operating organizations of the TBE systems. The commissioning and interface management MUST be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A binding manual for commissioning and interface management is created. This contains detailed process descriptions, responsibilities (RACI matrix), and templates for interface definitions and acceptance protocols.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the manual for commissioning and interface management. Checking the acceptance protocols of recently completed commissionings for completeness and conformity with the defined process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The defined processes for commissioning and interface management are reviewed regularly and also as needed, and readjusted if necessary. In particular, in the event of changes within the BA systems, the specifications are proactively adapted to ensure functionality.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review process for the management manual is established. Changes to BA systems automatically trigger a review of the affected interface documentation, which is supported by a change management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the minutes of the annual reviews. Review of change requests to determine whether the impact analysis on the interfaces has been documented and implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Commissioning and interface management is fully integrated into a higher-level quality and configuration management system. Interface tests are automated and performed before commissioning. The documentation is dynamically generated from a central configuration management system (CMS) and is always up to date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A test framework for the BA is used to automatically verify defined interfaces before go-live. The CMS is coupled with the BIM model, so that changes to the configuration are directly reflected in the planning documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the automated interface test. Verification of consistency between the configuration in the CMS, the generated documentation, and the physical setup. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/verify-ga-interfaces --from-cms --all`

controls.title: Secure connection of TBE systems and BA systems (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The connection of TBE systems to BA systems is done without defined security rules. It is not systematically determined which actions may be triggered, which can lead to unpredictable behavior.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Systems are integrated according to the principle 'what works technically, gets connected'. An analysis of the process and functional chains does not take place.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Interviewing administrators about the rules according to which TBE systems are connected. Checking whether documentation on permitted interactions between systems exists.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are basic specifications as to which TBE systems are allowed to interact with BA systems. However, the connection is not secured by technical measures and the process chains are not comprehensively planned or tested.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The connection is permitted at the network level, but the permitted actions at the application level are not restricted. Functional tests are limited to the 'happy path'.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the documentation of the permitted connections. Checking the configuration of coupling elements to determine whether security rules have been implemented. Review of the test documentation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all TBE systems, BA systems, and BA-relevant components, it MUST be specified whether actions may be triggered by other systems. Both the integration of TBE systems into a BA system and the non-interfering coupling of TBE systems to BA systems MUST be adequately secured. The connection of BA systems to each other MUST also be adequately secured. For this purpose, the process and functional chains within a BA system or between BA systems MUST be appropriately planned and tested. The specifications MUST be fully documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each connection, an interaction matrix is created that defines exactly which system may send which data to which other system and trigger which actions. These rules are technically implemented in the coupling elements (e.g. gateways, firewalls). Each connection undergoes a standardized test and release process.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the interaction matrices and the associated documentation. Checking the configuration of the coupling elements to verify the implementation of the defined rules. Inspection of the test logs of the process and functional chains.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If integration is permissible, it SHOULD be regulated which automated actions may be triggered by which information from a BA system. The process and functional chains SHOULD be tested comprehensively and readjusted in case of misconduct. The documentation SHOULD be checked regularly and additionally as needed to see if it is still up to date.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The rules for automated actions are specified in detail, including threshold values and plausibility checks. The tests also include failure scenarios (e.g. component failure, invalid data). The documentation is checked for currency annually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the specification of the automated actions. Inspection of the test plans and reports, especially for failure scenarios. Review of the logs of the annual documentation reviews.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All communication between TBE systems and BA systems is monitored in real time. Deviations from the defined process and functional chains are automatically detected and reported. In case of detected deviations, the affected interactions are blocked and an incident process is triggered. The test cases are automatically generated and executed from the specifications.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An OT security monitoring solution is used that analyzes the BA's data traffic and has anomaly detection. A Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR) system is used to respond to alarms automatically.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the monitoring system and the automatic alerting. Testing of a simulated attack to verify the reaction of the SOAR system. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/ga-traffic-analyser --watch --alert-on-deviation`

controls.title: Consideration of hazard alarm systems in the BA (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hazard alarm systems are partially integrated into BA systems without ensuring non-interference. The network connection is made via the general BA network.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For example, a fire alarm system is connected directly to the climate control system to shut it down. A malfunction in the climate control system could theoretically affect the fire alarm system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the network and system architecture plans to determine the type of connection of hazard alarm systems (HAS) to the BA.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hazard alarm systems are coupled to BA systems, but non-interference is only provided for conceptually and not technically enforced. The network connection is logically separated, but not physically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The HAS is in its own VLAN, but no gateway with diode functionality is used. The coupling is documented as unidirectional, but not technically enforced.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the configuration of the network components (e.g. VLANs, firewall rules) between HAS and BA.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Hazard alarm systems, including security systems, MUST be coupled to BA systems with guaranteed non-interference. They MUST NOT be integrated into a BA system. For the network connection, physically separate network components and physically separate segments MUST be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The connection of the HAS to the BAS is established via a dedicated gateway that only allows unidirectional communication from the HAS to the BAS (e.g., a data diode). The HAS and its connection components are located in their own network segment, physically separated from the BAS network, with their own switches.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Physical inspection of the network cabling and components to verify the physical separation. Review of the configuration and type of the gateway used to ensure it is free from feedback.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If radio networks are used for coupling, such TBE systems MUST be defined as primary users for the frequency ranges used. For communication via radio networks, certified mechanisms SHOULD be used.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When using radio (e.g., for smoke detectors), a frequency band is exclusively reserved for the HAS and registered with the Federal Network Agency. Only radio protocols with certified security (e.g., according to VdS guidelines) that offer encryption and authentication are used.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the frequency allocation certificate from the Federal Network Agency. Inspection of the certificates of the radio components and protocols used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Communication from the HAS to the BAS is additionally checked for integrity and authenticity at the application level. Any attempt at communication from the BAS to the HAS is actively blocked and reported as a major security incident. The physical separation is supplemented by tamper-proof housings and sealed ports.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The gateway between HAS and BAS checks cryptographic signatures of incoming messages. The firewall rules at the gateway are configured to log any connection attempt from the BAS side and report it to a SIEM. The network components of the HAS network are housed in locked cabinets.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Execution of a penetration test that attempts to bypass the non-interference. Review of SIEM logs for alarm messages during a simulated attack attempt. Physical inspection of security measures on network components. `test-command: nmap -sS <HAS-Gateway-IP> --source-port 12345 --reason`

controls.title: BAS documentation (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: BAS documentation is only available for individual components or systems. There is no overall overview of all components, access points, and their dependencies.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The documentation usually consists of manufacturer manuals and incomplete network diagrams. Changes are not documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the BAS documentation and checking it for completeness and currency. Comparing the documentation with reality through a few random checks.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is basic documentation that covers most of the components and access points of the BAS. However, it is not regularly reviewed or updated promptly when changes are made.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a central folder with the BAS documentation, but there is no fixed process to ensure that all changes (e.g., new devices, changed firewall rules) are incorporated there.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the central documentation. Comparison of the documentation with the current state at several points to assess its currency. Interviewing employees about the documentation maintenance process.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For the BAS, the multitude of different components and access points MUST be documented. In particular, all deactivated physical communication interfaces, protocols, and access points or access possibilities to the BAS MUST also be documented. Furthermore, all interactions and dependencies of BAS-relevant components as well as of TBE systems MUST be documented. The documentation MUST be reviewed and adjusted regularly and upon any changes within the BAS.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A comprehensive BAS documentation concept is created, which includes templates for network diagrams, component lists, interface descriptions, and dependency matrices. Every change to the BAS must go through a change management process that mandates an update of the documentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the BAS documentation concept. Inspection of the complete documentation. Review of recently implemented changes to determine if the corresponding documentation has been updated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The available and used security properties of the protocols used SHOULD be documented. The documentation SHOULD be harmonized across all BAS systems in terms of content and data structures to enable simple, cross-system evaluation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The documentation is maintained in a central database (e.g., CMDB) or a wiki with standardized templates and data fields. For each protocol, it is documented which security functions (e.g., encryption, authentication) it offers and whether they are enabled.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the CMDB or wiki for consistency and completeness. Random checks to verify whether the documented security properties of the protocols match the actual configuration of the components.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The BAS documentation is continuously created and kept up-to-date by automated inventory and scanning tools. Deviations between the automatically recorded reality and the target documentation (e.g., from the BIM model) are reported automatically.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An OT asset management solution is used that passively scans the BAS network, records all devices and their configurations, and writes them to the CMDB. This data is regularly validated against the planning data from the BIM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the automated inventory tool. Review of the process for reporting and handling deviations. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/ba-asset-scan --discover --diff-to-cmdb`

controls.title: Separation of BAS networks (B)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: BAS networks and office networks are not separated from each other. Building automation components are on the same network as office PCs and servers.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For convenience or cost reasons, BAS components are simply connected to the nearest office network switch. There is no segmentation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Analysis of a network scan or IP address ranges to determine if BAS components and office devices are operated in the same subnet.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: BAS networks are separated from office networks by a simple firewall, but its rule set is very generic and permissive ('any-any'). Communication is insufficiently controlled.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A BAS VLAN has been set up and a firewall placed in between. However, the firewall rules allow almost any communication from the office network to the BAS network so as not to impair functionality.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the firewall rule set between the BAS VLAN and the office network. Check for overly permissive rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: BAS networks MUST be at least logically separated from office networks and other networks of the institution. Any communication between BAS systems and other IT systems MUST be controlled and regulated. For this purpose, appropriate components with security functions, at least with firewall functionality, MUST be provided at all transitions of such a segmentation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BAS network is operated in its own VLAN or group of VLANs. At the transitions to the office network, firewalls with a restrictive 'Default-Deny' rule set are used. Only explicitly defined and necessary communication relationships are permitted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the network architecture for logical separation (VLAN concept). Review of the firewall rule set to ensure that it is based on the 'Default-Deny' principle and only allows minimally necessary ports and protocols.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: If the BAS is set up centrally for a building complex or a property, the cross-building BAS communication via LAN, WLAN, WAN, radio network, or internet connections MUST also be separated at the network level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Dedicated WAN connections or secure VPN tunnels with strong encryption and authentication mechanisms are used for cross-building communication. These connections are also protected by restrictive firewall rules.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the configuration of the WAN connections or VPN tunnels. Review of the firewall rules that govern data traffic between buildings.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: BAS networks are operated physically separate from all other networks. At the few necessary coupling points, Application Layer Gateways or data diodes are used to restrict communication to the absolute minimum and to perform protocol validation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BAS network uses a completely separate physical infrastructure (switches, cables). The coupling to the office network is done via a demilitarized zone (DMZ) in which an Application Layer Gateway is located, which only allows specific commands of the BAS protocol.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Physical inspection of the network infrastructure to verify the physical separation. Detailed review of the configuration of the Application Layer Gateway in the DMZ. Execution of penetration tests to check the effectiveness of the separation.

controls.title: Definition of a security policy for the BAS (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the institution's general security policy, the security requirements for the BAS SHOULD be specified in a BAS security policy. This policy SHOULD be known to all persons involved in the planning, procurement, implementation, and operation of the BAS systems and should be the basis for their work. The security policy SHOULD also specify the requirements for development and testing for the use of BAS systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A formal 'BAS Security Policy' document is created and approved by management. The document is published on the intranet, and all relevant employees (internal and external) are demonstrably trained. It contains clear requirements for the secure development, configuration, and testing of BAS components.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the adopted BAS security policy. Review of the training records of the persons involved. Random interviews with employees to check awareness of the policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The content and implementation of the required policy content SHOULD be reviewed regularly, adjusted if necessary, and the results of the review should be comprehensibly documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review process for the BAS security policy is established. As part of this review, the implementation of the policy is checked through internal audits. The results and agreed improvement measures are documented in an audit report and their implementation is tracked.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the audit reports from recent years. Review of the action tracking to determine whether identified deficiencies have been rectified.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Compliance with the BAS security policy is continuously monitored by technical measures. Automated compliance checks compare configurations of BAS components against the policy's specifications. Deviations lead to automatic alarms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Security Configuration Management tool is used, which regularly reads the configurations of firewalls, switches, and BAS controllers and compares them with the 'Golden Configurations' defined in the policy. The results are visualized in a compliance dashboard.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the compliance dashboard. Review of the configuration of the automated checks. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/check-ga-compliance --policy-file /etc/ga-security-policy.yml --all-systems`

controls.title: Requirement specification for BA systems (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the BA security policy, an overall requirement specification for the BA and a separate one for each BA system SHOULD be created. All essential elements for the architecture and design of the respective BA system and the coupling of BA systems SHOULD be derivable from the requirements. The requirement specification SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For each BA system (e.g., lighting control, HVAC control), a separate 'Requirement Specification' document is created. This document describes in detail the required architecture, the protocols to be used, the security functions, and the interfaces to other systems. It serves as a binding basis for procurement and implementation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the requirement specifications for the various BA systems. Check whether these documents cover all relevant aspects (architecture, design, coupling) and are consistent with the higher-level BA security policy.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirement specification SHOULD be regularly updated to the state of the art, and additionally as needed. Furthermore, the implementation of the requirements SHOULD be checked regularly. Only components that provide authentication via at least a changeable login name and a changeable password SHOULD be used in the BA.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirement specifications are reviewed annually and updated as needed (e.g., when new secure protocols become available). When new systems are accepted, a checklist is used to verify that all requirements from the specification have been implemented. Components that do not allow password changes are blacklisted and not procured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the minutes of the annual reviews of the requirement specifications. Inspection of the acceptance protocols and checklists. Review of the 'blacklist' for insecure components.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirement specifications are managed as formal models (e.g., in SysML). Test cases and configuration templates are automatically generated from these models. The implementation of the requirements is continuously checked by automated tests throughout the entire life cycle.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) tool is used to specify the BA systems. Test scripts for the acceptance tests and configuration snippets for commissioning are exported directly from the model. A continuous integration / continuous testing process is established.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the system models in the MBSE tool. Review of the scripts for generating test cases and configurations. Observation of the automated test process.

controls.title: Development of a BA concept (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the BA security policy and the requirement specifications, an overall BA concept SHOULD be developed for the BA. Derived from this, detailed concepts SHOULD be developed for all BA systems. The concepts SHOULD at least consider all integrated and coupled building services systems as well as all BA-relevant components with their communication links. The concepts SHOULD describe all technical and organizational specifications.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An overall 'BA Master Concept' document is created, which describes the basic architecture and the security zones. For each individual BA system (HVAC, lighting, etc.), a detailed concept is created that describes the specific implementation, including network plans, configuration details, and operational processes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the BA master concept and the detailed concepts. Check for completeness and consistency with each other and with the higher-level policies and specifications.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The created concepts SHOULD be regularly reviewed and, if necessary, updated to reflect changes in technology or requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An annual review cycle is established for all BA concepts. The results of the reviews and the resulting adjustments are documented. A change management process ensures that all changes to the systems are also reflected in the concepts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the minutes of the annual concept reviews. Random checks of recently implemented changes to determine whether the corresponding concepts have been updated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The BA concepts are managed as 'living documents' in a central configuration management system (CMS) or a wiki. The configuration of the real systems is automatically compared with the concept specifications. Deviations trigger an alarm and a formal investigation process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The concepts are stored in a machine-readable format (e.g., YAML, JSON) in the CMS. Scripts compare the live configuration of the BA components with these 'Configuration as Code' files daily. Any detected deviation (Config Drift) automatically creates a ticket in the service management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the 'Configuration as Code' files in the CMS. Demonstration of the automated configuration comparison. Analysis of the tickets created by configuration deviations in recent months. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/config-drift-detector --repo /etc/ga-concepts/ --live-systems`

controls.title: Creation of independent BA areas (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the BA, BA areas SHOULD be planned and implemented in such a way that dependencies between the BA areas are minimized and BA areas can be controlled independently. A fault in one BA area SHOULD have no or only minor effects on other BA areas.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The BA architecture is structured modularly according to BA areas (e.g., per floor, per fire compartment, per tenant). Each area has its own autonomous controller. Communication between the areas is restricted to the absolute minimum and is handled via defined interfaces.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Analysis of the BA architecture plans to verify the division into independent areas. Checking the configuration of the controllers and gateways to verify the communication restrictions between the areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In particular, the buildings within a building complex or property SHOULD be separately controllable. The established BA areas SHOULD also be visible accordingly in the BA management system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Each building on a property has a completely independent BA system that functions without connection to the other buildings. In the central BA management system (control center), the area structure is clearly displayed, and access rights are assigned on an area-specific basis.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the BA architecture at the property level. Checking the visualization and user permissions in the BA management system to verify separate controllability.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The independence of the BA areas is regularly checked by automated tests. This involves simulating the failure of an area controller and verifying that the other areas continue to function without disruption. The results of these 'Chaos Engineering' tests are used for the continuous improvement of the architecture.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Test scripts are developed that specifically disable individual controllers or network connections between areas. During this time, monitoring systems monitor the function of the remaining areas. This test is performed quarterly in a maintenance window.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the planning, scripts, and logs of the failure simulation tests. Analysis of the test results and the improvement measures derived from them. `test-command: /usr/local/bin/ga-chaos-test --fail-area 'floor-7' --verify-others`

controls.title: Securing freely accessible ports and access points of the BA (S)

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Freely accessible ports (Ethernet, USB) on BA components are organizationally intended for deactivation, but the implementation is not controlled. Network access control is not implemented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is an instruction to deactivate unused ports, but there is no technical verification. Ports temporarily activated for maintenance purposes are often forgotten and left open.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Physical inspection of freely accessible BA components (e.g., in hallways, public areas) and checking whether unused ports are active. Connecting a test device to check the network connection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The connection of components, especially unauthorized, unknown components and third-party devices, SHOULD be controlled and restricted, particularly on freely accessible Ethernet ports, USB ports, and other interfaces of the BA. Freely accessible interfaces for temporary maintenance purposes, such as USB ports on BA components, SHOULD only be activated when needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All unneeded physical ports on BA components are disabled in the software on the switch or in the device's operating system. Temporary activations for maintenance work must be requested and are automatically deactivated again after a specified time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the switch configurations to verify the deactivation of unused ports. Inspection of the process for temporary port activation and review of the corresponding tickets.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For freely accessible LAN or WLAN access points, network access control according to IEEE 802.1X or comparable security mechanisms SHOULD be used. The connection of an unauthorized or unknown component SHOULD be recorded in the event logging. Direct IP-based communication from such components with BA systems SHOULD be prevented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: 802.1X with certificate- or MAC address-based authentication is activated on all freely accessible network sockets. Devices that cannot authenticate are moved to a quarantine VLAN that has no access to the production BA network. Every failed authentication attempt is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the configuration of the RADIUS server and the switches for 802.1X. Performing a test by connecting an unauthorized device to a port. Checking the system logs for corresponding entries. `test-command: Connect-TestDevice -Port 42; Get-FirewallLog -Filter 'quarantine-vlan'`

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The connection of unauthorized devices is not only prevented but also triggers an automated security incident. The affected port is immediately physically shut down, and a notification containing the exact location of the port is sent to the security team. Communication in the quarantine network is actively monitored to detect attack attempts.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The network access control solution is integrated with the SIEM and a SOAR system. In case of an 802.1X failure, the switch port is set to 'shutdown' via script, and a ticket with the port designation from the documentation is created. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is active in the quarantine VLAN.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live test of the entire process by connecting an unauthorized laptop. Verification of whether the port is blocked and whether a corresponding alarm and ticket are generated in the SIEM/ticketing system.

parts.name: introduction
parts.title: Introduction
parts.prose:
Building automation (BA, also known as Building Automation and Control Systems, BACS) fully or partially automates the cross-trade operation of buildings and provides the technical infrastructure for this purpose. Essential technical functions of a building are provided by the technical building equipment (TBE), which is operated, maintained, and further developed with the services of technical building management (TBM). BA is thus a central tool of TBM for implementing the set objectives for building operation. It includes all products and services for the comprehensive, automated operation of the TBE. Criteria for the objectives can be functionality, energy efficiency and sustainability, security, availability, or comfort. BA can be scaled for services for buildings, building complexes, properties, or property portfolios. In the following, the term "building" is used uniformly for this purpose. Exceptions to this will be explicitly mentioned.
BA performs automation tasks such as automated measuring, controlling, and regulating (MCR), as well as tasks for monitoring, service and diagnosis, optimization, operation, and management for a building's TBE.
Within a building, BA is provided for one or possibly several demand organizations, for example, tenants. For this purpose, the TBE is usually controlled separately for different BA areas, for example, for demand organizations or for parts of the building.
In a building, BA can be implemented by several parallel BA systems, depending on the TBE used. A BA system represents the technical implementation of BA and can also be used across multiple buildings within a building complex or a property. Different BA systems can cooperate, but they can also be operated completely independently of each other.
While in the past, TBE was often not operated in a comprehensively automated manner, today BA systems are increasingly used for the superordinate, cross-trade control of TBE. For this, techniques that were originally only used in information technology (IT) and industrial process control and automation technology (Operational Technology, OT) are also being used more and more, e.g., communication via the Internet and cloud services.

parts.name: objective
parts.title: Objective
parts.prose: The objective of this module is to establish information security as an integral part of the planning, implementation, and operation of BA.

parts.name: usage
parts.title: Delimitation and Modeling
parts.prose:
The INF.14 Building Automation module is to be applied to the building automation (BA) of an institution as soon as the technical building equipment (TBE) in buildings is controlled by means of BA. The module is only to be applied to the interfaces of the BA to the TBE systems; the TBE systems with their internal networks and network structures are not the focus of this module.
The INF.14 Building Automation module deals with systems and services that must be considered and fulfilled when the BA, possibly consisting of several BA systems, is planned, set up and operated. It also deals with specific conditions that apply to networks and network components of the BA.
The following contents are also of importance and are dealt with elsewhere:
• The general requirements for BA and TBE that do not address the predominant aspects for integrated, automated measuring, steering and control are dealt with in the INF.13 Technical Building Management module. This must always be considered as well.
• Requirements for the general infrastructure, in particular buildings and rooms or workstations, are dealt with in the modules of the INF Infrastructure layer (e.g. module INF.1 General Building).
• If parts of the BA required for an institution are provided by another institution, e.g. by service providers in the role of building operators (operating organization), the OPS.2.3 Use of Outsourcing module must be applied for the provision and operation of the BA.
• Specific requirements for BA components that can also be used for industrial IT or OT are dealt with in the modules of the IND Industrial IT layer (see e.g. module IND.2.3 Sensors and Actuators or module IND.2.7 Safety Instrumented Systems).
• The NET.1.1 Network Architecture and Design module deals with the fundamental aspects of networks, as they are applicable not only to office IT but also to BA and industrial IT. General requirements for securing network components are dealt with in the modules in NET.3 Network Components (e.g. module NET.3.1 Routers and Switches).
• In addition, all suitable organizational and technical modules for servers and applications must be applied. For example, the OPS.1.2.5 Remote Maintenance module must be applied for remote access to the BA components.
• If buildings are networked on a cloud basis, the OPS.2.2 Cloud Usage module must also be applied.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Inadequate planning of the BA
parts.prose:
The BA serves for the coordinated, comprehensive control of TBE systems. Inadequate planning of the BA can thus lead to property damage or financial losses and, in the worst case, to personal injury.
This can happen, for example, if the central control system of a turnstile system fails due to insufficient redundancy planning and people are trapped in an airlock.
The described threat situation is also exacerbated in BA by the complexity of the planning. Here, heterogeneous groups of TBE systems (trades) as well as a multitude of different service providers and BA areas must be taken into account.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Faulty integration of technical building equipment systems into the BA
parts.prose:
The BA controls the TBE systems comprehensively. If just one system is faulty or inadequately integrated, the functionality of the entire BA can be restricted.
For example, incoming messages may be misinterpreted or messages may not reach the BA, causing the BA to react incorrectly or not at all. For instance, if the information from the access control system is not received correctly or at all, the heating and shading for the corresponding rooms may not be controlled appropriately.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Use of insecure systems and protocols in the BA
parts.prose:
In the technical building equipment systems controlled by the BA, components are often used that, for example, no longer receive updates due to their age, have vulnerabilities, or no longer correspond to the current state of the art. This often results from insufficient quality in the development and maintenance processes of the manufacturing companies or from software that uses insecure protocols due to a lack of computing and storage capacity.
Furthermore, the manufacturing companies often do not provide patches, so that insecure BA-relevant components are used for a very long period of time. The threat is exacerbated by the fact that access to such components must also be enabled in the BA.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Incorrect configuration of the building automation
parts.prose:
Depending on which areas of the BA are incorrectly configured, this can lead to impairments in operational processes, unauthorized physical access to protected areas, damage to systems, and even building and personal injury.
Examples of this are:
• Incorrectly configured air conditioning, which can lead to overheating and failure of IT systems or, in corresponding weather conditions, even to impairments to people's health.
• Uncoordinated configured building technology systems can lead to personal and system damage if, for example, power and fire extinguishing systems are not operated in a coordinated manner.
• Likewise, incorrectly configured access systems can lead to personal injury if doors cannot be opened in an emergency.
The threat is particularly relevant for the BA, as a faulty configuration can often not be detected before going live due to a lack of testing possibilities. This can also occur with a faulty update or a faulty update history that renders a BA system unusable.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Manipulation of the interfaces from standalone technical building equipment systems to the building automation
parts.prose:
Manipulated interfaces between BA systems and coupled TBE systems can lead to faulty reactions in the BA.
An example of this is that a manipulated message from a fire alarm system can cause all doors to be opened automatically, thus granting unauthorized persons access to the building.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Insufficiently protected access to the BA
parts.prose:
The BA comprises a multitude of components that provide, exchange, and receive cross-system information, e.g., for personnel location tracking or for room automation. The devices communicate via LAN and WLAN, but also via other wireless technologies such as Bluetooth.
If such network access points are not adequately protected, DoS attacks can be carried out through them. The BA systems can also be manipulated or sabotaged, and in some cases, even the entire IT of the institution can be reached. Manipulated BA systems can then cause an increased volume of data, leading to an overload of networks and components. Data leakage or the introduction of malware is also possible via an inadequately protected access point.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Insufficiently secured control elements of the BA
parts.prose:
If easily accessible control elements of the BA are inadequately secured, the BA can be attacked via them. Examples include wall-mounted control panels or control elements used by gate personnel to open remote doors or gates, for example.
If access to such control elements is inadequately protected, e.g., due to a lack of authentication, unauthorized access can be enabled.
Likewise, inadequately protected connections of control elements, such as LAN or USB interfaces, can provide unauthorized access.

parts.name: risk
parts.title: Insufficiently secured mobile connections
parts.prose: Particularly at the field and automation level, it is often necessary to use BA components that are connected via a cellular interface to the respective manufacturing company or to service providers such as a weather service. If these interfaces and the communication are inadequately protected and permanently active, they offer unauthorized persons or attackers access to the BA network.

controls.title: Definition of requirements (B) [Building services, Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only basic, informal, and mostly undocumented requirements for the security of the data center or server room exist. A concept for security zones is completely missing or not enforced.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Requirements are determined ad hoc in discussions. There is no formal documentation or approval process. The separation of areas such as logistics and IT operations is done arbitrarily and without any security-related justification.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check whether written and approved requirements documents for the data center exist. Conduct interviews with staff to determine if the requirements are known and understood. Verify if a physical or logical zoning is recognizable.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The basic technical and organizational requirements for the data center are documented, but are often generic and not specifically tailored to the protection requirements.
