A simple division into a secured IT area and an unsecured external area exists, but fine-grained zoning is missing.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A document describes general specifications (e.g., 'the room must be cooled'). However, this document is not regularly reviewed or updated. The IT operations area is secured by a locked door, but support and logistics areas are located in the same security zone.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the document with the data center requirements. Check if this document meets the basic operational requirements (power, climate). Conduct a site inspection to check the basic physical separation between the IT area and public areas.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Appropriate technical and organizational specifications MUST be defined and implemented for a data center. When a data center is planned or suitable premises are selected, appropriate security measures MUST also be planned, taking into account the protection requirements of the IT components (especially availability). A data center MUST be designed as a closed security area overall. It MUST also have different security zones. For this purpose, areas such as administration, logistics, IT operations, and support MUST be clearly separated from each other.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The requirements are formally documented in a dedicated security concept for the data center. This concept defines clear security zones (e.g., Zone 1: Logistics, Zone 2: Support/Technical Rooms, Zone 3: IT Operations Room) with specific security measures for access, fire protection, and environmental conditions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the data center security concept. Check if the concept provides for the separation of administrative, logistics, IT operations, and support areas. During a site inspection, verify if the zones defined in the concept are physically implemented and if the separation is effective.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The defined requirements are formally reviewed, versioned, and are directly linked to the institution's business continuity plans. For server rooms, it SHOULD be checked whether different security zones can be established. The zoning concept is worked out in detail and also considers the protective effect of the structural shell of the respective zones.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The data center security concept is reviewed annually or upon significant changes and approved by management. For server rooms, a risk analysis is performed to decide whether a subdivision into different zones (e.g., for critical vs. non-critical systems) is useful. The resistance classes of doors and walls between the zones are documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check the approval and revision history of the data center security concept. Review the risk analysis for server rooms, if available. Verify that the documented resistance classes of the structural elements between the zones are plausible and meet the requirements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The requirements are based on a formal risk analysis that is aligned with international standards such as DIN EN 50600 or ISO/IEC 27001. The security zone concept is fully implemented with physical and logical separation, is monitored by automated systems (e.g., access control, video surveillance), and its effectiveness is regularly verified through audits and tests.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The design of the security zones is directly derived from the protection requirement assessments of the business processes. The transition between zones is controlled by interlocking doors (mantraps). Compliance with the zone rules is monitored by a Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system, which generates alarms for unauthorized access attempts or zone breaches.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the risk analysis and the comparison with DIN EN 50600. Check the configuration of the access control and SIEM system with regard to zone monitoring. Observe the operation of personal interlocks and check the alerting for rule violations.

controls.title: Creation of fire compartments (B) [Planner]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only the legally required, minimum fire protection requirements are implemented, without special consideration for the protection of IT systems or availability. Existing fire compartments may have unsealed openings.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: During the construction phase, the building code requirements were met, but later cable penetrations were not properly sealed. There is no specific plan to protect the IT operations area as a separate fire compartment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of walls and ceilings for unsealed cable and pipe penetrations. Comparison of the building plans with the legal minimum requirements at the time of construction.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The central IT operations room is designed as a separate fire compartment. However, support areas such as technical or storage rooms are not protected by separate fire compartments and pose a risk.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The server room is enclosed by F30 or F90 walls and a T30 door. However, the adjacent rooms, where the UPS or air conditioning system is located, are part of the general building fire compartment.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review the building plans and the fire protection concept to identify the boundaries of the fire compartments. Check if the IT operations room forms its own fire compartment and how the support areas are treated in terms of fire protection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Suitable fire and smoke compartments MUST be established for the premises of a data center. The fire and smoke compartments MUST provide protection for the technical equipment located within them and their availability, beyond the scope prescribed by building law. The spread of fire and smoke MUST be prevented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A fire protection concept defines separate fire compartments for the IT operations area, the essential support areas (e.g., electrical room, UPS room), and logistics areas. All penetrations are professionally sealed with certified firestops and documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the fire protection concept. Check if separate fire compartments are defined for all critical data center areas. Conduct a random check of the firestops and their documentation (e.g., declaration of conformity).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the case of a server room, it SHOULD be checked whether suitable fire and smoke compartments can be implemented for the premises. The fire resistance class of the walls, doors, and firestops is explicitly documented and regularly checked for integrity, especially after construction work.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: For server rooms, an analysis is carried out to assess the feasibility and benefit of establishing separate fire compartments. A register of all firestops is maintained, which is updated with every change. After every construction measure, a formal acceptance of the newly installed or modified firestops is carried out by a fire safety officer.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review the analysis for the creation of fire compartments for server rooms. Request the firestop register and compare it with the conditions found during a site inspection. Check the process documentation for the acceptance of fire protection measures after modifications.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire compartments are designed with a higher fire resistance class (e.g., F90/F120) than legally required. Ventilation ducts that penetrate fire compartments are equipped with automatic fire dampers, which are controlled by the fire alarm system to actively prevent the spread of smoke and fire.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The design of the fire compartments is based on a risk analysis that also considers the scenario of a fully developed fire in a neighboring area. The fire dampers are included in the regular tests of the fire alarm system to ensure their correct function.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check the risk analysis and the fire protection concept for the justification for the selected fire resistance class. Request the test logs of the fire alarm system and explicitly check if the control of the fire dampers was part of the tests.

controls.title: Use of an uninterruptible power supply (B) [Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Individual, small UPS systems (desktop class) are used sporadically for a few servers considered critical. Network components, storage systems, or the air conditioning control are not protected.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees procure small UPS devices for their systems as needed. There is no central planning, monitoring, or maintenance of these devices. The batteries are never tested or replaced.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the racks for the presence of UPS systems. Check if infrastructure components (switches, etc.) are also connected to a UPS. Ask the administrators about the process for maintenance and battery replacement.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central UPS is installed that supplies the IT loads. However, its capacity is not regularly adjusted to the actual consumption, which poses a risk of overload. The air conditioning system is not connected to the UPS. For a server room, the necessity of a UPS is only checked based on availability requirements.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single, central UPS was installed when the room was set up. Since then, many new servers have been added without checking the UPS load. In the event of a power outage, the IT would continue to run, but the air conditioning would fail, which would quickly lead to overheating.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check the current load display of the UPS and compare it with its nominal capacity. Check the circuit diagram to determine if the air conditioning control is supplied by the UPS. For server rooms, request the analysis that led to the decision for or against a UPS.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An uninterruptible power supply (UPS) MUST be installed for all operationally relevant components of the data center. The UPS MUST be sufficiently dimensioned. At least the control of the air conditioning systems MUST be connected to the UPS. The UPS MUST be regularly maintained and tested for functionality according to the manufacturer's specifications. For UPS systems with a battery as an energy store, the battery MUST be kept within the required temperature range.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A centrally planned UPS is in use, its capacity covering the current demand with a safety margin. A maintenance contract with the manufacturer is in place, and the annual maintenance is logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the UPS planning documents and comparing the nominal power with the current consumption. Requesting the maintenance logs from recent years. Verifying compliance with manufacturer specifications for maintenance intervals. Checking the temperature records of the battery room.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The UPS battery SHOULD preferably be located separately from the UPS power electronics to minimize mutual interference (e.g., from heat or in case of fire). The UPS load is continuously monitored, and automatic warnings are generated when the load approaches a threshold.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The UPS batteries are housed in a separate, air-conditioned room that is designed as its own fire compartment. The UPS is connected to a monitoring system that sends a notification to the IT department when 80% of the nominal load is reached.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the premises to verify the physical separation of UPS electronics and batteries. Checking the configuration of the monitoring system and the defined thresholds for load evaluation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A modular, redundant (e.g., N+1) UPS system is used, in which the failure of one component is compensated for without interruption. The UPS performs weekly automated self-tests and semi-annual automated load tests, the results of which are logged and centrally evaluated. This ensures consistently high availability and reliability.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A UPS system with three power modules supplies a load for which two modules would be sufficient (N+1 redundancy). The UPS firmware is configured to perform a battery test every Sunday at 3 a.m. and a test under load (via the bypass) on the first day of each quarter. The logs are automatically sent to the central log management system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Verification of the UPS system architecture for modularity and redundancy. Requesting the configuration files and automated test logs of the UPS from the log management system for the last 12 months.

controls.title: Emergency Power Off (B) [Building Services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A single, unprotected emergency power off switch is present, which, when activated, shuts down the entire data center, including the UPS and safety-related systems (e.g., emergency lighting). This poses a high risk of data loss and consequential damage.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A red mushroom button is installed next to the door. It is not covered and can easily be activated by accident. Activating it leads to a complete power outage in the entire area.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the emergency power off switch for protective devices (e.g., a protective cover). Requesting the circuit diagram to understand the effects of activation. Interviewing staff to determine if they know what the switch does.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Emergency power off switches are present, but they are not clearly labeled or adequately protected against incorrect operation. It is unclear which areas or systems are affected by which switch.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Several emergency power off switches are distributed in and around the server room. Their labeling is faded or missing. The staff is unsure about the exact function of each individual switch.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the emergency power off switches for clear and understandable labeling and for protective covers. Interviews with the operating personnel to determine their level of knowledge about the function of the switches.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There MUST be suitable means to de-energize electrical consumers in the data center. It MUST be considered if and how an existing UPS is integrated. If classic emergency power off switches are used, it MUST be ensured that they do not shut down the entire data center. The emergency shutdown MUST be reasonably partitioned and targeted. All emergency power off switches MUST be protected against unintentional or unauthorized activation.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Emergency stop buttons are installed at the entrances and exits of the data center, protected by a flap to prevent accidental activation. The buttons are clearly labeled (e.g., 'EPO IT ROOM', 'EPO CLIMATE CONTROL'). Activating them specifically shuts down only the respective consumer groups, while, for example, the UPS-supported emergency lighting remains active. The concept is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the concept for the emergency shutdown. On-site inspection of the labeling and protection of the emergency power off switches. Comparison of the partitioning described in the concept with the actual circuits (based on circuit diagrams).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency power off system (referred to as NOT-HALT in Germany) is zoned and allows for the targeted shutdown of individual areas (e.g., a rack row) or systems (e.g., the cooling generation). The system is clearly documented, and the staff is regularly trained in its use to be able to act correctly and without hesitation in an emergency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a separate, clearly marked emergency power off switch for each rack row. The documentation contains a detailed plan of which systems are affected by which switch. Annual safety training includes a module on emergency shutdown.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the documentation of the zoned emergency power off system. Reviewing the training materials and records of the staff. Checking the labeling and arrangement of the switches in the data center.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The emergency power off system is integrated into the fire alarm and extinguishing system. An activation is managed via a central building management system and requires two-factor confirmation to prevent incorrect operation (e.g., button activation and software confirmation by a second person).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: When the gas extinguishing system is triggered, the power supply in the affected area is automatically and selectively shut off to prevent short circuits and re-ignition. A manual trigger via a button must be confirmed by an authorized person in the building management system within 60 seconds, otherwise the command expires.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the technical documentation of the coupling of the fire alarm system and the emergency power off system. Checking the configuration of the workflow for the 2-factor confirmation in the building management system. Analyzing the logs from integration tests.

controls.title: Compliance with air temperature and humidity (B) [Building Services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Air conditioning is available, but it is not monitored. The temperature is only checked sporadically and manually (e.g., by feel), without systematic recording.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A simple air conditioner runs in continuous operation. There is no thermometer in the room. Whether it is too warm or too cold is judged based on the personal feeling of the employees.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection to see if a thermometer and a hygrometer are present in the room. Interviewing employees on how and how often temperature and humidity are checked.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Temperature and humidity are monitored by sensors, but there is no automated recording of the values or alerting when thresholds are exceeded. The values must be read manually from a display.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A digital thermometer/hygrometer with a display is installed in the room. The employees are instructed to pay attention to the values during their daily inspection rounds. There is no long-term recording.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking for the presence of monitoring devices with a display. Requesting manually kept logbooks or checklists in which the values are entered. Checking whether there are instructions for what to do in case of a deviation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It MUST be ensured that the air temperature and humidity in the IT operating area are within the limits prescribed by the manufacturers. The actual heat load in the cooled areas MUST be checked at regular intervals. Any existing air conditioning system MUST be regularly maintained. The parameters temperature and humidity MUST be recorded in such a way that it is possible to retrospectively determine whether limits have been exceeded.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Sensors for temperature and humidity are installed. Their values are recorded every minute in a central system (e.g., monitoring software like Nagios or Zabbix) and stored for at least 30 days. The heat load is reassessed semi-annually by measuring the power consumption of the racks. There is a maintenance contract for the air conditioning system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Reviewing the historical data of the monitoring system to check for past compliance with the limits. Requesting the documentation for the last heat load calculation. Checking the maintenance logs of the air conditioning system.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automated alert is set up for any deviation from the defined thresholds for temperature and humidity. The recorded data is regularly analyzed to identify trends and proactively adjust the cooling performance before problems occur.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: If a threshold is exceeded, the monitoring system automatically sends an email and an SMS to the on-call service. The recorded temperature trends are evaluated quarterly to identify hotspots or creeping temperature increases and to adjust the air guidance or the setpoint temperature of the air conditioning units.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the configuration of the alerting rules in the monitoring system. Triggering a test alarm to verify the notification chain. Requesting the reports from the quarterly trend analysis.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A highly developed environmental monitoring system with sensors at several strategic points (e.g., air intake and outlet of each rack, in the cold and hot aisle) is in use. The system is integrated into a building management system (BMS) or DCIM (Data Center Infrastructure Management) and enables automated, dynamic control and optimization of the cooling systems, for example through cold aisle containment.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Temperature sensors are installed at the front and back of each rack. This data is collected by a DCIM software. The software dynamically controls the speed of the fans in the air conditioning units to keep the temperature in the cold aisle exactly at the setpoint, thus minimizing energy consumption. The cold aisles are physically contained to prevent mixing of cold and warm air.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the sensor layout in the data center and in the racks. Requesting the configuration and control documentation of the DCIM/BMS. Analyzing the historical data on cooling efficiency (e.g., PUE value) and the stability of temperatures at the rack intakes.

controls.title: Access Control (B) [Building Services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The server room door is secured with a simple mechanical lock. Keys have been issued to an indefinite number of people without formal documentation or a return process.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A standard profile cylinder is used. It is no longer traceable who has a key. There is no logging of who enters the room and when.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the key issuance list. If no list exists, the requirement is not met. Interviewing employees about who has access and how it is regulated.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An electronic access control system (e.g., with a card reader) is installed at the main entrance of the data center. However, the access logs are not evaluated regularly or only in case of a specific suspicion.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Employees receive transponder cards for access. The system logs all entries. However, there is no process for regularly reviewing the logs for unauthorized or unusual access attempts.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the functionality of the electronic access control system. Request for the access logs of the last 30 days. Interviewing those responsible about the process for reviewing these logs.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access to the data center MUST be controlled. Access rights MUST be assigned according to the specifications of module ORP.4 Identity and Access Management. For personnel working in the data center, it MUST be ensured that they do not gain access to IT systems outside their area of responsibility. All access points to the data center MUST be equipped with access control devices. Every access to the data center MUST be individually recorded by the access control system. It MUST be regularly checked whether the regulations are being complied with. The requirements MUST be documented in a policy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A documented access policy defines who receives access and for what reason. The assignment of access rights follows a formal approval process. All doors, including emergency exits, are equipped with readers and contacts. The logs are checked weekly for anomalies. The revocation of permissions during personnel changes is ensured.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the access policy and the process description for rights assignment. Reviewing the access logs and the logs of the reviews. Comparing the list of authorized persons with the institution's current personnel and role list.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the case of a server room, it SHOULD be checked whether monitoring all access points is appropriate. For particularly sensitive areas within the data center, a two-factor authentication system (e.g., card + PIN) is used. The review of access rights (re-certification) is carried out at least quarterly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A card reader with a PIN pad is used for the main server room. Windows or other possible access points are monitored by magnetic contacts. Every three months, the respective supervisors are presented with a list of their employees authorized to access for confirmation.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the technical implementation of two-factor authentication. Request for the analysis on monitoring all access points. Inspection of the logs from the last re-certification rounds.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Access is controlled by biometric features in combination with mantraps to effectively prevent tailgating (the unauthorized passage of a second person). The access logs are automatically analyzed in real-time for anomalous patterns (e.g., access at unusual times, repeated denied attempts), and security alarms are triggered in case of suspicion.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A mantrap with an integrated fingerprint reader and weight sensor is installed at the entrance to the IT operations area. The access data is streamed to a SIEM system, which is configured with rules for anomaly detection. An alarm is forwarded directly to the security service.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Observation of the mantrap's function during operation. Review of the configuration of the anomaly detection rules in the SIEM. Analysis of the alarm logs of the last three months for generated and processed security incidents.

controls.title: Locking and Securing (B) [Employees, Facility Management]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Doors to the server room are often left open or propped open with wedges for convenience, especially during maintenance work.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is no binding instruction or culture to keep doors closed at all times. Staff find the constant opening and closing to be a hindrance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Unannounced walk-throughs of the premises at different times of the day to check if doors are left open. Interviewing staff about the applicable rules.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Doors and windows are kept closed but are of standard construction and offer only minimal resistance to forced entry. There is no privacy screen.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Standard interior doors and normal windows are used. From the outside, one can see into the room and at the equipment through the windows.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the construction type of doors and windows. Checking whether the room can be seen from the outside. Requesting the building description to check the resistance classes, if available.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All data center doors MUST be kept locked at all times. Windows MUST be avoided in the planning phase if possible. If they do exist, they MUST, like the doors, be kept locked at all times. Doors and windows MUST provide adequate protection against attacks and environmental influences appropriate to the security level. They MUST be fitted with a privacy screen. It MUST be noted that the structural design of all space-enclosing elements must be equivalent in terms of the required protective effect.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All doors are self-closing and self-locking. Any existing windows are fitted with frosted glass film to prevent viewing. The resistance of the walls, ceilings, floors, and doors is coordinated and documented in the security concept.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking whether all doors are equipped with door closers and close correctly. Checking the privacy screen on windows. Requesting the security concept to check the defined and coordinated protective effect of the room elements.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Doors and windows are certified to a defined resistance class (e.g., RC 2 according to DIN EN 1627). Door opening sensors are installed, which are monitored and trigger an alarm if a door is open for too long (door-open alarm).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The doors are certified as RC 2 doors and are marked accordingly. The access control system is configured to send an alarm to the security center after a door has been open for 60 seconds.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the certificates or markings of the doors and windows. Triggering a test alarm by intentionally keeping a door open and checking the alarm chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All building envelope elements (walls, doors, windows) are certified to a high resistance class (e.g., RC 3 or higher). In addition, intrusion detection systems (e.g., motion detectors, glass break sensors) are installed and connected to a central alarm system that detects and reports an intrusion attempt.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The entire outer shell of the data center is constructed in RC-3 design. The interior is monitored by infrared motion detectors, which send a silent alarm to an external security service provider in case of unauthorized presence (outside of normal operating hours or when the room is declared 'empty').

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the certification documents for the building envelope elements for the high resistance class. Requesting the concept of the intrusion detection system. Performing a functional test of the intrusion detectors in coordination with the security service provider.

controls.title: Use of a fire alarm system (B) [Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only the standard, battery-operated smoke detectors required by building codes are present. These are not networked and only trigger a local acoustic alarm.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Simple smoke detectors from the hardware store are installed in the rooms. There is no forwarding of an alarm. If no one is on-site, a fire will not be noticed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the installed smoke detectors. Checking if there is a connection to a central fire alarm control panel. Checking the test and maintenance records for the detectors (e.g., battery replacement).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central fire alarm system is installed but only monitors the main IT room. Support areas such as electrical rooms or UPS rooms are not connected to the fire alarm system.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Automatic fire detectors are installed in the server room, which are connected to a fire alarm control panel (FACP) in the building. The adjacent technical rooms, from which a higher fire risk often originates, are not equipped with detectors.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the detector group overview of the fire alarm system. Comparing the monitored areas with the floor plan of the data center. Identifying critical areas that are not monitored.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A fire alarm system MUST be installed in a data center. It MUST monitor all areas. All messages from the fire alarm system MUST be appropriately forwarded. The fire alarm system MUST be regularly maintained. It MUST be ensured that there are no special fire loads in the rooms of the data center.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A comprehensive fire alarm system is installed that monitors the IT operations area, raised floors, suspended ceilings, and all support areas. Messages are forwarded to a permanently staffed location (e.g., reception, external service provider). A maintenance contract according to DIN 14675 exists. Organizational rules prohibit the storage of flammable materials (e.g., cardboard boxes) in the technical rooms.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the concept and maintenance logs of the fire alarm system. Reviewing the alarm and intervention plan. Inspecting the rooms for unauthorized fire loads.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The fire alarm system is addressable, i.e., it can display the exact detector that triggered the alarm on a display. This allows for quick localization of the fire source. The system is connected to a certified emergency call and service control center (NSL).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In case of an alarm, the exact detector number and a plain text description of the location are displayed on the FACP display (e.g., 'Smoke detector 14, DC raised floor row 3'). The connection to the NSL is made via a certified transmission path.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the technical specification of the fire alarm system for addressability. Requesting the contract and conformity certificate for the connection to the NSL. Triggering a test alarm to check the correct display on the FACP and the report to the NSL.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An aspirating smoke detection (ASD) system, also known as a very early warning fire detection system, is used. This system detects fire particles in the air long before a conventional smoke detector would trigger. The ASD is integrated into the extinguishing system control and the emergency power off system to initiate automated countermeasures.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A VESDA (Very Early Smoke Detection Apparatus) system with multiple alarm levels is installed. At the first level (Information), a message is sent to the administrators. At the second level (Pre-alarm), the fire department is alerted. At the third level (Main alarm), the gas extinguishing system is triggered and the power supply in the affected area is shut down.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Requesting the concept and project documents of the aspirating smoke detection system. Reviewing the configuration of the different alarm levels and the associated actions. Analyzing the logs of integration tests of the entire action chain (detection, alarming, extinguishing, shutdown).

controls.title: Use of an extinguishing or fire prevention system (B) [Facility Management]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are a few portable fire extinguishers, but they are unsuitable for fires in electrical systems (e.g., water extinguishers). The staff is not trained in their use.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single powder extinguisher is located in the hallway outside the server room. Its use in the server room would lead to massive consequential damage to the IT equipment. Staff have never received instructions on its use.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of existing fire extinguishers for their suitability for electrical fires (note the labeling). Request for training certificates for the use of fire extinguishers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There are sufficient portable fire extinguishers with a suitable extinguishing agent (e.g., CO2) available, and they are regularly maintained. Staff have received basic instruction. However, there is no automatic extinguishing system or a defined rapid response team.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: CO2 extinguishers are clearly visibly mounted in and in front of the server room. The inspection stickers are up to date. All employees have participated in a general fire safety briefing, which also included the handling of fire extinguishers.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Checking the number, placement, and maintenance status of the fire extinguishers. Requesting the attendance lists from the last fire safety briefing.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In a data center, either a state-of-the-art extinguishing or fire prevention system MUST be installed, OR technical (especially comprehensive early fire detection according to INF.2.A17) and organizational measures (trained personnel and response plans) MUST ensure an immediate response (within a maximum of 3 minutes) to early fire detection alerts. In server rooms without such systems, a sufficient number and size of portable fire extinguishers with suitable extinguishing agents MUST be available, and all employees MUST be trained in their use.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Since there is no automatic extinguishing system, a detailed response plan has been created. The early fire detection (aspirating smoke detection) is linked to a permanently staffed location. The personnel there are trained as fire wardens and are instructed to rush to the server room with CO2 extinguishers immediately upon an alarm. The maximum response time of 3 minutes is ensured and logged through regular drills.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the response plan and the training certificates of the fire wardens. Review of the logs from the last drills to check compliance with the 3-minute deadline. If an extinguishing system is present: Request for the planning and acceptance documents.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An automatic gas extinguishing system (e.g., with inert gases like argon or nitrogen, or chemical extinguishing agents like Novec 1230) is installed in the primary IT operational areas. Response plans for a release are practiced quarterly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The server room is equipped with an argon gas extinguishing system. Before release, there is an optical and acoustic pre-warning period to allow people to leave the room. The drills for evacuation and behavior after an extinguishing event are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the planning, acceptance, and maintenance documentation of the gas extinguishing system. Request for the logs of the last evacuation drills.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A fire prevention system using oxygen reduction is installed. This system permanently creates an atmosphere in which a fire cannot ignite in the first place. The system is continuously monitored and represents the highest level of protection, as it proactively prevents fires rather than just combating them.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A hypoxic air technology system permanently enriches the room air with nitrogen, lowering the oxygen content to approx. 15%. This value is permanently monitored by redundant sensors. It is still safe for personnel to enter the room. The system prevents the outbreak of fire and thus avoids any downtime or damage from fire or extinguishing agents.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the planning and safety documentation of the fire prevention system, including evidence of its harmlessness to health. Review of the historical data from the oxygen sensors to check compliance with the setpoint.

controls.title: Inspection and maintenance of the infrastructure (B) [Maintenance personnel, building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Maintenance and inspection work is carried out purely reactively, i.e., only when a component has already failed. There is no preventive maintenance.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The air conditioning system is only repaired when it no longer cools. A defective fire barrier is only discovered by chance during the next construction project.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for maintenance plans and logs. If none exist, the requirement is not met. Review of trouble tickets to see if maintenance always follows failures.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic maintenance plan exists for the most important systems such as UPS and air conditioning. However, it is not always strictly followed or is documented with gaps.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: There is a checklist for annual maintenance, but the dates are sometimes postponed by months when other tasks seem more important. The logs are only partially completed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the maintenance plan and the associated logs. Comparison of the planned with the actual maintenance dates. Checking the logs for completeness.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: For all components of the physical and technical infrastructure, at least the inspection and maintenance intervals and regulations recommended by the manufacturer or specified by standards MUST be observed. Inspections and maintenance work MUST be logged. Fire barriers MUST be checked to ensure they are intact. The results MUST be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Maintenance contracts exist for all essential infrastructure components (air conditioning, UPS, emergency power generator, fire alarm system, extinguishing system). The maintenance intervals comply with the specifications of the manufacturers and relevant standards (e.g., DIN VDE). All work and tests carried out, including the visual inspection of the fire barriers, are recorded in a central maintenance log.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the maintenance contracts and the central maintenance documentation. Random comparison of the intervals with the manufacturer's specifications. Checking the logs for completeness and traceability, especially the inspection of the fire barriers.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A computerized maintenance planning system (CMPS) or a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) is used for planning, controlling, and documenting all maintenance activities. This system automatically generates maintenance orders and escalates overdue work.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All infrastructure systems with their maintenance plans are recorded in a CMMS. The system automatically creates tickets for due maintenance and assigns them to the responsible technicians. The status of all maintenance work can be viewed transparently at any time.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for an extract from the CMMS showing the maintenance history of a selected system (e.g., air conditioning system) for the last two years. Review of the configuration for automatic order creation and escalation.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Predictive maintenance techniques are used. Based on sensor data (e.g., vibrations, temperatures, run times) and analyses, failures are predicted before they occur, and maintenance work is planned proactively and as needed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Vibration sensors are attached to the motors of the air conditioning units. An analysis software monitors the vibration patterns and reports when bearing wear is likely, so the bearing can be replaced before it fails. Similar procedures are used for UPS batteries (impedance measurement) and other critical components.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the concepts for predictive maintenance. Review of the analysis software and the historical sensor data. Request for examples where maintenance was successfully carried out based on a prediction.

controls.title: Automatic monitoring of the infrastructure (B) [Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no automatic monitoring. The functionality of the infrastructure is only determined through manual walk-throughs or in the event of a failure.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A leak is only noticed when water is visible on the floor. A UPS fault is only noticed during a power outage when the IT systems fail anyway.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Ask about the process for monitoring infrastructure components. If it is purely manual, the requirement is not met. Review the checklists for walk-throughs, if available.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Some systems, such as the UPS, have local alarms (e.g., a red light or a beep). However, there is no central monitoring or an automatic notification system that forwards the alarms to responsible personnel.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The UPS beeps when it switches to battery power. But if no one is in the room to hear it, the fault goes unnoticed. There is no connection to a network monitoring system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the infrastructure components for local alarm indicators. Check whether these alarms are connected to a central system (e.g., via SNMP or Modbus). Simulate an alarm (if possible) to see what happens.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All infrastructure facilities, such as leakage monitoring, air conditioning, power, and UPS systems, MUST be monitored automatically. Detected faults MUST be forwarded and processed as quickly as possible in an appropriate manner. The responsible employees MUST be alerted promptly.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All critical infrastructure systems are connected to a central monitoring system via potential-free contacts or network interfaces (e.g., SNMP). In the event of a fault, a ticket is automatically created in the ticketing system and an email is sent to the on-call service. The response times are defined in an SLA.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the concept for infrastructure monitoring. Review of the monitoring system configuration and the alarm chain. Analysis of trouble tickets to check compliance with the defined response times.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In the case of a server room, IT and support devices that do not require, or only rarely require, operation by a person SHOULD be equipped with a remote display for faults. A central Building Management System (BMS) or a Data Center Infrastructure Management (DCIM) tool consolidates all alarms and provides a unified dashboard for a quick overview.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A DCIM system visualizes the status of all infrastructure components on a dashboard. In addition to alarms, operating parameters such as power consumption, temperatures, and UPS load are displayed in real time. This enables rapid root cause analysis in the event of faults.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Live demonstration of the BMS or DCIM dashboard. Check which systems are connected and what information is visualized. Check whether the remote display is also implemented for devices in server rooms.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The monitoring system uses AI/ML-based methods to correlate events from different systems, identify the root cause, and predict potential future failures based on patterns of minor alarms (AIOps).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An AIOps platform analyzes the logs and metrics of all infrastructure and IT systems. If the temperature in a rack slowly increases and at the same time the CPU load on the servers in this rack increases, the system correlates these events and proactively suggests increasing the cooling for this area before a temperature alarm is triggered.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the concept and architecture of the AIOps platform. Review the implemented correlation rules and analysis models. Request reports showing how the system has proactively identified and helped resolve problems in the past.

controls.title: Use of an early fire detection system (B) [Planners, Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: An early fire detection system is installed, but it only triggers a local alarm and is not forwarded to a constantly staffed location. A response to the alarm is not guaranteed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An aspirating smoke detection system is present, but its alarm signal only results in a light illuminating on the front of the device. There is no forwarding via network or contact.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review the configuration of the early fire detection system. Check if alarm forwarding is configured. Simulate an alarm (e.g., with test gas) to observe the response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The system forwards alarms to a staffed location, but the response time is not defined, guaranteed, or practiced. It is unclear how quickly and with what measures a response will be made.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An alarm message appears on a monitor in the gatehouse. However, there are no clear instructions on what the gatekeeper should do and how quickly they must react.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the alarm and intervention plans. Check whether clear instructions and time limits exist for early fire detection alarms. Interview the staff at the staffed location about the procedure in case of an alarm.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A data center MUST be equipped with an early fire detection system. The alarms from the early fire detection system MUST be forwarded to a constantly staffed location that can initiate a control and protective response within a maximum of 3 minutes. Alternatively, an automatic protective response MUST occur. To achieve a balance between fire protection and availability, it MUST be ensured that redundant facilities are not located together in the effective area of the same power disconnection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An aspirating smoke detection system (ASD) is installed. Its alarm is forwarded to a 24/7 staffed control center. The intervention plan stipulates that the control center immediately informs trained fire safety assistants, who must be on-site for reconnaissance within 3 minutes. The A and B power supply lines are each coupled to separate ASD systems.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the concept for the early fire detection and the intervention plan. Check the logs of alarm drills for compliance with the 3-minute deadline. Review the circuit diagrams to verify the separate supply of redundant systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A server room SHOULD be equipped with an early fire detection system. The system uses highly sensitive aspirating smoke detection systems (ASD/VESDA). Response drills are conducted and documented regularly to ensure the reliability of the manual intervention chain.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Even smaller, but critical, server rooms are equipped with an ASD. Unannounced alarm drills are held quarterly, during which the response time is measured and logged. The results are incorporated into the continuous improvement of processes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check whether server rooms outside the central data center are also equipped with early fire detection. Request the logs of the last four alarm drills and evaluate the measured response times.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The early fire detection system is multi-stage and combines aspirating smoke detection systems with thermal imaging cameras to ensure extremely fast and reliable detection. It is directly coupled to an automatic gas extinguishing system. The system can distinguish between different event types (e.g., dust vs. smoke particles) to minimize false alarms.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A multi-stage alarm concept is implemented: An ASD pre-alarm leads to verification by personnel. A simultaneous alarm from the ASD and a thermal imaging camera leads to the automatic activation of the extinguishing system. The sensitivity of the system is dynamically adjusted to the ambient conditions.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the concept for the multi-stage detection and response system. Review the logic and configuration of the trigger matrix (which combination of events leads to which action). Analyze the system logs for false alarms and their causes.

controls.title: Avoidance and monitoring of unnecessary lines (B) [Building services, Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Water, sewage, or gas pipes that are not for supplying the data center run unprotected directly above or next to the IT racks. The risk posed by these pipes is ignored.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A sewage pipe from the upper floors runs across the server room under the ceiling. There is no protective tray or monitoring.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the ceilings and walls in the data center for the presence of foreign supply lines. Check whether protective measures against leaks are in place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The presence of foreign supply lines is known and documented. However, no specific measures have been taken to minimize the risk.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The building plans note that a heating pipe crosses the room. However, neither an enclosure nor leakage sensors have been installed.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the documentation on foreign supply lines. Compare the documentation with the on-site conditions. Check whether risk minimization measures are described and implemented.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: In a data center, ONLY lines that serve the direct supply of the technology installed in the data center MAY be laid. If, for structural reasons, it is unavoidable to run lines through the data center, this MUST be documented, including the justification. The risks posed by such lines MUST be minimized by suitable measures, e.g., by enclosure and monitoring. The aforementioned lines may be run through server rooms, but they MUST be treated in the same way. Messages from the monitoring of the lines MUST be checked and evaluated immediately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Foreign, water-carrying pipes are laid in a welded stainless steel tray. Inside the tray, a leakage sensor cable is installed, which is connected to the central monitoring system. The necessity of the pipe routing is justified in writing and approved by management.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the approval documentation for the routing of foreign lines. Review the implementation of risk-minimizing measures (e.g., enclosure, sensors). Trigger a test alarm at the leakage sensor to check the notification chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All foreign lines (especially water-carrying ones) are routed in dedicated, sealed enclosures or shafts. These are equipped with leakage sensors connected to the central monitoring system. Monitoring is ensured around the clock.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A separate installation shaft was constructed for the foreign lines. This shaft is designed as its own fire compartment and is monitored for leaks. Access to the shaft is only possible for authorized personnel.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review the structural design of the installation shaft. Check the connection of the sensors to the 24/7 monitoring system. Review the access concept for the shaft.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The planning of the data center fundamentally prohibits the passage of non-essential supply lines through the IT operating rooms. Necessary lines, such as for the cold water supply of the air conditioning system or for the extinguishing system, are double-walled and are permanently monitored for pressure drops to detect leaks immediately.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The cold water pipes of the air conditioning system are implemented as a double-walled pipe system. The intermediate space is monitored by pressure sensors. A pressure drop in the outer or inner pipe immediately triggers an alarm, long before water can escape.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the planning guidelines for the data center that prohibit foreign lines. Review the technical specification and the monitoring configuration of the double-walled pipe systems.

controls.title: Perimeter protection for the data center (S) [Planners, Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is no clearly defined perimeter around the data center building. The property line is unmarked and freely accessible.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The data center is located on a company site that is not fenced. There is no visible demarcation from public space.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Inspection of the outdoor area to check for the presence of fences, gates, or other markings of the property line.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A simple fence (e.g., chain-link) is installed as a physical barrier around the property. However, there is no additional monitoring of the perimeter.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 2-meter high chain-link fence surrounds the site. Gates are secured with a simple padlock. There are no cameras or motion detectors on the fence.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the fence for condition and height. Check whether additional monitoring technology such as cameras or detection systems are installed on the fence.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: There is a defined perimeter with physical barriers (e.g., a sturdy fence). There are signs to deter unauthorized persons from entering and to indicate that surveillance is in place. Access is controlled via controlled gates or portals.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A bar fence secures the site. A video intercom system is installed at the gates, which is connected to the gatehouse. Signs indicate that the site is under video surveillance.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review the design of the fence and the access gates. Check the signage. Test the functionality of the intercom system at the gate.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Data centers SHOULD have perimeter protection. Depending on the defined protection requirement, the perimeter protection SHOULD consist of the following components: outer enclosure, security measures against unintentional and intentional non-violent overcoming of the property line, open-area security measures (e.g., video surveillance), external person and vehicle detection, and automatic alarming.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A high-security fence with anti-crawl protection is installed. The outdoor area is monitored by cameras with motion detection. When motion is detected in the secured area, an alarm is automatically sent to a security control center and the corresponding camera is switched on.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the concept for perimeter protection. Review the technical implementation of the various components (fence, cameras, detection). Conduct a test by having a person enter the detected area and check the alarming chain.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The perimeter protection includes multiple staggered defense lines and measures against intentional violent overcoming. This includes a climb-proof fence with integrated detection technology, a sterile zone with microwave or infrared barriers, and seamless coverage by PTZ cameras (Pan-Tilt-Zoom) that can automatically track intruders (Auto-Tracking).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A 3-meter high fence is equipped with a fiber-optic detection system that reports climbing attempts. Behind it is a 5-meter wide, cleared zone monitored by infrared light barriers. If a sensor is triggered, the nearest PTZ camera pans to the point, zooms in, and automatically tracks the target.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the detailed concept for multi-level perimeter protection. Review of the specifications and configuration of the various detection systems and PTZ cameras. Analysis of the logs from integration tests of the overall system.

controls.title: Planning and installation of hazard detection systems (S) [Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Individual hazard detectors (e.g., a water detector) are installed, but they only trigger a local, acoustic alarm and are not part of an overall concept.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In the basement under the server room, a water detector is lying on the floor, which starts to beep upon contact with water. There is no forwarding of the alarm.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection for the presence of individual hazard detectors. Check whether they are connected to a central system. Simulate an alarm (e.g., by moistening the water detector) to test the response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A central hazard detection system (HDS) is installed, but the transmission path to the external alarm receiving center is not designed with redundancy (e.g., only via an internet connection). If this path fails, alarms go unnoticed.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The intrusion and water detectors are connected to an HDS. This transmits alarms via the company's internet connection to a control center. If the internet fails, the alarm transmission is interrupted.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the HDS concept. Review of the technical design of the transmission path. Inquire about the procedure in case of a failure of the primary transmission path.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Based on the building's security concept, a plan is made for which hazard detection systems (HDS) are needed for which areas. The handling of alarm messages is defined. An HDS suitable for the intended purpose is installed. The messages from the HDS MUST be transmitted to an alarm receiving center, which must be reachable at all times and able to react appropriately to the threat.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An HDS concept defines that intrusion, water, and unauthorized access are monitored. The HDS is connected to a certified emergency call and service control center (NSL). The contract with the NSL defines clear action plans for each alarm type. The concept is adapted when the use of rooms changes.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the HDS concept and the contract with the NSL, including the action plans. Check whether the concept is up-to-date and matches the building's use. Trigger a test alarm to verify the NSL's response.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The transmission path between the deployed HDS and the alarm receiving center SHOULD be designed with redundancy in accordance with the Technical Connection Conditions (TAB) and where possible. All existing transmission paths MUST be tested regularly. The concept SHOULD always be adapted when the use of building areas changes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The HDS is connected to the NSL via two independent paths, e.g., primarily via a leased line (IP) and secondarily via the mobile network (4G/5G). The system automatically tests both transmission paths daily. The test results are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the technical design of the HDS for redundant transmission paths. Request for the logs of the automatic path tests. Simulate the failure of the primary path to verify the automatic switchover to the secondary path.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A high-quality, certified HDS (e.g., VdS Class C) is used. Alarms are not only forwarded to an external location but also trigger automated local responses through integration with other security systems, such as activating video recordings, locking areas, or switching on additional lighting.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: In case of a nighttime intrusion alarm, all lights in the affected area are automatically switched on, all exterior doors are locked, and the PTZ cameras record the area. This coupling maximizes the chances of securing evidence and identifying perpetrators.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the certificate of certification for the HDS. Review the configuration of the couplings between the HDS and other systems (e.g., video, access control). Perform an integration test to verify the correct triggering of the automated local responses.

controls.title: Use of an emergency power system (S) [Planners, Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A mobile emergency power generator is available but not permanently connected or regularly tested. In an emergency, manual connection and startup are required, leading to long downtimes.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A diesel generator on a trailer is in the garage. The cables for connection are lying next to it. No one has practiced connecting and starting it since it was purchased.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the generator and connection devices. Request for test logs and process descriptions for emergencies. Questioning of staff about the procedure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A permanently installed emergency power system (EPS) is in place and tested weekly at no-load. However, no tests are performed under load, so it is unclear whether the EPS can carry the full load of the data center in an emergency.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The EPS starts automatically every Monday at 10 a.m. and runs for 15 minutes without load. The operating hours and fuel level are logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the logs of the weekly test runs. Check whether load tests are also documented in the logs. If not, the requirement is only met at a basic level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The power supply of a data center SHOULD be supplemented by an emergency power system (EPS). If an EPS is used, it MUST be regularly maintained. The fuel supply of an EPS MUST be regularly checked to ensure it is sufficient and still usable. For a server room, a UPS with an appropriate autonomy time SHOULD be implemented as an alternative.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An EPS is installed that stores enough fuel for at least 24 hours of full-load operation. There is a maintenance contract that includes annual inspections. The fuel level is checked monthly. A sample of the fuel is tested annually for contaminants (e.g., diesel bug).

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the EPS concept and the maintenance and inspection logs. Review of the logs for fuel level and quality checks. For server rooms: Review of the design and autonomy time of the alternative UPS solution.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: During regular maintenance, load and functional tests as well as test runs under load MUST also be carried out. The refueling processes for fuels MUST be logged, including the type of fuel, additives used, date of refueling, and quantity. If possible, low-sulfur heating oil SHOULD be used instead of diesel fuel to avoid the so-called diesel bug.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: At least once a year, a load test is performed in which the EPS takes over the actual load of the data center for at least one hour. This is done through a planned switchover. A detailed fueling log is kept. Only low-sulfur heating oil is used, and a biocide additive is mixed in.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the logs of the annual load tests. Review of the fueling log for completeness and traceability. Check which fuel type is used.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The data center has two or more redundant emergency power systems in a 2N configuration. The fuel is kept in a clean state by an automatic filtering and polishing system. The monthly load tests are carried out under the full load of the data center for an extended period (e.g., 4 hours).

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Two identical EPSs are installed, each of which can carry the entire data center load. An automatic fuel treatment system continuously circulates the fuel through filters and water separators. The monthly tests are performed fully automatically, and the results (voltage, frequency, load) are logged in the DCIM system.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the power supply architecture for EPS redundancy (2N). Request for the specification and operating logs of the fuel treatment system. Analysis of the logs of the monthly 4-hour full-load tests.

controls.title: Surge protection device (S) [Planners, Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Only commercially available surge protection power strips are used for the IT devices. An overarching protection concept does not exist.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The servers are connected to power strips with integrated surge protection. The building's electrical installation itself has no protection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the racks and power distribution. Check the electrical distribution boards for the presence of central surge protection devices (SPDs).

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A coarse protection (Type 1 SPD) is installed at the building entrance. However, a coordinated system with medium (Type 2) and fine protection (Type 3) closer to the end devices is missing. This can lead to insufficient protection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A lightning current arrester (Type 1) is installed in the main distribution board of the building. However, further protection levels are missing in the sub-distribution boards for the data center and at the racks themselves.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check the main and sub-distribution boards for the presence of Type 1, 2, and 3 SPDs. Check if a coordinated protection concept is in place.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A basic but documented surge protection concept is implemented. This includes at least a coordinated coarse and medium protection (Type 1 and Type 2 SPD) for the power supply of the data center. All surge protection devices are regularly subjected to a visual inspection.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: An electrical contractor has created and implemented a simple protection concept. A combined arrester Type 1+2 is installed in the main distribution board. The function of the SPDs is checked as part of the annual electrical inspection.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the surge protection concept and the logs of the electrical inspections. Review of the documentation for the coordination of the protection levels.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A lightning and surge protection concept SHOULD be created based on the currently valid standard (DIN EN 62305 Parts 1 to 4). The lightning protection zones (LPZ) required for the proper operation of the data center must be defined. For all required facilities, this SHOULD be at least LPZ 2. All surge protection equipment SHOULD be subjected to a comprehensive inspection once a year in accordance with DIN EN 62305-3, Table E.2.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A lightning protection specialist has created a detailed protection concept according to DIN EN 62305. This defines the lightning protection zones LPZ 0A, 0B, 1, and 2. A coordinated system of Type 1, 2, and 3 SPDs is installed for all lines leading into the data center (power, data, climate). The annual inspection by a specialist company is documented.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for the detailed lightning and surge protection concept according to DIN EN 62305. Review of the planning documents for the definition of the LPZ. Request for the logs of the annual, comprehensive inspection.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The protection concept is fully implemented with coordinated SPDs of Types 1, 2, and 3. All SPDs are equipped with remote signaling, which reports their functional or defect status to the BMS/DCIM system. This allows for proactive replacement of defective protection modules before the protective effect is impaired.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: All installed SPDs have a signaling contact. This is connected to the central monitoring system. If an SPD fails or reaches its end of life, a fault ticket for its replacement is automatically generated.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check of the technical specification of the SPDs for the presence of remote signaling contacts. Check of the monitoring system's configuration for monitoring these contacts. Simulate a failure (if possible) to test the reporting chain.

controls.title: Air conditioning in the data center (S) [Planners]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Comfort air conditioning (standard office air conditioners) is used, which is not designed for 24/7 continuous operation or the high sensible heat load of IT equipment. This often leads to failures and inadequate cooling.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A mobile air conditioner or a split air conditioner from a hardware store is used for cooling. The condensation water must be emptied manually.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Visual inspection of the installed air conditioning units. Check of the technical data to determine if they are precision air conditioning units for IT use.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A dedicated precision air conditioning unit is installed, but it is only a single unit without redundancy (N configuration). If this unit fails, the entire cooling system fails.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: A single air conditioning unit, designed for IT operations, cools the server room. There is no backup unit. A failure inevitably leads to rapid overheating.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Check the number of installed air conditioning units. Request the air conditioning concept to check the redundancy design. If only one unit is present, the requirement is only met at a basic level.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: It SHOULD be ensured that suitable climatic conditions are created and maintained in the data center. The air conditioning SHOULD be sufficiently dimensioned for the data center.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Precision air conditioning units are installed, their total capacity covers the calculated maximum heat load of the data center with a safety margin. The design is documented. The airflow is designed to achieve uniform cooling of the racks.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the planning documents for the air conditioning system, including the heat load calculation. Compare the calculated load with the installed cooling capacity. Check the airflow in the data center for plausibility.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: All relevant values (temperature, humidity) SHOULD be constantly monitored. If a value deviates from the norm, an alarm SHOULD be automatically triggered. The air conditioning systems in IT operating areas SHOULD be designed to be as fail-safe as possible, e.g., through N+1 redundancy.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Three air conditioning units are installed, although two would be sufficient for the maximum load (N+1). If one unit fails, the other two take over the full load. The temperature is monitored at several points in the room and in case of deviations, an automatic notification is sent to the on-call service.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Review of the redundancy concept (N+1) of the air conditioning system. Check the configuration of monitoring and alerting. Simulate the failure of an air conditioning unit (if possible) to test load transfer and alerting.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: A fully redundant (2N) cooling system is in use, often combining different technologies (e.g., chilled water system and direct expansion). Cold aisle or hot aisle containment is implemented to maximize efficiency. The entire system is dynamically controlled by a DCIM platform based on real-time temperature data at the rack level.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Two completely independent cooling systems (A and B supply) serve the data center. The cold aisles are physically contained. The DCIM software regulates the air conditioning units to keep the supply air temperature at the rack fronts constant at 22°C, which maximizes energy efficiency.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the planning documents for the 2N cooling system and the containment. Check the configuration of the DCIM control. Analyze the historical temperature and efficiency data (PUE) to assess the effectiveness of the control.

controls.title: Performing functional tests of the technical infrastructure (S) [Building services]

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Functional tests are only performed reactively, after an incident has revealed a weakness in the interaction of the systems.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: After the emergency power system failed to start during a power outage, a test was conducted. There are no regular, proactive tests.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request for logs of planned, regular functional tests. Comparison of data from fault reports and subsequent tests.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Regular functional tests of individual components are carried out (e.g. a UPS test, a generator no-load test). However, the interaction of the systems in a complete response chain is not tested.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: The UPS is tested monthly and the generator weekly. However, it has never been tested whether the UPS holds the load long enough until the generator has started and taken over the load.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the test protocols. Check whether the tests cover only individual components or the interaction of several systems.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: The technical infrastructure of a data center SHOULD be tested regularly (at least once or twice a year) as well as after system modifications and extensive repairs. The results SHOULD be documented.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Planned functional tests of the most important infrastructure components are carried out semi-annually. After the replacement of a UPS module, an unscheduled test is scheduled. All tests and their results are documented in a central log.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the test plan and test logs from the last two years. Check if additional tests were performed after major changes to the infrastructure.

parts.name: statement
parts.prose: Especially entire reaction chains SHOULD be subjected to a real functional test. The tests are comprehensive and simulate, for example, a failure of the public power supply to verify the seamless transition from grid to UPS and then to the emergency power system and back.

parts.name: guidance
parts.prose: Once a year, a 'pull-the-plug' test is performed, during which the main power supply to the data center is intentionally shut down. The entire reaction chain (switchover to UPS, start of the emergency power system, load transfer to the emergency power system, synchronization, and switch back to the grid) is tested under real load, and the times and parameters are precisely logged.

parts.name: assessment-method
parts.prose: Request the detailed test plans and protocols for the tests of the complete reaction chains. Check the recorded parameters (e.g., switchover times, voltage and frequency stability) for compliance with the setpoints.

parts.name: statement
